items.statement: Revenue growth guidance maintained at 15% for FY25
items.quote: We would like to maintain the guidance we have given already in our previous con call, which will be 15%. So, revenue growth will be around 15% compared to last year for the full year.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance maintained at Rs 25,000 crore for FY25
items.quote: This guidance for this year what we had promised 25,000 crores, we will definitely retain that and we will meet this expectation and we will get this orders of 25,000 crores.

items.statement: Order book stands at Rs 76,705 crore as of 31 July 2024
items.quote: The order book position as on 31.7.2024 is Rs.76,705 crores.

items.statement: Order inflow of Rs 4,800 crore plus received in Q1 FY25

So, around 4,800 crores plus orders we have received in the last quarter.

items.statement: Major orders executed in Q1 include LRSAM Rs 842 crore, CBIT Rs 300 crore, Hammer Missile Rs 235 crore
items.quote: One of them is LRSAM, which we are anyway executing year-by-year. But this quarter we have achieved around 842 crores through this particular project. Then this CBIT project which is our Civilian Sector-1 project which we are doing for Central Board of Indirect Taxes, etc., For them around 300 crores worth of order we executed. One Hammer Missile System we had executed around 235 crores.

items.statement: Expected major orders in FY25 include ADFT, EW suite for Mi-17 V5, security and surveillance system for army, mountain radar, MFR X-band radar, EW system for ground based, each Rs 1,000-2,500 crore
items.quote: are going to get this year some major order, one is ADFT or Apulia. We are expecting that order very soon, then EW suite for our Mi-17 V5 for which the trial has been almost at the last stage we are going to get RFP soon, then security and surveillance system for army that is for their army depots, etc., we are expecting a good order from that, mountain radar also, a good order is BH/lMTElECTfiON/

items.statement: QRSAM order expected Rs 25,000 crore plus in April-June 2025
items.quote: No, we are expecting more than 25,000 crores order for QRSAM, but the value may change based on the final configuration, number of regiments, number of missiles to be added as per regiment, etc., that is a strategic call which our Indian Air Force and Indian Army are taking.

items.statement: Base order inflow expected at Rs 25,000 crore each for FY25 and FY26 excluding QRSAM
items.quote: What we are doing is excluding QRSAM, the base order of current year is expected to be 25,000 crores and next year also 25,000 crores expected excluding QRSAM. So, both the year it will be 50,000 crores.

items.statement: Sukhoi-30 upgrade first batch (84-100 jets) expected to bring Rs 4,000-5,000 crore order for BEL
items.quote: If I am not wrong 230 upgrade right now is planned for first 84 or 100 numbers only. And after that only they will go to the next batch. So, this first one itself, we are expecting this much order quantity to us.

items.statement: Kavach opportunity estimated Rs 20,000-30,000 crore over 5-6 years, Rs 4,000-5,000 crore per year for BEL after 2 years
items.quote: Kavach is actually a very big program. And right now, I believe railways is struggling with the supplies, means, the vendors are not able to supply the quantities. Knowing BEL infrastructure and capability to invest further by BEL, that's why railways has come forward to us for this development. But it will take, as I said earlier also some 18 to 24 months to start generating business or revenues

items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 800 crore for FY25 for new factories at Palasamudram, Nimmakuru, Hyderabad, Nagpur and capital equipment
items.quote: CAPEX is around 800 crores is planned during the current year. On what areas, are we planning to do this CAPEX on? There are quite a few factories coming up as you may be knowing already; one is coming up in Palasamudram , one is already almost completed in Nimmakuru, one more is coming up in Hyderabad, Ibrahimpatnam, so 3-4 factories are coming up, one more is coming up in Nagpur. In addition to

items.statement: Machilipatnam unit operational in FY25, Nimmakuru completed, other new factories operational next year
items.quote: In FY'25 the Machilipatnam unit will be operational, Nimmakuru what we are talking, all others will be in the next year only.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin around 41-42%, not 45%
items.quote: Current quarter, the gross margin is around 41%, 42% only, not 45, and going forward as we have already guided the EBITDA margin, I mean effectively will be around 23% to 25% is the guidance which we maintain for the current year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue mix: services 11%, goods 89%
items.quote: Presently, during the 1st Quarter, the services are around 11% and goods were around 89%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 segment mix: defence 84%, non-defence 14%, exports 2%
items.quote: This defense is 84% during the current quarter, non-defense is 14% and exports is 2%.

items.statement: Order book mix: defence 85.8%, non-defence 11.3%, exports 2.9%
items.quote: Percentage wise defense is around 85.8% and non-defense is around 11.3% and around 2.9% is export. So, that is the breakup between the defense, non-defense and export for this order book which we have currently.

items.statement: Long-term mix expected at 85% defence, 15% non-defence
items.quote: So, typically we are earning average is 85%-15%, 85% is defense, 15% is non-defense, minor 1% or 2% variations are there between these combinations because of the different type of product mix sometimes it happens but on an average it is 85%-15%.

items.statement: Repeat orders ~50%, new orders ~50% of expected Rs 50,000 crore base inflow over FY25-26
items.quote: Around 50% you can assume as a repeat order, 50% is the new order

items.statement: 70-80% of future orders expected to be single tender/nomination due to R&D investments
items.quote: Nomination as of now because we only have put all the efforts, and these are the strategic programs where we had put for last six to eight years R&D efforts. So, many of these programs are single tender for us, because we only have done all the investments in that. So, as of now I think out of what we have or what is the future projection, around 70% to 80% we are expecting to be single tender.

items.statement: Major exports: TR modules to Thales (€25.75 million order), onboard naval equipment to L&T/SEZ, Airbus T295, solar plants Guatemala, Compass from Israel
items.quote: Recently, we have received an export order of €25.75 million, that was from TRDS. So, that is for supply of TR modules for various airborne platforms for them.

items.statement: Positive Indigenisation Lists at system/subsystem level on track; component-level indigenisation will take 5-10 years
items.quote: Our experience of the entire PIL is very, very good, because these PILs are at system and subsystem level. So, these system and subsystems which were earlier imported, now we have indigenous capability to develop them either our own or with the help of DRDO. So, that confidence we have given to our defense users and that's why they have come out with these PIL based on our capabilities. So, system

items.statement: Order book to revenue ratio expected at 2-3x
items.quote: And 70,000 order book generally we are expecting to have a order book to revenue ratio of two to three times.

items.statement: Israel supply chain issues for missile programs largely overcome, volume catch-up underway
items.quote: The situation was a problem but we are in the right direction and it is under control now. There were some challenges because of some supplies of subsystems from Israel as you have rightly told. But that challenge is now overcome, now it is the volume game to catch up again for this. So, that is happening.

items.statement: MoU with Rosoboronexport for upgraded fuses for Russian ammunition; business volume details in 6-9 months
items.quote: Firstly, this is a totally different product than whatever products we have handled till date. But it is a similar product like you can say it is an upgraded version of the fuses what we are supplying and it is for the different type of ammunition. We have just signed an MoU right now. The details of the business volume, work share, keeping the indigenization content more than 50% those detailed d

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 guidance: 15% revenue growth, 23-25% EBITDA margin, minimum Rs 25,000 crore order inflow
items.quote: So, future outlook as was told earlier, we are committed to that, that revenue growth of 15%, the EBITDA margin of 23% to 25% and order inflow of minimum 25,000 crores. So, these three definitely we are giving further guidance or reassuring that we are going to achieve this target in this year.

items.statement: SG&A expected at 27.5-28% of sales for full fiscal
items.quote: We expect our SG&A to be in the range of 27.5% to 28% for the full fiscal.

items.statement: R&D spend expected at 8.5-9% of sales for full fiscal
items.quote: Overall, R&D continues to be a cornerstone of our growth strategy and we expect the investment to be in range of 8.5 to 9% for the full fiscal.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected at 24-25% for fiscal
items.quote: We expect our normal ETR to be in the range of 24% to 25% for the fiscal.

items.statement: US generics business expected to grow in single digits year-on-year excluding lenalidomide
items.quote: We have the capability - and I'm excluding even lenalidomide in this kind of discussion - to grow in single digit, meaning, to compensate for any price erosion on a year-to-year basis.

items.statement: India base business expected to grow double digits for the year
items.quote: The baseline of India, without acquisitions, will be double digits this year.

items.statement: Capital investments of Rs 491 crores in Q1FY25
items.quote: Our capital investments in this quarter stood at Rs. 491 crores, which is $59 million.

items.statement: Bachupally biologics facility expansion to 50 KL over next two years from current 15 KL
items.quote: The intent is to become something like 50 kilolitre in that facility. This probably will take us additional two years to reach that level.

items.statement: Aurigene CDMO biologics facility investment of few hundred crores
items.quote: The level of investment is a few hundreds of crores, I don't remember exactly how much.

items.statement: Aurigene inaugurated 70,000 sq.ft. CDMO biologics facility in Hyderabad
items.quote: Our CDMO, Aurigene Pharmaceutical Services, inaugurated a 70,000 sq.ft. state-of-the-art CDMO biologics facility in Genome Valley, Hyderabad, India.

items.statement: Bachupally facility current capacity 15 KL targeting 50 KL
items.quote: I think 15, if I remember, 15 KL.

items.statement: Nicotinell acquisition expected to close early Q4 CY2024 adding ~$300M revenue
items.quote: The transaction is expected to close in early Q4 of the calendar year 2024 and operations will transition to us in a phased approach.

items.statement: Consumer healthcare portfolio currently ~$320M, with Nicotinell addition reaching $600M+
items.quote: The new acquisition, once completed, will be somewhere around a US$300 million, so altogether it is US$600 million-plus and growing.

items.statement: Nestlé JV operational from August 1st combining both companies' nutraceutical products
items.quote: Progressing very nicely and we hope that in the beginning of August we can announce 'Day 1', likely, August 1st, but we will announce when it will come.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 170bps YoY and 183bps QoQ to 60.4% on favorable mix and overhead leverage
items.quote: Consolidated Gross Profit Margin stood at 60.4% for the quarter, an increase of 170 basis points over the same quarter in the previous year and 183 basis points sequentially.

items.statement: US generics pricing pressures partly offset by volume growth and market share gains
items.quote: The increase was largely volume led, coupled with higher market share in certain products, partly offset by pricing pressures in some key products.

items.statement: Freight cost spike of Rs 50-60 crores due to Red Sea route issues
items.quote: It should be around Rs. 50 crores or Rs. 60 crores or something like that.

items.statement: USFDA issued Form 483 with 2 observations at Duvvada formulations facilities and 4 observations at Srikakulam API facility
items.quote: In May, the USFDA completed a routine GMP inspection at two of our formulations manufacturing facilities in Duvvada, Vizag and issued a Form 483 with two observations. In June, the USFDA completed a GMP inspection at our API manufacturing facility in Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh and issued a Form 483 with four observations.

items.statement: Will address and resolve USFDA observations within stipulated timelines
items.quote: We will address and resolve the issues within the stipulated timelines.

items.statement: Operating working capital increased Rs 262 crores to Rs 11,555 crores
items.quote: Operating working capital as of 30th June 2024 was Rs. 11,555 crores, which is $1,387 million, an increase of Rs. 262 crores, which is $31 million over 31st March 2024.

items.statement: Lower free cash flow due to factoring rollback in US markets
items.quote: The reason the free cash flow is a bit on the lower side is because of fluctuation in factoring. You know, we do the factoring in various markets, largely in the US, depending on the interest rates and the benefit we get.

items.statement: Net surplus cash of Rs 6,731 crores ($808M) as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Consequently, we now have a net surplus cash of Rs. 6,731 crores, i.e. $808 million as on June 30, 2024.

items.statement: Financial capacity of ~$2.5B for inorganic investments without rating impact
items.quote: Indeed, a very important strategic, question. First, we believe that we have about US$2.5 billion that we can invest inorganically. That depends, of course, on the time, but we have enough financial capacity without even changing dramatically ratings or anything like that.

items.statement: Nicotinell acquisition to close early Q4 CY2024; more consumer healthcare assets planned
items.quote: Likely, that we want to build on the platform of the NRT acquisition and to add more assets in the future.

items.statement: India acquisitions only if returns exceed cost of capital; not buying EBITDA at current valuations
items.quote: If the deal is better than our cost of capital, absolutely, we'll do it. And India will be absolutely a priority.

items.statement: Annualized ROCE at 33%
items.quote: Reported EBITDA margins stood at 28% and annualized ROCE stood at 33%.

items.statement: Red Sea shipping disruptions causing air freight costs; duration uncertain
items.quote: So most of it is related to, obviously, the conflict in the Middle East. We need to circle Africa and in some of the cases, because of the timeline, we need to fly material, instead of shipping it by sea.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance: telecom equipment segment ~Rs.2,000 crore (vs Rs.143 crore FY24); passive connectivity solutions Rs.250 crore (vs Rs.66 crore FY24), targeting Rs.750 crore in 2-3 years; overall revenue growth 25-30% YoY
items.quote: With the introduction of new products and markets, our revenue from Telecom Equipment Segment is expected to rise substantially. We expect the revenue from this segment during FY25 to reach approximately Rs.2000 crores from just Rs.143 crores in FY24.

items.statement: FY26-28 outlook: expects 20-30% annual revenue growth; telecom equipment, fiber optic cable, and EPC each targeting ~Rs.3,000 crore in three years
items.quote: In three years' timeframe our telecom equipment business should be around INR3,000 crores. Similar number would be the fiber optic cables. Similar number would be the EPC business.

items.statement: Total order book ~Rs.6,776 crore as of Q1 FY25; revenue mix shifted favorably toward products; private customers 51%, international 9.82%
items.quote: Our total order book now stands at ~ INR 6776 crores as on Q1 of FY25. While our order book has been stable, revenue mix has favourably changed towards products business.

items.statement: Strong demand for 5G FWA CPE (Rs.623 crore order received); UBRs: >500,000 units delivered globally, >70% India market share; BSNL ordered 30,000 UBRs for 4G backhaul
items.quote: HFCL has already received an order worth Rs.623 crores of this equipment.

items.statement: Optical fiber cable demand in temporary global slowdown; expects recovery from Q3/Q4 FY25; BharatNet Phase III tender ~Rs.60,000 crore capex + Rs.40,000 crore O&M over 10 years
items.quote: It is expected that globally Optical Fiber Cable market will start witnessing growth again from the last quarter of financial year 2024-25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 16.00% (vs 15.78% Q4 FY24, 16.04% Q1 FY24); PAT margin 9.55% (vs 8.25% Q4 FY24, 7.59% Q1 FY24); telecom products net margin ~8-10% plus PLI benefit
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 185 crores as compared to INR 209 crores in Q4FY24 and INR 160 crores in Q1FY24; EBITDA margin stands at 16.00% for Q1FY25 as compared to 15.78% for Q4FY24 and it stood at 16.04% in Q1FY24.

items.statement: OFC capacity utilization ~45% in Q1 FY25 due to global slowdown; margins pressured but expected to improve in next 2 quarters as demand recovers
items.quote: So capacity utilization is just 45%, 50% this quarter. So that is impacting the overall margin of this product segment.

items.statement: Fiber capacity expanding from 14M to 33.9M fiber km; cable capacity from 25M to 35M fiber km; Poland plant ~Rs.145 crore for 3.5M fiber km cable, commercialization within CY25 (~9 months)
items.quote: Current capacity for fiber is about 1 4 million fiber kilometers which is getting into 33.9 million. Cable was 25 million which is getting into 35 million.

items.statement: Preform plant (backward integration) under active evaluation; make vs buy decision expected in 1-2 months; involves large capex and supply sustainability considerations
items.quote: We are under discussions for this because it involves a reasonably large capex. So we are discussing at this point of time the capacity which we should install and the capex per ton or per kg, whatever you call it, of plant which should be there to make it economically viable against the purchases.

items.statement: European Commission exempted HFCL and HTL from anti-dumping duty on OFC (others face 8-11% duty); verdict dated 14 June 2024 after extensive verification
items.quote: In a landmark verdict on 14th June, 2024, the European Commission has decided not to impose anti -dumping duty on optical fiber cables manufactured by HFCL and its subsidiary HTL, whereas provisional anti -dumping duty has already been imposed on all other Indian Optical Fiber Cable Manufacturers.

items.statement: Eligible for Design-Linked Incentive (DLI) of 6% (vs 5% PLI) on telecom/networking products; total eligible ~Rs.650 crore; benefits expected from current fiscal year
items.quote: The total is about INR650 crores we are eligible for . We will start getting it from the current financial year itself because our is not PLI, but DLI. It is de sign-linked incentive, which is 1% higher than the PLI

items.statement: Telecom products revenue share 61.42% in Q1 FY25 (vs 27.33% Q4 FY24, 66.56% Q1 FY24); OFC & related 44%, telecom & networking 56% of segment revenue
items.quote: Segment revenue for telecom produc ts during the quarter stood at 61.42 % as compared to 27.33% in Q4 FY24 and 66.56% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: New products: 5G FWA CPE (first Indian IPR), UBRs up to 2 Gbps (target 4 Gbps), Wi-Fi 7 APs, IP/MPLS routers, defence fuzes, thermal sights, surveillance radars, high-fiber-count cables for data centers (1,764F developed, 3,400F under trial
items.quote: Our comprehensive, new cutting -edge products such as the first Indian IPR owned and Made -in-India 5G Fixed Wireless Access Customer Premises Equipment, Unlicensed Band Backhaul Radios, Switches, IP/MPLS Routers, open -source Wi -Fi 7 Access Points, new generation defence products such as Electronics Fuzes, Thermal Weapon Sights for Assault Rifles, Light Machine Guns and Rocket Launchers, Ground

items.statement: BSNL payment cycle improved to twice monthly; BSNL ordered 30,000 UBRs; BharatNet Phase III tender via BSNL (~Rs.60,000 crore capex) with USO fund backing
items.quote: Moreover, with this improved financial position, BSNL's payment situation for their own tenders have improved substantially. What we earlier had a situation where payments were not coming from BSNL, now BSNL is releasing payment twice a month, which is a very much improved situation what we had experienced last year or even in the beginn ing of the current year.

items.statement: Electronic fuze export inquiries mainly from European region; advanced discussions, expect sizeable export order book in current fiscal
items.quote: We have received inquiries and we are in advanced stage of discussion, mainly from European region, and we expect good results very soon.

items.statement: UBR market leadership: >70% share in India, >500,000 units globally; UBRs cheaper than E-band/microwave, save spectrum cost; anti-dumping exemption gives price advantage in EU vs Indian peers (8-11% duty) and Chinese competitors
items.quote: HFCL has become the largest supplier of UBRs in India and one of the prominent global supplier, having delivered over 500,000 units globally. HFCL now dominates over 70% of the UBR market in India.

items.statement: BharatNet Phase III: ~10 lakh km OFC opportunity (~Rs.5,000-6,000 crore); EPC portion ~2x cable; equipment (routers, optical) similar magnitude; ducts/other ~Rs.5,000-6,000 crore
items.quote: OFC component we are expecting a total it is being under some bit of a revision by government itself, but assuming certain numbers we expect about something like 10 lakh kilometers of optical fiber cable. So if you take a price of roughly about INR50,000 per kilometer so it's roughly about INR5,000 crores to INR6,000 crores of fiber optic cable opportunity.

items.statement: Global OFC slowdown due to geopolitics, high inventory, delayed govt programs, capital/logistics costs; temporary impact on revenue and margins; polymer compound manufacturing discontinued (buy cheaper at ~Rs.6/kg lower)
items.quote: Presently, Global optical fiber cable market is going through a relatively slowdown phase. Geopolitical situation throughout the world and its impact on important aspects of business i.e. cost of raising capital, cost of logistics, large inventory built with operators and delay in major government funded programs have resulted in this temporary slowdown.

items.statement: Promoter shares: no pledged shares; 44.5% shown as pledge is actually non-disposable undertaking to financial institutions for company loans; representations made to exchanges/depositories to correct format
items.quote: There is not a single share of the HFCL which is pledged anywhere let me be very clear. This is only non disposable undertaking. There is no pledge.

items.statement: Drone detection radar field trials expected by end of Q2 FY25; BMP-2 armament upgrade RFP expected soon after clearing User Trial Readiness Review (only 5 companies shortlisted)
items.quote: Our Drone detection Radar is also in advanced stage of development. Its field trial is expected to start by the end of Q2 of FY25.

items.statement: HTL wire harness BU performing well: supplying PDUs, APUs, wire harness assemblies for fighter aircraft, battle tanks, APCs, missile launchers, towed guns, military radar/communication systems
items.quote: The wire harness bus iness unit of HTL, a subsidiary company, has been consistently performing well by supplying Power Distribution Units, Auxiliary Power Supply Units and Wire Harness Assemblies for various defence programs like Fighter Aircrafts, Battle Tanks, Armoured Personnel Carriers, Missile Launchers, Towed Gun Systems, Military Radar Systems and Military Communication Systems.

items.statement: AI integration planned for telecom/networking products to enhance resilience, reliability, security for network providers and end users
items.quote: We also plan to integrate Artificial Intelligence to our Telecom and Networking products which will enhance the experience for network service providers as well as en d users.

items.statement: Stopped taking lower-margin EPC orders to conserve working capital and trained manpower; turnkey margins vary (8-25%), long-term target ~10% PBT
items.quote: We don't take any lower margin orders of EPC. We have left away a number of such contracts because we are not interested in wasting our resources, manpower, trained manpower as well as working capital on contracts which are of a lower margin.

items.statement: Export revenue target of Rs.1,500 crore for OFC not achievable this year due to global demand slowdown; overall OFC revenue (India+abroad) expected ~Rs.2,000 crore vs Rs.2,800 crore two years ago
items.quote: No, it would not happen this year because, as I said, the global demand has gone down. So it will be considerably lower. And overall revenue from fiber optic cable business is expected in India and abroad both about INR2,000 crores, what we had about IN R2,800 crores 2 years back because of the lower revenue from the global market.

items.statement: Raddef Private Limited (subsidiary) developing advanced surveillance radars using FMCW technology; participated in ISRO RFP for coastal surveillance; Indian Navy visited Bangalore R&D facility and expressed appreciation
items.quote: HFCL, through its subsidiary, Raddef Private Limited, has been at the forefront of designing and developing a range of cutting -edge surveillance radars to meet diverse operational needs.

items.statement: Non-agri segment targeting 20% volume growth for FY25
items.quote: Yes, the focus has been on that segment, and we are still slated to grow aggressively in that segment.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance of INR 150 crores; expansion plan to be finalized next quarter
items.quote: We normally have a capex guidance of almost INR 150 crores for the year. And as soon as we have the plan for this expansion ready, we will be announcing it.

items.statement: New capacity addition of 100,000-150,000 metric tons per annum planned; lead time 18-24 months
items.quote: All our plants are approximately 100,000 to 150,000 metric tons each per annum capacity. We believe that this business thrives on scale. And any where between 100,000 and 150,000 is what we typically plan for additional capacities.

items.statement: Incremental capacity of 5-10% possible through debottlenecking in 6-8 months at Ratnagiri and Masar
items.quote: So up to about 5% to 10% would be what we'll be able to.

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings capacity ~470,000 metric tons annually; peak monthly production 30,000 tons pipes, 3,500 tons fittings
items.quote: Yes, it's approximately 4,70,000 metric tons, Pipes & Fittings together.

items.statement: Plants operating at 80-85% utilization; practical max ~85% of rated capacity
items.quote: We have been operating anywhere between 80% and 85% in our plants.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 Pipes & Fittings volume 90,620 metric tons, down 1.69% YoY; revenue INR 1,123 crores, down 2.67% YoY
items.quote: Volume in the segment decreased marginally by 1.69% year -on-year to 90,620 metric tons in Q1 FY '25 against 92,181 metric tons in corresponding last quarter.

items.statement: PVC Resin volume up 51.11% YoY to 69,625 metric tons; revenue INR 548.23 crores
items.quote: Volume in the segment increased significantly by 51.11% to 69,625 metric tons in Q1 FY '25 against 46,074 metric tons in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings EBIT per kg improved to INR 14-15 range from INR 7-8 previously; driven by product mix shift to Non-agri and Fittings
items.quote: Now we are in the INR 14 to INR 15 EBIT per kg. And these will improve as we further improve the product mix.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 18.12% in Q1 FY25 vs 12.93% in Q1 FY24; driven by operational efficiency and controlled discounts
items.quote: EBITDA margin during this quarter stood at 18.12% compared to 12.93% in corresponding previous quarter of Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: PVC price Q1 FY25 avg $855 vs $805 in Q1 FY24; PVC/EDC delta $533 vs $468; PVC/VCM delta $184 vs $133
items.quote: If you look at the PVC price, in Q1 FY '24, the average price was about $ 805, whereas in Q1 FY '25, it was $ 855, the average.

items.statement: Current PVC price $820 (25 July 2024); PVC/EDC delta $480; PVC/VCM delta $80
items.quote: If you were to look at the prices as of now, probably 25th of July 2024, the PVC prices had come down to $ 820. The PVC/EDC delta was $ 480 and the PVC/VCM delta had come down to $ 80.

items.statement: EDC stocking strategy changed; no longer storing large quantities before monsoon, insulating from price fluctuations
items.quote: Now we have found alternative solutions for that. And therefore, we don't have to store EDC in large quantities, and therefore, insulate ourselves from huge price fluctuations.

items.statement: Agri/Non-agri volume mix 70/30 in Q1 FY25; target 50/50 in 3-4 years; Fittings contribution 3-4% in Agri vs 15-25% in Non-agri
items.quote: For this quarter, it is 70/30.

items.statement: Fittings capacity increased ~25% in March 2024; focus on growing Non-agri and Fittings sales for margin improvement
items.quote: If you remember, last March, we had our Fittings capacity increased by almost 25%.

items.statement: Dealer network ~900, retail network ~30,000; retail network growing faster than dealer network
items.quote: We already have, approximately, dealer network of s900 and retail network of almost 30,000. So the reach will continue to increase.

items.statement: Not pursuing PVC-O pipes; focusing on UPVC and CPVC only; watching market development of new products
items.quote: So we are currently focusing on UPVC and CPVC only at this point of time. The new products which are coming into the market, it's under observation.

items.statement: BIS norms for PVC may impact pricing; implementation timeline uncertain (possible August-September or postponement)
items.quote: So it is much more of a wait and watch as to whether the BIS norms come into effect immediately, or it is likely to see a further postponement as we have seen sometime in the past.

items.statement: Debtor days: Non-agri 60-70 days, Agri 0 days; channel inventory at normalized levels
items.quote: Credit days for the debtor days is roughly around 60 to 70 days for the Non -agri sector. And Agri sector, we are at 0 credit days.

items.statement: Net cash surplus ~INR 2,400 crores as of 30 June 2024 vs INR 1,650 crores a year ago
items.quote: The company continued to have a strong balance sheet with a net cash surplus of roughly INR 2,400 crores as of 30th June 2024 compared to INR 1,650 crores in the corresponding previous year's quarter.

items.statement: No inorganic growth planned; only organic capacity expansion
items.quote: No, no. This is going to be organic growth only. We are not looking at any inorganic growth.

items.statement: Excess cash beyond expansion needs to be returned to shareholders; Board to decide
items.quote: And whatever is not needed for expansion will be given back to the shareholders.

items.statement: Early monsoon onset (June 1 vs July last year) caused significant Agri demand drop in June; Q2 typically weak quarter
items.quote: This quarter, we had rains set in quite early compared to last year. Okay? So when you act ually see, June 1 onwards we had rains set in into the country.

items.statement: PVC price volatility driven by China/US housing weakness, import inflows, BIS norms uncertainty, and logistics easing
items.quote: They are mainly driven by housing market in both China and U.S., which have shown a sign of weakness. And therefore, we have seen a lot of material coming into India and resulting in price drops.

items.statement: Resin segment EBIT INR 69.11 crores in Q1 FY25 vs INR 3.12 crores in Q1 FY24; captive consumption increasing
items.quote: EBIT in Resin segment stood at INR 69.11 crores in Q1 FY '25 compared to INR 3.12 crores in corresponding previous year's quarters.

items.statement: IMFL proprietary segment revenue growth target 12-14% in FY25
items.quote: we are targeting to grow this segment by 12 % to 14% in FY'25. This will be a mix of volume as well as price growth.

items.statement: Company EBITDA margin target 11-13% in FY25 and 13-14% in FY26
items.quote: year FY '25, we are targeting a range of 11 % to 13% in terms of EBITDA. In FY'26, we have a range of somewhere between 13% to 14

items.statement: Revenue growth target 12-14% in FY25 excluding ethanol plus ethanol addition of INR 300 cr
items.quote: Revenue guidance for FY'25, our revenue should grow with 12% to 14% on top line apart from ethanol. So ethanol will give additional 300.

items.statement: Revenue growth target 13-14% in FY26
items.quote: in FY'26, the overall revenue should grow between 13% to 14%, the similar range.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 11%, flat YoY but up 300 bps QoQ despite higher grain prices
items.quote: Our EBITDA stood at INR 28 crores with EBITDA margin of 11%, which is in line with Q1 FY24 despite a significant increase in the grain prices. But there is a 300 bps margin expansion in comparison to Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Ethanol plant operating at full capacity 130 KLPD, sold 9 million litres in Q1 FY25
items.quote: this quarter we have done 9 million and so we expect this to be in a similar range. So this is the peak capacity which we have done in the quarter 1.

items.statement: FY25 capex ~INR 80 cr, FY26 capex ~INR 90 cr for UP project and bottling expansion
items.quote: FY '26, it is partly for the UP and partly we are planning to further expand our bottling plant in the existing premises. So, that work is underway. So, half will be done this year, half will be done next year. So, it is combined of that.

items.statement: UP project: land acquisition completing, bottling plant first then distillery, long project
items.quote: we have just come in the process of completion of land acquisition and that should start the project sometime next quarter and then from there, it will take some time. So, it is a long project, b ut for this year there are two, three projects in the existing factory which is going on

items.statement: Grain prices elevated, maize at INR 23,000/tonne in Q1 FY25, rising to ~24,000 in Q2
items.quote: Currently, today, we are sitting at Rs 23,000 of the maize which is coming. So, current quarter, if we have done an EBITDA on the ethanol front, it is around 7%.

items.statement: ENA realization INR 66/case, ethanol realization INR 71.8/litre (maize-based)
items.quote: ENA this quarter, average realization was around 66. And ethanol, it's a government -driven price, so currently it is 71.8.

items.statement: Launched Hillfort premium whiskey in Q1 FY25; RTD 'Culture' and tequila planned for Q2-Q4
items.quote: Q1 we have launched Hillfort. There are two, three products which are again lined up for Q2, Q3, Q4. We have RTD which is in the launch and we have the tequila in the plan. These are the products which we will be launching in Q2, Q3.

items.statement: One distributor per state; Nicobar registered in Delhi, UP, Chhattisgarh; supply starting soon
items.quote: We have one distributor in each state. We work with only one distributor.

items.statement: IMFL proprietary revenue split: 40% Madhya Pradesh, 60% Kerala, rest minimal
items.quote: IMFL proprietary, 40% will be MP, 60% will be Kerala and a miniscule number will be coming from other states, which should increase in coming quarters.

items.statement: Preferential allotment of 11 lakh warrants at INR 679/share raising ~INR 75 cr for malt plant and UP bottling-cum-distillery
items.quote: The board has approved the preferential allotment of 11 lakh share warrants to four investors to be issued at a price of INR 679 per share. Warrants arrived at further relevant provision of SEBI ICDR regulation, aggregating to approximately INR 75 crores. The fund will be used for meeting capital requirements for future expansion projects, including a major project in the pipeline, the mal t plant

items.statement: Term debt INR 65 cr as of June 2024, post-subvention cost ~4.5%, no working capital drawn
items.quote: debt currently is around INR65 crores. So, we have started repayments. As of June, it is standing at INR65 crores a nd the post subvention the debt cost will be somewhere around 4.5

items.statement: Future expansions funded via internal accruals and small debt if needed; no further equity foreseen
items.quote: we will be able to do the expansion through our debt s orry through our internal accruals and a small debt if required that two also we don't foresee there is a big number which is coming in debt. Majorly, it should be through internal accruals we will be able to do it

items.statement: IMFL proprietary volume 433,000 cases, licensed volume 387,000 cases, merchant ENA 4 million litres, ethanol 9 million litres in Q1 FY25
items.quote: IMFL proprietary volume sales for Q1 FY '25 stood at 433,000 cases. IMFL license brand volume reached to 387,000 cases. Merchant ENA sales volume was around 4 million litres. Ethanol volume sold during the quarter was 9 million litres.

items.statement: IMFL licensed price hike from INR 600 to 625 per case for FY25
items.quote: we have got a yearly increment which we get during the term. So, IMIL businesses are all licensed. So, we have got an increment from 600 to 625 this year.

items.statement: Maize cost rising from INR 21,000 to 24,000/tonne compressing ethanol EBITDA to 7%
items.quote: as we talk about right now, maize would be around 24,000.

items.statement: No plans to enter beer segment; focus remains on IMFL opportunity
items.quote: of now, nothing? Any specific reason? Anshuman Kedia: No, actually beer is a totally different beverage. As of now, there is a lot of opportunity in the IMFL segment. So, we are focusing on that

items.statement: Management expects year-end order booking for domestic 1G ethanol to be higher than previous years.
items.quote: we also have a reasonable visibility for the year-end order booking, which is likely to be higher than the previous years.

items.statement: Order intake in Q1 FY25 was Rs 8.88 billion with 58% domestic; order backlog at Rs 40.44 billion with 67% domestic.
items.quote: The order intake during the quarter was Rs. 8.88 billion, with 58% from the domestic market. Of the total order intake, 52% came from Bioenergy, 38% from engineering and the balance 10% from PHS business. The order backlog as of 30th June 2024 is at Rs. 40.44 billion comprising 67% of domestic orders.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved 291 bps YoY due to input cost moderation and revenue mix; contribution margin up ~4% with 2% from input costs and 1.5-2% from mix.
items.quote: EBITDA margin has seen an improvement of 291 basis points over corresponding quarter last year. This Improvement is on account of moderation in input cost as also the composition of revenue.

items.statement: Export orders carry higher margins than domestic as they exclude low-margin construction/EPC activities.
items.quote: in the export orders generally we undertake engineering technology and the supply of equipment, and we don't undertake the construction activity, which are generally forming a part of EPC activity, which generally happens in domestic order.

items.statement: Mangalore GenX facility dispatched first equipment; revenue ramp-up expected from H2 FY25, full potential in 2 years.
items.quote: we believe that starting from second half of this year onwards, we will see the revenue generation will start from this facility.

items.statement: Mangalore facility full revenue potential of Rs 2000-2500 crore expected within 2 years from production start.
items.quote: That could easily be a two-year kind of timeframe from the time we start rolling out product.

items.statement: Domestic 1G ethanol slowed due to unresolved feedstock policy (molasses B/syrup, FCI rice embargo); resolution expected during the year.
items.quote: This quarter witnessed a slowdown of activities mainly from the unresolved feedstock situation as also central elections. The prospective customers await for a clear long-term direction to emerge on clearance to use Molasses B/ Syrup as feedstocks and removal of embargo on issue of rice from FCI, for ethanol production.

items.statement: CBG pipeline developing healthily; blending mandate in ~18 months to drive project starts in H2 FY25.
items.quote: the blending mandate becoming compulsory in about 18 months' timeframe. Projects will have to start moving, especially in the second half of the year.

items.statement: SAF demand emerging globally; CORSIA mandate from Jan 2027 to drive domestic SAF activity by end of CY2024.
items.quote: come January 2027 and CORSIA agreement will kick in and under which 1% blending will be mandatory for all international clients. So, there is a clear demand, so as probably and given the 18 months, 18 to 20, 24 months kind of time cycle required for a SAF project to come alive, we will probably see activity we are already in dialogue, but we will probably see major traction build up towards the en

items.statement: IOCL 2G plant recommissioning progressing; targeting full-scale commissioning by end of CY2024.
items.quote: IOCL plant recommissioning is progressing as per plan. We are working closely with the IOCL team to resolve the unique situations and ramp up production in a gradual manner.

items.statement: Feasibility study commenced for straw-based 2G ethanol plant in Spain for a Spanish multinational.
items.quote: We have commenced feasibility study for a straw -based Ethanol plant i n Spain for a Spanish Multinational

items.statement: Over 75% of domestic bioenergy order book from starchy feedstock plants; maize availability improving.
items.quote: We continued to see new capacity built up dominated by starchy feedstock with over 75% of our domestic order book coming from starchy feedstock based plants.

items.statement: Export revenue 23% of Q1 FY25, up 24% YoY; strategy to increase international share for margin accretion.
items.quote: Export revenues accounted for 23% of Q1FY25, showing 24% increase over corresponding quarter of the last year.

items.statement: Union Budget supports agri-industry ecosystem, biomanufacturing, climate finance taxonomy, and GBA as global HQ.
items.quote: The budget strongly supports the agri -industry ecosystem which will help address feedstock related challenges and boost biomanufacturing. National Cooperation Policy for systematic, orderly and all -round development of the cooperative sector will inspire biofuels industry stakeholders to favorably consider long term investments.

items.statement: US IRA 45(Z) clarification awaited to provide impetus for low carbon ethanol projects.
items.quote: there is an important consideration from the IR A's perspective for notifying the 45(Z) applicability that's grid legal requirement and that is still not clarified and everybody including the industry is awaiting the clarification of 45(Z) once that is available, it will provide further impetus to the element.

items.statement: PHS business setting up large fermentation complex for a pharma company in southern India.
items.quote: PHS is setting up a very large fermentation complex for a reputed Pharma company in southern India.

items.statement: Produced first batch of Lactic Acid 90% at Jejuri demo plant; milestone for indigenous biopolymer technology.
items.quote: We have produced the first batch of Lactic Acid 90% at our newly setup demonstration plant at Jejuri. This is a milestone development in the biomanufacturing domain.

items.statement: Pilot plant being set up in US for RNG generation from waste-stream in grain-to-ethanol project.
items.quote: We are setting up a pilot plant in the United States for testing RNG generation from waste -stream in a Grain to Ethanol project, in collaboration with a US-based organization.

items.statement: Received significant engineering order for full modularization of US SAF project on ATJ pathway and modularized carbon capture for European blue hydrogen project.
items.quote: We have received a significant engineering order for complete modularization of a SAF Project in United State s on ATJ Pathway. We have received another contract of modularized solution for Carbon Capture for a Blue Hydrogen Project in Europe

items.statement: Be8 contract in Brazil as opinion leader opening doors; several leads and engineering contracts firming up.
items.quote: The Be8 contract that we mentioned has helped us a great deal because Be8 is an opinion leader in the region, and that particular project for whom we have be gun the engineering now will help us to actually establish our credentials even further

items.statement: Unique ZLD modularization technology with no comparable competition in India or nearby regions.
items.quote: the development is extremely unique. There is no other company in India or anywhere near about, we have even been able to develop and demonstrate this technology.

items.statement: Input costs moderated and expected to remain range-bound; fixed-price contracts prevent pass-through but current softness benefits old order execution.
items.quote: material prices are more or less look like to be in a range. The future projections from all the experts are also giving that kind of an indication. So, we don't see any kind of impact coming up because of the input costs going forward.

items.statement: Cash in hand Rs 8.3 billion as of June 30, 2024.
items.quote: Cash in hand as on June 30, 2024, is Rs. 8.3 billion.

items.statement: Shareholders approved final dividend of 300% per share at AGM.
items.quote: In yesterday's AGM, shareholders have approved the payment of final dividend of 300% per share.

items.statement: Domestic ethanol execution impacted by feedstock policy uncertainty and national elections; ~5% of order book (Rs 200-250 crore) considered slow-moving.
items.quote: I don't think more than 5% of our order book can be considered as the slow moving in that sense. May be 200 to 250 crore order book.

items.statement: Established Centre of Excellence with Vasantdada Sugar Institute for farm-to-fuel model and alternate feedstock intercropping.
items.quote: Praj has established Centre of Excellence & Innovation (CoEI) with Vasantdada Sugar Institute for the Integration of Farm to Fuel Model. The CoEI will focus on developing alternate feedst ock through intercropping models, for example: Sweet Sorghum with Sugarcane, Maize with Casava, etc

items.statement: Management reaffirmed 3x growth target by 2030 and expects order booking to improve by year-end
items.quote: Somebody asked me right at the beginning of this call , that would you actually achieve the guidance that you gave of 3x growth by 2030. And I said, yes, we are on track, there is no reason for us to believe otherwise life.

items.statement: No revenue guidance provided; CFO forgets mathematics when asked for revenue numbers
items.quote: Sorry to disappoint you we don't give revenue number guidance. When you talk revenue guidance, my CFO forget his mathematics, he is otherwise a brilliant guy, but he forgets.

items.statement: Order book mix shifted to 52:48 domestic:export and engineering:PHS from historical 80:20; export business now 42% of order book
items.quote: We are now at about 5 2:48 ratio. If you are seeing our past numbers, they will be more like 80:20 put together but now it's more like 52:48. And also our export business is almost 42% of our order book.

items.statement: Expect order booking to improve by year-end despite Q1 slowdown due to elections and feedstock policy uncertainty
items.quote: As per the year end is concerned, we stay very positive that we will do better than the year went by as far as the order booking numbers are concerned.

items.statement: US low carbon ethanol opportunity driven by SAF mandate: 2 billion gallons needed by 2030, requiring 20+ plant conversions at $10-30M each
items.quote: If it's a billion gallons of SAF, it will need 2 billion gallons of ethanol. That's the equation so, 2 billion gallon of ethanol will have to be low carbon ethanol in United States.

items.statement: Domestic ethanol inquiry pipeline remains healthy; 200-300 crore liters capacity still to be built for 20% blending target
items.quote: So, a ballpark figure of 200 crore to 300 crore liters can we put it that way, because 500 crore was four quarters back? Shishir Joshipura: Yes

items.statement: CBG ecosystem developing; expect activity to build up in second half of the year with SATAT scheme envisaging larger outlay
items.quote: As we go through the year, maybe in second half of the year we will start seeing activity built up on the CBG space.

items.statement: International business is higher margin accretive than domestic; export share increase supports margin continuity
items.quote: The international business for us happens to be higher margin accretive compared to domestic business. So, all those indicators are yes, the exact numbers time will tell.

items.statement: FY25 capex estimated at Rs 75-100 crores for GenX, PLA pilot plants, and potential IOCL JV allocation
items.quote: It should be in a range of around 75 to 100 crores.

items.statement: Capex may increase in FY26 if CBG and SAF projects kick off; exploring multiple funding avenues beyond internal resources
items.quote: Next year naturally it will be a little bit on a higher side because if it is CBG plus SAF plant if you are thinking of and which is on the anvil in any case, then the capital allocation will be a little on the higher side.

items.statement: Engineering orders for SAF/ATJ pathway take 8-15 months execution; non-engineering orders take 12-15 months
items.quote: the engineering order itself will get executed over a period of at least from eight months to 15 months kind of a period because the scope is pretty , pretty large for those engineering orders

items.statement: First indigenous technology to convert local feedstocks to lactic acid 90% for PLA; customer dialogues opening but early for revenue numbers
items.quote: Actually, we are the first company to have indigenously developed a technology that uses local feedstocks and can convert this to, so the critical step is to convert that to lactic acid 90%.

items.statement: First low carbon ethanol project using lactose from milk for US dairy customer in Michigan; niche but promising application
items.quote: an interesting one, because this is actually Shailesh, this qualifies low carbon ethanol very low carbon intensity score. So, this is low carbon ethanol

items.statement: Working capital days expected to remain stable despite revenue growth and higher export order share
items.quote: Even if we see in future the revenue to grow, the working capital will remain in more or less similar kind of number of days what we have seen in the last year.

items.statement: Export orders mix of FOB and CIF terms depending on customer logistics arrangements
items.quote: It's actually a combination, I will not say that everything is FOB, or everything is CIF, it's a combination of both depending on how the customer is looking at.

items.statement: CBG blending mandate in CGD networks resolves offtake issue; feedstock policy uncertainty still holding back domestic ethanol projects
items.quote: There is a clear mandate now to blend CBG into the CGD networks. So, that's a very welcome step, which takes care of a very, what I would call as a major issue of where I sell my gas.

items.statement: Low carbon ethanol technology reduces carbon intensity by ~30 points without carbon capture; approved under GREET framework
items.quote: That's exactly what our offering is , that if you cannot do CCS, we will still be able to get you down by nearly 30 points on the CI scale.

items.statement: Building local international teams with natives on the ground in US, Europe, Brazil; senior leadership travels frequently for business development
items.quote: We are building a team, which is local in nature, so all the people on the ground now that we are building our local people. When I say locally, they are natives of that place.

items.statement: Q1 order intake impacted by central elections (first two months lost) and feedstock reprioritization causing project delays
items.quote: First quarter with Central Elections in our business, which is agri industry policy driven. Too many factors at play for a central election quarter to actually so first two months were lost in a manner of speaking.

items.statement: No further land sales or exceptional items expected; sold land was only excess piece not usable after move to Mangalore
items.quote: This is the only piece of land which we had as excess land you can call it, I am not expecting any more exceptional item like this going forward.

items.statement: Promoter Dr. Chaudhary remains involved in strategic technology direction; professional management structure in place for next 5+ years
items.quote: Dr. Chaudhary is very much involved in strategic direction with the company, what we do on the technology front, how we are developing technology, how we are prioritizing ourselves.

items.statement: Expects Valia nitrile latex capacity utilization to be 50-70% for next couple of quarters.
items.quote: So, going forward, we do expect capacity utilization to be in the range of 50% to 70% for the next couple of quarters.

items.statement: Expects Taloja additional capacity to reach 100% utilization over next 1 to 15 months.
items.quote: And we expect to go to 100% over the next one year, 1 year to 15 months.

items.statement: Expects margins to improve slowly, with Q2 better than Q1.
items.quote: We're saying margins will improve slowly. In fact, we're already seeing margins in Q1 have been marginally better than Q4, for example, and we expect Q2 to be marginally better than Q1.

items.statement: Expects overall margins to be in 13-17% range over next 4-5 years.
items.quote: So, this is how I think things will go, will happen as long as we keep growing and growing at a reasonable margin.

items.statement: Plans to overhaul R&D center and build new R&D building, value to be announced later.
items.quote: One is the complete overhaul of our R&D center so that will require some CAPEX and we're planning to build a new R&D building and invest in our R&D.

items.statement: Will announce additional investment for styrene butadiene latex in next 3-6 months.
items.quote: the second investment is which we will announce again in the next 3 to 6 months is additional investment for our styrene butadiene latex products because we expect that capacity to be utilized by end of next year.

items.statement: No decision taken on expanding Valia nitrile latex capacity from 50,000 to 80,000 tonnes.
items.quote: No, 100%, we have not taken any decision. Given the margins where we are, I think we'll wait for some time.

items.statement: May use Valia space for current styrene butadiene and latex products; decision in 3-6 months.
items.quote: We may actually use that space where we had left some space for the additional capacity for Nitrile Latex. We actually use it to manufacture current styrene butadiene and other current latex products. That decision will be taken in the next 3 to 6 months.

items.statement: Glove segment pulling down margins; other segments also have lower margins due to capacity additions.
items.quote: Of course, the glove segment is pulling it down. A couple of other segments also, we have built capacity, some of our competitors have built capacity that is in the short term.

items.statement: Nitrile latex project is EBITDA neutral, with some quarters negative and some positive.
items.quote: It is about EBITDA neutral, I would say, some quarter negative, some quarters positive, but overall EBITDA sort of zero EBITDA neutral, yes. EBITDA breakeven rather.

items.statement: Glove industry showing green shoots; Q2 expected better than Q1.
items.quote: We do expect, I mean we're seeing some green shoots. I mentioned it last quarter also we saw initially some green shoots in Q1 was slightly better than Q4 of last year, but Q2 is expected to be even better.

items.statement: Export volumes grew 12% YoY in Q1.
items.quote: On the international front, export volume grew by 12% year-on-year.

items.statement: Overall volume growth of 14% YoY in Q1.
items.quote: I think we're up, Sachin, by about 14% this quarter. So, Q1 against Q1 of last year, volume growth is up by 14%.

items.statement: Freight and container availability issues impacted exports, absorbing some costs.
items.quote: We've seen that impact the margins as well to some extent because we've had to absorb some of those paid costs. Of course, we try and pass it along as well, but it takes time sometimes, so yes.

items.statement: NBR margins lower due to China slowdown and Russian NBR entering Asia.
items.quote: The Russia NBR, which used to largely go to Europe because of the sanctions are now finding its way towards Asia. So, I think there's a little bit of a glut of NBR in the Asian region causing the margins to be muted.

items.statement: Flooding at plant caused damage, but plant resumed in less than a week; assessing damage.
items.quote: So, we had to keep the plant closed for safety reasons for a few days. Of course, there was a lot of damage. We are still in the middle of assessing the exact damage.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% revenue CAGR over next 4 years and 25-30% ROCE
items.quote: We look forward to achieve revenue growth of 25% to 30% CAGR for t he next 4 years. We are also confident of hitting 25% to 30% of ROCE despite these proposed investments supported by working capital efficiencies

items.statement: Targets consolidated revenue over INR 2,600 crore by FY27
items.quote: And FY '25, FY '26, FY '27, we believe that we should be more than INR2,600 crores of revenue by FY '27, right?

items.statement: Targets Apollo Pipes standalone revenue INR 1,250-1,260 crore in FY25 and INR 1,600 crore by FY27
items.quote: This year, we expect INR1,250 crores, INR1,260 crores from Apollo, including whatever contribution we get from O-PVC, Varanasi, somewhat window profiles and, of course, the existing business, including a recovery in HDPE, right?

items.statement: Targets Kisan revenue INR 450-500 crore in FY25, INR 600-650 crore in FY26, INR 750-800 crore by FY27 with 10% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Going forward, we want to take this sales for Kisan to INR450 crores to INR 500 crores in the current financial year. That's what our target is. Then in the follow ing year, take it to around INR600 crores to INR650 crores and eventually around INR750 crores to INR800 crores by FY '27, with 10% of EBITDA margin

items.statement: Kisan Q1 EBITDA margin 7-8%, targets 10-12% in next 2 years
items.quote: So Kisan, see I mean, in Q1, you saw 7%, 8% of EBITDA margin, right? We plan to sustain these levels for full year. And going forward, in the next 2 years, we plan to take this company at 10% to 12% EBITDA level.

items.statement: Apollo Pipes targets 12-13% EBITDA margin after capacity ramp-up, currently around 10%
items.quote: So Apollo should move towards a 12% to 13% EBITDA margin, but as of now, we will remain around 10% for the next 2 years becau se of a lot of capex, which is coming

items.statement: Total capex ~INR 150 crore for Varanasi, O-PVC, window profiles; balance ~INR 250 crore remaining
items.quote: Total capex is around INR 150 crores. I'm glad to share that our balance sheet remains debt free despite such commitments.

items.statement: Annual capex INR 100-150 crore for next 2-3 years funded by internal cash flows and promoter equity
items.quote: Next 2, 3 years, we will be doing around INR100 crores to INR150 crores on annualized basis, which will be mainly funded from the internal cash flows and plus the balance equity infusion, whi ch is due from the promoter and employees as part of the preferential allotment

items.statement: Varanasi plant adds 40,000 tons, 70-80% operational by Q4 FY25, full by FY26
items.quote: Varanasi expansion is on track, which will add 40,000 tons to our overall capacity. With this plant, we will have a Pan-India presence.

items.statement: O-PVC first line operational Q1 FY25, two more lines by end FY25; window profiles by end FY25
items.quote: We started the first line for O-PVC Pipes in Q1 FY '25, which is a highly profitable product. This has placed Apollo Pipes among top companies in India to cater such a product segment. Two new lines will be coming -- will become operational by the end of FY '25.

items.statement: Current utilization ~55% for both Apollo Pipes and Kisan individually and consolidated
items.quote: Individual. So separate also, we are around 55% and consol also around similar number

items.statement: Kisan shifted from project/OEM to trade sales; Q1 revenue INR 65 crore with INR 5 crore EBITDA
items.quote: If you look at last quarter of FY '24, the number was much higher. But at that point of time, the company was mainly doing project business, which was -- they were taking advances from the project contractors, and then they were just doing OEM kind of business.

items.statement: Trade sales ex-HDPE grew 10% YoY; HDPE sales collapsed from 15% to below 5% due to elections and delayed budget
items.quote: So if we look at our trade sales, ex of HDPE pipes, our volume increased by 10%, okay, ex of HDPE. So this does demonstrate our continued market share gains and leveraging our brand and distribution network, right?

items.statement: cPVC revenue up 20% YoY, water tanks up 30%+ YoY in Q1
items.quote: For that matter, I want to highlight that our cPVC revenue was up by 20% on Y-o-Y basis in Q1. And our water tank segment also increased by more than 30% on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: cPVC prices expected to rise due to anti-dumping on resin imports
items.quote: The price should be on the upward side because of some antidumping -- new antidumping on resin coming into the picture. The prices should be on the upper side for cPVC.

items.statement: Balance sheet remains debt-free despite capex commitments
items.quote: I'm glad to share that our balance sheet remains debt free despite such commitments.

items.statement: No cannibalization between Apollo and Kisan brands; will run both parallelly to gain share from unorganized players
items.quote: we don't see any cannibalization between Apollo brands and -- Apollo and Kisan brands because Apollo wasn't strong in Western India anyways. We were catering through a very small plant in Ahmedabad, right? So looking at like how Q1 panned out, we don't see any concern of cannibalization. In fact, what we want to do is we want to run both brands parallelly

items.statement: O-PVC has high entry barriers (technology, approvals, capital); replacing ductile iron pipes in water infra
items.quote: Here, the entry barrier is the capital investment. Entry barrier is the access to technology. Entry barrier is the product approval from the government authorities. So we are -- as of now, given the current situation, we are pretty bullish on this category.

items.statement: Consolidated volume 26,500 tons (+25% YoY); standalone Apollo 20,900 tons (flat ex-Kisan)
