items.quote: Our inventory has come down from Rs. 682 crores as of March 2024 to Rs. 640 crores as of 30th June, 2024, which is a reduction of about Rs. 42 crores.

items.statement: Digital platform deals are between one and three years; television movie licenses are for five years.
items.quote: Typically, digital platform deals are between one and three ye ars, not more than that, because space is evolving and growing in different speeds. So, what is relevant today may not be the relevant price or commercial model two years down the line. Television is a much more stable platform, so we typically license our move. And that's again a trade practice, industry licenses movies for five years

items.statement: In last three years, generated about Rs. 50-60 crores free cash flow net of new business investments.
items.quote: If we look at net of that, each of the last about three years, we have been generating probably about Rs. 50 crores to Rs. 60 crores free cash flow.

items.statement: Gaming and metaverse industry in infancy; no immediate major monetization potential, investing just enough to be future-ready.
items.quote: Right now, we do not see any immediate, in the immediate future we do not see any ma jor monetization potential there. However, there could be a lot of possibilities opening up in the future. What we are doing is investing just enough to be future‐ready

items.statement: Capacity guidance for FY25 maintained at early double digits.
items.quote: And for the seasonally weak second quarter, we are expecting to add around high single digits capacity as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 passenger unit revenue (PRASK) expected stable year-over-year.
items.quote: Further, on the revenue side basis the early trends of July, we are estimating a stable revenue environment on a passenger unit revenue which is PRASK basis in the second quarter of financial year 2025 as compared to the same period last year.

items.statement: Firm orderbook of 975+ aircraft enables receiving more than one aircraft per week.
items.quote: With our firm pending orderbook of 975 plus aircraft that will enable us to receive more than one aircraft per week and the mitigation measures we remain firm on our capacity guidance of early double digits for the financial year 2025 .

items.statement: Goal to become a 600+ aircraft airline by end of decade.
items.quote: We continue to utilize part of our free cash towards future growth and our goal to become a 600 plus aircraft airline by the end of the decade.

items.statement: Will induct 6 more aircraft from Qatar Airways on wet or damp lease subject to approvals.
items.quote: In addition to this, subject to regulatory approvals we will induct 6 more aircraft from Qatar Airlines for the Doha route on wet or damp lease in the coming quarters.

items.statement: Will continue to add more aircraft on finance leases to diversify financing sources.
items.quote: Going forward, we will continue to further diversify our sources and will add more aircraft on finance leases.

items.statement: Aircraft groundings expected to start reducing towards start of next year.
items.quote: We are working with Pratt & Whitney towards constant supply of spare engines and basis the current estimates we expect the groundings to start reducing towards the start of the next year.

items.statement: Compensation from Pratt & Whitney will not fully cover all costs; will be less than overall cost.
items.quote: No, it's not going to be neutral, like I said, it's always going to be less than what the overall cost is going to be.

items.statement: Solid demand seen in July; no change in capacity guidance or planning.
items.quote: Looking at the overall outlook for July, we see a solid demand. And therefore, we have no change in our capacity guidance.

items.statement: Average fare stable around Rs.5,000 to Rs.6,000 range for last couple of quarters.
items.quote: If you look to our yields, we see an average fare still in that range around Rs.5,000 to Rs.6,000 range, which is a very stable setting actually for the last couple of quarters.

items.statement: Increased costs in fuel, navigation, and airport fees will need to be reflected in prices.
items.quote: And clearly, some of the increased cost in fuel and navigation and airport fees will have to find their way back in the cost.

items.statement: International share of ASK is around 27% and expected to grow.
items.quote: Therefore, today, the international share of IndiGo is around 27% of the ASK. We have announced earlier that that percentage is expected to grow, and we'll continue to build on that.

items.statement: International routes are more accretive than domestic.
items.quote: But definitely, international is definitely more accretive than what the domestic is for us.

items.statement: Compensation accrual in Q1 included catch-up from prior quarters; going forward no catch-up.
items.quote: So, this particular quarter, because of finalization of the agreement, there's catch-up. Going forward, there's no catch-up that is needed to be done.

items.statement: Management reiterated full-year EBITDA guidance of Rs 10-12 per SCM and volume CAGR of slightly more than 6-7% for MGL standalone.
items.quote: Overall I think it is a comfortable position whatever guidance we have been giving in the past Rs. 10 to 12 per SCM EBITDA, we are hopeful that we will be able to achieve that for the year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 overall gas sales volume rose 13.1% YoY to 3.858 mmscmd; CNG up 11.7%, domestic PNG up 10.4%, industrial/commercial up 23.8%.
items.quote: Overall, average gas sales for Q1 of the current year compared to the corresponding Q1 of the previous years has increased to 3.858 mmscmd from 3.412, which is an increase of 13.1%.

items.statement: CNG vehicle additions ~20,800 in Q1 FY25 (14,200 cars/taxis, 5,000 three-wheelers, 1,200-1,300 small commercial, rest medium/heavy commercial and buses).
items.quote: During the quarter, roughly 20,800 odd vehicles were added on to CNG. This is compared to, let's say, 20,100 in the last quarter of last year.

items.statement: MSRTC added 90 CNG buses in Q1; management expects another ~200 in next two quarters; total MSRTC fleet touching MGL GAs ~6,000 out of 17,000.
items.quote: MSRTC added about 90 buses during the quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA Rs 418 cr, margin 26.33% vs 25.13% previous quarter; net profit Rs 285 cr vs Rs 265 cr.
items.quote: Current quarter EBITDA is Rs. 418 crores compared to the previous quarter EBITDA of Rs. 394 crores. EBITDA margin is 26.33% for the current quarter as compared to the previous quarter of EBITDA margin of 25.13%.

items.statement: Management confident blended gas cost will remain in current range, supporting Rs 10-12/SCM EBITDA guidance, subject to APM allocation not dropping drastically and stable exchange rate.
items.quote: So, as of now we are confident that more or less gas cost will remain in this range.

items.statement: CNG price increased by Rs 1.5/kg in July 2024 to maintain margins amid gas cost pressure.
items.quote: We have also taken a price increase, as you may be aware, in the month of July of Rs. 1.5, so our endeavor is to maintain margin in line with the gas cost available to us.

items.statement: APM gas allocation for priority sector (CNG+domestic) was ~69% in Q1 FY25, down from 73-74% previous quarter; currently stable at same level.
items.quote: Current quarter APM allocation for the priority sector, that is CNG and domestic put together, was in the range of around 69%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex ~Rs 250 cr; FY25 target >50 new CNG stations for MGL and ~25 for UEPL, total ~75 stations.
items.quote: During the quarter, we have incurred CAPEX in the range of around Rs. 250 crores. And with stations, we are going to add; we have set up a shift target around more than 50 stations we expect to add this financial year in MGL alone, and maybe another 25 stations will be added in Unison Enviro.

items.statement: UEPL: 57 CNG stations, 27,339 domestic connections, 57 I&C customers, 0.168 mmscmd sales in Q1.
items.quote: During the quarter, they have achieved an overall average sales volume of 0.168 mmscmd as against 0.146 mmscmd in the previous quarter, which is an increase of 14.51%.

items.statement: LNG station at Savroli selling ~4,100 kg/day; tank capacity 20 tons, max potential 12-13 tons/day; currently seeding market, margins not comparable to CNG.
items.quote: is almost more than 4,100 kgs a day. That is the volume. Sabri Hazarika: And what is the maximum potential for this? Management: The tank is 20-ton capacity, so typically we have to make some volume already in the tank, maximum we can go up to 12 tons, 13 tons per

items.statement: Signed term gas contracts covering ~0.76 mmscmd Henry Hub-linked, ~0.5 mmscmd HPHT, tenors 5-6 years; portfolio balanced with spot/exchange for flexibility.
items.quote: Already we had up to quarter end around 0.76. And after that also we are taking up one or two contracts. HPHT was already around 0.5 million, and we proposed to take little more again in the times to come.

items.statement: CNG vehicle base crossed 1 million; factory-fitted OE vehicles dominate additions (~20k/quarter), retrofits ~900/quarter.
items.quote: So, these are predominantly factory fitted OE vehicles. Retrofitment number is hardly about 900 or so out of this 20,000 – 21,000.

items.statement: Management sees no near-term impact from hybrid/EV two-wheelers; CNG two-wheeler launch (Bajaj) adds new segment, ~130 delivered, Bajaj projects ~700/month.
items.quote: In short, maybe that doesn't move the needle, hybrid vehicles, the number is too small right now. Management: It is not going to have any impact as of now because the overall volumes are much heavy and the volume of potential to get petrol vehicles or the diesel vehicle on CNG side is much, much

items.statement: Infrastructure exclusivity extension sought from PNGRB; marketing exclusivity guiding principles repealed, matters sub-judice with stay orders protecting MGL.
items.quote: sought extension from PNGRB, and we are expecting that it will be processed and given to us. Because there's a precedence and provisions in the regulation to give 10 year block extension on the request. Regarding the marketing exclusivity, there have been several developments like guiding principle they have been repealed by PNGRB. 54 notices which they have issued to different entities have also

items.statement: UEPL Q1 revenue ~Rs 88 cr vs Rs 82 cr previous quarter; EBITDA/SCM similar to MGL, maybe Rs 1 higher; PAT ~Rs 10 cr, breaking even at EBITDA level.
items.quote: roughly Rs. 88 crores for the quarter Q1 of this year, as against Rs. 82 crores in the last quarter. S. Ramesh: So, in terms of the earnings, EBITDA or EBITDA for SCM, can you give us some insight? Management: EBITDA is more or less in similar range as MGL. Not sharing the exact number because there are certain costs which are specific to this Q1 and we taking over, so not very right way to compar

items.statement: Commercial vehicle market growth lagging across fuels; management targeting market share gains in CNG segment.
items.quote: One point we would like to add about the commercial goods vehicles is that, whatever reports in media we are seeing on that segment, the commercial vehicle additions across fuels is lagging slightly. I do not know if it's because of the economy or what, but however, we are still attempting to claw out a larger market share for CNG out of whatever comes new in the market.

items.statement: Targets disbursements of over INR60,000 crores this year, with 20% done in Q1.
items.quote: And this year, the target is around 60,000 plus kind of disbursement, out of which 20% disbursement has been done in this quarter.

items.statement: Confident to grow deposits by 25% this year.
items.quote: Overall, we remain confident to grow our deposits by 25% this year, but we will continue to revisit our deposit strategy quarterly based on ma rket liquidity conditions and the rate of interest dynamics.

items.statement: Expects credit cost for the year to be in the range of 1.10%-1.15%.
items.quote: As we guided in our March call that overall, we believe that the kind of market we deal in, the kind of yield we deal in the assets, normalized credit cost would be in the range of 1.10 %- 1.15%.

items.statement: Aims to defend ROA of 1.6% for the year.
items.quote: So we really want to stick to our earlier guidance that we should defend our last year ROA, which is 1.6%.

items.statement: Guides full-year NIM corridor of 5.7% to 5.8%.
items.quote: I think for now, our guidance remains that our margins -- full year margins for this financial year will be in the corridor of last year's, which was about 5.5 %, so maybe add about 10, -15 basis points on that, but allow us to come back on that. I think anything around about -- I'll be happy with anything between 5.7% to 5.8%.

items.statement: Plans to raise around INR25,000 crores of deposits in the next 9 months.
items.quote: So I believe that we will be able to build around INR25,000 crores of deposits in the next 9 months.

items.statement: Expects cost to income ratio for the year to be around 61%-62%.
items.quote: So I believe over the year, it will be around 61%-62%. That's my sense.

items.statement: Guides credit cost for credit card business at 6.5% to 7% for the full year.
items.quote: The quarter was a bit seasonal, but I think for the full year, we have guided for anywhere between 6.5% to 7% that should remain.

items.statement: Plans to issue around 5 lakh credit cards for the full year.
items.quote: Yes. No, I think for the full year, we remain on -- very similar to last year number, around 5 lakhs cards. So it will pick up as we go along the year.

items.statement: Expects cost of funds to increase by around 35 basis points for the year.
items.quote: So that's the sense that we want to really be guiding you that maybe around 35 bps, our cost can go up.

items.statement: Aims to achieve approximately INR2,000 crores in acquisition from Samriddhi branches.
items.quote: We aim to achieve approximately INR2,000 crores in acquisition from these branches which are aligning with AU productivity and should reach similar run rates by quarter 3.

items.statement: Plans to take 3% annualized credit cost on microfinance portfolio.
items.quote: And the second one was that we will have a credit cost of 3% annualized beginning first. And we have started that process now, right . We have taken it -- we haven't waited for the year, but we have started doing it from the first quarter itself.

items.statement: Expects branches launched until FY20 to breakeven in FY25.
items.quote: Our focus on branch profitability will leverage the comprehensive product suit we offer to cross-sell and upsell to liability customers aiming for branches launched until FY'20 to breakeven in FY'25.

items.statement: No capital raise envisaged in this financial year.
items.quote: No, no, no capital raise resolution is a very routine, enabling one. So we don't envisage any kind of capital raise in this financial year

items.statement: Expects other income to sustain at 1.7% of assets.
items.quote: For the overall fees, I think we delivered about 1.7% of assets this particular quarter. And if the last full year as well, we were around 1.7% kind of level. So we do hope that we can sustain that number, if not grow.

items.statement: Targets 15 to 18 SME IPOs this year, with profit at least 5x bigger than last year.
items.quote: So this year, we have already helped two companies to get listed on BSE SME and target is 15 more companies should be coming in the rest of the 9 years. And when I'm saying 15, that means we are already working on the DRHP, and some has been filed and some are to be filed in the next 2 months. So 15 plus 2, 17 -- 15 to 18 companies we are targeting this year.

items.statement: Targets MTF book of INR250 crores by end of this financial year.
items.quote: And we started MTF -- for the retail, we started MTF last year, and I proudly say when we are talking, we have MTF book of INR150 crores right now, and we are targeting INR250 crores of MTF book by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Targets NBFC loan book of around INR500 crores by 2027.
items.quote: So right now, once we will build like secured book, definitely we will get support from the banks and organically and inorganically, we are targeting at least INR500 crores book by 2027.

items.statement: MTF book should be around INR700 crores by 2027.
items.quote: I will -- next time, I will also give the projections about the insti business, merchant banking, MTF should not be less than INR500 crores, it's a concern again, by 2027, I guess should be around 700 crores.

items.statement: Expects to maintain 28% net profit margin for the year; 25% was the lowest.
items.quote: But I think as the year will progress, we'll see that we're able to manage this 28% margin overall in the year. So that's kind of margin we're expected. We're not expecting anything in 40s or 45 because in that case, you have to stop new verticals, you have to stop incurring big costs.

items.statement: Long-term profit margin range is 30% plus or minus 3%.
items.quote: Yes. So even in our previous con calls, we had always maintained that 30% plus, minus 3% is approximately the long-term range that we are looking at for the profit margin percentage.

items.statement: Plans to apply for AIF and PMS licenses this year, start operations next financial year.
items.quote: So we are planning to apply for AIF very soon and PMS license with the SEBI. Once we get the license, we hope next financial we start the operations also.

items.statement: STT increase and capital gains tax changes pose short-term challenges but expected to be absorbed in 2-3 months.
items.quote: Yes, it is a challenge. It will definitely take some time to get absorbed. But I think in next -- once it is applicable, then in 2 to 3 months, things will change as per the new cost structure.

items.statement: Bullish on uTrade Algo product, expects it to be a game changer in next 3 years.
items.quote: And this product will be widely accepted in coming years like the next 3 years, we are very bullish on this product and it can change the entire course of the company in the coming years.

items.statement: Plans to start wealth management division next year, applying for licenses this year.
items.quote: So wealth is one we are announcing that we'll start next year. We are applying for the licenses this year.

items.statement: GNPA for NBFC subsidiary this quarter around 3%.
items.quote: The GNPA for this quarter should be around 3% approximately, give or take, yes, around 3%, give or take, yes.

items.statement: Total loan book currently around INR200 crores, reduced from INR250 crores last quarter.
items.quote: So the total loan book is around INR200 crores currently. It has reduced from last quarter, which was around INR250-odd crores due to a certain impact in Punjab and Haryana territory.

items.statement: Board committee approved acquisition of 11-acre beachfront land in South Goa for 5-star deluxe resort with ~170 rooms, approvals in place, construction to start post-monsoon, completion targeted in 3 years
items.quote: A Committee of our Board has approved a transaction to purchase a la nd in Goa for the development of 5 -star deluxe resort. The closure of the acquisition process will take a couple of weeks and we will send out an update in the near future

items.statement: Expect better flow-throughs and higher margins for rest of FY25 as Dukes renovation completes and Courtyard Aravali exits weak season
items.quote: it is now safe to say that we can expect better flow-throughs and higher margins for the rest of the year.

items.statement: Target 90% leasing of 2.4 msf office portfolio by end of calendar year 2024
items.quote: We continue to expect 90% of the office portfolio leased out by end of the calendar year.

items.statement: Expect double-digit revenue growth in subsequent quarters on same-store basis after 9% same-store growth in Q1 despite election impact
items.quote: I'm pretty confident that in the subsequent qua rters, we will get the double-digit growth that we are targeting

items.statement: Expect annualized rental income of ~INR 280 crore at 95% occupancy once current 2.4 msf office portfolio fully leased
items.quote: Once we've got the current 2.4 million square foot leased out, we expect roughly mid of INR280-odd crores from these assets on an annualized basis.

items.statement: Capex plan of INR 15 billion over next 7 quarters for announced projects, largely funded through internal accruals; Goa investment separate
items.quote: The company continues to invest in its growth and has a capex plan of around INR15 billion for the next 7 quarters for the announced projects, which will be largely funded through internal accruals.

items.statement: Capex breakdown: INR 650 cr for new commercial, INR 600 cr for hotels (DIAL, Dukes, Bangalore), INR 250 cr including INR 100 cr maintenance
items.quote: Around INR 650 crores is basically for the new commercial task. Around INR600 crores is for the hotels which includes DIAL, Dukes, our Bang alore addition as well. And INR250 crores out of which INR100 crores is our normal repair

items.statement: Pipeline of ~1,000 rooms over next 3 years: 2 hotels adding capacity (Marriott Bengaluru +130 rooms, Dukes +37 rooms Phase 1), 2 new hotels (Taj Delhi Airport, Hyatt Airoli ~660 rooms), plus Goa ~170 rooms
items.quote: So roughly, our pipeline is now 1,000 rooms over the next 3 years or so.

items.statement: Taj New Delhi Airport hotel: substructure work ongoing, Chalet team to start MEP work by January, target completion last quarter FY26
items.quote: As of now, we expect our team to get into the site by January to start lower floor work on the MEP side. And then as they keep handing over every floor to us, we'll continue improving. Our current target continues to be last quarter FY '26.

items.statement: Q1 impacted by elections, heatwave, no wedding dates; July looking very strong on both occupancy and rate; expect sharp growth from October as H2 is seasonally strong
items.quote: July is looking very strong, both on occupancy and rate front.

items.statement: Hospitality adjusted EBITDA margin 41.2% in Q1; consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin 40.2%; expect margins to improve as Dukes renovation completes and new assets stabilize
items.quote: The hospitality segment during the quarter also deli vered an adjusted EBITDA of INR 1.3 billion, marking a growth of 12% with a margin of 41.2

items.statement: Confident of sustaining and growing margins above 40%
items.quote: We are confident on growing those margins.

items.statement: Goa beachfront 5-star deluxe properties currently charging INR 17,000-25,000 ARR; expect to open in that range adjusted for 3-year inflation
items.quote: So look beachfront properties in the 5-star deluxe category, are hovering around the INR17,000 to INR25,000 price point. So that's the range, I think, when it opens 3 years from now with an adjusted inflation for those 3 years, we should be able to open at.

items.statement: Residential project at Koramangala selling at INR 21,548/sq ft in Q1, 14% higher than FY24 average; expect rate buoyancy to continue
items.quote: We have sold 17 new units during the quarter commanding a rate of INR 21,548 per square feet which is 14% higher than the rates averaged in FY '24.

items.statement: Net debt INR 15 billion as of June 30, 2024, marginally up from post-QIP level; majority allocated to CWIP and non-operational assets expected to generate 18-20% ROCE
items.quote: The net debt as on 30th June '24 was at INR15 billion marginally up from our debt post QIP in April.

items.statement: Cost of finance improved to 8.43%, down 44 bps from March 2024; ICRA maintained positive outlook with rating upgrade to A from A-
items.quote: We closed the quarter with a significant improvement in cost of finance standing at 8.43%, a reduction of 44 bps from March '24. I'm also happy to add here that ICRA has maintained positive outlook for Chalet with a new rating of A and upgrade from A minus.

items.statement: Peak debt expected to remain around INR 1,500 crore with marginal increase; funding largely from internal accruals, no significant leverage increase
items.quote: So right now, the debt is around INR1,500 crores. This may go up marginally over some period of time. Very little, but that will probably be the peak.

items.statement: Residential project at Koramangala surpassing sales expectations; anticipate substantial cash flows over next 6-7 quarters
items.quote: We anticipate substantial cash flows from this project over the next 6 to 7 quarters.

items.statement: Portfolio RevPAR grew 2% YoY to INR 7,361 in Q1 FY25; same-store RevPAR grew 4%; occupancy 70.5% (+85 bps), ADR INR 10,446 (+1%)
items.quote: As a result, the RevPAR has been up by 2% year-on-year to INR7,361 for Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Hyderabad Mindspace: 13% RevPAR growth with equal rate/occupancy mix; Westin HITEC: 15% RevPAR growth driven by 15% rate growth at 100% occupancy
items.quote: Hyderabad Mindspace 13% RevPAR growth, Hyderabad HITEC 15% RevPAR growth.

items.statement: Vashi hotel saw 7% RevPAR decline due to significant room supply increase in Navi Mumbai micro-market over last couple of years
items.quote: The Vashi hotel saw a 7% dip in RevPAR. This was due to significant increase in room supply in similar category hotels in Navi Mumbai micro market over the last couple of years.

items.statement: Novotel revenue grew 15% but RevPAR lower due to 88-room capacity addition needing 1-2 quarters to stabilize
items.quote: Novotel had lower RevPAR on account of increased capacity of 88 rooms which will take another quarter or two to stabilize. However, the hotel had revenue growth of 15% over the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Goa land acquisition comes with all municipal, environment and other approvals in place, enabling quick construction start post-monsoon
items.quote: All municipal, environment and other approvals are coming as a part of the deal.

items.statement: Election impact on Q1 was larger than expected, causing travel slowdown across industries; Q1 considered aberration not trend
items.quote: I got that wrong. I thought the impact will be minimal. But somewhere during the election process, I think the mood and dynamics and the tone and tenor changed, which caused everyone to wait and watch. And that sort of slowed down travel for a lot of people in India.

items.statement: Net zero greenhouse gas emissions pledge by 2040 aligned with Paris Agreement 1.5°C goal, announced on World Environment Day June 5
items.quote: Another pivotal focus for us is our pledge to net zero greenhouse gas emissions by 2040, aligning with the Paris Agreement's goal of limiting global temperature rise to 1.5 degrees Celsius.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin target for FY25 is around 16.4% (Q4 FY24 level)
items.quote: Remember, we had guided in the last conference call after the post -quarter results that we are expecting MDF margins to be around what we achieved in Q4 last year, which was, I think, around 16.4%.

items.statement: Plywood volume growth guidance maintained at 8% for FY25
items.quote: At this point of time, I think we woul d like to maintain the 8% growth that we have initially projected.

items.statement: MDF EBITDA margin at 12.1% in Q1 FY25 impacted by wood price increase and lower volumes
items.quote: MDF EBITDA margins at 12.1% were impacted by steep increase in wood prices, 5.8 % sequentially and 30.9% year-on-year, lower domestic volumes on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Plywood operating margin at negative 2.2% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Plywood volumes were low both sequentially and year-on-year and operating margins at negative 2.2% were impacted due to the same.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 10.9% in Q1 FY25, down 780 bps YoY
items.quote: EBITDA margins were down by 780 basis points at 10.9%.

items.statement: MDF margins expected to improve in Q2 FY25 on volume recovery
items.quote: I think the margins have bottomed out. Definitely, since we are seeing volume improvement in Quarter 2, I think margins will definitely be better in Quarter 2 as compared to Quarter 1.

items.statement: Target FY25 MDF margin of 16% to come from operational leverage, not price increases
items.quote: At the moment , we are not looking at any price increases. We are rather looking at price stability for the current quarter. So, basically it will come from operational leverage and lower operating expenses.

items.statement: MDF domestic volume grew 10.2% YoY in Q1 FY25; export volume fell 21% due to logistics
items.quote: MDF domestic volume had increased by 10.2% year-on-year for the quarter, export volumes contracted by 21% due to logistics issues.

items.statement: Plywood volumes down 22.8% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Plywood sales volumes were lower by 22.8% at 1.22 million square meters and the unit operated at 52% during the quarter.

items.statement: Election impact and dealer incentive pull-forward contributed to low Q1 volumes; pickup expected from Q2
items.quote: Yes, I think to some extent we also had the election impact just as April is also a slow starter because dealers increased volumes in March to avail the highest slab of incentive, so all those factors definitely contributed to low volumes in Q1FY25, and we are confident that we will start seeing the pickup from the current quarter.

items.statement: MDF industry demand estimated at 2.5-2.6 million CBM; capacity at 3.5 million CBM with 600k CBM additions in FY25
items.quote: If we look at it, current capacity would be around 3.5 million cubic meters and including our own capacity of 230,000 cubic meters, we expect 600,000 cubic meters to be added during the current year. We should take the overall capacity to about 4 million cubic meters whereas current demand is approximately 2.5 to 2.6 million cubic meters.

items.statement: MDF imports down ~50% YoY in Q1 FY25 to ~17,000-18,000 CBM/month
items.quote: Quarter, I said it was approximately 50% of the last year's average of 35,000, so somewhere between 17,000 to 18,000 cubic meters per month.

items.statement: Uttarakhand MDF plant at 76% utilisation, AP plant at 74%, blended at 75% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Uttarakhand MDF plant operated at 76% and AP plant operated at 74% with blended capacity utilization at 75 % for the quarter.

items.statement: New MDF expansion (230k CBM) to start production in Q3 FY25
items.quote: That is correct. It will start production in Q3FY25.

items.statement: New thin MDF line to target 1.9-2.5mm segment not currently served
items.quote: The new line that we have is going to be specialized for thin MDF production. It is a segment that we are not currently very actively present in, the 1.9 , 2.1, 2.5 millimeter market, which is a huge market and we don't actively participate in the market because it is not viable to produce it on larger lines.

items.statement: Wood prices up 5.8% QoQ and 30.9% YoY; North plant Rs 6.75/kg, South Rs 5.50/kg, blended ~Rs 6/kg
items.quote: It was Rs. 6.75 for the North plant and Rs. 5.50 for the South plant and blended was approximately Rs. 6.

items.statement: Domestic MDF realisation down 10% YoY to Rs 29,603/CBM; export realisation up 11.7% to Rs 20,051/CBM
items.quote: Domestic realizations were lower by 10.01% at Rs. 29,603 per cubic meter while export realizations were higher by 11.7% at Rs. 20,051 per cubic meter.

items.statement: Import parity: FOB $190-195/CBM + freight $30-35/CBM = $225-230 CNF; no duty under FTA
items.quote: As of now, what we are seeing, there is not too many imports coming in, so it is not very clear. What we know is that from Southeast Asian countries, they are trying to maintain an FOB price of $190 to $195 . And on the freight side, I think today we a re talking at least a number of $30 to $35 per cubic meter to bring it into India. So, that would result in a price of $225 to $230 CNF.

items.statement: Basic MDF realisation Rs 22,695/CBM; value-added Rs 37,482/CBM
items.quote: If you look at the basic products, which is the industrial and the commercial grade products, the average realization comes to Rs. 22,695 and those for the value-added segment comes to Rs. 37,482.

items.statement: OEM channel contributes 25% of domestic MDF volumes
items.quote: The OEM contribution was 25% of the domestic volumes.

items.statement: Organised players (Century, Greenply, Action, Rushil) driving price competition; unorganised players struggling
items.quote: I would say so that the organized segment competition is definitely of a bigger concer n than the unorganized segment a nd I could probably name the companies where we face challenges from that would be Century, that would be Action, that would be GreenPly, and to a certain extent, Rushil Decor.

items.statement: BIS implementation deferred to February 2025; will create import barrier
items.quote: At the same time, we had plans for BIS being implemented, which unfortunately got deferred by a year. So, this will get implemented next February, which would already create a barrier for imports coming into the country.

items.statement: Net working capital at 36 days, up 8 days sequentially due to wood inventory build for monsoon
items.quote: Net working capital at 36 days has shown a sequential increase of 8 days due to increase in wood inventory in preparation for the monsoon season.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 103 crore (including Rs 214 crore expansion debt); net cash Rs 111 crore ex-expansion debt
items.quote: Net debt stood at Rs. 103 crore as on 30th June, 2024. However, it stands at negative Rs. 111 crore, excluding debt for expansion project.

items.statement: Debt-to-equity at 0.21 as of June 2024 vs 0.13 a year ago
items.quote: Growth debt to equity ratio now stands at 0.21 as on 30th June 2024, compared to 0.13 as on 30th June 2023.

items.statement: Expansion project debt Rs 214 crore; new plant commissioning Q3 FY25
items.quote: Net debt as on 30th June stood at Rs. 103 crore, including debt of Rs. 214 crore for the expansion project.

items.statement: Timber price cycles historically 5-6 years; current cycle inflated by paper mill and MDF demand
items.quote: No, you see in timber, we always go through these cycles because demand goes up, prices start going up and plantations start happening. And then, when plantations do become available, demand is sort of similar, then the prices will go down. We have seen this, there is always a 5-6 year cycle when this always happens.

items.statement: Full year revenue growth expected close to last year's 16-18%, could be better depending on H2.
items.quote: At this time, I would say that for the year, full year, depending on how things pan out in the second half of the year, we could see a growth of somewhere definitely close to what we did last year, which is in the 16% to 18% range.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to return to 23% by Q3, with potential for higher in Q4 if revenue grows.
items.quote: We also do anticipate that as revenue continues to grow through the course of this year, we will be able to see some of that operating leverage kick in and so we should be back at those 23% odd levels by Q3 is the estimate at this point in time.

items.statement: Gen-AI pipeline over $4 million at closure stage.
items.quote: At this point in time, our Gen-AI pipeline is also looking fairly strong, over $4 million worth of conversations that are at a closure stage and many more in the top stages of the funnel.

items.statement: Pipeline of $45 million for the year, with varying conversion probabilities.
items.quote: On top of that, there are other projects where extensions are feasible. And in addition to that, we have almost $45 million pipeline for this year itself, meaning that this is revenue that can convert in this year if all the stars align.

items.statement: Confirmed revenue and high-probability extensions to contribute 10%+ growth.
items.quote: So, 10% of growth will come just from all the confirmed work and the high potential extensions that we have.

items.statement: Wage hikes and visa costs caused EBITDA contraction; these costs expected to reduce in coming quarters.
items.quote: The incremental visa plus the professional and advisory fees contributed about 0.9% of the EBITDA contraction and wage hikes contributed about 1.2% of the EBITDA contraction.

items.statement: Acquisition of Decision Point for INR 330 crores, to be consolidated from Q2.
items.quote: However, with the acquisition of Decision Point that was concluded on July 1st close to about INR 330 crores of the cash balance will be invested for closing this acquisition and therefore, you will see some impact of the lower investment balance that we will carry on the other income.

items.statement: Data engineering currently 20% of revenue, expected to increase.
items.quote: I mean, today about 20% of our revenue comes from doing that type of work. We are expecting that percentage could go up in the coming quarters, in the coming years.

items.statement: Retail sector is a concern; other sectors show positive momentum.
items.quote: I would say that the sector where we are concerned at this point in time is only retail. We are seeing a positive momentum in all of them.

items.statement: New logos starting smaller, but some have potential to grow; three marquee logos added.
items.quote: New logos, I would say, are still harder to come by and even when we win that, it is starting off on a much smaller scale in comparison to what we were experiencing maybe a year and a half back.

items.statement: Effective tax rate expected to be 24-25% going forward.
items.quote: Both these two mains that are at ETR for this year and this should be fairly reflective of how our ETR will be going forward as well, will be between 24% to 25% going forward.

items.statement: Europe contribution expected to double to 3%+ by end of fiscal year.
items.quote: If things go well even in the remainder of the year, I would expect the contribution to double for the current fiscal itself. We should be approaching the 3% plus mark in terms of overall contribution as we close this year.

items.statement: BeagleGPT generated $1 million revenue last year, potential for more this year.
items.quote: BeagleGPT has good potential. It's already generated a million dollars of revenue, right, for Decision Point in the last year. And this year, if conversations are anything to go by, it could generate even more revenue.

items.statement: Won a $1 million Generative AI engagement with a large account.
items.quote: One of the largest accounts that we work with, we were able to win a $1 million Generative AI engagement, right, this year already, and we are executing on that.

items.statement: M&A advisory fees for the quarter were INR 9 million to 1 crore.
items.quote: So the M&A advisory fee for the quarter would be close to about in terms of rupees that we would have paid close to between INR 9 million to about INR 1 crore that we would have paid in this quarter.

items.statement: Export share to be more than 25% for entire year.
items.quote: So we believe it should be more than 2 5% for the entire year going forward on the side of export.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA per kg to improve by 3-5% this year.
items.quote: And for this year, I believe it will be 3% to 5% incremental should be there.

items.quote: And I believe this will change to more than 50% sort of number, 54% to 55% towards welded and balance towards seamless.

items.statement: First phase of capex to complete by March 2025.
items.quote: Our capex remains on track with first phase set for completion in March '25 only.

items.statement: Order book at around INR270 crores.
items.quote: At roughly around INR270 crores.

items.statement: Finished goods prices expected to not decrease much from current quarter.
items.quote: It seems this price, which was there in this quarter, we believe it should not be much decreased from there.

items.statement: Demand picking up post-election from chemical, oil and gas, power, engineering sectors.

So we are seeing demand from there. Oil and gas, the demands are there. Po wer industry, the demands are there. From the engineering sector, the demands are there.

items.statement: No plans to set up facility in Middle East currently.
items.quote: Right now we don't have any plan to set up a facility over there.

items.statement: Export share to be maintained at more than 25% going forward.

items.quote: Yes, the capex, which is coming in two phases, which is predominantly a total of INR175 crores and INR115 crores is the first phase.

items.quote: So this should be majorly spent by this financial year '24- '25 and leftover should be spent in the coming FY'25-'26.

items.statement: Other income to be similar to last year's INR3.20 crores, maybe slight depletion.
items.quote: Last year, it was INR3.20 crores on an annual basis. I predominantly see this sort of number, maybe a slight depletion.

items.statement: Inventory days at 90 to 100 days.
items.quote: Sort of -- what we have been earlier also sort of 100 days, 90 to 100 days.

items.statement: Branch expansion to continue at similar pace as last year's 53 branches.

items.quote: in the long run we feel that the industry will grow at around 7% to 8%.

items.quote: in the next quarter you will see a growth there in that segment. A lot of things which are in the pipeline will also come into mass production, which will further enhance the export growth and export is a very strong focus area for us.

items.statement: India order book is about INR1,000 crores; consolidated total orders about INR1,800 crores.
items.quote: At the India level, o ur order book position is about INR1,000 crores and at consol level, total orders at about I NR1,800 crores

items.statement: Margins should improve over 2 years due to mix shift to retail and better fixed cost absorption, but not spectacularly.
items.quote: So all in all, structurally speaking, I would say that over 2 years, you will see definite improvement overall level in terms of margin. But it won't be all that spectacular increases at margin level.

items.statement: Price transmission in pipe business is efficient, with price increases passed on same day as raw material price hikes.
items.quote: So our price transmissions nowadays are, especiall y in pipe business are quite efficient in a sense, if I see raw material price increase today m orning, by afternoon, we also increase the prices in the marketplace

items.statement: Expects strong season from mid-October to May with positive monsoon and election disruptions behind.
items.quote: So we are expecting from mid-October onwards to May to be very positive season with the whole election disruptions behind us as well as the monsoon, assuming it continues its good run also being there.

items.statement: UP could develop to be one of the large states for micro irrigation over next couple of years.
items.quote: So I think over the next couple of years, UP could develop to be one of the large states.

items.statement: Plans to process more crops like garlic, tomato, and North American ginger to balance seasonality.
items.quote: So for example, while w e have been primarily doing mango and onion, we are seeing garlic as something to grow mo re upon. We are seeing tomato, we could process more. As a part of spices, we are looking to process more of North American ginger

items.statement: Maharashtra state elections expected in September could cause some disruption.
items.quote: And there are state level elections expec ted sometimes in September for the state of Maharashtra legislative assembly and there could be some disruption around that time

items.statement: Government receivables of about INR900 crores outstanding; most expected to come through but some variation possible.
items.quote: There, I talked about, right, that approximately th e total government project in the pipe division and drip irrigation division is close to about INR900 crores

items.statement: Sold 0.86% of food company shares to Mandala Capital for INR9.9 crores with profit of approximately INR5 crores.
items.quote: I think as a part of overall holding and discussion s with Mandala -- this is less than 1%. I think 0.86% of the food company shares, which were sold to Mandala with a profit of approximately INR5 crores in that

items.statement: Expects FY25 to be another best-ever year benchmark
items.quote: there is a reasonable indication, the way it is looking, we can see in the 1st Quarter itself that this year is likely to be, again, probably a new benchmark for best ever.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to ~17.8% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA-to-sales ratio has also moved, improved upwards.

items.statement: Order book continues to grow with healthy execution
items.quote: If you see at this point of time, the order book continues to grow. Whatever we had for quarter, we have added something more to it and the execution is also healthy.

items.statement: Large diameter pipe order book exceeds 6.5 lakh tons
items.quote: at present we have more than 6.5 lakh tons of order for large diameter pipes

items.statement: JHESL JV order book $1.6 billion (~16 lakh tons)
items.quote: That's about 16 lakh tons.

items.statement: UAE DI pipe order book $251 million (2.25 lakh tons)
items.quote: That is 2,25,000 tons, order book is $251 million.

items.statement: JHESL JV operating at >85% capacity, Board constituted team to evaluate expansion
items.quote: They are profitable in Q1 itself, operating at a capacity of more than 80%, 85%.

items.statement: Sathavahana de-bottlenecking to increase capacity to 2.5 lakh tons
items.quote: So, that will be 2.5 lakh tons; it will take the capacity to upward of 2.5 lakh tons.

items.statement: No new capex projects announced; conserving capital and building reserves
items.quote: No, we have not announced any project as yet. See, when the company starts doing well, and we are at this point of time conserving capital within the company

items.statement: Standalone debt rose to Rs 3,900 crore from Rs 3,200 crore due to working capital increase
items.quote: the debt on a standalone basis, June 30th, March 31st, Rs. 3,200 crore has gone up to Rs. 3,900 crores, primarily because the term loan has come down from Rs. 1,760 crores to Rs. 1,400 crores, but the working capital has gone up from Rs. 1,500 crores to Rs. 2,500 crores

items.statement: Maintains coking coal inventory of 1.5 ships in yard plus one on sea; locks steel project-wise
items.quote: coking coal, we normally get four shipments a year. And we like to keep one ship on the sea, more than one and a half ships in the yard, so that we do not have any disruption. And as far as the steel is concerned, we do not block steel like this. We keep steel which is project wise.

items.statement: Water infrastructure demand secular; temporary blip due to delayed budget allocations
items.quote: We hope that there will be a catch-up, because we do not see a downward trend in the water infrastructure. But this temporary blip is only because of the budgetary allocation getting delayed by a few months.

items.statement: SAW pipe demand not sluggish; no hard landing expected
items.quote: Is SAW pipe demand getting sluggish? No. Are we worried that it is having a hard landing? No.

items.statement: Consciously moving towards value-add products; stainless steel volume target 20-25k tons
items.quote: Largely what we are going to achieve in our stainless-steel this year would be somewhere around between 20,000 and 25,000 metric tons of stainless-steel welded and seamless would be in the market or would be sold in the market.

items.statement: Export mix 70:30; water pipes to Middle East, oil & gas globally; UAE DI exports to 30+ countries
items.quote: Export, largely water sector goes to Middle East; oil and gas, we do across the globe.

items.statement: UAE DI facility targeting >2 lakh tons dispatch in FY25
items.quote: This year they should hit a good capacity, more than 2 lakh tons for sure.

items.statement: India OCTG import market ~$200 million annually; targeting self-reliance
items.quote: Roughly, OCTG annually $200 million are getting imported per year, putting ONGC, Oil India, Reliance, Vedanta, all put together $200 million.

items.statement: Order book split: 70% water, 30-35% oil & gas, 5% industrial
items.quote: Order book, I would say, oil and gas is about 30%, 35%, water is rest. The industrial sector is a very small. So, 70% is water, 5% is others, and the rest is oil and gas.

items.statement: Centre-state funding mechanism with multilateral agencies ensures project progress
items.quote: Government of India has come up with, I would say, a balanced scheme, where most of these projects of great importance, they participate, but their funds get released only if state s bring in their contribution

items.statement: Tender spacing causes temporary bumps but no structural demand decline
items.quote: Sometimes there are some spacing that happens in between tenders, and therefore you may have some small bumps, but definitely it is not a trend

items.statement: Industry demand forecast for FY25 revised down to 6-7% from earlier 7-8%; company expects to outperform industry by 1-2 percentage points
items.quote: Industry, we see that earlier the forecast was 7%-8% of demand this year FY25 for the industry. Now this has been down revised to 6-7% and we feel that we are going to do better than this at least by a percentage or 2.

items.statement: Udaipur Line 2 targeting 60% utilization by end of FY25 and 70-75% combined utilization for both lines; full 75% utilization expected by Q4 FY26
items.quote: So, unfortunately, because of general election during Quarter 1, that impacted overall demand. You know that because you know industry has not grown the way it was expected and in fact, because of this Quarter 1 subdued demand, overall forecast for the demand for this year also has down revised. But yes, nevertheless our plan holds and still we stick to that that at least 60% utilization we’ll ach

items.statement: East region EBITDA per ton at least Rs. 200 higher than North and West in Q1 FY25; company outperformed industry margins in East
items.quote: Yes, so there is a difference. East, we are doing well. Last quarter, if you look at our EBITDA is at least Rs. 200 higher than north and west, right? And if you look at industry, I think we have done better than industry in terms of really driving all those priorities which we have.

items.statement: Prices slid further by Rs. 5-7 per bag across all regions in July 2024 due to low demand and aggressive competition
items.quote: Region-wise would be difficult, but my sense is at least prices have gone down by Rs. 5 to Rs. 7 in different markets.

items.statement: Standalone capex of Rs. 90 crore in Q1 FY25; expect Rs. 800-900 crore more in remaining 3 quarters (total ~Rs. 900-1000 crore for FY25). Consolidated capex Rs. 150-160 crore in Q1; Rs. 1,500-1,650 crore for full FY25
items.quote: And going forward, we expect another Rs. 800 crores to Rs. 900 crores in the remaining 3 quarters. That is FY25.

items.statement: Future capex guidance: Rs. 1,300-1,400 crore for FY26 and ~Rs. 1,200 crore for FY27, barring spillovers
items.quote: And for FY26 broadly and FY27 last time, we spoke around Rs. 1,300 to Rs. 1,400 crore and in FY27 around Rs. 1,200 odd crores. So, that also number remains the same? Management: That remains the same, barring any spill over, that's all

items.statement: Consolidated sales volume 30.37 lakh tons in Q1 FY25 (27.89 lakh cement, 2.48 lakh clinker); flat vs 30.36 lakh tons in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Consol basis, we have done a total sale of 30.37 lakh tons out of which 27.89 lakh tons is the consol cement number and 2.48 lakh tons is consol clinker. That is in the current quarter. Corresponding quarter, it was 30.36 lakh tons total, 28.31 lakh tons cement and 2.05 lakh tons clinker

items.statement: Premium products at ~30% of sales; blended cement proportion 65% consolidated (64% standalone); trade share 54-55%
items.quote: In terms of premiumization, our premium product was at 30%, close to 30%, which is a good moment and that has impacted our bottom line to an extent.

items.statement: AFR at 12% for JK Lakshmi (up from 7% FY24 avg); renewable energy at 48% (up from 39% FY24 exit); lead distance reduced to 372 km from 384 km avg
items.quote: For instance, AFR if you take, AFR in case of JK Lakshmi Cement, it was close to 12% last quarter, which is much higher than last year avera ge of 7%. In terms of renewable energy, last quarter we have closed at about 48%, which is much higher than the exit overall average of last year which was 39

items.statement: Standalone net debt Rs. 325 crore (gross Rs. 700 cr, cash Rs. 375 cr); Consolidated net debt Rs. 1,650 crore (gross Rs. 2,050 cr, cash Rs. 400 cr) as of June 2024
items.value: Standalone net: Rs. 325 cr; Consol net: Rs. 1,650 cr
items.quote: On a standalone basis, the gross debt on a standalone was about Rs. 700 crores and about Rs. 375 crores of cash. So, that leaves a net debt of Rs. 325 crores. That is on a standalone basis. And as far as on a consol level is concerned about Rs. 2,050 crores of gross debt and Rs. 400 crores of cash mean Rs. 1,650 of net debt.

items.statement: Target consolidated net debt/EBITDA 2-2.25x and gross debt/EBITDA 3-3.5x despite ongoing expansion capex over next 5-6 years
items.quote: In spite of these all expansion, which are going to happen over the next 5, 6 years, we don't see our debt to EBITDA crossing anywhere between 3 to 3.5 and a net debt to EBITDA about 2 to 2.25.

items.statement: Current consolidated capacity 16.5 MTPA; Surat grinding unit (1.4 MTPA) in FY25 takes to 18 MTPA; Durg brownfield (4.5 MTPA in 2 phases) by FY27 takes to 22.5 MTPA; Northeast (2.5 MTPA) takes to ~25 MTPA; further Nagaur, Kutch, Udaipur line
items.quote: We are today sitting on a capacity of 16.5 million tons together with Udaipur, and then immediately we have 1.4 million tons of Surat coming in, so that takes up to 18 million tons. Then another 4.5 million tons coming in 3 years' time for the brownfield expansion in 2 phases, that takes us to 22.5 million tons. And another 2.5 million coming from Northeast makes it almost 25 million tons.

items.statement: Northeast project land acquisition nearing completion; environment clearance application underway; approvals expected by end of CY2024; civil work to start Q4 FY25; plant commissioning in 14-16 months thereafter (spillover to FY27)
items.quote: What we believe that, we are in July, so by end of this year, we are going to have approvals in place. And somewhere quarter 4 of this year, we'll start the civil work.

items.statement: Merger of UCWL into JK Lakshmi approved; swap ratio 4:100; post-merger promoter holding ~45.12%; synergies from fixed cost savings, common procurement, logistics alignment but difficult to quantify exact savings
items.quote: The swap ratio is 4 shares for every 100 shares held in Udaipur. And the post-merger promoter's holding is likely to be about 45.12%.

items.statement: Conveyor belt project awaiting final approvals; expected in couple of months
items.quote: So, we are still awaiting approvals. That is in the final stages. And we are expected to get that maybe in another couple of months' time.

items.statement: Distribution strategy unchanged: focus on core markets (Rajasthan, Gujarat, East) where company is relevant player; not venturing into new markets; will consolidate position before expanding
items.quote: So, we are not venturing into new market. First, we want to consolidate, make ourselves relevant. And then maybe I think we will look for opportunity when things are conducive, and we will go to other markets.

items.statement: Pricing pressure intense across regions; competitors aggressive to gain market share; company maintaining price positioning to bridge gap with leaders rather than chase volume
items.quote: We definitely don't want to really dilute our price positioning. That's very, very important because we look for an opportunity for us to reduce the gap with the leaders, right? So, to an extent, I think that is also our strategy because during this time, when everybody is dropping prices and trying to push volume which is perhaps not there in the market, our strategy is little different that how

items.statement: Realization drop driven by higher clinker sales (lower realization), adverse geographic mix (West prices lower), and competitor aggression in some markets; no change in geo mix (lead distance stable at 372 km)
items.quote: So, as I told you, little more clinker sales. So, because of that, that is reason number one. Second, some of the geographies, price drop was more and where our reliance is a little bit on higher side. For instance, West. West, prices were lower, much lower than other geographies, right? And third, I thin k in some of the other market, other than West also, competitors were quite aggressive

items.statement: Cost reduction initiatives: renewable energy expansion, AFR phase 2 at Sirohi (target 17-18%), Durg AFR to 10-12%, pyro-process optimization via technology; supply chain lead optimization; expect cumulative Rs. 50-75/ton improvement
items.quote: And I'll not say the drastic cost reduction is going to happen. But I think all those things are going to put together definitely Rs. 50 to Rs. 75 higher.

items.statement: No specific EBITDA/ton or price increase guidance for FY25; management refuses to forecast during lean months as unreliable
items.quote: I think this is going to be speculative. So, I think as of now I would not really comment on this. Because anything you forecast during lean months, then I think your forecast is going to be on other side of it.

items.statement: Expects CV industry to be flattish at worst, with possible growth for the full year.
items.quote: We think at worst, industry would be flattish, but we can also expect some kind of growth in the overall CV industry as well for the whole year.

items.statement: Expects next three quarters to continue the momentum.
items.quote: It does seem the next three quarters should continue the momentum.

items.statement: Expects Power Solutions business to register healthy growth on a full year basis.
items.quote: On a full year basis, we expect this business also to register healthy growth.

items.statement: Aims to double defense business in the next 2 to 2.5 years.
items.quote: So, now our intention is to double the defense business again in the next 2 to 2.5 years.

items.statement: Plans to double defense top line again in the next two years or so.
items.quote: And now going forward, based on a very strong pipeline of orders and visibility of orders that can come in, we hope to double that number again in the next two years or so.

items.statement: Retained earlier capex estimate of around 750 crores.
items.quote: On the CAPEX side, I would say that we have retained our earlier estimates as Shenu had indicated earlier. It could be around 750 crores.

items.statement: May invest another 500 to 750 crores in associate companies, primarily Switch and OHM.
items.quote: It could be around another 500 to 750 crores of the investments in the associate companies , primarily, Switch and OHM.

items.statement: Switch has order book of 560 for Delhi, 300+ for Bangalore, 100 for UP, and 400 for Delhi after April.
items.quote: Switch has an order book of 560 for Delhi up to March 31st, 300 plus for Bangalore and another 100 for U P. And after April, we have an orde r for another 400 for Delhi as well

items.statement: Expects to do better on margin front due to operating leverage and cost headroom.
items.quote: So, we think we should be able to do better on the margin front.

items.statement: Not taken any price increase in Q1 or Q2 so far.
items.quote: So far, that’s the status.

items.statement: May not go for any commodity provision in the next quarter.
items.quote: But as of now, it appears, as Shenu indicated, it appears that we may not go for any provision in the next quarter.

items.statement: Expects tipper segment to start improving from July or August onwards.
items.quote: So, from July or August onwards, we think even the tipper segment would start improving.

items.statement: Expects cargo segment to start growing maybe August onwards.
items.quote: So, with the tipper segment coming up, the cargo segment also should start growing, we think, maybe August onwards.

items.statement: Plans to launch four more LCV products in the next few quarters within the year.
items.quote: We will be launching four more LC V products in the next few quarters within the year.

items.statement: DFC impact is medium-term, no major significant impact in next couple of years.
items.quote: A lot remains to be seen, but we don’t think there will be a major significant impact in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Rights issue expected to close on 19th August; proceeds to repay short-term debt for acquisitions.
items.quote: We announced the rights issue. We expect to close on 19th August. And as announced, we will use the proceeds to repa y short-term debt finan cing raised for acquisitions.

items.statement: Committed to move growth businesses from 20% to 30% of portfolio; 30% will grow at 30%.
items.quote: We had committed last quarter when we finished the acquisitions that we will move our growth businesses from being 20% of the portfolio to 30% of the portfolio. W e had also committed saying 20% of the portfolio was growing 30% and that 30% will grow at 30%.

items.statement: Committed to complete Organic India integration in 100 days.
items.quote: While the Capital Foods integration is largely complete, the transactions for Organic India was completed on 16th April and we have made a commitment of completing it in 100 days.

items.statement: Plan to aggressively expand vending machine installed base from 1700 machines.
items.quote: We now have an installed base about 1700 odd machines and the plan is to aggressively expand that going forward.

items.statement: Expect gross margins for acquisitions to return to stated levels and climb higher.
items.quote: Ultimately, we do expect gross margins to come back to the numbers that we stated which is significantly accretive to our current portfolio. In fact, if anything, the gross margin should climb higher and not stay where they are.

items.statement: Confident to deliver business case for Capital Foods and Organic India acquisitions.
items.quote: So, right now, we are working on what we have. And we remain quite confident that we will be able to deliver the business case.

items.statement: Amortization charge for acquisitions is about Rs. 55 crores per quarter, likely static.
items.quote: So, on the acquisition as I mentioned while discussing the financials, that is a charge of about Rs. 55 crores per quarter and that is likely to remain static quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: No intention to move energy drinks into PET bottles; cups are key differentiator.
items.quote: And there is no intention currently of moving into PET bottles. Cups is my single biggest differentiator, helps me manage the price point, helps me build the imagery and therefore currently we will stick to it.

items.statement: Will provide more specific volume and pricing data going forward.
items.quote: But point taken, we will try to be more specific as we go forward.

items.statement: Will consider aligning segment reporting with management commentary for transparency.
items.quote: Fair point. Vivek, we will de finitely look at, I mean, we have got this feedback, I think, from multiple people in the past one hour or so. So, the idea is we want to be very transparent in the numbers that we put out.

name: Cholamandalam Investment and Finance Company Ltd

items.statement: Management expects 20-25% volume growth for FY25 and EBITDA margins to sustain at current ~20.8% levels for FY25, with visibility for next 2-3 quarters.
items.quote: We should be achieving an overall growth in terms of volume as compared to what we did in the previous year, upwards of 20%. It could be even 25% if there is going to be a good strong calendar year '25 also.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to sustain at current levels for FY25-26 if global outlook remains stable, with better clarity by December on FY26 contracts and raw material inputs.
items.quote: But broadly if the global outlook and, the global foray is going to be as it is, you can expect the margins to continue even in the year FY25-26.

items.statement: Prigiv JV greenfield expansion in Mahad is at advanced stage, expected to commercialize by Q3 FY25, manufacturing 40+ products exclusively for Givaudan.
items.quote: Our greenfield expansion under Prigiv project a JV between Privi and Givaudan in Mahad is at an advanced stage of implementation and is expected to commercialize by Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Galaxmusk and Camphor running at 85%+ utilization, expected to reach near 100% in coming quarters with strong order book and spot sales.
items.quote: Galaxmusk and Camphor have really done very well, and we expect in this quarter that it could be almost at 100% capacity as we talk about.

items.statement: Strong order booking for Galaxmusk (80%+ sold out), Camphor season strong, Prionyl gaining traction; 65-68% of sales on long-term contracts, 30-35% spot/Indian market.
items.quote: Normally our contracts are about 65% and about 35% is for the Indian markets and the spot market because Indian markets normally believe in not giving very, very long term orders.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 20.8% vs 14.6% YoY, driven by operating efficiencies (efficient boiler, heat recovery, yield improvements, process optimization) and favorable raw material coverage.
items.quote: The company has made an EBITDA margin of close to INR97 crores, which is a growth of about 60% over last year and the margin percentage for this year has been about 20.8%.

items.statement: Finished goods prices rising on spot market due to raw material shortages; some freight cost pass-through to customers; camphor prices up 7-8% in last 1.5 months.
items.quote: Last one, one and a half month, we have seen close to about maybe 7% to 8% or so in fact.

items.statement: Revenue mix: Pine 59%, Musk & Specialty 24%, Citral 9%, Phenol 8%, Value-added ~1%; Value-added share grew from 1% to 4% over 2-3 years.
items.quote: Pine as a space, you know pine-based chemicals, aroma chemicals have contributed 59% of the total revenue. Musk and speciality chemicals contributed about 24%.

items.statement: Demand for key aroma chemicals remains strong, driven by FMCG and fragrance brands across all product tiers; industry growing 5-6% annually.
items.quote: Demand for the key products which we manufacture remains strong, underscoring the segment's stability and the essential role they play in the industry.

items.statement: Gaining market share from competitors due to quality, service, on-time logistics, and sustainability (zero liquid discharge, EcoVadis Gold); customers prefer Privi for sustainability credentials.
items.quote: On those counts, we are rated extremely high. On quality, of course, we are very good, but on sustainability scale, we are immensely high, and which is what is, resulting in customers preferring Privi.

items.statement: Net working capital days improved from 155 to 147 days (consol) in Q1; targeting 130-135 days.
items.quote: We are close to in this quarter from in a moved down from 155 in the previous quarter to this quarter of about 147 days on a consol basis.

items.statement: Standalone debt INR868 crore; consolidated debt INR992 crore (including Prigiv JV) as of Q1 FY25.
items.value: Standalone INR868 cr; Consolidated INR992 cr
items.quote: On a standalone basis, it is about INR868 crores. On a consol, including Prigiv, we are at about INR992 crores.

items.statement: Privi Fine Sciences acquisition pending shareholder approval (postal ballot closes 12 Aug); integration plan ready post-approval for cost synergies.
items.quote: We are still in the process of obtaining the shareholders' permission and the postal ballot is on. Too early for me to comment anything.

items.statement: Menthol project using side-streams from CST/GTO processing; 18-month implementation; expected 200-300 bps ROCE improvement over 3-4 years.
items.quote: You will find that about 200 to 300 odd basis point increase in the return on capital employed and also corresponding return on equity also will increase.

items.statement: Backward integration with CST and Pinene; monthly/quarterly raw material planning optimizes feedstock quality and cost; opportunistic Gum Turpentine Oil buying.
items.quote: On a monthly basis, we plan the raw materials which are required, okay, Alpha pinene, Beta pinene, and also what quality of Alpha pinene we require.

items.statement: Volume sold 10,672 MT in Q1 FY25 vs 7,541 MT YoY; second consecutive quarter above 10,000 MT.
items.quote: The volume for this quarter has been an impressive 10,672 metric tons as against 7,541 metric tons that was done by us in the Q1 of June 23.

items.statement: New products volume split: Pine 7,065 MT, Phenol 1,408 MT, Citral 443 MT, Musk & Specialty 1,482 MT, Value-added 274 MT.

items.quote: Pine as a space for this quarter has been 7,065 metric tons. Phenol has been 1,408. Citral as a segment is 443 tons. Musk in speciality is 1,482, and value added is about 274 tons.

items.statement: US FDA approval for Camphor expected by year-end 2024.
items.quote: The company is one more step in the process of obtaining the U.S. FDA and we definitely are poised to get the U.S. FDA by this year-end or so.

items.statement: Latin America growth constrained by payment risks; focusing on customers with upfront payment or solid bank channels via US subsidiary.
items.quote: We are doing our best to ensure that those customers who are in a better position to pay us upfront or where they are in a position to open up with solid banks through US, we have been selling through our Privi US office.

items.statement: Organization governed by professionals with 20+ years average experience; 1000+ employees driving growth.
items.quote: The organization is governed and managed by professionals who are having more than an average of 20 years of experience with requisite qualification and their domain expertise.

items.statement: NIM was 4.36% in Q1-2025, down from 4.40% in Q4-2024 and 4.78% in Q1-2024
items.quote: The net interest margin was 4.36% in Q1 -2025 compared to 4.40% in Q4 -2024 and 4.78% in Q1-2024.

items.statement: NIM expected to be range-bound with no sharp movements from current levels
items.quote: What we mean by range-bound is that the process is largely done. And from here , we don't expect sharp movements.

items.quote: The domestic loan portfolio grew by 15.9% year-on-year and 3.3% sequentially at June 30, 2024

items.statement: Retail loan portfolio grew 17.1% YoY and 2.4% sequentially; personal loans grew 24.9% YoY and 1.5% sequentially

items.statement: Credit card portfolio grew 31.3% YoY and 4.2% sequentially; business banking grew 35.6% YoY and 8.9% sequentially
items.quote: The credit card portfolio grew by 31.3% year -on-year and 4.2% sequentially. The business-banking portfolio grew by 35.6% year -on-year and 8.9% sequentially.

items.statement: SME business grew 23.5% YoY and 4.0% sequentially; rural portfolio grew 16.9% YoY and 3.4% sequentially
items.quote: The SME business, comprising borrowers with a turnover of less than ₹250 crore, grew by 23.5% year -on-year and 4.0% sequentially. The rural portfolio grew by 16.9% year-on-year and 3.4% sequentially.

items.statement: Domestic corporate portfolio grew 10.3% YoY and 3.1% sequentially at June 30, 2024
items.quote: Growth in the domestic corporate portfolio was 10.3% year-on-year and 3.1% sequentially at June 30, 2024

items.statement: Total period-end deposits increased 15.1% YoY to ₹14,26,150 crore at June 30, 2024
items.quote: Total period-end deposits increased by 15.1% year-on-year to ₹14,26,150 crore at June 30, 2024

items.statement: Average deposits increased 17.8% YoY and 3.3% sequentially to ₹13,78,658 crore during Q1-2025
items.quote: Average deposits increased by 17.8% year -on-year and 3.3% sequentially to ₹13,78,658 crore during Q1-2025

items.statement: NIM guidance range of 13.5% to 14% steady state

items.quote: On the portfolio quality for the microfinance business, we continue to maintain provisioning at 80%. The quarter saw GNPA increase to 2.6% from 1.63% a year ago, which is an increase of about 97 bps. Sequentially, GNPA increased by 109 bps, which was reported end of March.

items.statement: NNPA at 0.53%, up 4 bps QoQ

items.statement: PAR 1-30 bucket at 3.1-3.2%
items.quote: To your question on the 1 to 30, it's typical. If you see the past trends also, it is 1 to 30 equivalent to your 31 to 90. So at this point in time, it is 3.1%, 3.2%.

items.statement: Stage 2 coverage increased sharply to 47-48% from 37-38% due to ECL model update
items.quote: We have updated the model last quarter, if you recall, and we have kind of smoothened the data across the 8-year period in the ECL model and have taken out all the biases, which were running in the model from a, let's say, COVID-perspective or from a Demonetisation perspective or any other aberration that was there in the business?

items.statement: No weakening demand seen; disbursement toned down voluntarily for quality

items.statement: NIM at 15.2%, up 91 bps YoY and 58 bps QoQ due to lower cost of borrowing
items.quote: NIM for the quarter was 15.2%, which is up 91 bps Y-o-Y and 58 bps quarter-on-quarter. NIMs improved as a result of lower cost of borrowing.

items.statement: Yield on portfolio at 24.4%, up 35 bps YoY

items.statement: Passed on 1% rate reduction to customers in 6th cycle and above from April 1

items.quote: The bench strength in 60% branches has been enhanced by 20% because as a preemptive measure of attrition, we are just ensuring that we strengthen our bench strength, so that immediately, there is no disruption.

items.statement: AUM grew 72% YoY to INR11,723 crores

items.statement: Acquired 200,000 customers in Q1; stopped lending to new-to-credit borrowers

items.quote: We expect these 2 lines of business to scale up to about INR500 crores by end of the current financial year.

items.statement: Bank borrowing mix increased to 59%; target 60-70%
items.quote: Likewise, if I look at the borrowing mix, we now have a more healthy mix with bank's contribution increasing to 59% at the end of quarter 1. We intend to optimize our borrowing mix with banks contributing about 60% to 70%.

items.statement: Received two rating upgrades: India Ratings to A+ Stable, ICRA to A+ Stable; CARE at A+
items.quote: During the quarter, we got 2 upgrades from the existing rating agencies. The first was India Ratings, which upgraded us to A+ Stable from A Stable. Then we had ICRA, which upgraded us to A+ Stable from, again, A Positive.

items.statement: Operations expected to normalize in 3-4 months; challenges deemed transitory
items.quote: We believe these challenges are transitory in nature and operations should normalize within the next 3 to 4 months.

items.statement: No structural over-leverage issue seen in industry; attrition and fraud controls are key risks
items.quote: My personal belief and having looked at multiple data points, I personally do not believe there is a systemic over-leverage issue across the industry. I firmly believe that. There could be a few pockets, a few institutions here and there. But my sense is -- forget Spandana, my sense is that it will at best to be in a single digit, cannot be more.

items.quote: Because weekly, overall, if you would have seen our numbers, we have also given weekly branches in the INR1,400 crores portfolio's performance is at 98% collection efficiency compared to 94% on an overall basis.

items.quote: So on a cadence basis, if you see, 25% of our disbursement is weekly. On an AUM basis, obviously, AUM operates at a lag, it is about 15%.

items.quote: With the expansion of the fractionation capacity to 40,000 per ton, we anticipate a significant surge in our revenues. Thus, we are upgrading our guidance to INR 750 crores plus for the fiscal year 2025 along with an increase in profitability due to the economies of scale, margin improvements and multiple other efficiencies which we are achieving.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 in range of 20% to 22% with full benefits expected in FY26
items.quote: So the company will try to maintain this margin in the range of 20% to 22% in the coming financial year and it could of course can surpass more, but the company will be in a better position to guide it further beyond 20% to 22 % as the quarter passes by.

items.statement: Fractionation capacity expanded from 15,000 to 40,000 metric tons with latest 25,000 metric tons expansion commissioned July 2024
items.quote: With an initial fractionation capacity of 15,000 metric tons in the year 2020-21, Manorama has successfully expanded its operations, reaching a current fractionation capacity of 40,000 metric tons. The latest expansion of 25,000 metric tons was commissioned in July 2024.

items.statement: Total capex invested around INR 212 crores including INR 100+ crores for new expansion with extraction, refinery, interesterification and fractionation plants
items.quote: To date, the company has invested around INR212 crores in the capital expenditures, including a significant expansion of 25,000 metric tons capacity.

items.statement: New capacity expansion cost over INR 100 crores including extraction plant 90,000 tons, refinery 30,000 tons, interesterification 15,000 tons, fractionation 25,000 tons per annum
items.quote: For the new capacity, we have spent more than INR 100 crores on this new capacity expansion, which includes the extraction plant of 90,000 tons, the refinery plant of 30,000 metric tons per annum, the interesterification plant of 15,000 metric tons per annum, and the fractionation plant of 25,000 metric tons per annum, along with the other supporting infrastructure and needs.

items.statement: New expansion at peak utilization expected to generate INR 600-800 crores revenue by end of FY27 at asset turnover 6-8x
items.quote: At peak utilization, the new expansion should generate a revenue which is close to INR600 crores to INR800 crores on an asset turnover ratio of ranges between 6 to 8. At today's pricing, we expect we should reach our optimum utilization of the new capacity by the end of FY'27.

items.statement: Global CBE and specialty fat butter market to surpass USD 2,030 million by 2032 at 6.1% CAGR; global exotic butter and fat industry over 2 million tons growing at 7% annually
items.quote: As per the industry's business size, the global CBE and specialty fat butter market is likely to surpass USD 2,030 million by 2032, growing at a 6.1% CAGR.

items.statement: No new global capacity added in recent years; newer applications increasing demand for specialty exotic fats and CBE
