items.quote: Secondly, in the last few years, there has been no new capacity, less capacity, which has been added globally. Additionally, there are newer and newer applications that are getting developed which increases the demand for our specialty exotic fats and cocoa butter equivalent.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded 335 bps YoY to 20.1% from effective cost management and operational efficiencies
items.quote: EBITDA margin expanded by 335 basis points and year-on-year at 20.1% in Q1FY25. This margin improvement reflects effective cost management strategies and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: CBE realization improved 10-15% vs last year due to global demand surge; margins sustainable at 20-22% with operating leverage and better mix
items.quote: So, on average, we can take on a jump of around 10% to 15%. On the pricing chart, we have initiated our booking accordingly and we are taking our contracts as per the revised price for our new products.

items.statement: Value-added products (CBE + stearin) currently 50-60% of production; target CBE wallet share 20-30% in FY25, up to 50% in FY26; combined value-added target 70%
items.quote: 50%-60% whatever the company currently produces is the value-added product. So, of course, we have actually increased our wallet share for our value-added products. Currently, it is 50%-60% combining both CBE and stearin. So, we aim to increase our wallet share of CBE to 20%-30% for the current financial year

items.statement: Existing plant at 100% utilization; new plant expected 60-70% utilization in FY25, 80-85% in FY26; optimum utilization >90% possible
items.quote: For the new capacity, we expect our utilization to be around 60%-70%. And for the existing capacity, we expect 100% utilization.

items.statement: 80+ global clients including Ferrero, Mondelez, Nestle, Hershey, Mars, Body Shop, Barry Callebaut, L'Oreal, Lush; expanded to US, Europe, Russia, Middle East, Turkey
items.quote: Today, we have more than 80 global clients. We also have -- we have expanded our business to US, Europe, Russia, Middle East, Turkey, and various other countries.

items.statement: CBE pricing not directly tied to cocoa butter prices; CBE has own value chain and demand; most freight cost increases from Red Sea crisis passed to customers
items.quote: The increase of cocoa butter definitely increases the price. But our basic model is whether whatever the price of cocoa butter is there, the CBE has its own value chain and its own requirement all over the world.

items.statement: Interest cost INR 8.5 crores in Q1 at 9% average borrowing cost; INR 250 crores net working capital for raw material procurement; INR 95 crores surplus FDR
items.quote: It will continue for these three quarters. And we are debt-free means we have a surplus fund of our cash FDR, so technically we have -- around INR250 crores is only working capital for the procurement of raw materials, net debt.

items.statement: Target to be 100% debt-free in 3-4 years; currently INR 95 crores fixed deposits; all borrowings for working capital procurement
items.quote: The clear intention of Manorama is to be 100% debt-free. We already have INR 95 crores of fixed deposits in the bank also and our plan is to be debt-free in the next three to four years.

items.statement: Sal seed procurement 80,000-100,000 tons annually (<10% of India's 1.5M tons); Shea nut procurement 40,000-80,000 tons annually (Africa produces 1.76M tons); no major supply risk
items.quote: According to the government reports, India produces 15 lakh metric tons of sal seeds annually. Manorama procures around 80,000 to 1 lakh metric tons of sal seeds accounting for less than 10% of the available supply.

items.statement: Raw material procurement on spot prices from tribal collectors; payments through banking channels to village heads; no contracts with forest dwellers
items.quote: On Shea nuts and all you have to understand this is procured by millions of tribal women and when we use the word tribal and forest travellers they are natural forest people of India and West Africa and there cannot be any contract. All the nuts what we buy from them are on the prices of that day.

items.statement: Exports 73% of Q1 FY25 revenue (INR 97 crores); domestic 27%; container freight doubled due to Red Sea crisis but mostly passed through pricing
items.quote: Exports contributed INR97 crores, making up 73% of total revenue. This indicates strong international market performance.

items.statement: FY20-24 track record: Revenue 25% CAGR, EBITDA 14% CAGR, PAT 15% CAGR
items.quote: Highlighting our Long-term performance for FY20-24 track record, revenue registered 25% CAGR. EBITDA clocked 14% CAGR. PAT had 15% CAGR during the period.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue grew 19.6% YoY to INR 133 crores; EBITDA surged 43.6% YoY to INR 26.8 crores; PAT grew 17.2% YoY to INR 13.5 crores
items.quote: Manorama Industries achieved a notable 19.6 year-on-year increase in its revenue, reaching [INR 133] crores. This growth is attributable to robust demand across the company's product portfolio in both domestic and international markets.

items.statement: Subsidiaries in West Africa for shea procurement; Russia, Dubai for local sales to smaller chocolate companies; Australia for market presence
items.quote: The subsidiaries in West Africa, Africa's subsidiaries are for procurement of shea nuts from the tribals and villagers of those regions like we do in India whereas the subsidiary in Russia is for selling to the local small companies which are based in Russia where we need to be present to cater to the smaller companies.

items.statement: Raw material supply subject to seasonal variation and natural calamities; Red Sea crisis doubled container freight to some markets
items.quote: The volumes available for both our products are in millions of tons of Sal in India or Shea in Africa or even Mango Kernel in India. So we are quite sure unless and until there is a major natural calamity or something.

items.statement: Further expansion projects under feasibility study; will announce after board approval; teams working simultaneously on future expansions
items.quote: There are a couple of projects in pipeline which companies preparing the plan and working on the feasibility and details and once we are ready we will come to our board for approval of the thing.

items.statement: HALS volume target 150-200 tons/month in next 3-4 months; FY25 ~2,000 tons; FY26 ~5,000-6,000 tons (50% capacity utilization)
items.quote: So roughly 150 to 180 tons per month, we should start achieving now going forward. I mean, of course, let a quarter go because we these products have just started commercial production. But probably in the next 3 to 4 months' time, our target is to touch 150 to 200 tons a month of all those together.

items.statement: Pharma intermediates commercialization by Q3 FY25
items.quote: We are on track to commercialize the production of the Pharma intermediates by Q3 FY'25.

items.statement: Performance Chemicals novel process plant capex INR150 cr, commercialization H1 FY26, addressing 15% global market demand
items.quote: The total capex towards the production block at our subsidiary is estimated to be INR150 crores, and the plant is expected to commercialize by H1 FY'26 with the capacity which could address 15% of the market demand.

items.statement: Third capex ~INR150 cr for water treatment chemical, construction start Sep/Oct 2024, commercialization ~12 months later
items.quote: See, typically, it is a 10 to 12-month process for us from construction to plant direction to water trials. So assume if we start in September or October, you can add 12 months to that.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex ~INR100 cr primarily investment in subsidiary CFCL
items.quote: We have incurred a capex of about INR100 crores during the quarter 1, which was primarily towards investment in subsidiary.

items.statement: Three capex projects: Pharma intermediates INR30 cr (Q3 FY25), Performance Chemicals novel process INR150 cr (H1 FY26), Water treatment chemical INR150 cr (start Sep/Oct 2024)
items.quote: So 150, 150 and 30 crores.

items.statement: HALS monthly sales volume scaled to 125 tons/month (770 + 701); target 150-200 tons/month in 3-4 months
items.quote: For this particular quarter, the HALS monthly sales volume scale d to 125 tons per month for the HALS series, which is 770 and 701 put together.

items.statement: CFCL HALS installed capacity 9,000-10,000 tons; currently <20% utilization
items.quote: Because see, our overall capacity installed would be around 9,000 tons to 10,000 tons, which I think over the next 3 to 4 years, we will ramp up to take it to 80% capacity utilization.

items.statement: CFCL subsidiary at loss in Q1 due to high fixed cost vs low sales; fixed cost ~INR5-6 cr/quarter (employee, power, other)
items.quote: For subsidiary, apart from raw material, we have incurred employee expense , power & fuel cost, and also other expenses, which is in the range of INR5 crores to INR6 crores.

items.statement: Realizations stable QoQ, no price increase seen; possible improvement over next 2-3 quarters
items.quote: Stable. I am not seeing any increase in prices and it would be possible over the next 2 or 3 quarters.

items.statement: US destocking prolonged due to transit times; Europe grew with new customer onboarding; some US entities shifting procurement to Europe
items.quote: There is nothing specific. Of course, overall, there was the highest destocking was there in the U.S. because of the geographical -- the transit time distances. So you know the destocking took longer compared to other parts of the globe. But other than that, there is nothing significant to pinpoint here. Like if you see our Europe business grew. So we were able to onboard some new customers. And s

items.statement: Revenue mix: Performance Chemicals 69%, Pharma 18%, FMCG 13%; Performance volume-led, Pharma volume & realization, FMCG volume-led
items.quote: The revenue contribution from Performance Chemicals, Pharma and Agro intermediates and FMCG Chemicals were 69%, 18% and 13%, respectively. The Performance segment witnessed strong growth led by increased volumes. Pharma segment growth was led by improved volume and realization and FMCG segment growth was primarily volume-led.

items.statement: CFCL commercialized HALS 770 in Q1; added HALS 622, 944, 783 in July; HALS 119 by Aug 2nd week; target full basket to match competitors
items.quote: During the current quarter, at CFCL, we stabilized 770 HALS production and reported revenues only for HALS 770. During the month of July, CFCL commercialized three additional new products under the HALS segment, which a re HALS 622, HALS 944 and HALS 783. Soon within a couple of weeks, we will also be commercializing HALS 119.

items.statement: HALS customers waiting for full product basket to switch; aspire 70-75% India market share; export to Asia, US, Europe picking up with full basket
items.quote: we typically aspire that we should have 70% to 75% of Indian market becaus e of a variety of reasons compared to what people are importing. So the aspiration is to have 70% to 75% of Indian market. And of course, grow in Asia, in American and European markets which now has started picking up because, again, the same issue, a lot of customers were reluctant to only test 1 product

items.statement: Chinese competitors have cost advantage at scale; CFCL at <20% utilization vs competitors 15+ years; need 2-3 quarters to cover fixed costs and improve margins
items.quote: See because today it's a very large facility and the base is too high, I mean, in terms of costs. Hence, until we reach a proper scale and size, it will be difficult to be cheaper than the Chinese because today, we are running at probably less than 20% capacity utilization, whereas I'm competing with people who have been in this business for 15 -odd plus years.

items.statement: CRISIL reaffirmed long-term rating AA-/Stable and short-term A1+
items.quote: CRISIL has reaffirmed long term rating at CRISIL AA-/Stable and short -term rating at CRISIL A1+.

items.statement: Investing in 6 MW solar plant to moderate power bill and enhance green footprint
items.quote: We are pleased to announce additional investments towards setting up 6-megawatt solar plant, which will moderate our power bill and enhance our green footprint.

items.statement: Pharma intermediate samples approved by some customers; others need commercial samples
items.quote: The pilot samples are approved by some of the customers because not all pharma customers are okay testing pilot samples, they need commercial samples.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 40-45% range; moving beyond 45% requires sustainability over a couple of years
items.quote: It remains in the range of 40% to 45% as of now, because we have to see sustainability of enhanced margin.

items.statement: Issuer Solutions revenue growth guided at mid-20s (20-25%) for FY25 including IPO revenues
items.quote: We are looking to mid-20s, only 20s to mid-20s growth profile this year.

items.statement: International acquisition expected to add 10-15% to annual top-line and bottom-line
items.quote: The value expansion from a top line stand could be a decent profile anywhere between 10% to 15% over our current numbers, in terms of the annual top-line numbers and the bottom-line.

items.statement: International acquisition targeted at USD 50-75 million, to be funded from internal accruals (INR 450-500 crores cash); expected to close in 4-5 months
items.quote: Our sweet spot is anywhere around USD50 to USD75 million and of course, smaller the better. But at USD50 to USD75 million, as you could imagine, that easily could be financed with our own internal accruals.

items.statement: Won ~280 corporate registry clients including Hyundai IPO; 30+ IPO mandates expected to go live in coming 2-3 quarters based on DRHP filings
items.quote: We have won near about 280 clients in corporate registry, our second largest business. Very, very proud of my team's execution capabilities in terms of having won what could be the largest IPO in India, that of Hyundai.

items.statement: Alternatives AUM crossed INR 1 trillion; significant committed vs drawn-down capital gap provides revenue visibility
items.quote: Our AUM has crossed a trillion and that offers really well in terms of our overall growth. And a series of the funds that we have already won, where the capital had been drawn down to a certain extent, there is a significant gap in terms of commitment versus drawn down capital.

items.statement: Mutual fund industry AUM grew from $500B to $600B in 7-8 months; SIP inflows remain strong; KFin maintains or improves market share across all segments
items.quote: In just a matter of seven to eight months, the mutual fund industry had grown from $500 billion to about $600 billion, and that just speaks volumes in terms of the resilience this particular market has.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 42% (up 315 bps YoY); highest ever Q1 margin; expect margins to improve further in Q2-Q4 as revenue scales
items.quote: This quarter at near about 42% EBITDA margin is probably the highest Q1 that we've ever had, right? And if you saw last year, it was 37% the year before that.

items.statement: International business EBITDA margin at 30-35%; yields at 5.2 bps vs 3.6 bps in India; expect margin improvement as large deals materialize
items.quote: International business continues to be hovering around 30%-35% EBITDA margins. And as Sreekanth mentioned that as the new deals, which are large deals, get fortified, this will improve further.

items.statement: IT expenses increased due to cloud migration; revenue realization from these investments expected in subsequent quarters
items.quote: The increase in IT expenses because of movement towards cloud, that we see the overall expenses going up in the first quarter, the realization of that the corresponding revenue will happen in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Three milestone-based tech contracts (data lake, digital assets) signed; two already generating revenue in Q2, third starting within fortnight; recurring annual maintenance revenue
items.quote: For two of the three contracts, the milestones have already started to kick in. All of these contracts are milestone-based, some at the signing time, some at the development, some at the testing, so on and so forth.

items.statement: Mutual fund AUM market share expanded to ~42% from 37% YoY; corporate registry DMAT growth at 32%
items.quote: Mutual funds, for example, we have seen our overall AUM market share at roughly 42% as compared to 37%.

items.statement: Pension business grew 27% YoY vs industry 12%; NPS market share gains continue
items.quote: The industry grew at 12%. We continued to outperform the industry by a factor of two, a little over two. We grew at 27% in the case of pensions.

items.statement: International investor solutions revenue grew 56.8% YoY and 11% QoQ; now 11.5% of total revenue vs 10.5% last year
items.quote: the international and other investor solutions have seen a robust growth in terms of revenue by 56.8% year -on-year and about 11% s equentially quarter-on-quarter

items.statement: Hexagram acquisition revenue grew 80% YoY and 54% QoQ; Webile Technologies revenue doubled YoY
items.quote: The Hexagram acquisition that we did has really contributed in terms of sale of platform and implementation of this platform along with the services that we offer, 80% growth year-on-year and almost 54% growth sequentially in terms of revenue.

items.statement: Mutual fund yield marginally compressed from 3.72 to 3.66 bps due to contract renegotiations effective April 1; all large contracts renegotiated; no further significant compression expected unless telescopic pricing triggers at higher AUM
items.quote: Almost all our large contracts have been renegotiated as of 1st of April this year. So we do not anticipate significant compression, except of course what may come through in the form of any big changes in the form of the telescopic pricing kicking in.

items.statement: Domestic alternatives pricing at 3-4 bps; happy if it settles near 4 bps; international alternatives pricing 7-20 bps; KFin earns separate TA and FA fees
items.quote: Three to four basis points is a pretty reasonable number, for the Indian alternatives in the context of the scale. I'd be very happy if it settles, anywhere near four at the higher end of the threshold.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents at INR 452 crores; will be utilized for M&A; debt-free company
items.quote: We are now having strong cash and cash equivalent of almost INR452 crores w hich will be utilized towards the M&A that we are working on

items.statement: ESOP cost for FY25 estimated at INR 15-16 crores (vs INR 2.6 crores in FY24); new ESOP pool to be created after shareholder approval; cost may rise marginally next year with international hiring
items.quote: For the current year, you can assume about INR15, INR16 crores of full year hit. And next year onwards, it may be slightly higher because there will be new ESOP pool, there will be new ESOP grants to new talent that we are acquiring in the international territory.

items.statement: Working with regulator on REIT market solution expected to go live in coming quarter; new asset class (between MF and PMS) seen as significant opportunity
items.quote: We are currently working with the regulator to create a solution to the REIT market, which hopefully will go live in probably into the coming quarter.

items.statement: Two large international contracts signed in Malaysia in last 4-5 weeks; each ~USD 1.7-2M near-term revenue plus ~USD 0.75M annual recurring; Thailand Phase 2 go-live late September (INR 12 crore contract)
items.quote: These two are decent-sized contracts and materially sized contracts in the context of the global fund services, roughly anywhere between USD1.7 to USD2 million of revenue in the near term, followed by a little about three quarters of a USD1 million revenue to come through on an annual basis.

items.statement: Holds ~60% of GIFT City funds; signed first two insurance-based funds in GIFT City; believes localization and cost-to-serve create moats against global administrators (SS&C, IQ EQ, Apex)
items.quote: We have nearly 60% of all the GIFT City funds being managed by us. We recently also signed the first and the second insurance-based fund that is listed in the GIFT City.

items.statement: International presence: ~75 contracts in Asia (45 RTA, 30 fund accounting/admin); added 12 clients in past 12 months; pipeline growing
items.quote: We today stand at roughly about 75 contracts in the Asian market. With the issuer solutions on the RTA, we're at about 45, and the accounting and administration solutions at about 30.

items.statement: General Atlantic (PE promoter) may sell further blocks over next few years; management says professionally run board mitigates impact
items.quote: General Atlantic is actually a PE, and they have evergreen funds, does not mean that they will not give returns to their investors. So it's their choice. I don't think it impacts us in any way as a company.

items.statement: International revenue share increased to 11.5% from 10.5% YoY; Southeast Asia (Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand) driving growth; higher AUM per transaction vs India
items.quote: It has moved up overall in terms of international as an investor solutions from an overall 10.5% of the total revenue last year to about 11.5% this year.

items.statement: No debt raise planned for acquisition; will use internal accruals; open to leverage if it enhances shareholder returns
items.quote: By the time the acquisition would conclude, we would have generated, you know, that much more cash so that we do not need to leverage. But should we ever need to, we can.

items.statement: Three equal factors caused EBITDA decline: lower realizations from competition and Chinese dumping, preventive maintenance shutdown, and inventory markdown on high-value orders
items.quote: Equal weightage for all three factors.

items.statement: Sales realization fell due to increased competition, lower raw material prices, and Chinese dumping in certain segments; discussions with authorities ongoing
items.quote: The first reason is the fall in sales realization, which has been on account of increased competition, lower raw material prices, and some dumping from Chinese manufacturers in certain segments.

items.statement: Preventive maintenance shutdown in one mill caused ~15,000 tonne production loss; mill resumed production at start of Q2 FY25
items.quote: Production loss in terms of tonnage would be around 15,000 ton nes. However, what we had done was, there was quite a bit of WIP, which was with us, which we managed to finish and dispatch

items.statement: Order book increased from Rs.1,754 crore to Rs.1,812 crore; demand environment conducive for manufacturing and oil & gas sectors
items.quote: Our order book has increased from Rs.1754 crores to Rs.1812 crores. The order book remains good as demand environment is conducive for manufacturing industry and oil and gas sector.

items.statement: 51% of order book from ONGC and Oil India; balance 49% includes significant oil & gas orders; ERW order book dip due to confirmation lag, not demand
items.quote: A better indicator would be the position of our current order book in which 51% of our order book is from ONGC and Oil India and o f the balance 49%, quite a bit is from the oil and gas sector

items.statement: Telangana finishing line deferred by at least 9 months to December 2025 due to 12-month equipment gestation; hot mill upgrade to follow after Telangana commissioning
items.quote: The Telangana finishing line was expected to be completed by March 2025. But, I don't think that will happen, in all probability it will be deferred by at least nine months, because we have recently placed order for some equipment, those orders have been finalized, purchase order has been issued. However, the gestation period for that order is 12 months. So, reasonably speaking, the Telangana unit

items.statement: No significant capex spent in Q1 FY25; equipment orders placed after negotiations concluded; major capex spend expected in FY26
items.quote: There wasn’t any significant expenditure on CAPEX in the first quarter. However, w hat we have done in the first quarter is placed orders for certain equipment which was pending for some time . They were under negotiation and those negotiations have concluded and a purchase order has been placed on the vendor

items.statement: No volume growth expected in FY25; volume growth in FY26 only after Telangana finishing line completes and reaches commercial production
items.quote: I don't think there will be any volume growth in FY25. And in FY 26, volume growth will only happen once the Telangana finishing line has been completed and is open for commercial production.

items.statement: Inventory markdown on high-value orders due to raw material price fall during quarter; markdown to reverse when orders dispatched in Q2/Q3 FY25
items.quote: When these high value orders are dispatched in subsequent quarters, the impact of marking down inventory will be nullified.

items.statement: Selling prices not expected to fall significantly from current levels; raw material price direction uncertain
items.quote: I don't think the selling price is expected to fall significantly from where it is right now.

items.statement: Cylinder pipes are high value-addition product; one of two manufacturers in India; aim to increase value-addition pipes as percentage of total dispatches
items.quote: Margin profile for all high value addition pipes are better than regular pipes. So, cylinder pipes are a h igh value addition product that we manufacture. We are one of two manufacturers of cylinder pipes, and we want to increase the contribution of the value addition pipes as a percentage of total dispatches

items.statement: ERW segment: 20% oil & gas, 80% water in Q1 FY25 leading to lower margins; EBITDA per tonne range Rs.6,000-11,000 +/- Rs.1,000 depending on mix
items.quote: For the first quarter, around 20% of dispatches were in the oil and gas sector and 80% of dispatchers were in the water sector which has led to lower margins in the ERW segment.

items.statement: Exports slow for over a year; no exports to Middle East due to Chinese presence and lack of anti-dumping duties; US/Canada market large but not revived for company
items.quote: We don't export to the Middle East, exports have not revived, exports have been slow for more than a year. Market size in US and Canada is very big, but they have not revived for us.

items.statement: No ICDs to unrelated entities or corporate guarantees outstanding; commitment from two years ago fully resolved
items.quote: In line with the commitment made to shareholders two years ago, there are no ICDs to unrelated entities or corporate guarantees outstanding. We have come a long way from the time when this used to be the main cause of concern and that has been fully and completely resolved.

items.statement: FY24 dividend quadrupled vs FY22; no specific dividend distribution plan announced yet; no buyback update
items.quote: Dividend for FY 24 has been quadrupled f rom what was distributed for FY 22. Whilst a specific dividend distribution plan has not been announced yet, we remain mindful to the points raised by shareholders

items.statement: Capital goods, infrastructure, and oil & gas sectors witnessing strong medium-term demand; seamless pipes market buoyant driven by capex and oil & gas spending
items.quote: Finally, I wish to reiterate that capital goods and infrastructure in general and oil and gas specifically continue to witness strong demand for medium term. This directly impacts the seamless pipes market, which remains buoyant, driven by capital expenditure and spending in the oil and gas sector as we are seeing our order book being replenished and improved at good levels.

items.statement: Capacity utilization generally 70-80%; Q1 lower due to one mill shutdown; annual capacity 550,000 tonnes, dispatched ~400,000 tonnes in Q1
items.quote: Generally speaking, we remain in the range of 70% to 80%.

items.statement: EBITDA per tonne fell from Rs.22,000 to Rs.9,000 in Q1 FY25 due to three equal factors including inventory markdown
items.quote: It is significant, so significant that our EBITDA per tonne fell from Rs.22,000 a tonne to Rs.9,000 per tonne.

items.statement: Discussions with relevant authorities ongoing to address Chinese dumping; process is long-drawn
items.quote: We are in discussion with relevant authorities to address the issue of Chinese dumping, but that is a long-drawn process.

items.statement: Chinese imports impacting realizations significantly; peers selling different products in Middle East, not seamless pipes
items.quote: It is impacting us, which is why our realization has fallen so significantly.

items.statement: Two of three EBITDA impact factors are temporary and one-off; operations and execution remain strong; order book improved QoQ; domestic demand very good
items.quote: At least two of those reasons are temporary and one off in nature and may be a function of the accounting standards that we follow rather than a question mark on the operations of the company. The operations of the company are very good, it is also reflected by the way our order book has improved quarter-on-quarter, domestic demand is very good.

items.statement: Treasury at Rs.2,203 crore as of June 30, 2024; generated >1/3 of total earnings in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The treasury is at Rs.2203 crores as on 30th June 2024. It has improved more than anticipated and is generating good returns for us. In fact, in Q1 FY25 more than 1/3rd of total earnings was from treasury segment.

items.statement: Almost entire order book hedged with raw material; insignificant portion kept open
items.quote: Almost the entire order book is hedged with raw material and insignificant portion is kept open.

items.statement: Not supplying pipes for hydrogen segment; such pipes not manufactured in seamless segment in India
items.quote: We are not supplying pipes for the hydrogen segment; those pipes are not being manufactured in the seamless segment in India.

items.statement: ERW pipe dispatch range 80,000-105,000 tonnes annually; no capacity expansion planned as focus remains on seamless pipes
items.quote: Generally speaking, ERW pipes would b e dispatched in the range of 80,000 to 1,05,000 tonnes every year. And since we are not expanding any ERW pipe capacity, our dispatch would remain within this range at all

items.statement: Marketing sour service subsea seamless pipes in export markets; encouraging inquiries but no orders crystallized yet; regions not disclosed due to competition
items.quote: We are marketing our sour service subsea seamless pipes in the export market. However, we have not yet been successful. We have had encouraging inquiries, but none of those inquiries have actually crystallized into orders yet.

items.statement: Earnings will revive from Q3 FY25 as Jindal Supreme redeploys at higher rate; one rig to get new contract in FY26
items.quote: Our earnings will revive from the 3rd Quarter of FY25 onwards as the rig under refurbishment commences operations at a much higher rate. Further, one of our rigs will get onto a new contract next year in FY26.

items.statement: Acquisition of Jindal Pioneer rig from JV pending statutory approval; currently operating in Mexico at $40,000/day bareboat charter till Dec 2025
items.quote: The rig which we propose d to acquire from the joint venture company is currently deployed in Mexico at a rate of $40,000 per day. That rate is a bareboat charter rate, which means that no expenses are incurred by the rig owner

items.statement: Jindal Pioneer rig to undergo refurbishment after Dec 2025 contract completion, then deployed with ONGC in India
items.quote: Once the contract is completed in December 25, the rig will go for a few months of refurbishment and then it will be brought back to India for possible deployment with ONGC.

items.statement: Gross debt to reduce rapidly over next 12 months as all rigs contracted at higher rates on new ONGC contracts
items.quote: As all rigs are now contracted at higher rates on new ONGC contracts, gross debt will reduce rapidly over next 12 months.

items.statement: Rig efficiency in excess of 98.5%; 5 offshore jackup rigs operated with ONGC
items.quote: The efficiency of our rigs in operation are in excess of 98.5% and we are extremely proud of that statistic.

items.statement: ONGC is primary customer for over three decades; private player contracts are shorter and less preferred
items.quote: We've been supporting and serving ONGC for the past three decades in their drilling programs. They are our satisfied customer and we have always explored opportunities with them.

items.statement: Private player contracts are much smaller, sometimes ten days; rigs suited to private players but strategy favors ONGC
items.quote: The private players , the contracts are usually much smaller . W e have always preferred to go with ONGC because it was three to five year contracts. Obviously, you get better revenues with private players because it's shorter period and when I say short period , it's like sometimes it's ten days also

items.statement: International day rates remain at high levels, not declined despite Saudi rig removals; expect slight dip from last rate due to higher competition
items.quote: internationally the day rates are still at the high level. It has not really declined. The rigs which have been removed from operation in Saudi will not be coming into India. So, it does not affect our demand. So, we expect the rate to dip slightly from our last rate because of higher competition, but not significantly, as i t does not really affect our supply

items.statement: Government wants more rigs to increase oil production; demand will aggregate and more rigs expected in next ONGC tender
items.quote: Obviously the demand is there. The government wants more and more rigs to increase oil production. They can only increase oil production if they deploy more rigs. The reason for why these contracts were cancelled is unknown. I'm sure the demand will aggregate and there'll be a lot more rigs coming in in the next tender.

items.statement: Acquisition of Jindal Pioneer from JV pending final regulatory approval; delayed over three months
items.quote: It was expected on yesterday basis. But we have not yet received the final approval from the regulator. We are following up with them. We wanted to do it as early as possible. We still want to do it as early as possible, but we just have to wait till we obtain necessary approval.

items.statement: ONGC contract cancellation earlier this year; reason unknown but hopeful of redeployment at good rates in FY26
items.quote: Whilst there was cancellation of an ONGC cont ract earlier this year, we remain hopeful of redeployment of our rig at good rates in next financial year

items.statement: Arbitration matter with ONGC pending in Supreme Court; management not commenting as it is ongoing
items.quote: No, since it's undergoing, we're not really commenting on that right now.

items.statement: Management apprehensive about providing NAV valuation due to market volatility; will wait for earnings stability
items.quote: However, the NAV that is being given also depends on what could be the future cash flows generated. So, since the market has been quite volatile and we recently started investor engagement, we are a little apprehensive as to how that will work out.

items.statement: NIM guidance for FY25 is 2.75% to 2.8% by March 2025
items.quote: Our Q1 NIM was at 2.69% and we intend to keep the NIM at between 2.75% to 2.8% for the March '25 year-end.

items.statement: RoA guidance for FY25 is 0.65% to 0.75%
items.quote: As far as the return on assets is concerned we are at 0.50% and we intend to have it between 0.65% to 0.75%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income ratio guidance for FY25 is 68% to 69%
items.quote: The cost to income ratio, we will gradually reduce and bring it down to below 69% by the end of March and maybe, if possible, below 68% also, but it will be between 68% to 69%.

items.statement: RoE guidance for FY25 is 9% to 10%
items.quote: Return on equity we will try to move forward between 9% to 10%.

items.statement: Credit growth guidance for FY25 is 12% to 14% and for FY26 is 14% to 16%
items.quote: This year, we should grow at 12% to 14% and the next year, maybe between 14% to 16%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 NIM improved to 2.69% YoY and sequentially
items.quote: The NIM has improved to 2.69%, it has shown improvement on Y-o-Y and on sequential basis.

items.statement: Yield on advances improved to 8.70% and cost of deposits reduced to 5.64% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The yield on advances has improved to 8.70%. We have been able to reduce the cost of deposit from 5.71% to 5.64%.

items.statement: Gross NPA reduced 208 bps YoY to 4.72%; Net NPA down 36 bps YoY to 1.59%
items.quote: The gross NPA, with thanks to the recovery efforts of our department, has now been reduced by 208 bps to 4.72% as on 30th June. The net NPA has gone down to 1.59%, a reduction by 36 bps Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Slippages contained at Rs 276 crore in Q1 FY25 vs Rs 451 crore YoY and Rs 370 crore QoQ
items.quote: Our slippages have been contained in this quarter and the slippages has been only Rs.276 crores in the June quarter, which is against Rs.451 crores of June quarter last year and Rs.370 crore of March quarter.

items.statement: Collection efficiency focus paying dividends in containing slippages, especially in agri and MSME
items.quote: Our collection eﬃciency has been given a lot of focus and it is now paying dividends in terms of some of the containment in the slippages front, particularly on the agriculture and the MSME front

items.statement: Corporate credit pipeline of Rs 6,000 crore for the year
items.quote: We have got a reasonable pipeline as well as of now for the year, somewhere around Rs.6000 crore.

items.statement: Co-lending portfolio increased to Rs 800 crore on TReDS platform; exploring direct assignment for retail and MSME
items.quote: We have increased our portfolio to Rs.800 crores in TREDS platform that again builds up the MSME portfolio. We're also looking for direct assignment opportunities where we are really looking for retail and MSME portfolios.

items.statement: IT investment plan of Rs 800 crore over next three years
items.quote: In fact, we have already chalked out a plan of around Rs.800 crores of IT investment spread over three years and these are very important sort of investments which are required just to sustain the ecosystem that we are working on.

items.statement: Plan to open 100 branches in FY25 (5 opened in Q1); focus on semi-urban/urban areas outside northern belt
items.quote: endeavor to expand our branches w ill continue to happen. As of now, we are having 1,569 branches. We have opened 5 branches in the ﬁrst quarter. We are having a plan of increasing branches by 100 for the entire year. Our ATMs will also be increased as we open new branches. While opening n ew branches we w ill be focusing on the semi - urban areas and the urban areas, other than the northern belt

items.statement: BC network to expand from 2,000 to 4,500 by March 2025 and 6,000 by March 2026 via corporate BC model
items.quote: So, we have taken v arious measures and maybe after learning from the experience we intend to increase the number to 4,500 in the current year and to 6000 BCs by the end of March '26

items.statement: Capital raise approved: Rs 2,000 crore QIP, Rs 5,000 crore infra bonds, Rs 3,000 crore AT1/Tier 2 bonds (total Rs 10,000 crore)
items.quote: We have given the disclosure that the bank has now got an approval of around Rs.10000 crores overall, Rs.2000 crores of QIP, Rs.5000 crores of infra-bond and Rs.3000 crores of AT-1/Tier 2 bonds.

items.statement: Capital raise proceeds to support credit growth, LCR compliance, and IT investments
items.quote: So, these sorts of areas will not only help our LCR to be under control, it will also help us to grow in our credit and also take care of our future IT investments that we are going to have.

items.statement: RBI draft LCR norms: additional 5% runoff for digital banking customers; bank estimates 10-12% impact vs system 10-20%; LCR maintained at ~130%
items.quote: Our back of the envelope calculations have shown that our impact will be between 10% to 12%. We are suﬃciently cushioned at this point as we normally maintain LCR around 130

items.statement: RBI revised investment valuation norms: Rs 4,200 crore MTM loss on recap bonds (Rs 11,672 crore) adjusted against general reserve; bonds not tradeable
items.quote: We are having recap bonds of Rs.11672 crores and as per the Reserve Bank Circular, Rs.4200 crores has been adjusted with the general reserve of the bank. The treatment of these Bonds is as per RBI guidelines and similar treatment has also been done by other Banks.

items.statement: Hiring CXOs and specialized roles from market; sending top executives for training in India and abroad
items.quote: We have taken CXOs from the market, we are 10 taking specialized positions from the market, we are increasing the capacity of our top executives, sending them for trainings in India and abroad and these are all investments for us

items.statement: Reaffirmed FY25 revenue growth guidance of 20-25% and expects similar CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: we are reaffirming our guidan ce of 20% to 25% growth in terms of revenues for this financial year as well. And we expect in the next 3 years to maintain that kind of CAGR as well

items.statement: Expects FY25 execution growth of 22-25% over FY24 revenues of INR 1,000+ crores
items.quote: So we expect a 22% to 25% growth compared to last year in terms of the execution. So last year, we did reven ues of INR 1,000 - plus crores. So we expect a 20% to 25% increase in this financial year

items.statement: Net unexecuted order book of INR 3,669 crores as of June 30, 2024, representing 3.6x FY24 revenues
items.quote: As on June 30, 2024, we have a net unexecuted order book of INR 3,669 crores, representing almost 3.6x our FY '24 revenues, providing strong visibility to the management and their investors.

items.statement: Order inflow of INR 812 crores in Q1 FY25, largest single order INR 549 crores from RVNL
items.quote: The order inflow during the quarter was INR 812 crores, with the larg est single order of INR 549 crores from RVNL for construction of an elevated corridor over the Kona Expressway near Calcutta.

items.statement: Targets FY25 order book of INR 3,700-3,800 crores, implying INR 1,300 crores new orders for balance of year
items.quote: We ideally like to maintain 3x our order book. So year, we should close at almost INR 3,700 - odd crores of order book, INR 3,700 crores to INR 3,800 crores, which means that for the balance year, we wou ld get almost close to INR 1,300 crores of new orders

items.statement: Ghana factory advance payment received, factory to start in 1-2 months, expects INR 35 crores revenue in FY25
items.quote: the swift message of the transfer has already been shared yesterday. So we expect that to hit our bank account sometime today, tomorrow. Once that comes, we will start the factory in the next 1 or 2 months, and we expect r evenue to be booked during this financial year from the Ghana factory as well.

items.statement: Expects EBITDA margins around 13-14% for FY25, improvement expected from Ghana factory commissioning
items.quote: We expect the margins to b e around the 13% to 14% mark. Obviously, like I said in my opening remarks, with the Ghana factory getting commissioned and revenues getting recognized from there, the margins will improve, because that has a higher margin level.

items.statement: Maintains EBITDA margin threshold of 12.5-13% for new contracts, will not compromise on margins for growth
items.quote: We don't want to compromise on the ma rgin. We need to have a very disciplined growth strategy. So as long as we meet the margin threshold of 12.5%, 13% in terms of EBITDA, we are okay to take on contracts.

items.statement: QIP of up to INR 175 crores, 75% for working capital debt repayment, balance for long-term working capital and general corporate purposes
items.quote: So the idea is to raise up to INR 175 crores. It will be primarily used to pay some existing working capital debt on the balance sheet. Up to 75% will be used for that and the balance will be used for long - term working capital and other general corporate purpose.

items.statement: Finance cost expected to reduce from INR 31 crores in FY24 to below INR 20 crores post QIP
items.quote: Post the QIP, we expect the same to come down to below INR 20 crores.

items.statement: Current bidding capacity up to INR 1,000 crores per contract, post-QIP expected to increase to INR 1,200-1,400 crores
items.quote: Right now, we can take up to INR 1,000 crores. I think that post the raise, with the net worth increasing, the bidding capacity also increasing, we would be eligible to about INR 1,300 crores, INR 1,400 crores, close to maybe INR 1,500 crores

items.statement: QIP of up to INR 175 crores underway, closes August 7, 2024, primary issue with no promoter dilution
items.quote: As you are well aware, the company is undergoing postal ballot for qualified placement of up to INR 175 crores, which will close on 7th August 2024.

items.statement: Completed 1:1 bonus issue in Q1 FY25, second bonus in 3 years
items.quote: This quarter, the company has also completed the bonus issue in the ratio of 1 equity share for every equity share held by the shareholders. This is the second bonus issue by the company in the last 3 years

items.statement: Infrastructure segment 93% of revenues, key contracts Prayagraj NHAI, Mathura-Jhansi, Ghazipur-Byculla driving performance
items.quote: segment reported revenue of INR 225 crores for the quarter ended June 30, 2024. This segment contin ues to be the backbone of GPT Infraprojects Limited August 0 1 , 202 4 our business, contributing almost 93% of our total revenues in the quarter

items.statement: Supplies concrete sleepers directly to government entities in South Africa, Namibia, Ghana and India, EPC companies less than 10%
items.quote: So in South Africa, in Namibia, and Ghana as well, we're supplying directly to the government. And so -- even in India. So concrete sleeper as a product, the gover nment is a major buyer for this product. There are some smaller quantities which get delivered to these EPC companies like you mentioned, but they are not very significant amount, less than 10%.

items.statement: Concrete sleeper order book of INR 250 crores with 2-year execution period, expects new orders in FY25
items.quote: Yes. So that INR 250 crores in the Concrete Sleeper segment has also got an execution period of almost 2 years, which will be an average speed of that. We are expecting some new orders also to come in, in this financial year in that business.

items.statement: Adding senior and middle management to improve execution bandwidth, SAP deployed across all project sites
items.quote: We are adding on some senior management people as well as middle management as well to improve the bandwidth like you're suggesti ng. The management is very conscious of that. So we are taking a couple of key people on board as well, which will improve our execution capabilities.

items.statement: Cash flow to EBITDA conversion north of 100% in FY24, strong focus on cash flow management
items.quote: Our cash flow to EBITDA conversion last year has also been north of 100%. And that is, again, a very steady focus of the management to have a strong cash flow and a good margin threshold as well.

items.statement: Order pipeline strong but Q1 muted due to elections and code of conduct, expects ordering activity to pick up post-budget
items.quote: Obviously, the first quarter was slightly muted on account of the elections and code of conduct that was there. And so new contracts could not be t endered out. Now with the budget exercise also getting completed, we expect ordering activity to again pick up.

items.statement: Discussing EPC contracts in Namibia, previously did bridge rehabilitation in Mozambique
items.quote: In South Africa, Namibia and Ghana, honestly, we've not explored. But recently, we have been discussing for some contracts in Namibia. Let's see how it pans out.

items.statement: Budget reaffirmed government commitment to capital outlay on national infrastructure pipeline
items.quote: During the budget, the Honorable Finance Minister has reemphasized the commitment for the central government to expand on the capital outlay on the national infrastructure pipeline, which is a blueprint for the government's focus on the infrastructure segment

items.statement: Infrastructure segment doing metro viaducts and prestressed girders (Byculla cable-stayed bridge, Ghatkopar bridge, Calcutta Metro)
items.quote: we are doing a lot of metro work in our Infrastructure segment. We are doing the viaducts and prestressed girder that you're speaking about. So we have done in -- in fact, in Bombay city, not for the metro, but we are doing the prestressed over the Byculla Railway Station, cable - stayed bridge ov er Byculla Railway Station

items.statement: Order book execution cycle 2-2.5 years, monthly run rate >INR 100 crores in June 2024
items.quote: the June month has seen a bounce back in the performance, and we are currently at a monthly run rate of more than INR 100 crores.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected between INR500-600 crores similar to last year
items.quote: So, capex, I think for last year we did almost INR550 crores. We expect a similar run rate of INR550 anywhere between INR500 crores to INR600 odd crores this year.

items.statement: Mobile phone monthly order book 9-10 lakh units including exports for Motorola; Xiaomi at 7 lakh from July
items.quote: There is strong growth in volume for Motorola smartphones and a monthly order book of almost 9 lakhs to 10 lakhs per month, including a decent order book on exports. Xiaomi business has also now ramped up, and now we are clocking around 7 lakhs per month from July and higher volumes are expected in coming months of the festive season.

items.statement: TV order book: current month ~250k, August ~400k, September ~400-450k targeting 1 million total
items.quote: So, I'll say the current month, we want to close it around 250,000. August's order book looks particularly good. It would be around 400,000. And we feel that September also is going to be 400,000, 450,000. So, 1 million.

items.statement: Healthy order book in refrigerators at 80-85% capacity utilization; planning capacity expansion
items.quote: We are clocking production of almost 80,000 refrigerators a month, which is 80%, 85% of our capacity. So, the project has taken off very well. Now we are planning another capacity expansion because the order book is significantly increasing.

items.statement: Healthy order book in Rexxam Dixon JV for inverter controller boards; exploring exports and PLI investments
items.quote: We have an extremely healthy order book in this business. We're exploring the possibility of accruing more investments under the recently announced revised scheme of PLI for white goods by DPIIT.

items.statement: Mobile capacity 45M smartphones + 10-12M from Ismartu acquisition = 55-60% of opportunity pool; 40M feature phones = 65-70% of national capacity
items.quote: Now we have created a capacity of 45 million smartphones and another 10 million to 12 million is going to be added after Ismartu acquisition which is around 55% to 60% of the opportunity pool in this business. Further, we have a capacity of 40 million feature phones, which is again almost 65% to 70% of the capacity required for the feature phones in this country.

items.statement: Chennai IT hardware campus planned: 1.5M units/year initial capacity, INR150 crore capex, operational Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26
items.quote: So initially, the capacity is going to be almost 1.5 million units per year. And the capex the plant is going to be somewhere in the range of around INR150 crores.

items.statement: Display module plant Phase 1: 2M units/month, production start end of FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: In Phase 1, it's going to be 2 million units a month. We have found our customers, and they're open to it. They are extremely positive for this local manufacturing because it's saved for them the inventory cost.

items.statement: TV market declined ~17% volume in Q1; washing machine volumes grew 10% (semi-auto) and tripled (fully-auto)
items.quote: On the LED TV side the market has been extremely slow. And there is a decline in volume. There is a decline in volume by almost 17%. That's being reflected in the Q1 numbers.

items.statement: Lighting segment: pricing pressure stabilizing, QoQ revenue growth 15%, worst behind
items.quote: In Q-on-Q, you see, Abhishek the numbers have grown by 15%. So clearly, we see that the worst is behind us as far as the pricing is concerned, the component intensity is concerned. So, it can only get better from here.

items.statement: Home appliance margin dipped 40bps YoY to 10.6% due to freight costs from Red Sea crisis; QoQ expanded 40bps
items.quote: Natasha if you see the reduction in margin is 0.4%. It has gone down from 11% last year to 10.6% in the current quarter. And quarter-on-quarter if you see there's an expansion of 0.4%.

items.statement: Refrigerator operating margins expected 8-9% once ramped up; currently in ramp-up phase with initial costs
items.quote: As far as the refrigerator is concerned, it's only in the ramp-up phase. The initial ramp-up cost has gone into these numbers. But finally, the numbers which have been earlier on the sharing, the operating margins are going to be in the range of around 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Display module project expected to be margin accretive with mid-double digit EBITDA margins from Year 2
items.quote: But from year 2, it's going to be a good, extremely good, margin accretive project let me assure you of that.

items.statement: Added interactive flat panels (65-100 inch) and digital signages to TV portfolio; extending lighting into DOB floodlights, streetlights, high-voltage battens, COB downlighters
items.quote: In addition to our existing product portfolio, we have added interactive flat panel displays and digital signages to our TV product portfolio. These are the solution from 65 inches to 100 inches.

items.statement: Started mass production of 5G FWA devices (ODU/IDU) for Nokia; manufacturing GPON, ONTs, set-top boxes
items.quote: We have started mass production of 5G fixed wireless access devices along with access point GPON, ONTs and Internet set-top boxes. We have started manufacturing 5G fixed wireless access devices both ODUs and IDUs for both domestic markets for Nokia.

items.statement: Laptop/IT hardware: Acer production started, Lenovo NPI begun with mass production Q3 FY25; two new global brands targeting Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26
items.quote: We are already manufacturing for Acer. And we started the NPI process for Lenovo notebooks and the mass production for Lenovo will commence in Q3 of this fiscal. We have also got two new customers which are the largest global brands for notebooks. We're in the process of signing the definitive agreements. We target to start production for these two global brands in Q1 of next fiscal.

items.statement: Mobile: Motorola 9-10L/month, Xiaomi 7L/month from July, Compal global brand by Sep'24, Longcheer 4-4.5L/month targeting 7L, one more large global brand coming
items.quote: There is strong growth in volume for Motorola smartphones and a monthly order book of almost 9 lakhs to 10 lakhs per month, including a decent order book on exports. Xiaomi business has also now ramped up, and now we are clocking around 7 lakhs per month from July and higher volumes are expected in coming months of the festive season. Manufacturing for another global brand through Compal is expect

items.statement: IT hardware: Contracted Lenovo and Acer; two new top-5 global brands in definitive agreement stage
items.quote: We have already finalized contracts with Lenovo and Acer. We are already manufacturing for Acer. And we started the NPI process for Lenovo notebooks and the mass production for Lenovo will commence in Q3 of this fiscal. We have also got two new customers which are the largest global brands for notebooks. We're in the process of signing the definitive agreements.

items.statement: Nokia: Manufacturing 95-96% of Nokia/HMD India sales; smartphone exports started, expanding capacity for exports
items.quote: We are doing 100% of -- not 100% we are doing almost 95%, 96% of what Nokia sells in India both on feature phones and smartphones. 100% of their smartphone both on the Nokia brand and HMD are done by us. We're already manufacturing for exports for them. Exports have already started under the Nokia brand. And we have had deliberations and discussions with Nokia. And we'll be expanding the capacity

items.statement: Ismartu acquisition: CCI approved, financial consolidation in 4-7 days (7-10 days per CFO); FY24: INR8,200 cr revenue, INR320-325 cr EBITDA, INR240 cr PAT
items.quote: On the Ismartu deal, we have received the approval of the Competition Commission of India this month, and we will start consolidating those financials, I think, in the next 4 to 7 days for the completion of CP's.

items.statement: Sold 50% stake in AIL Dixon to Aditya Infotech; taking 6.5% stake in Aditya Infotech pre-IPO (Q4 FY25/Q1 FY26)
items.quote: We have sold our 50% stake in AIL Dixon to our JV partner Aditya Infotech. In return, we are taking a 6.5% stake in Aditya Infotech which will be going for IPO. Aditya Infotech is a highly profitable company, and we'll be going for an IPO by Q4 of this fiscal or Q1 of next fiscal.

items.statement: Mobile PLI scheme ends March 2026; government likely to replace with component-focused incentive scheme before then
items.quote: Post '26 when this scheme goes away it's going to be replaced by a scheme focusing on value addition and components. And strategically that's what we're trying to do in Dixon that we are strategizing, and we are deeply getting involved with the component ecosystem.

items.statement: Custom duty cut on mobile phones minimal impact: imports only INR7-8K cr in INR3L cr market; 97-98% phones made in India
items.quote: So, please appreciate the seasonal imports of mobile phones are minuscule. If my numbers are correct, the total imports in an INR3-lakh crores market are nearly INR7,000 crores to INR8,000 crores. So, I think the government wants to send a message globally because there have been some kind of observations from the context and the custom duty structures in India should be rationalized.

items.statement: Mobile exports currently confined to Motorola (25-30% of production); Nokia smartphone exports started small (10-11k units Q1)
items.quote: So, at present, Dhruv, the mobile phone exports are largely for Motorola. We feel that almost 25% to 30% of Motorola's production is going to be for global markets. And that's a significant jump. For the other brands, as of now, it's for the domestic market.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle negative 7 days as of June 30, 2024; gross debt-to-equity 0.1%
items.quote: With earnings improvement and effective working capital management, we were able to expand the ROCE and ROE to 38.4% and 27% respectively as of 30th June, '24 with further strengthening of the balance sheet and gross debt-to-equity ratio of 0.1% and cash conversion cycle of negative 7 days.

items.statement: Mobile PLI incentive booked: INR40 cr in Q1 FY25 vs ~INR4-5 cr in Q1 FY24
items.quote: So last year it was -- yes for this quarter we had booked almost INR40-odd crores as PLI incentive for mobile business.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 production volumes: smartphones 4.1M (ex-Samsung) + 1.1M Samsung; feature phones 6.6M
items.quote: That should give you probably a run rate for what we are talking about for the entire year. Yes, so smartphones we did almost -- so between -- excluding Samsung, we did almost 41 lakhs, 4.1 million and Samsung was around 11-odd million -- sorry, 1.1 million.

items.statement: Component ecosystem development critical for export competitiveness; India 2-3 years from global competitiveness
items.quote: So, we feel that once the component ecosystem is being created in India. India is going to keep on acquiring competitive strength. And that would help in becoming globally competitive. So, I think that journey has already started. We are a couple of years away from where India is going to stand on its own feet to compete in the global market.

items.statement: Targets 60-80 bps EBIT margin improvement in wire and cable segment for FY25
items.quote: We reiterate our guidance to improve our EBIT margins by 60 to 80 basis points in FY25, driven by increased export of value-added products and operational efficiencies.

items.statement: Expects FMEG segment to break even in next three to four quarters
items.quote: Our revenue growth in the FMEG segment is ahead of the industry and we anticipate achieving break even in the next three to four quarters.

items.statement: Targets 20% volume growth in exports for full year FY25
items.quote: So, there is not the problem of demand. The only thing in quarter one shipment got delayed and it got postponed to second quarter. It may have some later effect also but still on a yearly basis we are on line to have achieved this 20% volume growth in export as well.

items.statement: Expects domestic wire volume growth of 13-14% and cable volume growth of 30% for FY25
items.quote: We may expect to grow wire also at 13%-14% and maybe cable at 30%, something like that.

items.statement: Targets 25-30% revenue growth in FMEG segment for FY25
items.quote: So at revenue, we are expecting 25%, 30% of revenue growth on yearly basis.

items.statement: Planned capex of INR 500 crores over FY24-25 to be completed by March 2025
items.quote: The planned capital expenditure of INR 500 crores, said to be completed by March '25, will further help us to maintain our healthy volume growth targets.

items.statement: Capex cash outflow of INR 300 crores in FY25 after INR 200 crores in FY24
items.quote: So like, last year we did capex of INR 200 crores, and this year, what already we have done and what is planned to do will be INR 300 crores of cash flow outflow for capex point of view.

items.statement: New capex plans from April 2025 to be finalized by end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: At the same time now we are working on our new capex plans also which will start from April 25 onward. Right now we are making these plans and will be like finalized by this quarter end.

items.statement: Cable capacity utilization at 90-95%, wire at 65-70% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So even if I see a cable it is 90% to 95% and wire it is around 65% to 70% in that category we are okay.

items.statement: Cable capacity doubling by March 2025 with phased commissioning from September-October 2024
items.quote: What capacity expansion we have planned for March 25th that is 100% like doubling our capacity in compared to previous year. So like this will be coming in phases. So a few machines will be operational in September, October also.

items.statement: Healthy export order book with regular distribution-driven orders
items.quote: Still we have very healthy order book and we have continuous order since our major exports are distributiondriven and regular order.

items.statement: Domestic volume growth of 20% in Q1 FY25 driven by cables (50% growth) and wires (7% growth)
items.quote: If we further break down this geographically, the domestic volume growth is approximately 20%, mainly coming from cables.

items.statement: Industry demand strong for next 6-8 years driven by infrastructure, railway, defense, solar
items.quote: And even going forward also it seems all the growth indicators are intact and we see based on this domestic demand and even the demand from export market it seems like next six to eight years are very good for this industry particularly for cable and wire will also grow simultaneously.

items.statement: Wire and cable EBIT decreased 9.3% to INR 113 crores in Q1 FY25 due to raw material volatility and cable mix shift
items.quote: However, the EBIT decreased by 9.3% in Q1 FY25, reaching to INR113 crores due to volatility in raw material prices and slowdown particularly in domestic wires.

items.statement: Cable margins currently lower than wire but expected to improve with scale by year-end
items.quote: For time being, these are lower. But as we are on the path of getting scalability and availability of inventories, so we are expecting -- we are expecting margin improvement by year end.

items.statement: Copper prices rose ~12% in April-May then fell ~20% in June-July; prices adjusted when raw material moves +/-3%
items.quote: And if you see we have seen the price hike also in this quarter when in April and May there was almost 12% copper prices were on the higher side and at the same time in the month of June and July we have seen almost 20% decline also.

items.statement: Wire and cable revenue mix 70% wire, 30% cable; domestic volume mix 50% cable growth, 7% wire growth
items.quote: So like wire and cable mix is almost 70% comes from wire and 30% revenue comes from cables in my wire and cable segment.

items.statement: Launched FireX LS0H-EBXL halogen-free wire meeting 2023 CEA regulations for public/commercial buildings
items.quote: Our new product, FireX LS0H-EBXL, represents a major innovation in safety standards. This product aligns with the new 2023 regulations by Central Electrical Authority (CEA), which mandates halogen-free wires for public and commercial buildings.

items.statement: Exports contribute 24% of total revenue; Europe largest market; Q1 flat due to container shortage and shipment delays
items.quote: We continue to be the largest exporter of wire and cable from India, which is contributing approximately 24% of our total revenue.

items.statement: Export mix similar to domestic at 70% wire, 30% cable
items.quote: It's like almost in that line only like in export also our share is almost 70%-30% only, so since we have not done any volume growth in this quarter, so the ratio remains the same.

items.statement: Working capital days maintained at 67 in Q1 FY25, targeting further improvement
items.quote: During Q1 FY25, the company maintained its working capital days at 67 and going forward we are working towards improving this further, demonstrating our commitment to sound financial management.

items.statement: Capex fully funded through internal accruals and reserves, no term loans needed
items.quote: So even from cash flow point of view, this will be met through our internal accruals and reserves, what already we have. So there will be no, like term loan or great facilities for this.

items.statement: Strong in west and north India; expanding distribution in south and east regions
items.quote: So in wire, if you see from geographic point of view, we are very strong in the west and north part of the country. At the same time, we are growing and exploring our growth opportunity in the south and east region also.

items.statement: FireX LS0H-EBXL product aligned with 2023 CEA mandate for halogen-free wires in public/commercial buildings
items.quote: This product aligns with the new 2023 regulations by Central Electrical Authority (CEA), which mandates halogen-free wires for public and commercial buildings.

items.statement: Company volume growth 18-20% trailing 12 months vs industry 13-15%, maintaining market share leadership
items.quote: And even in last 12 months also if you see we have achieved volume growth of almost 18% to 20% which is like either at par or above the industry average of 13% to 14% or 15%.

items.statement: Sharp copper price volatility (up 12% then down 20% in quarter) impacted Q1 margins despite pass-through mechanism
items.quote: See, there will always be volatility, but anything which is very sharp impact our margins to some extent for a particular quarter.

items.statement: Reiterated deposit growth guidance of 10%-12% and advance growth guidance of 12%-14% for the full year
items.quote: We again hold the same guidance of Deposit growth 10%-12% and Advance growth at 12%-14%.

items.statement: Maintained NIM guidance at 3.15% plus/minus 5 bps for the full year
items.quote: Although our guidance has been at 3.15, plus/minus 5 bps, which we continue to hold on this quarter.

items.statement: Maintained slippage ratio guidance at 1-1.25% and improved credit cost guidance to below 0.75% from earlier less than 1%
items.quote: In terms of the guidance that we had given to the market earlier. In terms of the Slippage ratio between 1-1.25, the current quarter has been 1.05. The Credit Cost, which is again, earlier we said it would be less than 1 and now we are improving that to less than 0.75.

items.statement: Targeting recovery of Rs 10,000 crore for the financial year
items.quote: We're targeting 10,000 crores recovery this financial year.

items.statement: Maintained ROA guidance at 1.10% or above
items.quote: So, we continue to hold that ROA this time also, it is 1.13 and we said last time that we need to maintain 1.10. So that is what actually I can guide you at this point of time.

items.statement: Intend to maintain ROE in excess of 15-16%
items.quote: And normally if you see the June quarter because the profit is not added back to capital, you see a d ip vis a vis March. But in our case, it has gone up 54bps which is not also, if you compare the peer CRAR, that they have not had. Because of the elevated capital level, because of one investment reserve getting into, because of the accounting norms, ROA has gone down to 17.5% or something but on

items.statement: Targeting 5-year CAGR of ~13.5% for balance sheet growth, implying doubling from March 2024 levels
items.quote: Let me share that earlier we, announced to the market also that there is something already in the domain of public information, that we want to grow at a CAGR of almost 13.5% for the next 5 years. That’s a ro lling plan. Because in the earlier years also, you must have seen FY23, the growth has been almost 16 %. This year, because of the liquidity issue as system liquidity issue, it’s not one bank

items.statement: Reported NIM of 3.18% in Q1 FY25, down from 3.27% in Q4 FY24 but up 4 bps vs normalized Q4 NIM of 3.14%
items.quote: Our margin is posted at a very comfortable at 3.18. If I compare that with the Q 4, it is a dip from 3.27 to 3.18. However, if I normalize last quarter NIM with the higher year end recoveries, it becomes 3.14. As compared to that, we have posted a NIM of 4 bps higher at 3.18.

items.statement: Yield on advances improved 15 bps YoY to 8.55%
items.quote: Yield on Advances has improved from 8.40% to 8.55%, 15 bps higher.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved 63 bps YoY to 2.88%; Net NPA improved to 0.69% from 0.78%
items.quote: We are having a stronger and robust asset quality and our Gross NPA has improved by 63 bps from 3.51 to 2.88. Similarly, as against our guidance of Net NPA of less than 1%, we continue to be at 0.69; improved from 0.78.

items.statement: Provision Coverage Ratio at 93.32%; Slippage ratio at 1.05%; Credit cost improved to 0.47% from 0.70%
items.quote: Provision Coverage Ratio is comfortable at 93.32%. Slippage Ratio, our guidance was 1-1.25 and we are at 1.05 , maintained at the same level as of Q1 FY24. The robustness of our quality of the asset is depicted in our Credit Cost which has improved from 0.70 to 0.47%.

items.statement: SMA book at 0.18% of standard assets; Collection efficiency improved to 99%
items.quote: As far as our portfolio is concerned, we are not facing any incipient sickness in our portfolio. SMA book is only 0.18% of our total standard asset and collection efficiency , a s compared to March, it has improved to 99%.

items.statement: MSME asset quality stabilized for last 4 quarters; comfortable to increase growth
items.quote: MSME, actually, asset quality for last 4 quarters has fairly stabilized. And if you look at my asset quality on MSME, it is I mean one of the good levels as compared to many of the peers in the market. So, we think a very stable outlook on the MSME for last many quarters.

items.statement: Retail advances grew 21% YoY; Home loans 14.7%, Mortgage 11%, Education 18.8%, Auto 25%, Personal loans 39%
items.quote: Segment wise if we say, we are going strong with the Retail growth of 21%, Agriculture is around 9.1%., MSME 9.8%, Corporate is at 2.5%. In the Retail portfolio itself the secured portion, that is Mortgage as well as Home Loan, we have grown 11% and 14.7%. Education; we have grown by 18.8%. Auto Loan by 25%. And as we said earlier also, we have moderated our growth as far as the Personal Loan is c

items.statement: Targeting MSME growth of 14-15% supported by budget measures and cash management product rollout
items.quote: I think the MSME growth should normally get into that 14% to 15% growth model, and that is what will be the budget has a lot of positive things.

items.statement: Raised Rs 20,000-25,000 crore via infra and capital bonds last year; overseas borrowing channel available
items.quote: We raised last year almost 20,000 odd-25,000 through infra and the capital bonds. So, we have an overseas channel open to us.

items.statement: Plan to raise ~Rs 7,500 crore capital (Tier 1/2 substitution) in FY25; no equity raise planned given comfortable CRAR
items.quote: There is no plan to raise capital because of a comfortable CRAR but as a substitution of tier1 and tier 2, we have announced to the market that roughly around 7500 crores capital we'll be raising in this year.

items.statement: Reduced bulk deposits by ~Rs 24,000 crore QoQ (from Rs 2.24 lakh crore to Rs 2 lakh crore) to improve liability quality and protect margin
items.quote: if you have the number, the b ulk deposit outstanding as of March’24 was 2,24,000 crores and the bulk deposit outstanding as o f June end is 2 lakh crores. So, there is a d ip of 24,000

items.statement: CASA grew 6% YoY to 40.62% of total deposits; better than peers
items.quote: if we look at our CASA, our CASA has grown by 6%, which is better than the peer banks also, and we are continuing our CASA ratio more than 40% and it is 40.62% as of 30th June 2024

items.statement: LCR improved to 138% from 122% QoQ driven by lower borrowings against excess SLR and raising liabilities with lower run-offs
items.quote: So, in fact Sir, we have brought down our borrowings against the excess SLR, that is one point. The 2nd point is that in terms of raising the fresh liabilities which have lower run-offs, that is also one contributing factor to the increase in LCR, quarter on quarter.

items.statement: New RBI investment valuation norms impacted treasury income; bank reclassified portfolio leading to Rs 3,200+ crore reserve boost to CET1 (30 bps)
items.quote: At the same time, if you look at the reserve that we have created in the CET1 because of this stance of putting in-money in the AFS, that is in excess of 3,200 crore. That has contributed to the CRAR on the CET1 to the extent of 30 bps.

items.statement: No specific capex guidance disclosed; focus on IT and digital platforms under ED Sanjay Mudaliar
items.quote: Then we have with us Mr. Sanjay Mudaliar. He looks after the IT part of it and the Retail Asset and Retail Liability and couple of other platform function.

items.statement: CD ratio maintained at 82%; target operating band 80-82% with bias towards 80%
items.quote: And as on today, with all this, we are at the LDR of 82% and we intend to operate between a band of 80%-82% and slightly the bias would be towards 80%.

items.statement: CET1 improved to 13.08% from 12.54%; Overall CRAR improved to 16.82% from 16.31%
items.quote: Similarly, the bank is enjoying a robust capital position with CET1 improving from 12.54 to 13.08 and overall CRAR has been improved from 16.31 to 16.82.

items.statement: Full-year deposit growth guidance maintained at 10-12% and advances growth at 12-14%
items.quote: The deposit of full year would be around 10 to 12% and the advances would be 12 to 14%.

items.statement: Full-year NIM guidance maintained at 3.15% plus/minus 5 bps
items.quote: The NIM already I highlighted, our guidance would continue to be 3.15 plus/minus 5 bps.

items.statement: Full-year credit cost guidance lowered to below 0.75% from earlier less than 1%
items.quote: So, the guidance that we are making for full year on the credit cost would be lower than 0.75.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance maintained at 1-1.25% for full year
items.quote: On the guidance side, we'll continue to have the same guidance of the slippage ratio between 1 to 1.25.

items.statement: Corporate loan book growth guidance for Q2 FY25 at 10-12% and full year at 10-12%
items.quote: So, in that scenario what we're looking at because overall we're giving a guidance of 12% to 14%, I think for September quarter, the growth would be almost at 10% to 12% for the corporate book.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 NIM at 3.18%, up 4 bps sequentially on normalized basis excluding year-end recoveries
items.quote: As compared to that, our net interest margin has improved to 3.18% with an increase of 4 bps.

items.statement: Cost of deposits flat sequentially at 5.06% in Q1 FY25 vs 5.06% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: One important data point also, please note that, the cost of deposit has been flat vis -a-vis June over March.

items.statement: Yield on advances improved 15 bps YoY to 8.55% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The yield in the advances has improved by 15 bps from 8.40 % to 8.55%.

items.statement: Gross NPA improved to 2.88% in Q1 FY25 from 3.51% YoY; Net NPA at 0.69%
items.quote: As you can see, there is a decline in the gross NPA percentage from 3.51% to 2.88%. Similarly, as we have given the guidance earlier, the net NPA position is 0.69%.

items.statement: Slippage ratio at 1.05% in Q1 FY25, within guidance range of 1-1.25%
items.quote: One of our significant metrics – the slippage ratio is 1.05 % which is maintained at the same level as that of previous Q1.

items.statement: Credit cost improved to 0.47% in Q1 FY25 from 0.70% YoY, better than guidance of 0.75%
items.quote: Credit cost has improved due to the improvement in the asset quality. It has improved from 0.70% to 0.47% as against our guidance of 0.75%.

items.statement: SMA book at 0.18% of standard assets in Q1 FY25, down from 0.48% YoY; collection efficiency at 99%
items.quote: Our SMA book is on a lower side of 0.18% of the total standard assets, and collection efficiency is comfortably placed at 99%.

items.statement: Provision coverage ratio at 92.32% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are comfortably placed as far as provisional coverage ratio is concerned at 92.32%.

items.statement: CET1 ratio improved to 13.08% in Q1 FY25 from 12.54% in Q4 FY24; overall CRAR at 16.82%
items.quote: The Bank enjoys a strong capital position with CET1 increasing from 12.54% Q4 to 13.08%, with tier 1 increasing. And overall CRAR is improved from 15.84% to 16.82% YoY.
