items.statement: LCR at 138% in Q1 FY25; draft LCR guidelines impact estimated at 12-15% but manageable
items.quote: The bank enjoys a comfortable LCR of 138%, and we are having a stronger capital position.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to Rs 7,500 crore via Tier 1 and Tier 2 bonds to replenish maturing capital
items.quote: We have also informed to the Stock Exchange that we are looking at Tier 1 and Tier 2 to largely offset the maturing Tier 1, Tier 2 and the amount is 7,500 crores.

items.statement: Total deposit growth at 8.9% YoY in Q1 FY25; CASA growth at 6% YoY; CASA ratio at 40.62%
items.quote: There is a growth of around 8.9% in overall deposit. However, our CASA growth remains at a higher pace of 6% and better than our peer banks. Coming to the CASA ratio, we are above 40%, and as of Q1 we are at 40.62%.

items.statement: Wholesale/bulk deposits reduced by Rs 24,000 crore QoQ in Q1 FY25 to ~Rs 2,00,000 crore; real reduction ~Rs 7,000 crore after reclassification
items.quote: If you look at the numbers which has been published there in the presentation, on the wholesale book, which was of the bank on the deposit side was almost 2,24,000 crores, which has gone down in June from March to almost 2,00,000 level.

items.statement: Retail loan book grew 21% YoY in Q1 FY25; retail share increased 258 bps YoY
items.quote: The retail continued to be growing very strong at 21%. And in terms of last one year between June ‘24 over June ‘23, the retail book has almost increased by 258 bps.

items.statement: Personal loan growth moderated to 39% YoY in Q1 FY25 from ~80% YoY previously; sequential growth down to 2-3%
items.quote: On the personal loan if you look at the corresponding quarter growth it was 80 odd percent, right, as against 80 odd percent Y -o-Y for this Q1 has been 3 9%.

items.statement: Agri and MSME loan growth at ~9% YoY in Q1 FY25; focus to optimize growth in Q2
items.quote: Secondly, two elements you would have noticed on the Agri and MSME side. So there the growth has been almost at 9%.

items.statement: International advances grew 6.4% YoY in Q1 FY25; international NIM improved above 2%
items.quote: It has not shrunk; the growth is 6.4%.

items.statement: RAM (Retail, Agri, MSME) mix improved to ~59% of loan book in Q1 FY25 from ~56% YoY; target 64% over couple of years
items.quote: If I compare the June 24 over June 23, the RAM book has increased almost by 300 bps now. So, earlier also we gave a guidance that at some point of time we'd like to have almost 64% as a RAM book.

items.statement: Operating expenses growth controlled at 16% YoY in Q1 FY25 vs 25% previously; cost-to-income ratio focus on process automation long-term
items.quote: If you look at the operating expenses, we have a fair bit of control if you look at this quarter, as against a growth of almost 25% operating expenses the growth has been 16% this time.

items.statement: Divestment process ongoing for Nainital Bank and IndiaFirst Life (IPO/OFS); BOB Card not on sale; IndiaFirst timeline 12-18 months
items.quote: As far as our divestment currently we are only looking at two assets which can be divested. One is Nainital as you said, other one is India First in terms of OFS and IPO for that entity. So, Bob Card is not on any scheme of things at this point of time.

items.statement: New RBI investment classification norms led to Rs 3,200 crore MTM gains moving to AFS reserves, boosting CET1 by ~30 bps
items.quote: Almost 3,200 crore of in-money position has gone to the reserve in the CET1.

items.statement: Expect deposit cost moderation in H2 FY25 (Q3/Q4) as rate cut outlook improves; liquidity scenario turned positive systemically
items.quote: Slightly on the expectation side w e are more positive in terms of a rate cut maybe happening in the Q3 or Q4 and that possibly would moderate the rate structure in the market.

items.statement: BOB World app ban lifted during Q1; channels reopened in graded manner; expect full transaction recoupment by Q2 FY25
items.quote: I think in Q2 I will be in a fair position to t ell how much we have recouped vis -à-vis the earlier pre-ban transaction level

items.statement: Management guided for around 10% growth with existing facilities via debottlenecking, productivity and product mix
items.quote: We have given a guidance that we should be able to maintain our growth of around 10% with the current existing facilities by way of debottlenecking, enhancing productivity, enhancing product mix.

items.statement: Furnace relining and debottlenecking project initiated in Q1 FY25 on track for completion in early August 2024
items.quote: Our ongoing furnace relining and debottlenecking project, which we initiated this quarter, is on track for completion in early August 2024.

items.statement: Next scheduled furnace relining planned for FY28
items.quote: With the next scheduled relining planned for FY28, we're strategically positioned to meet the rising demand for glass containers while optimizing our operational efficiency.

items.statement: Commissioned 2.8 MW solar rooftop at Hyderabad plant, raising total solar capacity to 19.56 MW
items.quote: we successfully commissioned a 2.8 MW solar rooftop project at our Hyderabad plant, increasing the company's overall solar capacity to 19.56 MW.

items.statement: Specialty glass plant utilization close to 70%; aim to reach 100% then debottleneck further
items.quote: Utilization rate is close to 70%.

items.statement: Base capacity around 1,600 tons/day; debottlenecking added ~100 tons in commercial glass and ~30 tons in specialty glass; new furnace expected to add 70-80 tons
items.quote: 1,600 tons is the capacity, which we had the initial capacity and 154 is for cosmetic plant., We de-bottlenecked 30 metric tons further in specialty glass, and de-bottlenecked 100 tons in the commercial glass.

items.statement: Brownfield expansion from ordering machines to commissioning takes 2.5 to 3 years
items.quote: you can say anywhere between 2.5 years to 3 years should be the normal one.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA ₹147 crore, up 4.7% YoY with stable margin of 25.4%
items.quote: The Company's recorded an EBITDA of ₹147 crore, achieving 4.7% year-on-year growth, with stable margin of 25.4%.

items.statement: Gross margin improvement driven mainly by cost-side debottlenecking and efficiency gains, not just price increases
items.quote: the big part is on the cost side and other part is on the selling price side. So, selling prices can be adjusted now and then, because of the change in the formula or whatever is the cost, but the real cost reduction, which has happened is with the de-bottlenecking and other synergies.

items.statement: Realization more or less flat with small formula-based adjustments; long-term contracts insulate from demand-supply swings
items.quote: Realization is more or less flat. It has been more or less same as it has been the earlier one with a small adjustment on the prices because a major part of our supplies is adjusted with the formulas.

items.statement: Fuel mix optimization across furnace oil, gas and other fuels contributes to cost reduction
items.quote: we have a options of using various fuel mix depending on the fluctuation in the market prices and to take advantage of cost, we keep on shuffling use of fuel from one fuel to the other.

items.statement: Q1 sales slightly lower due to election-related liquor restrictions; alcohol industry growing 8-9% per public data
items.quote: First quarter was a little difficult for the sales, because of the elections. So, there have been some prohibitions and restrictions on the consumption of one of the biggest segments in our glass industry, i.e. liquor, beer segments.

items.statement: PET substitution in spirits is a novelty factor with limited life; not a major concern given overall liquor growth
items.quote: there is a novelty factor, which has attracted the glass, attracted the people and novelty factor has a timeline or they have a life and which we have to expect that. So, what we expect that these types of conversions or these type of switching and swapping is very common.

items.statement: Dormant industry capacity exceeds operating capacity; no major new capacity announcements in public domain
items.quote: total capacities, which I can say the dormant capacities are higher than the operating capacity, it is sure. The second thing is that which we hear, here and there every time that somebody is like to put here capacity out there. I cannot comment on that, because if there is somebody who publicly announced only those capacities can be we can officially tell at such a platform.

items.statement: HNG acquisition sub-judice in Supreme Court and NCLT; hearing expected mid-September 2024
items.quote: The matter is sub-judiced and it's in front of Supreme Court and NCLT. Hearing is expected in middle of September.

items.statement: Planned furnace shutdown caused 16,000 tons production loss in Q1; part spills into Q2 but managed via seasonal stocking
items.quote: we were not able to produce 16,000 tons of glass in this quarter. Because of this. I'm talking quarter. So my quarter ends on 30th of June.

items.statement: Cullet usage ~50% in India and at AGI; furnaces capable of up to 90% but limited by collection system
items.quote: In India, the collection system has been quite poor, and we are restricting ourselves less than 50%. And AGI is also using close to 50%.

items.statement: Cullet price practically same as virgin raw material; preferred for energy savings and sustainability
items.quote: Practically the price of cullet and the price of virgin raw materials is almost same. But sometimes, it all depends on because using more cullet is good for sustainability. It saves a bit of energy, easy to melt also.

items.statement: Exports ~10% of revenue; limited impact from shipping freight increases; imported raw materials locked in long-term contracts
items.quote: Because we are not in the export market as such in a big way, we are just close to 10%. So it has not impacted us so much. On the raw material side, only one of the raw materials, which is being imported, and they are locked with the long-term contracts.

items.statement: Long-term export opportunity driven by China Plus One policy and India's demographic advantage

So obviously, the growth potential from India, with China Plus One policy is there.

items.statement: Specialty glass plant (cosmetics/perfumery) performing well; achieved IGBC Green Factory Platinum rating
items.quote: Our state of the art specialty glass plant is well-positioned to capitalize on the growing demand for high-margin products such as cosmetics and perfumery, driving overall profitability.

items.statement: Machining efficiency improved from 83-84% five years ago to higher levels year-on-year
items.quote: our efficiency on machining of the bottle 5 years back was somewhere around 83%, 84%, which year-on-year, we have been able to increase.

items.statement: Market risk always present but operational commitments make EBITDA per ton sustainable year-on-year
items.quote: I think we have been with you guys for the last so many years, and we are talking the same story. So, it is a sustainable year-on-year, on quarter-on-quarter, the numbers have been same, it is similar or what we are projecting. And market risk is always there, which is in every business.

items.statement: R&D Center and Chemical Lab secured NABL accreditation; Bhongir and Hyderabad plants won CII EHS Excellence Gold and Silver awards
items.quote: Our R&D Center and Chemical Lab secured NABL accreditation, demonstrating our commitment to delivering high-quality, innovative solutions to our customers. Additionally, our Bhongir and Hyderabad plants were recognized with Gold and Silver awards at the CII EHS Excellence Awards 2023.

items.statement: FY25 volume guidance unchanged for metal and silver
items.quote: I am proud of my team who delivered very significant cost reduction of 7% over last year to help the Company register a massive growth in net profit by 19% over last year on the back of a growth in total income by 12%.

items.statement: FY25 cost of production guidance kept at $1,050-1,100 per ton
items.quote: We have given the guidance as a lower quartile of a 1,050 and to 1,100. We achieved $1,107 and it is partly on account of , you are right softened coal prices as well as the RE power which started coming from Serentica.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance kept intact
items.quote: I hereby let you know that we are confident in achieving our cost guidance and hence are keeping the cost and CAPEX guidance intact.

items.statement: Debari roaster 160 ktpa commissioning targeted by Q4 FY25, fertilizer plant 510 ktpa by Q2 FY26

items.statement: Bamnia Kalan mine development started after consent to operate, first ore expected around Aug-Sep 2026

items.quote: We have sold forward 90 kt of the zinc production for the fiscal year around 10% of our annual production of zinc, demonstrating our agile decision making and flexibility to harness right opportunities.

items.statement: Renewable power from Serentica started May 2024, 8.5% of power mix in Q1, targeting 13% for FY25
items.quote: I am happy to announce that Hindustan Zinc has preponed the commencement of renewable power supply from Serentica to May 2024 with around 8.5% of our overall power requirement being catered through renewable energy during the quarter.

items.statement: Domestic coal share 45% in Q1 (linkage + e-auction), up from ~22% last year; revamped plants to use 100% domestic coal
items.quote: This year we have a 45% of the linkage coal connection. And the last year it was almost half of it.

items.statement: Launched EcoZen low-carbon green zinc (<1 t CO2e/t Zn), 75% below global average, ~60 kt/yr initially (8.5% of production)
items.quote: We have marked a significant milestone in the metal and mining industry by launching Asia's first low-carbon green zinc, EcoZen expanding our zinc product portfolio which is currently one of the largest in the world.

items.statement: Domestic primary zinc market share expanded to 78% from 75% last year
items.quote: With concentrated efforts, we have also expanded our domestic primary zinc market share to 78% from 75% last year.

items.statement: MoU with VEXL for waste-to-product pilot; partnership with AEsir Technologies as preferred zinc supplier for Ni-Zn batteries
items.quote: We have signed an MoU with VEXL Environ Projects Limited for establishing a pilot plan for producing saleable products from our waste streams, embracing environmental responsibility through circular economy.

items.statement: Silver inventory kept nil monthly, no impact from customs duty change
items.quote: So, silver if you are talking for the inventory which is lying in our stock, there is no impact because we don't remain any finished good silver in the books at any month. It's always nil.

items.statement: Cash Rs 10,885 cr, debt Rs 11,200 cr as of Q1 FY25 end
items.value: Rs. 10,885 crores and around Rs. 11,200 crores of debt
items.quote: So, we have the cash of Rs. 10,885 crores and around Rs. 11,200 crores of debt.

items.statement: Paid Rs 4,225 cr dividend in Q1; total shareholder return Rs 387/share (133% on prior year close)
items.quote: During the quarter, the Company paid Rs. 4,225 crore as dividend. As one of the leading companies in our country, our ultimate priority is to maximize the distribution of the value created amongst the shareholders in a sustainable manner.

items.statement: Rajasthan environment/health cess Rs 142 cr contingent liability; Supreme Court order reserved, retrospective application uncertain
items.quote: You are right, this remain as a part of the contingent liability and of course one of the argument we had the royalties not a tax but apart from this also, from a legal evaluation point of view, this is one of the argument which we had in the court.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 mined metal 263 kt, refined metal 262 kt (highest ever Q1); saleable silver down 7% YoY due to WIP accumulation
items.quote: I am pleased to inform you that Hindustan Zinc has recorded its highest ever first quarter mined and refined metal production at 263,000 tons and 262,000 tons respectively.

items.statement: Target 5-7% metal production growth and 3-5% silver production growth in FY25 over FY24
items.quote: With the rest of the commissioned projects ramping up, we have marked a great start of the year and would like to build on this momentum going ahead to finish the year with 5% to 7% growth in metal production and 3% to 5% growth in silver production over last year.

items.statement: Metal price outlook uncertain till Dec 2024; expects improvement post US elections and Russia-Ukraine war resolution
items.quote: I don't expect the situation to improve drastically anytime sooner from between now till about December. Hope that by November when the US elections are over and whosoever new government comes may set right a new global agenda.

items.statement: Trained India's second all-women underground mine rescue team; won awards for employee management, talent acquisition, HR technology
items.quote: It gives me immense pleasure to inform you that Hindustan Zinc has trained India's second all-women underground mine rescue team following the remarkable success of the first batch.

items.statement: Targets INR 150-200 crore revenue from new value-added specialty chemicals in FY25
items.quote: I think in the financial year we are targeting to do INR 150-200 crores kind of top line through new value-added products, which in my opinion, if we are able to do is a very good start.

items.statement: Kashipur distillery expansion from 400 to 500 KLPD and Gorakhpur from 110 to 290 KLPD to complete in Q3 FY25
items.quote: Regarding the CapEx, which we are already in for the increase in the capacity in Kashipur from 400KL to 500KL, we hope that CapEx will be completed in Q3. And as far as the CapEx, which we have undertaken in Gorakhpur, from 110 to 290KL, I think that will also be completed in Q3.

items.statement: INR 60 crore capex spent in Q1 FY25 across all ongoing projects
items.quote: And with respect of the expenditure on the CapEx in Q1 FY25, we have spent around INR 60 crores on all the CapEx whatever is going on right now, and hopefully, will be capitalize once these are complete.

items.statement: Expanded ethanol capacity of 25-26 crore litres annually from November/December 2024
items.quote: We will be able to start both the plants adding the 50% of additional capacity from the new ethanol year, maybe November second half or first week of December, which would be adding our 50% additional capacity.

items.statement: Grain distillery to operate 340-350 days per year vs 260-270 for sugar-based
items.quote: But grain distillery would run around 350 days in a year. And sugar mills, whatever they will store the molasses at the last working days, they again can be utilized in 3-4 months maximum depending upon their storage capacity of molasses. So, you can say sugar based on an average they are running around 260-270 days and grain based roughly 340-350 days.

items.statement: Ethanol blending program on track; expects 14% blending in 2023-24 and 18%+ by 2025-26
items.quote: And we see that the blending program will move up from 15% to 17% to 20%. And it will be fair to assume that even by 2025-26, even if we don't do 20%, hopefully we will do, it will be fair to look at the track record and say that we probably end up doing 18%-plus blending.

items.statement: National ethanol demand expected at 1,100-1,200 crore litres for 20% blending
items.quote: 1,100-1,200 crore liters.

items.statement: Biofuels EBIT margin improved from ~5% to ~8% YoY; Q1 FY25 at 7.82% vs 7.9% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: For Q4 FY24, the EBIT margin was 7.9%, while in the current quarter it is 7.82%. So as CEO Sir is saying, it has improved.

items.statement: Potable Spirits EBIT margin at 17.5% in Q1 FY25; expected to remain same in Q2
items.quote: No, margin would remain same because both prices because mostly country liquor, all the raw material prices, basically feedstock prices is already fixed by the government. So, we don't think any negative impact in the Q2.

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma margins under pressure from nicotine and Thiocolchicoside; expected to remain same in Q2 with potential improvement from Q3
items.quote: The revenue would be more than whatever we have done in the last year. But certainly, the margins are under pressure, and it would remain under pressure. We are just waiting to see the Q3 performance, then if it then improves then there is a possibility that we would surpass the last year numbers, otherwise it will remain same, almost same.

items.statement: JV with Clariant gross margin improved upwards of 35% due to better cost position and Equinox supply
items.quote: And now you see whilst the joint venture top line has seen nominal growth, but there has been quite a significant growth in terms of the gross margin, which is upwards of 35%. And a lot of it is on account of the improved cost position and Equinox side that we supply to them.

items.statement: Government ethanol procurement prices: damaged food grain INR 64, surplus rice FCI INR 58.5, maize INR 71.86 per litre
items.quote: the government has supported its mandate by increasing the procurement price for ethanol, which can get close to INR 64 for damaged food grain-based ethanol, surplus rice-based FCI at 58.5. We see going forward an encouragement for people to also start using India Glycols Limited July 31, 2024 5 maize and the supporting price for that ethanol is also good by the government at point in time is clos

items.statement: Targeting 20-25% maize self-sufficiency from catchment area by 2025-26; maize requires 40% less water
items.quote: And we are expecting approximately 20-25% would be the self-placement area maize availability in 2025-2026. So certainly, we are focusing on the variety, which would increase the ethanol yield. And second, the catchment area in which we are focusing, we would like to ensure the back-to-back logistics, so that the entire approximately 70-80% maize which is grown by the farmer would be made availabl

items.statement: Total debt ~INR 1,000 crore including fresh borrowings of INR 165 crore in June/July for capex and working capital
items.quote: Our debt is around INR 1,000 crores right now. Regarding the money, which is to be received from Clariant, that is still outstanding and that will come by 31st March 2025.

items.statement: INR 250 crore loan maturity due in FY25 including EPBG
items.quote: In the current year, approximately INR 250 crore maturity including EPBG.

items.statement: Finance cost unlikely to reduce drastically in FY25; expected to decline from FY26 as capex capitalizes
items.quote: So that is hurting us and of course we are planning to reduce the finance cost, but in this year, we are not hopeful for drastic reduction of the finance cost. Maybe from the next year onwards, maybe FY25-26, yes, the finance cost will start coming down.

items.statement: Fresh borrowing of INR 165 crore from Exim Bank and two other banks in June/July for capex and working capital
items.quote: That is the fresh borrowing, Manish.

items.statement: Clariant JV proceeds of outstanding amount expected by March 31, 2025
items.quote: Regarding the money, which is to be received from Clariant, that is still outstanding and that will come by 31st March 2025.

items.statement: Oil company ethanol allocation conversion at 90-95%; expects trend to continue
items.quote: And the tender allocation product for us starting with November 2023, we have seen that the actual orders that the oil companies placed have been only slightly lower than the allocations that they have given. And I don't have the exact numbers, but it has been 90-95% of the allocation that has been given.

items.statement: Potable Spirits growth driven by country liquor in Uttarakhand and IMFL in UP plus paramilitary sales
items.quote: Sales have been driven mainly by increase in country liquor sales in Uttarakhand, and we continue to maintain our dominant positions, a big dominant position in Uttarakhand, but also a dominant position in the UP market. In terms of IMFL sales or Indian-Made Foreign Liquor sales, our sales have been driven with excellent growth in the UP market and also a relatively new area for us, which is our p

items.statement: Ennature Biopharma pursuing US FDA and CB certifications for branded nutraceuticals; pure nicotine supply tie-ups with local bodies
items.quote: Shortly we are going to have US FDA and one CB audit over there to get the certifications done. After that we would be able to sell our branded nutraceuticals in the European and American markets. Other than that, there are other few major products like Thiocolchicoside is facing pressure but still we are maintaining the pole position in all of India by supplying the maximum Thiocolchicoside.

items.statement: Government promoting maize for ethanol; state government assisting catchment area development
items.quote: Because the government is continuously insisting to promote maize to increase the profitability of the industry and the farmer both. So, industry and associations are doing hard and we have already started our maize farming in our own catchment area of Gorakhpur and we are going to start from Kashipur.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 FY25: Gross Revenue INR 2,283 cr (+21% YoY), Net Revenue INR 969 cr (+41% YoY), EBITDA INR 128 cr (+21% YoY), PAT +18% YoY
items.quote: So as you may have had an opportunity to look at, we've had a good quarter, I can say, especially I know over the last couple of years or probably more than that, we have been through a bit of a tight situation on the India Glycols front for all the reasons that we have discussed with you and several questions that we have answered. But it appears that broadly in terms of the strategy of the compa

items.statement: Chemicals segment revenue +17% YoY; Biofuels revenue INR 139 cr vs INR 65 cr YoY; Potable Spirits revenue INR 280 cr (+19% YoY); Ennature Biopharma +8% YoY
items.quote: And the biofuels business on a YoY has improved from INR 65 crores to INR 139 crores, which contributes significantly. And the Potable spirits business has also done very well to grow by 19.1% YoY. Our Ennature Biopharma business has also seen a modest, relatively speaking, the modest top line growth of 8%.

items.statement: Biofuels margin dependent on grain prices, DDGS sales, ethanol procurement price; government regulates pricing limiting upside
items.quote: I would imagine the right thing to assume would be that the government is committed for the blending program and because the government is significantly involved in regulating it, regulating it and controlling it in some way, they will keep it profitable, but it is not a business where suddenly if the demand is high and the supply is low, you can fetch a huge amount of price.

items.statement: MEG/ethylene oxide capacity 600 tonnes/day but running lower for cost optimization; profitability now from bio-based MEG
items.quote: Our total capacity in terms of MEG equivalent, ethane oxide as well as MEG put together is about 600 tonnes per day.

items.statement: Active order book for TMD is around Rs 2100 crores out of total Rs 3380 crores
items.quote: if we were to take that as a benchmark, which we measure, we are looking at an active order book of around Rs 2100 odd crores, is what we are looking at.

items.statement: Total TMD order book stands at Rs 3380 crores with active portion expected to execute in next 12 months
items.quote: Currently, with respect to the order book, we hold an order book of Rs 3380 crores out of which ihe active part is lined up for execution.

items.statement: Domestic demand and order booking sharply dipped due to cotton price, yarn demand, fabric imports, and logistics costs
items.quote: The impact of cotton price, demand for yarn, the import of fabric, incremental logistics and product cost for our customers has resulted in a sharp dip in the domestic demand and the order booking and machine offtake.

items.statement: Order inflow has been lower over last 3-4 quarters and trend continues
items.quote: We have seen a lower inflow of orders over the last 3 -4 quarters and this trend is continuing as of now.

items.statement: Expect demand revival in next two quarters as yarn margins improve
items.quote: So, we feel that yes, with the margins on the yarn going up, it will trigger demand for the next two quarters it should start going back and order flow should improve and also the offtake should improve.

items.statement: TMD and Foundry capacity utilization at 45-50%, operating 5-day week
items.quote: The current capacity utilisation of the plant for textile machinery is closer to around 45% -50%. We currently have a layover of one day so we work five days right now for the textile machinery and Foundry division.

items.statement: MTD capacity utilization at 64-70% with 30% headroom to scale
items.quote: We are at a capacity utilization of somewhere from 64%-70% today, so, there is enough possibility for u s to scale the business of what the current investments what we have already done.

items.statement: Autoconer soft launch with 3 machines placed, 2 more en route; commercial launch post Jan 2025
items.quote: With respect to Autoconer as mentioned by our Chairman yesterday, we have placed around three machines with customers and two on the way. By Q4, I think it will start, it is a soft launch at the moment. So as and when further information we will be sharing and like you mentioned yesterday it will be post Jan 2025

items.statement: Airjet loom development advanced, targeting launch in FY26
items.quote: Airjet, yes, it is in the works. Again, yesterday it was mentioned that during the year 2025 -2026, it will be out. It is a technically complicated machine from what we currently do, and we are working fairly well and advanced in that particular machine.

items.statement: MTD margins under pressure due to Japanese yen depreciation making imports cheaper
items.quote: For t he machine tools business, we are under price pressure because of the global scenario where the currency has, Japan has depreciated and that is making it cheaper for imports

items.statement: ATC profit dropped due to composite division investment costs while metallics stable
items.quote: I think we are doing well in the metallic segment and decent margins, but we are also investing in the comp osite. And as what was mentioned yesterday, even in the AGM speech, we are building the composite division, and the composite division is incurring cost at the moment

items.statement: Focus on maintaining bottom line alongside topline growth
items.quote: I think the focus would always be topline but we will also focus on the bottom-line.

items.statement: MTD faces intense competition from Japanese, German, Chinese imports; foreign players establishing local facilities
items.quote: I think it is a fast-changing landscape, like I said. Perhaps quite different 5 years from now. We internally are also trying to see how we can give our best product because ultimately the challenge here for the customer who buys this machine, is that he needs per piece of the product to be the lowest.

items.statement: ATC revenue 90% export-driven with 3-10 year visibility; domestic defence play focused on composites
items.quote: With respect to ATC, I think one of the main things to understand is that most of this is, almost 90% of this is export. We focus on exports. So, our local domestic business with HIL is to that extent, is limited.

items.statement: MTD serves fragmented market with thousands of customers; auto consumes ~50% of machine tools
items.quote: Of course, the auto segment is a large part of machine tool business, probably consuming closer to 50% of the machine tool, but then you have a whole host of other segments of this business.

items.statement: Export turnover across divisions ~Rs 1000 crores annually; UAE subsidiary investment to consolidate China and Dubai holdings for export focus
items.quote: our general export turnover, if you add up over the last couple of years, I think would come closer to Rs 1,000 odd crores across the divisions and also across these companies.

items.statement: Higher capex allocated to MTD and TMD exports; new MTD facility commissioned; invest at 90% utilization threshold
items.quote: we have an allocation of a higher capex for them and expanding the area as well. I think there is an opportunity for us to grow in these segments.

items.statement: Customer advances ~Rs 330 crores out of ~Rs 1500 crores cash balance
items.quote: With respect to the cash balance, whatever you mentioned in the amount, it is closer to, Rs 330 cr would be customer's. That is what we initially spoke about, the order book.

items.statement: PLI scheme for textiles had muted offtake; government considering second PLI scheme
items.quote: I think the offtake in textile, perhaps has been a little bit muted. And that could be for many other reasons, I mean, we are talking about very challenging, at least till the last quarter, because of the cotton price, it was very challenging.

items.statement: Automation solutions offered across spinning value chain including robotic auto piecing, lap transport, link winder; retrofit possible depending on plant layout
items.quote: And within ring frame, we have a product called robotic auto piecing, in which technically you don't have to have any manpower, and this has been offered as a solution for the new machines. But I think your question was specifically whether it can retrofit into an existing machine. I think there will be possibility it's only depending on the layout of the plant

items.statement: LMW China team rebuilt to ~6 expats and ~100 local staff after visa issues resolved
items.quote: With respect to people, we have close to half a dozen people right now or expats in China. And thanks to all the efforts by the embassy on both sides, we have been able to get visas last year and they are all gone there. Of course, within China, we also have the local people we have closer to 100 odd people is what we employ there.

items.statement: Geopolitical situation in Middle East reducing machine offtake; Japanese yen depreciation increasing import competition
items.quote: The global geopolitical situation in countries in which we operate has re sulted there as well in lower offtake of machines.

items.statement: TMD revenue declined 53% YoY to Rs 439 crores; registered loss of Rs 12.72 crores vs profit of Rs 82 crores
items.quote: TMD revenue for the quarter stands at Rs 439 crores as against Rs 944 crores during the quarter ended June 2023 resulting in a 53% decline. TMD registered a loss for the quarter at Rs 12.72 crores as against a profit of Rs 82 crores during the quarter ended June 2023.

items.statement: MTD revenue declined to Rs 206 crores from Rs 243 crores; profit fell to Rs 6.5 crores from Rs 17 crores
items.quote: the revenue for the division for Q1 stands at Rs 206 crores compared to Rs 243 crores during the quarter ended June 2023. The division's profit stood at around Rs 6.5 crores as against Rs 17 crores for the quarter ended June 2023.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue flat at Rs 39 crores; profit dropped to Rs 1.5 crores from Rs 4.39 crores
items.quote: the revenue in this division was Rs 39 crores in Q1 compared to Rs 40 crores during the quarter ended June 2023 and ATC has clocked in a profit of Rs 1.5 crores as against Rs 4.39 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Consolidated turnover Rs 636 crores vs Rs 1055 crores YoY; PBT Rs 16.25 crores vs Rs 122 crores
items.quote: The company has achieved a turnover of Rs 636 crores during the June 2024 quarter compared to Rs 1055 crores during the June 2023 quarter, resulting in a 45% reduction. The PBT stands at Rs 17.5 crores for the current quarter as against Rs 121 crores during the quarter ended June 2023. On a consolidated basis, it stands at Rs 16.25 crores for the current quarter as against Rs 122 crores during the

items.statement: UAE investment of ~Rs 200 crores to consolidate China and Dubai subsidiaries under Dubai holding structure
items.quote: We are trying to bring in a consolidated structure for holding subsidiaries under the Dubai entity. That is the substance for the investment plan of the holding company.

items.statement: 5-axis machine not yet commercially launched; will inform when launched
items.quote: The 5-Axes is not commercially launched as of now. So, when we launch, we will definitely keep you informed about that.

items.statement: Auto volume growth target maintained at mid-to-high teens for FY25
items.quote: We would be inclined to drive growth and which is why we stay with the mid to high teens as the objective for the year because with 3 XO still ramping up with five door Thar coming in and with what we are doing on other brands we think we will easily get to mid to high teens.

items.statement: Tractor domestic growth outlook kept at ~5% for FY25, with positive bias
items.quote: But we will wait two, three months to give you a more numeric answer, right now we will stay with the 5% odd growth rate.

items.statement: EPS growth target of 15-20% on longer term basis
items.quote: We feel pretty good that we will be on track to deliver 15 % to 20% growth on a longer term basis on EPS.

items.statement: ROE target maintained at 18%
items.quote: We are at 19.4% and yes, the bar is still at 18, not going up to 19.

items.statement: Logistics Express business targets breakeven by end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: The Express business did have a loss but the management team has promised to turn around and a breakeven by end of the current quarter that we are in and t hat's something that is on track at this point in time

items.statement: Auto industry demand environment described as tepid with low buoyancy
items.quote: Overall, let's say the buoyancy as an industry clearly, that's not there. We got to be honest about that.

items.statement: Tractor demand showing green shoots with improving terms of trade, good monsoons, higher rural spending
items.quote: We clearly see some green shoots. One is improving terms of trade for farmers. We've been seeing that, but in quarter one seen a more dramatic improvement with output prices going up, MSPs improving, input inflation not being so high.

items.statement: Auto standalone margin expanded to 9.5% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Volume was up 11%, margins up 23%, and that's primarily coming on the back of the significant improvement in PBIT. 9.5% in the case of auto and 18.5% in the case of farm.

items.statement: Auto margin expansion driven by commodity benefits and full quarter impact of price increases
items.quote: On the auto side, it was a little bit of commodity benefits. So, we did get some of that. The benefit if I may use that word or some of the price increases were taken got fully baked into the full quarter numbers.

items.statement: XUV700 pricing actions expected to have negligible financial impact on margins
items.quote: We believe will have a negligible effect on the financials over this quarter or the next. So, we are not really factoring in that as a major driver, what will affect our margins.

items.statement: XUV700 capacity increased from 3,500 to 10,000 units per month over 3 years
items.quote: Capacity has gone up in the meanwhile. We s tarted at 3,500, we went to 6,000. Now we are at 10,000

items.statement: Auto capacity up 3x in last 4 years enabling market aggression and operating leverage
items.quote: capacity is up 3x in the last 4 years. And that is enabling us to be a little Mahindra & more aggressive in the market now. And also gain operating leverage, which is helping in terms of margins

items.statement: XUV700 bookings increased 40-45% month-on-month in July
items.quote: We did have a very healthy increase in bookings in XUV700 during the month, up from the previous month by more than 40%-45%.

items.statement: XUV700 prices increased by Rs 3.8-4 lakh over 3 years due to commodity costs and chip premiums
items.quote: We took the XUV700 price, up from launched which is over 3 years by 3.8 lakhs to 4 lakhs. This was a function of commodity prices, premiums that we were paying for importing chips which we had to.

items.statement: XUV700 AX5 Select variant launched below Rs 20 lakh with anniversary promotion on higher variants to improve accessibility
items.quote: The first initiative we took was to introduce a new version called AX5 Select which came with Panoramic Sunroof and so on at a more reasonable price point way below 20 and we did feel that we at least in the short run need to run a promotion which we branded as a third anniversary offer to kind of make the two higher versions as more accessible as well.

items.statement: XUV700 AX7/AX7L mix improved from 50-55% to 70-75% in June after pricing actions
items.quote: We have been seeing, over quarter one, the overall ratio of AX7, AX7 L was 70%, 75% in quarter one that was by June, we had come to 50%, 55%.

items.statement: Thar 5-door launch on August 15 expected to open wider segment
items.quote: Wider segment. Pramod Kumar: How wide? Rajesh Jejurikar: You may want to wait for 15th August to hear how wide, but it will be pretty

items.statement: Strategy to reduce customer waiting periods by increasing capacity, moving away from booking-driven model
items.quote: The reason we've been doing that is, of course, that we fully leverage the opportunity in front. But also more importantly, we bring down the waiting period for customers. And when we aspire to bring down waiting period to customers, clearly the concept of booking is an antithesis to that.

items.statement: Mahindra remains #1 in SUVs with 130bps market share gain, #2 in LCV revenue share for 8 quarters
items.quote: Auto we continue to be the number one player in SUVs. Volume is up 24%, we had talked about mid to high teen growth at the start of this year as a commitment for F25 or as an expectation rather than for F25. We are at 24% to start the first quarter.

items.statement: Tractor market share reached 44.7% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our tractor volumes were up mainly because we gained market share, the market had a slight degrowth but it was a good gain in market share to get to 44.7.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance GNPA at 3.6% in Q1 FY25, up from 3.4% at start of year
items.quote: We were down at 3.4% at the start of this year, a marginal increase to 3.6 which is the first quarter increase that typically happens.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance AUM grew 23% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Beyond that , assets up 23% and profit up 37% also helped by lower credit costs and this is something that is on the back of a good quarter last year for Mahindra Finance as well.

items.statement: Mahindra Finance PAT at Rs 497 crore in Q1 FY25, up 37% YoY
items.quote: And therefore, profit after tax, Mahindra Finance in this quarter is just very slightly shy of Rs. 500 crores. It's a good market reach for us, and we close the quarter at 497.

items.statement: Hospitality occupancy at 90%, membership at 300,000, average unit realization up 31%
items.quote: Mahindra & Hospitality continues to be a strong spot, 90% occupancy. Membership's growing 300,000 members now. Average unit realization is up 31%.

items.statement: Real estate pre-sales up 3x, GDP acquired up 68% YoY
items.quote: Real estate continues to grow at a very rapid pace, aided by an aggressive approach by the team. A lot of changes made there in terms of how the team's approaching the marketplace as well as the overall market buoyancy. So, a combination of that resulting in a 3x increase in pre-sales and GDP acquired is 68% higher than last year.

items.statement: EV three-wheeler policy flux (FAME 2, EMPS, FAME 3, PLI) creating margin uncertainty
items.quote: It's a difficult question to answer because of so much uncertainty in the regulatory environment with FAME 2 going away, EMPS coming in, FAME 3 coming back, in the process of that the quantum of FAME 2 came down.

items.statement: FAME 3 incentives seen as essential bridge to 2030 when EV three-wheelers expected to reach 100% penetration without subsidies
items.quote: FAME 3 will be essential to continue that momentum because the price gap is fairly high and consumer is not going to be able to take the impact without FAME 3 nor will the business be able to take the impact and therefore that's an important bridge that's required, but once we get to 2030 we are not going to need incentives beyond that.

items.statement: FY25 effective tax rate expected at 23-24%
items.quote: For FY25, it is going to be roughly around 23% effective ta x rate, could be 23 -24

items.statement: MHCV market share target 5% then 7% over 3-4 years
items.quote: So, we would like to see 3.9, get back to 5, and then the 5 to 7, over a three-to-four-year period.

items.statement: Farm machinery business expected to turn profitable in a couple of years
items.quote: The farm machinery we would expect a couple of years for us to start making money.

items.statement: BEV percentage margins lower than ICE due to denominator effect; per-unit margins expected similar at steady state
items.quote: So, we have said in the past that the percentage margin on BEVs will be lower, because the denominator effect and we will call that out separately, so you will be able to see the BEV margin separately from ICE.

items.statement: No margin guidance given to avoid short-term decisions; focus on sustainable growth and margin trade-offs
items.quote: We do want to make sure we are doing the right thing so that we get sustainable growth in business, volumes and in margins, and for which sometimes you got to take some short-term action so that you do not lose the momentum of what you are trying to get to.

items.statement: Scorpio booking run rate moderating as customers no longer willing to wait 2-6 months; fresh bookings sufficient for mid-to-high teens growth
