items.statement: Adjusted PAT grew 2.8x to INR 83.9 crores; reported PAT INR 68.3 crores (best ever quarterly)
items.value: INR 83.9 crores adjusted, INR 68.3 crores reported
items.quote: It has translated to a 2.8x growth in our adjusted PAT which came in at INR 83.9 crores, and our reported PAT of INR 68.3 crores reflects our best ever quarterly PAT performance.

items.statement: Invested INR 51.5 crores in growth capex in Q1, fully funded from operating cash flow
items.quote: We invested INR 51.5 crores in growth capex, and this was completely from the cash that we generated during the quarter.

items.statement: Fill-finish capacity expansion to 200 million devices requires ~$50 million over 3 years
items.quote: Around $50 million, and it will take us about 3 years.

items.statement: Soft gel capacity expanded from 1B to 2.4B units; expanded capacity fully sold out
items.quote: Well, the expanded capacity is fully sold out.

items.statement: Network optimization largely complete; no major new capex needed beyond automation and compliance
items.quote: We still have some capacities that needs utilization, which we hope -- so we don't think other than automation and compliance capex, we will not require any new capex.

items.statement: Reduced net debt by INR 36.7 crores in Q1 to INR 1,998 crores; net debt/EBITDA 2.3x
items.quote: With the operating cash generation, we have also reduced the net debt to less than INR 2,000 crores, so at INR1,998 crores with a N et Debt-to-EBITDA ratio of 2.3x

items.statement: Net interest cost steady at INR 67.7 crores; expected to improve in H2 with growth and debt reduction
items.quote: Our net interest costs are steady at INR 67.7 crores and we expect this will also improve in H2 with both growth and debt reduction playing out.

items.statement: U.S. portfolio shifting from acute to chronic; 35 products constitute ~$250M business with recent launches >$10M each
items.quote: We have mentioned that 35 products constitute almost $250 million of business. So it's a fairly linear situation. Nonetheless, the recent launches have quite significant higher dollar numbers, upwards of $10 million, not in all products, but most of them.

items.statement: 35 U.S. products are #1 or #2 in market position
items.quote: 35 products we are actually number one or number two.

items.statement: Freight rates escalated; incurred airfreight for launches and administered FY25 pay hikes; expect op cost/revenue ratio to improve in H2
items.quote: Our expenses for the quarter have been high. We saw freight rate escalations, and we also incurred airfreight for our product launches and administered pay hikes for FY '25. We expect our operating cost to revenue ratio to improve in tandem with a growth in H2.

items.statement: U.S. price erosion product-specific; disciplined launches only if meeting price targets; buyers more partner-like
items.quote: We've been telling your that with the luxury of over 250 ANDAs, we have launched only 67. The logic vein is that we will only launch a product if it meets our price tag. So I'm not saying that price pressures are not there, it's very product specific.

items.statement: OneSource matter admitted by NCLT; credit meeting expected soon; positive outcome hoped within FY25
items.quote: The matter on OneSource has been admitted by the NCLT court. We expect to have a credit meeting call out very soon, and we are on track to hope to have a positive outcome within this financial year.

items.statement: ROCE improved to 16.3% in Q1 from 12.8% at end of FY24
items.quote: Our rigor on operational excellence is visible in a consistent improvement of our ROCE. ROCE has improved to 16.3% in Q1 compared to 12.8% where we ended in FY'24.

items.statement: Credit rating outlook improved from A- negative to A Stable
items.quote: I'm also happy to report that our credit rating outlook also improved from A- negative to A Stable.

items.statement: Badree Komandur appointed CEO; Vikesh Kumar appointed CFO; Aditya Arun appointed Executive Director; two new independent directors (Ameet, Subir) elected
items.quote: I'm very happy that my colleague for several years, almost 15 years, Badree who has played multiple roles in the company takes over the CEO of the company while I continue my executive role as Chairman. And I'm also pleased to welcome Aditya as an Executive Director of the Board, but most importantly, we also very pleased that our homegrown talent, Vikesh, who joined us in our finance department s

items.statement: Promoter pledge at 65%; expected to reduce significantly post OneSource NCLT process and listing
items.quote: The pledges are directly linked to the investments that we had to make at Stelis. Now that we are very close to an NCLT process and listing, we believe that our pledge positions will come down quite significantly.

items.statement: Deposit growth guided at 8-10% for FY25; Q1 achieved 10%
items.quote: We had also guided that the deposits will be growing between 8-10% and we have grown by 10% in Q1.

items.statement: Advances growth guided at 11-13% for FY25; Q1 achieved 12%
items.quote: In advances, we said that we'll grow between 11 - 13%. And we grew our book by 12%.

items.statement: CD ratio guided close to 80%; currently at 79%
items.quote: Further, we also said that we'll maintain our CD close to 80% and we are at 79% right now.

items.statement: Full-year recovery target Rs 7,000 crore; Q1 recovered Rs 1,937 crore
items.quote: Out of the full year guided recovery estimate of Rs.7,000 crore, we have recovered Rs.1,937 crore in Q1.

items.statement: NIM guidance range 3.4% +/- 10-15 bps; Q1 NIM at 3.53% within range
items.quote: Our margins was at 3.53% which is again within our guidance range of 3.4%, plus/minus 10 bps, 15 bps.

items.statement: Credit cost guided lower than 0.71%; ROA on increasing bias from 1.20%
items.quote: so. So, our credit cost will be lower than 0.71% and we are continuously declining. As far as ROA is concerned, it is in an increasing bias – it was 1.15% last quarter and now it is 1.20

items.statement: NIM improved to 3.53% from 3.52% QoQ; cost of deposits up 4 bps to 5.05%, yield on advances down 12 bps to 8.69%
items.quote: NIM has improved from 3.52% to 3.53%, the return on asset improved from 1.15% of March quarter to 1.20%, the likewise ROE improved from 19.06% to 19.76%, the cost to income has improved from 47.99% to 44%.

items.statement: Yield on investments rose to 7.15% from 6.88% QoQ; HTM 7.08%, AFS 7.17%, FVTPL 7.79%
items.quote: yield on investment has increased from 6.88% to 7.15% because from last one year, we are working on investment and you see the investment yield is 7.15%. Here, the HTM holding yield is 7.08% and AFS is 7.17% and FVTPL is 7.79%.

items.statement: Cost-to-income improved to 44% from 47.99% QoQ; below 40% may take time
items.quote: the cost to income has improved from 47.99% to 44%.

items.statement: GNPA improved to 3.77% from 3.95% QoQ; NNPA improved to 0.39% from 0.43%; PCR improved to 96.66%
items.quote: The GNPA which was 3.95% in March quarter improved to 3.77% and the net NPA which was 0.43% has improved to 0.39%. The PCR which was 96.34% as of Mar’24 improved to 96.66% as of Jun’24.

items.statement: Slippages Rs 1,928 crore (1.5%); MSME Rs 900 cr, Agri Rs 600 cr, Retail Rs 400 cr; recovered Rs 312 cr post-June
items.quote: The slippage was Rs.1,928 crore which was 1.5% as against 1.57% of the last year. Slippages of Rs.900 crore came from the MSME book, close to Rs.600 crore came from the Agri book and the balance Rs.400 crore came from the Retail book.

items.statement: Recoveries Rs 1,937 crore exceeded slippages Rs 1,928 crore; collection efficiency 95%
items.quote: This time again, the recoveries is more than the slippages. The recoveries is Rs.1,937 crore as against the slippage of Rs.1,928 crore.

items.statement: SMA book declined to 0.47% from 0.48% QoQ; two corporate SMA accounts totalling Rs 365 crore
items.quote: I think our SMA declined from 0.48% in Mar 24 to 0.47% in Jun 24. So, in our SMA book we have 2 corporate SMA accounts – Rs.263 crore and Rs.102 crore – summing up to Rs.365 crore.

items.statement: AUC recovery target Rs 2,000 crore for FY25; Q1 recovered Rs 500 crore; expect Rs 1,500 crore for rest of year
items.quote: We said that we will have close to Rs.2,000 crore of AUC recovery. So out of that, we have recovered Rs.500 crore.

items.statement: CASA grew 6% YoY; CASA ratio maintained at ~41%
items.quote: In deposit, the CASA has grown by 6% and we could maintain our CASA ratio at ~41%.

items.statement: RAM credit grew 13% YoY; Retail 14% (Housing 13%, Jewel 10%, Auto 55%), Agri 18%, MSME 6% (Standard MSME 11%)
items.quote: RAM credit (Retail, Agri and MSME) has grown by 13% and under RAM, retail has grown by 14%. Under Retail, housing loan has grown by 13%, jewel loan grown by 10%, auto loan by 55%.

items.statement: Corporate loans grew 9% YoY; Standard corporate grew 10%
items.quote: The corporate loan has grown by 9% YoY and the standard corporate loan has grown by 10%.

items.statement: Overseas advances grew 27% YoY; focus on syndication loans for better margins
items.quote: Basically, in overseas, advances have grown by 27%. So, we'll continue to focus on a syndication loan because the margins are better.

items.statement: Gold loan book ~Rs 81,000 crore; Agri gold loan ~Rs 73-74k crore growing 23%; 650 gold loan branches with karat meters
items.quote: We are having, virtually, close to Rs.81,000 crore of a gold loan book. And obviously, Rs.73,000-74,000 crore, is in Agri, which is growing at 23%.

items.statement: Mid-corporate centres (27) growing 25-30%; adding two more in Erode and Namakkal
items.quote: We are having a good growth of 25-30% in these centres and the margins are also good. The customer base is also increasing. And today, we are having close to 27 mid-corporate branches and we are adding two more in Erode and Namakkal.

items.statement: Digital transactions 90% of total (up from 85% YoY); mobile banking users 175 lakh (+33%), UPI users 185 lakh (+30%), UPI transactions 11,829 lakh (+56%)
items.quote: As far as the transaction at branch and digital transactions, it has gone up from 85% in Jun 23 to 90% in Jun 24. So now, digital transactions at the Bank is 90% and 10% at branch level.

items.statement: Digital business Rs 36,678 crore in Q1 (4x YoY); e-RAM Rs 29,987 crore; e-deposits Rs 6,670 crore (+176% YoY)
items.quote: As far as the digital business is concerned, for this quarter, it has gone up from Rs.9,000 crore to Rs.36,678 crore, which is close to 4x and e -RAM, which was Rs.6,700 crore, has gone up to Rs.29,987 crore.

items.statement: Completed 78 digital journeys last year (Rs 81,250 cr business); added 6 in Q1, plan 15 in Q2, 44 for full year
items.quote: last year we completed 78 journeys, which gave us digital business of Rs.81,250 crore. This year we have added another six journeys in the last quarter and planning to add another 15 journeys in Q2 and the year as a whole, we are planning for 44 journeys.

items.statement: Cost of deposits may rise 3-5 bps further; MCLR increased 5 bps each in June and July to offset
items.quote: Cost of Deposit is slightly higher because the Banks are taking money at a special term deposit rate. So, cost of deposit may further inch up by 3 bps-5bps. But we have increased the interest rates in MCLR book too during June and July by 5 bps each.

items.statement: Draft project financing/ECL norms: 2% provision by FY25 (amortised over 4 quarters = 0.5%/quarter); not material; will charge customers
items.quote: the draft guidelines tells you to make 2% provision by FY25, 3.5% provision by FY26 and then 5% by FY27. And that 2% also you can amortize over a period of four quarters. So virtually it comes to 0.5% per quarter, which is not a material amount.

items.statement: No capital raise planned for draft norms impact; CET1 16.47% (17%+ with Q1 profits); excess SLR Rs 44,000 crore
items.quote: And that will not be a major impact considering the present projects in hand.

items.statement: LDR 79%; can go 1-2% higher; deposits and advances growing in lockstep (Rs 60k cr each in FY24)
items.quote: LDR we are at 79%, 1 or 2% here and there we can go and basically what we do is we raise resources based on the need also. So, we basically match everything.

items.statement: Slippages not new normal; driven by seasonality, elections, heatwaves; expect recoveries > slippages
items.quote: We are definitely not happy with slippages of Rs.1,900 crore. There are two, three reasons for this. One is, of course, the seasonality is involved. Second one is, in the first quarter, because of election, and heat waves, there is a problem in getting money. But what happened, out of

items.statement: Deposit growth challenge to persist for ~1 year per RBI FSR; credit growth > deposit growth; managing via MCLR repricing (61% of book) and investment income
items.quote: Even the FSR of the Reserve Bank of India also said that the cycle of high credit growth and the low deposit growth will continue even for one year or so. So, we think that going forward also, the deposit will continue to be a challenge.

items.statement: PSLC commission Rs 627 crore for FY25; amortised over 4 quarters (Rs 157 crore booked in Q1)
items.quote: So that's Rs.627 crore of PSLC commission we booked. And as per our policy, we amortize over four quarters and thus Rs.157 crore is booked in the current quarter.

items.statement: Penal interest Rs 42 crore shifted from interest income to other income in Q1
items.quote: Yes, around Rs.42 crore has been booked, has shifted from the interest income to the other income.

items.statement: Targets pre-IndAS EBITDA margin of 7-8% for FY25 and 8-9% going forward
items.quote: So, if we talk about pre -IndAS numbers, this year we are targeting an EBITDA of 7% to 8%. And going forward we want to target a pre-IndAS EBITDA percentage of 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Targets PAT margin of 4.5% for FY25 and 4.5-5.5% going forward
items.quote: I think in FY24 our net margin was about 3.5%, so you can expect this year's PAT margin to be 4.5%. And going forward it should between 4.5% to 5.5%.

items.statement: Targets ROE of 20-22% going forward
items.quote: So, the ROE number that we're targeting going forward should be around 20% to 22%.

items.statement: Targets minimum 10% same store sales growth from next year onwards
items.quote: I think 10% is a very good number. So, going forward even if we achieve a 10% SSG I t hink that's very good for the business because it's a fixed cost business where even if you grow your sales by 10% your profitability grows multifold

items.statement: Targets 15-20% same store sales growth for remaining nine months of FY25
items.quote: Again, I would not want to revise the guidance for next year. We have already revised the guidance for this year, the rest of the nine months. But if you talk about next year onwards, we want a minimum SSG of 10%, any double digit SSG is good enough for us. Sameer Gupta: And the next nine months you are saying 15%? Akash Agarwal: Yes, 15% to 20

items.statement: Targets 30-40% revenue and EBITDA growth for FY25 and next 3-4 years
items.quote: So, the first target is for the next 3 to 4 years to grow at least 30% to 40% both in terms of revenue and EBITDA.

items.statement: Plans to add 40-50 net stores in FY25 (10 already opened in Q1), targeting 127 stores total
items.quote: 40 to 50. We have already added 10 stores and the plan is to add about 30 to 40 more.

items.statement: May open 60-70 stores in FY26 if execution remains strong
items.quote: If we continue to see the kind of growth that we are seeing and the kind of product acceptance that the market is showing us, then after these 40 to 50 stores this year we might open another 60 to 70 stores next year.

items.statement: New stores start at 20% lower sales per sq ft than mature stores and take 12-24 months to mature
items.quote: So, new stores typically start at a 20% lower PSS than old stores and it takes about 12 to 24 months for any new store to mature.

items.statement: Targets gross margin of 27-29% as strategic choice to pass value to customers
items.quote: So, we pass on all the benefits from our own production as well as private labels to the customers. So, we do not get an extra gross margin on our private labels and we are selling more at full price. But now our input margin is strategy is such that we are targeting a gross margin percentage ranging from 27% to 29% because we want to give maximum value to the customer and we want to be the market

items.statement: Private label contribution at 80% (calendar year Jan-Jul), targeting 100% in 1-2 years
items.quote: Our private label contribution is almost 80% and going forward the target is to make it 100% private label business. So, we are moving in that direction because one year back that percentage used to be 60%. So, in one or two years we want to be a 100% private label business.

items.statement: In-house design share at 30-35% of goods, targeting 80% going forward
items.quote: till 2 years back only about 5% of the goods in our stores were designed in -house whereas now that number has almost reached 30%-35%. Going forward we are targeting this number to reach 80

items.statement: Owned manufacturing at 16% of sales, no plans to add more units, share will decline with growth
items.quote: So, about 16% of our sales are owned manufacturing but we don't plan to open any more units. So, as we are opening more stores and as our sales are growing this contribution is going to come down.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 same store sales growth of 37%, volume growth of 55%, full price sales at 93%
items.quote: So, the growth across all our stores have been encouraging trans lating into a robust same store sales growth of 37% in Quarter 1. We have been able to consistently deliver high double digit SSG for the last few quarters due to this approach . The volume growth was 55% in the first quarter. The full price sales contribut ed 93% in the first quarter compared to 84% in the corresponding quarter last

items.statement: July same store sales growth better than Q1, expects momentum to continue in Q3
items.quote: I think this trend should continue because we are getting a very good feedback from our customers, both about the price proposition as well as the product offering. I think this is a trend that should continue in the future quarters because we have seen this in July also. So, in July our same store sales growth is actually better than the Q1 numbers.

items.statement: Inventory aging >1 year reduced from 23% to 7%, targeting zero by end of next year
items.quote: So, a couple of years back more than one year inventory was almost 23% and now that number is down to 7%. And the idea is to take this number down to zero by end of next year.

items.statement: Targets inventory days of 90-100 for this year, 80-90 going forward
items.quote: So, the target inventory number is 90 to 100 days that we're looking at. And going forward we would like to reduce it to 80 to 90 days.

items.statement: Current debt at Rs 78 crore, primarily cash credit limit used for vendor bill discounting
items.quote: I think the current debt on the books is about 78 crores. So, what we have is, it's a CC limit that we have from the banks, and we give a bill discounting feature to all our vendors where they can get an early payment of their bills. So, mostly we use the limit for those purposes.

items.statement: Rent fixed at Rs 54 per sq ft, expected to remain at similar levels with inflation adjustments
items.quote: It's completely fixed rental basis and our rental cost are Rs. 54 per square feet and I think it should be at this level just accounting for inflation obviously but it should remain at similar levels. We're not seeing a big change.

items.statement: Marketing spend (ex-COG) less than 1% of sales, expected to remain at similar levels
items.quote: than 1% of total sales. Naveen Baid: Is it going to be around similar levels? Akash Agarwal: Yes. Because we have understood that the product is the best brand ambassador and there's a lot of word-of-mouth marketing that's happening because all this growth is actually we have reduced our marketing spends from previous years

items.statement: Kids-wear contributes 26% of sales, attracting family customers with two-wheeler ownership profile
items.quote: But what we have found out is our kids -wear contributes almost 26% of sales. So, we have a lot of family customers coming into the stores whereas Zudio kids-wear is almost nonexistent. So, I think one big reason is that and the second reason is like I said it's a completely different target customer with very little overlap. That is why I think we haven't seen much impact on our sales in tho se p

items.statement: Sees limited overlap with Zudio due to different target customer (ASP 80% higher) and product mix (kids-wear 26% vs nonexistent)
items.quote: So, there are different tiers of competition. So, one would be the local mom and pop stores which is the unorganized retail, one is the national level retailer. So, there is a certain level of overlap because Zudio starts selling their t-shirts for 199 but their ASP is almost 80% higher than ours. So, like there is competition from each space , I would say, whether it's Vishal, V-Mart, Zudio but w

items.statement: Top stores achieving Rs 1,400-1,500 monthly sales per sq ft, targeting Rs 1,000 annual average this year
items.quote: Like I would not want to share those numbers but I would tell you that we have a lot of store s that are doing above Rs. 1,400-1,500 per square feet monthly sales also. So, there is no potential. It all depends on the kind of execution and the kind of product assortment that you have in the stores because in terms of capacity it's huge.

items.statement: New stores expected to reach Rs 1,000 annual sales per sq ft in 1-2 years vs 2-3 years previously
items.quote: If you spoke to me last year, I would have said the store will take 2 to 3 years. If you talk to me this year , I will tell you that it's 1 to 2 years and maybe next year if we continue this growth then the new stores from the first month itself are doing Rs. 1,000 per square feet.

items.statement: Store expansion fully funded through internal accruals, no external fundraising planned
items.quote: we plan to open 40 to 50 stores and the investment required for that is about 110 crores which we will be completely financed through internal accruals.

items.statement: Evaluating omnichannel model using store inventory for same-city delivery, will comment next quarter
items.quote: Yes, we are evaluating the omnichannel model where we'll use the store inventory and we'll use all the stores as a warehouse and deliver to the same city because that saves a lot on the return and the logistic cost. So, we are evaluating that and we are working on it. We will comment on it I think in the next quarter.

items.statement: Employee cost increase driven by new store hirings 1-2 months before opening, per sq ft cost stable
items.quote: So, most of it is because of the new store additions. So , a lot of the hirings needs to be done at least a month or couple of months prior to the opening of the store. So, every quarter you know we plan to open 15 to 20 stores. So , if you look at the per square feet basis , there's not much change. But in the absolute numbers as we keep growing the store base ,this number will rise.

items.statement: Underpromises on ROE (20-22%) and payback (3 years) despite potential for higher returns
items.quote: We like to under promise and over deliver. So, we are happy with a 20% ROE also. Like if we get more than that then good enough. But the guidance that we give going forward like even if you're getting an ROE of 20% to 22%, we are happy with those numbers.

name: Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone Ltd

items.statement: Maintains 15% volume growth guidance for FY25.
items.quote: Yes, it is a challenge, but we still keep 15% as our guidance. We try to achieve that.

items.statement: Pharma revenue expected to grow to INR5-6 crores each in Q3 and Q4.
items.value: INR5 crores to INR6 crores each
items.quote: But in the third and fourth quarter, it can go up to INR5 crores to INR6 crores each.

items.statement: Overall pharma guidance of INR15-20 crores for the year.
items.quote: So our overall guidance of around INR15 crores to INR20 crores, we are still confident in pharma, which will be coming at a much higher EBITDA.

items.statement: Targets EBITDA per kg of 40 in FY25.
items.quote: Our target is in FY '25. Let's see how it pans out.

items.statement: Aims for close to INR1,000 crores top line in FY26.
items.quote: Yes, '25, '26 is where we will be aiming close to INR1,000 crores top line.

items.statement: PAT can cross or close to INR100 crores if pharma contributes.
items.quote: And obviously, if that comes through pharma, as I anticipated, PAT can cross or close to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected at INR75-80 crores.
items.quote: So most probably, we'll end up somewhere around INR75 crores to INR80 crores capex for the current year compared to INR140 crores last year.

items.statement: ABG volumes to double, with capacity expansion ready by December.
items.quote: It will be coming in '25 itself. We are planning to bring the volumes ready by December this year.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg target of 40, currently at 37.1.
items.quote: Yes. Again, our target is 40. We are not close to that. Now in the Q1, it is only 37.1. 40 is our internal target.

items.statement: Raw material cost per kg reduced to INR95 due to recycled plastic use.
items.quote: But by virtue of RCP being used, which is as per the direction of the clients and needs of statutory compliance, the per kg of raw material has come down from INR98 to INR95.

items.statement: Qpack demand strong, expecting 40-50% volume growth.
items.quote: Probably, it's not that much, at least 40% to 50% volume growth is possible in Qpacks.

items.statement: Pharma EBITDA per kg expected at INR100-150 depending on mix.
items.quote: So the band could be INR100 to INR150 depending upon the production. We are into all the products. So it is wise to take somewhere around INR120 per kg as a contributor -- contribution.

items.statement: Competition in ice cream packs impacting sales.
items.quote: Yes. As I said, competition in some sectors of ice cream, especially in the interior sections in North and South, deep in the South, we are losing due to some competitors holding up with the standard ice cream packs.

items.statement: Pharma plant capacity at 1,500-1,600 tons, turnover potential INR60 crores.
items.quote: In terms of volume, it will be, say, something like 1,500 tons to 1,600 tons now currently. That is our production volume.

items.statement: Booking value guidance for FY25 is INR27,000 crores
items.quote: So from a booking perspective, it's at INR27,000 crores. I think we're well on track to do that given the strong start to Q1 and actually we're very happy with the strong start to Q1.

items.statement: Collections guidance for FY25 is INR15,000 crores
items.quote: We've guided to about INR15,000 crores of collections for the year, we did about INR3,000 crores in the first quarter, but are confident of meeting and hopefully exceeding by a bit the annual guidance.

items.statement: Gearing target range is 0.5:1 to 1:1
items.quote: So I think we've guided typically we'd like to be in a gearing range of 0.5:1 to 1:1. So we're kind of towards the middle end of that range, and quite comfortable.

items.statement: Residential real estate sector in India has been strong and sectoral tailwinds will continue over next few years
items.quote: The residential real estate sector in India has been strong over the past few years and we believe the sectoral tailwinds will continue over the next few years as well.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 booking value grew 283% to INR8,637 crores, highest quarterly booking value across listed developers
items.quote: GPL achieved the highest quarterly booking value and volume across listed developers in India for the second consecutive quarter. Booking value grew by 283% to INR8,637 crores.

items.statement: Booking volume of 8.99 million sq ft is highest volume sold by any listed developer in India
items.quote: Booking volume of 8.99 million square feet of area is the highest volume sold by any listed developer in India, surpassing GPL's previous best of 8.17 million square feet in Q4 FY '24.

items.statement: Godrej Woodscapes Bengaluru achieved booking value of INR3,156 crores from 3.4 million sq ft
items.quote: Godrej Woodscapes Bengaluru achieved a booking value of INR3,156 crores from 3.4 million square feet of area sold and Godrej Jardinia, Noida achieved a booking value of INR2,377 crores from 1.6 million square feet of area sold.

items.statement: Added two group housing projects across Pune and Bengaluru with estimated booking value of INR3,000 crores in Q1
items.quote: a business development perspective, I'm happy to announce that Godrej Properties added two group housing projects products across Pune and Bengaluru with estimated booking value of INR3,000 crores in the first quarter

items.statement: Q1 embedded margin slightly higher than FY24 levels
items.quote: In Q1, I think we are very happy with the kind of number we've seen. There's a similar but slight uptick in margin over FY '24 levels.

items.statement: Invested in building engineering and execution capabilities across zones and head office over last 9-12 months
items.quote: But over the last, say, 9 to 12 months, what we've done is we've kind of invested in building up capabilities on certain engineering and execution side in various zones as well as in HO because we could clearly see this as a lead indicator for us in the

items.statement: Invested in contractor ecosystem, brought prominent contractor for Godrej Reserve project
items.quote: And coupled with that, we've also managed to bring some very good contractors in projects which we've seen sort of had slowed down. Like Godrej Reserve, we've got listed in it a very prominent contractor.

items.statement: No pricing pressure in Gurgaon market, seeing good offtake with price appreciation
items.quote: So I don't see pricing pressure at the moment. Yes, there is a bit of consolidation that in the initial first 6 to 18 months of NCR offtake, especially in Gurgaon, there was like everyone was practically able to push inventory.

items.statement: 99% of Q1 sales were front-ended, cost of sales extraordinarily low vs competition
items.quote: Our 99% of last quarter was all front-ended sales, 1% because, the title of some projects is linked with OC which gets tagged as PLP.

items.statement: Collection efficiency was 94% in Q1, industry median is 60-70%
items.quote: Just to share with you some numbers, we track something called a collection efficiency which is basically how many customers tend to pay you within 30 days of raising invoice, right? The industry median would be about between 60% and 70% and last quarter for Godrej Properties was 94%.

items.statement: Collections grew 54% to INR3,012 crores in Q1
items.quote: s net operating cash flow grew 737% to INR988 crores led by a 54% increase in collections to INR3,012 crores in Q1

items.statement: Comfortable with current gearing at middle of 0.5:1 to 1:1 range, operating cash flows expected to be very strong
items.quote: We do expect operating cash flows through the rest of the year to be very strong. We've guided to about INR15,000 crores of collections for the year, we did about INR3,000 crores in the first quarter, but are confident of meeting and hopefully exceeding by a bit the annual guidance.

items.statement: Would not rule out equity raise if valuations attractive and opportunities beyond moderate BD arise
items.quote: If we see opportunities beyond that, we wouldn't rule out an equity raise if valuations are also in an attractive range.

items.statement: Net profit increased 316% to INR520 crores, highest ever quarterly PAT
items.quote: GPL also recorded its highest ever reported PAT numbers on a quarterly basis. Our total income for the first quarter increased by 25% and stood at INR1,638 crores. Our EBITDA increased by 237% to INR774 crores and net profit increased by 316% to INR520 crores.

items.statement: Ashok Vihar project delayed due to tree removal approvals and court matters in NCR
items.quote: The essential issue there is the trees on the site and how they are to be treated and at NCR unfortunately, over the last 12, 18 months there has been a huge focus on tree removal and there's several matters in the court.

items.statement: Godrej Reserve project has all approvals in place, no notice received from government agencies
items.quote: On Reserve, we have not received any notice from any government agency. There has been, of course, as was reported a little bit of to and fro between these agencies. As of now, the project continues in full swing, we are in full compliance with all the laws, we have all our approvals in place.

items.statement: Election-related approval delays possible in Mumbai and Pune, but 80% of near-term approvals likely to come through
items.quote: Yes, there is always going to be that risk, but it seems very likely that these should come in, more or less 80% of these will come in.

items.statement: Real estate cycles will cool off within 4-5 years, need to be agile on business development and capital strategy
items.quote: Within that, of course, there will continue to be real estate cycles. We're currently in probably the early to mid-stages of an up-cycle. But within the 4-, 5-year timeline you indicated, it's quite likely that the cycle will cool off and start moving in the other direction.

items.statement: Plotted developments will remain minority part of business, not exceeding 10-15% of topline
items.quote: I don't think so in the very near term, we see this from a top line going beyond 10% to 15%. But yes, plotted also giv es you a great opportunity to, one, address the market need, it's very quick turnaround and profit recognition is also a little faster

items.statement: Q1 FY25 footfall fell 9% YoY to 10.02 lakh due to heat wave, water shortage, election disruptions and post-COVID discretionary spending slowdown
items.quote: Footfall for the quarter were mainly affected by an unprecedented heat wave, water shortages and disruptions related to election activities, especially in our key markets like Bangalore and Kochi, leading to the decline.

items.statement: Management expects to claw back Q1 footfall loss over next 2-3 quarters, targeting similar or slightly better full-year footfall vs prior year
items.quote: The footfall growth this year because we've lost some footfall in the Q1, it will be -- we will try to kind of make up for the loss in the next 2 to 3 quarters and we might end up in a similar kind of footfall number to the previous year or maybe slight improvement also, but it's hard to predict at this point.

items.statement: ARPU growth for FY25 likely 5-6% vs earlier 10-12% target due to potential discounting to drive footfall
items.quote: We may not get 10%, 12%, you may get like 5%, 6% ARPU.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 54%, down 1,000 bps YoY; adjusted EBITDA margin higher after excluding ESOP and Bhubaneswar launch costs
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the quarter stood at 54%, degrow by 1,000 basis points on Y-o-Y basis.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain historical EBITDA margin levels quarter-on-quarter, with some shifts due to new park ramp-up
items.quote: You can just take the previous history, we try to maintain with the same levels on a quarter-on-quarter basis. But quarter-to-quarter, there will be some shift in the EBITDA margins as well as in the PAT margins.

items.statement: Chennai park budget unchanged at ~INR500 crore; opening delayed to Dec 2025 or Jan 2026 from earlier June 2025 target
items.quote: No further changes. And the timelines are also intact? Arun Chittilappilly: Timelines, there is some delay. We were supposed to open in June '25, but I think that will get delayed to about December '25 or maybe Jan '26, something like that

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park (4th park) commenced operations on 50 acres; Chennai park (5th) under construction targeting Dec 2025/Jan 2026 opening
items.quote: I'm also excited to announce that we have officially commenced operations at our fourth park in Bhubaneswar. This has -- this remarkable new destination stands over 50 acres.

items.statement: Board approved fundraising for 7-8 year expansion; planning 5 additional parks beyond current 4 operating + 1 under construction
items.quote: We are planning to add up another 5 parks into the equity presently, we have about 4 parks operating and then 1 park is under construction, which is Chennai. And then additionally, 5 more locations, we are in a discussion at various stages with various state governments.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park ARPU ~INR1,300 (35% non-ticket) vs earlier INR800-1,000 estimate; footfall trending 130% of internal target for first 38 days
items.quote: As of now, we are trending about 130% of footfalls in Odisha, but again, like I said, the first year is very difficult for us to predict. So it could go up and down. As of now, we are above this thing. Our ARPU is also higher. I think we are close to, what was it? Saji K. Louiz: Arun Chittilappilly: INR1,300 is our ARPU

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park targets ~4.5 lakh footfall in Year 1, double-digit growth for 2-3 years, reaching 7-8 lakh in 4-5 years
items.quote: Yes, we are expecting footfalls of roughly about 4.5 lakhs for the first year. And it should grow in double digits for the first 2 to 3 years. It should get to about 7-8 lakh visitors in about 4 or 5 years.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 ARPU grew 3% YoY to INR1,680 driven by non-ticket revenue; ticket price growth muted due to promotional offers to offset heat wave footfall loss
items.quote: Our ARPU for the quarter stood at INR1,680, a growth of 3% Y -o-Y. The increase in ARPU was driven by mostly through non -ticket revenue. This encouraging response from walk -in groups and all aspects of our customer base. The ticket prices were slightly muted -- growth was muted mainly because we had to run a lot of extra offers to try and get back some of the footfalls

items.statement: Repeat customer rate ~50% across mature parks
items.quote: It is roughly 50% for us.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park operational for 38 days in Q1: revenue INR9 cr, EBITDA ~INR85 lakh (near breakeven); total expenses INR11 cr including INR3.6 cr marketing launch spend and INR3 cr depreciation
items.quote: So the Bhubaneswar Park, we closed the total revenue of about INR9 crores and then our EBITDA from this park alone, which is about -- almost like a breakeven, about some INR85 lakh is the total EBITDA from this part separately.

items.statement: Board approved fundraising (equity/debt) to support 7-8 year expansion plan covering 5 new parks beyond current pipeline
items.quote: As part of our expansion strategy, the Board has also given us approval to explore fundraising options to support our project for the next 7-8 years.

items.statement: Competitive advantage: higher-calibre rides/attractions at lower cost; differentiated as full amusement park (not just water park) offering better value proposition
items.quote: I think we will be able to give a much better experience, the kind of ride and attractions we have will be of a higher calibre and we'll be at -- come at a lower cost also. So I think -- also, we are not just an amusement park. We have -- sorry, we are not just a water park, we are an amusement park.

items.statement: Bhubaneswar park created ~450 new jobs (mostly semi-skilled), already filled, benefiting local community
items.quote: This new development is set to create approximately 450 new jobs, which we have already filled and particularly within the semi -skilled sector.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 25% over FY24 revenue of INR3,300 crores
items.quote: As of now, guidance continues to be a 25% growth over last year's revenue.

items.statement: Order inflow target of INR4,500-5,000 crores for FY25
items.quote: Overall, in the year, if you ask me, our aspiration is that we should secure anywhere between INR4,500 crores to INR5,000 crores of orders this year.

items.statement: Consolidated margin aspiration to reach 11-12% in next few years from current sub-10%
items.quote: See, definitely, long term, we do have an aspiration that as a -- consolidated in the company, we must move beyond 10% margin. Currently, we are at below 10% margin for the company. And certainly, we think that there is an opportunity -- a very clear opportunit y for us to move into the 11%, 12% consolidated basis for the company in the next few

items.statement: Interest cost as percentage of revenue target below 4.5%
items.quote: Our aspiration is to go below 4.5%.

items.statement: Polymer business target INR1,000 crores revenue in 2-3 years with double-digit margins
items.quote: So we think once we are closer to INR1,000 crores kind of a number, you will -- you can expect a double-digit kind of margin performance in the...

items.statement: Order book at INR5,844 crores, 2.1x FY24 Engineering and Infra sales, visibility for 2-3 years
items.quote: Our current order book stands at a high level of INR5,844 crores, well diversified across sectors and segments. With an order book to Engineering and Intra-segment sales ratio of 2.1x FY '24 sales, we have revenue visibility for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 order inflow of INR765 crores from domestic and export markets
items.quote: During the quarter, company secured significant sized domestic contract from PGCIL and SEB and export markets in Middle East and Africa, contributing to a total inflow of over INR765 crores.

items.statement: Bidding pipeline at all-time high of INR18,000 crores
items.quote: The tender pipeline remains weak with the current bidding pipeline at an all-time high of INR18,000 crores, reflecting strong opportunities in both domestic and international markets.

items.statement: Order win ratio averages 25% of bidding pipeline
items.quote: On an average, we have been able to secu re about 25% of the order pipeline -- or the bidding pipeline and being able to convert 25% into actual contracts

items.statement: Strong T&D demand driven by rising power demand and renewable energy investments globally
items.quote: There are basically -- there are 2, 3 changes that h ave happened. Power demand has also taken a very good uptick, peak power demand, as you must have noticed, is -- has been rising consistently in India. And the second thing, what has been happening is that there is a lot of stress on renewable power

items.statement: Telecom demand consistent, BSNL network expansion driving opportunities
items.quote: Government is very focused on enhancing BSNL network coverage. So I would say that yes, there will be plenty of telecom opportunities for us in the future.

items.statement: Engineering segment EBITDA margin at 11% in Q1 FY25, consistent 11-12% range maintained
items.quote: The Engineering segment EBITDA margin for the quarter stood at 11%. We have c locked the desired margin range of 11% to 12% now for the past many quarters

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 9.6% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The net revenue for the quarter stood at INR1,092 crores against INR555 crores. The segmental revenue breakup are as f ollows: Engineering, INR829 crores, up by 99%; Infra segment, INR168 crores, up by 1,600%; and Polymers INR95 crores down by 26%. The company's engineering export sales almost doubled reaching INR251 crores against INR127 crores and constituted 30% of overall Engineering segment r

items.statement: Capex of INR200+ crores to expand capacity by 75,000 tonnes (25% increase) to 300,000 tonnes, expected incremental revenue INR800-1,000 crores
items.quote: Only the capacity increase because the overall capex will go towards enhancing our other services capability also and as well as our overall debottlenecking of the plant. So I would say that this capex, which we are doing presently will lead to additional revenue of about INR800 crores to INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Current capacity 300,000 tonnes/year, utilization 70% last year, expected 90% this year
items.quote: Currently, our capacity, which is about 300,000 tonnes a year. Last year, we were at roughly about 70% utilization. This year, we expect to be about 90% utilization.

items.statement: Engineering contracts use IEEMA formula for raw material pass-through (steel, zinc, labor); Polymer prices are pass-through
items.quote: On the Polymer front, it's generally pass-through. So whatever there is an increase, we pass it to the market. On the engineering front, it's a combination of a fixed price contract as well as variable price contra ct. So there is an I EEMA driven formula, which derives what benefit needs to be paid. So that takes into consideration all the zinc -- raw material steel as well as the labor price

items.statement: Engineering exports doubled to INR251 crores (30% of Engineering revenue); order book export share 14%
items.quote: The company's engineering export sales almost doubled reaching INR251 crores against INR127 crores and constituted 30% of overall Engineering segment revenue.

items.statement: India-Australia FTA removed 4% duty on products; RoDTEP provides 1% export benefit
items.quote: I believe the duty was about 4% earlier.

items.statement: Work with 200-250 global EPC contractors, repeat business across geographies
items.quote: We work globally with about 200 to 250 global EPC contractors. And obviously, we do a lot of repeat business with a lot of them.

items.statement: 8-10 manufacturers in India; limited competition at 765/800kV; Turkish and Chinese players dominant in North America
items.quote: In our segment, we have competition from about 8 to 10 manufacturers.

items.statement: Qualified for highest voltage EPC projects (765/800kV) with limited competition
items.quote: Our qualification to undertake EPC project at the highest voltage level of 765 and 800 KV give us a strong advantage as there is very limited competition at this level.

items.statement: Debt comfortable, mostly working capital; rights issue INR50 crores received, balance planned this year to reduce debt
items.quote: we have recently don e a rights issue to boost the working capital -- growing working capital requirements of the company. We have already secured the first tranche of the right issue payment, about INR50 crores. And for the crores also, we do have a plan to take it -- to call for the balance money in this financial year itself. So this will go towards the reduction of overall debt

items.statement: Moderate debt growth expected in line with top line due to capex and working capital expansion
items.quote: In terms of the overall debt number, there may be some increase, because we are in a capex mode now, and we have taken up a capex of INR200 crores plus this year to enhance capacity. And also the working capital, there may be some expansion as the growth comes. So again, you can expect some moderate growth in the overall debt number in line with the overall top line of the company.

items.statement: International marketing team of 30-40 people across 6-7 countries, plus representatives in 70-80 active markets
items.quote: We have sales and marketing people in almost about 6 to 7 countries right now, which are Skipper employees. And also, we work with a lot of representatives and other associates in various markets in close to about 70 to 80 active markets for us.

items.statement: Polymer volumes 8,000 tonnes in Q1 FY25 (down 10% YoY), retail sales up 20%
items.quote: The volumes that we have done in this quarter is about 8,000 tonnes.

items.statement: Polymer FY24 revenue INR450 crores
items.quote: So last year, we did almost about INR450 crores.

items.statement: No significant replacement demand currently; demand driven by new renewable infrastructure
items.quote: Currently, we are not -- we are seeing most of our demand coming from new infrastructure build only and not really replacement build.

items.statement: Confident of profitable revenue growth >25% for next 2 financial years
items.quote: We are confident of delivering profitable revenue growth with a consistent margin in the current year and expect to gross revenue growth in excess of 25% each year for the next 2 financial years on back of fu nding Engineering and Infra contracts, an improvement in Polymer segment performance

items.statement: Margin expansion expected from Q3 FY25 in staffing segment; consistent profit improvement from Q2 FY25
items.quote: This, coupled with economies of scale in general staffing business, helped us improve profits and expand margins from Q3 FY '25 in the staffing segment.

items.statement: Full-year EdTech profit projected to increase steeply due to new university sign-ups and student pipeline
items.quote: However, on a full year basis, we are projecting a steep increase in EdTech profit, given the sign-up of new universities and student pipeline.

items.statement: General staffing net addition of 15,450+ associates in Q1 FY25, highest in 10 quarters
items.quote: During this quarter, we witnessed notable progress in general staffing with a net addition of nearly 15,450-plus associates, marking the highest number reported in the last 10 quarters.

items.statement: BFSI sector showing cautious revival in microfinancing, affordable housing, payment services; larger NBFCs flat
items.quote: We are now seeing a cautious revival as far as BFSI is concerned. So microfinancing, affordable housing and payment services are seeing a revival while larger NBFCs are still flattish.

items.statement: Telecom workforce growth over 36% YoY; consumer durables up 35% YoY; BFSI up 7% YoY
items.quote: Telecom has registered a year-on-year volume growth of over 36%, followed by consumer at 35% and BFSI was more muted 7%.

items.statement: Specialized staffing IT hiring demand higher than last year Q1 but driven by low bench strength, not new demand
items.quote: It is higher compared to last year quarter Q1. However, that's purely because these companies now have no or very low bench strength.

items.statement: GCCs contribute 55% of specialized staffing net revenue; semiconductor and ERD sectors increasing tech hiring
items.quote: GCCs actually have given us about 55% of our net revenue in the last quarter on the specialized staffing business.

items.statement: General staffing signed 43 new logos in Q1, 2/3 on variable markup models
items.quote: Our sales effort in Q1 has resulted in 43 new logo sign -ups, primarily in the consumer, financial services and manufacturing segment. 2/3 of our clients signed on available models.

items.statement: Degree Apprenticeship added 32 new logos in Q1; 13% new logos and 22% existing customers added learning component
items.quote: And in Q1, we were able to add 32 new logos into the apprenticeship program. Now learning was successfully embedded both into the new logos as well as expansion of our current logos as well.

items.statement: Specialized staffing added 13 new logos, 7 large strategic accounts; strong sales pipeline for rest of fiscal year
items.quote: We've added 13 new logos. Out of it, about 7 of them are large and strategic accounts. Our sales pipeline continues to be strong, and we expect this momentum to continue for the rest of this fiscal year.

items.statement: Group EBITDA declined in Q1 due to core employee appraisal (INR4.5 cr), EdTech seasonality (INR8 cr), NEEM final leg (INR2 cr)
items.quote: Overall, on a Q -o-Q basis, the 3 items that have impacted the group EBITDA are: one, core employee appraisal of INR4.5 crores; two, EdTech seasonality of about INR8 crores; and three, NEEM final leg of INR2 crores impact.

items.statement: General staffing PAPM flat at INR679 in Q1; 75% of business still on fixed markup limiting gross margin improvement
items.quote: Yes, we are currently at INR679 of PAPM for this quarter, which is almost same as last quarter.

items.statement: DA business PAPM: INR300-350 for administration, INR400-500 additional for education linkage; INR100 goes to PLSU
items.quote: So on a broader basis, Krunal, I think about INR300, INR350 is for the regular administration purpose and anywhere between INR400 to INR500 per month for the education linkage over and above the INR300.

items.statement: Advanced stage discussions for M&A in HR Tech, small ticket deals under INR50 cr, profit accretive
items.quote: From a capital allocation perspective, we are at an advanced stage of discussions with a couple of M&A opportunities under the HR Tech business. These opportunities provide us with the required capabilities and scale to penetrate into HCM market. These are of small ticket size deals with less than INR50 crores exposure and are profit accretive.

items.statement: General staffing FTE improved 2% to 379 including DA; digital transformation improving operational efficiency
items.quote: Our FTE has improved by 2% to 379, including the degree apprentice business, owing to a 6% increase in associate headcount in Q1. Our digital transformation efforts have yielded significant improvements in operational efficiency, allowing us to support an expanded customer base with our current workforce.

items.statement: Salary inflation impacting gross margin percentage despite variable markup growth; 75% of staffing business on fixed markup
items.quote: That's right, Dhvani, because with the consistent increase in associate salaries, the salary inflation is impacting the gross margin as a percentage. So while the incremental growth is happening mostly on variable markup model, given the large base that is on fixed markup, almost 75% of our business is still on fixed markup model, that's kind of impacting the gross margin percentages.

items.statement: DA business shifting to learning-embedded model: 60% of Q1 additions had learning component customers willing to pay more
items.quote: And the good thing is that we saw an expansion in the PAPM numbers as well. And that is because primarily 60% of these additions came in with a component of learning where the customers were willing to pay more towards the education initiative.

items.statement: Specialized staffing exiting low-margin mandates: 5% sequential headcount drop, 17% YoY drop, but revenue up 4% YoY
items.quote: We constantly exited few low -margin mandates, which has resulted in a 5% sequential headcount drop and a 17% year-on-year drop. However, our revenue has increased by 4% year-on-year and decreased 1% sequentially as we focus on replacing the low-margin mandates with higher margin and higher -value mandates.

items.statement: General staffing large/medium accounts show no attrition; smaller accounts 25-30% churn
items.quote: So on an average, some of the -- I mean, in the large to medium accounts, we don't lose any. So they have kind of -- we have not had any loss over the past few quarters. Typically, there's no attrition there. The smaller accounts typically which are in the single to double-digit numbers is where the churn happens either because there's no business requirements or numbers have kind of had a natural

items.statement: Government sent 180,000 notices to companies for apprenticeship non-compliance; budget emphasizes skilling and employment
items.quote: As per the news article in Business Standard, there were 180,000 notices, which the government had sent to companies to adopt their apprenticeship scheme.

items.statement: Balance sheet metrics including receivables, DSO, working capital ratio, ROCE, debt ratios steadily maintained
items.quote: Balance sheet metrics like receivables, DSO, working capital ratio, ROCE, debt ratios are all steadily maintained.

items.statement: Free cash balance improved to INR439 cr as of June 30, 2024, due to INR115 cr TDS refund with full 80JJAA allowance
items.quote: Free cash balance has improved during the quarter, owing to TDS refund of INR115 crores received during this quarter with full allowance on our 80JJAA claims. Total cash balance stands at INR439 crores as of 30th June 2024.

items.statement: Core employee appraisal impact INR4.5 cr in Q1; no further core employee cost increases expected for rest of year
items.quote: Yes. The net increase in core employee costs sequentially is INR4.5 crores. Out of which, almost INR1.5 crores is into staffing segment. And as I called out earlier, for subsequent quarters, we are not expecting any further increase in costs, be it on core employee front or any other fixed costs for any other business.

items.statement: Budget scheme details awaited; immediate impact uncertain; DA scaling depends on government policy operationalization
items.quote: We still await the details to be notified around the various schemes that have been announced to make an exact call on the immediate and longer -term impact for business.

items.statement: General staffing revenue grew 8% QoQ, 22% YoY; group revenue grew 6% QoQ, 19% YoY
items.quote: In terms of revenue, we had an 8% quarter-on-quarter growth and 22% year-on-year, reflecting the positive momentum in our business.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit revenue growth for the portfolio and aims to expand profits faster than revenue growth.
items.quote: So overall, our ambit i on continues to grow in double -digit for the portfolio as a whole and expand our profits better than the revenue growth

items.statement: Consumer sentiment shows early signs of improvement; intense summer boosted cooling product sales but supply glitches limited upside.
items.quote: We are keenly watching consumer sentiments and the underlying demand scenario, which is showing some early signs of improvement.

items.statement: Standalone material margins improved to 31.3% YoY; EBIT margin ex-A&P was 14.9% (+1.6% YoY, +30bps QoQ); ECD EBIT ex-A&P 19.8% (+2.3% YoY); Lighting EBIT ex-A&P 11.3% (+20bps QoQ).
items.quote: Despite an increase in raw mater ial prices during the quarter, our standalone material margins improved to 31.3% versus 29.4% a year ago

items.statement: Solar pumps executed ₹21 crore in Q1; healthy pipeline being built but order book not disclosed.
items.quote: We executed orders worth about ₹21 crores in the quarter that went by. And in the meanwhile, we have been building up a pretty robust and healthy pipeline of further orders in this segment.

items.statement: No specific capacity expansion plans disclosed; strategic sourcing plan rolling out to control key value chain parts.
items.quote: None that we are in a position to disclose yet.

items.statement: Fans manufacturing roughly equally split between in-house and outsourcing; payback on in-house investments tends to be quick due to high asset turnover.
items.quote: Roughly, we are equally split for the in- house and outsourcing for fans a s a business

items.statement: Price increases of ~1.5% in fans taken mid-May; fourth consecutive quarter of hikes; further increases evaluated based on commodity basket.
items.quote: Overall, from a Q1 perspective, the price increase that we have taken in fans is about 1.5% and that has been taken around mid- May.

items.statement: Commodity prices (copper, aluminium, ABS) trended up in Q1; copper cooled recently but expected to move northwards.
items.quote: We have seen increase in copper prices, in aluminium and ABS, while copper, we have seen a little bit of cooling down in the recent past, but we do expect the trends i n future to move northwards

items.statement: Premium saliency in large domestic appliances improved to 25.6%; fan premiumisation moved from 17-18% to ~25% portfolio share targeting 40% in 3-4 years.
items.quote: Premium saliency of large domestic appliances also improved and was at 25.6%.

items.statement: Alternate channels grew 30% YoY to 17% of sales; e-commerce delivered ₹100 crore+ for fourth consecutive quarter (82% YoY growth).
items.quote: We remain focused on alternate channels, which have again grown at about 30% YoY. Now alternate channels comprise 17% of Crompton sales, whic h is up from about 16% last year

items.statement: Competitive intensity never abates; market share in fans estimated at 28-29% (up from 25-26%); BLDC fan position #2 targeting #1.
items.quote: Our broad estimate is that we are between 28 -29% market share in the business.

items.statement: Union Budget positive: 3 crore additional houses, solar duty exemptions, ₹11.11 trillion infra spend augur well for demand.
items.quote: Under the r ecently introduced union budget, the announcement of 3 crore additional houses in rural and urban regions is positive for durable products like ours

items.statement: ₹300 crore NCD paid in Q1; ₹300 crore outstanding from Butterfly acquisition to be repaid by July next year; company net cash positive.
items.quote: You are aware on the balance sheet side that we paid ₹300 crores towards NCDs that we had taken on for the acquisition of Butterfly. We still have ₹300 crores of debt left from that acquisition.

items.statement: No M&A planned; organic portfolio has enough headroom; cash to fund innovation, manufacturing, supply chain, digital.
items.quote: At the same point of time, it's not that we are looking at any M&As to grow the business if that's the other question that you have.

items.statement: Dividend payout consistent and improving; capital allocation prioritises strong dividend, debt reduction, and operational investments.
items.quote: Our dividend payment has been consistent and has been reasonably improving over a period of time, and we'll continue to focus on that.

items.statement: Butterfly CBO Swetha leading turnaround; Vector Consulting engagement work in progress.
items.quote: Swetha and team was first working to get that corrected. And as we get that completed, we would start seeing business growing from H2 onwards.

items.statement: Fans volume growth ~15% YoY (price-led growth limited); air cooler volume growth 68%; mixer grinder highest-ever June sales.
items.quote: In fact, our sales for air coolers were the highest it's ever been, and the volume growth in air cooler segment last quarter was 68%.

items.statement: Weather patterns unusual; supply chain glitches limited cooling product sales; commodity price volatility; regulatory headwinds persist.
items.quote: Weather patterns have been quite unusual, and while this created a spike in demand in this season, it's of course difficult to see how this pans out.

items.statement: Crompton among top 10 in MSCI Emerging Markets Small Cap SRI ESG Universal Select Index; product carbon footprint assessment started.
items.quote: Crompton is one of the only two Indian companies, which is a constituent of the top 10 MSCI Emerging Markets Small Cap SRI ESG Universal Select Index.

items.statement: Expect margins to improve from Q2 onwards as OAM and GTS businesses recover from seasonal slowdown
items.quote: We expect margins to improve as these businesses recover from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Expect to recover 20 basis points in WFM margins as IT staffing opens up in subsequent quarters
items.quote: So as we move forward we will definitely recover some basis points about 20 basis points back in margins because IT staffing is opening up and we are seeing green shoots as the mandates have gone up.

items.statement: Expect to return to 4% margin levels by end of Q2 or early Q3 FY25
items.period: end of quarter two or early quarter three
