items.quote: Overall credit cost for the year will be in the range of 20 to 30 bps. To that extent, because of 1 or 2 quarters, it has not really altered the overall story.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 NIM at 4.36% impacted by 40 bps from penal charges reclassification and interest reversals from slippages
items.quote: Net interest margin w as 4.36% for the quarter, impacted by higher cost of funds and regulatory guidance on penal charges

items.statement: Normalized gross yield on advances expected at 11.6%-11.8% from Q2 onwards after removing one-off impacts
items.quote: Generally it has been in the range of 11.6% -11.8% at an overall portfolio level. We do not see that there will be any major change in the mix of the portfolio in quarter or the full year also.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 slippages of Rs 103 crores driven by SME, corporate, agri and MFI; largest single slippage Rs 33 crores
items.quote: I think the overall slippage for the quarter as in the investor presentation is about Rs. 100 odd crores. Some slippages happened in the Agri and MFI portfolio a s well

items.statement: Gross NPA 1.69%, Net NPA 0.68%, PCR 82.53%; accelerated provisioning policy continued with Rs 182 cr buffer
items.quote: Gross NPA ratio was at 1.69%. Net NPA ratio was at 0.68% and prov ision coverage ratio at 82.53%. We are continuing with the accelerated NPA provisioning po licy of providing higher than RBI requirements and are holding the contingency provisions intact

items.statement: Elevated slippages in last two quarters seen as one-off; expect normalization from Q2 with recoveries from written-off accounts picking up
items.quote: If we go back couple of quarters, our slippage ratio was less than 1% on an annualized basis. Only for the last two quarters, we have seen elevated slippages and going forward, we do not expect slippages at these levels.

items.statement: Net advances grew 18% YoY vs industry 14%; gold loans grew 24% YoY; SME grew 28% YoY with 35% full-year target
items.quote: We had a net advance growth of 18% year- on-year, whereas industry has grown at about 14% year-on-year. Gold portfolio registered a growth of 24% year-on-year.

items.statement: Corporate banking book to be flat YoY in FY25 due to portfolio rejig; steady growth expected from FY26
items.quote: year will be kind of a complete rejig of the corporate banking portfolio and probably on the corporate b anking book, we will be flat CSB Bank July 29, 2024 as compared to last year

items.statement: Deposits grew 22% YoY vs industry 11%; CASA ratio 24.9%; bulk deposits 25-26% of total
items.quote: Deposit growth has been 22% ye ar-on-year as against the industry growth of around 11%. The CASA ratio stands at 24.9

items.statement: Cost of funds elevated but managed via refinance, FCY borrowings (Rs 1000 cr in 12 months), CDs (Rs 900 cr); SA cost ~3%
items.quote: Our overall cost of SA is in the range of 3%. These measures help us in maintaining our overall cost of funds.

items.statement: Added 15 branches in Q1 (794 total); moderate branch expansion to continue in FY25 for pan-India presence
items.quote: During this quarter, we have added 15 branches. We will continue with our branch expansion plans on a moderate scale this financial year.

items.statement: CD ratio at 83.89%; comfort level maintained at 85% with below 90% intent
items.quote: We are currently at a CD ratio of 83.89%. Our guidance was also earlier that we are comfortable up to 85% of the CD ratio and we will continue with that guidance.

items.statement: LCR average 118% in Q1; new RBI guidelines expected ~10% impact from April 2025; 3 quarters to adjust
items.quote: For the quarter, our average LCR was about 118%. The guideline s, of course, will apply to the entire industry as well as to us, but ballpark at least 10% impact will be there on the LCR

items.statement: CAR 23.61%, Tier-1 22.23%; RWA to exposure 43-44%; book value Rs 217, EPS Rs 26.2, ROE 12.69%
items.quote: Our capital adequacy ratio continues to be strong at 23.61% with a tier one ratio of 22.23%. We have a very low proportion of risk-weighted assets compared to the industry.

items.statement: Fee income contributing 1.92% of average assets; robust fee performance over last 5 quarters
items.quote: Even for this quarter, f ee is contributing at almost 1.92% of my average assets, which is very good number to have

items.statement: Staff cost flat YoY; OPEX elevated due to branch additions (76 in FY24, 15 in Q1), tech investments, and business-linked costs
items.quote: Actually, as compared to Q1 of FY24, staff cost is almost flat.

items.statement: Cost-to-income, GNPA, NNPA, credit cost peaked in Q1; expect improvement from Q2 with NIM >4.5% and ROA >1.5%
items.quote: We believe that the cost to income, GNPA, NNPA and credit cost ratios have peaked out as of now and net interest margin will go back to the trajectory upwards of 4.5% and ROA upwards of 1.5% from Quarter 2 onwards.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue grew ~27% YoY in Q1 FY25; India standalone revenue grew ~29% YoY with strong SSSG across all markets despite gold price volatility.
items.quote: The quarter was a fantastic one, and we recorded consolidated revenue growth of around 27% and stand -alone India revenue grew by around 29%.

items.statement: Non-South market revenue share increased to 49% from 44% in prior year.
items.quote: Our share of revenue from the non -South market is now at 49%, up from 44% in the prior year.

items.statement: Share of new customers exceeded 35% in Q1 FY25; studded jewelry share drove marginal gross margin improvement at showroom level.
items.quote: We continue to see encouraging trends around the share of new customers, which was in excess of 35% for the recently concluded quarter.

items.statement: Gross margins at showroom level improved marginally due to higher studded jewelry share in both South and non-South markets.
items.quote: Gross margins at the showroom level improved marginally, driven largely by higher share of studded jewelry in both South and non -South market.

items.statement: Signed documentation to increase stake in Candere and convert it to a wholly-owned subsidiary; Candere added 13 showrooms in FY25 so far out of targeted 50.
items.quote: We have signed documentation to increase our stake in the business and convert Candere to a wholly-owned subsidiary of Kalyan Jewellers India Limited. Candere has added 13 showrooms in the financial year so far out of the targeted 50 showrooms during the year.

items.statement: Plan to convert four Middle East showrooms to franchise in Q2 FY25 and use proceeds to reduce regional debt; first US showroom expected before Diwali.
items.quote: We plan to convert four showrooms in the region to franchise once during the ongoing quarter and utilize the proceeds to reduce the debt in the region. The first showroom in the U.S. is expected to be launched before Diwali.

items.statement: Opened 5 Kalyan and 2 Candere showrooms in July; on track to launch 35 more Kalyan and 20 more Candere showrooms before Diwali.
items.quote: During the month of July, we opened five Kalyan and two Candere showrooms and are on track to launch another 35 Kalyan and 20 Candere showrooms before Diwali.

items.statement: Post customs duty cut in late July, last 10 days saw stronger SSSG than Q1, driven by customers preponing purchases; demand surge expected to last 1-2 weeks.
items.quote: But post the duty cut, again, when the price comes down by 7%, 8% customers who were waiting would have come in immediately. So the last 10 days have been very good, especially weekends. And it is stronger than Q1 in terms of SSG.

items.statement: Revenue per showroom declining as franchisee stores (INR 50 cr revenue/store) dilute owned store average (INR 90+ cr); trend to continue as more franchise stores added.
items.quote: Our own showrooms are at INR 90 crores plus when it comes to per showroom revenue. But when you come to franchisee new stores, the revenue will be only in the range of INR50 crores. So the more number of new showrooms you open, the revenue per showroom will come down.

items.statement: Interest cost includes lease interest (Ind AS 116) which rises with store additions; excluding lease interest, interest cost fell INR 3-4 cr QoQ and INR 11 cr YoY.
items.quote: So with regard to interest cost, the number includes lease interest, which definitely will go up as we increase number of showrooms, if you remove lease interest, you can say Q-o-Q it has come down by INR 3 crores to INR 4 crores. And year-on-year, it has come down by INR 11 crores.

items.statement: Franchisee capex model: first 30-35 of 80 FY25 showrooms funded by Kalyan, rest by franchisees; franchise model adds ~0.25% gross margin increment.
items.quote: The first 30, 35 showrooms will be in our old model wherein the capex will be put by Kalyan. The rest of the showrooms, the franchisee partners will put the capex fit out also. So , that is the plan. And margin, as I indicated in the past, there will be an increment of, say, 0.25% on the gross level.

items.statement: No meaningful demand for lab-grown diamonds at stores; not promoting due to price instability risk to brand trust; monitoring closely.
items.quote: Yes, lab-grown, we have not seen any demand so far in the store level. There is no -- it's like literally 0 demand at our store level. Customer inquiry is very minimalistic and we are surely looking into what is happening on ground.

items.statement: New large competitor entry (INR 5,000 cr investment) not an immediate threat; organized segment has room for 3-4 more players; Kalyan's hyper-local strategy takes years to replicate.
items.quote: It has to be -- even now we are talking the 35%, 40% of organized segment. So there are -- there is an easy vacuum or easy space for at least three or four more players in the sector. That is the first thing which we have to understand.

items.statement: Customs duty cut helps organized players by pushing unorganized to invoice-based buying and allowing Kalyan to increase inventory volumes without extra investment as gold prices fall.
items.quote: So this has been the case over the last two, three years. But now if you see, we are on the other side, wherein they will maintain the same volume at the store. We will be able to increase the volume at the store, meaning inventory level by volume can be increased without in further investment, which we think that is going to help to gain more market share for an organized player.

items.statement: Two new procurement centers opened in Bihar and UP with minimal capex; focused on artisan/vendor network integration rather than capital investment.
items.quote: Yes. The capex will be very minimal. So it's not about capex. It's more about networking of local artisans and what you call vendor ecosystem, more than a capex. So majorly, the new offices were started in regions where we expanded heavily like Bihar and UP.

items.statement: MyKalyan staff declined as franchisees opted for local marketing initially; now reverting to MyKalyan as stores mature, expecting ramp-up in employees.
items.quote: But now it is the franchisees call whether they need a MyKalyan or local marketing. So we give them two options, whether they want local marketing to be done in that region, or they want MyKalyan infrastructure. So as we speak now, people have started coming back because it's all one year, 1.5 year showroom, almost a year done.

items.statement: Middle East revenue grew 16% YoY, SSSG 10%, PAT grew 11%; FOCO model and rising interest rates pressured margins; debt reduction via franchise conversions to improve finance cost.
items.quote: Revenue in the Middle East for the just-concluded quarter came in at about INR 811 crores versus INR 700 crores when compared to the corresponding quarter of the previous year and EBITDA in the Middle East came in about INR 64 crores versus INR 55 crores for the same period in the previous year.

items.statement: No debt reduction in Q1 FY25 in India or Middle East; India cash balance increased to ~INR 75 crores; Middle East conversions to start in Q2.
items.quote: So India, we are not reduced, but the cash balance has been increased to around INR75 crores, but we have not reduced any debt in Q1 in India and Middle East because Middle East we have not converted any showroom in Q1.

items.statement: Middle East FOCO showrooms reduce gross margins vs owned stores; finance cost pressure from rising rates to ease as conversions proceed and rate base normalizes.
items.quote: And again, FOCO, when you do FOCO showrooms, the margins will come down. And surely, that will have an impact on the gross margin. Ok ay. And interest, if you look at actually, the interest rates have been going up last year. So next year, that will be the base, right? So then again, we will not have this kind of issue is what we feel

items.statement: No formal revenue guidance for FY25-26; targeting SSSG and revenue growth in current range supported by 80 store expansion plan and stronger July SSSG.
items.quote: I will not be able to give a guidance, but what we will say is that you know the store expansion plan, which we have 80 showrooms. SSSG for the year 2, year three are usually higher than insurance. And again, July if you see, the SSSGs are even stronger than in Q1, okay? So all put together, I think this will be the range where we need to target for our SSSG and for our revenue growth.

items.statement: Studded jewelry mix expected to settle in mid-to-late 20s% for next few quarters as 80 new FY25 showrooms are predominantly in non-South tier 2/3 markets with lower studded ratio.
items.quote: So I think this will settle down in this level for some time because the expansion now, the 80 showrooms which we are opening in this financial year are predominantly in non-South tier two, tier three markets where studded ratio cannot be like tier 1 or Metro.

items.statement: Post-duty-cut demand surge (wedding + discretionary) seen as temporary, likely lasting only 1-2 weeks as customers preponed purchases.
items.quote: And we also believe that it cannot last too long. It can be maybe one week, 10 days or 15 days. That is what we also think will be the case.

items.statement: Confident of full-year margin expansion despite Q1 miss; will reassess in 2 quarters; Q2 operating leverage expected to improve with revenue growth.
items.quote: If you ask me, I am still confident of margin expansion for the financial year, that's why I'm asking for a two quarter wait to decide whether we should forecast numbers.

items.statement: Targets INR25,000 crores top line by 2026-27 with sustainable EBITDA margins in line with current levels
items.quote: And we expect that, you know, in next by 2026, 2027, we should be able to do a top line of around INR25,000 crores.

items.statement: Expects CAGR of more than 30% to continue for next four to five years
items.quote: if you see the past also, we are going with meet a CAGR of more than 30%, and we hope so that we will continue with this run rate in the next four to five years.

items.statement: Incurred INR4,948 crores capex till Q1 FY25, 40% of INR10,025 crores three-year plan; INR308 crores spent in Q1
items.quote: We have incurred a capex cost of INR4,948 crores till first quarter of the current financial year, which accounted a more than 40% of the total capex exercise to the tune of INR10,025 crores in the last three years

items.statement: Targets INR2,000 crores capex in FY25, INR2,000 crores in FY26, balance in FY27
items.quote: We are targeting INR2,000 crores, which will be incurred in the current financial year and INR2,000 in the next financial year and balance will be in the financial year 2026-2027.

items.statement: INR1,160 crores capex over next three years to increase stainless steel manufacturing via primary route
items.quote: We have a capex of INR1,160 crores spend over next three years to be increased the stainless-steel manufacturing facility through the primary route

items.statement: Commissioned 0.15 mt DRI and 20 MW captive power at Ram Sarup Kharagpur; blast furnace at Jamuria expected in 45-60 days, Kharagpur by Dec 24, sinter plant by Sep 24
items.quote: We had further 12 capex line items to be announced in current financial year, comprising of Coke Oven plant with a capacity of 0.45 million tons, which light up is already been done. The blast furnace which will be implemented in Jamuria. The heat are expected shortly and the commercial production expected to be start in next 45 to 60 days. The blast furnace at Kharagpur, the project expected to b

items.statement: Plans to double aluminium foil capacity; setting up foil stock plant for backward integration
items.quote: We are going to double the capacity of the foil in the Aluminium since the demand is very good, and to integrate the complete business from the supply chain side, we are setting up a foil stock plant where we will be making our own foil stock

items.statement: Targets 0.7-0.8 mt stainless steel capacity in next 3-4 years with flat product focus
items.quote: in next three to four years, which should be close to 0.7 to 0.8 million tons of stainless steel

items.statement: DI pipe plant at Ram Sarup shifted from Jamuria, targeting commissioning in FY26
items.quote: this plant is going to be commissioned in FY'26 because we have shifted this plant from the existing Jamuria plant to the Ram Sarup

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA INR488 crores, up 18% YoY; EBITDA margin 13.5%
items.quote: The company has been able to book an EBITDA of INR488 crores and which is increase of 18% over the current over the quarter one of the last financial year and the EBITDA margin of the current financial year was 13.5%

items.statement: Captive power at 82% of requirement, cost INR2.37/kWh; blended power cost INR3.12/kWh
items.quote: Therefore, our total power requirement, we are sourcing 82% of the total power requirement from our captive sources with a lowest cost of INR2.37 per kilowatt, which will improve our margins as well. Therefore, we are achieving, or we are maintaining our sustainable margin quarter-on-quarter basis, while average power cost, including the grid power, our total power cost is approximately INR3.12 pe

items.statement: Stainless steel EBITDA per ton around INR8,000 in Q1
items.quote: As far as EBITDA per ton is concerned and that is in the case of Stainless Steel for the quarter, it is around INR8,000 per ton.

items.statement: Aluminium foil utilization 80-85%, exporting 55% to US and Europe; stainless steel demand growing 18-20% YoY
items.quote: Today our utilization is more than 80, 85% in the Aluminium. And we are – we should be very proud to know that more than 55% we are exporting to the best of the country.

items.statement: Construction activity slow due to monsoon but decent overall; expects post-Diwali pricing equal to or better than Q1
items.quote: Currently I would say it is decent and because of the monsoon side and all, the construction activity is a little slow but more or less, I would say it is not bad.

items.statement: Value-added products contribution to rise to 80% of revenue in 5 years from >50% currently
items.quote: The contribution from the value-added product in our revenue is likely to move up to 80% of our revenue in next five years from the present contribution of more than 50% to the revenue presently.

items.statement: Stainless steel products accepted by large EPC contractors like Ashoka Buildcon and LNG
items.quote: Our company has been able to stabilize the quality and product to this sector and our product is now well established and is being accepted by the largest EPC contractor like Ashoka Buildcon and LNG and many others.

items.statement: Signed MOU with top battery manufacturers for EV battery foil; samples approved, expecting full swing FY25-26
items.quote: We have already signed the MOU with the best of the battery manufacturers in the country, and we are expecting that they will be in full swing from FY'25-FY'26.

items.statement: Highest exporter of aluminium foil in India; >55% exported to US and Europe
items.quote: We have become the highest exporter of Aluminium foil in the country today and we have been able to develop the product fitment into numerous applications of our product, which is now given us the confidence to announce and enhance the further capacity with further capex for the metal for future.

items.statement: Debtor days 15-30, inventory days 70-90; sales mainly on advance or LC basis
items.quote: In Shyam Metalics Group the working capital Shyam Metalics and management is very prudent and the group focusing mainly on the selling, either on the advance or letter of credit. This is leading to our lower debtors and inventory period to the tune of 15 to 30 days and 70 to 90 days, respectively

items.statement: Net cash INR1,338 crores in Q1 FY25 vs INR1,514 crores in Q4 FY24; reinvests 70% of cash generation, retains 20%, returns 10% as dividend
items.quote: we have been consistently cash positive with a net cash of INR1,338 crores in quarter one of the current financial year, as against the positive of INR1,514 crores in last quarter of the last financial year

items.statement: Budget reduction in stamp duty for ferroalloy, nickel has marginal impact given business portfolio
items.quote: Not really, actually. For the very rare minerals and lithium and nickel is one of the components it will definitely make some betterment on this from the nickel front but with the kind of business portfolio it will have a very marginal support.

items.statement: Coal prices stable, abundant Indian coal supply; not dependent on coking coal volatility; iron ore prices corrected marginally
items.quote: We are in line, I think more or less the coal prices are very stable. I don't see this much changes. I'm talking as an overall seeing the scenario and all because the coal is available in abundance. And I don't see there is any kind of a challenge which will come up in the time to come from the coal stack.

items.statement: Captive power consumption to remain around 80% post-expansion
items.quote: So, lot of expansion is happening. You know, everywhere will be requiring powers and all and just finishing plant expansion, we are putting up an SMS will be and, you know, doubling the CRM capacity, which is going to be commissioned. So all these are in line maybe six months here and there, but everything is in line with the manifesto that we have to be more than 80% should be our captive.

items.statement: No aggressive acquisition plans; evaluating proposals but nothing attractive on board currently
items.quote: So, we keep on evaluating all the proposals. But you know, you wouldn't like to invest anything which has a the supply chain or the strategy part. But this is ongoing day in, day out. It's not no from my side, but we are not doing anything aggressive as well because I don't see anything very attractive as on date on the board where we see that, we are going very strong on that.

items.statement: C.S. Verma, ex-CMD of SAIL and NMDC, joined board as Independent Director
items.quote: We are pleased to have a blessing and the mentorship of Mr. C. S Verma, who has been a stalwart consented to join our board as an Independent Director. He was the ex CMD of SAIL, NMDC and the Chairman of International Coal Venture Limited.

items.statement: Net debt target of Rs 3,500-4,000 crore by March FY25 to enable expansion
items.quote: we are comfortable with the debt level anywhere between 3,500 to 4,000 crores. So, beyond that, we will have to fund our growth.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs 300-400 crore; FY26 capex ~Rs 900-1,000 crore including development capex
items.quote: this year, as I said in the previous call, 300 to 400 crores, that's the kind of ballpark number which we have.

items.statement: FY26 development capex ~Rs 700 crore plus Rs 200 crore sustaining capex
items.quote: we are looking at close to about 700-odd crores of development CAPEX or new factory CAPEX coming in FY '25. So, CAPEX could be the tune of ~900 to ~1000 crores next year.

items.statement: First expansion priority: second line at Chittoor plant (2-2.5 mt clinker) with split grinding unit
items.quote: Our initial first priority will be to expand in North/West, which will be an additional line Brownfield expansion coming in our Chittoor plant.

items.statement: East capacity sufficient for 2 years: 9.5 mt clinker and 19 mt cement
items.quote: we have got close to 9.5 mt of clinker and 19 mt of cement capacity in east and there is sufficient headroom for Nuvoco to grow in the East at least till two years from now.

items.statement: Project Bridge 2.0 on track to deliver Rs 50/ton annualized savings by FY25 end
items.quote: I think during the course of this year, we will be able to deliver Rs.50 per ton at a annualized level clearly.

items.statement: Blended fuel cost at 11-quarter low of Rs 1.57/Mcal; target Rs 1.50/Mcal
items.quote: The Company has reached the lowest blended fuel cost in the last 11-quarters at Rs.1.57 per Mcal.

items.statement: Headroom to reduce fuel cost to Rs 1.50/Mcal via higher WHR, linkage coal, AFR
items.quote: With improvement in AFR, increase WHR generation, maximizing linkage coal, there is good headroom to reduce this Rs.1.57 p er MCal to around Rs.1.50

items.statement: Cement prices under pressure; near-term outlook challenging; expect improvement post-monsoon
items.quote: Regarding industry prices, we believe that cement prices will remain under pressure and the near-term outlook appears challenging.

items.statement: Q1 volume 4.8 mt; soft demand due to elections, heat wave, early monsoon, SAP disruption
items.quote: We delivered a volume of 4.8 mt. Some part of volume moderation was on account of our internal program with respect to upgradation of SAP across the

items.statement: Demand recovery hinges on infrastructure and housing spend; expect pickup post-monsoon in Q3/Q4
items.quote: We believe recovery in demand hinges upon spending on infrastructure and housing.

items.statement: Premiumization at 40% of trade volumes in Q1, up from 37% previous period
items.quote: During the quarter under consideration, premiumization recorded a high of 40% of trade volumes, registering an increase from 37% in the prev ious period

items.statement: Trade mix at 73%; premiumization and trade-centric strategy supporting realization
items.quote: we are a trade-centric player, we are a Company with premiumization, those are two levers which worked for us - at 40% premiumization in 73% trade mix.

items.statement: Fuel mix: coal 42% (linkage 23%, non-linkage 18%, imported 1%), pet coke 49%, AFR 9%
items.quote: coal was 42% and in 42% linkage coal was 23% and non -linkage coal was 18%, a small bit of 1% of imported coal, pet coke came at 49% which w as 3% lower than Q4 and AFR slightly reduced, it should improve, AFR Q4 was 12%, we were 9% in. Q1

items.statement: Linkage coal rates trending Rs 1.4-1.45/Mcal; new linkages from Eastern, SECL, Western collieries signed
items.quote: all the new linkages for us have materialized now once from the Eastern collieries in Bengal, from southeastern collieries in Chhattisgarh and Western collieries from Maharashtra.

items.statement: Incentive income booked on realization basis from April 2024; Q1 revenue/EBITDA excludes incentives
items.quote: effective 1st April 2024 as a conservative accounting practice, we have decided to book the incentives income on realization basis. Accordingly, revenue and EBITDA for the quarter does not include any incentive income.

items.statement: Net debt Rs 4,358 crore at June 30; target below Rs 4,030 crore (March level) by March FY25
items.quote: in terms of our net debt, as we entered June 30th, was 4,358 crores.

items.statement: Q1 capex ~Rs 100 crore; balance FY25 capex Rs 200-300 crore for brownfield completion and sustenance
items.quote: in Q1, we have spent close to about 100 crores which was a little bit of the Brownfield projects which we spent in Q1. Other than balance three quarters, we will do about 200 to 300 crores.

items.statement: Railway siding at Sonadih expected Q2 FY25, Jajpur (Odisha) by Q3 FY25
items.quote: Project at Sonadih is expected to be completed by Q2 FY '25 and Odisha by Q3 FY'25.

items.statement: CO2 emissions 457 kg/ton cementitious in FY24; lowest in industry
items.quote: our audited figure for FY'24 stands at 457 Kg CO2 per ton of cementitious materials.

items.statement: Demand outlook uncertain; pricing not sustainable at current levels; government spend timing unclear
items.quote: I think the current pricing not only in East, in North and West of the regions, we don't participate, but in general, we operate in some parts of Central, East, North and parts of West. Pricing is not encouraging at all.

items.statement: SAP migration completed in Q1; caused ~6 days disruption in April; customer/vendor apps coming in 1-2 quarters
items.quote: During the quarter, we successfully completed the SAP upgradation across organization to facilitate the Company's digital transformation journey.

items.statement: Launched Concreto UNO (hydrophobic concrete) and Ecodure Thermal Insulated Concrete in RMX
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched two innovative products: first, Concreto UNO Concrete, which is India's first-ever hydrophobic concrete that repels water, setting a new benchmark in construction technology.

items.statement: Bihar premium growth ~18%; Jharkhand volume +3%; Odisha impacted by SAP; Bengal weak
items.quote: In Bihar, we have done quite okay in Q1. We have not seen a territory in Bihar. In fact, all our premium growth, Concreto growth is close to about 18% in Bihar and overall premium percentages happened in Bihar.

items.statement: Remain on track for 50 bps claims improvement and 50 bps expense improvement YoY
items.quote: No, we remain on track, Avinash. When we spoke to you about that in the end of June, we were aware of the situation and we are remaining on track as far as that particul ar commitment is concerned

items.quote: Coming to our Q1 FY '25 Performance for the three months ended June '24, our (Gross Written Premium) GWP grew at a rate of 18% to Rs. 3,476 crore compared to Rs. 2,949 crore during the same period last year.

Retail fresher premium and agent activation rate also grew in the mid-teens in Q1 FY '25. Coming to B anca, fresh business grew by 25% with an uptick in the partner count to 61. We expect the share of

items.statement: Wellness and prevention costs added 0.66% to claims ratio in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The preventive health check, telemedicine, OPD and wellness contribution in the claims ratio was 0.66% in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Claims management expense is 1% of GWP, stable YoY

items.statement: Market sentiments improving with new inquiries from key markets ahead of festive season
items.quote: Market sentiments are improving with new inquiries from key markets. As the festive season approaches, we are optimistic about a successful FY'25.

items.statement: Wamsutta brand acquisition completed for INR85 crores through internal accruals
items.quote: The successful acquisition of Wamsutta, the U.S. national brand, through internal accruals of INR85 crores, reinforces our global home textile vision.

items.statement: Licensed brands Fieldcrest & Waverly added during Q1 FY25
items.quote: And Fieldcrest & Waverly have been just added in order to complete the demographic and the existing consumer space and the customer segment.

items.statement: Major capex projects completed; future capex focused on renewable energy and maintenance
items.quote: Our major capex projects are completed, setting the stage for sustained growth. Moving forward, we will strategically invest in renewable energy and essential maintenance capex.

items.statement: Board to evaluate capacity expansion in FY27; land available at Bhilad to double capacity
items.quote: in FY'27, the Board will look at the capacity utilization and the business overall, and we'll take appropriate decisions. We are a debt -free company. So we have all the means to expand our capacity. And I have mentioned in my last call as well that in our Bhila d capacity, we have got appropriate land to double our capacity going forward

items.statement: Current capacity at 153 million meters; aim to utilize effectively
items.quote: When we put up on the drawing board our 153 million meters capacity, our endeavour is to see how we reach this number very quickly and sell this capacity very quickly.

items.statement: Logistics costs increased due to container availability and freight challenges; situation fluid
items.quote: During the quarter, we faced challenges on both the availability and the cost of the containers and the freight cost.

items.statement: Employee expenses increased by INR6 crores QoQ due to new talent for Wamsutta brand management
items.quote: And to correct one aspect, the employee expenditure, it has gone up by only INR6 crores between the 2 quarters. So we've peaked there now.

items.statement: Entered fashion, utility and institutional bedding segments with new fashion bedding unit
items.quote: Since entering key bedding segments, such as fashion, utility, and institutional bedding, supported with adequate brand strategy and capacity, it will help us significantly to improve our overall business growth.

items.statement: One sheet in every five sold in US is from Indo Count; adding new customers and geographies
items.quote: Now as a company, we are well-positioned. So one sheet in every five sheets sold in the U.S. is the market share which we enjoy.

items.statement: FTAs with Australia and UAE helping gain market share; UK FTA would be additional boost
items.quote: Even the FTAs in Australia and UAE had helped us to certain extent into growing our value proposition to the new customer base out there.

items.statement: Inventory levels increased to secure supply chain amid logistics volatility; cotton covered until October
items.quote: Because there are so many volatilities and headwinds on the logistics side, like container availability, the cost of the containers, the freight charges, and the availability of other raw material goods as well. So we are investing into supply chain.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free; Wamsutta acquisition funded through internal accruals
items.quote: We have already mentioned that in our investor deck that we have paid nearly INR85 crores through our internal accruals, where we haven't drawn any debt to make payment for our brand.

items.statement: Bhilad unit operates at 90% renewable energy; freshwater intake reduced to 25%
items.quote: Our Bhilad unit now operates at 90% renewable energy, significantly reducing our carbon footprint. We've achieved a freshwater intake to 25% through upgraded RO and ETP facilities.

items.statement: Logistics situation fluid with container availability improving but costs remain high
items.quote: There are some green shoots into getting the containers as we speak. So going forward, it may improve, but currently, it has not improved. That much I can say.

items.statement: FY25 expected to be a year of modest growth and normalized margins; higher growth anticipated from FY26
items.quote: As previously stated, we expect FY25 to be a year of modest growth and normalized margins, and that outlook remains unchanged.

items.statement: FY25 is a year of consolidation and normalized revenues and profits; momentum expected from FY26
items.quote: FY25, as we have stated earlier, will be a year of normalized revenues and profits as we will be in the investment phase. And we expect our businesses to once again be momentum from FY26 based on our current visibility of our portfolio products.

items.statement: Q1FY25 EBITDA margin 28.9%, up 174 bps YoY; gross margin 66.1% vs 55.2% in Q1FY24
items.quote: Our EBITDA excluding exceptional items of Rs. 20.6 crores excluding that stood at Rs. 128.6 crores with a margin of 28.9%, an increase of 174 b ps over Q1FY24

items.statement: Management intentionally not giving numeric margin guidance for FY25; margins have structurally improved due to business mix shift
items.quote: I think we have left our commentary using the same words, right I think normalized margins and moderate growth. I think it's something that we intentionally are using words and not numbers and we are not intentionally referring to any past performance.

items.statement: CMS revenues of Rs. 235 crores in Q1FY25 driven by commercial molecules; order flow gives confidence in medium and long-term prospects
items.quote: The CMS revenues of Rs. 235 crores were driven by molecules in the commercial segment. The associated drugs seem to be doing well in their end markets, and we expect to continue serving the customers well.

items.statement: Phase-2 pipeline up YoY; 60% from organic progression, 40% from new business
items.quote: So, it's a mix, but I think if I were to put the number there, I would say that it is almost 60-40, means 60% in terms of progression and 40% in terms of new businesses that we are brought in.

items.statement: Rs. 59.1 crores capex in Q1FY25; Unit-3 new production blocks to be completed by FY25, commercial production H2 FY26
items.quote: We continue to invest in upgrading our facilities, we have invested Rs. 59.1 crores in capital spends during Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Additional capex approved for Unit-1 expansion on adjacent 5-acre land for GDS volume growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: There is some CAPEX that was approved today, which will be deployed for expanding capacity in unit one, which is largely for GDS products, just because we have increase in volumes for some of the GDS products, we anticipate increase in the next 2-3 years, and we want to service that demand, and therefore this CAPEX is being deployed for that reason.

items.statement: Unit-2 and Unit-3 capacity utilization close to 90%+; Unit-3 expected at 30-40% utilization in FY25
items.quote: So, currently the capacity utilization in Unit-2 and Unit-3 is close to 90 plus percent. As far as Unit-3 is concerned, this year it will be around 30%-40%.

items.statement: Unit-3 capacity creation ready by end FY25, commercialized in H2 FY26; Unit-1 expansion underway for GDS products
items.quote: The Unit-3 capacity creation will be ready by end of F Y25 and will be commercialized in the second half of

items.statement: Ezetimibe transitioned from specialty to prime segment this quarter; specialty APIs Dorzolamide and Donepezil performed well; prime products Mirtazapine, Levetiracetam, Escitalopram did well
items.quote: Please note that we have transitioned Ezetimibe to the prime segment this quarter, which means that there is a marginal impact on the salience of the specialty segment because Ezetimibe was being counted as a specialty product, but now going forward it will be counted as a prime product.

items.statement: Biotech customers being acquired by Big Pharma; continuity of engagement maintained and excited about future opportunities
items.quote: In terms of our biotech clients being acquired by Big Pharma, we feel the co ntinuity of customer engagement and are actually quite excited about future opportunities and possibilities

items.statement: Hedging position kept open; difficult to predict USD direction; will monitor and take suitable call
items.quote: And we made a conscious decision that we will leave our hedging position open for now. Having said that, it's hard for us or anyone to predict where exactly the dollar is going to go in the future.

items.statement: Working capital at 107 days to sales; free cash flow of Rs. 50.9 crores generated in Q1FY25
items.quote: At the same time, we continue to focus on cash to optimize our working capital, which stands at 107 days to sales and thereby we have generated a free cash flow in Q1FY25 of Rs. 50.9 crores.

items.statement: Repaid Rs. 8.7 crores debt in Q1FY25; net debt position negative at Rs. 110.2 crores (net cash)
items.quote: We also repaid some part of our debt of around Rs. 8.7 crores. Consequently, our net debt position, which is negative, stands at Rs. 110.2 crores.

items.statement: CMS business lumpy in nature; annual progression better indicator than quarterly
items.quote: The CMS business is lumpy in nature, and therefore an annual progression is a better indicator than a quarterly progression.

items.statement: Actively managing three key risks: alternate sourcing from China, commodity price volatility (de-risked), and currency/geopolitical instability; total risk register has 116 risks
items.quote: One is this whole alternate sourcing, bringing our supply chain closer to home, having an alternate supply to our Chinese partners. That's one thing which is an active strategy that we continue to pursue. In the past, we were impacted by this whole Russia, Ukraine situation because some of the metal prices went up, catalyst prices we nt up, there were some short supplies. We have de-risked that as

items.statement: Biosecure Act: no tangible RFPs or business inflow yet; heightened customer visits, RFIs, meeting requests as lead indicators; Big Pharma moving faster than biotech
items.quote: As I had mentioned in my comments, we don't see any tangible RFPs or business inflow yet. But having said that, there's obviously a heightened level of customer visits, RFIs, meeting requests, things like that, which could be considered as lead indicators of the behavior of US pharma, US biotech.

items.statement: Stock split suggestion will be discussed at board level and with advisors
items.quote: I think with regards to the stock split, the second question, I think that's something that we will definitely take into consideration. I think we have been getting this input, but we haven't really processed it. Yes, we will discuss it at the board level and also talk to other advisors and then probably figure out what's the best way forward.

items.statement: Peptide DMF for Difelikefalin (chronic kidney disorders) to be filed; commercialization post-2030; 6-7 DMFs targeted this year, mostly specialty, ~50% long-term
items.quote: So, I think in terms of the peptide molecule, I think we have discussed in the past that this is a molecule called Difelikefalin, which is more used for chronic kidney disorders and is also in development for other indications. Having said that, I think we will be filing, but the commercialization will happen only post 2030.

items.statement: Expects 10-15% revenue CAGR from FY26 and EBITDA margins of 18-20% in next few years post FY26
items.quote: I think rather giving forward guidance, expecting 10% to 15% growth coming back from next financial year. Once the Crop Protection business comes back on track , I think we should be getting back to those numbers and the EBITDA numbers historically of 18% to 20% is what we can achieve in the next few years after post from FY26 onwards.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is Rs 120-140 crore, mostly debottlenecking and maintenance
items.quote: So, we are doing about Rs. 120 to Rs. 140 crores in that range, depending approximately. Nothing significant, it's mostly debottlenecking and maintenance CAPEX. There's no major significant CAPEX right now.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated EBITDA Rs 58 crore at 14.3% margin, up 16% YoY; PAT impacted by Rs 10 crore higher depreciation and interest from new asset capitalization
items.quote: For Q1 FY25, the EBITDA stood at Rs. 58 crores, which is 14.3% compared to Rs. 50 crores, which is 12.9% on a year -on-year basis, resulting in a growth of 16%. The same is not being reflected in the profit before tax and profit after tax due to the increase in depreciation and interest cost on account of capitalization of new assets during the last 12 months. The combined impact amounts to Rs. 10

items.statement: Crop Protection Q1 EBIT margin 11.6%, up 110 bps YoY driven by high-margin CDMO product mix
items.quote: In Q1 FY25, revenue of our Crop Protection business was Rs. 177 crore with EBIT of Rs. 21 crore and EBIT margin of 11.6%, showing a year-on-year increase of 110 basis points. Our product mix for the quarter was more leverage d towards our CDMO portfolio, leading to improved margins.

items.statement: Pharma Q1 EBIT Rs 9 crore, margin down 60 bps YoY due to capacity expansion shutdowns and delayed CDMO deliveries
items.quote: Our Pharmaceutical business reported revenue of Rs. 229 crores and EBIT of Rs. 9 crores. This was a decrease of 60 points as compared to year -on-year. We are anticipating good volume growth in our API business in the coming years, and therefore, we took capacity expansion and debottlenecking shutdowns, which will give us increased operating leverage in the next few quarters.

items.statement: CDMO pipeline healthy with growing inquiries and conversions; two products in production expected to peak in 2 years; two NCE intermediates in Phase-3 trials ramping by 2026-27
items.quote: Our CDMO business is showing positive results with two products currently in production that are e xpected to reach their peak potential within the next two years. Furthermore, two of our advanced intermediate s for NCEs are progressing well in Phase-3 of the clinical trials with innovators and are anticipated to start ramping up by 2026-27.

items.statement: Animal Health facility operational, 5 products validated, more validations by year-end; regulatory filings initiated globally
items.quote: Furthermore, our new multipurpose plan for Animal Health is operational and we have successfully completed the validation of five products with several more products undergoing validation, which is expected to be completed by year end. These will then be submitted for registration and eventual commercializatio n.

items.statement: Crop capacity utilization ~60% due to demand contraction; Pharma utilization ~65% in Q1 due to annual shutdown and debottlenecking, expected to rise from Q2
items.quote: Crop utilization is on the lower side, it's about 60% because of the demand contraction in the current scenario in crop. Pharma, you have done significant amount of shutdown because of, as part of our annual shutdown, also debottlenecking of our capacities for the future. So, we had to take shutdowns in the 1st Quarter. And that's why the pharma capacity utilization is about 65% for this quarter,

items.statement: Crop Protection pricing under pressure from aggressive Chinese dumping on commoditized molecules; specialty/CDMO pricing intact
items.quote: Yes, so I think crop protection industry pricing from China is very aggressive and they're dumping product at a very low price. So, that is definitely impacting crop protection pricing power, and this continues for the older molecules which are commoditized, but for the new molecules which is what we are focusing on in the CDMO space, which are under -patent, the pricing is intact.

items.statement: Blended gross margin ~45%; new niche Pharma/CDMO/Animal Health projects expected to drive contribution margins significantly higher than current blended levels
items.quote: If you look at our blended g ross margin of the company, we are between close to 45 % today. This is even after the pricing pressure in the crop business. And the generic part of our pharma business are some of the older molecules, right? As our portfolio moves to more niche, specialty-based products in crop, and also when we ramp up the animal health business and our pharma in NCE, so the new pro

items.statement: R&D spend at ~4% of total sales in Q1 FY25
items.quote: About 4% of our total sales.

items.statement: Intense price competition and overcapacity in Crop Protection from Chinese players impacting commoditized molecules
items.quote: the Crop P rotection industry continues to face challenges due to de-stocking, overcapacity and intense price competition from China

items.statement: Crop Protection recovery timeline uncertain; Pharma/CDMO project commercialization subject to clinical trial success and innovator decisions beyond company control
items.quote: There's a relative uncertainty which is beyond our control in terms of where those products land, whether they actually go through commercial to market and that's beyond our control. So, when we look at our future growth projections, we have a discount rate which we use in terms of what potentially could come to market.

items.statement: Sustainability: Signed UN Global Compact, received EcoVadis Bronze rating; developed environmental strategy roadmap
items.quote: Our commitment to sustainability is substantiated with Hikal becoming a signatory to the United Nations Global Impact Program, and we received the Bronze Rating awarded by EcoVadis. In order to make a positive environmental impact through our operations, we have developed a clear future strategy and roadmap.

items.statement: Double-digit growth expected for FY25, mostly volume-driven
items.quote: We are still looking at a double-digit growth and I don't think there should be an issue with all our plants completely up and ready as far as we are concerned.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement of 1-1.5% expected in FY25, subject to stable gas prices
items.quote: EBITDA margins, like I mentioned earlier, with the caveat of gas prices not spiking, we should be able to improve 1%, 1.5% EBITDA basically on the riding on the better capacity utilization and better product mix and also a 10% plus growth or double-digit growth over there.

items.statement: No major capex planned for next 12-18 months; capacity utilization at 81% leaves little headroom
items.quote: So, obviously, we started thinking about it. But there is no serious CAPEX currently in the next 12 to 18 months in our plant.

items.statement: Operating margin maintained at 8.5% in Q1 FY25 vs 8.7% YoY; gross margin improved 230 bps YoY to 35.2%
items.quote: So, we have been able to maintain the operating margin at 8.5% versus 8.7% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: GVT share rose to 37% in Q1 FY25 from 33% YoY; ceramics fell to 35% from 39%; PVT flat at 28%
items.quote: Q1 FY '25 ceramic is 35%. The same quarter last year was 39 %. PVT is 28%. Last year was also same as 28 %. GVT has improved to 37 % from 33%.

items.statement: July better than May-June but still tough; H2 demand pickup expected from Q3/Q4 driven by real estate completions
items.quote: July has also been a tough month. After the budget, it's been a tough month. But we do, it's been better than May and June is what I can say.

items.statement: Exports recovered to Rs 1,650-1,700 crore/month in Apr-Jun from Rs 1,300-1,350 crore lows in Jan-Feb
items.quote: The exports have improved since the lows of January and February where it had gone down to Rs. 1,300 crore, Rs. 1,350 crore levels. It's come back to Rs. 1,650 crore to Rs. 1,700 crore levels per month between April, May and June.

items.statement: Max plant at 35-40% utilization in Q1; expected to reach EBITDA breakeven at 60-65% utilization over next 2-4 quarters
items.quote: Max plant, currently we are operating virtually at very low capacity. It is around 35%-37% which is coming for this quarter, and it would ramp up gradually over next 2-3-4 quarters.

items.statement: Morbi cluster at 65-70% utilization; 150 units shut, 200 more may shut; aggressive one-time sales and tax evasion observed
items.quote: As far as the capacity utilization is concerned , I ha ve given to understand it's between 65% and 70 % capacity utilization. So, there is more than enough capacity available in Morbi

items.statement: Gas prices stable in Q1; Kassar Rs 43/scm (vs Rs 45-46), Morbi Rs 45 (vs Rs 43), South Rs 47 (vs Rs 55); no significant change since
items.quote: Gas prices have helped us. They have been largely stable during the quarter, and going forward also, we believe that this would be largely stable.

items.statement: Brand spend annualized at 2.75-3% of sales; Q1 at 2% due to seasonality
items.quote: The brand spend is going to be maintained annualized between 2.75% to 3%. However, the brand spend in Quarter 1 is generally lower. So, it's at 2% in Quarter 1.

items.statement: Working capital days at ~13 days in Q1 vs 8 days in Q4; receivables down 5 days QoQ; DSO improved to 43 days from 48 days in March
items.quote: Working capital days have also largely been maintained at approximately 13 days in Q1 as compared to 8 days in Q4.

items.statement: Sanitaryware utilization at 96%, faucets at 90% (single shift); spare capacity available in faucets
items.quote: As far as the other capacity utilization is concerned, which is sanitary ware and faucets, sanitaryware ran at 96%. That is up from the previous levels.

items.statement: Consolidated gross debt stable at Rs 335 crore; annual term loan repayment of Rs 35-40 crore on schedule
items.quote: So, 335 Cr consolidated we have in March gross debt and the same level is there in June also.

items.statement: Double-digit CAGR targeted for next 3-4 years driven by middle-end tiles, Max plant ramp-up, and sanitaryware/bath fittings expansion
items.quote: So, I was saying that at the top end of the prism driven by Max fortifying the middle end of the tile segment and the sanitaryware and bath fitting put together we should be looking at a double-digit CAGR growth for the next 3-4 years.

items.statement: Full-year volume growth guidance of 10-15% for conductor division
items.quote: But for the full year basis, we are expecting about volume growth to be anywhere between 10-15 percentage.

items.statement: Cable division annual revenue growth guidance of 25% and EBITDA margin range 10-12%
items.quote: Yes. margins are likely to be in the range of 10 -12 percentage. And overall, value also, we are looking at about 25 percentage growth on an annual basis.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR300-350 crores for FY25, similar range for FY26
items.quote: We are looking at capex of about INR300 crores to INR350 crores in this financial year.

items.statement: Conductor order book at INR6,725 crores with 41% premium products; Q1 order inflow INR1,794 crores
items.quote: Overall, our order book is at INR6,725 crores, with premium products contributing towards 41% of the order book. There was a new order inflow in the quarter of INR1,794 crores.

items.statement: Cable division order book at INR1,571 crores
items.quote: The overall order book came in at INR1,571 crores.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 43.4% YoY; export revenue declined 25.9% due to high US base and logistics issues
items.quote: The domestic business actually grew by 43.4% vers us last year. The export revenue degrew by 25.9%, essentially due to the high base of US revenues in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: India transformation capacity addition expected at 1,16,490 MVA in FY25, highest historically
items.quote: As for the CEA, the current fiscal year FY '25, which is from 1st April '24 to 31st March '25, is expected to see as much as 1,16,490 MVA of substation capacity coming on stream.

items.statement: Conductor EBITDA per metric tonne post-forex at INR38,532 driven by premium product mix
items.quote: EBITDA per metric tonne post -forex adjustment came in at INR38,532 per tonne. On the back of execution of higher-margin product orders, especially with a higher amount of HTLS conductors getting executed in that period.

items.statement: Oil division EBITDA per KL post-forex at INR6,935, up 15% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA post forex adjustment came in at INR6,935 per KL, which is 15% higher than last year.

items.statement: Cable EBITDA margin at 10.3%, down 110 bps YoY due to lower exports and geographic mix
items.quote: The EBITDA margin came in at 10.3% in Q1, which is down 110 basis points versus last year. And this, we can attribute to lower level of exports as well as a geographic mix.

items.statement: Copper and aluminum price changes do not affect margins due to full hedge book; only working capital impact
items.quote: So, copper and aluminum rates doesn't affect our margins because we run our full hedge book for all the orders that we have.

items.statement: Cables and conductor divisions running at over 90% capacity utilization
items.quote: Capacity, we are running over 90 percentage on our cables and conductor division.

items.statement: Chinese competition increased with predatory pricing; US duties on Chinese aluminum conductors/cables raised by 20-25 percentage points to 60%+
items.quote: Chinese competition, however, has increased considerably, especially in areas where there are no barriers to entry for Chinese products. Due to predatory pricing, however, duty on Chinese goods which include aluminum conductors and cables have been increased by up to 25% further in the U.S.

items.statement: New domestic conductor entrants (KEC, Diamond Power) face technology barriers (AL-59), PGCIL approval delays, and EPC conflict of interest
items.quote: the product, which is now being used in India, which is AL -59, is not an easy product to manufacture for a new entrant. So, it is possible that some o f these companies may actually start off with the conventional ACSR conductors and it may take some time for them to actually qualify and make the product as per the requirement of PGCIL and other customers

items.statement: Export shipments worth over INR270 crores postponed in June due to container shortage and freight disruption across all three divisions
items.quote: If you look at the total exports that got postponed across the 3 divisions, it is in excess of INR270 crores.

items.statement: US cable inquiry rates and order inflow have increased; US conductor orders delayed by regulatory approvals
items.quote: I think so because our inquiry rates have substantially increased. And even the order inflow has started increasing. So, when you are looking at this first quarter versus first quarter of last year, first quarter of last year was still at a fairly high level.

items.statement: Auto oil growth driven by B2B distributors, OEMs, direct industrial sales; gained share from existing OEMs and added new product lines
items.quote: On the automotive side, besides these 3 channels, the OEM portion, APAR has actually gained market share or share of business from some of the existing OEMs. And that has also resulted in the higher numbers coming in on the automotive side.

items.statement: Major supplier to Vande Bharat trains; railway cable business growing; copper conductor orders down but offset by copper transpose conductors for transformers and busbars
items.quote: We are the major supplier into the Vande Bharat train. And as the manufacturing and execution of that is incr easing, ours suppli es to the railways is also increase.

items.statement: US regulatory clearances for transmission projects taking longer; higher interest rates delaying foreign project implementation
items.quote: The foreign regulatory bodies are more demanding, and there are a lot of more procedure for their various permissions compared to our Indian counterparts. So, to get the project clearances itself takes many years.

items.statement: Export logistics disruption affected FOB shipments where customers provide containers; freight rates increased due to Red Sea issues and China-US pre-tariff rush
items.quote: The number which we mentioned of INR270 crores of shipments having got stranded, which would have otherwise been planned for dispatches in Q1, are largely comprising of FOB shipments, where the client was supposed to actually provide for the logistics and the container costs.

items.statement: India renewable energy capacity at 195 GW (85.5 GW solar, 46.7 GW wind); 134.85 GW pipeline (85 GW solar, 30 GW wind)
items.quote: As of the end of June 2024, the total renewable energy capacity stands at 195 gigawatts, of which 85.47 gigawatts comes from solar, 46.7 gigawatts come from wind. The total capacity under pipeline, which is being added, is 134.85 gigawatts.

items.statement: Data center power demand in Navi Mumbai alone exceeds 3,000 MW for announced projects; driving transformer and cable demand
items.quote: If you take the data centers which are being added in Na vi Mumbai alone, once this current set, which have been announced are added, we need in excess of 3,000 megawatts of power to service them.

items.statement: Board approved slump sale of hydro and gas businesses to related parties GE Power Electronics India and GE Renewable Energy Technologies, subject to minority shareholder approval
items.quote: As disclosed by the company on 10th of July 24, the Board of Directors of the company have approved the sale and transfer of its hydro business undertaking to GE Power Electronics India Private Limited, a related party, and the gas power undertaking of the company to GE Renewable Energy Technologies Private Limited, a related party.

items.statement: Hydro business valued at negative Rs 1,001 million; GE Vernova offers nominal purchase price of Rs 1 (Rs 100 crore premium to valuation)
items.quote: The fairness opinion on the valuation is provided by RBSA Capital Advisors LLP, a SEBI-registered company. Merchant banker RBSA and GT in their valuation report have recommended a positive valuation of Rs. 438.6 million for the gas power business and a negative valuation of 1,001 million.

items.statement: Gas business valued at positive Rs 438.6 million by Grant Thornton and RBSA Capital Advisors
items.quote: Merchant banker RBSA and GT in their valuation report have recommended a positive valuation of Rs. 438.6 million for the gas power business and a negative valuation of 1,001 million.

items.statement: Company net worth depleted to Rs 57 crore as of March 31, 2024; rating at BBB negative; further deterioration could lead to negative net worth and loss of tender eligibility
items.quote: The current net worth of the company has depleted to Rs 57 crores as on 31 st March 2024 and this has been constantly depleting quarter-on-quarter for past se veral quarters due to the cost and project updates in the hydro power projects

items.statement: Transaction expected to provide net worth boost of Rs 296 crore excluding taxes; closing comments cite Rs 252 crore net liability reduction plus Rs 44 crore gas consideration
items.quote: This transaction would have an impact of positive Rs. 296 crores excluding taxes which will provide net worth boost to the company.

items.statement: Hydro business requires additional Rs 500 crore debt and guarantees over next 2 years; Rs 700 crore non-funded limits and Rs 500 crore cash consumption limit to be unlocked post carve-out
items.quote: the hydro basically is going to require additional Rs. 500 crores of debt and additional guarantees. A bank guarantee should be issued, which is going to not c onvert into margin and cash in

items.statement: Steam services booked highest ever core order value in 4 months, surpassing 3-year annual average; upgrades booked ~Rs 700 crore including Wanakbori and Vindhyachal (~Rs 600 crore)
items.quote: in these four months, we have book ed and announced orders more than we have done in the average annual order of 3 years. S o just in 4 months, we have surpassed the average annual of the last 3 years

items.statement: Target double-digit EBITDA and debt-free in 2 years; positive free cash flow and dividend-paying capability; stable quarter-on-quarter performance from four focus areas
items.quote: With these four business areas, we are very confident that the company will deliver quarter-on-quarter double digit EBITDA performance in two years from now, that we will have positive free cash flow to be able to deliver dividends and it's a sustainable roadmap.

items.statement: Hydro EBITDA projected at ~7% on Rs 1,000-1,100 crore topline for next 3 years vs -16% last 3 years; net free cash flow still negative for 2025-26
items.quote: However, if you look at the next, I mean, till 2030 you have the projection, but let's say, apple to apple 3 years, if you look at the next three years, average Rs. 1000 crores – Rs. 1,100 crores of topline is what we are forecasting for hydro. At an EBITDA level which is there what you're able to see is around 7%.

items.statement: Hydro projects face constant delays from geology, topology, land acquisition, environmental clearances, labor unrest; valuation assumes zero future delays and three new orders without slippage
items.quote: However, we are seeing constantl y delays on the hydro projects because of several factors like geology, topology, land acquis ition, environmental clearance, labor unrest, etc. All these are continuing every year and theref ore we are assuming no further delay in the cost, no further cost update in the valuation for t he contract

items.quote: our OPEX to average AUM ratio witnessed a consistent improvement dropping to 5.5% on a standalone basis , decreased by 27 basis point on a year-on-year basis. Likewise, our cos t to-income ratio improved to 41.4% as a gainst 48.9% on a standalone basis.

items.quote: OPEX, our sense is that we have put in our collection team during this quarter. So, whatever little increase had come has also been factored in. items.quote: I am also happy to share with you that we have welcome d Mr. Joydeep Datta Gupta, former partner of Deloitte India and Miss Jyoti Da var, Director General at FICCI to our Board as Independent Directors.

items.statement: Adding new wholly-owned subsidiary in technology space to provide tech solutions to financial services sector
items.quote: I am pleased to share with you that we are adding a new wholly-owned subsidiary to our offerings in the technology space. This company will aim to provide technological solutions to the financing services sector.

items.statement: Observing stress in pockets of Odisha and Rajasthan; proactive measures taken; UP and Bihar stable despite floods and Kawar Yatra disruptions
items.quote: Commenting in the ongoing concern, we state that as of now we have not encountered any significant stress in UP and Bihar. However, aligned with industry trends, we are observing some challenges in Odisha and Rajasthan for which we have already taken proactive measures.

items.statement: Delinquency increase in Q1 due to heat waves, election disruptions, harvesting season; expect stabilization as seasonal factors settle
items.quote: Coming to the asset quality , we observed a temporary increase in delinquency during the 1st Quarter. This was due to the severe heat wave across several region s, operational constraints during the general election, which impacted regular collection and follow-ups in the delinquent buckets.

items.statement: Management targets EBITDA margin of 30% as a healthy level given business complexities
items.quote: See, I mean, I have always been saying that in the current scenario and the way we deal with possession, if we reach an efficiency of 30%, I would believe that's a nice spot to be in, given the nuances of the business.

items.statement: Industry volume growth is about 2% while revenue growth is around 5-6% on average
items.quote: See, the volume growth for the industry as seen in available data is about 2%. We work on increased here, that's the core business that we are talking about. So, I would want to believe the industry's revenue growth is around five to 6%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expanded 260 bps YoY to 27% in Q1 FY25 driven by operating leverage and cost management
items.quote: Our EBITDA surged by 25% YoY, while our EBITDA margin stands at 27%, a notable increase of ~260 basis points. This achievement highlights our unwavering commitment to improving operational efficiencies and effectively implementing cost management strategies.

items.statement: Costs are expected to average out for remaining quarters with only potential digital-led incremental costs in Q4
items.quote: Yes, I would want to believe, unless the revenue figures stand for whatever the industry numbers are, our costs will play out because that is something which we see is going to be maybe in the last quarter, if there's any investments which are digital-led, those kinds of incremental costs.

items.statement: Inventory utilization at 71% with headroom for volume-driven revenue growth for next two quarters
items.quote: Like I said, our inventory utilization still is at 71% , so there is headroom for revenue growth through volume at least for the next two quarters.

items.statement: Yield grew 8% YoY in Q1 FY25 largely due to political ads at premium pricing
items.quote: Yes, there has been an 8% yield growth for us. But I do not think at this point in time we should get carried away, because that is largely because of political ads. While the ratio has not been really much, it comes at a fairly high premium.

items.statement: Ad rates at 90% of pre-COVID levels with 8% increase over last year
items.quote: It will still be about 90% of pre-COVID levels.

items.statement: DAVP rate increase of 10-12% will average out by end of next quarter as growth has played out
items.quote: That average over the period will be around 10% to 12%, but that will end at the end of next quarter, because then that growth has already been played out in the last two quarters of the year, right, the increased DAVP rate.

items.statement: Digital business grew 45% YoY contributing 10% to revenue
items.quote: Our digital business continues to be our core focus, having achieved an impressive 45% YoY growth with contribution of 10% to our revenue.

items.statement: Non-FCT revenue contribution is approximately 25% excluding digital
items.quote: Non-FCT contribution, if I keep digital away, it's approximately close to about 25%.

items.statement: Radio City added 1,700 new clients in Q1 FY25 representing ~40% of industry new client additions
items.quote: 1,700 clients in this quarter Radio City has added new into our fold.

items.statement: 40% of industry client base and 32% of newly acquired radio clients chose Radio City
items.quote: We are delighted to see that Radio City continues to be the top choice for advertisers with 40% of the industry's client base opting for our platform. Furthermore, 32% of newly acquired clients in the radio sector have chosen radio for their advertising needs.

items.statement: Expect at least 3 out of 10 advertising solutions to include influencers by end of fiscal year
items.quote: I will want to believe at least three out of 10 advertising solutions will have influencers as part of the solution that we are offering.

items.statement: Top three players hold close to 50% market share; Radio City maintains 19% volume market share
items.quote: This quarter, we have maintained a market share of 19% according to the Volume Data.

items.statement: Pricing power limited due to unsaturated inventory among smaller players and cash-strapped competitors
items.quote: It is, no, because when you look at the total, if I put an average of 10 or 11 players in the larger market and five, six players in the smaller market, the inventory play for the rest of the players is still not at the saturation point.

items.statement: SMINCO platform investment approximately Rs. 1 crore from platform perspective
items.quote: So, you could say, there is an investment of approximately Rs. 1 crore from a platform perspective.

items.statement: Government advertising contributed Rs. 7 crores from political ads at higher prices in Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, that's basically political that we are talking about from the base that we have got, we have got a total of about seven crores of political advertising that is coming, which has come at a higher price.

items.statement: Influencer marketing opportunity estimated at Rs. 3,300-3,600 crores over next two years per FICCI
items.quote: If you look at, FICCI says that currently in the next two years, our influencer marketing -led advertising business is worth Rs. 3,300-odd crores or Rs. 3,600-odd crores, which in my mind will be equivalent to what the radio business is.

items.statement: Cash reserves stood at Rs. 338 crores as of June 30, 2024 providing flexibility for opportunities
items.quote: Our cash reserves stood at Rs. 338 crores as of June 30th, 2024. Our liquidity position remains strong, and as stated previously, this liquidity allows us the flexibility to take advantage of present and prospective future opportunities.

items.statement: NOTIF policy trial recommendations still under MIB consolidation with no decision yet
items.quote: No, that is still going on. Those trial recommendation is still being put to the MIB and the MIB is consolidating things to take an overall decision.

items.statement: Revenue dependent on environment; radio business cyclical and subject to external factors
items.quote: Yes, I mean, if you look at it, it should be better, but we never know how the industry shapes up because we are far more dependent on the environment around us. Because radio being radio, a lot of things are dependent on the environment around you.

items.statement: Target standalone AUM of INR9,500 crores and consolidated AUM of INR12,500 crores for FY25

items.quote: we are looking at close to INR9,500 crores in the stand-alone and on an overall basis of about INR12,500 crores. It's the AUM that we are looking at.

items.quote: We should possibly go down by about 10, 15 -- 10 bps a quarter and go to a figure -- so let me say, around 10.5 in the fourth quarter.

items.quote: the segment I'm in, we can expect a 1.5% to 2% credit cost. We will remain in that territory only.

items.quote: Over the past 2 years, if you see the used commercial vehicle industry has surged by more than 30% due to limited supply.

items.quote: Our emphasis on Focus 4, something which I mentioned some time back, Focus 4 products has led to an increase in our yield by about 70 bps in the -- over the last 3 quarters besides the insurance income that we have started generating from the previous quarter

items.quote: we have a policy of ensuring that we keep at least funds to take care of the next 2 months of repayment.

items.quote: Our return on assets are at 3%, and we maintain a strong capital adequacy of 56.2% and a debt-to-equity of 2.6x.

items.quote: The implementation of the scrappage policy, and this is likely to support the new vehicle growth.

items.quote: So definitely maybe a little improvement vis-a-vis the Q1, but by and large definitely settling down to a blended margin in the range that we have seen in this quarter.

items.quote: last few years we have been growing at a rate of about 35% to 38% on a CAGR basis. And we still like for this year as well we have a similar kind of plan.

items.quote: The company has delivered first lot of indigenously developed loitering munition to the armed forces.

items.statement: Defence order timelines uncertain due to government decision-making delays post-elections
items.quote: Pinaka orders are also likely to come soon, but because of elections and then government formation, certain decision-making has slowed down for a couple of months

items.statement: Targets EBITDA margin of 27-29% by Q4 FY25, with Q2 around 24-25%
items.quote: By Q4, certainly, Nikhil, we are going to target reaching those kind of EBITDA levels. However, a word of caution, the next quarter, again, is going to be similarly balanced about 24%, 25% EBITDA levels because of pricing pressures, and raw material input costs are rising this quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 25.51%, PAT margin 13.61%
items.quote: For the quarter under review, operating revenue was around INR281 crores, with EBITDA reaching INR72 crores and EBITDA margin at 25.51%. The profit after tax for the quarter was INR38 crores, resulting in PAT margin of 13.61%.

items.statement: Average selling price fell to INR69,150/tonne from INR74,000/tonne; wheat straw cost dropped INR2,000/tonne to INR4,200/tonne
items.quote: The selling price, on the oth er hand, reduced by about INR5,000 per tonne from the previous quarter. From a level of about INR74,000 per tonne, we are down to INR69,000 per tonne on average. Some of our products sell at INR70, INR71 per kilo as well, but the average pricing for all o ur products in a cumulative fashion is INR69,150 per

items.statement: Wood prices risen from INR7,000 to INR9,500-11,000/tonne due to plyboard/MDF competition; expected to stay high for 3-4 years
items.quote: And from levels of about INR7,000 p er tonne, which we were achieving and procuring till about a year back, they have moved up and now touching between INR9,500 to about INR11,000 per tonne currently. And even on the imported pulp side, because of ocean freights, the costing of imported pulp remained on a higher

items.statement: INR735 crore modernization to expand capacity 50% to 675 tpd by upgrading existing machines; funded by INR535 crore debt and INR200 crore internal accruals
items.quote: So we are targeting expanding by 50%. From the current 450 tonnes per day, we are planning to reach 675 tonnes per day on all our existing machines only. They are not going to be any new machine that is going to be added and which is going to help reduce our cost of production going forward.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 record avg finished paper production 434 tpd and pulp production 359 tpd; targeting 675 tpd post-modernization
items.quote: The company also achieved its higher ever -- highest ever average finished paper production of 434 tonnes per day and a record-breaking average pulp production of 359 tonnes per day for the Q1 FY 24-25.

items.statement: Specialty papers ~20% of mix, commanding INR1-1.5/kg premium; writing/printing split: 25% Copier, 45% Maplitho, balance Creamwove
items.quote: But to tell you that about 20 %-odd is Specialty paper, which is commanding ab out INR1 to INR 1.5 per kilo higher NSR from the normal writing and printing paper grades. Within the writing and printing paper grade segment, we are doing about 25% Copier, about 45% Maplitho and the balance is normal Creamwove segments

items.statement: Current debt INR385 cr; peak debt under INR600 cr by March 2026 after INR430 cr new debt and INR220 cr repayment
items.quote: So currently , our debt is at a level of INR 385 crores. By the time these projects are commissioned, which would take about 2 years from today, our further deb t that we will undertake is INR430 crores, which will take it up to INR815 crores. But in the interim -- in the 2 years, we would have repaid INR 220 crores of existing debt, so our peak debt will be under INR600 crores as of March 2026

items.statement: Surface water at INR5/cu m vs groundwater INR18/cu m saves ~INR60-65 lakh/month (from INR95 lakh to INR35 lakh)
items.quote: So ground water extraction in the state of Punjab is costing us INR18 per cubic meter and that translates to a cost of a lmost between INR90 lakhs to INR1 crore every month. Against this, surface water is going to cost us INR5 per cubic meter. That's a Government of stipulation, and that is where we will be sort of being rewarded or benefited healthily by way of a red uced cost, and that should --

items.statement: Industry (IPMA) representing to Government for anti-dumping duty; PIMS import monitoring system curbing unregulated imports
items.quote: Yes, the industry through our body called IPMA, we are repre senting to the Government. We are getting opportunities to voice our opinion and thought with them. And I'm sure in succeeding times, we are going to see some kind of judgment, some kind of decision being taken in, which is going to help us going forward.
