items.statement: Red Sea crisis hurting exports; displaced volumes pressuring domestic prices; expects improvement from Q3
items.quote: We are not being able to export in the volumes and quantities that we were earlier, and that entire volume is finding its way in the domestic market and disturbing the demand -supply situation. And that is also one of the reasons why the current pricing is und er pressure and not being able to rise in the way that it could have

items.statement: Targets EBITDA/tonne of INR25,000 in 2-3 years via machine optimization and AI (vs current ~INR20,000)
items.quote: And I think going forward, we ourselves are targeting reach ing EBITDA margins of about INR25,000 per tons in the next 2 years to 3 years, by way of implementing various initiatives that we are doing, which means optimizing o ur existing machines leading to lower cost of production as well as integrating AI mechanisms in our operations

items.statement: Engaged VOITH/BTG for AI implementation across mill operations; expects 5-15% bottom-line delta
items.quote: And lastly i s that we've engaged with the best in the world, a VOITH company called BTG, and they are helping us implement AI across our mill operation, and that could potentially lead to a delta of between 5% to 15% on our bottom line

items.statement: Wood pricing to remain high for 3-4 years until new harvest; imported pulp costs elevated due to ocean freight
items.quote: But internally, domestically, the wood pricing is going to remain on a high for at least about 3 to 4 years till a new harvest of crop comes in. And industry is making a h uge effort in terms of replenishing and renovating and increasing the footprint of wood availability by way of social forestry programs

items.statement: Social farm forestry expanded to 8,000+ acres benefiting 11,500+ farmers; targeting 1 crore saplings in 3 years covering 50,000 acres
items.quote: Additionally, we expanded our social farm forestry program, footprint by up to 8,000 acres -plus in this quarter cumulatively and then -- this is then going to be benefiting more than 11,500 farmers over the years.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target INR 950 crore; FY26 additional INR 250-270 crore from new projects plus 10-12% organic growth
items.quote: So, broadly we can say this financial year we are targeting around INR950 crores. And coming to next financial year, over and above what we are achieving this financial year, the normal growth of 10% to 12% will be there in terms of the existing capacity. And for the new project of Ply and laminate, we can expect around INR250 to INR270 crores turnover next year additional.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target 14% for FY25 and better than 14% for FY26
items.quote: In terms of margins, we are targeting around 14% EBITDA for this financial year and at least better than that in the next financial year.

items.statement: MDF capacity utilization 91% in Q1 FY25, targeting 95% for full year; Chikmagalur plant ran at 113% in Q1 and up to 126% in a month
items.quote: From 89%, we have achieved 91% capacity in this financial year. I mean, in this quarter only. If you see our production capacity in Q4, it was 89%. This quarter, it's almost 91%. And this financial year, we are targeting 95%.

items.statement: Domestic laminate demand expected to pick up with festive season; MDF domestic demand back on track after Q1 slowdown due to financial year-end targets
items.quote: We believe that now the festive season started, so laminate demand will move on from now. And it looks pretty good in coming days. And as long as MDF market is concerned, yes, it is also going good. Because in Q4, people have to finish their financial targets for 23-24. So, Q1 was a bit slow, but now onwards it will be again on track.

items.statement: Net debt-to-equity ratio improved to 0.45x through deleveraging
items.quote: Additionally, we have strengthened our financial position by further deleveraging, with our net debt-to-equity ratio now at 0.45x. This improvement reflects our ongoing commitment to enhancing financial stability and optimizing our capital structure.

items.statement: MDF market growing at 15-20% CAGR; India MDF market share 20-22% vs 80% globally, indicating ample growth space
items.quote: As mentioned by Keyur bhai, this industry is growing at 20% CAGR. If we see the world analysis today, MDF and particle board plays at 80% of the total capacity installed in other nations, while 20% is taken care by Finger Joint Board and Plywood. In India, the scenario is different. Currently, the MDF market share is roughly around 20% to 22%. So, we have ample space to grow, and we don't see any

items.statement: Export obligation completed by end of FY24, removing pressure and allowing selective export orders based on margins
items.quote: So, first of all, we had an export obligation which we duly fulfilled by the end of last financial year. So, the pressure over the exports or making the export target oriented was not a pressure this time. So, we healthily picked up the customers who are able to give us a good realization.

items.statement: Freight cost increases passed through to customers (CIF/FOB mix); not retained as profit
items.quote: I would not say no, it won't be higher because we are already putting to our customers, we are already charging that to our customers . We are not keeping that to ourselves, or we are not booking any kind of profit from transportation

items.statement: Export strategy shifted from volume-driven obligation to margin-selective orders; focusing on value-added exports (30-35% of export volume in Q1)
items.quote: We are now in a better position to take very specific export order. Rather than just doing export for the sake of export obligation. So now we have got option to take export order considering our pre-decided margins. And we are also going for other continents also. So domestic, definitely we have better margins. But in export also, if you see current quarter we have improved in both angles. In ter

items.statement: Stock split approved at 10:1 ratio to enhance liquidity and retail participation
items.quote: In addition to the expansion, we are implementing a stock split at a 10:1 ratio. This decision aims to enhance the liquidity and encourage wider participation from the retail investors, making our stock more accessible and attractive.

items.statement: Confident of achieving INR 2,500 crore revenue milestone set earlier
items.quote: So, yes, we have already been planning and accordingly we are acting, and we are very confident that the target which we have set for ourselves as a company, we are already on the track to achieve it.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 order intake grew ~19% YoY to INR 531 crore; backlog at INR 1,300 crore, up 15.5-16% YoY
items.quote: We have grown by about 19% in orders, and we stand at INR531 crores. And in sales we actually have grown by 19.7% and stand at INR593 crores which is the quarter 1 results. Now at the same time, I'm happy to share that the momentum of order intake has been good, and we are sitting at a backlog of about INR1,300 crores which is typically about 15.5% to 16% up than what it was last year at the same

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 3.6 percentage points YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by price/volume mix and cost optimization
items.quote: At the material cost level, we are up by only 13% as compared to the 19.7% growth in sales. And then coming to the gross margin or the material margin level, we are up by 3.6 points, which is basically a resultant of the price and volum e mix and the cost optimization measures that we have taken

items.statement: EBITDA grew ~63% YoY in absolute terms; EBITDA margin expanded 3.8 percentage points YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to share a high EBITDA growth by almost 63% in absolute numbers, and it is actually up by 3.8% over last year. EBIT, again similar, almost similar growth, 68% in terms of absolute value and similar traction of 3.8 points growth over last year, same quarter.

items.statement: Kolkata factory expected to be commissioned in April 2025 (FY26)
items.quote: We are working hard to make it work from, say, beginning of next year, next fiscal. Apoorva Bahadur: Financial year '26 onwards. Udai Singh: Yes. So sometime in April is what we anticipate will go on full

items.statement: No transformer capacity expansion planned; focusing on higher-value digital/green transformers within existing ~7,000-8,000 MVA capacity
items.quote: There's nothing which I'm aware of, no. And we are -- what we are trying to do is there is a demand, and we are trying to find whatever capacity, which you said is slightly more than what we actually have. But what we are trying to do is we are trying to find out as to who are those users and buyers who really are appreciated for a quality product, which is consistent and also maybe have more leve

items.statement: Q1 FY25 sales mix: transactional 19%, services 13%, equipment 39%, projects 8%, inter-company 22%
items.quote: For the transactional part, we are 19%; services, 13%; equipment, 39%; projects, 8% and inter -companies -- within group sales is about 22%. So all these put together make it 100%. So this is basically the split between the different activities that we do.

items.statement: Export orders ~7-8% of order backlog; three export orders won in Q1 FY25 (Nepal, Australia, Qatar); open to more exports but not chasing generically
items.quote: So you had said -- you were asking about the numbers. We -- typically, this would be, if I would say maybe about 7% to 8% of backlog, which we hold. And going forward, we are trying to see -- we are not making it a generic line, but wherever we have an opportunity, we actually want to serve those international customers from India, if they accept India advisory.

items.statement: Sales split by end-market (approx): power & grid 30-40%, industries & buildings ~25%, metals/minerals/mines ~10-12%, mobility ~10%, data centers ~7-12%; composition varies quarterly
items.quote: Now the composition of this keeps changing. It keeps changing that typically if you really ask me, 30%, 40% is power and gas, then we have about 10% mobility, maybe about 10%, 12% MMM, maybe about industries and oil and gas put together m aybe about 25%. The data center is basically about 7% to 12%. So it changes

items.statement: Employee count: 1,267 in June 2023 vs 1,292 in June 2024
items.quote: Employee count. So it was 1,267 in June '23 and now it is 1,292.

items.statement: Flat to single-digit revenue growth and at least 200 bps EBITDA margin improvement expected for FY25
items.value: flat to single-digit growth; >=200 bps EBITDA margin improvement
items.quote: we see a flat to single-digit growth in this financial year. But we would see that there is a significant jump in the margin as compared to last financial year. And we see that there should be at least 200 basis point jump in the margins -- EBITDA margins as compared to last financial year.

items.statement: Demand weak in Q1 but improving from July; positive outlook for Q2 and Q3
items.quote: We are seeing some positive offshoots starting July as compared to June and even August has begun well. So I think that going forward, work seems to be behind us. And we are looking forward for a positive start from quarter -- Q2.

items.statement: Normal monsoon and strong wedding season expected to drive rural demand
items.quote: One is the monsoon has been normal, so -- which is actually putting us in a sweet spot that this will drive the rural economy. And secondly, we see a very big wedding season coming ahead as compared to last wedding season in India.

items.statement: EBITDA loss narrowed to INR2.3 crore in Q1 FY25 from INR4.1 crore in Q1 FY24
items.quote: We had an EBITDA loss for the quarter of INR2.3 crores, which has narrowed from a loss of INR4.1 crores in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Expect significant margin improvement in FY25 versus FY24
items.quote: we would see that there is a significant jump in the margin as compared to last financial year. And we see that there should be at least 200 basis point jump in the margins -- EBITDA margins as compared to last financial year

items.statement: Inventory under control after corrective actions; 10-15% of last year's inventory being sold fresh this year
items.quote: Out of that inventory, at least 10% to 15% inventory is going into fresh in this financial year. So that is giving us a lot of money as compared to normal scenario where we sell it in our discounts when we sell it in a loss.

items.statement: Normal capex of INR15-20 crore for maintenance and warehouse expansion; no new factory capex
items.quote: So normal capex of around INR15 crores to INR20 crores, that includes some replacement of machines and also some expansion of warehouses and all. Management: No new... Sandeep Jain: But no new capex is

items.statement: COCO store capex ~INR2,000/sq ft; ~INR30 lakh per 1,500 sq ft store; INR2-3 crore annual capex for company-owned EBOs
items.value: INR2,000 per square feet; INR30 lakh per store; INR2 crores to INR3 crores per year
items.quote: the capex is around INR2,000 per square feet. So approximately, if a EBO is 1,500 square feet, so INR30 lakh capex per store. So you can assume around INR2 crores to INR3 crores of capex per year as far as company-owned EBOs are concerned.

items.statement: COCO stores to remain 10-12% of total EBOs; located in high-rental, high-footfall areas
items.quote: See basically, if we see that the COCOs are basically around 10% to 12% of total EBOs. So this ratio will be for this and next financial year also.

items.statement: Online sales growing, especially own website; home textiles and Rock.it brand performing well
items.quote: Our online sales have picked up, particularly from our own website. Home textiles also will continue to show good growth this year. Brand Rock.it has also performed well and has been widely a ccepted by the market

items.statement: E-commerce sales INR14 crore in Q1 FY25 (INR4 crore own website, INR10 crore marketplaces) vs INR9 crore in Q1 FY24
items.quote: So I think until our first quarter, we've done a total e-commerce sale of around INR14 crores as compared to INR9 crores. And out of this, around INR4 crores is from our own website and the rest INR10 crores is from different marketplaces.

items.statement: Footwear getting good traction online; reducing offline footprint to focus on online and larger format stores
items.quote: we are getting a very good traction when it comes to online sales of footwear. So right now, our focus is towards developing a range, which caters to the online market, and we've got very encouraging results when it comes to online sales.

items.statement: Rock.it athleisure: opened 1 store, targeting 2-3 stores in FY25; no plans for sportswear
items.quote: We've just opened one store a couple of months back. We've seen good results from that. We are targeting to open 2 or 3 stores, not more than that in this financial year.

items.statement: No exports to Bangladesh; no imports from Bangladesh; Bangladesh situation a non-event
items.quote: we are not affected by Bangladesh situation because we are not having any exports presence as of now. And also, we do not import anything from Bangladesh. So this is something which is a non-event for us.

items.statement: Working capital days to remain at current elevated level (~158 days); no further improvement expected
items.quote: It will remain same at this level only. I don't see any further improvement in working capital.

items.statement: Management noted shareholder suggestion for buyback before Oct 1 deadline; will discuss internally
items.quote: Yes, thank you for the suggestion. We have noted your point. And definitely, we'll discuss in the management meetings.

items.statement: Marketing spend to remain at 3-3.5% of revenue
items.quote: Look, we will be sticking to an average marketing spend of 3%, 3.5% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Blanket/quilt sourcing 2-4% cheaper than last year; no plans for in-house manufacturing
items.quote: even actually, we are getting at least 2% to 4% cheaper as compared to last year, the blanket and the quilts. So it doesn't make any sense to put up any manufacturing unit.

items.statement: COCO store inventory: INR30-35 lakh in summer; INR70-80 lakh in winter
items.value: INR35 lakhs to INR30 lakhs; INR70 lakhs to INR80 lakhs
items.quote: In summer season, the inventory is approximately INR35 lakhs to INR30 lakhs. In winter season, it becomes around INR70 lakhs to INR80 lakhs.

items.statement: Guidance may be revised after Q2 once summer trade show and winter season sales data available
items.quote: we can revise our guidance after Q2. So once we have our -- even summer trade show in our hand, which is happening in August last week and also some of the winter season sale, which starts in September and October, so we can revise our guidance.

items.statement: Focus on profitable growth: closed unprofitable stores and SOAs; shifting dependence from winter to summer wear
items.quote: our focus changed completely to profitable growth. So we have to close some of these stores, which were unprofitable. And to compensate that, we have opened some new stores and also we have closed some SOAs in other areas where we were actually incurring some losses.

items.statement: No plans to enter ethnic wear segment; focusing on existing brands and home division
items.quote: See, as of now, we don't have any plans for ethnic wear. We are just concentrating on our existing range. And also on the newer brands, which we've launched in last few years like Rock.it like Cloak & Decker and also our home division.

items.statement: Management targets 12-14% tonnage growth for FY26 and expects EBITDA margin of 15-16% with rate hikes
items.quote: See -- in terms of tonnage growth, see, always every year, at least we expect around 12% to 14% growth because the base has increased now.

items.statement: Management expects 5-6% realization improvement for future periods after June rate hikes
items.quote: Considering the increase in costs, including the increase in diesel rates by some of the states post the election, we increased the freight rates from late June. We increased the rates across all our revenue segments and expe cting the improvement in realization by almost around 5% to 6% for the future periods

items.statement: Capex for FY25 expected around INR200 crores, not more than INR45-50 crores per quarter
items.quote: Yes, around INR200 crores capex even in the -- with the normal growth.

items.statement: Management plans to add around 100 branches in FY25, not less than that
items.quote: Yes. Actually, we are planning to add around 100 branches for the complete full financial year. The number may go up a little bit, but it will not come down. It will not be lesser than that.

items.statement: July tonnage grew 7-8% YoY with 6% price realization improvement
items.quote: Based on the rate increase in June, the price relations per ton is improved by around 6% with a growth in tonnage by around 7% in the month of July.

items.statement: Q1 volumes impacted by driver absenteeism during elections and heatwave, some bookings stopped in Delhi area
items.quote: Yes, even the volumes have been impacted in the current quarter. See, basically, what happened, there were a lot of delays in the services in some of the key transshipment hubs. That's the reason there were some delay in services. And because of these reasons, we were in a position to stop some of the bookings also in some selective areas.

items.statement: EBITDA decreased 8% YoY to INR102 crores, margin down ~2% due to higher vehicle running, employee, toll and rent costs
items.quote: The EBITDA is decreased by almost 8% in absolute terms from INR111 crores to INR102 crores, and percentage to revenue also decreased by around 2%.

items.statement: Vehicle running cost increased 1.36% of revenue (50% absolute) due to higher km by owned vehicles and driver incentives
items.quote: The key reasons for decrease in EBITDA is, one, with a vehicle running head cost, which has increased by almost 1.36% to the revenue. In absolute rupees, it increased by almost around 50%, on account of increasing kilometers covered by the own vehicle and also due to increase in the r ates of driver earnings and incentives

items.statement: Employee cost rose 1.5% of revenue to 17.81% from annual increments and 1,161 more employees
items.quote: The another key cost impacted on the EBITDA margin is around employee cost. This expenses increased by around 1.5% to the revenue from 16% to 17.81%. And the increase in employee cost is mainly on account of annual increments effective from September '23 and also internal promotions on selective basis.

items.statement: Fuel cost decreased 1% of revenue to 29% due to stable diesel prices and higher refinery procurement (33% vs 31%)
items.quote: On the other side, the fuel cost, which is a major cost in our operations, almost around 30% to the Revenue. The fuel cost has not been increased. In fact, it has decreased almost by 1% to the revenue from 30% to, say, 29%.

items.statement: Lorry hire expense % of revenue reduced due to higher owned vehicle km and lower dependency on hired vehicles
items.quote: The lorry hire expenses as a percentage to the income has been reduced. One is because of the increase in our own vehicles, the dependency on the lorry, outside vehicles have been reduced.

items.statement: Freight rates increased 5-10% across categories from mid-June, realized 6% improvement in July across all customers
items.quote: Yes, it is across all our customers. And since we started this exercise in mid of June itself, in the month of July, we saw that the realizati ons are improved around 6%. So this will continue -- around 6% is going to continue

items.statement: Rate hike sufficient to absorb current cost increases; further hikes only if drastic cost changes
items.quote: No, in our view, considering the current again, market conditions also, thi s is enough to take care of whatever increase in expenses as of now. Going forward, if any drastic changes in the expenses, again, we can rethink about the

items.statement: Q1 capex INR50 crores mainly for trucks; own vehicle capacity reached 86,405 tons; debt rose only INR12 crores to INR274 crores
items.quote: In quarter 1 of the current year, we invested almost around INR50 crores into ca pital expenditures, which is predominantly for the purpose of addition of the trucks. With this, our own vehicle capacity has reached to around 86,405 tons as of 30th June

items.statement: Capex slowed after Q1 disturbances; will wait for Q2 tonnage growth before deciding further vehicle additions
items.quote: see initially, we did -- in the month of April, actually, w e did the capex, but post these disturbances and considering our volume impact, actually we have slowed down on the capex as of now. Again, depending on the movement or growth in the tonnage, again, we will decide to increase those vehicles

items.statement: Added 36 branches in Q1, 105 YoY; new branches contributed 3.55% to tonnage; new branch tonnage growing 17-20% YoY
items.quote: We continued our initiative to increase the branches in the current quarter and added around 36 branches.

items.statement: Rent expenses increased due to branch expansion and extra space at key transhipment hubs for expected growth, causing lower utilization
items.quote: The rent expenses is increased on account of increase in the branches and increase in space in key transhipment hubs during the year. We increased the space in key location considering our expected growth in tonnage for the subsequent period.

items.statement: Customer base grew from 8 lakh to 9 lakh YoY; top customers on contractual agreements, rate hikes negotiated individually
items.quote: Further our customer base has increased from 8 lakh to 9 lakh customers over a period of last 1 year.

items.statement: Lease depreciation INR39 crores and finance cost INR16 crores in Q1 under Ind AS accounting for rental expenses
items.quote: Yes. With respect to depreciation, it is around INR39 crores and for finance cost is around INR16 crores. These are related to the rental expenses and accounted as depreciation and finance cost on account of Ind AS entries.

items.statement: Debt increased marginally from INR262 crores to INR274 crores despite INR50 crores capex due to strong operating cash flows
items.quote: Even after investment of 49 Crores, the debt -- correspondingly the debt is not increased. The debt has increased hardly from INR262 crores to INR274 crores. This is on account of good cash flows from our operations.

items.statement: Revenue grew 9% YoY to INR742 crores; tonnage up 8% to 10.7 lakh tons; price realization up 1% to INR6,724/ton
items.quote: During the quarter, we maintained a revenue growth of around 9% from INR683 crores to INR742 crores on a year -on-year ba sis. The growth in revenue is on account of growth in volumes by almost 8% from 10,00,000 tons to 10,70,000 tons, the tonnage has been improved

items.statement: Monsoon season supportive for commodity growth; textile and agro commodities recovering after weak FY24
items.quote: Based on the current trend of monsoon season, we are expecting good support in growth in commodities, which were under performed in FY '24.

items.statement: Local route-wise competitors follow rate increases; minimal volume sacrifice expected as competitors also raising rates
items.quote: In that case, most of them actually the moment we increase the rate, again, they will follow and increase the rate.

items.statement: Temporary workforce hired at higher rates during Q1 disruptions; driver earnings and incentives increased across routes
items.quote: To maintain our workflow, we also appointed the temporary workforce with higher rates that resulted into additional costs. We also increased the rate of driver earnings and incentives between many routes resulted into additional vehicle running costs.

items.statement: Toll booths increased from 1,268 to 1,438 YoY with higher toll rates impacting costs
items.quote: The toll charges have further increased in the current quarter, as compared to year-on-year basis. The number of toll booths have been increased from 1,268 to 1,438 across India and also the rates of toll charges have been increased.

items.statement: No further land monetization planned; sold property had low operational dependency and was used by media business
items.quote: Earlier part of this property is even used by that media business also. That's the reason since our dependency or our usage of that property in our operation was very less. That's the reason considering the low dependence on that particular property, we decided to sel l it, but there are no such -- some surplus assets, again, which are going to be monetized in the going

items.statement: Targets 14-15% CAGR for India business FY25-FY27 and 10% annual growth for overseas business
items.quote: we are trying to have a 14% to 15% CAGR growth rate starting from finan cial year '25 till financial year '27. Overseas business on a top line is anticipated to have a growth of around 10% per annum

items.statement: Expects India business EBITDA margin of 14-15% in next three years after brand reinvestment of 2-3% of sales
items.quote: we anticipate that in the next three years we should be touching 14% to 15% EBITDA margin. Not because the savings, we could not have gone beyond that. With the amount of savings, we could have gone 2% to 3% higher on that. But we need to reinvest on the brand so the investment in the brand would go up by around 2

items.statement: FY25 consolidated EBITDA margin expected to be more than double-digits, around 10-11%
items.quote: short-term EBITDA guidance giving is a difficult job, but I can certainly tell you that it would be more than double-digits. So 10% plus maybe 11% or something of that sort of.

items.statement: India business gross margin improved ~0.5% QoQ to ~44% despite product mix shift to lower-margin online segment
items.quote: from quarter four my gross margin has increased by approximately 0.5% on an India business level which is the right metric to look at it.

items.statement: Targets higher gross margins as remaining INR100-150 crore integration savings materialize over next 6-9 months
items.quote: there is an incremental savings efficiency of INR100 crores to INR150 crores, which will come over the next six months to nine months. So definitely you should see an enhancement in the gross margin over this period

items.statement: Overseas margins compressed due to lower raw material prices impacting top line; prices now stabilized and costs being reduced
items.quote: these numbers are appearing because of reduced raw material prices. And those areas we supply foam to the brand owners and to the mattress manufacturers and therefore the raw mater ial prices impact is far more. These prices are stabilized, or have stabilized. And second, we are also bringing some of our costs down

items.statement: Consumer durables sector (ex-ACs) seeing lukewarm or lower turnover vs prior period; only ACs growing due to intense heat
items.quote: if you look at the last six months, the only consumer durable which is growing is the air conditioners and that's because of intense heat that was there. But all the o thers have been having an absolute lukewarm or actually a little lower turnovers compared to the previous time

items.statement: Integration 85-90% complete; RDCs reduced from ~55 to ~16; distributors now handling Kurlon products; system running smoothly post-quarter
items.quote: the entire integration process is about 85% to 90% complete and we are ready for the upcoming season.

items.statement: Kurlon Q1 revenue ~INR170-175 crore (disrupted); Sheela Foam India ~INR440-450 crore; combined India business normalized FY24 revenue ~INR2,700 crore
items.quote: Kurlon, because of disruption, has been a little bit lower this time. It would be somewhere around say INR170 crores, INR175 crores, whereas Sheela Foam would be around INR44, INR45 crores.

items.statement: Australia capacity expanded from 10,000 to 15,000 tons/annum; Spain from 12,000 to 18,000 tons/annum; both fully commissioned
items.quote: Australia has gone up from about 10,000 tons to 15,000 tons per annum and in Spain we have gone from 12,000 tons to 18,000 tons, which ensures that we are very future-ready as far as those places are concerned.

items.statement: Closed two factories peacefully during integration; fixed cost savings actualized in Q1
items.quote: we closed down two factories very peacefully with all the people being taken care of, and there have been benefits which have ensued thereof. Some of them are already beginning to flow in.

items.statement: Increased online segment sales and 'mattress for every Indian' range; lower gross margin but no marketing costs; effective margin improved 0.1% vs expected 0.4% decline
items.quote: We have increased the sales of online segments. We have increased the sales of the mattress, which is mattress for every Indian, there the gross margins are lesser for the EBITDA of the same because they don't involve marketing costs, et cetera. So effecti vely this margin should have gone down by 0.4% whereas it has increased by 0.1

items.statement: Launched 3-fold PU foam mattress (INR2,000+ with 3-year warranty) for Small Town India to replace cotton mattresses; rolled out in 70-75% of country with positive response
items.quote: we have rolled out a pure PU foam mattress, which is three-fold. So the consumer can actually fold the mattress and put it in one corner. And then they want to use it, they can take it out and unfold it. So we give them the comfort of a home mattress. The product comes with a three-year warranty price point starting from approximately INR2,000 upwards for a single mattress.

items.statement: Urban distribution: ~7,000 outlets (3,000 EBO, 4,000 MBO); added ~700 outlets in Q1; Small Town India: ~5,000 outlets, targeting 7,500-8,000 by FY end
items.quote: both the brands put together would be getting sold in the urban market for approximately 7,000 outlets now. In the last quarter, we would have added stroke revised approximately about 700 odd outlets for both the brands. And this doe s not build in the Small Town India where we have a completely independent channel which we have created

items.statement: Plans ~10% urban channel expansion in current financial year; volume growth from new products, communication, and channel expansion combined
items.quote: active channel, we are looking at approximately expanding the channel by 10%. Means, if I am at 7,000 outlets we will expand by another 10% the channel in the urban market, if that helps answer your question.

items.statement: Not losing market share; Sleepwell grew volume and value; Kurlon up 5-6% last quarter; expanding market via Small Town India and premiumization
items.quote: we are not losing any market share. We may not be gaining on any at the moment but we are not losing any market share. On the other hand, we are expanding the market by the Small Town initiatives or the village initiatives that we are doing

items.statement: New entrants like Nilkamal offering heavy discounts; company focuses on consumer demand creation over channel incentives; brands not comparable in scale
items.quote: there are a set of brands who are driving sales by throwing money at the channel, but that can only take you to a certain distance. We are looking at creating consumer demand and driving growth. So therefore there is a difference there.

items.statement: Furlenco: pre-acquisition run rate INR12 cr/month (INR150 cr/yr), PBT -INR10 cr/month; turned PBT positive Feb at INR14.5-15 cr/month; now INR17 cr/month (INR200 cr+ run rate); option to invest INR100 cr for 9% more by Aug 29
items.quote: Post February, the company turned into PBT positive when it was at a run rate of around say INR14.5 crores, INR15 crores per month top line. Happy to say that the company has last month crossed INR17 crores top line which is a run rate of INR200 crores plus and is PBT positive and gradually improving on the profitability thereof. As regards investments, we have an option of getting another 9% in t

items.statement: Dividend policy debated at Board; historically retained earnings for acquisitions; majority would go to family; not close to paying dividends but recognizes role
items.quote: It's also debated very hotly as far as our Board is concerned. But the few primary reasons is, for example, we kept the money aside for an acquisition like this that has happened. And we always believe that when you give -- I know there are advantages of giving dividends, tax-wise it's definitely on the negative side. We also believe that the majority of the dividend would come just to the family.

items.statement: Integration caused temporary revenue disruption (~INR70 cr vs Q4) and EBITDA margin compression; now 85-90% complete and system running smoothly
items.quote: the revenue was disrupted temporarily because of the integration process and now it is all on track. So as soon as in the next quarter we see this revenue coming up, I think whatever was to be done on the cost side has already been done and you should observe a much better EBITDA on the cost side.

items.statement: ERP integration completed in <1 week vs typical 6-12 months by pre-training staff and switching at FY start (Apr 1)
items.quote: Normally the integration takes -- takes six months to 12 mont hs, but we did that in less than a week and ensuring that all the security, the cybersecurity were taken care of and are being taken care of as we move

items.statement: India business normalized FY24 revenue ~INR2,700 crore; targeting 14-15% CAGR FY25-27
items.quote: Around INR2,700 odd crores for the Indian business last year. On it, we are intending, and I would say we are making efforts and that is what we have been communicating in the past. So we are trying to have a 14% to 15% CAGR growth rate starting from finan cial year '25 till financial year '27

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 revenue INR810 cr (+26% YoY); EBITDA INR60 cr (-23% YoY); margin 7.4%; net profit INR47 cr (+8% YoY)
items.quote: On a consolidated basis for the first quarter under review, we reported revenues of INR810 crores which increased by around 26% year-on-year. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR60 crores, down by about 23% on a year-on-year basis. EBITDA margins were reported at 7.4% for this quarter and the net profit stood at INR47 crores which has actually increased by about 8% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Standalone Q1 revenue INR504 cr (+10% YoY); EBITDA INR48 cr (-22% YoY); margin 9.45%; net profit INR32 cr (-25% YoY)
items.quote: For the first quarter under review on a standalone basis, we reported revenues of INR504 crores which increased by around 10% year-on-year. EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR48 crores which declined by about 22% year-on-year. EBITDA margins were reported at 9.45% for this quarter and the net profit stood at INR32 crores which is down by about 25% this year.

items.statement: Intercompany arm's-length pricing (5-6% margin on COGS) between SSL and KEL reduces reported standalone gross margin; India business level is correct metric
items.quote: when you do it at arm's length, the profit margin that you get from the sister company is much lower. It cannot be as you are telling it to a third party. So generally you take a 5% to 6% profit margin on cost of goods sold. Because of this, the intercompany sales gross margin would be much lesser.

items.statement: Factory closures handled peacefully with all people taken care of; HR practices under review post-integration
items.quote: we closed down two factories very peacefully with all the people being taken care of, and there have been benefits which have ensued thereof. Some of them are already beginning to flow in. On the services side, I shared with you the ERPs, or integration of ERPs as we all know how important IT services are these days.

items.statement: Merger with Kurlon Enterprise Limited filed with NCLT effective Oct 2023; will be seamless conversion at corporate level when order comes
items.quote: we have gone one step ahead to even consolidate both the corporate entity and have already filed for a merger with effect from October 2023. That is the date of the acquisition. And when we chose to do this, there were some actions and some steps taken by us immediately.

items.statement: Outstanding order book at Rs 5,890 crore, up 11% YoY
items.quote: As on Q1FY25, the outstanding order book was to the extent of Rs.5,890 crore, a YoY growth of 11%.

items.statement: Order inflow of Rs 297 crore in Q1 FY25, major order Rs 229 crore for Palladium Mall Surat
items.quote: During Q1FY25, the order inflow was to the extent of Rs.297 crore, major order received was Rs.229 crore for the construction of Palladium Mall, Surat.

items.statement: Revenue guidance of Rs 2,800 crore for FY25
items.quote: See INR2,800 crores, which is what we have thought of for this year , and I definitely feel that we should be in position to reach to INR2,800 crores.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 10-11% for FY25
items.quote: Yes, we can expect, but I too expect as I said there can be some expenses to the last quarter, which is the closing quarter for UP. So there can be some expense, but not to this extent, but that can interfere to some extent but otherwise we can expect 10% to 11% of all throughout the projects.

items.statement: Order inflow guidance of Rs 3,500 crore for FY25
items.quote: Yes, it's 3.5 and we should be able to reach to 3.5.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 12%, down from 12.69% YoY
items.quote: EBIDTA Margin is at 12% vs 12.69%.

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin excluding SDB revenue around 8-9% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: And that margin comes to around 8 to 9%.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 17 crore in Q1 FY25, projected Rs 60 crore for full year
items.quote: INR 17 crores we have already done and you can take it multiplied by 4 or more or less around INR60 crores projected capex during the year.

items.statement: Precast facility utilization at 50-60%, revenue of Rs 180 crore last year, targeting Rs 200-250 crore this year
items.quote: I think this year we wer e able to make a revenue of INR 180 crores out of precast. So probably this year we should be in the range of INR200-250 crores.

items.statement: Precast Phase 2 expansion considered when utilization reaches 70-80% in next 2 years
items.quote: So basically, probably, in next 2 years' time, probably you may reach 70%, 80%, then you can look for Phase 2, right, sir? P. S. Patel: Yes

items.statement: Fund-based debt at Rs 200 crore as of June 30 2024, down from Rs 260 crore after Rs 60 crore directors' loan repayment
items.quote: Yes, I have already mentioned bank borrowing is around INR200 crores.

items.statement: SDB receivables at Rs 225.37 crore as of June 30 2024, Rs 104 crore received in July, Rs 121 crore remaining in 4 tranches by October 2025
items.quote: We have still to receive INR121 crores from SDB, and mainly timeline will be by end of like October '25.

items.statement: UP project receivables at Rs 100 crore, delayed due to PMC strike, expecting resolution in a week
items.quote: Presently, there won't be any claim, but there is one issue which is related to area, which is under discussion, which we are thinking that it will be positively solved. Otherwise, outstanding today is in the range of INR100 crores.

items.statement: UP project incurred Rs 20-25 crore extra costs in Q1 FY25 due to material escalation, overheads and scope confusion
items.quote: So all put together, extra cost was INR20 crores to INR25 crores, significantly affecting the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Expect additional Rs 5-10 crore costs on UP project in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Therefore, we could consider spending not more than INR5 - 10 crores, in the next quarter.

items.statement: Bid pipeline of Rs 6,429 crore across 14 projects, 25% Gujarat, 75% other states
items.quote: I think we have already said that there is about INR6,400 crores of bid pipeline.

items.statement: Expect 1-2 new order confirmations in next 15-20 days or by August end
items.quote: Yes, there are few orders which we are expecting to confirm that in the presently it is at near to closer. So we expect one or two orders maybe in next 15, 20 days or maybe by August end.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 10-15% annually beyond FY25
items.quote: So we are sure that we should be in position to grow every year by 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Most projects have escalation clauses (RBI index for government, item rate for private), UP project was exception without escalation
items.quote: Most of the projects which we are doing today carries that escalation. So if it is a government project, that carries through RBI index escalation o r if it's a private project is Item rate project. So that was the only project which are not having any escalation related to cement, steel, material or labor.

items.statement: UP project scope dispute of Rs 13-14 crore being contested but work executed to avoid defect liability
items.quote: I think it is about INR13-14 crores.

items.statement: Large corporates like Reliance and Adani now accepting precast technology for faster execution
items.quote: At the same time some of the large corporates like Reliance, Adani, these people are also now considering precast as the acceptable technology to move faster because there is always a little bit failure on the project because of the consistency of labor availability and the seasonal issues.

items.statement: Precast business gearing up with focus on building sites, 1-2 orders for execution this year
items.quote: We are now focusing a little bit more on building sites. We have one or two orders on building sites which we are going to execute in this year. So in general if I say the precast business is now gearing up.

items.statement: SMC Highrise project faced labor scarcity post-election and monsoon disruption, now fully mobilized at 3rd floor above basement
items.quote: As we all are aware, after the election, there was a little bit scarcity of labour in the first quarter and presently also there is little bit disturbance since last 15 days because of huge rain in Gujarat. So Surat municipal Corporation Highrise building project is going on there. Now the labour stand has fully mobilized. As such we have reached to third floor of the above the basement and probab

items.statement: Finance cost run rate similar at Rs 13 crore quarterly despite debt reduction due to new project bank guarantee charges and FDOD interest
items.quote: Yes, we can see. P. S. Patel: It will be little bit less. Hetal Patel: It will be a little bit less In terms of this SDB bank guarantee also because we have already received back as on 30 June. So from July onwards, that charge will not be there. And to some extent, other bank guarantees we may also receive on an interest

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin target 20-21% in next couple of years; core hospital segment target 23-24%
items.quote: So, I think even the previous quarters or so I've explained that at a consolidated level in next couple of years, we can look at going from current 17.7% to 20 % to 21% and specifically the core segment, which is a hospital and clinic segment, that is something which is currently at 21% can go up to 23% and 24%.

items.statement: Total project capex for 1,700 bed addition is INR 1,200 crore; INR 200 crore already spent; INR 1,000 crore to be spent over FY25-27
items.value: INR 1,200 crore total; INR 1,000 crore remaining
items.quote: So the 1700 beds on overall basis, the capex of the project cost we are looking at is something like INR 1,200 crores. So out of INR 1,200 crores, INR 200 crores plus has already been incurred in the last 2 023 and 2 024 yea r. So we're expecting the additional INR 1,000 crores to be incurred in the year FY25, FY26, and FY27.

items.statement: Plan to add ~1,700 beds by FY27, taking total to 6,500 beds; 60% brownfield expansion at MedCity, CMI, Whitefield
items.quote: We remain committed to our robust expansion plans, which include the addition of approximately 1,700 beds, taking the total bed count to 6,500 beds by the end of FY 2027.

items.statement: Material cost reduced to 21% of revenue in Q1 FY25 from 23% YoY; target further 100 bps reduction via standardization and consumption optimization
items.quote: Now 21% is not really the best if you ask me, if we can still have a squeezing of another 100 basis points is something which we can still do.

items.statement: India hospital bed density only 15 per 10,000 vs global 29; significant infrastructure shortage creates growth opportunity
items.quote: India has a low hospital bed density with only 15 beds per 10,000 people, significantly lower than the global average of 29 beds. This shortage of basic healthcare infrastructure creates a significant opportunity for us to expand our specialized services to meet the growing healthcare needs and improve the overall healthcare infrastructure in India.

items.statement: Added 446 beds in last year; 12 patient experience centers in Kerala and 2 pharmacies in Karnataka in Q1 FY25; total 229 PECs and 217 pharmacies as of June 2024
items.quote: During this quarter, we added 12 patient experience centers in Kerala and 2 pharmacies in Karnataka in Q1 FY25, reaching a total of 229 patient experience centers and 217 Aster pharmacy branded retail stores as of 30th June 2024.

items.statement: ARPOB grew 12% YoY to INR 44,200 in Q1 FY25; excluding O&M hospitals ARPOB rose 15% to INR 46,800; Whitefield ARPOB ~INR 70,000
items.quote: The ARPOB for Q1 FY25 saw an overall growth of 12% increasing from INR 39,400 to INR 44,200. Excluding O&M hospitals the ARPOB rose by 15% from INR 40,800 to INR 46,800.

items.statement: Insurance payor mix increased 200 bps to 30% in Q1 FY25; scheme business reduced correspondingly; no single specialty >15% of hospital revenue in FY24
items.quote: The payor mix has seen a positive shift, with the contribution from the insurance business increasing by over 200 basis points, reaching 30% now. This growth was offset by a corresponding reduction in their scheme business.

items.statement: Whitefield Hospital occupancy 65% with 350 beds operational; 40 more beds to operationalize; Block D expected later this fiscal year to make it 500+ beds
items.quote: Yeah, see if Bangalore overall is something like 62% occupancy and specifically your Bangalore Whitefield Ho spital, the Aster Whitefield Hospital is something like 65% occupancy.

items.statement: ALOS reduced to 3.2 days in Q1 FY25 from 3.4 days; Kerala cluster ALOS 3.1 days; reduction driven by scheme mix change
items.quote: See our ARPOB growth. Even in my speech I called there are many levers which is driving. The first one I would say is the ALOS reduction. So ALOS usually Aster India ALOS used to be around 3.4 days. And now in the quarter, it has reduced to 3.2 days.

items.statement: No promoter exit intention; evaluating inorganic opportunities and M&A to become top 3 player; may have concrete update in next couple of quarters
items.quote: There is no intention from the promoters to exit. I think the only thing we are quite keen on is building Aster India and like I mentioned in my opening remarks as well our Chairman's vision has always been how do we become one of the top three. So just looking at the right opportunities in terms of mergers, acquisitions that are available that will help us facilitate.

items.statement: Actively seeking inorganic growth in Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu; focusing on multi-specialty hospitals in existing or neighboring states
items.quote: We are actively seeking inorganic growth opportunities with the objective of becoming one of the top three healthcare players in India. We're focusing on acquiring multi-specialty hospitals in states where we already have a presence or in neig hboring states such as Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu.

items.statement: O&M asset-light model paused for 1-2 years to study talent challenges in tier 2/3 cities; Tirupati and Kollam hospitals performing well at double-digit EBITDA margins
items.quote: But right now, we are put a pause we are not acquiring more O&M model but we are studying this present model. We probably need one more year time to understand the O&M model going forward in the tier two, tier three cities.

items.statement: Talent acquisition and retention in tier 2/3 cities is biggest challenge for quaternary care model; O&M model used to derisk
items.quote: But there's always an inherent risk of how do you kind of ensure, because our model is a quaternary care model. We believe in developing quaternary care model in the smaller towns, not the primary and secondary, but quaternary care. So to do that, the talent availability is the biggest challenge.

items.statement: Aster CMI first hospital in South India to achieve NABH Digital Platinum Accreditation
items.quote: Additionally, Aster CMI has become the first hospital in South India to achieve the NABH Digital Platinum Accreditation as well.

items.statement: ROCE surged 200 bps YoY to 16.5%; hospital/clinic ex-O&M ROCE 23.8%; mature hospitals ROCE 30%
items.quote: Optimized capital allocation coupled with margin improvement our ROCE has experienced a significant growth. ROCE surged 200 basis points YoY reaching 16.5%. Hospital and clinic segment, excluding O&M asset light hospital, ROC E rose to 23.8% from 22.3%. Matured hospitals saw an impressive increase in ROCE by over 300 basis points, reaching to 30% in Q1 F Y25.

items.statement: Karnataka/Maharashtra cluster occupancy improved to 62% from 55% YoY; Whitefield scaling drove improvement
items.quote: With the scaling performance of a new Whitefield Hospital at Bangalore location, the cluster witnessed a notable improvement in occupancy levels, rising to 62% in Q1 FY25 from 55% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Price increases contribute only 3-3.5% to ARPOB growth; main drivers are ALOS reduction, case mix, Whitefield ramp-up, robotic surgeries (400-500 in Q1)
items.quote: In addition to this, the price increase is something which we, you know, it's contributing only to 3%-3.5% but in addition to this one, it's also a case mix. We are doing more robotic surgeries. If you know that last year, we've done more than 1,200. But what I see is that in only the last quarter, we have done more than 400 to 500 surgeries.

items.statement: Wholesale pharmacy business outsourced causing 3% YoY revenue decline in labs/pharmacy segment; retail pharmacy EBITDA margin focus
items.quote: So Harith, that is primarily because our wholesale part of the business to an extent we have, you know, we were working on a strategy where we outsource some of this wholesale business and that is resulting in this reflection on the number.

items.statement: No specific dividend or buyback mentioned; focus on growth and M&A deployment of INR 1,700 crore cash
items.quote: And as of now, we have not yet decided it how do we deploy it? We are still looking at a lot of inorganic opportunities and looking at the various acquisition opportunities also.

items.statement: Price revisions are strategic, spread across geographies and departments; not a uniform annual hike.
items.quote: So, we don't take at one go across all hospitals because it all depends on the geography and the departments and the hospitals.

items.statement: Cash patients are price-sensitive; insurance contracts fixed for 2-3 years; pricing decisions consider local competition and value proposition.
items.quote: Earlier it used to be kind of every year we used to take a price revision to cover the inflation but now it's not the case because the insurance penetration has increased in the larger metro cities.

items.statement: Promoter pledge at 98.87%; goal to reduce it by end of this financial year as overseas loan is small and pledge requirement lower.
items.quote: I think our efforts are towards reducing the pledge definitely. There is a goal towards kind of reducing it towards the close of the year.

items.statement: ARPOB expected to grow 7-8% CAGR over next 3-4 years, driven by case mix change and non-metro pricing scope.
items.quote: we should be really able to grow at least 7 to 8 percentage. I think that is something which is very much possible.

items.statement: Price increase contribution ~3-3.5% annually; insurance contracts yield double-digit hikes every two years.
items.quote: Around three, three and half percentage is something which we always look for price increase growth.

items.statement: Inorganic focus on South India and adjoining states (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu); UP a long-term option; target hospitals 350-400 beds expandable to 500+.
items.quote: Our prime focus continues to be South India. We are the dominant player in South India with the second largest number of beds right now and aspiring to become largest through our expansion plans and M&A opportunities.

items.statement: Open to merging with a platform to accelerate growth; evaluating opportunities actively post-segregation; firmer view in next couple of quarters.
items.quote: if you're looking at merging with a platform, that would save us some time and help us accelerate the growth. So we are keeping our eyes open.

items.statement: Andhra Ramesh target: mid-teens EBITDA margin in next 2-3 quarters, eventually close to 20%; Telangana Prime hospital mid-teens comfortable.
items.quote: The target is to take the EBITDA margins to the mid-teen and eventually all our efforts is to see if we can take it beyond 20%, or close to our, not beyond, at this point, closer to 20% EBITDA margins.

items.statement: Whistleblower complaint under investigation; relates to undisclosed related party transactions and conflicted business activities; financial impact not significant.
items.quote: this is something related to conflicting business activities and all like some of these whistleblower was related to those activities and all like some of the related party transaction which was not intimated properly.

items.statement: Non-metro greenfield capex INR 1-1.4 crore per bed; brownfield/leased INR 60-75 lakh per bed.
items.quote: in case of a non-metro, if it's a greenfield project, we may be able to spend something like 1 to 1.4 crore per bed if it is a greenfield project and if it is like a brownfield or a say or the leas ed project, we are looking at something like INR 60, 70 to 75 lakh rupees per bed would be the leased

items.statement: Revenue mix: Kerala 55%, Karnataka+Maharashtra ~38%, Andhra+Telangana 11%; Karnataka share may exceed 40% due to non-metro growth.
items.quote: Kerala's 55% and Karnataka and Maharashtra is around 35%, 38% revenue contribution and 11% is the Andhra and Telangana.

items.statement: EBITDA contribution: Kerala ~60% (INR 120 cr), Karnataka+Maharashtra ~35% (INR 70 cr) of INR 200 cr hospital/clinic EBITDA.
items.quote: Out of 200 crores, which is contributed by hospitals and clinic, 120 crores is contributed by Kerala. That's almost come to 60%. And when it comes to Karnataka and Maharashtra, again, it's 35% is the contribution from the EBITDA point of view also.

items.statement: Blended EBITDA margin target 20-21% in 3-4 years (from ~17%); hospital/clinic segment target 23-24% (from 20.8%).
items.quote: from current to 20 to 21 percentage. And specifically in terms of hospitals and clinic segment, which is where we get 94% of our revenue. There we are currently 20.8, and that is something which we can think sustainably. We can maintain something like in 23 to 24% in next two, three to four years.

items.statement: Kerala cluster ARPOB ~INR 42k, EBITDA margin 22.7% can mature to 25% via brownfield expansion and manpower optimization.
items.quote: we see that with the current EBITDA margin of 22.7 %, it can really mature at 25% so that is something which is possible for Kerala cluster.

items.statement: Karnataka+Maharashtra cluster ARPOB ~INR 60k (ex-Whitefield >INR 70k), EBITDA margin 21% (ex-Whitefield 23.2%) can reach near 30% with occupancy improvement.
items.quote: If you are something at INR 70K specifically in Karnataka, Maharashtra, you can look at my EBITDA margin something like near 30%.

items.statement: Andhra+Telangana cluster ARPOB ~INR 30k, EBITDA margin 10% can go to near 20% with government scheme re-entry and capital Amaravati development.
items.quote: Andhra Telangana anyway, Dr. Nitish has already called out previously. Currently it's at a low at 10%, but it has got a potential with INR 30,000 ARPOB go up to near 20% margin.

items.statement: Total capex for 1,700 bed addition ~INR 1,000 crore; funded by INR 1,500 crore cash from GCC sale plus operating cash flows; no immediate dilution needed.
items.quote: The CAPEX requirement that we have is nearly INR 1000 crore for all these 1700 beds. So that basically clearly indicates that the India cash flow will more than be sufficient to take care of the CapEx requirements going forward.

items.statement: No equity raise planned for expansion; dilution only if share swap for M&A/merger with platform; excess cash may be returned to shareholders.
items.quote: we are definitely not looking at unless dilution is happening naturally as Alisha was highlighting, you know, if ther e are some share swap opportunities and which leads to addition of assets or you know which leads to you know a potential merger or integration with another you know platform that could only lead to dilution

items.statement: Kerala occupancy 75% in Q1 (seasonally low); brownfield adds 100 beds each at Medcity (80% occ) and Kannur (95% occ); daycare surgeries rising.
items.quote: Aster Medcity is where I have 80% occupancy, near 80% occupancy, with a 750 bed hospital, I'm adding 100 beds. So and also in Kannur, where I'm 95% occupancy, I'm adding another 100 beds.

items.statement: Kerala super-specialty growth: oncology +31%, cardiology +26%, gastro/liver transplant +21-22%; high-end cases (transplants, DBS, TAVI, robotic) rising.
items.quote: oncology growth has been a very good growth in the last quarter, quarter on quarter. So almost a 31% oncology growth we have, and specifically th e cardiology department has grown by 26

items.statement: High-end quaternary care in large hospitals (>300 beds, 60-70% quaternary) is margin-accretive due to asset leverage, insurance coverage, and daycare migration.
items.quote: It is going to be margin-accretive to not dilute the margins because we are able to spread the assets and leverage on the expertise available.

items.statement: Strong demand in tier-2/3 cities; Kerala cash patients 60-80% enabling pricing power; insurance penetration improving affordability for high-end care.
items.quote: the future aspiration is in tier two, tier three cities. And we see there is a great demand for quality health care.

items.statement: Andhra government scheme re-entry enabled by political change; renewed economic activity around Vijayawada/Amaravati capital development.
items.quote: Earlier we had to stay away from the government scheme patients there, but now we've taken initiatives to open up the government scheme patients, which is a norm in Andhra.

items.statement: GCC sale did not impact international patient inflows; post-segregation incentives may increase referrals from GCC hospitals.
items.quote: the inflow of the patients from the GCC to India was independent of the GCC's patient referred from the GCC hospitals, but post segregation, nothing much has changed, but we are further evaluating opportunities there because at present, we are not concerned about the dip in the numbers.

items.statement: Excess cash may be returned to shareholders if not deployed in M&A within a year.
items.quote: If we are able to utilize it well, you know, we would use them for these opportunities. And if not, I think we would also find out where to return it back to the shareholders.

items.statement: Pricing strategy monitors price leaders in each geography; Kerala cash-patient dominance differentiates from metro peers.
items.quote: if I'm market leader, then I should be the first one to really take up the pricing risk. So it all depends on the market mix geographies and also the case mix, which helps us to do the pricing.

items.statement: No new greenfield capex planned; regular capex for NPDs and capacity improvements only
items.quote: Our large capex was on Hyderabad plant, which we've done. Our purpose is to now leverage that. As of now the regular capex of NPDs and expansions and capacity improvements and other things that we do, any large capex as of now, not yet, but if there is, we will come back to you.

items.statement: Hyderabad greenfield plant started commercial production; will take a couple more months to stabilize operations
items.quote: We've initiated commercial production at our greenfield Hyderabad plant designed as an Industry 4.0 facility. This plant would deliver superior products at competitive costs and offer proximity to South and Western India markets. It will take a couple of more months to stabilize the operations, but we are confident of being fully ready for the next seasonal pickup.

items.statement: ECD segment grew 5.8% YoY in Q1; Jan-Jun period grew 14.5% in ECD and high-teens in fans
items.quote: mark-to-market sell-in performance has been lower in Q1. And I will explain the sell -in performance. Let me touch upon the ECD. Summers have been actually very good for the cooling categories, fans and coolers. But this has also led to inventory stock -outs in several pockets for Orient. The summer started early in some, followed by West and then a late intense one in East and North. This propell

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 249 bps YoY and 237 bps QoQ to 33.1% driven by price increase, mix and cost savings
items.quote: For the quarter of April to June, quarter one, our overall revenue grew by 7% year-on-year, standing at INR755 crores. Gross margins expanded by 249 basis points year-on-year, and 237 basis points quarter-on-quarter sequentially, and stands at 33.1%, driven by a combination of price increase, mix and cost savings.

items.statement: Price increases of 3-3.5% taken in fans category in two tranches during Q1
items.quote: We've done price increase in our fans category in two tranches in quarte r 1. One was early April and the other one was in June, largely in the ball park tune of about 3% to 3.5% is what we passed on to the consumers

items.statement: Spark Sanchay program delivering ~2% annualized cost reduction
items.quote: Our Spark Sanchay program aimed at driving cost leadership is deeply ingrained in the organization, consistently delivering approximately 2% annualized cost reduction and helping us in mitigating commodity and pricing risk.

items.statement: Value-added and differentiated SKUs in ceiling fans gaining traction; premium and super premium fans among top market share players
items.quote: Value-added and differentiated SKUs in ceiling are gaining traction for us and large size inquiries and tenders have started regenerating post -elections. Overall, our Lighting and Switchgear business has grown by 10.2%.

items.statement: DTM states now 10 (added J&K and Himachal); DTM states grew 23% in fans; DTM revenue share ~one-third
items.quote: Our complete drive behind the DTM strategy, with focused distribution expansion and sales execution excellence, is resulting in better growth and market share gains in these states. We have now added two more states in quarter one, Jammu & Kashmir, along with Himachal Pradesh, taking our total count to 10 states. Our DTM states have grown by 23% in Fans category in quarter one, which is a strong p

items.statement: Direct service network expanded to 16 states; significant improvement in service ads and perceptions
items.quote: With consumer centricity as a cornerstone of our strategy, we are also expanding direct service network. We've added seven more states, and now we do 16 states through direct service network for better consumer experience. And we are seeing a significant i mprovement in our service ads and perceptions.

items.statement: E-com channels delivered high double-digit sell-out growth in cooling; gained market share in ceiling fans on e-comm platforms
items.quote: We have done high double-digit sell-out growth on e-com channels for cooling category, which is for both fans and coolers. We have gained market share in the ceiling fan category on e-comm platforms.

items.statement: Lighting and Switchgear business grew 10.2%; consumer lighting high-teens volume growth despite value contraction; B2B deep double-digit value growth
items.quote: The consumer lighting segment continued to face price erosion, but showed high -teens volume growth, a steep increase in the B2B segment and improved distribution of switchgears and wires, leading to double-digit growth this quarter. Value-added and differentiated SKUs in ceiling are gaining traction for us and large size inquiries and tenders have started regenerating post -elections. Overall, ou

items.statement: Market share inching up or holding across geographies based on third-party data for Jan-Jun period
items.quote: So, if you look at the complete impact of sell -in and sell-out across two quarters, our market share based on third-party data is inching up or holding across geographies.

items.statement: Exports degrew due to geopolitical issues in African market with large dependency
items.quote: We degrew in exports because we were slightly dependent on one African country where there have been geopolitical situations. but that's the larger impact.

items.statement: Employee cost at INR77 cr (up 15% YoY); senior management onboarding completed; no major restructuring planned
items.quote: So Achal, this quarter, the employee costs had impact of the increments and other things. Over a period of time, as I said, we've made investments on the structure, and I think is this the going rate. Obviously, the structures have been put , we will leverage this employee structures much better to get our top-line growth and other things.

items.statement: No changes to ESOP pool yet
items.quote: Aditya Bhartia: And any changes in the ESOP, sir Ravindra Singh Negi: Sorry, I didn't get. Aditya Bhartia: Employee stock option pool. Any changes being made over there as well? Ravindra Singh Negi: No, not yet.

items.statement: TPW contribution to fans industry estimated at 25-30%; company in line with industry
items.quote: Firstly, the industry, depending on brand to brand, would hover between 25% to 30% as TPW contribution to the overall fans. Now when we look at our fans business, and when we talk about DTM ma rket and non-DTM markets, that's general trade. We've got large format retail. We've got e -com and we have got exports. So on the general trade, we've seen growth. We had a sell-out approach. And that's why

items.statement: Capacity constraints in TPW fans limited sell-in during peak summer demand
items.quote: This propelled unanticipated demand for fans, especially TPW category, while capacity limitations restricted our ability to meet peak demand, we saw encouraging sell -out growth. Having said that, we could have done more sell-in, but for the capacity constraints, specifically in TPW , all this resulting in a modest 5.8% growth in the ECD segment, but that is for Q1 standalone.

items.statement: McKinsey costs will not continue from Q2 FY25 onwards
items.quote: As far as Mckinsey is concerned, we've said in the last call also that this will be the last quarter, where we will have a payout impact. We do not quantify the Mckinsey payout. But yes, next quarter onwards, it will not be there in the expense item.

items.statement: Hyderabad plant to cater to South, West and export markets; supplier ecosystem also investing in Hyderabad
items.quote: Our entire purpose is to get our cost structures of manufacturing TPW there. While it will cater in the beginning to the South and Western part of India, we also expect with our cost structures coming down there, we will be able to create a competitive product for exports also. So the work is on. We will start leveraging the entire Hyderabad cost efficiencies in the next couple of quarters. So we

items.statement: DTM strategy to remain hybrid model; no fixed target for number of states; constant quarterly evaluation
items.quote: So Dhruv, we are very clear and when we articulated our strategic pillars or strategy in action, that we will have a hybrid model. The purpose of DTM states was saying, any state where there is a larger potential for the brand, and we are not able to lever age that potential, we went ahead and did. There are states which are run by our master distributor, and we are able to justify and do get good

items.statement: Revenue growth expected to be higher than Q4 FY24 (5%) and targeting high single digit to double digit; EBITDA margin expansion guidance of 100 bps maintained for FY25
items.quote: Our guidelines has been that we want to grow EBITDA by at least 100 basis points, even in the current really difficult market condition, we are committed and you look at this quarter also the EBITDA has gone up by 100 basis points and is now close to 13%.

items.statement: Medium-term revenue growth target of 12-15% with focus on profitable growth
items.quote: Medium term, we would love the growth rates to move to 12% to 15%, but we are hoping for the market to correct, and we are also very watchful on profitable growth.

items.statement: Capex guidance of Rs 100 crore for FY25, primarily for Tommy Hilfiger COCO stores, IT and store renovations
items.quote: So, our capex is likely to be in the range of 100 crores, largely to be spent on some COCO stores on the PVH side, some IT capex and some renovation of stores.

items.statement: Added 40,000+ sq ft net retail space in Q1 FY25 with ~30 new stores; committed to 15% net square footage growth for FY25
items.quote: We have added more than 40,000 square feet net of retail space in Q1 with opening of nearly 30 high quality stores. We remain committed to growing net retail space by around 15%.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 80 bps to 55.2% in Q1 FY25 driven by better price realization, premiumization and sourcing efficiency
items.quote: GP has moved up to 55.2%, a gain of 80 basi s points with dual benefit of better price realization as well as lower, more efficient product cost

items.statement: EBITDA grew ~20% to Rs 123 crore with 100 bps margin expansion to ~12.9% post-IndAS
items.quote: Most of these GP gain has flown into EBITDA which saw nearly 20% growth to Rs. 123 crores versus last year value of Rs. 103 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 impacted by elections, heat wave and fewer wedding dates; markets remain subdued but slightly better than last year
items.quote: Markets have been subdued for a while and this quarter saw impact of elections, peak heat wave and fewer wedding dates which impacted t raffic across offline and online channels

items.statement: Adjacent categories (footwear, womenswear, kidswear, innerwear) now >20% of AFL revenue, growing double-digit; USPA adjacent share ~30%
items.quote: The share of adjacent category like footwear, womenswear, kidswear, innerwear has crossed 20% revenue share of AFL and has grown in the last one year at double digit.

items.statement: Online D2C business grew >60% YoY with improved channel profitability; B2C now ~50% of online and growing faster
items.quote: There is handsome growth in online direct -to-consumer b usiness that has grown more than 60% year -on-year and delivered higher channel profitability as well

items.statement: Gross working capital days stable; inventory days reduced by 3 days, stock turns improved to 4x with flat inventory value despite 10% revenue growth
items.quote: With tight control on inventory, business has grown by 10% with flat inventory value overall and delivering stock turns of four with lowering of inventory days by three days.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 225 crore end-Q1; may rise ~50 crore next quarter due to seasonal inventory build but will be pared with free cash flow
items.quote: Our net debt was around 225 crores. There is a seasonality, next quarter it could go up by 50-odd crores here because we have to build the inventory for the season and a bigger scale.

items.statement: Delayed EOSS to end-June vs industry mid-June; tight discounting control improved price realization and sell-through
items.quote: A key highlight was control on discounting where we delayed EOSS to end of June, while industry had been discounting by mid-June.

items.statement: Like-to-like retail growth 1.5% in Q1 FY25 vs normal expectation of >5%; satisfied given industry negative LTL
items.quote: As far as like-to-like growth is concerned, while our normal expectation is above 5%, but in the current market condition, it would be a very satisfying number because we have seen in the industry, the like-to-like numbers are negative.

items.statement: A&P spend ~3% of revenue in Q1 (typically 3-4% for full year); campaigns weighted toward season-end
items.quote: So, in Q1, typically it is slightly lower than 3% because the campaigns happens towards the end of season. So, we are in between that 3% to 4% spend, but for this quarter it was around 3%.

items.statement: Converted 60 Tommy Hilfiger stores from FOFO to COCO; no CK stores converted
items.quote: We have 60 stores in Tommy Hilfiger which are now COCO stores.

items.statement: Arrow brand at low single-digit EBITDA; targeting mid-single digit in near term as wedding season improves and scale builds
items.quote: Arrow remains in a low single digit brand and our first task is to take it to mid-single digit brand and in the current market condition believe the wedding dates are in the second half that the performance will improve.

items.statement: Flying Machine at breakeven/low single-digit EBITDA, ~1 year behind Arrow in turnaround journey
items.quote: So, we have said we are on that journey. It's a very, very low single digit close to about breakeven kind of a number.

items.statement: Footwear adjacency facing regulatory changes; engaging with policymakers and preparing supply chain for compliance
items.quote: As far as the footwear results is concerned, there are some regulation changes, and we are in touch with the policymakers and we are making sure that our supply chain is geared for whatever the change required.

items.statement: Market conditions remain challenging and subdued; growth dependent on external environment improvement
items.quote: Markets have been difficult for a couple of quarters. Summer, there were some specific issue linked to elections for example. The global warmin g or warming in India is the reality, May saw that. The markets are sort of challenging and subdued currently

items.statement: Minority interest impact seasonal; non-PVH portfolio profitability expected to improve in H2 with festivals and wedding calendar
items.quote: What happens is that there is a seasonality in different businesses and the PVH part benefit from premiumization. So, that's really helping. But w e get a little more business in H2, in some other brands, the festivals and the wedding calendar, makes a little better difference

items.statement: Volume growth guidance of 15% for FY25 maintained; long-term EBITDA margin guidance of 12-13% ex inventory gains/losses reiterated
items.quote: No, I think on a long -term basis, 12% to 13% EBITDA margin is sustainable. This quarter was impacted slightly by product mix.

items.statement: April-May demand was robust; June saw weakness due to PVC price decline and channel destocking, continuing into July; last-mile demand remains strong due to affordable raw material, real estate and infrastructure growth
items.quote: So you're right, April and May demand was robust. And like I said, we have plans to aggressively debottleneck existing facilities as well.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin at 9.6% due to adverse product mix (higher agri share) and higher A&P spend (>2.5% of revenue); long-term 12-13% EBITDA margin sustainable ex inventory gains/losses
items.quote: The two major reasons for that one has been product. While we have grown across segments, both have been higher in the agriculture space where the

items.statement: Bihar plant (45,000 tonnes phase 1) to be operational by January 2025, preponed from March; debottlenecking of 35,000-40,000 tonnes across existing plants (Jaipur, Silvassa, Kolhapur, Haridwar, Chennai) over 3-4 quarters; unbudgeted capex a
items.quote: We expect Bihar to be operational by January, which will add -- so previously, we had guided for end of quarter 4, and we have tried our best to prepone that.

items.statement: Overall working capital improved to 80 days in June from 95 days in March; receivables improved to 61 days from 83 days; inventory days increased to 70 from 52; channel finance sanctions increased to Rs.155 crores
items.quote: Our overall working capital stood at 80 days in June as compared to 95 days in March 2024. As we had guided, Receivables have shown marked improvement at 61 days in June '24 from 83
