items.quote: Net debt stood at INR3,832 crores as of June '24, higher by 3% over March numbers due to increase in working capital borrowing. Leverage ratios sustained over March '24 levels. Net debt to Equity and Net debt to EBITDA remained at 0.80x and 1.76x respectively.

items.statement: EPR cost of INR25 crore charged to P&L in Q1; will be passed through going forward
items.quote: There is still some cost of about INR25 crores which has been charged to the P&L. Going forward, this will also be passing through this as well.

items.statement: Mobility Solutions business contributes 3-4% of revenue, growing faster than core business
items.quote: However, as of now, it contributes to around 3% to 4% of the overall top line. But it's a business that is growing at a much faster rate as compared to the other part of the business.

items.statement: JK Tornel Mexico sales declined 13% YoY to MXN1,234M (INR600 cr); EBITDA margin sustained at 8.7%
items.quote: JK Tornel Mexico registered the quarterly sales of MXN1,234 million, equivalent to nearly INR600 crores, lower by about 13% on a year -on-year basis. EBITDA margins sustained at 8.7%, that is MXN108 million equivalent to INR52 crores.

items.statement: Cavendish Industries revenue INR975 cr with 14.3% EBITDA margin in Q1
items.quote: Cavendish posted a top line of INR975 crores with a n EBITDA of INR139 crores, registering an operating margin of 14.3%.

items.statement: Consolidated capacity utilization over 80%; radials at 90%+
items.quote: Consolidated capacity utilization for the quarter was over 80%.

items.statement: PCR and TBR project of INR800 crore completed; ongoing expansion INR1,400 crore
items.quote: PCR and TBR project of INR800 crores has been completed and the ongoing expansion is about INR1,400 crores project, which is in the TBR, Passenger car radial and All steel light truck radial category.

items.statement: Company does not provide specific revenue or earnings guidance
items.quote: As you all are aware, Nucleus Software does not provide any specific revenue earning guidance.

items.statement: No saturation in domestic market; good traction in domestic and international markets
items.quote: No, there's no indication or belief that the market is saturated. In fact, as we have been maintaining, we are getting good traction both from domestic market as well as from outside markets.

items.statement: Conversations ongoing with prospects in at least 8 countries for FinnOne Neo or FinnAxia rollouts; pipeline building reasonably well
items.quote: we continue to talk to customers in at least 8 countries about rolling out FinnOne Neo or FinnAxia products for adding value to their businesses. And simultaneously, our pipeline is also building reasonably well.

items.statement: Repricing pending for 20% of customer base; nothing happened this quarter; timeline uncertain
items.quote: So as we had mentioned in the media interview, nothing has happened in this particular quarter on that front. And the balance 20% we are talking to them both in terms of either they upgrading to FinnOne Neo platform or continuing with the FinnOne platform.

items.statement: Majority of repriced customers continue on old version rather than migrating to newer version
items.quote: As of now, I think the higher percentage is on continuing on the old version.

items.statement: Employee cost increase is normal run rate; hikes above industry average to retain and attract talent
items.quote: As far as that is concerned, it is a normal run rate and we have done, what I mentioned in the media interview was, we have done more than the industry hike.

items.statement: Revenue growth slower than expected; exact reasons to be shared next quarter
items.quote: So it's slower than what we had expected, that which we can certainly say. The exact reasons, maybe we'll come back to you next quarter.

items.statement: No customer lost due to repricing
items.quote: No. We have not lost any customer because of the repricing.

items.statement: Entire Q1 revenue from existing customers; no revenue from new customers
items.quote: This quarter's entire revenue is from existing customers.

items.statement: Product revenue Rs 168 crore, services revenue Rs 27 crore out of total Rs 195 crore
items.quote: INR 168 crores is from products and INR 27 crore fees from services, out of 195.

items.statement: Domestic revenue 58%, international 42% in Q1 FY25 vs 48% domestic, 52% international in Q1 FY24
items.quote: For India revenue domestic revenue 58% of our total revenue and international is 42%.

items.statement: Pricing based on value delivered; no fixed formula; can be per loan, per transaction, or portfolio size based
items.quote: The pricing of both our products, the older product as well as newer product is directly dependent on the value that these products are able to deliver to our customers.

items.statement: Single-digit number of customers moved off older version; no breakup of old vs new version customers provided
items.quote: So there are single digit number of customers, which who have moved out of our older version, that is there. But we may not be able to give you the breakup of how many are on the old and how many are on the new.

items.statement: Lead times higher due to pricing complexity; working to minimize lead times
items.quote: Yes. So lead times are higher and part of the lead times being part of the existing lead times are higher is also this is bit of complexity in pricing and so on.

items.statement: Board will decide on buyback or dividend; cash retained for investments in revenue, tools, new technology
items.quote: Whereas the other questions related to buyback or dividend is concerned, that decision will be taken by the board and we will update you guys.

items.statement: Building Islamic version of FinnOne Neo for Middle East and Malaysia markets
items.quote: the latest enhancement is in FinnOne Neo, we are now building the Islamic version, which is used in the Middle East, Malaysia etcetera.

items.statement: Added 62 employees in Q1; plan to onboard sales senior leadership in different regions
items.quote: Yes, we have added 62 Nucleics to our team and talking about growth in Southeast Asia, Australia, etcetera, yes our conversations with the customers in those geographies, they are continuing and we are quite confident that the growth will start happening in coming quarters.

items.statement: Order book Rs 813.4 crore (Rs 752.2 crore product, Rs 61.2 crore projects/services) vs Rs 780 crore previous quarter
items.quote: The Order book position is Rs. 813.4 crore, including Rs. 752.2 crore of product business and Rs. 61.2 crore of project and services business.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA Rs 28.8 crore (14.7% margin) vs Rs 58 crore (27.6%) QoQ and Rs 62.3 crore (30.1%) YoY; cost of delivery 75.5% of revenue vs 63.5% QoQ and 60.5% YoY
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is at Rs. 28.8 crore (14.7% of Revenue), against Rs 58 crore (27.6% of Revenue), QoQ and Rs. 62.3 crore (30.1% of Revenue) YoY.

items.statement: Gross fixed asset addition Rs 3.02 crore (Rs 2.6 crore computers/servers, Rs 0.3 crore furniture, Rs 0.1 crore office equipment, Rs 0.02 crore software)
items.quote: During the quarter, there is a gross addition of fixed assets of Rs. 3.02 crores, consisting primarily of Rs. 2.6 crores on computer & servers, Rs. 0.3 crore on Furniture and Fixtures, Rs. 0.1 crore on Office Equipments and Rs. 0.02 crore on Software.

items.statement: Receivables Rs 175.4 crore vs Rs 166.2 crore previous quarter
items.quote: With regard to receivables, we are at Rs. 175.4 crore against Rs. 166.2 crore previous quarter.

items.statement: USD 3.0 million forward contracts at average rate 83.82; mark-to-market gain Rs 0.04 crore in hedging reserve
items.quote: In terms of foreign currency hedges, on June 30, 2024 we had USD 3.0 million dollars of forward contracts at an average rate of 83.82.

items.statement: Order book execution timeline typically 3-10 years, average 5-7 years
items.quote: It will be executed in the long term in the sense that when we sign the deals, we sign for typically 3 years to 10 years as well. So probably 5-7 years

items.statement: Q1 margins not sustainable; confident of improvement from current 14.7% EBITDA margin but no number provided
items.quote: what you see in Q1 is, what all we are going to improve from that. How much? Is something we will not be able to provide a number.

items.statement: Hoshin Kanri initiative based on Toyota Production System for continuous improvement and enhanced customer experience
items.quote: This is called Hoshin Kanri, based on Toyota Production System Principles. This is to bring in continuous and long term improvements in all areas of our work for the ultimate objective of significantly enhancing our end customer experience.

items.statement: Focus shifting more to international markets including developed markets like Australia and Japan; domestic traction remains good
items.quote: the focus is now more and more on international markets beginning with, including both whether where we are operating already and we are also looking at developing a couple of developed markets getting into.

items.statement: Both CapEx and subscription pricing models available domestically and internationally; cloud enabling subscription model for smaller customers
items.quote: Okay we have actually both models now, pricing models now on level. If that is your question, we go for a CapEx model also. We go for a recurring subscription model also.

items.statement: Expect double-digit operating margin for full year FY25, better than 10.7% in FY24
items.quote: So, we are looking for certainly a double-digit margin. But always, the first quarters are good in terms of margin as it's a very heavy quarter from a battery perspective. But for the full year, definitely, we are looking for double-digit operating margin.

items.statement: Target mid-single-digit growth in battery segment, double-digit growth in flashlights, and strong growth in lighting
items.quote: We are looking forward for a mid-single-digit growth in the battery coming time, double-digit growth in the flashlight and in lighting it is a very wide space available.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 180 crore investment for alkaline battery plant with 360 million units capacity
items.quote: And lastly, for an update, in line with our progress in the alkaline battery segment and our optimistic outlook on this category, the Board of the company has approved an investment of Rs. 180 crore to set up an alkaline plant with a capacity of 360 million units.

items.statement: Alkaline plant to be commissioned within one year, targeting 50% capacity utilization in 3-4 years
items.quote: We are setting up this plant, which will come into commission within a year's time, at which point of time we think that we will grow much higher than the current level.

items.statement: Carbon-zinc battery market muted due to weak rural demand; alkaline batteries growing at ~20%
items.quote: The segment of carbon-free batteries, which still constitutes nearly 90% of the battery market by value, remained muted during the quarter, primarily due to weak rural demand, and our performance was in line with the market.

items.statement: Alkaline battery market growing at around 20% and expected to continue in foreseeable future
items.quote: Yes. It is already growing at double-digit. It is growing at around 20% odd. And we expect that trend to continue for, I mean, in the foreseeable future at least.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA and PAT increased 14.2% and 18.5% respectively due to cost initiatives and favorable input costs
items.quote: For the quarter, both increased by 14.2% and 18.5%, respectively. These came as a result of cost initiatives and favorable input costs.

items.statement: Lighting segment turned EBITDA positive at 3.1% vs break-even last year
items.quote: Even our small professional luminous business showing 50% growth, the overall business would show a marginal growth of 1.4% only in revenue due to the higher prices prevailing in this period of last year. Also the business turned with a positive EBITDA at 3.1% vis-à-vis the break-even situation last year.

items.statement: Alternative channels (modern retail, e-commerce, quick commerce, institutional) at 15% of revenue, targeting >16% by year-end
items.quote: So, currently we are at about 15% of the alternative channels that I mentioned, and I think obviously it is our day-to-day endeavor to go higher than that and maybe by the end of the year, we would try to go beyond 16% at least, if not more.

items.statement: Alkaline battery revenue grew 67% YoY; rechargeable flashlights now 35% of flashlight portfolio
items.quote: Though of a small base, on the back of a 52% growth last year, we realized a 67% increase in value terms during the quarter.

items.statement: LED bulb volumes up 6%, emergency bulbs up 66%, consumer luminous up 12%, professional luminous up 50%
items.quote: We had handsome volume growth in LED bulbs by 6%, emergency bulbs by 66%, consumer luminous by 12%. Even our small professional luminous business showing 50% growth

items.statement: Value alkaline manufacturing in India provides at least 10% cost advantage over imports
items.quote: I would say for the value alkaline; the difference would be certainly at least 10% in cost where we will be favorable by making it in the country.

items.statement: Battery-operated flashlight degrowth slowed to 3% from 15%+ trend; rechargeable flashlights gaining traction
items.quote: This resulted in the battery-operated flashlight revenue de-growing by a very small 3% against 15% plus trend noticed in the previous year.

items.statement: Duracell leads alkaline market at 5x Eveready's size; Eveready is second player
items.quote: Major player is, of course, Duracell. So, we are second, but they are quite a lot ahead of us. They will be 5x at least of our size.

items.statement: Flashlight market has spurious and semi-spurious products creating challenges for organized players
items.quote: We are facing challenges there, not from developing a portfolio or any such thing. We have a very decent portfolio now. There are other spurious kind of products and all kinds of, what shall I say, informal products because they do not comply with the formal norms, that's why we call them informal product.

items.statement: CCI penalty appeal at NCLT has seen no movement since last reported
items.quote: So, there has to be no movement since we spoke last or whatever that we reported in our year-ending report, there has been no further movement.

items.statement: Alkaline plant funding partially internal accruals, mostly borrowed funds for interest benefit
items.quote: So, that will be looking, but yes, partially it will be given internally, but most of that will be a borrowed fund.

items.statement: KKR arbitration deferred to November; claimants seeking settlement with primary borrowers; real estate sales embargoed till resolution
items.quote: As far as KKR is concerned, I am unable to give any further sort of report on any progress because the claimant has sought adjournment of the arbitration proceedings, which the arbitration panel which was supposed to be in the month of July has now been pushed to November.

items.statement: Onboarded senior business leaders spearheading segment growth; talent pool vital for growth actualization
items.quote: As for the people, the company has onboarded senior-level business leaders who are each spearheading growth within segments. These new initiatives being taken up by these leaders which are opening up pockets of growth for us.

items.statement: Battery-operated flashlight degrowth may not have bottomed out; past D-size battery experience shows continued decline
items.quote: We do not know, Saket. We have to be very clear. We don't know whether this moderation is sustainable, whether it has sort of settled out to this level forever because you are very familiar with the company, earlier D size batteries when they've started degrowing after a period of degrowth, we thought that okay the worse is over and now it will settle down at this level. But it just kept degrowing

items.statement: A&P expenses sustained at 9% of revenue as necessary investment for brand building
items.quote: A&P expenses were sustained at a high level at 9%, which I had called out as a necessary investment in my earlier remarks.

items.statement: Lighting segment targets breakeven at Rs 400 crore turnover; mid-to-high single-digit EBITDA margin in 2-3 years thereafter
items.quote: As of now, our full focus is to make lighting neutral, right, breakeven. Over the last couple of years, we are at loss because lighting business to become a breakeven, it is probably Rs. 400 crore turnover milestone we have to cross first time, and we are looking forward to that. And so this year, our effort has to be at least we cross breakeven level. And the next that mid to high level of I thin

items.statement: Entered mosquito racket segment during quarter with variants at Rs 499, 599, 799 consumer price
items.quote: We already entered that segment. We already entered that segment during the quarter, with a very small turnover, but we plan to be a reasonable player in that segment as well. Saket Kapoor: And what are the entry prices sir, for the sale? Suvamoy Saha: I think the consumer price, we have got 2, 3 variants. One is at, I think, Rs. 499, Rs. 599 and Rs. 799, which is the

items.statement: RTM implementation challenges mostly resolved; full benefits expected from H2 FY25
items.quote: Most of those challenges are behind us. Some still remain, which we are working upon. And I think the full benefit of the RTM and, let us say, no challenge kind of operation would certainly happen from the second half of this year.

items.statement: Credit growth guided at 13-14% and deposit growth at 11-12% for FY25
items.quote: As far as our guidance is concerned, in line with the growth of the economy, the credit will be growing at around 13 % to 14% and deposit growth we will be around 11 % to 12% for FY 25.

items.statement: NIM guidance for March 2025 set at 2.90%
items.quote: On the guidance side, what we are saying for March 2025, NIM, we are seeing a guidance of 2.90%, considering the fact that the cost of deposit is going up and the Yield on Advances is not coming to that extent.

items.statement: Yield on Advances guidance for FY25 at around 8.50%
items.quote: As regards the Yield on Advances is concerned, there also, presently we are at 8.60%, and we feel that at around 8.50% plus, the guidance will be there as far as that is also concerned.

items.statement: Net Interest Income growth guidance for FY25 at 13%
items.quote: Net Interest Income growth has been at around 13% in FY24. And on the guidance side, we say that the Net Interest Income guidance will again be at 13% for FY25.

items.statement: Credit cost guidance for FY25 at 0.70%
items.quote: On the guidance side, we would say that the Credit Cost would be at 0.70% for the current financial year.

items.statement: Slippage ratio guidance for FY25 at around 1.20%
items.quote: We are confident that we will be able to keep the slippage ratio at around 1.20 % only during the current financial year.

items.statement: Gross NPA guidance for March 2025 at around 4%
items.quote: As regards the guidance is concerned for FY25, we are saying that we will be at around 4% by March'25 on the Gross NPA numbers.

items.statement: Net NPA guidance for March 2025 at around 0.90%
items.quote: On the Net NPA, we were at 1.22 % in March '24. We have now closed at 0.99 %. On the guidance side, we are saying that we will be at around 0.90% by March'25.

items.statement: ROA guidance for FY25 at 0.80%
items.quote: For the guidance we are giving at 0.80% for FY25, for the entire financial year, for FY25 0.80%.

items.statement: Targeting at least 5% recovery from written-off accounts in FY25
items.quote: We are targeting at least 5% recovery from written off account during this financial year. That is the internal target we have kept for the field.

items.statement: Global NIM improved 4 bps to 3.07% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Global N IM has improved by four basis points to 3.07% in Q1 FY25, as against 3.03% in Q1 FY24

items.statement: Domestic NIM improved 6 bps to 3.43% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The domestic NIM improved by 6 bps to 3.43% in Q1 FY25 against 3.37% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: International NIM at 1.25% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In fact, the global Net Interest Margin is 3.07% and for domestic, it is 3.43%, and for the international, it is at 1.25%.

items.statement: Gross NPA ratio improved 205 bps YoY to 4.62% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Gross NPA ratio stood at 4.62%, improved by 205 b ps on a Y-o-Y basis for Q1 FY25

items.statement: Net NPA ratio improved 66 bps YoY to 0.99% in Q1 FY25, below 1% for first time
items.quote: Net NPA ratio at 0.99% improved by 66 b ps on a Y-o-Y basis, and for the first time, we have been able to reduce the Net NPA to the below 1% number

items.statement: Slippage ratio at 0.35% in Q1 FY25 vs 0.53% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: As regards the slippage ratio is concerned, the present slippage ratio is only 0.35%, which was 1.58% for the entire year and 0.38% for the March quarter. And in the last year it was 0.53%.

items.statement: Expecting large ticket NPA recovery of around Rs.500 crore in Q2 FY25
items.quote: We are expecting a good recovery in the big ticket size of around Rs. 500 Crores, if I give a ballpark number in this quarter itself on the large ticket NPA accounts.

items.statement: SMA rise in Q1 due to staff transfers, election duty, heat wave; normalizing from July
items.quote: There was lot of Staff transfers in the system, another thing was a lot of our staff was deployed in the election duties during Q1FY25 and also the heat wave which was there. So collection efficiency in the entire system got impacted.

items.statement: Roll forward in SMA decreased from 26% to 22%, roll backward increased from 22% to 29%
items.quote: Regarding the Roll Forward segment, we have also improved their roll backward, we have increased from 22% to 29% and then roll forward, which should be low, we have decreased from 26% to 22%.

items.statement: CASA ratio at 42.68% in June 2024, up 5.5% YoY
items.quote: CASA has increased by 5.50% on a Y -o-Y basis from Rs.2.60 Lakh Crores in June ’23 to Rs.2.75 Lakh Crore in June’24, with incremental growth of around Rs.15,000 Crores and a C ASA ratio of around 42.68% for this June quarter

items.statement: RAM advances grew 18.78% YoY to Rs.2,84,000 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: RAM advances have increased by 18.78% on a Y-o-Y basis to Rs.2,84,000 Crores in Q1FY25.

items.statement: Retail advances grew 20% YoY, Agriculture 22%, MSME 13%+ in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Advances have also increased by 20% and Agriculture advances by 22%. And finally, the MSME have also grown by 13% plus during this quarter

items.statement: Domestic advances grew 17.29% YoY to Rs.5,08,000 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Domestic advances have increased by 17.29% on a Y-o-Y basis, from Rs.4,33,000 Crores in June '23 to Rs.5,08,000 Crores in June'24, with an incremental growth of around Rs.75,000 Crores.

items.statement: Global advances grew 15.82% YoY to Rs.6,00,000 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Global Advances have increased by 15.82% on Y-o-Y basis from Rs.5.18 Lakh Crore in June'23 to Rs.6,00,000 Crore in June'24, with incremental growth of nearly Rs.82,000 Crores.

items.statement: Global deposits grew 9.74% YoY to Rs.7,64,000 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Global Deposit has also increased by 9.74% from Rs.6,96,000 Crores in June '23 to Rs.7,64,000 Crores in June'24 with incremental growth of Rs.68,000 Crores.

items.statement: Plan to raise Rs.5,000 crore capital via Tier-I and Tier-II bonds in FY25
items.quote: Also, we have a plan to raise around Rs.5,000 Crores in capital in the form of Tier-I and Tier-II. Tier-II, we will be raising in this current quarter and Tier-I, maybe in the quarter three or quarter four.

items.statement: IT and digital budget around Rs.2,000 crore for FY25, onboarding Big 4 consultant for transformation
items.quote: On the expenditure side, as far as the digital and IT is concerned this year also the budget is around Rs. 2,000 Crores and we expect that good amount of money will be spent both on the digital and the IT side for this year also.

items.statement: Targeting 55% RAM and 45% corporate lending mix going forward
items.quote: Our continuous focus on the credit side will be that 55% will be booked on the RAM side and 45% on the corporate lending side.

items.statement: RAM mix at 56% currently, targeting 60-65% in medium term
items.quote: If you look at my RAM mix, it is slowly going up. It is now 56%. So naturally, the RAM mix is giving me a little uptick in terms of yield and once it is going to go up like this because our long term trajectory, including the medium term trajectory, is that now we should be at least 60 to 65% RAM book.

items.statement: No incremental staff cost increase in FY25 as bipartite settlement provisions completed
items.quote: So staff cost will remain the same for the simple reason that as per the bipartite settlement, whatever amount had to be paid and the provision which had to be done has been done, so no more provision to be done, all actual cost has been taken.

items.statement: LCR draft guidelines may reduce LCR by 10-15%, feedback submitted to RBI
items.quote: The ballpark calculation that we have done on these numbers, and what the industry has also done is that the LCR may come down by between 10% to 15%.

items.statement: DCCO circular impact on CET-1 around 10-15 bps, credit cost impact around 15 bps
items.quote: On the C ET-1 side, the impact will be at around 10 to 15 basis points, because overall the guideline is such that it will not impact the CRAR. So CET-1 impact will be around 10 to 15 bps. And on the credit cost side, it will be also at around 15 basis point

items.statement: ECL provisioning expected to be spread over 5 years, manageable with profitability and capital raise
items.quote: We are expecting when the guidelines come, it will be spread across the five year period, and once it is spread across the five year period, we have sufficient cushion with respect to the profitability, which we will be achieving and improvement in the CRAR, which will happen.

items.statement: Personal loan book grew 40% YoY to Rs.10,000 crore, secured by salary cash flows and CIBIL >700
items.quote: The entire personal loan book is secured with the cash flows. So, predominantly this Personal Loan book is to the salaried class and salaried class where the salary is coming in the Bank of India saving accounts.

items.statement: Personal loan slippages only 1% of total slippages in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The total slippages of Personal Loan out of the total slippages is only 1% for this quarter.

items.statement: Credit card outstanding Rs.500-600 crore, NPA 100% provided for
items.quote: Within that there is the credit card outstanding also, which is there. Again that number is not very high. It is only Rs.500 to Rs.600 crores and whatever the NPA is there in credit card, it is 100% provided for.

items.statement: AAA corporate lending at 7.60-7.80% with 20% RWA, significant undercutting among banks
items.quote: If you go for AAA advances, there also there are a lot of challenges on the pricing side. So a lot of undercutting is happening within the banks also. Like banks are lending at 7.60% to 7.80% to these AAA advances where the RWA is only 20%.

items.statement: Japan rate hike impact limited to Japan branch funding costs until other central banks follow
items.quote: As regards the Japan rate hike on the financial markets, it will impact when other countries also start doing that, like UK and USA. So till that thing happens, not much of global impact will be there on the market.

items.statement: NARCL transfers mostly in March-April, no new activity in last 2-3 months, resolutions expected in 2-3 quarters
items.quote: So a lot of activity happened in NARCL. That activity mostly happened in the month of March and April. So no new activity has happened in the last 2 or 3 months on the NARCL side.

items.statement: NARCL SRs: 15% cash recovery, 85% investment with 100% provision, government guaranteed
items.quote: It is with us only. It will move to investment. What happen s is that this is a 15% and 85%. So 15% is a cash recovery, which we get and 85% moves from this book as an investment to the NPA, which we make 100 % provision

items.statement: Dividend of Rs.1,200 crore declared for FY24 accounted in Q1 FY25, reducing net worth
items.quote: See what happened was for last year, we have declared dividend to shareholders of Rs. 1,200 Crores and that has been accounted for this time. So naturally, there is a drop in net worth.

items.statement: Investment valuation reserve adjustment negative but not large
items.quote: Naturally for all banks. Ours is not a big number. But most of the banks it is negative.

items.statement: Management remains positive on FY25 growth but refuses to give hard revenue or PAT margin numbers
items.quote: We would want to refrain from giving any hard numbers per se, Aman, but we continue to remain hopeful.

items.statement: Target EBITDA margin of 25% overall, varies by contract mix
items.quote: Typically, we target to have a 25% EBITDA.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin improved to 5.5% from 2.3% QoQ due to one-off hedge loss in Q4 and revenue diversification
items.quote: Because of it, the margin was squeezed in previous quarter. But however, looking forward, we remain very bullish in terms of being able to maintain the current margin levels.

items.statement: Order book described as healthy and looking up but exact numbers not disclosed
items.quote: Order book is looking healthy. Can't comment on exact numbers at this point because they're all at various stages. But it's looking up.

items.statement: Renewed large PSU managed services deal at better price for 7 years; closed transmission services deal
items.quote: We were able to renew one of our large managed services deal with the PSU at a better price. So that has been a fantastic win for us in this quarter. We also closed the transmission services deal.

items.statement: Won 2 new logos in Americas (Central America and US), one direct and one via partner
items.quote: This quarter, we closed 2 small logos in the Americas, one in Central America and one in the United States.

items.statement: Customer base includes 3 of top 5 banks and 7 of top 10 insurers in India
items.quote: In India we hold a very healthy share of the BFSI, private sector, the BFSI market, insurance, life insurance, general insurance, Health as well as banking, 3 of the top 5 banks, 7 of the top 10 insurance are our customers.

items.statement: Green shoots (new revenue streams) contributed ~30% of Q1 revenue
items.quote: we have seen very healthy growth in our green shoots, which has contributed close to 30% of our QI number

items.statement: Shifting from license+AMC to transaction-based revenue model (per communication/onboard)
items.quote: We have been very consciously trying to move towards a more transactional-based revenue, Tushar. I will say that a lot of our older engagements were license plus AMC plus services, which continues to remain, but some of the newer engagements we are trying to see how we can move it to more per transaction per communication per onboard, these kind of engagements.

items.statement: Investing cash reserves in sales capabilities, US expansion, government deals, AI/blockchain tech, and partnerships
items.quote: We are deploying our cash reserves to strengthen our sales capabilities. We have also sent a senior presales turned sales resource from India to the U.S. to ensure that we now have solid presence in the U.S.

items.statement: Headcount ~535; attrition below industry; hiring only in sales; senior presales resource relocated to US
items.quote: There are about 535 people, as we speak. Attrition rates are not too bad at industry level, I would say or below. And in terms of hiring, we continue to hire in sales.

items.statement: DSO ~150 days, range-bound, no election-related sluggishness
items.quote: Our DSO is range bound. It's about 150 days -- quite in the same range of what we had in Q4. We haven't seen any sluggishness due to elections or anything as additional factors impacting our payments.

items.statement: Government customers (including BSNL) pay after 90+ days but do not default
items.quote: I mean, you know how it works with government. I mean they don't even consider -- not just BSNL, any government, they don't even consider your invoice until it is 90 days plus. So those kind of issues are there, but payments come, they don't default.

items.statement: Competitors include Matrix; space crowded but differentiation via innovation
items.quote: There are quite a few companies, Matrix is there. Quite a few names in the industry. It's a pretty crowded space. But if you have innovation and you will have the cutting edge, this thing, you stand differently.

items.statement: Annuity engagements growing; revenue recognition milestone-based with spillover to future quarters
items.quote: annuity engagements continue to grow. And then in terms of Q1 quarter that we've had, we have seen very healthy growth in our green shoots, which has contributed close to 30% of our QI number

items.statement: Hardware-inclusive contracts lower margins; margin varies by contract construction
items.quote: See, the thing is what happens is you know that hardware once we have in a contract, the margins drop. If there is no hardware, only software and the transaction is there, the margins are high. So it depends on how contract is constructed and how it comes out.

items.statement: Named in Gartner and Omdia reports for communications space
items.quote: I'm extremely happy to let you know that two very, popular analysts like Gartner, one of them is Omdia Both are very established analysts, reputed analysts in the U.S. region. And we have been named in both of their reports to look forward to in the communications space.

items.statement: Seeing steady revenue growth ahead, not lumpy; Q1 revenue INR40.55 cr (26% QoQ, 69% YoY)
items.quote: We are looking at a healthy base, steady growth as we are moving in. It will not be working as mentioned in the last earnings call, we are not looking at the lumpiness of 1 quarter at drop, we're looking at a steady revenues going forward as much I can tell you.

items.statement: AI used to suppress redundant communications saving one customer INR100 cr/year; AI auto-designs complex statements cutting implementation time
items.quote: By doing this, in fact, one of our customers have saved almost INR100 crores in their communication spend in a year.

items.statement: AI leveraged for test case generation and platform implementation efficiency
items.quote: We've been able to leverage AI to rewrite those test cases everything in them. So these kind of measures have helped us improve on our efficiency internally.

items.statement: No acquisitions mentioned; focusing on organic growth via Project Butterfly
items.quote: Overall as things are looking positive, we continue to remain on the same strategy that we set out for ourselves 1.5 years back.

items.statement: Government modernization of urban local bodies and smart city surveillance/ERP projects are focus areas
items.quote: There is a lot of activity from sponsored this thing from central government, for urban local bodies to modernize them across the thing. That's a big domain we are focusing on, that is the other one. And a couple of -- we are also working on some smart city ones.

items.statement: Three core platforms; enhancing with AI/low-code rather than building new platforms
items.quote: We are trying to innovate around these three and consolidated focus on these three and add more as we were speaking earlier, Al and other things to it as we go along and expand this.

items.statement: Strengthening US partnerships and sales presence; targeting dollar revenue growth
items.quote: We are investing in partnerships for now strengthening our operations in the U.S. and seeing how we can focus more on generating dollar revenue.

items.statement: Company well placed on cash flows and reserves; no debt details discussed
items.quote: As a company, today we are well placed in terms of our cash flows, in terms of the reserves to make investments to further growth areas marketing part of it.

items.statement: Appointed Ketan Kulkarni as Deputy Managing Director for Gati Express and Supply Chain Private Limited
items.quote: I would like to start by introducing the new Deputy Managing Director for Gati Express and Supply Chain Private Limited, Mr. Ketan Kulkarni.

items.statement: Launched first module of new technology platform GATE (Gati Associate Tracking Engine) for real-time associate tracking
items.quote: On the technology front, I'm happy to share that we have launched the first module of our new technology. We have named it GATE, Gati Associate Tracking Engine.

items.statement: Phase 1 infrastructure update implemented; Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Pune hubs to start this quarter
items.quote: We have successfully implemented Phase 1 of the infrastructure update. And as already mentioned, we will continue with our journey to modernize the same in order to be future ready. We now have Ahmedabad, Kolkata and Pune, which we will start from this quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 operational KPIs: PIFOT 90.5%, DIFOT 84.4%, delivery efficiency 90.4%
items.quote: Our PIFOT, DIFOT and delivery efficiency stood at 90.5%, 84.4% and 90.4%, respectively.

items.statement: Express gross margin improved 100 bps QoQ to 27% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Corresponding gross margin has improved by 100 basis points and stands at 27 percentage for Q1 FY'25 as compared to 26 percentage for the quarter ended March 2024.

items.statement: Express EBITDA grew 33% QoQ to INR20 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the Express business stood at INR20 crores in Q1 FY'25 as against INR15 crores in Q4 FY'24, representing a growth of 33 percentage.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 plan mix: KEA 63%, SME 19%, retail 18%
items.quote: Plan mix for the quarter ended June 2024 for KEA, SME and retail stood at 63 percentage, 19 percentage and 18 percentage, respectively.

items.statement: Aspirational customer mix target: 60-40 KEA to SME/retail first, then 55-45
items.quote: So our first benchmark is to bring 60-40, and then the aspirational is 55-45.

items.statement: Targeting 30%+ gross margin and 10%+ EBITDA margin by FY26-27
items.quote: We are looking at getting us to the 30-plus percent gross margin and 10-plus percent EBITDA. And we strongly believe that we should achieve this by '26, '27.

items.statement: Revenue target INR3,000 crore by FY26 including Contract Logistics business
items.quote: It is with the Contract Logistics business, yes.

items.statement: Contract Logistics business expected to grow at 30% CAGR over next 3 years
items.quote: Although small, we are looking at this bu siness growing at a CAGR of 30% in the next 3 years because the opportunity that is available in the market is huge

items.statement: Targeting yield increase of INR0.10 per year for next two years through mix change
items.quote: We are hovering at an overall yield of about INR11.8. So we look to increasing it by INR0.10 paisa for the next two years by changing the mix.

items.statement: Targeting year-end FY25 customer mix of 60-40 KEA to SME/retail
items.quote: So we would be looking at ending the year with a mix of about 60-40.

items.statement: Allocated INR30 crore for technology and INR40 crore for infrastructure over next two years from QIP proceeds
items.quote: So we have set aside very clearly when we did our QIP also INR30 crores for technology and another INR40 crores for infrastructure, which means the size of the new hubs that we lease out as we move forward.

items.statement: Company debt-free with net cash of INR196 crore after QIP of INR169 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: I am happy to share that as on June 30, 2024, the company is debt-free with a net cash positive of INR196 crores after a successful QIP of INR169 crores.

items.statement: QIP of INR169 crore completed for growth capital; no immediate further fundraising planned but not ruled out
items.quote: So we have done this for the growth s trategy. As you know, the group has now got 4 separate listed entities, and each entity has its own management MD and should have its own funds. And therefore, we did a QIP by which we now have growth capital for ourselves, which we will invest in infrastructure, in technology as well as other processes, which we require. So yes, to answer your question, we ha

items.statement: Merger with Contract Logistics business filed with stock exchanges and SEBI; expected completion by Q1 FY26
items.quote: So we have filed with the stock exchanges who have given their approval, and the file is SEBI. Post that, it will go to the NCLT. So we believe that the latest by first quarter of next year, we should get the merger done.

items.statement: Average wallet share with large customers ~30%; significant scope to increase
items.quote: Today, on an average, our wallet share is about 30% w ith the large customers. So we still have a good opportunity to increase our wallet share

items.statement: Key account definition: customers with annual revenue above INR20 lakh
items.quote: So the way we have set it up now is that all customers who are above INR20 lakhs of revenue annual are in key accounts.

items.statement: B2B express has high entry barriers; only 2 new players from B2C side attempting entry
items.quote: The number of players that you're talking about according to me is just two, first of all. I don't know more than two players. Having said that, B2B networks are very different from B2C networks, and it becomes extremely difficult if somebody has to start a B2B network today and make it a pan-India play.

items.statement: Yield improvement strategy focused on mix optimization (SME/retail) not price hikes; logistics costs in India still high
items.quote: So like I have been saying before, as far as the yield is concerned, the way we will improve our yield is by improving our mix and not by going to the customers because in India, logistics costs are still extremely high. And therefore, it is important for us to first optimize the costs rather than asking customers to pay more.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 5% in Q1 FY25 vs 3% in Q4 FY24 and 4% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q1 FY'25 stood at 5 percentage as against 3 percentage during Q4 '24 and 4 percentage in Q1 FY'24.

items.statement: Q1 volumes subdued due to elections and natural calamities; expect strong Q2 on pre-festive inventory build
items.quote: Coming to the first quarter, yes, there were a couple of things. One is, of course, the election. Second is we did have some natural calamities in certain parts of the country. And therefore, volumes were subdued. But this quarter, July, August, September, as you know, is supposed to be the -- one of the largest quarters for the pre -festivities inventory. And therefore, we should see a very good

items.statement: Legacy ECLM provisions reduced over last 4 quarters; 99% of old legacy issues resolved
items.quote: You've seen the ECLM provisions reduced in the last 4 quarters from what it was 4 quarters back. That in itself gives the confidence that most of the old legacy issues are now over.

items.statement: Technology rollout will enable further employee cost reduction in S&OP; current S&OP cost as % of sales higher than competition due to old technology
items.quote: If you see our below gross margin, S&OP for employee costs, it is as a percentage of sales larger than competition. This is basically because our technology is very old. So as the new technology rolls out, we have opportunity to reduce a large number of people from our S&OP cost.

items.statement: Maintains sales growth guidance of 10%+ with EBITDA margins 12-14% for plywood; 15% EBITDA margin guidance for MDF on standalone basis by Q4 FY25
items.quote: We continue to maintain our guideline of sales growth of 10% plus, with EBITDA margins between 12% to 14%.

items.statement: Expects 40%+ value growth for MDF with some EBITDA margin improvement; particle board facility to start by end of FY25
items.quote: Going forward, we expect 40% plus value growth with some improvements in EBITDA license.

items.statement: MDF plant capex increased to INR730 crores from INR700 crores due to cost escalation, not capacity addition
items.quote: Costs have been shooting up. And I think there are certain elements that we had expected to be completed at lower cost for instance, roads in media, et cetera, have cost, slightly higher than what we had thought.

items.statement: No substantial capex planned for next 1-1.5 years after particle board commissioning; sharp deleveraging expected
items.quote: At this point in time, yes. Because currently, we don't have any closing capex. And I think considering the current scenario, and we have already taken on large capex. We are not going to go for any substantial capex for the next year, 1.5 year after So they'll be sharp deleveraging effect taking place.

items.statement: Andhra MDF facility ramping fast, expects EBITDA positive by Q3 FY25; current utilization <20%, targeting 85-87% at steady state
items.quote: Currently, at Andhra first quarter, we are at a very low utilization. As you know, we will be at less than 20%. Quarter 2, of course, we are planning to ramp it up substantially higher. And in sharper capacity, we will be running at close to 85% to 87%.

items.statement: Plywood capacity at ~340,000 cubic meters with 75% utilization; increasing 5-10% annually across plants
items.quote: So our capacity is now at 3,39,000 about 3,40,000 cubic meters and utilization in '24, '25 is about 75%. We are actually increasing our capacity across all our plants. We are nearly 5%, 10% every year.

items.statement: Andhra laminate facility at <10% utilization in Q1, existing laminate at 75%+ utilization; Andhra laminate peak turnover ~INR250 crores
items.quote: On the existing Laminate capacity in Q1, we will be at a 75% -plus utilization. For Andhra as you know, scale-up is taking time, we will be at less than 10%.

items.statement: Particle board new facility expected to start by end of FY25; targets 50%+ utilization by end of year 1, breakeven at 50%
items.quote: I think by the exit of year 1, we would comfortably be at 50% plus capacity utilization.

items.statement: Plywood EBITDA margin 14.4% in Q1 FY25; maintained 12-14% guidance despite 4% price hikes (2% May, 2% Aug) offset by raw material cost increases
items.quote: Plywood division posted better -than-expected year-on-year growth of 14.9% with EBITDA margins of 14.4%.

items.statement: MDF standalone margin at 14% in Q1, guided as bottom; expects 15%+ by Q4 FY25 with Andhra ramp-up and value-added mix improvement
items.quote: If you look at our -- if you look at our standalone numbers, so we had about 14% margin. And I think that, yes, this would be the bottom because going forward, we are going to attempt to increase value -added products, we are going to attempt to increase ca pacity utilization

items.statement: Laminate EBITDA margin improved to 12.3%; 3% price hike taken on Aug 1 due to kraft paper and chemical cost increases
items.quote: Although Laminate division this growth guideline improved EBITDA margin to 12.3%.

items.statement: Plywood: 4% price hike implemented (2% June, 2% Aug); raw material costs increased, limiting margin expansion
items.quote: As far as the price increase is concerned, we increased 2% from 1st of May, and we have increased 2% from 1st of August. We have increased 2% from 1st of June and 2% from 1st of August. The 4% price has been taken across in all of our plywood products. But the cost of raw material has gone up.

items.statement: MDF: No clear visibility on price hikes but logical to expect increases given industry margins; value-added share rising with pre-lam line start in July
items.quote: Yes, in MDF currently, while there is no clear visibility of price hike, but considering the state of margin across the industry I think it is only logical that prices should start to increase.

items.statement: Laminate: 3% price hike on Aug 1 due to kraft paper and chemical cost increases
items.quote: We have already taken a price hike as on the 1st of August. And this is close to a 3% price, this is due to raw material cost.

items.statement: Timber prices: North INR6.5-7/kg, South ~INR5.5/kg; increased 5-7% sequentially, may rise further next 2 quarters due to plantation cycle
items.quote: In an MBS in North, our timber price is between INR6.5 to INR7 per kg. In South, it is about INR1 cheaper. So it's in the range of INR5.5 per kg.

items.statement: Imported raw material 3-4% costlier than domestic but better quality; strong supplier linkages in Brazil, Vietnam and port-based factories provide strategic advantage
items.quote: Yes. It's the imported raw material is a little higher. Say about 3%, maybe 3.5% or 4% is higher than the local, but the quality is better. The imported raw material quality is much better.

items.statement: MDF volume growth 47.3% YoY in Q1 FY25; Andhra facility ramping exceptionally fast in first quarter of operation
items.quote: Newly setup MDF facility at Andhra has picked up exceptionally fast in very first quarter of operation. And a year-on-year growth of 47.3% volume to MDF segment.

items.statement: MDF imports down ~50% to 15,000-16,000 CBM/month in last 3 months due to freight crisis; normally 25,000-30,000 CBM/month
items.quote: If I look at the last 3 months data, I would believe it's about in the range of 15,000 to 16,000 CBM. So it's come down by about 50%.

items.statement: No substantial MDF capacity additions expected in next 2 years; smaller peers under pressure, one line near completion only
items.quote: I don't think there's going to be any substantial in MDF capacity going forward. In fact, a number of the smaller peers under tremendous pressure and quite a few of the peers, even the ones that have recently set up a -- so currently, in this scenario, I don't see much crash additioning happening in the next couple of years.

items.statement: BIS norms for MDF imports: imported boards don't meet Indian standards; compliance would increase importer costs by ~20%, limiting impact
items.quote: For them, it will be a 20% cost increase in order to meet the current standard acquiring manufactured by us or the other branded domestic player.

items.statement: Andhra MDF pre-lamination line started July H2; zero pre-lam in Q1, rising share to improve realization; laminate facility focused on compact/large-size for higher NSR
items.quote: Pre -lamination line also started producing from the second half of July, we actually had a much lower share of Pre-lam MDF in our Andhra facility. Going forward, we are going to increase our value -added products and that should give us slightly higher realization.

items.statement: PBC board facility at Andhra started May 2024, ramping fast, expected to add ~INR100 crores revenue by next year
items.quote: We have also set up PBC board facility at our Andhra location. This has started production in the month of May 24. This facility is also ramping very fast and will add to almost INR100 crores revenue by next year.

items.statement: Singapore subsidiary sale completed April 2024; INR24.06 cr impairment in FY24, INR13.33 cr exceptional item in Q1 FY25 for derecognition
items.quote: The conviction on account of sale of our Singapore subsidiary along with lowest step -down subsidiaries as completed in the month of April '24. We have taken impairment loss of INR24.06 crores for the same in our last year accounts, which was reflected in our spend on accounts as exceptional items.

items.statement: Employee cost increased due to annual increments and scaling up for MDF growth targets; provisioning for larger growth ahead
items.quote: We have actually increased our term fee substantially we are investing towards in MDF, as you know, we have a massive growth target for this year. So yes, in focus more on the market. So I think there are number of things where increment has played a role. But other than that we're also scaling up and we are provisioning for a larger growth going forward.

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty (Bangladesh, Israel) creates unpredictability; may revise plywood guidance if Q2 sustains high growth but currently cautious
items.quote: Will be the all less series going around, Bangladesh and what is happening with Israel, we really don't know what is going to achieve.

items.statement: MDF industry EBITDA margin cyclicality: historically ~25% over 5-year cycles; variability expected to reduce as value-added share rises and market premiumizes
items.quote: I think if we look at this as a product category in any 5 -year horizon, you typically guide for 25%. The last cycle that we were talking about over the year 2018, '19. So any 5-year cycle, we'll be looking at close to 25%.

items.statement: Domestic revenue grew 19.3% YoY to INR109.4 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, we clocked the domestic revenue of INR109.4 crores, representing a robust growth of 19.3% year -on-year.

items.statement: Radio FCT revenue grew 10.8% YoY to INR75.2 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our FCT revenue for the quarter was at INR75.2 crores as compared to INR67.8 crores, a growth of 10.8% year -on-year.

items.statement: Radio volume market share at 24.3% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We have a volume market share of 24.3%.

items.statement: Non-FCT segments including digital grew 43.6% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Non-FCT segments, including digital, witnessed a growth of 43.6% year-on-year on the back of subscription revenue from Gaana.

items.statement: Digital revenue reached INR17.8 crores, 25% of radio revenue in Q1 FY25
items.quote: This led to a strong digital revenue of INR17.8 crores, contributing almost 25% of our radio revenues as compared to 11.8% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Digital revenue target of 25% of total revenue achieved in Q1 FY25
items.quote: You would recall that we had guided earlier that our aspiration and ambition is to get 25% of revenues from the digital segment.

items.statement: Invested INR15 crores in Gaana platform in Q1 FY25, expected to decrease in subsequent quarters
items.quote: We have made investments on this new platform, which is close to INR15 crores this quarter. However, the key takeaway is that this is expected to come down in the subsequent quarters.

items.statement: EBITDA excluding digital at INR20.5 crores with 21.8% margin in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA for the year, excluding digital, stood at INR20.5 crores as compared to INR19.2 crores in Q1 FY '24. EBITDA margins were at 21.8%.

items.statement: PAT rose to INR5.8 crores from INR4.4 crores YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our PAT rose to INR5.8 crores as compared to INR4.4 crores in the same period last year.

items.statement: International business EBITDA positive at INR1.5 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our international market continues to be EBITDA positive at INR1.5 crores for Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Cash balance of INR355 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Our balance sheet remains robust with a cash balance of INR355 crores as of June 30, 2024.

items.statement: Radio inventory utilization at 72% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The inventory utilization for this quarter is about 72%.

items.statement: Radio pricing increased ~5.8% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to political business
items.quote: There was some bit of price increase, about 5.8% of price increase. But I would not read much, it's one time because of the political event.

items.statement: Radio pricing stable excluding political business, no further drop expected
items.quote: So, if I remove elections also this quarter, our price has remained stable. So , I don't see any further drop in pricing happening.

items.statement: Gaana subscription price increased from INR299 to INR599 from July 1, 2024
items.quote: But recently, you would have seen from 1st July, we have increased the price to INR599.

items.statement: Gaana investment costs frontloaded in Q1-Q2 FY25, expected to decrease in subsequent quarters
items.quote: So, it's a planned expense. I would say for the first quarter, it's a little on the higher side. But as we see for the next quarter, this cost will come down.

items.statement: Gaana revenue growth expected to be more robust in subsequent quarters with price increase impact
items.quote: So, you'll see much more robust in the subsequent quarters. As I said, this is the second quarter only, after we took over.

items.statement: Potential price increases in H2 FY25 starting September as media business skewed towards H2
items.quote: Generally, media, not just radio, any media, the price is based on supply demand in the H2, we believe, starting September could have a chance where we could look at certain price increases as the business comes back and the media is always skewed towards H2.

items.statement: Political and government business contributed 10-11% of radio volume in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The political and government business contribution in this quarter is almost about 10% to 11%.

items.statement: Multimedia solutions grew except digital content show pushed to next quarter for margin reasons
items.quote: So, if you look at our multimedia solutions, business has grown well, except for one business, which is the digital content, Kareena Kapoor Khan show, the original content, which we have pushed into this quarter because as I said earlier also, our principal remains profitable growth.

items.statement: Activation business grew 42% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: activation has grown by about 42%.

items.statement: Gaana operates as pure subscription model with no advertising revenue
items.quote: No. So, for our Gaana business, it's pure subscription. We do our digital advertising business separately. But for Gaana, it is a pure paid model.

items.statement: Gaana blended price will take time to reflect full INR599 as existing subscribers renew at old price
items.quote: The old customer continues at the same price. We have sold the product at old price. We'll continue that. When he comes for a renewal that is the time he will change. So, the blended price will take a while to become double.

items.statement: Gaana investment focused on tech, recommendation engine, product experience and marketing
items.quote: By the time you stabilize the business, you realize certain things which we want to invest in, on data sciences, on recommendation engine, on getting the product experience better.

items.statement: M-Ping business robust, expanding from audio to video inventory in FY25
items.quote: We're now looking at more and more accretion in our inventory. Audio inventory, we have almost everything. We are now looking at video inventory also

items.statement: Radio pricing still below pre-COVID levels, recovery not expected soon
items.quote: So pre-COVID level, we are still down. We don't see that coming up very fast.

items.statement: Management expects similar quarter-on-quarter growth going forward
items.quote: Yes, we can see a similar growth quarter on quarter. Yes.

items.statement: Operating margins under pressure due to new contracts and higher coal mix; expected to improve as ash share rises and contracts mature
items.quote: The major reason in the first instance being the coal and ash handling business because there are new opportunities, new businesses coming up. We are taking time to learn and understand the actual cost involved in every tender. Going forward, this margin will get better and also the mix of coal and ash also will get better with ash taking over majority where we will have a larger margin. The margi

items.statement: Immediate capex of about INR100 crores for EV and ash/coal fleet; may increase as business grows
items.quote: Currently, I think we immediately have current capex which is close to about INR100 odd crores for both the fleet, both EV and just put together. But going forward, yes, as the business goes, this might grow also. This might increase also.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for INR1000 crores fundraise approved; no immediate deployment plan, intended for future working capital needs
items.quote: No, we have not taken approval for fundraise. We're only taking an in -principle approval enabling provision so that in future if there's a requirement we can get this cleared in the AGM. We don't need to go to a process because we are a very fast -growing c ompany. If there's a potential requirement, this will only be an enabling factor.

items.statement: Promoter holding company Sherisha repaid INR27 crores of INR46 crore loan; balance to be repaid by 15th September
items.quote: This loan out of the total INR46 crore loan, INR27 crore of the loan has been repaid as on day and balance also will get repaid by 15th of September. And this will all be utilized, as you rightly said, for the working capital rather than borrowing from the banker. This will all be utilized for the working capital.

items.statement: Working capital cycle 60-90 days; pay suppliers in 15 days, collect from customers in 60-90 days; no improvement expected
items.quote: Currently, working capital cycle is between 60 to 90 days. Where our supplier, we pay on a 15-day basis. But from the customer, we get between 60 to 90 days.

items.statement: Current daily handling 50,000 tons of coal and ash combined; not full capacity, can scale by adding fleet
items.quote: Yes, 50,000 tons per day we are handling as of today. Management: That is not the capacity. We can do much more. Currently, we are doing 50,000 tons. Yashwanti: 50,000, okay. Management: Yes, we can do much more. It is purely a sector of engaging more fleet and bringing more people on the ground depending on the

items.statement: Strategic focus shifting to ash handling over coal trading due to larger market potential; coal business expected to reduce
items.quote: Yes, our focus is more majorly on ash, because that's one area which we think is going to grow a lot in the country. So, major focus will be on ash going forward.

items.statement: Ash handling pricing varies by distance and disposal avenue: INR400/ton at 100km, INR800-900/ton at 200km
items.quote: Different customer, different location has different pricing depending on the number of kilometres you have to dispose the ash for. So it ranges if it's 100 kilometres it is INR400 a ton if it's 200 it's INR800, INR900 a ton and also depending on where it is being disposed it' s also priced disbursal.

items.statement: Main organized competitor is Ashtech; rest of market is unorganized
items.quote: Currently, there's a company by the name [Ashtech 0:21:47], which is an organized player and competitor. They are an unorganized player. And this business is growing continuously.

items.statement: Legacy pond ash (1.7 billion tons) must be cleared in 3-6 years due to Ministry of Environment fines; fly ash 70% utilized daily
items.quote: The legacy pond ash has to be cleared within the next three years. There is already a fine and penalty being imposed by Ministry of Environment. But looking at the volume, I think it might go up to five to six years to remove the legacy ash. On the fly ash, they are removed on a daily basis. At least 70% of it is removed on a daily basis based on generation and the requirement of the cement plants

items.statement: Monsoon causes seasonal slowdown in Q2; Q1, Q3, Q4 stronger quarters for ash disposal
items.quote: to look at as compared to quarter 2? Management: It depends also like example if it is in South India, state Tamil Nadu quarter 3 could be a little slow because monsoon is during that time, but majority of the country quarter 2 is the monsoon. So that quarter will be a little slow quarter

items.statement: No plan to hire separate CFO; Dinesh Agarwal continues as Whole-Time Director and CFO supported by strong accounts team

items.statement: Launching 9th hotel Ibis Styles Mysore (130 rooms) under Accor management; second hotel in Mysore.

items.statement: Brigade Enterprises ranked 38th in Great Place to Work top 100 midsized workplaces; 10+ years consecutive recognition.
items.quote: We're also happy to share that the Brigade Enterprises Limited was recognized amongst the top 100 great midsized workplaces by the Great Place to Work Institute. items.statement: Target 30.67 GW capacity by FY29-30 via organic and inorganic expansion
items.quote: In addition to this, we are also evaluating further brownfield expansion projects of 4,800 MW and inorganic opportunities of more than 1,000 MW, which together will take our target capacities to 30.67 GW by FY 29-30.

items.statement: Mahan Energen Phase II 1600 MW ultra-supercritical expansion targeted for completion by June 2027
items.quote: Speaking of the future, the Mahan Energen Phase II Ultra-supercritical expansion project of 1600 megawatt capacity is well underway to achieve its targeted completion by June2027.

items.statement: Advanced preparation started for three 1600 MW projects at Raipur, Raigarh, and Mirzapur
items.quote: We have started advanced preparation for setting up three more projects of 1600 MW each at Raipur, Raigarh, and Mirzapur.

items.statement: Awaiting NCLT approval for Lanco Amarkantak (1800 MW operating + 1320 MW under-construction) and Coastal Energen (1320 MW) acquisitions
items.quote: We are awaiting NCLT approval of the resolution plans for Lanco Amarkantak and Coastal Energen, which will expand our operating capacity by 1800 MW and add another 1320 MW of under-construction capacity.

items.statement: Government revised peak demand projection to 400 GW by FY31-32 requiring 80-90 GW additional thermal capacity
items.quote: The government has revised its power demand projections within just two years. It estimates that peak demand will grow from 250 GW currently to 400 GW by 2031-32. This will call for 80 to 90 GW of additional thermal power capacity to meet peak demand.

items.statement: Merchant contribution improved to Rs 4.56/unit from Rs 3.71/unit YoY due to lower coal costs
items.quote: In merchant sales, we had a revenue realization of Rs. 7.45 per unit on an average for the quarter and the fuel cost was Rs. 2.89 per unit, so there was a contribution of Rs. 4.56 per unit.

items.statement: Import coal prices lower YoY leading to 17% fuel cost growth vs 29% revenue growth
items.quote: Import coal prices for Q1 FY25 were lower as compared to Q1 of last year. Due to this, tariff realization in some PPAs with pass through of import coal prices was slightly lower. This reduction in import fuel price was also reflected in the significantly lower growth in fuel cost for Quarter 1

items.statement: Bangladesh PPA payments regularized with 4-5 months average arrears similar to Indian DISCOMs
items.quote: As far as payment is concerned, we have started getting good payments from last few months and every process is well established now. On an average 4 to 5 months of arrears is there for all the power suppliers of Bangladesh, so it is not that we are getting some different treatment.

items.statement: Finance cost reduced to Rs 811 crore from Rs 883 crore YoY through debt prepayment and improved credit ratings
items.quote: Finance cost for Q1 FY25 was Rs. 811 crore as compar ed to Rs. 883 crore in Q1 FY24. On the other hand, depreciation was higher at Rs. 996 crore versus Rs. 935 crore in the two quarters respectively due to the commissioning of Godda plant

items.statement: Credit available for merchant capacity as banks accept standalone viability given mature merchant market
items.quote: Credit is available nowadays even for merchant capacity also. There is a clear indication from Government of India that since now the rates in the market are quite attractive, the financial institutions and banks should look at standalone viability of the capacity now since the merchant market is quite matured.

items.statement: Carbon tax would be treated as change in law and passed through under PPAs like existing Rs 400/tonne GST Compensation Cess
items.quote: See, any carbon tax would be a change in law and therefore it would be passed through under the PPA. In fact, you may be aware that we already have a charge of Rs. 400 per metric tonne, which was called initially as Green Cess, which was later renamed as the GST Compensation Cess.

items.statement: Merchant strategy maintains 80% PPA / 20% merchant split for existing and expansion capacity
items.quote: As per our internal assessment, we are keeping around 20% under merchant. That should be a sort of balancing act, whereby we don't want to expose ourselves to market risk for more than the 20%, which is sufficient to take the advantage of higher rates from the market. So we are of the view that we should keep it around this 80%-20% ratio.

items.statement: Merchant sales 70-80% via bilateral contracts <1 year, 20-30% via power exchange

items.statement: PLF improved sharply to 78% in Q1 FY25 from 60% in Q1 FY24 with 26 BU dispatch
items.quote: During the recently concluded quarter, APL posted a sharp year-on-year growth in PLF to 78% and greater power dispatch across all plants, aggregating to 26 billion units.

items.statement: Continuing operating revenue grew 29% YoY to Rs 14,717 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Continuing operating revenue for Q1 F Y25 grew by 29% to Rs. 14,717 crores as compared to Rs. 11,370 crores in Q1

items.statement: Continuing PBT nearly doubled to Rs 4,483 crore in Q1 FY25 from Rs 2,303 crore in Q1 FY24
items.quote: This outstanding operating performance and cost control led to continuing profit before tax for Q1 FY25 nearly doubling to Rs. 4,483 crore versus Rs. 2,303 crore in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: KSK Mahanadi bid submission due end of business hours; evaluating other inorganic opportunities >1000 MW
items.quote: KSK Mahanadi is under bidding, and its submission is probably today by end of business hours. So, it is still under bidding.

items.statement: Inorganic expansion focused on acquiring good sites with quick turnaround rather than as primary growth strategy
items.quote: Primarily, inorganic expansion is not really the key strategy that we are following. It is actually to get access to good sites, get access to capacities that can be turned around quickly and fulfill the demand niche that we find in the market.

items.statement: Green ammonia co-firing at Mundra in technical feasibility study stage; viability depends on technical success, ammonia pricing, and PPA pass-through
items.quote: We are carrying out a pilot study. So first we have to establish whether the green ammonia can be co-fired with the coal or not. Therefore, we are in the state of technical study at this stage. Once the technical possibility is established, then we have to consider the viability of the price of ammonia and also whether that would be available as pass-through under the provisions of PPA.

items.quote: We are following an agile business model and integrated approach for augmenting assurances on project execution and operational front. We are also focusing on enhancing fuel security through commercial mining licenses under an asset light model.

items.statement: Advertisement revenue was INR 219 mn in Q1FY25 vs INR 235 mn in Q1FY24; corporate ad revenue INR 160 mn vs INR 182 mn; government ad revenue grew 55% to INR 59 mn from INR 38 mn.

items.statement: Theatrical revenue was INR 240 mn in Q1FY25 vs INR 248 mn in Q1FY24; exhibitor revenue grew 39% to INR 443 mn from INR 318 mn.

items.quote: Our revenue from product sales has grown by 84%, from INR 14 crores last year to INR 26.5 crores this quarter, carrying an operating margin of approximately 20-22%. Correspondingly, the cost of purchased goods has also gone up.

The cost associated with TSR is around INR 3.3 crores per quarter.

The key is to ensure continuous growth in advertisement revenue, allowing us to meet the expectations of exhibitors who anticipate added value through increased r

items.statement: Central government ad allocations remain low; no meaningful revenue received in Q1FY25; focus shifted to state governments and political ads (INR 4 cr this quarter).
items.quote: Yes, the challenges with central government allocations for cinema networks persist. We haven't received meaningful revenue from them this quarter. Given the election period, even regular spending by the central government would have been low , making this a particularly dry qua rter for central government funds

items.quote: key players in the market include Qube, Cinematica in Andhra, and TSR in the South. Additionally, there are smaller players like K Sera Sera. Ashish Malushte: Two big players, Ufo and Qube, if I have to simplify the answer to your question

items.statement: Historically maintained cash reserves over INR 150 cr pre-pandemic; distributed INR 60 cr to shareholders in March 2020; philosophy to return excess cash if not utilized; current net cash ~INR 50 cr.
items.quote: Historically, we've maintained a substantial cash reserve, with over INR 150 crores pre-pandemic. This was to seize business expansion opportunities. When some merger opportunities didn't materialize, we distributed excess cash to shareholders, including INR 60 crores on March 10, just before COVID hit on March 22. Our philosophy is to return excess cash if it's not being utilized.

items.statement: Business model dependent on movie releases and performance; Q1 uniquely affected by elections and IPL; underperformance of tent-pole films hurts advertising more than fewer releases.
items.quote: However, with fewer movies being released, the proportion of new films decreases, leading to a decline in CDC revenue. But more than this, t he bigger impact is from the underperformance of movies. When this happens, even though shows are running with old films or the same films throughout the quarter, advertisers don’t return with the same intensity. This affects revenue more than the reduction i

items.statement: Smaller films like Munjya, Laapataa Ladies, Crew, Article 370 performed well without big stars; South Indian dubbed films gaining acceptance in North; 8-week OTT window supports theatrical footfall.
items.quote: Film like Munjya, with a relatively new cast and the horror genre, exceeded INR 100 crore in revenue. Similarly, smaller films such as Laapataa Ladies, Crew, and Article 370, despite lacking big star casts and big production set ups , still attracted audiences. This indicates that t he film business remains robust

items.statement: Multiplex screens run 45-50 movies/year vs 30-35 for single screens; higher CDC revenue per screen; ad rates uniform across network but multiplexes run more shows and ads.
items.quote: Generally, the number of movies played per screen in multiplexes are higher than single screens, making multiplexes a better unit for CDC revenue. For example, a single screen is running, say 30-35 movies a year, a multiplex per screen may run 45-50 movies a year. This difference means multiplexes generate more CDC revenue, despite having the same service fee rate.

items.statement: Caravan ad business has good margins but revenue tied to number of vans; not a major revenue driver like core ad network; core network has potential to expand from 2.5 to 15-18 minutes with rate doubling without additional CapEx.
items.quote: With the existing screens, we're only utilizing two and a half minutes, but we have the potential to expand to 15-18 minutes, with rates that could also double, all without requiring additional CapEx. In contrast, for the caravan business to scale significantly, we would need to invest in more vans.

items.statement: Employee costs up 14% YoY due to normalization after converting 20% fixed salary to variable pay last year; SG&A up only 2% YoY.
items.quote: Although this 14% might seem high, it's due to last year's adjustment in our payout structure, where we converted 20% of fixed salaries into variable pay. This year, some normalization occurred, leading to the increase.

items.statement: Animal Feed EBIT/MT improved to ₹2,258 in Q1 FY25 from ₹1,443 in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Further, EBIT/MT improved significantly from ₹ 1,443 in Q1 FY '24 to ₹ 2,258 in Q1 FY'25 and also sequentially.

items.statement: Animal Feed segment margins improved to 6.8% in Q1 FY25 from 4.2% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: In Animal Feed, the segment margins improved sharply from 4.2% in Q1 FY'24 to 6.8% in Q1 FY'25 on account of favourable commodity position.

items.statement: Standalone Crop Protection segment margins improved to 45% in Q1 FY25 from 32% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: The stand alone Crop Protection segment results witnessed strong growth in Q1 FY '25, as segment margins improved significantly from 32% in Q1 FY'24 to 45% in Q1 FY'25, primarily due to higher realization in herbicide and pesticides categor ies.

items.statement: Dairy EBITDA margins improved by 490 basis points in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, our Dairy segment demonstrated robust margin expansion, with EBITDA margins improving by 490 basis points.

items.quote: This has been extraordinarily good quarter. So, my sense is that last year, we had a margin of 8.2%. This year 10.8% and I feel that anything between 9% to 10% is something which we think we will be able to maintain in rest of the quarters.

We'll continue to grow that number by 60% to 70% this year, and we are well on target to achieve those numbers.

items.statement: Astec enterprise demand expected to recover fully by end of FY25, export prices may take 1-2 more quarters to firm up
items.quote: On the enterprise side, as I mentioned, the demand is likely to come back or we are seeing some green shoots in the demand starting this quarter, specifically from the domestic market. And I would say, by end of this year, the demand is likely to come back fully, and the prices might take another quarter or 2 to firm up.

items.statement: ₹110 crore Animal Feed plant sanctioned in Maharashtra, completion in ~2 years
items.quote: So, this ₹ 110 crore plant, the sanction has been taken in anticipation, because it takes us normally 2 years to complete one plant.
