items.statement: Additional ₹70-80 crore for OPP refinery and herbicide plant capitalization in FY25
items.quote: Point number two is capex this year, definitely, we are going to have one more refinery in OPP. And with these attachments, etcetera, of ₹ 70-80 crores. Apart from that, there is a capitalization of herbicide. Money is already invested 99% of that.

items.statement: No new capex committed for Astec beyond debottlenecking, quality, and environmental projects
items.quote: But at least, as of now, we are not committing any capex in Astec LifeSciences other than debottlenecking, quality improvement projects and some environmental control investments that far.

items.statement: CDMO order deferrals due to China supply chain issues, revenue to be realized in Q2
items.quote: On the CDMO side, actually few of our project or the volume sales were being deferred to the subsequent quarter because of the supply chain issues on some of the raw materials coming in from China.

items.statement: Animal Feed volumes impacted by subdued milk prices and lower placements, cattle feed degrowth ~4%
items.quote: However, volumes were impacted due to subdued milk prices and lower placements.

items.statement: Astec enterprise products face pricing pressure and demand headwinds, especially in export markets with Chinese dumping
items.quote: Astec LifeSciences continued to experience pricing pressures and demand headwinds in the enterprise products business, which adversely affected top line and margins, which also necessitated inventory write -down in enterprise products.

items.statement: Vegetable Oil revenues impacted by lower FFB arrivals and lower opening stock
items.quote: Our Vegetable Oil segment revenues in Q1 FY'25 was impacted by lower Fresh Fruit Bunch arrivals and lower opening stock in Q1 FY'25.

items.statement: Dairy Value-Added Products salience improved to 42% from 36% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: The salience of Value-Added Products has improved from 36% of total sales in Q1 FY'24 to 42% in Q1 FY'25, reflecting our successful portfolio optimization efforts.

items.statement: Poultry focusing on branded business, reducing live bird exposure
items.quote: The Poultry segment recorded a decline in revenues, primarily due to lower volumes in the live bird business as we continued to focus on branded business and reduced our exposure to the live bird business.

items.statement: Animal Feed raw material position favourable, corn area up 11%, good monsoon expected to support bumper crop
items.quote: I believe that prices are not going to increase in season also significantly, because corn is the only area where we have seen inflation and there is an 11% growth in corn area. That is point number one. Point number two, the rain has been extremely good. If it starts tapering in a week or 10 days ' time, we will see a bumper corn production, which should take care of the increased demand of starc

items.statement: Poultry protein costs (soya, DDGS) at comfortable levels, lower than last year
items.quote: So even if corn has increased for some time, but if you see protein, particularly soya bean and DDGS because of huge increase in production of ethanol. So, the protein prices are very, very, I would say, at a very comfortable level. They are much lower than last year.

items.statement: Astec took ₹18 crore inventory write-down and ₹4-5 crore credit notes in Q1 due to price deterioration
items.quote: Yes. We have taken inventory write-downs in Q1 on tune of almost ₹ 18 crores. We brought all the inventory to the existing pricing level in the market.

items.statement: Bangladesh JV operations temporarily halted due to political unrest, expected to resume in 1-2 days as essential service
items.quote: However, the political developments there are unfortunate. And I must say that definitely last 1 week was very, very difficult for us and our employees because we have several staff with families there, and they were not able to move houses.

items.statement: Acquired 100% stake in Godrej Tyson Foods JV for agility in decision-making and future restructuring flexibility
items.quote: We felt that we would be better off managing it alone and that is what, I would say, motivated us to go for acquiring 100% stake in this business. Now having said that, apart from the opportunities which we can capture in this business because of agility and investments, etcetera, yes, there is other, I would say, freedom. This thing gives us our ability to do M&A or restructure this business, tak

items.statement: Consolidated PBT (ex-non-recurring) grew 36% to ₹169 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Profit before tax, excluding non-recurring items, improved by 36% to ₹ 169 crores as compared to ₹ 124 crores in Q1 FY'24.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue declined to ₹2,351 crore in Q1 FY25 from ₹2,510 crore in Q1 FY24
items.quote: The Company recorded consolidated revenue from operations of ₹ 2,351 crores in Q1 FY'25 as against ₹ 2,510 crores in Q1 FY'24.

items.statement: Palm oil OER expected to improve from August, FFB production target maintained for full year
items.quote: And in case we follow the last few years pattern, the OER improvement should also start from August onwards, and we should start clawing up in OER also. So I have still not given up. I strongly believe that, definitely, we will achieve last year's numbers come what may.

name: Aptus Value Housing Finance India Ltd

items.statement: Targets 25% CAGR revenue growth going forward
items.quote: I would say that I have always claimed that we have had a growth of 25% CAGR always, we work to see that how is it that we can continue to maintain this or better this.

items.statement: API capacity expansion from 100 KL to 250 KL with Rs 60 crore capex
items.quote: Our current production capacity stands at 100 KL, and we plan to expand it to 250 KL with an estimated CAPEX of around Rs. 60 crores.

items.statement: CCS facility at Dahej with Rs 90 crore capex for 1,800 MTPA initial capacity
items.quote: We are in the process of setting up a CCS facility at Dahej which is located 1 kilometer from the original unit. This facility would be dedicated for the production of Cross Carmellose and complex excipient products. With an estimated CAPEX of nearly Rs. 90 crores, the initial production capacity will be 1,800 metric tonnes per annum, which will be scalable up to 3,600 MTPA.

items.statement: MCC capacity utilization dropped to 66% in Q1 FY25 due to 7,000 MT expansion; expects full utilization by FY26
items.quote: Capacity utilization, by 31st March, 2024, we were at around almost, from unit wise if you see, Dahej around 93.4% and Jhagadia it was 97.3% and Hyderabad unit also 93%. Overall, it was around 94%. And during the 1st Quarter, Dahej unit it is around 56% and Jhagadia it is 53%, and Hyderabad it is 86%. Overall, it is 66%. This is because the expanded capacities, we have increased the capacities in

items.statement: API capacity utilization at 70% currently
items.quote: Capacity utilization is around 70%.

items.statement: O&M segment EBITDA margin typically 21-23%
items.quote: Yes, it's usually between 21% to 23% EBITDA.

items.statement: MCC pricing moderate this quarter, focusing on volumes; stable but not increasing
items.quote: This pricing is little in this quarter this is on moderate, there is no not much growth in pricing because we are concentrating on the volumes to our capacities. And going forward it will increase.

items.statement: MCC market expected to grow 7-9% CAGR in Southeast Asia to 2035
items.quote: See, there are market research studies which indicate that MCC market is expected to grow, especially in the Southeast Asian region it's expected to grow between 7% to 9% up to 2035.

items.statement: Healthy six months order book in place for MCC
items.quote: We have a healthy six months order book in place.

items.statement: Repeat orders constitute 80% of volumes and value; 20% new business development
items.quote: So, repeat orders are typically 80% of our volumes and value, 20% is the new business development which comes in. Sometimes it goes to 85%, sometimes it even touched 90%. But we have historically seen that 80% is the repeat order, 20% is the new customer or the new grade.

items.statement: Filed 3 CEP filings for APIs in EU; target 9 CEP filings this fiscal; expect approvals in ~9 months (Q4 FY25)
items.quote: For the current financial year we have a target that we will find in a total of nine CEP filings for our APIs. Once these CEP filings are approved, then of course the regulatory sales commence. We believe that in the next nine months or so we should start having approvals coming in from the EDPM.

items.statement: CCS facility environmental clearance expected in next four weeks after Gujarat Pollution Control Board review
items.quote: So, just four days back we have had another review by the Gujarat Pollution Control Board EC Committee, and I believe we have cleared all their queries. I do not foresee any further queries coming in. So, that should imply that in the next four weeks we are expecting to get the EC clearance document.

items.statement: Target to reduce operating cycle by at least 30 days this year; MCC debtor days 60-95, O&M ~45 days
items.quote: At least 30 days it will come down overall, and then slowly we will reduce it.

items.statement: Aims to reach near-zero debt by end of FY25; repaid using preferential warrant proceeds and internal accruals
items.quote: Yes, definitely by end of this year, almost debt would be zero level would be there.

items.statement: Raised Rs 100 crore via preferential share warrants of Rs 160 crore total for Trimax acquisition and expansion; Rs 60 crore earmarked for API expansion
items.quote: Already we have raised preferential share warrant for this. We have raised around 100 Cr for the total Rs. 160 crores for recreation and expansion. And there are Rs. 60 crores kept aside for the expansion of the API facility from existing 100 KL to 250 KL.

items.statement: Targets 35-40% revenue from API, 20-25% from O&M, balance from excipients (MCC + CCS) in 3-5 years
items.quote: I believe, that at least 35% to 40% of our revenue should be coming in from the API, operations and management should add in to around 20%, 25%, and the balance should be from the excipients, not just MCC because we will also have Cross Carmellose sodium.

items.statement: Q1 FY25: Operating income Rs 96 cr (+13% YoY), EBITDA Rs 21 cr (+28% YoY, 21.94% margin), PAT Rs 12.8 cr (+17% YoY, 13.38% margin)
items.value: Revenue Rs 96 cr, EBITDA Rs 21 cr, PAT Rs 12.8 cr
items.quote: Operating income exhibited a year-on-year revenue increase of 13% to Rs. 96 crores. EBITDA demonstrated a similar strength, rising by 28.05% year-on-year to Rs. 21 crores, translating to a margin of 21.94%. Net profit also recorded substantial growth, surging by 17.43% year-on-year to Rs. 12.8 crores with a PAT margin of 13.38%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 segment revenue: MCC Rs 71.83 cr (+2.79% YoY), O&M Rs 10.10 cr (+18.54% YoY), API Rs 8.99 cr
items.value: MCC Rs 71.83 cr, O&M Rs 10.10 cr, API Rs 8.99 cr
items.quote: Revenue from MCC has experienced a year-on-year growth of 2.79%, increasing from Rs. 69.88 crores to Rs. 71.83 crores. In Q1 FY 2025, revenue from operations and management grew by 18.54% to Rs. 10.10 crores from Rs. 8.52 crores. Revenue from the API segment for quarter one financial year 2025 is Rs. 8.99 crores.

items.statement: Saudi JV $180M sales target not achievable this year due to working capital constraints; premature to give revised number
items.quote: Now when we look at it deeper, we realized that we need to be gradual in this because $180 million, there is market potential available. But for that, for the kind of bid bond, for the kind of tender valuation which we have to put in money, it will be tremendous and probably our working capital and our cash flow will not permit us to put in that level of funding upfront.

items.statement: Bromine production target for FY25 is 22,000-25,000 metric tons including captive use
items.quote: We aim to produce nearly 22,000 to 25,000 metric tons of Bromine for the year, including captive requirements.

items.statement: Salt volume target for FY25 maintained at 4.5 million metric tons range
items.quote: Yes, it has been in 4.5 range.

items.statement: SOP sales expected to start in Q3 FY25 with meaningful contribution in H2 FY25
items.quote: So, it is a work in progress as we have said before and we continue to expect meaningful contributions in H2.

items.statement: Acume Bromine derivatives expected to contribute in H2 FY25 with sales starting September-October
items.quote: I think the sales will start coming through in H2 as I indicated. At the moment, I think we would probably be in a better position to tell you maybe on the next call or over the next couple of months, the ramp up is going on and on the demand side, I think we remain encouraged seeing the response we are getting.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbon business expected to start from H2 FY25 with revenue target of 200+ crores
items.quote: We are still hoping to reach the 200 plus mark on the sales and I think that is what we are endeavoring to.

items.statement: Flame Retardants Phase-2 capex approximately Rs 100 crores, commissioning not before March 2025
items.quote: For sure, we won't do it before March '25.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbon refurbishment budget Rs 40 crores for all plants, currently only starting two plants
items.quote: So, I think we anticipated that we would spend maybe at the outermost about Rs. 40 odd crores. So, I think we are well within budget and that was for all the plants, but at the moment we are only starting with two.

items.statement: Chemical industry seeing green shoots with demand restoration and stabilization in recent months
items.quote: The chemical industry has been seeing some green shoots recently and after a brief period, we are also witnessing the same. There is some restoration and stabilization of demand in the chemical industry in the last few months.

items.statement: Bromine demand steady domestically and encouraging pickup on export side from agrochemicals, pharma, flame retardants
items.quote: We continue to see a steady demand from the domestic market as well as encouraging market pickup on the export side from all end users like Agro Chemicals, Pharmaceuticals and Flame-Retardant manufacturers overseas.

items.statement: Salt demand firm with customer contracts in place, dispatch delays due to logistics temporary
items.quote: However, the demand remains firm, and customer contracts continue to be in place, and we only believe this to be temporary.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 38% maintained through operational efficiency measures
items.quote: EBITDA for this Q1 stood at around Rs. 849 million with a margin of 38%. Various operational efficiency measures have been undertaken across all activities to hold on to this margin range.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improvement driven by shift from co-generation to cheaper grid power, further improvement expected
items.quote: As I indicated in my earlier calls, we are trying to move away from the core generation plant to a grid system. So, half the capacity now comes from the grid. That savings is what you are seeing also help improve the EBITDA margin and subsequent quarters you will see a better improvement as we further enhance the grid capacity and take most of the power from the grid, which is cheaper than the co-

items.statement: Logistics challenges at ports (vessel/container shortage, freight costs) impacted dispatch and shipments in Q1
items.quote: We on the other hand has experienced some delays on availability of vessels, containers and increased freight costs which pose some challenge for Indian manufacturers. This has impacted the overall dispatch and business momentum across the board.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbon starting two plants in phased manner for Oil & Gas drilling and CBF products
items.quote: I think it will be in a phased manner because they are different plants. So, they would, we are exercising caution. We don't want to jump in and start spending money everywhere. So, I think we would like to be a bit more pragmatic in what we think we should start. So, we are starting the two plants that have direct connection to the Oil & Gas, Drilling industry, as well as the Clear Brine Fluids p

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue mix: Bromine 44%, Industrial Salt 55%, SOP 1%
items.quote: Bromine contributed around 44% of the total revenue and Industrial Salt contributed around 55%. The balance of 1% has come from SOP.

items.statement: Acume has 10 client approvals for CBF and PTA Synthesis, engaging with >1/3 of client base
items.quote: The response to CBF and PTA Synthesis is very encouraging and has already received approval from around 10 odd clients. We are in discussion with more than one-third of our total client base.

items.statement: Salt contracts long-term (1-2 years), all signed contracts continue, no sales side challenge
items.quote: So, as you all will be aware, we have fixed contracts on Salt and those contracts continue to run. So, there is no challenge for us on the sales side. All those contracts have already been signed and continue to come through.

items.statement: Bromine competition exists but first-mover advantage, infrastructure and delivery capability provide moat
items.quote: I think competition in any industry is going to happen. It is just about having a first mover advantage. So, there are I think couple of more people who are producing. I think the question will always remain the capacity that we have, the infrastructure that we have and the ability to deliver the volumes that we have.

items.statement: Leasehold land renewal with Gujarat Government work in progress, position unchanged from last call
items.quote: So, I think that is a work in progress. The position has not changed since the last call. I think we continue to actively engage with the government and we are hoping sooner than later on that front.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 volumes: Salt 660,000 tons, Bromine 4,700+ tons, SOP 66 tons
items.value: Salt 660,000 tons, Bromine 4,700+ tons, SOP 66 tons
items.quote: Volume, the sold quantity of Salt around 660,000, Bromine is around 4,700 plus and SOP is around 66 tons.

items.statement: Bromine domestic revenue Rs 58.8 crores, export revenue Rs 34.9 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Coming to your first question, my domestic sale of Bromine is around Rs. 58.8 crores and exports around Rs. 34.9 crores.

items.statement: Monsoon dilution in brine concentration historically weakens H2 but prepared and not deviating from targets
items.quote: Historically it is a bit weaker simply because of the rain and there is some amount of dilution in the concentration levels in the brine. But I think we are prepared for that as we are every year, and I don't think we will deviate too much from what we set out as targets even historically.

items.statement: Bromine pricing stabilized over last few quarters, no reason seen for price drop
items.quote: I think the pricing that we are seeing now, I think is stabilized over the last couple of quarters and I don't see a reason for it to drop.

items.statement: Oren Hydrocarbon NCLT order received July 9, 2024, acquisition for Specialty Mud Chemicals and CBF products
items.quote: We received the NCLT order on 9th of July 2024 for acquiring this unit. This unit focuses on the Hydrocarbon space and serves the Oil & Gas and drilling industries. The key rationale behind this acquisition was to offer a product basket to clients by adding Specialty Mud Chemicals and CBF products.

items.statement: Raised INR800 crores via QIP, primary infusion, 2.5x oversubscribed, allotted to long-only funds
items.quote: I am pleased to announce that we have successfully closed and raised INR800 crores of equity via the QIP. The funds raised through this QIP is primary in nature and infused into the company entirely.

items.statement: Guidance to launch two projects per quarter in FY25
items.quote: This is in line with our guidance of launching two projects per quarter this year.

items.statement: Pre-sales INR611 crores in Q1 FY25, up 22% YoY; area sold down 16% YoY
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, Rustomjee Group recorded pre -sales of INR611 crores, reflecting a robust 22% year-on-year growth compared to INR502 crores in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Average realisation increased from INR17,367 to INR25,164 per sq ft YoY
items.quote: Hence, average realisation rate has gone up from INR17,367 per square foot in Q1 FY '24 to INR25,164 per square foot in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Collections steady at INR485 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our collections remain steady at INR485 crores, demonstrating our ability to generate strong cash flows.

items.statement: Launched two projects with 0.63 msf saleable area, GDV ~INR2,000 crores; 20% inventory sold in first few weeks; new launches contributed 42% of Q1 pre-sales
items.quote: We launched two new projects in this quarter. The saleable size of these two projects was 0.63 million square feet and the estimated GDP of these projects is about INR2,000 crores.

items.statement: Entered plotted development with 88-acre Kasara Phase 1 (1.5 msf, ~500 plots); RERA received, launched in Q2 FY25
items.quote: Separately, we are excited to announce our foray into the plotted developments with our first acquisition in Kasara in July of 2024. This first phase of 88-acre land parcel, nestled amidst the scenic beauty of the mountains, is a strategic addition to our portfolio.

items.statement: RERA received for two Urbania towers (GDV ~INR1,700 crores), launching August 2023; added redevelopment project 0.35 msf, GDV ~INR984 crores in Q1
items.quote: In addition to Kasara, we have also received RERA registration for two towers in Urbania, Thane, which we will be launching in August '23, and these have a GDV of approximately INR1,700 crores.

items.statement: Operating cash flow INR108 crores in Q1 FY25; investment in new projects INR158 crores (20% QoQ, ~4x YoY)
items.quote: Given strong collections, the company has generated an OCF Operating Cash Flow of INR108 crores in Q1 FY '25. Investment in new projects in Q1 FY '25 is INR158 crores, showing a 20% quarter-on-quarter and approximately 4x year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Revenue INR422 crores (+55% YoY), EBITDA INR58 crores, PAT INR26 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Moving to the consolidated key financial numbers, the revenue of Q1 FY '25 stands at INR422 crores of 55% year-on-year basis. The EBITDA and PAT for this period stand at INR58 crores and INR26 crores respectively.

items.statement: Gross debt INR458 crores, gross D/E 0.18:1, net debt nil; ICRA upgraded rating to A with positive outlook
items.quote: With respect to our liquidity position, the gross debt stands at INR458 crores and the gross debt-to-equity ratio is 0.18:1 at the end of Q1 FY '25, which is very well within our guidance. The net debt for this same period is nil.

items.statement: Land payment run rate ~INR150 crores per quarter (INR550-600 crores for FY25)
items.quote: I think we are going to pretty much maintain the run rate of about INR150 crores every quarter, which means that about INR600 crores for the whole year.

items.statement: Crown project: balance cost to complete INR700-800 crores (mainly C tower & amenities); good receivables from sold stock
items.quote: So, Neel, on the crown, we have about INR700 to INR800 crores of the balance course to complete. Largely, it is related to the C tower because, as you know, the bulk of the A and B towers we have completed.

items.statement: Mid-market (INR1-3 cr) and aspirational (up to INR7 cr) segments remain strong growth drivers; Q1 seasonally slower but sales up 22% YoY; mid+aspirational Q1 sales INR361 cr vs INR258 cr YoY
items.quote: We continue to be extremely strong and bullish on the mid-march, which is INR1 to INR3 crores, and aspiration, which is up to INR7 crores from there. The largest part of our acquisitions also continue to take place in this segment.

items.statement: Basant Park (Chembur) launch expected Q4 FY25; Bandra Bandstand work started, launch timing under deliberation
items.quote: If I am to make a studied guess, I think it would be in the fourth quarter of this year is when we would be launching that project for sales.

items.statement: Bandra-Ajmera redevelopment: sales work initiation expected end of FY25 or Q1 FY26
items.quote: We're hoping that we'll be in a position to initiate work on that project in terms of the sales work on that project also maybe end of this year or maybe in the first quarter of the next year itself.

items.statement: Economic share: 100% in most projects; Urbania 51%, Kamal Kunj 50-50, Goregaon 50-50/51-49, Jariwala DM fee 17% top line + incentive; smaller JVs at 73%, 23%
items.quote: Other than those projects, we have a 100% economic share. Urbania, our economic share is 51% on the residential side. Keppel is a partner at Urbania and in this joint venture, the Keppel holds 49% interest.

items.statement: Employee cost steady-state after one-time Crest consolidation bump of INR36 crores in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The Crest, where we take care of the after-sales service. That we started consolidating and about INR36 crores of the Crest manpower there was a one-time bump-up.

items.statement: Plotted development strategy: focus on MMR and areas serving MMR customers (e.g., Mumbai-Pune corridor); strong landowner interest due to brand trust
items.quote: So all those places that can serve our customers in MMR are the ones that we will strongly consider to take up for plotted developments.

items.statement: RERA registrations received for Kasara plotted project and two Urbania towers
items.quote: As on date, we have received the RERA registration of the same and have launched the project in the current quarter, that is Q2 FY'25.

items.statement: ESG initiatives: employee survey, human rights policy integration, green tariff adoption in Mumbai suburban projects, net zero exploration
items.quote: We have diligently engaged our internal stakeholders through a comprehensive employee survey, reinforcing our dedication towards sustainable development. The integration of our human rights policy into our employee handbook marks a pivotal step forward.

items.statement: EBITDA growth guidance of 10-12% for FY25 and ~15% annual growth over next three years
items.quote: We remain optimistic about the future and maintain our guidance to achieve EBITDA growth of approximately 10% to 12% in FY 25 and long-term goal of around 15% annua l growth in next three

items.statement: CDMO/CMO revenue growth guidance of 25-30% YoY for FY25
items.quote: We are thoroughly optimistic that we should be able to grow this segment by 25% to 30% Y-o-Y, in FY25.

items.statement: Total FY25 capex outlay of Rs.500-550 crores including Xanthine, Atali and solar projects
items.quote: So, basically the outlay, what we are saying is around Rs.500 to 550 crores would be the CAPEX that would be done in this year.

items.statement: Xanthine expansion capex of Rs.150 crores to increase capacity to 9000 MT by early FY26
items.quote: Yes, so we are anticipating close to Rs.150 crore CAPEX for the Xanthine project. This will be spent across two sites that we use for the Xanthine project

items.statement: Atali project capex of Rs.375 crores, commissioning by Q4 FY25
items.quote: the Atali project has a total outlay of approximately Rs.375 crores. And the solar project, which is on the verge of completion, is around RS.90 crores.

items.statement: Solar power plant capex of Rs.90 crores, commissioning in Q1 FY25, to generate 1/3rd of power needs
items.quote: Lastly, setting up of a new solar power plant at Akola Maharashtra is progressing well and estimated to get commissioned in the current quarter . This project is estimated to generate 1/3rd of our power requirement

items.statement: Xanthine capacity expansion from 5000 to 9000 MT, completion by early FY26
items.quote: We expect to complete this project in the beginning of FY26 and thereby achieve a total production capacity of 9000 metric tonnes.

items.statement: Atali project adding 450-500 KL capacity (25-30% increase) by Q4 FY25
items.quote: Atali we are going to add almost 400 to 500 KL, close to 500 KL of volume capacity and which will significantly increase our capacity almost by 25%, 30% from the current level.

items.statement: Current CDMO/API capacity utilization at 85%
items.quote: See, currently we are using the facility for CDMO/CMO and Intermediate and API combined. So, overall our occupancy is 85%.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO projects increased from 40 to 53 in six months, with 27 commercial and 26 development projects across 18 customers
items.quote: Yes, as we have informed you, that earlier we were having close to 40 projects that we were doing, and this quarter that number swelled to 53 projects.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO commercial projects grew from 16 to 27 in one year, with 2 new customers added
items.quote: in six months we have added commercial projects from 16 to 27 and we have a strong pipeline of early phase projects also. So, now we have total 53 projects which are currently live with 18 customers.

items.statement: Strong Xanthine export growth despite Chinese competition, 57% of Xanthine revenue from exports
items.quote: But still, as you have seen that we have been able to grow our export business overall. And this quarter we have been able to do almost 57% of the Xanthine was exported.

items.statement: Biosecure Act driving increased CDMO/CMO inquiries and project wins from US companies shifting away from China
items.quote: Yes, the Biosecure Act has forced US companies to shift away from China, and that's why other non-Chinese suppliers of these intermediates and the GMP intermediates are seeing more inquiries, and we are benefiting from this.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin dipped to 17% from 21% QoQ due to lower CDMO contribution (2% vs 18%)
items.quote: if you look at quarter-on-quarter, you will see some up and down, because the CDMO/CMO business, which basically contributes, or which is the highest margin business for us, that basically goes up and down on quarter-on-quarter basis, as you have seen in the last quarter, it was 18%, its contribution to the overall revenue of the quarter, which has come down to 2% in this quarter.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin at 48% vs 54% last quarter, expected to recover as CDMO revenue picks up
items.quote: Yes, so that is definitely the CDMO/CMO segment revenue is less this quarter, and of course it will get picked up in subsequent quarters of this year, and which will rationalize overall percentage.

items.statement: Overall gross margin range of 50-55%, with CDMO/CMO highest, API/Intermediates better than Xanthine
items.quote: So, at the overall level we have a gross margin of around 50% to 55%.

items.statement: Xanthine spot prices down 15-20% YoY, tracking raw material cost declines, expected to stabilize at current levels
items.quote: Xanthine has many molecules, so we won't be able to share but overall, the pricing has come down by around 15%, 20% over last year in the spot market.

items.statement: Chinese aggression continues in Xanthine spot market, but contract-spot mix helps maintain margins
items.quote: China is as aggressive as ever, and the pricing have been reduced in the spot market, so we have a balance of contrac t and spot. So, it is challenging for the spot business

items.statement: API/Intermediates: 55% regulated markets, 35% rest of world, 10% non-regulated
items.quote: Out of this turnover the regulated market contributed 55%, and the rest of the world market contributed 35%, and the balance 10% was from the non-regulated market.

items.statement: CDMO/CMO serving 18 customers with 53 projects, added 2 new customers in last six months
items.quote: We are presently working with 18 customers on 53 projects, of which 27 projects are on the commercial stage at the customer's end, and 26 are under different stages of development at customer's end.

items.statement: Chinese competition aggressive in Xanthine spot market, but company gaining share via customer relationships

items.statement: Targeting minimum 4 JDA projects per year with upward of INR5,000 crore GDV
items.quote: Of course, our target and our desire is to add minimum 4 projects every year, and upward of INR5,000 crore GDV is what we are targeting.

items.statement: Lifestyle business targeting 200-plus store additions in FY25
items.quote: We had given our guidance of doing around 200-plus store footprint in the year. We are continuing to accelerate on that.

items.statement: Engineering business expects mid-to-late teens growth over next 2-3 years
items.quote: So basically, in terms of growth, we have a mid- to late-teens growth, that will happen, of course, based on a lot of things that are now developing.

items.statement: Real estate booking of INR611 crores in Q1 FY25 driven by Thane and Bandra projects
items.quote: In first quarter fiscal '25, the company achieved a strong booking of INR611 crores, primarily driven by the demand for The Address by GS Season 2 in Thane and the recently launched The Address by GS in

items.statement: Total real estate revenue potential of INR32,000 crores from Thane land bank and 4 JDA projects
items.quote: With the development of Thane land bank and current 4 JDAs, gives the company a potential revenue of INR32,000 crores over the next few years.

items.statement: Engineering business has long-term contracts providing visibility for 3-10 years
items.quote: We generally have long-term contracts and orders. So rather than giving you a number, it varies depending on certain contracts are 3 years, certain contracts are 5 years. We also have contracts up to 10 years.

items.statement: Raymond Limited Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 16.2%, up 82% YoY
items.quote: During the quarter, the company has delivered an EBITDA of INR162 crores in the first quarter of fiscal year 2025 with an EBITDA margin of 16.2%.

items.statement: Real estate EBITDA margin 17.5% in Q1 FY25, lower due to marketing and initial costs of new projects
items.quote: The EBITDA margin stood at 17.5% for the quarter is lower as compared to the same quarter last year, majorly due to marketing and initial cost of new projects.

items.statement: Engineering EBITDA margin 13.2% in Q1 FY25 due to product mix change
items.quote: During the quarter, the business reported an EBITDA margin at 13.2%, mainly due to change in product mix.

items.statement: Branded Textiles EBITDA margin 10% in Q1 FY25 due to scale deleverage and mix change
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was at 10% in the first quarter of fiscal '25 due to decline in revenue and average selling price because of the change in the product mix.

items.statement: Branded Apparel EBITDA margin 4.8% in Q1 FY25 due to early end-of-season sales and higher marketing
items.quote: The segment delivered an EBITDA margin of 4.8% in the first quarter of fiscal '25 compared to 6.4% in the same quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Garmenting EBITDA margin 3.5% in Q1 FY25 due to product mix change and capacity ramp-up costs
items.quote: During the quarter, EBITDA margin was at 3.5% as compared to 9.8% reported in the previous year, mainly due to change in product mix.

items.statement: Invested INR200 crores in garmenting capacity expansion, nearly doubling capacity
items.quote: We have expanded our capacity by investing INR200 crores, which will be highly beneficial as this capacity can be quickly utilized to meet customer demand.

items.statement: Garmenting capacity nearly doubled with INR200 crore investment, can be quickly utilized
items.quote: Our capacities are already being almost close to double, and we have vertically integrated play already.

items.statement: Real estate demand sustained with strong interest from first-time homebuyers and affordable luxury segment
items.quote: The real estate market maintains its upward momentum, driven by increasing residential demand with expectations for this trend to persist in the forthcoming quarters.

items.statement: Engineering consumables weak in domestic and export markets due to heatwave, inflation, elections and logistics costs
items.quote: Engineering consumables has been weak, both in domestic as well as export markets. Further, the aerospace sector is also showing promising signs.

items.statement: Lifestyle business impacted by negligible wedding dates, prolonged heatwave and general elections in Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the quarter, lifestyle business witnessed weaker revenue due to discretionary spend, continued to remain under press ure, prolonged heatwave, which impacted footfalls in retail outlets, general elections, negligible wedding dates impacted demand in

items.statement: Strong wedding season expected in H2 FY25 with 45 wedding days across 4-5 months
items.quote: The second half has got a very, very large number of weddings, almost the second half of the season has got some 45 days of wedding across, spread over 4, 5 months.

items.statement: Real estate margin progression: lower in launch year, peaks towards project end, average 20-25%
items.quote: Over a 4- or 5-year project, the margin of the project keeps going up and it peaks towards the end of the project so that the average margin comes to around 20%, 25%.

items.statement: Engineering aerospace business at ~INR75 crores run rate with 25% margin, lower revenue recognition in Q1 due to shipping delays
items.quote: Basically, if you see, the aerospace business always is very high margin. And what has happened is because the customers and the shipping delays, which is there due to lack of availability of containers, the proportion of revenue recognition for the aerospace is significantly lower proportioned compared to the auto as well as the engineering consumables.

items.statement: Lifestyle business secondaries higher than primaries, no channel inventory buildup concern
items.quote: In fact, our secondaries versus primary gap has been on the positive side there, in fact, our secondaries have been higher than primaries.

items.statement: Garmenting acquired new customers and expanded into new geographies driving 5% revenue growth
items.quote: This growth was driven by acquiring new customers and enhancing our presence in new geographies.

items.statement: Bangladesh exporter challenges creating opportunity for Indian garmenting, Raymond reached out to customers sourcing from Bangladesh
items.quote: In the last few days, challenges faced by the exporters in Bangladesh have presented a great opportunity for all the Indian exporters and particularly Raymond Lifestyle, due to our integrated supply chain from fabric to garment.

items.statement: Raymond Limited net-debt-free with net cash surplus of INR618 crores, up INR117 crores from March 2024
items.quote: We continue to remain a net-debt-free business with net cash surplus of INR618 crores, which has increased by INR117 crores compared to March '24.

items.statement: Gross debt INR870 crores including MPPL acquisition debt and MPPL working capital debt
items.quote: Our total gross debt stood at INR870 crores, which includes the debt taken to acquire MPPL business and existing working capital of MPPL.

items.statement: Real estate vertical demerger announced July 4, 2024, expected to complete in 14-16 months
items.quote: Vertical demerger of the real estate business, which was announced the 4th of July 2024, and will take almost 14 to 16 months to complete the demerger of the real e state business

items.statement: Engineering restructuring into two subsidiaries (aerospace/defense and auto/engineering consumables) expected to complete in FY25
items.quote: The restructuring of the engineering business, which we expect to complete in this fiscal year.

items.statement: Maini Precision acquisition completed March 29, 2024, consolidated from Q1 FY25
items.quote: Raymond Limited completed the acquisition of Maini Precision Products Limited, MPPL, on 29th of March 2024. Starting from first quarter of fiscal '25, the company has consolidated the performance of its engineering business to include MPPL.

items.statement: Real estate sales increased 108% YoY to INR488 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our Raymond Realty business, which offers affordable luxury apartments ranging from 1 to 4 BHK that caters to multiple segments of society, and our proven ability to execute the project at a faster pace, enables our sales to increase by 108% to INR488 crores in the first quarter of fiscal '25 from INR235 crores in the first quarter of fiscal '24.

items.statement: Engineering segment sales doubled to INR419 crores in Q1 FY25 including MPPL consolidation
items.quote: The segment sales stood at INR419 crores in the first quarter of fiscal '25, doubling revenue compared to INR209 crores in first quarter of last fiscal.

items.statement: Lifestyle business revenue declined 8% YoY to INR1,249 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In the first quarter of fiscal '25, the lifestyle business revenue stood at INR1,249 crores, lower by 8% compared to INR1,353 crores in the first quarter of fiscal '24.

items.statement: Lifestyle retail footprint at 1,539 stores across 600 towns including 118 Ethnix stores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: We continued to strengthen our retail footprint as we opened 21 new stores during the quarter as well taking the tally to 1,539 stores as on 30th of June 2024, which are spread across 600 towns and cities in India, which include 118 stores of Ethnix by Raymond brand.

items.statement: Capex guidance of INR20,000 crores for FY25 with 55-60% to renewables, 30% to T&D, 10-15% to thermal and new investments
items.quote: We have a very ambitious plan of INR20,000 crores investment in this year and we are on track to implement that.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex spend of INR4,000 crores with 60% in renewables and 40% in transmission and distribution
items.quote: And in this quarter, we have already spent INR4,000 crores of capex with nearly 60% in the renewable and balance 40% in transmission and distribution.

items.statement: 4 GW cell and module plant progressing well; module plant stabilized at full capacity, first 2 GW cell plant commissioning this month, next 2 GW next month, full production from Q3
items.quote: Our cell plant is ready to get commissioned in this month, the first 2 gigawatt will get commissioned. And in next month, we will have the next 2 gigawatt commissioning and we expect that it will get stabilized in the next 2, 3 months and the full capacity will start getting produced from the third quarter onwards.

items.statement: Nearly 8 GW of projects under implementation including 5 GW own and 3 GW third-party EPC; targeting 3+ GW commissioning in FY25 and 4 GW in FY26
items.quote: So we have nearly 8 gigawatt of projects, which is under implementation now. And we are fully tied up for all the projects for this financial year where we expect to do more than 3 gigawatts of implementation and next year of 4 gigawatts.

items.statement: Power demand grew nearly 11% in Q1 FY25 and continues to be very robust going forward
items.quote: And it continues to be very, very robust going forward also. In the last budget announced by our honorable Finance Minister. There are four things that she mentioned, which has a huge impact on us.

items.statement: 600 MW hydro plant in Bhutan with Druk Green Power finalized; INR6,900 crores investment, 40% equity, construction starting later this calendar year, completion within 5 years
items.quote: We have also now finalized an agreement to execute a 600 megawatt hydro plant in Bhutan with Druk Green Power. This is a project which will produce power in Bhutan and partly will be consumed in Bhutan, especially during the winter months. And in the summer months, it will be sold in India.

items.statement: Pumped hydro storage: 2,800 MW pipeline with 1,000 MW possibly starting later this calendar year and 1,800 MW by mid next year
items.quote: As you are aware that in Tata Power, we have already taken initiatives. We have given 2,800 megawatts out of which the 1,000 megawatt should po ssibly start in this year, later part of this calendar year once we get all the necessary approvals. And the other 1,800 megawatt should start by mid of next year

items.statement: Delhi Distribution Q1 operating profit increased sharply to INR554 crores vs INR321 crores YoY, includes one-time tariff order impact of INR163 crores
items.quote: Yes. There is a onetime tariff order impact of INR163 crores and that has been established.

items.statement: Net debt increased by INR4,300 crores to INR42,000 crores; net debt to underlying EBITDA less than 3x, net debt to equity less than 1.1x
items.quote: And we do expect that our net debt, which has gone up by INR4,300 crores to INR42,000 crores will be very, very calibrated when we look at the financial metrics of net debt to underlying EBITDA, which is less than 3x and our net debt to equity is less than 1.1x.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded from AA+ to AA+ stable by both ICRA and CARE, expected to lower financing costs and improve profitability
items.quote: We have got upgraded in terms of our credit rating from AA+ to AA plus stable, both from ICRA and CARE. And this will help us to further bring down our financing costs and to that extent to improve our profitability.

items.statement: Rooftop solar inquiries up 10x vs last year; meaningful revenue accretion expected from Q3-Q4 FY25
items.quote: There is a huge uptick. And it is something to the extent of 10x more than what we saw last year. So great opportunity. It's a question of how quickly we can convert them and execute these orders.

items.statement: Transmission projects: Part A of stressed assets commissioned, Part B completing FY25, two TBCB projects operational in FY26, new 765 kV Odisha intra-state project to complete in 24 months
items.quote: The two projects where we had started, which was under stressed assets which we took over, the Part A of that project is already commissioned and started giving us returns. The Part B is under implementation and will get completed in this financial year. The two projects that we won in the bids, in the TBCB bids last year, they are under implementation and will get implemented and become operation

items.statement: Negative working capital impact of INR2,500 crores in Q1 due to delayed payments from large EPC projects; partial collection in July, balance expected August-September
items.quote: Yes, there are some payments which we were expecting from some of our large EPC projects that we were executing. That got differed. Some of it has been collected in the month of July and balance in August and September.

items.statement: Focus shifting to complex hybrid and FDRE projects with storage rather than plain solar/wind; aggressively bidding for hybrid/FDRE projects
items.quote: So we will definitely look at accelerating some of these projects. But our objective is that we will be participating more in complex and hybrid projects and FDRE projects then just lean in our solar and wind projects.

items.statement: Tata Steel decarbonization: 966 MW hybrid projects signed (part commissioning FY25, balance FY26), 100 MW executed, another 100 MW under finalization
items.quote: We have already signed an agreement with them to make -- to provide them 966 megawatts of hybrid projects. Part of it will get commissioned in this financial year and balance in the next financial year.

items.statement: PM Surya Ghar program targeting 1 crore rooftop installations in 3-4 years; Tata Power already has 1 lakh+ installations and positioned as market leader
items.quote: The first is the focus on the PM Surya Ghar Program. And as all of you are aware, we have already got more than 1 lakh rooftop solar installations. And with the focus of the government to install nearly 1 crore in next 3 to 4 years.

items.statement: Transmission evacuation constraints: new lines only expected FY27-28, limiting ability to bid new renewable projects until evacuation tied up
items.quote: Also, what we have found is that while the renewable projects can be implemented in 24 months, the availability of evacuation arrangement transmission lines are taking much longer. And we expect the new set of transmission lines to only come in FY '27 and '28.

items.statement: Pumped hydro storage project construction timeline 44-46 months; approvals mostly received, balance expected by September-October, construction starting this year
items.quote: And we expect that the project will be completed in 44 to 46 months.

items.statement: Bhutan hydro project: 30-year PPA, returns not less than CERC norms, ISTS charges waiver expected per government policy for projects up to 2030
items.quote: Like a standard PPA will be there for any IPP. And this will primarily be for 25 or 30 years. The agreement is for 30 years. So we typically have a 30-year PPA for hydro plants.

items.statement: Section-11 currently in operation until October 15; expects extension or amicable solution
items.quote: It's already in other operations. It's there until 15th of October. And we expect either that will get extended or we will find any amicable solution.

items.statement: Indonesian coal JV profitability declining due to stabilized coal prices
items.quote: Yes, coal companies profitability has been comi ng down because the coal prices are not going up and they have stabilized at certain level. So this is the profit that the coal company has been able to share

items.statement: Rooftop solar: claims 50-60% market share in quality segments; fragmented competitors not seen as serious threat
items.quote: So whatever, whoevere is looking for quality products, longterm, we have 50% to 60% market share actually in those sectors. So I think no one has the type of market access and the product quality as we have.

items.statement: Solar manufacturing plant realization details to be shared in Q3 after stabilization
items.quote: Very difficult at this stage to say that the plant is still stabilizing. And we'll be able to share more details maybe in quarter 3, once the plant has stabilized for this.

items.statement: Merchant sales from Haldia (100 MW) and Prayagraj (150 MW) plants; specific sales and EBITDA numbers to be provided separately
items.quote: So our Haldia plant is a merchant plant. So it's 120 megawatts and I think the 20 megawatts is given to Tata Steel, balance 100 megawatts to merchants and so also our Prayagraj is nearly 150- megawatt is available for either short term or me rchant sales

items.statement: Transmission capex to continue aggressively alongside renewable bidding; balance sheet capability maintained for both
items.quote: There are so -- we'll bid both of them aggressively. I mentioned to you that we are also doing a large amount of capex in our transmission business and we'll continue to do that.

items.statement: Solar pump business: no new installations in FY24 or Q1 FY25 as no new orders received since FY22
items.quote: So, we have not installed any more solar pumps in this year because th e last order, which was given in FY '22 and whatever order was given, we have completed that. The new set of orders have not come and so we have not seen

items.statement: Expect to exceed 50% growth in defense business for FY25 while maintaining profitability
items.quote: Overall, I would st ill say that we will exceed 50% growth for the year and maintain our profitability

items.statement: Expect stable to positive year overall with industrial and defense businesses growing
items.quote: So, overall whether it is the automotive business or the defense business or the industrial business, we expect to see a stable year, stable to positive year.

items.statement: Aerospace business expected to grow 15-20% in FY25 and strong double-digit growth in FY26
items.quote: But we expect, this year, a 15% to 20% growth in our business, and next year a strong double-digit growth, and we are on track for that.

items.statement: Overseas subsidiaries expected to show substantial improvement in FY25, especially Europe
items.quote: I expect that we will see a substantial improvement in the overseas subsidiaries for this year as well, especially for Europe.

items.statement: US aluminum operations expected to reduce EBITDA loss substantially by end of FY25
items.quote: We are confident that the losses in the US will come down very substantially by the end of this fiscal and Europe should do better as well.

items.statement: European aluminum pricing repair to be completed by Q2 FY25 and implemented by Q4 FY25
items.quote: So, it will be done by next quarter fully. And, then it will be implemented, and it will be in place.

items.statement: European steel forging business right-sizing exercise to complete in 6-8 months
items.quote: We have to find the right s izing exercise, which will involve footprint optimization as well as manpower rationalization in the next six to eight months

items.statement: Combined capex for FY25 and FY26 expected to be around Rs.1,000 crores
items.quote: So, I would say overall, between this year and next year whatever we are spending will get spent over this year and next year be about a 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Secured new business worth Rs.980 crores in Q1 FY25 across defense, aluminum and ferrous castings
items.quote: During the quarter, company has secured new business worth almost Rs.980 crores across various sectors, including defense, aluminum and ferrous castings and core forging business.

items.statement: Defense order book at Rs.5,400 crores with current run rate of Rs.2,500 crores annualized
items.quote: new current run rate is somewhere around 2500 crores annualized, and the order book is somewhere around 5400 crores.

items.statement: ATAGS artillery order for 307 guns valued at Rs.4,000-4,500 crores expected to finalize by August 2024
items.quote: So, the current order of ATAGS that is supposed to open is roughly 307 odd guns. So, that itself is, roughly in excess of 40 00, 4500 crores.

items.statement: India CV market expected to be flat (+/-5%) for FY25 with heavier Q3 and Q4
items.quote: As far as India is concerned , the expectation for the year is Y TD it will be flat (+/-5%). So, we are seeing quarter progression in the same way , it seems like there will be a heavier quarter three and even heavier quarter four

items.statement: US Class 8 truck build rates stable with enough backlogs despite order intake decline
items.quote: There are enough backlogs in the system, the build rates are still stable, so it's not really affecting production in the US as of now.

items.statement: European demand weakness expected to impact top line growth for next 1-2 quarters
items.quote: Unfortunately, there is some trepidation on the demand side conditions in Europe currently because of macroeconomic and geopolitical issues, which are probably putting a slight question mark on the overall top line growth in the EU.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 260 bps YoY to 18.5% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins improved by 260 basis points on a Y-o-Y basis to 18.5% in this quarter, with bulk of improvement driven by Indian entities.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 28.1% in Q1 FY25, up 18.9% YoY
items.quote: Standalone, EBITDA grew by 18.9% on a Y-o-Y basis, translating into EBITDA margin of 28.1%.

items.statement: European aluminum operations posted EBITDA of Rs.37 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Despite a weak demand environment in Europe in this quarter, our European operations posted an EBITDA of Rs.37 crores.

items.statement: US aluminum operations reduced EBITDA loss to Rs.23 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: US operations reduce their EBITDA loss to Rs.23 crores.

items.statement: European aluminum operations target breakeven or slightly positive EBITDA by Q4 FY25
items.quote: On the Europe side we are getting resolution for the price repair. And we will see that by Q4 we will be 00, if not slightly positive.

items.statement: Old aluminum forging business in Europe running at 13-14% EBITDA margin
items.quote: Yes, that is running quite well.

items.statement: European aluminum utilization at 75%, US aluminum at 50% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Utilization in Europe and US aluminum was at 75% and 50%, respectively.

items.statement: European aluminum utilization at 70%, US at 50% currently
items.quote: In Europe it's about 70% and in US about 50%.

items.statement: US aluminum Phase 2 capex ongoing, 28-30 month implementation timeline, not being rushed
items.quote: Unfortunately, the CAPEX is a project. It takes about 28 to 30 months to implement. So, we are already in the middle of that, we are not going to rush to do it, but we have to do it anyway.

items.statement: Proposing fundraise of up to Rs.2,000 crores for growth in India, combination of organic and inorganic
items.quote: On the proposal for fundraising of up to 2,000 crores, the last time that Bharat Forge raised any funds, any equity was in 2010-11 during the global financial crisis. This fundraise is solely going to be growth oriented for deployment in India.

items.statement: Fundraise to be used for manufacturing footprint expansion in India for global and domestic opportunities
items.quote: It will be for growth of manufacturing footprint in India, for both global and Indian opportunities, and it will be a combination of both Greenfield and inorganic.

items.statement: All defense manufacturing licenses transferred to wholly owned subsidiary KSSL
items.quote: All the licenses that we have got from the Ministry of Home Affairs for defense manufacturing, which requires specific licenses have now been obtained for KSSL, so all that business will be in KSSL.

items.statement: VRS at Mundra plant to reduce few hundred employees over next couple of years for modernization
items.quote: We aim to reduce a few hundred people from this plant in the next couple of years.

items.statement: Freight cost increases in Q1 FY25 largely mitigated through customer recoveries and structural actions
items.quote: Overall, we have managed to mitigate almost all the freight cost increases for this quarter. And we will continue to work on that and between whatever we can do and whatever we structurally do with our customers, we will manage this.

items.statement: India CV market share increased despite market decline, revenue higher than underlying market
items.quote: Secondly, in the domestic market although the numbers have gone down in CV, production and sales, our market share has gone up and our revenue is higher than the underlying market.

items.statement: India needs ~4,000 artillery guns across categories; Bharat Forge has 9 platforms to compete in all
items.quote: India itself needs close to 4000 guns. It needs guns of several different kinds. It needs Towed guns, it needs mount ed guns, it needs tracked and self -propelled guns , it needs 105 mounted guns. Fortunately for us, we make all of these products , we have nine artillery platforms, so we can compete in any category that is envisaged or required

items.statement: Tork Motors investment impaired due to funding freeze and FAME subsidy norms impact
items.quote: On the impairment of investment in Tork, it's basically a victim of the fundin g freeze and the impact of the FAME subsidy norms. Twice, we were very close to getting investors, twice Tork was very close to getting investors in its company, but that did not materialize. As you are aware, we are investors in Tork, and we have invested slightly more than 150 crores over all

items.statement: Consolidated ROCE at 18.4% as of June 2024, moving toward target
items.quote: Consolidated balance sheet continues to remain robust, with ROCE moving in the right direction of our target. And currently we are at 18.4% as of June 2024.

items.statement: JSA Auto EBITDA grew ~50% YoY in Q1 FY25, expected to cross Rs.1,000 crores sales shortly
items.quote: Our JSA Auto has recorded an extremely good quarter. We have had close to 50% growth in EBITDA for the quarter Y-o-Y, and as you know that we have always strived to de-risk our business, while the defense is starting to show a glimpse of his true potential. The most exciting part is also JSA, we should cross the 1000 crores mark in sales very shortly.

items.statement: Passenger vehicle market grew 6% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by utility vehicle demand and positive consumer sentiment despite high inventory and heat waves.
items.quote: The passenger vehicles market in Q1 FY '25 grew by 6% compared to FY '24 due to high demand for utility vehicles and a positive consumer sentiment despite high inventory levels caused by low footfall at the showrooms due to heat waves and general elections.

items.statement: Heavy commercial vehicle segment grew 3% YoY in Q1 FY25 on a high base with slowdown in infrastructure activities.
items.quote: Heavy commercial vehicles experienced modest growth of 3% on a high base in Q1 FY '24, and a slowdown in infrastruct ure and construction activities due to the transitional period for the newly elected

items.statement: Light commercial vehicle segment declined 3% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to financing challenges and market share loss to 3-wheelers.
items.quote: Light commercial vehicle segment experienced a correction of 3% compared to Q1 FY '24, owing to financing challenges faced by first-time users and expected loss of market in less than 1-ton vehicles to 3-wheelers.

items.statement: Tractor production grew 1% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by above normal monsoon forecast and timely southwest monsoon arrival.
items.quote: Tractor production grew marginally by 1% compared to Q1 FY '24, driven by an above normal monsoon forecast and timely arrival of the southwest monsoon, improving the farmer sentiment.

items.statement: Two-wheeler segment grew 20% YoY in Q1 FY25 exceeding expectations due to rural sentiment revival and strong motorcycle demand.
items.quote: The 2-wheeler segment, started from a slow base, exceeded expectations with 20% growth in Q1 FY '25 driven by the revival of rural consumer sentiment and strong motorcycle demand.

items.statement: Three-wheeler segment grew 11% YoY in Q1 FY25 due to sustained demand for passenger transport and last-mile e-commerce deliveries.
items.quote: The 3-wheeler segment grew by 11% in Q1 FY '25 due to sustained demand for passenger transportation and last mile operators for e-commerce, food deliveries and other applications.

items.statement: Management maintains broad expectation of moderate growth for FY25 similar to FY24 despite election year dynamics and high base effects.
items.quote: Yes. The broad expectation of growth for the year holds. There is a change. We had already sort of indicated Q1 would be sort of a moderate or very weak growth, knowing that there would be an upcoming election, and we would also come into the summer months with not knowing how intense that summer was, but we had expected some slowdown.

items.statement: EBITDA margin improved to 12% in Q1 FY25 from 11.3% in Q1 FY24 due to revenue growth and reduction in other expenses.
items.quote: EBITDA as a percentage of total revenue improved from 11.3% in April-June '23 to 12% in April-June '24. The improvement in margin is mainly attributable to the growth in revenue and reduction in other expenses during the current quarter.

items.statement: Management aims to maintain double-digit EBITDA margin but will not provide future margin guidance due to technology transition uncertainties.
items.quote: We did now the first step coming back to a double digit, which was very important for us, and we do everything to keep this double digit. For the future, we have to see how the market is growing, what is the product mix, and how fast coming technologies in.

items.statement: Capex will be spent for feasible and profitable localization; no fixed range but investments made when they contribute to top and bottom line.
items.quote: Whatever we have to spend to have a feasible and profitable localization, we will spend.

items.statement: NOx sensor line investment includes export volumes to achieve better utilization and return on investment.
items.quote: Here we get a certain exp ort volume as well because we need in the overall production network, there were volumes which we could bring to India. And therefore, we will get a line where we have India plus export volumes, which is also favourable then for

items.statement: Second Lambda sensor production line inaugurated at Bidadi plant in April 2024; targeting over 8 million pieces annually by 2025.
items.quote: By 2025, we are set to achieve over 8 million pieces annually.

items.statement: Power Tools India elevated to independent region covering SAARC countries effective April 1, 2024; exports from Chennai plant to serve region.
items.quote: India now has become 1 of the 5 independent regions within the Bosch Power Tools global organization. India as a region is now responsible for consolidated figures for India, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan and Maldives, or the entire SAARC.

items.statement: Mobility business grew 4.1% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by aftermarket (8.1%) and Power Solutions (2.3%) growth.
items.quote: The Mobility business has grown by 4.1% in April to June '24 as compared to April to June '23, driven mainly due to the Mobility aftermarket business, which grew by 8.1% on account of higher demand for new generation diesel components. Power Solutions business, which grew by 2.3%, mainly due to growth in passenger car segment driven by high demand for utility vehicles.

items.statement: Building Technologies grew 19.4% YoY in Q1 FY25 on higher security system installation orders.
items.quote: The Building Technologies business grew by 19.4% on account of execution of higher number of orders for installation of security systems.

items.statement: Consumer Goods grew 5.1% YoY in Q1 FY25 driven by grinders, drillers, cutters demand.

items.statement: Opening ~30 company-owned stores (20 fast fashion, 10 ethnic wear) by March 2025, starting before Diwali
items.quote: We plan to start with a few stores just before Diwali and then keep opening the stores till the end of March.

items.statement: Q1 demand hit by heat wave and elections; recovery expected from H2 FY25 driven by festive and wedding season
items.quote: Despite experiencing sluggish consumer demand in textile and apparel industry, which was further impacted by the severe heat wave and election-related disruptions in sales channels, we are poised to benefit from the anticipated revival in retail.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 10.3% vs 8.6% YoY; PAT margin 3.6%; new stores may pressure margins
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter is INR34 crores as compared to INR31 crores in quarter 1 financial year 24. An increase of 11% year on year basis and EBITDA margin for the quarter is 10.3%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue mix: fabric 77%, garment 13%, yarn & others 10%
items.quote: During the quarter 1 financial year 25, fabric contributed 77%, garment 13% and yarn and others 10% of Q1 financial year 25 revenue.

items.statement: Price realizations stable; Q1 revenue decline driven by volume drop, not pricing
items.quote: Price realizations are generally quite standard and it is more to do with change in product mix. So, it is largely a volume decrease.

items.statement: New retail stores target mass-value (fast fashion) and mid-price (ethnic wear) segments in tier 1-3 cities
items.quote: Ethnic wear will entail basically menswear in the mid-price segment and the fast fashion will be a family store of men's, women's and kids in the mass value retail format.

items.statement: Organized retail growing as share of industry; Siyaram entering to capture unorganized-to-branded shift
items.quote: We can see that organized retail is increasing as a percentage of overall industry and industry size is also increasing. The industry size is very, very large and we want to participate in this new organized retail format.

items.statement: Exports mainly fabric to Europe; Bangladesh situation may offer long-term garment export opportunity
items.quote: We do have our export, very largely export fabric in Europe and other countries around the world and that is an opportunity that we can look at to sell garments as well.

items.statement: Other income INR24 cr includes INR13 cr capital subsidy (cash basis) and INR11 cr operational interest/rent
items.quote: This is also cash basis. What I said, as soon as we know that assurance is that we are getting that money, then only we recognize

items.statement: Hired separate retail professional teams for fast fashion and ethnic wear ventures
items.quote: We have hired retail professionals, people who understand this industry and this product individually for each segment.

items.statement: New stores expected to generate ~INR100 crore revenue in FY26 (first full year)
items.quote: In the next year, we can estimate a revenue top line of about INR100 crores from these 30 stores.

items.statement: New store economics unproven; management will assess actual vs planned after Diwali openings
items.quote: We have done our initial calculations and we hope to open these stores just before Diwali. So, while we have internal workings, we would like to experience this rather than on paper and on actual and then maybe discuss this further in the coming quarters.

items.statement: MHCV market expected to decline 5-6% in FY25, with Q1-Q2 weak and Q3-Q4 recovery to ~400k vehicles
items.quote: overall, we see the market last year is about 425,000 level. And as of today, this financial year, '24-'25, we are expecting about 5% to 6% down overall for the year.

items.statement: Next MHCV peak expected in 3-4 years driven by higher HP/tonnage vehicles and GDP growth
items.quote: probably the next peak will be around 3, 4 years down the line. The reason is, the trend in the market is to higher HP, higher tonnage vehicles

items.statement: Bus tender pipeline visibility of 1,500-2,500 buses for new product launch
items.quote: current forecast for this segment of Buses, it's about INR1,500 to INR2,500. Again, these are all tender base, so which can change overnight.

items.statement: Board approved ~INR100 crore capex for housing value stream and gear manufacturing upgrades
items.quote: Together, we'll be looking at close to about INR100 crores plus, and we already got an approval from the Board. This is, again, mainly we'll be investing in upgrading our housing value stream and also gear manufacturing.

items.statement: Current capacity utilization at 65-70% average, peaks at 80-85% in certain months
items.quote: We are close to about 65% to 70% level, 65% level is more or less is what I guess. It will fluctuate. At this moment of time, volumes, this is 65% to 70% level.

items.statement: Peak utilization limited to 90-92% due to product mix complexity
items.quote: real time, it's probably - - we can utilize because of the ratios and number of varieties of products and the mix of the products what we have, more or less, the time tested is about -- the utilization will be at 90% to 92% level and so -- in the peak.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 operating margin 29.8%, up 0.5% per SEBI circular; PBT 13.2% vs 13.5% YoY due to volume under-absorption
items.quote: The Q1 '24-'25, we have overall income of INR498 crores with operating margin of 29.8%. And as far as revenue is concerned, compared to the last quarter, we have degrown by 7.4%.

items.statement: Sustainable EBITDA margin target ~13% at full capacity utilization
items.quote: if the capacity happens at 100%, I think we can -- for the whole year, we can go in for about 13%.

items.statement: Commodity price impact minimal (~1% of degrowth); continuous cost reduction via supplier productivity, lightweighting, yield improvement since 2012
items.quote: as far as your commodity prices are concerned, that has a plan, but I don't think it's very significant. So that shows a degrowth on the top line. So it's hardly about 1%.

items.statement: New bus axle (noise-sensitive, EV-ready) launching Q4 FY25; upgraded construction equipment axle for high HP tippers SOP Q3-Q4 FY25; ICV brakes launch next quarter
items.quote: the new axle is getting launched Q4 of this year. And the second segment, the Construction. We already have a product which is upgraded now to meet the high HP requirements of the industry. So specifically the tippers where we see high HPs becoming more popular, we have an upgraded product that is getting into SOP in Q3 and Q4 -- between Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Brakes revenue share ~10-15% of total volume; axles dominant
items.quote: brakes basically being the low-priced products, definitely and also little bit of -- has a very -- compared to axles, it's very low in terms of the share. To be an indicative, brakes may somehow come to about 10% to 15% of the market share -- total volume share, sorry.

items.statement: Ashok Leyland grew 10% YoY in Q1 but AAL grew only 7.5% due to lower bus share; new bus axle targets 20-30% share in 6-12 months
items.quote: our aspirational target is to reach at least 20% to 30% over a period of 6 to 12 months.

items.statement: Brakes market share grew from 30-35% to ~40%; targeting 45-50% long-term via new ICV brakes and product launches
items.quote: our brakes share of business was somewhere around 30% to 35%. And as he mentioned, we have grown it up close to about 40%. And we have a plan to grow it up to 50%.

items.statement: Drum brake market has 2 players; AAL holds 40-45% share depending on model
items.quote: Coming to brakes, our predominant focus and the market also is in the drum brake segment. And there are only 2 players. Other than us, there is the competition. So we have 40, 60 or 45, 55 share of market share depending on specific models that we sell in the market.

items.statement: Exports ~double digits of revenue; 40% North America, 30% Europe, 10% Australia, rest South America/China; all via Meritor group
items.quote: Exports overall business, it's more close to the double digits. And we are working on the long-term strategy, how to improve on it.

items.statement: No non-Meritor export customers currently; focus on increasing content with existing Meritor sites
items.quote: At present, no. It's -- right now, we operate through the other Meritor locations. And at present, we don't see that changing other than what we have achieved.

items.statement: Other income increased due to surplus cash deployment; sustainability depends on capex funding decision
items.quote: If you see the balance sheet, probably, the March also, we have substantial cash in hand, okay? We are trying to maximize the return on the surplus cash, and that's how you see the increase year-on-year.

items.statement: Cummins-Meritor collaboration evaluating complementary powertrain applications with 1-2 OEMs; long-term journey
items.quote: we are evaluating and working with 1 or 2 OEMs on that. But like Ranga said, it's a long stretched process. It is a combination of both the worlds that we are trying to bring together.

items.statement: MHCV industry volume FY24: ~425,000 units; FY25 target: ~400,000 units
items.quote: we expect it to do well with Q3 and Q4 to reach to the 400,000 vehicle level.

items.statement: Off-highway addressable market only 40% (wheeled applications); tracked applications growing, EV transition possible; backhoe segment vertically integrated to OEM
items.quote: In that high-peak market, our addressable market is only about 40%. When I say 40%, that's mainly because we are in the wheeled applications. And in India, off-highway is more moving towards the tracked application where we do not have a presence even in the global market.

items.statement: 5-year strategy under Board review; will communicate soon
items.quote: We are currently working with the Board for the strategy, and we will come back to you on this soon.

items.statement: Management expects to achieve full capacity utilization within three years instead of four, but it is too early to give formal guidance.
items.quote: I think it's a little too early to give a guidance for that. But I think like we are seeing the engagement with customers, the inquiries, etc., we do feel that we will be able to achieve this within three years instead of four years.

items.statement: No capex planned for the current year; board has not approved any. Future expansion will be brownfield taking 6-12 months.
items.quote: We don’t expect, sir, any CAPEXs in the current year. So, the board has not approved anything. We don’t need any CAPEXs right now currently. And anyways, everything will be Brownfield expansion which will probably take six months to on e year

items.statement: Rieco has a healthy order book with comfortable contribution; revenue in Q1 was in line with projections.
items.quote: Rieco is having the healthy order book and also the contribution from the order book seems to be comfortable. In the current quarter, the revenue has been more in l ine whatever has been projected for the

items.statement: Pigment gross margin of 47.2% expected to remain in similar range, subject to raw material variability; EBITDA margin should improve with operating leverage as volumes ramp up.
items.quote: I expect this gross margin to remain in this range, subject to the raw material variability what we have already seen in the past. So, currently the raw material prices are more or less stable. And given the current market scenario, I expect this should range in the similar range.

items.statement: Directionally EBITDA margins should move closer to 17-19% range as volumes ramp up and operating leverage kicks in.
items.quote: Absolutely,. Directionally you are on the right are a. I would say, whether the gross margin would be in this area or slightly ahead, but the ma in advantage would be through operational leverage. So, as we ramp up our volumes , we should be able to improve our EBITDA margins

items.statement: Q1 saw normal demand increase; overseas demand improving with increased customer enquiries and product approvals after competitor insolvency.
items.quote: We have seen in Q1 is a normal demand increase. And normally Q4 is a seasonality effect and a strong quarter. We see demand improvement in the overseas geographies.
