items.statement: EBITDA margin to stabilize to previous levels by Q3-Q4 FY25 and grow further
items.quote: We expect the EBITDA margin will stabilize back to the previous level by Q3-Q4 of this year, which we expect it to grow further.

items.statement: Debt to EBITDA expected to be close to 3x by end of FY25
items.quote: We expect that the debt to EBITDA will be close to three by the end of this financial year.

items.statement: FY25 revenue target of INR 900+ crores with 19-20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: We are quite confident that we should be able to achieve what we have projected since potential of about INR900 crores plus in FY '25.

items.statement: FY26 revenue target of INR 1,200-1,300 crores with 90%+ capacity utilization
items.quote: We are expecting a revenue between INR1,200 crores to INR1,300 crores in FY'26 because of the selling price.

items.statement: Repair capex of INR 5-10 crores for FY25; no further expansion capex planned until 70%+ utilization achieved
items.quote: Well, generally company spend on a repair capex is about INR5 crores to INR10 crores not more than that for this year. And for the further capex we have not planned anything yet.

items.statement: Volume growth of ~27% YoY in Q1; export volumes grew despite shipping issues; export share 61% of revenue
items.quote: We achieved a notable volume growth of approximately 27% year-on-year. Despite current shipping issues, we have grown our export volumes. Export contributed 61% of our revenue.

items.statement: Trials ongoing with existing and new customers in export and domestic markets; long-term supply agreements expected post-trials
items.quote: We are working with a number of customers in an export and also into the domestic field. Couple of them are new customers who we have identified in the past who could be on our roll call and a couple of them are already existing but we can expand the line with them with the new capacity available.

items.statement: Current debt level sufficient for working capital needs; positive cash flow expected in FY25 as selling and raw material prices drop
items.quote: I think we will be able to manage with the current debt level. We don't expect too much requirement. Purely because of the sales, the selling prices drop and also the buying raw material prices drop. So the overall projection is not something which can be managed with the current thing. And also we will have some positive cash flow generated during this year.

items.statement: Competition from Europe, North America, China; benefit from Make in India and alternate supply chain preference
items.quote: Well, there is some competition come from Europe there is a competition from North America and also there is a competition from China itself. So, competition is always there. We are not in the monopoly zone anymore in today's world. But we are in a unique place with the government support make in India people preference of an alternate supply chain, which is helping us

items.statement: Geopolitical uncertainty may affect container availability and export stabilization timeline
items.quote: But we can't say due to the geopolitical situation what is going on currently. 100% nobody can say what is going to happen.

items.statement: Focus on industrial segment; expanding in South America, Middle East beyond Europe and USA
items.quote: Well, currently our focus is purely on to the industrial segment of the range and that is where we want to grow. Not only in Europe, USA we are also trying to establish ourselves in like South America, the Middle East and many other regions we are trying to capture.

items.statement: USP is specialty/performance chemicals not commodity; enables 400bps margin premium over largest competitor
items.quote: Well, we are not into the commodity, number 1. We are more into the performance and the so-called specialty chemistry within the rubber the space or also into the lubricant space. And a lot of our specialty chemicals are really specialized in that nature. And that is helping us to hold up the margin and allow us to grow.

items.statement: New customers prefer Yasho for better pricing, alternate supply chain needs, and proven delivery reliability since 2020
items.quote: Well, there are multiple reasons, but definitely one of the reasons could be the better pricing by Yasho offering to them. Number two, as I said earlier, that the people are looking for an alternate supply chain. So that's one of the major reasons also. And I think the last couple of years, since from pandemic 2020, we have proven ourselves that we can deliver the material despite of all the chall

items.statement: India auto segments grew YoY in Q1 FY25 except commercial vehicles; 2-wheelers up 19.6%, 3-wheelers 9.4%, PVs 5.8%, CVs down 1.4%.
items.quote: In Q1 FY'25, strong domestic macro factors resulted in most of the automobile segment growing on a year-on-year basis other than the commercial vehicle segment. The 2-wheeler segment grew by 19.6%, 3 -wheelers grew by 9.4%, passenger vehicles grew by 5.8%, but the commercial vehicles degrew by 1.4%.

items.statement: Overseas 2-wheeler markets (US, Europe) showed negative growth; Asian growth driven by low-end segments, premium struggling.
items.quote: The overseas market especially the U.S. and the European market also showed negative growth for 2 -wheelers. In the Asian region, the growth was largely driven by low -end segments and the premium segment continues to struggle for growth in this region.

items.statement: Overseas business H1 FY25 tough, gradual recovery expected over next 1-2 years.
items.quote: We explained it in the previous calls also that H1 is going to be tough for us for the overseas business. But thereafter, we should see a gradual recovery over the next 1 to 2 years.

items.statement: Consolidated PBT 2.9% in Q1 FY25 vs 3.6% YoY; EBITDA 9.1%; India gross margins improved ~1% YoY excluding Q4 government incentive.
items.quote: Coming to the profitability, we reported 2.9% PBT in Q1 compared to 3.6% last year. And EBITDA was at 9.1%.

items.statement: India margins to improve from current levels in outer quarters; overseas margins to stay flat; overall margin improvement expected.
items.quote: I mean, I don't want to put a number to it, obviously, but margins should certainly improve from the current level in the outer quarters as far as the India business is concerned. Overseas should more or less stay at this level. So on the whole, we should see improvement from the current levels.

items.statement: Renewable energy Phase 1 (36.6 MW solar) from Q2 FY25 to yield INR 200M annual recurring savings (~0.3% margin); Phase 2 (14 MW) approved for FY25 adding INR 70-80M annual savings.
items.quote: The first phase of this initiative is expected to result in 36.6 megawatts of power of sourcing from solar power starting from quarter 2 of this year and is expecte d to give us an annual recurring saving of around INR 200 million.

items.statement: Two new plants commissioned in Maharashtra (plastic moulding, fuel tanks for Bajaj Auto); start-up costs significant in Q1, losses to reduce significantly in Q2, margins from Q3.
items.quote: It's a significant number. And these are two plants which we have started in our plastic moulding business and also we're doing some fuel tanks in Bajaj Auto. So these are the plants we've set up for Bajaj Auto within -- in Bajaj Auto. And this is where I think these are the start -up costs. But going forward, we see that these losses in Q2 will be sig nificantly reduced. And then we start making

items.statement: Lifetime new business wins INR 7,959M in Q1 FY25; cumulative order wins expected to yield annual peak revenue ~INR 1,416M; 48% from EV players, 71% 4-wheeler, 85% non-Bajaj.
items.quote: In quarter 1 of FY'25, our lifetime new business wins was over INR7,959 million, the cumulative order wins are expected to result in an annual peak revenue levels of around INR1,416 million, nearly 48% of our business wins in this quarter has com e from the EV players revenue from supplying to EV players in quarter 1 FY '25 was approximately 8% of our overall revenues.

items.statement: EV revenue ~8% of total in Q1 FY25 (7.8% per CFO); 2-3 wheelers 78% of revenue; Bajaj Auto 44.6% of revenue.
items.quote: revenue from supplying to EV players in quarter 1 FY '25 was approximately 8% of our overall revenues.

items.statement: Two EV powertrain customers beyond Bajaj (one local, one foreign); SOPs expected within FY25; wins across lighting, painted polymers, full-service polymer parts for passenger cars.
items.quote: have 2 EV powertrain customers beyond Bajaj for whom development is ongoing. One is local, 1 is foreign. So those SOPs also, we would expect within this financial year

items.statement: Net debt reduced by INR 668M in Q1 FY25 to ~INR 9,160M; net debt/equity 0.59; net debt/EBITDA ~1.3x; RoCE ~16.3%.
items.quote: This resulted in a n et debt reducing by further INR 668 million in quarter 1 of FY '25 and our net debt to equity has improved to 0.59.

items.statement: Debt reduction trend ~INR 50-60 crore per quarter; to continue from free cash flow, barring potential land purchases for growth.
items.quote: So on the average, anywhere between INR50 crores to INR60 crores reduction per quarter has been the trend. So we should be able to continue this. Except that in between, we may have to invest some amount in terms of buying some additional land for our future growth.

items.statement: Interest cost ~INR 44 crore in Q1; reduction of ~INR 3 crore vs Q4 after adjusting for lease reclassification; further reduction expected as debt declines and one-time items cease.
items.quote: If you see Q4 number, Q4 interest cost. It also had a benefit of reclassification of leasing interest between interest line item and the other rental expense. So that way, if you really see in terms of the actual interest cost, there was a reduction of about INR3 crores. already between Q4 and Q1.

items.statement: EV 2-wheeler volumes grew 6.4% sequentially in Q1 FY25; new plant ramp-ups and EV volume growth expected to drive operating leverage in H2.
items.quote: In the current quarter, on a sequential basis, EV 2-wheeler actually registered a growth of close to 6%, 6.4%.

items.statement: Commodity price adjustments impacted revenue in Q1; described as normal transitory adjustments that should correct in outer quarters.
items.quote: These are some of the normal adjustments or price changes which keep happening in this industry, as you know. So this is again a transitory phase. So it should get corrected in the outer quarters.

items.statement: Increasing sourcing from renewable energy; Phase 1 (36.6 MW solar) from Q2 FY25, Phase 2 (14 MW) approved for FY25.
items.quote: We also mentioned earlier that we are increasing sourcing from renewable sources. The first phase of this initiative is expected to result in 36.6 megawatts of power of sourcing from solar power starting from quarter 2 of this year.

items.statement: Credit rating upgraded 1 notch to AA- (long-term); short-term rating A1+; net debt/equity 0.59, net debt/EBITDA ~1.3x, RoCE ~16.3%.
items.quote: This improvement has resulted in an upgrade to the credit rating of the company by 1 notch to AA minus for long term, and our short -term rating is at a top notch, which is A1 plus.

items.statement: Global economic uncertainty (geopolitical issues, US recession fears) persists; overseas volume recovery may take 1-2 years.
items.quote: The global economy continues to remain uncertain due to geopolitical issues in Europe and Asia and recession fears in the U.S.

items.statement: Overseas 4-wheeler degrowth driven by IMES (non-auto) and Romania electronics plant due to Europe situation; domestic 4-wheeler flat YoY.
items.quote: So the significant decline happened actually in 2 of our plants abroad, 1 is EMIS and the other was in our Romania Electronics plant, where we saw a substantial decline in the volumes because of the situation in Europe.

items.statement: Management says 20% topline growth is a sensible way to model the company for the next few years.
items.quote: I think that 20% topline growth is a sensible way to model our company at this moment, and we will continue to improve our margins, thus hopefully deliver higher growth on the bottomline.

items.statement: EBITDA margin was 20.1% in Q1 FY2025, up from prior periods.
items.quote: We achieved an EBITDA margin of 20.1%, delivering a strong operating margin expansion.

items.statement: Management targets gradual increase in operating profit margins for the rest of FY2025.
items.quote: As we look ahead to the rest of FY2025, we are poised to further accelerate our growth trajectory with gradual increase in operating profit margins and will continue to deliver greater value to all our shareholders.

items.statement: India and Emerging Markets revenue grew 24.8% y-o-y, contributing 73.2% of quarterly revenue.
items.quote: Our growth for India and Emerging markets combined, was about 24.8% y-o-y.

items.statement: Developed Markets revenue grew 36.9% y-o-y, contributing 26.8% of quarterly revenue.
items.quote: Our growth in Developed Markets was about 36.9% y-o-y and it contributed 26.8% to our quarterly revenues.

items.statement: CPCU conversions reached 90.8 million at a rate of Rs. 57.0, driving CPCU revenue of Rs. 5,177 million, up 37% y-o-y.
items.quote: Our CPCU business delivered about 90.8 million conversions during the quarter, at a CPCU rate of Rs. 57.0 that helped us achieve CPCU revenue of Rs. 5,177 million, an increase of 37.0% y-o-y.

items.statement: Gaming vertical led significant growth in both emerging and developed markets.
items.quote: We are seeing a n overall broad-based growth. But I would say that the growth in the gaming vertical, both in emerging markets and developed markets has been quite significant.

items.statement: Management expects CPCU rates to improve over the long term through premium inventory investments and deeper ecosystem partnerships.
items.quote: You will see a better CPCU premium pricing, and we would be able to work better in the market to attract the top dollars. Hopefully, helping us to achieve the higher margin that we intend to deliver because margin expansion is an important execution focus for us for the next few years.

items.statement: Inventory and Data Cost stood at 61.6% of revenue; management is comfortable defending this range.
items.quote: Our Inventory and Data Cost stood at 61.6% of revenue from operations in this quarter, while we continue our platform calibrations on to premium inventories, touchpoints and deeper ecosystem-level partnerships.

items.statement: Employee expenses expected to remain flattish despite revenue growth due to integration efficiencies and GenAI adoption.
items.quote: So as business expands, I would expect to keep our employee expenses largely flattish, at least for the foreseeable future. You will see much higher growth in revenues and a flattish to low growth in the employee expenses.

items.statement: No material changes in collection risk; working capital management remains efficient.
items.quote: We continue to prioritize efficient working capital management and as such there were no material changes in the collection risk.

items.statement: Google has decided not to deprecate third-party cookies and delayed Privacy Sandbox; Affle is prepared and sees status quo for several years.
items.quote: Google has clearly indicated even after 4+ years since it announced that it will deprecate cookies, it couldn’t overcome the complexities and challenges associated with its own privacy initiatives. Co nsequently Google’s privacy sandbox project is also delayed

items.statement: Not in a rush for M&A; will pursue if right target adds disproportionate value; open to developed or emerging markets.
items.quote: We are not in a rush. We have just completed YouAppi's integration. YouAppi is 1 year and full integration has been done in less than a year. So if we find the right acquisition target, we certainly would but we are not in a rush.

items.statement: Investing in premium inventory (CTV, iOS, premium Android) and deeper ecosystem partnerships to drive higher CPCU rates and margins.
items.quote: we are also investing into premium inventories . I see that effect being utilized from a margin perspective, right . Overall, the way Affle is strategizing itself is that we are going more and more premium in a way we are working with different strategic platforms, be it the app stores or the alternate of app stores

items.statement: Real Money Gaming impact in India is neutralized and considered over; new normal established.
items.quote: We are going more broad-based. Even in India, realigning the definition of gaming for us. I mean, looking at it in a much broader way than just RMG. We are neutralizing that impact. Yes, I would say for now that impact is over and this is our new normal, and we will continue to grow sensibly from here.

items.statement: Direct business remains 70-75% of mix; agency share fluctuates quarter to quarter but end advertiser focus remains.
items.quote: Now direct versus agency, it's within that range, 70% to 75% direct business. It is all in that range. So please don't read into 1 quarter or the other.

items.statement: Affle competes on value and lifetime value of users, not on pricing; competitive forces not pulling margins down.
items.quote: I would not say that because of competition, beca use we are not fighting the competition on pricing. We are fighting the m on value. What do I mean by value? So when we work with the advertiser, let's say somebody delivers a conversion for the same advertiser of a user A and another person delivers the conversion of user B. Now if user A has a higher lifetime value, the advertiser would be willin

items.statement: Global integration completed; operating as one cash-generating unit with 20 CXOs and VPs providing direct oversight.
items.quote: We have successfully consolidated all our business and platform operations with hands -on leadership providing direct oversight, thus creating a cohesively managed global business.

items.statement: Base business revenue growth guided at mid-teens for full year FY25
items.quote: The mid-teens, that's what we guided.

items.statement: Base business EBITDA margin guided at 32-33% for full year FY25
items.quote: So, EBITDA around 32%, 33%.

items.statement: Cenexi positive EBITDA expected in Q4 FY25 and next fiscal year with revenue exceeding €200 million
items.quote: a positive EBITDA for Q4 of this Fiscal Year and a positive EBITDA for the next fiscal year driven by increased revenue exceeding the €200 million threshold.

items.statement: US market demand remains strong with 30% volume growth year-on-year
items.quote: If you compared to the last year, the volume wise it's gone up by almost 30%.

items.statement: Consolidated gross margin 60% in Q1 FY25 vs 63% in Q1 FY24 due to product mix
items.quote: Our gross margin for Q1 FY25 was 60%, compared to 63% in Q1 FY24, impacted by the product mix at the base business for us.

items.statement: Base business EBITDA margin stable at 29% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our base business (excluding Cenexi) EBITDA margin remained stable at 29% in Q1 FY25

items.statement: Cenexi gross margin improved to historical level of 78% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: However, Cenexi's gross margin improved to its historical level of 78%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 19% in Q1 FY25 down from 25% in Q1 FY24 due to Cenexi consolidation
items.quote: Our EBITDA margin for Q1 FY25 stood at 19%, down from 25% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Filed 8 ANDAs and received 7 approvals in Q1 FY25; 356 total filed, 295 approved, 61 pending in US
items.quote: We filed 8 ANDAs during the quarter and received approval for 7 ANDAs. As of June 30th, 2024, Gland and its partners have filed 356 ANDAs in the United States, with 295 approved and 61 pending approvals.

items.statement: Invested INR 637 million in capex in Q1 FY25 largely for Cenexi upgrade and maintenance
items.quote: We invested INR 637 million in capital expenditure during the current fiscal year, largely allocated towards upgrading and maintenance capex of Cenexi business.

items.statement: New ampoule line at Fontenay site to be commissioned in August 2024 with commercial production early 2025, expected €10 million revenue in 2025
items.quote: This line will be commissioned during the summer shutdown period of August, with commercial production slated to begin in early 2025. We antic ipate this new line will significantly increase capacity, improve customer service, and generate approximately €10 million in revenue in 2025

items.statement: New aseptic gel line at Hérouville site to begin commercial production for key customer before end of year
items.quote: our new aseptic gel line will begin co mmercial production for a key customer before the end of the year

items.statement: Heparin volumes doubled due to new GPO contract diluting margins; contribution margin 25-30%
items.quote: The contribution margin on heparin is lower compared to that. So, the margin is, I think, around 25%, 30%. So, the volumes that were supplied for last quarter have almost doubled.

items.statement: Biologics CDMO attracting advanced-stage interest from multiple players for monoclonal antibodies and plasma proteins; discussions with leading biologics company for strategic collaboration on 4 biosimilars
items.quote: Our biologics facility in Genome Valley is attracting advanced-stage interest from multiple players for contract manufacturing of mono clonal antibodies and novel plasma-based proteins. In addition, we are in discussions with the leading biologics company for a potential strategic collaboration. This collaboration could involve large-scale contract manufacturing of 4 biosimilars with a possible in

items.statement: US FDA surprise inspections at Hyderabad sites resulted in 2 and 3 Form 483 observations; procedural and do not affect compliance status
items.quote: During the quarter, the U.S. FDA made two surprise inspections of our manufacturing sites in Hyderabad. The inspections concluded with 2 and 3 Form 483 observations at Dundigal and Pashamylaram, respectively. As previously communicated, these observations are procedural and do not affect our compliance status.

items.statement: Cash conversion cycle improved to 148 days in Q1 FY25 from 233 days due to inventory reduction
items.quote: The average cash conversion cycle improved, reaching 148 days for Q1 FY25, compared to 233 days in the previous period of the fiscal year due to the reduction of inventory.

items.statement: Group cash and equivalents INR 30,488 million; net cash position INR 27,430 million including Cenexi loans
items.quote: As of June 30, 2024, our total cash and equivalents on a group level stood at INR 30,488 million, and including the outstanding loans on Cenexi's books, our net cash position was lower at INR 27,430 million.

items.statement: R&D expenditure INR 489 million representing 5% of base business revenue in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Total R&D expenses for Q1 FY25 amounted to INR 489 million, an increase from INR 457 million in the same period of the previous fiscal year. This represents 5 % of our revenue from operations, excluding Cenexi.

items.statement: Cenexi Q2 FY25 revenue expected to be two-thirds of Q1 level due to 3-week extended shutdown for new line installation
items.quote: Yes, correct. So, that's correct. But at the same time, we are also using that time to install a new line, So which will help us actually to produce more volumes in the future.

items.statement: Biologics CDMO collaboration requires new investment in large batch manufacturing capacity
items.quote: While we can take on the CDMO and the smaller scale batches, this also requires investment to increase the capacities that we have. And since it is backed up by CDMO contracts and also the commercial volumes, that evaluation is happening.

items.statement: Domestic India business not intended to scale unless dedicated facility solution found; 19% revenue decline by design
items.quote: We don't intend to scale that up unless we have found the solution to have a facility which is more dedicated to the India business.

items.statement: Acquisition focus on complex injectables with high R&D and difficult-to-make manufacturing capabilities
items.quote: One is to look at opportunities on the complex injectable side, which has more to do with high R&D-focused investments. The second part, which we are very keenly evaluating, is building capabilities on the manufacturing side.

items.statement: US front-end hybrid model evaluation still on table but too early to comment; CDMO focus key for investment
items.quote: Yes, it is. It's on the table. We are evaluating, but we can't comment. I think it's too early. But it's not like our core focus will be CDMO, and we are also getting into more complex CDMO with a focus on the company, with more and more companies approaching us on the b io side

items.statement: Reported industry-leading growth for fifth consecutive quarter despite subdued market conditions; Kerala market showed negative growth for all players, dragging overall growth down.
items.quote: We have once again reported industry leading growth rate for the fifth consecutive quarter despite subdued market conditions.

items.statement: Expect sharp uptick in both top line and bottom-line growth from Q2 onwards.
items.quote: We sincerely hope that we shall exhibit a sharp uptick in both our top line and bottom-line growth from Q2 onwards.

items.statement: Standalone gross margin reduced from 47.6% to 47.0% due to price cuts, elevated channel discounts, and temporary spike in raw material prices.
items.quote: However, due to price cuts, slightly elevated channel discounts and a temporary spike in certain raw material prices, the gross margin reduced slightly from 47.6% in Q1 of FY24 to 47.0% in Q1 of FY25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin reduced from 17.2% to 15.6% largely due to sharp increase in employee cost of around 23% to 24% Y-on-Y.
items.quote: The EBITDA margin reduced from 17.2% in this quarter last year to 15.6% in Q1 of FY25 largely due to a sharp increase in employee cost of around 23% to 24% on a Y-on-Y basis.

items.statement: Employee cost increased 23-24% Y-on-Y due to 35-40% sales force expansion in Q2 FY24; no significant increase expected from Q2 FY25 onwards.
items.quote: Last year, we had drastically expanded our sales force size in Q2 of FY24 to increase the number of feet on the ground in more states. Hence, the employee costs in the quarter just gone by is significantly higher than the corresponding figure for Q1 of FY24.

items.statement: Work progressing well on state-of-the-art water-based paint plant and solvent-based plant at Jodhpur; expect new capacities to meet CAPEX requirements for next four years.
items.quote: On the CAPEX front, work is progressing well, on the state of the art water based paint plant being set up at Jodhpur and the solvent based plant also being set up at the same location.

items.statement: Tamil Nadu plant commissioned September 2023; Jodhpur brownfield expansion underway; capacity utilizations expected to inch up year-on-year over next four years.
items.quote: We expect, once the new capacities at Jodhpur come on board, we expect that this would more or less meet our CAPEX requirements for the next four years or so, during which time naturally, the capacity utilizations would inch up year-on-year at each plant.

items.statement: Active dealer count reached ~18,500; tinting machine population crossed 10,000 milestone to 10,210 as of June 30, 2024.
items.quote: As on 30th, June 2024, our count of active dealers was about 18,500 and the tinting machine population crossed the milestone of 10,000 numbers and closed at 10,210.

items.statement: Waterproofing segment contributing 5-6% of standalone top line; expect contribution to increase to 8-10% over next year to year and a half.
items.quote: Aside from the waterproofing and construction chemicals being marketed by our subsidiary Apple Chemie, we have also been selling similar waterproofing products in the retail space at Indigo Paints for the last year or so, and this segment is already contributing about 5% to 6% of our standalone top line.

items.statement: Primer and distemper segment witnessed over 29% value growth and 24% volume growth; putty segment saw healthy 8% value and volume growth.
items.quote: For the quarter Q1 FY25, the Company witnessed over 29% value growth and 24% volume growth in the primer and distemper segment, and the healthy 8% value and volume growth in the putty segment.

items.statement: Industry took price hikes of about 2% overall during July and August, which augurs well for gross margin improvement in future quarters.
items.quote: With the industry have taken much needed price hikes of about 2% overall during July and August. It augurs well for an improvement in gross margins in future quarters.

items.statement: Freight cost as percentage of top line declined compared to corresponding quarter last year.
items.quote: Our freight cost as a percentage of top line has shown a decline compared to the corresponding quarter of last year.

items.statement: Advertising and promotion spends as percentage of revenue decreased from 7.6% to 7.2%; overall A&P spend increase will be less than expected top line growth, so A&P percentage expected to continue declining marginally.
items.quote: The advertising and promotion spends as a percentage of revenue decreased from 7.6% in Q1 of last year to 7.2% in the quarter just gone by.

items.statement: No change in competitive landscape seen so far; no pricing pressure from new entrants; major competition remains from existing four larger players.
items.quote: We have not so far seen any change in the competitive landscape as far as our Company is concerned, and therefore there has been no pricing pressure as a result of any new incumbent entering the field.

items.statement: Tinting machine deployment typically increases dealer sales 3x-4x; wholesale dealer base now exceeds 700 with throughput of Rs.4-5 lakhs per wholesaler.
items.quote: And when the tinting machine is deployed at the counter typically the average sales just shoots up by 3x, 4x of the existing sale of that particular dealer.

items.statement: Tinting machine additions running at 1,300-1,500 per year; charge nominal amount on right-to-use basis to ensure effective utilization.
items.quote: The tinting machine addition speed is roughly to the tune of 1300 to 1500 per year. And we don't believe in giving free tinting machines to anyone, because we don't think that it generates much value or perceived value in the minds of the dealer.

items.statement: July witnessed high sales growth not seen in last 7-8 months; uncertain if growth will sustain into August and September.
items.quote: Finally, we have witnessed high sales growth in the month of July, of a kind which we have not witnessed in any single month during the last seven or eight months.

items.statement: Kerala market prolonged slowdown; July showed positive growth but sustainability uncertain due to landslides and heavy rainfall.
items.quote: But yes, July has come back into positive growth for us, as far as Kerala is concerned, but it has witnessed a prolonged slowdown, and therefore whether it sustains going forward is anyone's guess.

items.statement: Subsidiary Apple Chemie registered robust 47% growth in Q1 FY25; received NABL accreditation for laboratory; invested in sales force expansion and marketing to additional states.
items.quote: Our subsidiary Apple Chemie has registered a robust growth of about 47% in Q1 of FY25 on a Y-on-Y basis. We are pleased to announce that Apple Chemie is the first and the only construction chemical Company in India to have recently received NABL accreditation for its laboratory.

items.statement: Extended EV last-mile delivery to three more states; targeting 1 MW renewable energy via rooftop solar this fiscal; extended painter health insurance to Odisha and Chhattisgarh.
items.quote: We have extended the electrical vehicle last mile delivery service in three more states in India. We are also targeting installation of one megawatt of renewable energy via rooftop solar installations in this fiscal.

items.statement: Order book grew 12% YoY to Rs 1,246 crore
items.quote: Our order book has grown to rupees 1246 crore, 12% higher than Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Expect standalone revenue growth of 20-25% YoY in FY25
items.quote: Yeah. So, we are expecting growth of almost more than 20 % to 25% year on year even on standalone basis.

items.statement: Planned capex of Rs 150 crore for FY25, Rs 100 crore already in process for 3 new rigs
items.quote: So current year we have planned around 150 crores for CAPEX of which currently we are already in process of doing CAPEX of around 100 cr. We are buying 3 new rigs.

items.statement: Rigs 100% occupied, gas processing equipment over 85% occupied; 3 new rigs to be commercialized in 4-6 months
items.quote: Yes, our rigs are 100% occupied. Our gas processing equipment's are more than 85% occupied.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 45% in Q1 FY25; maintained 42-45% range historically
items.quote: Tight control over costing and operational efficiencies have helped us post 26.40% growth in EBITDA to Rs. 61.50 crore in Q1 FY25 with EBITDA margin of 45%.

items.statement: Margin expansion driven by better capacity utilization reducing costs
items.quote: Look, as we mentioned earlier also that as we scale up our capacities and use more of the capacity from the existing infrastructure, that will help us in bringing down our cost and that's what is helping us.

items.statement: Raw material prices range-bound (±3-5%) for last three quarters, stable outlook for next quarter
items.quote: The raw material prices for last three quarters more or less have been range bound with plus minus 3% to 5% changes. The forecast for the next quarter also seems to be stable. We don't see much of upside in raw material prices, at least for next one quarter.

items.quote: Lately, what has happened in last two quarters, we have seen that our export revenues have also grown and we are seeing good demand coming from West part of India also. So we are also now evaluating to add whether capacity in West part of Western part -- Western zone of India or to go first at Odisha.

items.statement: Added 25 significant new international and domestic customers in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We have added 25 significant new international and domestic customers in quarter one FY '25.

items.statement: Packaging products sales up 16.29% to INR61.35 crore; sheet sales down 11.62% to INR14.7 crore

items.statement: Barrier packaging revenue grew to INR6.75 crore from INR2.75 crore YoY
items.quote: We did around INR6.75 crores of revenue versus INR2.75 crore in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Developed and introduced over 7 new products in food packaging during Q1 FY25
items.quote: I am pleased to share that we developed and introduced over seven new products during the quarter, expanding our product base across food packaging.

items.statement: Export business at INR9.2 crore (11.5% of turnover) in Q1 FY25; participating in international shows
items.quote: In the terms of geographical sales, our export business stood at INR9.2 crores, accounting for around 11.5% of overall turnover for Q1 FY '25. We expect exports to grow further as we expand.

items.statement: Debtor days increased from 35 to 40 days; inventory days reduced from 158 to 126 days in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Yes, like outstanding, I think, so has increased from average 35 days to 40 days. Inventory has reduced from 158 days to 126 days. So yes, and our debtors have increased from 29 to 40 days. So that's done.

items.statement: Biodegradable products have CPCB approval but no commercial activity due to high raw material prices and low demand
items.quote: have approval on biodegradable products from CPCB, but at the moment, I would say there is not much demand coming for this particular product from the market due to the Rajshree Polypack Limited August 06, 2024 6 high prices of raw material. So the demand is less, so there is no point in going for commercial activity at this

items.statement: Tube laminates project on hold; will require dedicated line when revisited
items.quote: Yes, that's on hold at the moment. So as and whe n we will revise that particular segment, we will have a dedicated line for that particular segment. So that's how we will proceed with that particular segment as and when we proceed in the future

items.statement: Olive Ecopack commenced commercial production of 50+ SKUs out of 100; full range launch expected in Q2 FY25
items.quote: In case of Olive Ecopack, we have already commenced commercial production of more than 50 SKUs out of 100 SKUs and we are in the process of commencing production of remaining SKUs. We expect to launch the entire range of products during the quarter and start building the sales aggressively.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of INR 10.66 per share
items.quote: Board, which met yesterday, they unanimously approved the interim dividend of INR10.66 per share.

items.statement: Order backlog composition: 40-45% long-cycle projects, 55-60% short-cycle orders executed in 6-9 months

items.statement: Orders and revenues grew 13% YoY; export orders grew 39%
items.quote: We recorded a strong performance with orders and revenues growing by 13%. And we see a strong momentum with large orders from emerging sectors.

items.statement: Export orders grew 39% driven by specialty chemical service orders from an energy major
items.quote: Our export orders also grew by 39%, largely contribution from specialty chemical service orders from an energy major.

items.quote: Operational EBITDA was up 64% for the quarter. And Board, which met yesterday, they unanimously approved the interim dividend of INR10.66 per share.

items.quote: The major contributor, if you look at it from the structure of the P&L, you could see the largest gain has been due to reduction in the material cost, where we have moved 6% of almost 61%, 62%, 63% levels to 57%, 57.5% right

items.quote: The drivers for that was definitely better margin orders, we did have positive price movements across and we did benefit from steady material cost -- material commodity cost at this point of time.

items.quote: And order backlog and all time I have INR3,930 crores. I think we should be aware that this order backlog has a major orders of traction converters from railway segment and that service, long-term service order as well.

items.statement: Cash conversion maintained at 100%; cash balance INR 4,872 crores after May dividend payment
items.quote: And coming to the cash balance, we have INR4,872 crores, and this is after paying the dividend which we paid in the month of May.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free with strong cash position
items.quote: We continue to be a debt-free company with good cash on our balance sheet.

items.statement: Scope 1&2 GHG emissions ahead of plan; water positive locations; zero waste to landfill target for 2 of 5 locations by 2024
items.quote: in Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions, we are ahead of plan. Water recyclability is our focus. We have already converted a number of locations into water positive. And by 2024, we will have two locations out of 5, which will

items.quote: Post COVID, the mindset of the customers have changed and they look for more reliable products rather than cheaper products. So that's where, again, it is sweet spot for us.

items.quote: As far as India story is concerned is, as we say, it's an India story. It's an India story is about emerging market story, which should be seen in its own merit and its own isolated effect.

items.quote: We have actually tabulated renewable energy generation, green energy corridor, EV and charging infrastructure, and green hydrogen and certain data, that's how we read in the marketplace.

items.quote: But I think now that the prices are stabilizing at this point of time as what we see, that particular difference between the order booking to the execution time advantages will start to thin down going forward.

items.quote: Now given that we have our colleague, Morten Wierod who has taken over a CEO from 1st of August, and he was, by the way, also Chairman of ABB in India. He frequents India very well. He knows India very well.

items.quote: Our endeavour is, and I have stated this, is that we get it to basically mid to high single digits and we should see the efficiencies flow at a significant level.

items.quote: we should be looking at analysed about 120 to 140 stores. And as I gave an example, about 75 or 80% of them will be in the COCO, FOFO format.

items.quote: contributions which are upwards of almost 4.5% to retail business and continues to log in highest quarterly sales quarter-on-quarter.

items.quote: we should be looking at expanding it to almost 100 plus stores, ideally double of the 70 that we had.

items.quote: It's there in about 50 stores right now. We should have enough learnings in place. We should be looking at expanding that to about 70 stores within the Bata network.

items.quote: casual overall, sneakers and casual combined should be contributing to about 50% to 55% of our business. My sense is that going forward, this should become about 60% to 65% in the longer term over, let's say, three years.

items.statement: Gross margin flat to slightly positive in Q1 FY25 despite revenue decline
items.quote: Gross margin was flat, slightly positive, but mostly flat.

items.statement: COCO model more accretive than franchise above INR 2 crore annualized turnover threshold
items.quote: the threshold that we have seen is roughly in the range of about, you know, annualized turnover of about INR2 crores. So anything above 2 crores, then the COCO kicks in as much more accretive, right?

items.quote: Overall, it's not been too far from our ballpark of 250 to 300 basis points, but versus last year, yes, it's been a higher increase.

items.statement: New product launches contribute mid-teens (14-18%) of sales and inventory allocation
items.quote: The sales contribution is in the range of about mid-teens, so about 14 to 18%, depending on the month. The inventory allocation also is in the range of about slightly higher, about 14% to 18%.

items.statement: Evolite (EVA category at ~INR 500) showing strong traction in mass segment despite sluggishness
items.quote: we have invested in the EVA category at a price point of about 500 plus or minus. That's given extremely good results and has been doing extremely well despite the overall sluggishness in that segment

items.quote: we had a cumulative impact of one of expenses that we also charged off in this quarter on a conservative basis about 300 basis points on the EBITDA level.

items.statement: Capex plan Rs 450 Cr for FY25, Rs 750-800 Cr over 2-3 years
items.quote: We have not changed our capex plan; everything is in line with what was planned. So, the capex plan for the current year, we should be spending in the region of around Rs.450 Cr is the expectation.

items.statement: Industry room AC growth estimated 25-30% for full year FY25
items.quote: I think it could be even 25% to 30% this year and we have to watch what is going to happen in terms of other events like for example, the oil price.

items.statement: Export revenue expected to remain flat with marginal 6-7% growth in FY25
items.quote: So, our exports revenue will remain the same like last year with a marginal growth of some 7% or 6%.

items.statement: Year-end net cash position expected around Rs 350-400 Cr
items.quote: So, we expect that by year-end probably we should be back to around Rs.350 to 400 Cr cash position.

items.quote: And in Q1 April, the market grew by some 70%, again in May 70%, June only it came down to somewhere around 10% to 15%.

items.quote: I do not think the channel would have had inventory beyond one month, which is a normal norm, I do not think it would have been more than that at all.

items.quote: Close to in a year, we think that Rs. 1,000 Cr to 1,500 Cr worth of orders can be booked. It is in th e order of around Rs.1,000 Cr now. It can go up to 1,500 Cr

items.quote: the capex expenditure also was only around Rs. 30 to 35 Cr in this quarter. Large part of the capex is planned to happen around Q2 to Q4

items.quote: The costs are coming down as of now and due to vari ous measures: One is connected with the scale. Second is connected with the value engineeri ng. The third is connected with the indigenization that is happening and finally the subdued global commodity prices also help

items.quote: Due to better collections and release of working capital it has got converted into cash. Of course, as you now again build up the inventory, the cash is going to get used up because as come Q4, you need to have stocks in position, inventory in position.

items.quote: We estimate that our market share continues to remain at 13.75%.

items.quote: EBITDA, our guidance is 10% to 12%.

items.quote: We have successfully managed to increase the price of powdered camphor, and passed the price increase to most of our customers.

items.quote: Although there is an increase in price of certain inputs from our fragrance division, we are confident of maintaining the growth momentum in this division.

items.quote: Operating EBITDA margins stood at 10.29%, which increased by 64 basis points on Q-on-Q basis and 983 basis points on Y-o-Y basis.

items.quote: And there is also an increase in the price of the raw materials and we have been able to successfully pass on that price increase to the customers. So, I think a focus on quality, which is helping us differentiate ourselves from the others who are offering the product in the market.

items.quote: Yes, 1.7x brownfield and 1.2x something for the greenfield.
