items.statement: Capacity utilization at 76% in Q1; volume grew 8% YoY to 9.64 mt despite weak industry demand
items.quote: The utilization for the quarter stood at about 76%.

items.statement: Cash EPS increased to INR259 from INR248 YoY; cash profit rose to INR957 cr from INR898 cr despite EBITDA decline
items.quote: The cash profit for Shree in June '23 stood at INR898 crores, and it is at INR957 crores this year. If you look at cash EPS, then the cash EPS in June '23 was INR248 and it has reached to INR259.

items.statement: Nawalgarh plant subsidy tied to Rajasthan GST sales; cross-border sales to NCR only viable after Etah grinding unit commissioning in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Nawalgarh's logistic advantages will kick in only when we commission our Etah grinding unit in UP, which is likely to be in the fourth quarter of this year.

items.statement: Consolidation in industry keeping prices depressed as acquirers want lower valuations; long-term positive but near-term pain
items.quote: Yes, there are targets for acquisition. Yes, further consolidation will happen. But the guys who are the contender for such consolidation would like to keep the prices of cement depressed to have a better value.

items.statement: No EBITDA guidance given due to price uncertainty; cost normalization expected but pricing depends on demand revival from government spending
items.quote: I cannot give you an EBITDA guidance because I don't know what the selling price will be. So Q2, for sure, is not going to be good for the industry.

items.statement: Non-trade sales component increased in Q1; exact split not disclosed but confirmed by management
items.quote: Your observation is correct. I don't have the numbers readily available with me. Jajoo will share with you, but yes, the non-trade component has gone up.

items.statement: Depreciation guided at INR2,600 crores for current capacity base; increase due to capitalization of new assets, not rate change
items.quote: With this capacity, which is in vogue today, I will guide you a depreciation of about INR2,600 crores.

items.statement: Stabilization costs of INR52 crores for Guntur and Nawalgarh plants in Q1; normalization expected in 3-6 months but could take up to 12 months
items.quote: As on date, about INR52 crores in this quarter represents additional stores and spares consumed in Guntur and Nawalgarh.

items.statement: Clinker volume negligible at ~4 lakh tons out of 96.4 lakh tons total; Dachepalli grinding capacity balanced via logistic optimization
items.quote: So out of 96 lakh ton, hardly 4 lakh ton is clinker.

items.statement: Railway siding projects on schedule; detailed timeline per plant to be shared via email
items.quote: It's on schedule. It's on schedule.

items.statement: Water positivity >6x achieved in Q1; targeting >7x for full year with good monsoon progress
items.quote: In Q1 '25, the company achieved water positivity levels of more than 6x. With good progress on monsoon for the year as a whole, it aims to improve its water positivity level to more than 7x for the whole year.

items.statement: Alternative fuel usage: 0.27 lakh tons agro waste (80 billion kCal, 0.32 lakh tons CO2 saved) and 0.78 lakh tons hazardous waste (26.3 billion kCal) in Q1
items.quote: Notably, the company used about 0.27 lakh tons of agro waste in the quarter, thereby conserving fossil fuel equivalent to producing about 80 billion kCal and save about 0.32 lakh tons of CO2.

items.statement: Engineering business revenue grew 15% YoY in Q1 FY25; Excel recorded highest ever Q1 revenue
items.quote: We have started FY25 on a positive note with a reven ue growth of 15% over the corresponding period last year. Both Greaves Engines and Excel performed well with the latter registering its highest ever first quarter

items.statement: Engineering business diversifying beyond engines into industrial, marine, energy, agriculture, data centers, and green fuel engines
items.quote: I am pleased to report tha t we are making steady progress towards this, strengthening our portfolio with prod ucts designed for the industrial, marine, energy and agricultural sectors

items.statement: Export share expected to grow with greater revenue contribution from U.S. and EU regions in coming years
items.quote: We anticipate that export share will grow as our lines of business scale up with greater revenue contribution exp ected from the U.S. and EU regions in the coming years

items.statement: CPCB-IV+ regulations driving demand for environmentally friendly gensets in infrastructure, realty, industrial segments
items.quote: We introduced a range of cutting edge, robust and environmentally friendly CPCB-IV+ products during the quarter which received a positive response primarily driven by dema nd from infrastructure, reality and industrial segments

items.statement: Focused approach on improving efficiencies and inventory management resulted in improved working capital cycle for engineering business
items.quote: During the quarter, our focused approach on improving effi ciencies and better inventory management has also resulted in an improved working capital cycle for the

items.statement: Greaves Retail revenue Rs. 148 crores in Q1 FY25, up 7% YoY
items.quote: We had a good start to the financial year with revenues of Rs. 148 crores for Q1, up 7% Y-on-Y.

items.statement: Retail expanded into 2W multi-brand parts, EV parts, construction equipment parts; signed several new EV OEMs including one prominent player
items.quote: During the Quarter 1, we expanded our part lines, get ting into two-wheeler multi- brand parts, electric vehicle parts, and construction equ ipment parts beyond our traditional three-wheeler parts

items.statement: Greaves Care outlets expanded to 163 on franchisee model, now service multiple brand vehicles including electric 2W/3W and small commercial vehicles
items.quote: Our Greaves Care outlets have expanded to 163. These are on a franchisee-owned, franchisee-operated model. They now service a full range of multiple brand vehicles, small commercial vehicles, which include electric thre e-wheelers and electric two- wheelers, and other small commercial vehicles

items.statement: E-mobility 2W volumes up 10% QoQ, 3W volumes up 19% QoQ in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our two-wheeler volumes have increased by 10% and our three-wheeler volumes by 19% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Launched Ampere Nexus, India's first high performance family scooter with LFP battery at Rs. 1,09,900 ex-showroom, designed and manufactured in India
items.quote: One of the highlights for the quarter under review w as the introduction of Ampere Nexus. It is India's first high performance family sc ooter equipped with the safest LFP chemistry battery and hybrid swing arm with twin suspe nsion starting at a very attractive price of Rs. 1,09,900 ex-showroom

items.statement: Revised Eltra City pricing aggressively to on-road price of Rs. 3,70,000 with enhanced bill of material efficiency
items.quote: Furthermore, on the three-wheeler side, we have also revised Greaves Eltr a City pricing very aggressively to an on-road price of Rs. 3,70,000 with our enhanced efficiency on our bill of material

items.statement: Eltra City Passenger and Eltra Cargo already eligible under MHI scheme and receiving subsidies; Ampere 2W EVs eligible for EMPS registration and future MHI schemes
items.quote: On the subsidy front, our three-wheelers, Eltra City P assenger and Eltra Cargo are already eligible under the MHI scheme and are receivi ng subsidies. We are very happy to share that MHI has communicated that our t wo-wheeler electric vehicles under Ampere brand are eligible to be tested by the relevant testing agencies for EMPS registration and any other future schemes of MHI and secure subsidie

items.statement: Management does not give future guidance as corporate policy; Board directive and management committed to path to profitability for EV business
items.quote: Honestly, Kunal, as a corporate policy, we do not gi ve future guidance. But let me assure you that this is the directive of our Board, and this is what the management team is fully committed to

items.statement: Excel margin contracted due to product mix change; committed to 30% range long term
items.quote: In terms of margin, there has been a change in the product mix. And this will happen over a period of time as we grow the business. But yes, we are committed to a 30% range in the long term.

items.statement: Almost zero-debt position maintained with standalone cash of Rs. 550 crores to support future expansion and investment plans
items.quote: On the balance sheet front, we continue to maintain an almost zero-debt position with standalone cash of Rs. 550 crores, which will support our future expansion and investment plans.

items.statement: EV business working aggressively on bill of material cost reduction and cost rationalization; cost efficiencies sustainable in coming quarters
items.quote: What we have done in the last I would say, couple of months, we have worked aggressively on our bill of material in terms of key components, and we have been able to make con siderable inroads in terms of our costing of key components and products on

items.statement: EV business cost optimization reduced EBITDA loss; cost efficiencies sustainable and will continue to improve
items.quote: Yes, the answer is yes and that it will continue, th at effort will continue and next quarter you will see the results in the right direction and hence that is sustainable

items.statement: EV business passing on some cost benefits to customers where margins secured and competitive intensity high; retaining other portions
items.quote: Wherever we had our margins secured and competitive intensity high, we have passed on some portion of it. The other portions we have retained it. So, that is the complete and comprehensive work which is happening on all product and product portfolios.

items.statement: Excel manufacturing utilization in 70s-80s percent; modular system allows quick response to demand spikes without huge capacity overhead
items.quote: We are working on a fairly high level of utilization in terms of if you see the kind of growth that we have had in the last couple of years. So, they are in the 70s and 80s percent I would say overall.

items.statement: Non-auto genset market share less than 10%; significant headroom for growth as industry grows with infrastructure, railways, telecom, commercial complexes
items.quote: In terms of market share, we have a relatively low market share as of now which is why we see significant headroom for growth in this area.

items.statement: Board exploring all options for GEM and GFL including demerger; no concrete plans currently, commitment to build businesses
items.quote: So, I think as the Board has said in the past, this is a Board- related matter, they are exploring all options for b oth GEM and GFL, right, in terms of options. And as and when there is any other moment , we will explore that. But right now, the commitment is to continue to help build these businesses

items.statement: Management keeping close watch on geopolitical situation and potential impacts; being careful and selective on exports
items.quote: We a re also keeping a close watch on the current geopolitical situation and its potential impacts. Despite these external factors, we continue our internal efforts to enhance profitability

items.statement: E-mobility 2W market share 3.4% in Q1 FY25; among top five players in e-2W segment
items.quote: On the two-wheeler side, we continue to be among the top five players in the e-two- wheeler segment with a market share of 3.4% in Q1

items.statement: No guidance on definitive EV turnaround timeline; trajectory of last 4-5 quarters shows improvement but no forward guidance given
items.quote: that is the agenda, and if you take the traject ory of the last four quarters, five quarters, the management, as I said, has been focused e xternally on resolving the issues that have been raised by MHI, and internally, on improving the product portfolio, improving the systems process, working on cos t efficiencies, and the results are coming to show, right? But in terms of g uidance, I would not

items.statement: Expects Yarn division outlook to improve in Q2 and further in Q3-Q4; Fabric strong throughout; Garment to pick up significantly in Q3-Q4; not a disastrous year, sees inflection point
items.quote: So, I think that the outlook for the Yarn division in Quarter 2 will be better and Quarter 3, Quarter 4 will be even better. So, that's as far as the Yarn division is concerned. Fabric, it looks wonderful all throughout. And Garment will start to pick up also in Quarter 3, Quarter 4 in significant ways.

items.statement: Expects finance cost around Rs. 35 crores for FY25, changing quarter-on-quarter due to CAPEX
items.quote: It will be in the range of around Rs. 35 crores but let's see how we go ahead on the CAPEX and how do we increas e. So, it will be changing quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Estimated CAPEX of Rs. 180-190 crores over 18-24 months for FY25 and FY26
items.quote: So, expected CAPEX over a period of 2 years, if I can draw the line of sight then it will be in the range of around Rs. 180 crores to Rs. 190 crores, but it will be over a period of 18 to 24 months, not all at a time.

items.statement: Seeing demand recovery in H2 FY25 from Western markets including Eastern Europe
items.quote: Yes, we are seeing recovery in the second half of the year in demand from all markets in the West. It has been bad earlier, but now it seems to be improving quite well.

items.statement: Domestic formal wear pipeline empty, big wedding season ahead driving jacket demand
items.quote: by and large, the demand for jackets now seems to be on an upward trend, primarily because the pipeline for Indian domestic formal wear is quite empty and we see a big wedding season ahead.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to ~61% in Q1 FY25 from 56-57% earlier despite higher raw material costs, due to value-added products
items.quote: if you look at overall gross margin, and you compare our gross margin this quarter versus our gross margin last quarter or even over the previous financial year gross margin average to the gross margin in this quarter, this quarter is better with about 60 point some percent, 61% almost gross margin, whereas earlier, the gross margin w as like 56%, 57%.

items.statement: Simone brand has Rs. 25 crores bookings for FY25, targets Rs. 500-1000 crores in 5-6 years
items.quote: We have bookings of Rs. 25 crores already for this financial year in Simone. And we expect this brand to grow to really be a sizable brand in the coming years.

items.statement: Uniform business with Eastern European armies (Czechoslovakian, Slovakian) and working on Dutch, German uniforms
items.quote: you have seen that we have engaged with several diffe rent armies in Eastern Europe like we have the business from the Czechoslovakian Army, the Slovakian Army. We are working on the Dutch uniforms and the German uniforms.

items.statement: Targets Fabric utilization back to 80-85% by end of FY25; Garment to 60-80% by Q3-Q4
items.quote: we should be by the end of the year at back to 80%, 85% utilization as far as Fabric is concerned. Garment is the one which was the concerning one where we actually went down to almost 45% utilization. And we should try and get back there to the 60, 70s, 80s by Quarter 3, Quarter 4.

items.statement: Increasing external yarn sourcing (cotton, filament polyester, Chinese poly viscose) for Fabric business; internal yarn usage percentage to decline
items.quote: On regular yarns like filament yarns etc., we are sourcing more. And the percentage of fabric that we are producing based on cotton yarn that we buy from outside and filament polyester that we buy from outside is increasing. We are even importing certain Chinese poly viscose specialty yarns.

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest may benefit India long-term but not immediately; duty advantage for Bangladesh remains a barrier; Vietnam dominates knitwear
items.quote: Long term, yes, if customers have been rattled once and now are putting a question mark on the political stability in Bangladesh, long term, they will look towards India. So, we do expect benefits to happen down the road. Immediately, maybe it won't be such a big impact.

items.statement: Seeing good export demand from Eastern European countries (Poland, Czechoslovakia, Slovakia); uniform business with Eastern European armies
items.quote: we are seeing a lot of demand even in Europe, particularly from the Eastern European countries like Poland, Czechoslovakia, Slovakia and all of the countries, we are seeing a good demand.

items.statement: Finished goods inventory increased slightly in Q1 due to pipeline orders; raw material inventory stable; will be billed in subsequent period
items.quote: Yes, there is a little in this quarter, the inventory on finished goods has little been increased. But that is all because of the orders what we have in pipeline. So, it will get billed in a subsequent period.

items.statement: Long-term borrowings increasing due to CAPEX plan; finance cost expected around Rs. 35 crores in FY25
items.quote: we are looking for a CAPEX plan in our worsted and we are also looking for decongesting our mill and making some realignment. So, we are doing some civil work and all that. So, there will be addition in our long -term borrowings.

items.statement: Total income declined 10% YoY to Rs. 274.7 crores; EBITDA Rs. 20.8 crores; PAT Rs. 1 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our total income declined by 10% to Rs. 274.7 crores in Q1 FY '25 on a year-on-year basis. The EBITDA stood at Rs. 20.8 crores during the 1st Quarter. Profit before depreciation tax came in at Rs. 12.7 crores and the company recorded a PAT of Rs. 1 crore in the 1st Quarter.

items.statement: Tesca technical textiles turnover Rs. 19 crores in Q1; flat QoQ, down 16% YoY; defense technical textiles growing
items.quote: For Tesca Quarter 1, we did a turnover of about Rs. 19 crores. And our quarter-on-quarter growth seems to be flat, but the year-on-year sort of declined by about 16%. However, this again looks pretty good for Quarter 2, Quarter 3.

items.statement: Labor shortages during election season impacted Yarn division volumes in Q1 FY25
items.quote: The decline is attributed to the muted demand along with labor shortages due to the election season.

items.statement: This is the worst quarter in a long time; expects everything to be better from here onwards
items.quote: We do recognize that this has been the worst quarter that we have experienced in a long time in terms of the financial results. However, this is as bad as it gets. And we expect everything to be better from here onwards.

items.statement: Management expects EBIT margins for pump division at 18-20% and projects at 15-18%, with overall business in 15-20% range
items.quote: I think overall we plan for, as we mentioned, the businesses to be in the range of between 15% and 20%. So, I think that's the range we should look at, maybe the shifts sometimes depending on certain dispatches.

items.statement: Domestic project order book at Rs 3,914 crore and product order book at Rs 400 crore as of Q1 FY25
items.quote: The domestic order book on the projects business stood at round Rs. 3,914 crores and for the product business it was around Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: International order book grew to Rs 484 crore from typical Rs 450 crore
items.quote: Internationally, the order book has grown to Rs. 484 crores with a positive outlook across all segments.

items.statement: Strong demand in both water supply and irrigation sectors, with irrigation becoming government focus in medium term
items.quote: We are seeing both the sectors are performing well. As you said correctly, irrigation will be the thrust I think for the government in the medium term now, because water supply was the thrust in the last three, four years.

items.statement: No significant capex planned; growth to come from brownfield expansion and product development using existing low-utilization capacity
items.quote: We have sufficient capacity. I think most of our plants are working at very low-capacity utilization. So, we do brownfield expansion. It's not a significant investment needed

items.statement: Plants operating at very low capacity utilization; brownfield expansion sufficient for growth
items.quote: We have sufficient capacity. I think most of our plants are working at very low-capacity utilization. So, we do brownfield expansion.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic acquisitions internationally to grow product revenue and replace lost nuclear business revenue
items.quote: Our focus is to focus on inorganic expansion right now. We are looking at targets and we hope to be successful, because we lost revenue after the sale, so we look to increase our international revenues by more acquisitions.

items.statement: In advanced discussions for acquisitions in core industrial pumps; expects good results this year
items.quote: So, we are in various stages of the process. Some are in introductory discussion, some are in a bit more advanced discussions. And we will be updating, and we expect good results this year.

items.statement: Debtors and inventory expected to normalize to balanced levels in FY25 after accelerated Q4 FY24
items.quote: It will go back to a normalized level. We had accelerated last quarter, and I think we are hoping to have a more balanced revenue in this year, as we have seen in the 1st Quarter. So, we expect more balanced revenue, which will lead to a normalized level of debtor and inventory.

items.statement: Project order book split ~80% water supply, 20% irrigation; pump end-market split ~40% municipal water, 30% industrial, 30% irrigation
items.quote: Right now, I think that in the projects business there is a big focus on the water supply segment. And we expect the irrigation sector to grow going forward. But today, with the government thrust on the Jal Jeevan in the past, our order book is still majorly in the water supply segment, which is close to about 80%, I think.

items.statement: US market identified as major thrust area for geographical expansion; international business 3-4% of global pump market
items.quote: US is a very important market which we are looking to enter. So, exactly that. Geographically we are more focused because we have access to all the technologies, most of the technologies. So, maybe some sector market presence improvement is needed. But geographical reach is more important. So, the US is a major thrust area for us.

items.statement: Auditor flagged need for deeper study on capital gains tax applicability on Rutschi sale proceeds under Italian participation exemption rules
items.quote: Yes, I think we are testing it what is the capital gain tax applicable. So, it needs a deeper study that was pointed out by the auditor, and we are doing that deeper study.

items.statement: All disputed receivables (McNally Bharat Rs 9.99 cr, IVRCL Rs 4.3 cr) fully provided for in annual financials
items.quote: All are provided in the annual financials.

items.statement: Promoter MD personally focused on expansion and product development
items.quote: Expansion, I think product development.

items.statement: Ongoing litigation on one Madhya Pradesh project; eight other MP projects progressing well with three commissioning soon
items.quote: I think we have an ongoing litigation regarding the MP project, and as I mentioned that the other eight projects are moving well with three projects planned for commissioning in the next four months. So, no such impact as of now.

items.statement: Operates in critical pumps segment (24/7 working, drainage applications) above 5 HP, not in commoditized agriculture segment
items.quote: We do not operate in the commoditized domestic agriculture sector below 5 horsepower. So, the sector which is ours is mostly 24/7 working or critical drainage application working. So, there is good growth and good margins.

items.statement: Short-term guidance of meaningful recovery starting from latter part of Q3 FY25
items.quote: We are beginning to see early indicators of increased volume and improved customer sentiment. Even amidst persistent pricing pressure, we maintain our short -term guidance of meaningful recovery startin g from latter part of Quarter 3

items.statement: Early indicators of increased volume and improved customer sentiment seen
items.quote: We are beginning to see early indicators of increased volume and improved customer sentiment.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA grew 36% YoY to Rs. 328 crores; margins improved by 2%
items.quote: EBITDA grew 36% to Rs. 328 crores in Q1 FY25 compared to Rs. 242 crores in Q1 FY24. Margins have improved by 2% during the quarter.

items.statement: DPL set new record with quarterly IPA sales of 22,000 KT
items.quote: DPL set a new record with quarterly IPA sales of 22,000 KT showcasing our dedication to market demand and encouraging performance.

items.statement: Rs. 2,000 crores of projects in final stages of implementation, being commissioned during current financial year
items.quote: Various projects entailing an outlay of around Rs. 2,000 crores are in the final stages of implementation, and these are being commissioned during the current financial year.

items.statement: Rs. 14,000 crores MOU with Gujarat government for phenol, BPA, polycarbonate, aniline
items.quote: You are all aware, we have signed 2 MOUs with the Government of Gujarat, which encompass an investment to the tune of about Rs. 14,000 crores towards the fulfillment of these objectives.

items.statement: Land and infrastructure capex estimated at Rs. 300-350 crores out of Rs. 2,000 crores
items.quote: Around Rs. 300 crores to Rs. 350 crores.

items.statement: Capex split 60% upstream integration, 40% downstream after land/infra
items.quote: the remainder is about a 60-40, 60% upstream and 40% downstream.

items.statement: Acetophenone world-scale plant under implementation, likely commissioning in 12 months
items.quote: And this will be manufactured from recovered byproduct when we make phenol. This is under implementation and is likely to be commissioned in about 12 months.

items.statement: DASDA and OBA capacity expanded 18-20% in FY24 while reducing energy footprint
items.quote: In both of these products in the last year, we expanded our capacity by about 18% to 20% as well as improved our operational excellence as well as improved our carbon and water footprint.

items.statement: New R&D center in Vadodara expected to complete by end of current financial year
items.period: end of the current financial year
items.quote: Our new R&D center in Vadodara is expected to complete in the end of the current financial year and will enhance our innovation capabilities and support our strategic growth projects.

items.statement: Product mix improved in AI segment via new territories and customers
items.quote: Proactive steps to penetrate new territories and grow businesses with new customers offset a weak demand environment in the traditional territories of the Western world. This aided in an improvement in the product mix in the AI segment.

items.statement: Phenolics realization improved significantly; Advanced Intermediates realization under pressure
items.quote: EBITDA growth has been driven by the Phenolics business, which witnessed a significant improvement in realization. This is in contrast to the Advanced Intermediates segment, where the pressure on realization has resulted in reduced EBITDA.

items.statement: Commissioned first industrial multi-fuel boiler, eliminating fossil fuels at one location
items.quote: We also commissioned the first industrial multi-fuel boiler in the chemical industry, which helps us in completely doing away with fossil fuels in one of our locations.

items.statement: Reduced single customer/geography dependency; wallet shares intact and growing
items.quote: We have significantly reduced single customer or single geography dependency. In the short term, this does come at a slight margin squeeze. There's no doubt about it. But the good thing is that our credibility with all the key customers remains intact

items.statement: No significant increase in competition intensity in fine and specialty chemicals
items.quote: I think there are co-producers. I don't know whether there are more co-producers. The business landscape on those products remains more or less what it was.

items.statement: Expect licensing agreements for polycarbonate/methacrylates by end of calendar year
items.quote: In our AGM that just concluded, the Chairman updated that we expect to have licensing agreements in place by the end of the calendar year.

items.statement: Freight costs 10-15% higher YoY; impacts export competitiveness vs China
items.quote: I think one thing that I can tell you is that freight today is about 10% to 15% higher than it was last year.

items.statement: Net debt negative; cash generation ~Rs. 1,000 crores/annum; net worth ~Rs. 5,000 crores
items.quote: Since we have a very strong balance sheet and continuing cash generation of around Rs. 1,000 crores per annum and net worth position is around Rs. 5,000 crores, with the net debt negative, we are holding a very healthy financial position.

items.statement: ICRA reaffirmed Deepak Chem Tech long-term rating at ICRA AA with stable outlook
items.quote: Further, I am pleased to share that ICRA has reaffirmed Deepak Chem Tech Limited's long-term rating at ICRA AA with a stable outlook.

items.statement: Advanced Intermediates volume grew 5% QoQ; domestic volumes growing, export products soft
items.quote: volume overall there's a growth of 5%. As Maulik mentioned about the products where there was some softness, those are export products. Whereas domestic volumes are growing and domestic volumes are doing well.

items.statement: Bangladesh crisis impact unassessed; could be short-term positive or negative
items.quote: However, the potential impact of the ongoing crisis in Bangladesh is yet another black swan, whose short-term positive or negative effect is yet to be properly assessed.

items.statement: Agrochemicals demand still soft; recovery expected later this year
items.quote: While there was soft demand in agrochemicals, which is expected to recover later this year.

items.statement: Insurance claim of Rs. 127 crores for Nandesari fire fully approved and received
items.quote: Coming to our insurance claim, following the fire incident in Nandesari, we had submitted a claim of Rs. 127 crores, which was approved in full with the concluding payment received during the quarter.

items.statement: Polycarbonate compounding pilot plant of 30,000 tonnes separate from Rs. 14,000 crores capex
items.quote: Polycarbonate compounding is a separate project, not a part of this Rs. 1,200 crores whatever you are saying. So, R&D, and then next phase is polycarbonate compounding and the larger capexes.

items.statement: Backward integration benefits from fluorination/nitric acid projects expected to be tangible in Q4 FY25
items.quote: I think Q4 should be a good quarter with regards to many of these benefits being tangibly felt. There will be a partial boost that we will get in our Q3. But one would assume that Q4 is realistic in a key quarter.

items.statement: Polycarbonate chain projects deadline December 2027; production start committed
items.quote: December 2027 is the date. Maybe one quarter here and there maximum, but not beyond that, so that is the deadline.

items.statement: Medium-term growth target of 25-30% YoY for next 2-3 years with sustainable EBITDA margins of 12-13%
items.quote: We are looking at a growth in the range of about 25% to 30% year-on-year for the next two to three years that's I think is our internal target.

items.statement: Sustainable growth rate of 22-25% for next 3 years
items.quote: And on a sustainable level, I think, for the next 3 years I am pretty sure that we'll be able to maintain a growth rate in the range of 22% - 25%.

items.statement: Company growing faster than industry; industry growth estimated at 8-9%
items.quote: Industry should be growing by the range of 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Glass bottle prices stable YoY; higher new bottle usage and lower return rates in new states keep EBITDA margin guidance at 12-13%
items.quote: I think the main price component or the cost is of glass bottles. And the prices of glass bottles have been stable if I compare to June 2023 and June 2024.

items.statement: Q1 annualized capacity utilization: 100% at MP and Odisha plants, 70% at Karnataka (Woodpecker) plant post-expansion
items.quote: So, for this quarter we have operated at an annualized capacity utilization of 100% for both MP and Odisha. While for the Woodpecker, because we had just completed the capacity expansion in April this year. So, we have about 70% of capacity utilization for Woodpecker that is the Karnataka plant.

items.statement: Karnataka plant utilization expected to reach 85-90% by next season, potentially 90-95% in second year
items.quote: I think it should be about 85% to 90%.

items.statement: Odisha expansion capex of Rs 30-40 crore to start by December 2024, complete by April 2025; funded via promoter warrants and debt, no fresh dilution
items.quote: We have got one capex planned like I was discussing with the previous caller in Odisha, which we should start by December of this year. And hopefully, we should be able to complete it by April of next year.

items.statement: Evaluating acquisition opportunities for new state entry; Greenfield possible next year
items.quote: And we are also eyeing certain acquisition opportunities in states where we want to enter, or we might even look at a Greenfield but may be for next year.

items.statement: Premium product launch planned this financial year, priced around Kingfisher Ultra; premium segment ~15% of industry, growing fast but mass segment remains core
items.quote: We have certain announcements to make on this result for confidentiality reason, I cannot disclose the product launches, which we plan to do in this quarter or the next quarter, but I think definitely you will see some premium product being launched from us this financial year.
