items.statement: Capex guidance of INR300 crore for recycling plant and INR125 crore for POY/FDY expansion over next 2 years
items.quote: The capex guidance is, see, we will be investing in a subsidiary or recycling. The total capex there is INR300 crores, and we would be going in a mix of equity and loans. And then we are also planning, as the market improves, to invest around INR125 crores in increasing our POY and FDY facility as we have added cationic polymerization.

items.statement: Cationic yarn trial production started; commercial production expected in next week or 10 days
items.quote: The cationic yarn trial production has started. Commercial, I think we should be able to do in next week or 10 days. It was delayed due to some environmental clearances, which we wanted.

items.statement: Land procured for recycling plant near Dahej; registration in next 15 days; project completion targeted by end of December 2025
items.quote: We have procured the land and are in the process of seeking permissions to set our recycling facility as a greenfield project. In our assessment, we should be completing the project by end of December 2025.

items.statement: Second half FY25 demand expected to be very good due to seasonal winter demand, potential Bangladesh order diversion, and no new capacity additions
items.quote: I think second half should be very good. Normally, second half is always better than the first half. As in the winter, the demand for the fabric increases. And I don't know after this Bangladesh episode, we expect a lot of orders of export of garments also to be diverted to India.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin around 5-6%; no improvement expected in H1 FY25; H2 FY25 margins expected close to 9%
items.quote: First half, I don't think we'll have any improvement. But second half, I think second half margins should be very close to maybe 9%, something like that.

items.statement: Current spreads not very good; EBITDA margin around 5-6%; similar to last quarter with slight decline of 1-2%
items.quote: Currently, spreads are not very good. That's reflected in our results also. So I think around 5%, 6% EBITDA margin is going on.

items.statement: Significant margin improvement expected from Q3 and Q4 FY25, not in Q2
items.quote: Yes. From third and fourth quarter, we are expecting significant improvement. Not in the second quarter, we're not expecting so much improvement but third and fourth quarter should be significantly better.

items.statement: Export volumes very small at around 2%; no drastic increase expected until raw material parity with China is resolved
items.quote: We do export. But the export volumes are very small, maybe around 2%. I don't see export increases in the near future drastically, till the time the parity of the raw material between China and India is sorted out, I don't see exports of yarn going up.

items.statement: No new debt currently; INR150 crore debt planned for recycling subsidiary in FY26 to avail state interest subsidies
items.quote: See, right now, we're not taking any debt. Yes, for our recycling plant, we will take a debt in the subsidiary company because there are some interest-subsidies available from the state government. To avail that, we will take a debt. So that could be around INR150 crores but that will mostly happen in FY '26.

items.statement: Government considering minimum import price on fabrics for all HS codes; some HS codes already covered since March
items.quote: Government is considering fixing minimum import price on fabrics for import against all HS codes. The global textile industry is experiencing a significant shift.

items.statement: Yarn imports decreased from beginning of year but fabric imports continuing through uncovered HS codes
items.quote: See, yarn imports have definitely decreased from beginning of this year but the fabric import is continuing. And government had put in March some minimum import price on certain HS codes. But certain HS codes were left out.

items.statement: Developed patented molecule regeneration process for polyester recycling (T2T); pilot plant running; advanced discussions for 26,250 TPA commercial plant
items.quote: We have developed and patented a process based on molecule regeneration of polyester, which can be recirculated infinitely. We are running a pilot plant to use miscellaneous types of textile garment, home linen or pre-consumer waste. Simultaneously, we are in advanced stage of discussion with equipment suppliers for a 26,250 tons per annum capacity plant.

items.statement: Sourced around 30% energy from renewable sources to reduce carbon footprint
items.quote: We have sourced around 30% of our energy from renewable sources, thereby reducing the carbon footprint.

items.statement: Domestic demand subdued due to residual impact of massive fabric imports from China; rural demand recovery not translating to textile segment
items.quote: The domestic demand is still subdued. We can see the residual impact of massive imports of fabrics from China. Though rural demand is showing good signs of recovery, it is not translated to textile segment.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 sales volume 95,962 metric tons vs 100,211 metric tons in Q1 FY24; operating EBITDA INR61 crore (35% YoY growth); net profit INR32 crore vs INR18 crore
items.quote: We achieved a sales volume of 95,962 metric ton as against 1,00,211 metric tons in Q1 FY '24. The operating EBITDA is around INR61 crores, a growth of around 35% from INR44 crores in Q1 FY '24. The net profit has increased to INR32 crores in this quarter from INR18 crores in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 sales grew ~7% YoY; civil +6.2%, MES +20%; US election year slowing civil construction and EV projects on hold
items.quote: We have a sluggish quarter in the Q1. Sales are up by about 7% but due to increased employee cost and new addition of 190 trainees, the EBITDA has come down by about 14% and PAT is down by 17.5% from INR6.28 cr ores in Q1 last year to INR5.18 crores

items.statement: EBITDA fell ~14% YoY; EBITDA margin dropped to ~22% from 28% prior year due to employee cost rising to 68% of revenue from 64%
items.quote: EBITDA margin has gone up from somewhere around 18%, 19% three years ago to 28% in the previous financial year. It actually went 30% in '22, '23. And in '23, '24, it was somewhere around 28%. So currently, it is hovering around 22%.

items.statement: Expects flattish growth for full FY25 in both civil and MES due to US election slowdown; hopes for pickup after US elections or early next financial year
items.quote: Otherwise, this year will be more flattish due to the recession or if not a recession, the slowdown in the U.S. economic activity mainly in construction industry. But in MES, we are still opening those at Europe or other lines of activity like SPMs, press tools.

items.statement: Depreciation up 16.6% due to increased software purchases
items.quote: Depreciation is also considerably stable but it is up by 16.6% due to increased software purchases and depreciation there upon.

items.statement: Added 190 trainees in Q1; net addition of 150-200 employees over last 15-16 months; trainees take ~1 year before billable
items.quote: We have a sluggish quarter in the Q1. Sales are up by about 7% but due to increased employee cost and new addition of 190 trainees, the EBITDA has come down by about 14%

items.statement: Attrition ~15-16%; total employee strength ~1,200 including new trainees; implemented Performance Improvisation Plan to manage underperformers
items.quote: See, attrition rate is somewhere around 15% to 16% like in the industry. And the employee strength is now close to 1,100. With the new trainees, it may be now close to 1,200.

items.statement: In talks with two structural design companies for acquisition; one at advanced stage with financials shared and meetings lined up; open to INR50-200 cr deal size
items.quote: Right from INR50 crores to INR200 crores, any size of acquisition that suits us, we are ready to go for it.

items.statement: Civil work on hand ~$2.84M (flat vs March); MES work on hand ~$0.58-0.61M (up 5-10%); stagnation due to US market slowdown
items.quote: As on date, the job on work, work on hand as of the end of March '24, it was 2.8. Even today, current work on hand in civil is 2.84. In case of MES, it was 0.5 million last year, last quarter, that is the 31st of March. And today it is 0.58 million, 0.61 million, as of June 30th.

items.statement: Signed agreement with Spanish company for SPM work; will take couple of quarters to scale; hired US-based PE (licensed in 26 states) to scout structural/connection design work
items.quote: We have signed an agreement with a Spanish company for SPM work. But that to become a true big number, it might take a couple of quarters.

items.statement: Focusing on connection design growth; targeting structural design via acquisition; expanding MES into SPMs, heavy machinery, utilities, industrial machinery via new BDM hires
items.quote: We are now focusing on adding our BD team with seniors who have prior experience in not only electrical transmission and utilities, but also in industrial machinery and SPMs.

items.statement: Structural design EBITDA margins in US ~30%+; outsourcing model could improve further; acquisition of $3-5M company would add top line and credibility
items.quote: The beauty of the structural designing is the EBITDA margins even in the U.S. are very high. They're in the region of at least 30% and can be better with outsourcing, which will be our business model going forward.

items.statement: US construction slowdown due to election year; EV domain uncertainty (EV vs hydrogen); 25% of workforce non-billable during training; margin pressure if revenue doesn't recover
items.quote: if not 10%, a t least even 10% to 15% rise in construction activity we are sure will happen by end of this calendar year or maybe beginning of next financial year, that is January for them

items.statement: Company cash-rich with INR40-50 cr in deposits; bankers ready to support; investor interest for acquisition funding; no debt concerns raised
items.quote: Because the company is cash-rich. We have more than INR40 crores to INR50 crores worth of funds stacked in our various deposits. And apart from that, company bankers are ready to support.

items.statement: US-focused (Atlanta office); Europe not pursued seriously due to different standards (FAS vs metric); mechanical metric-based allows geographic diversification
items.quote: In fact, even opportunities in Europe we are not really purs uing seriously because the standards in our country, standards in UK or Europe are entirely different from U.S. standards

items.statement: Employee cost rose to 68% of revenue from 64% YoY; overall expenditure up 14.9%; finance costs stable
items.quote: employee costs have gone up by almost [12.3% to 8% 02:05] from 64% last year of the overall revenues to 68% so thereby imp acting the EBITDA

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margins to remain in similar range as Q1 FY25 (28%)
items.quote: we expect that the EBITDA should remain in similar kind of range

items.statement: Management does not provide revenue guidance as per company policy
items.quote: I don't think we would be in a position to provide any guidance first. That's something that is a policy we do not do.

items.statement: Full year FY25 capex estimated at Rs 125 crores including Rs 50 crores for Albumin project, Rs 50 crores maintenance, Rs 25 crores for Tranexamic Acid expansion
items.quote: I think we have mentioned that for the year we have about Rs 125 crores kind of CAPEX requirements in toto, about Rs 50 crores for our Albumin project, about Rs 50-odd crores for our maintenance CAPEX and all and around Rs 25-odd crores for our Tranexamic Acid expansion, that's the full year number.

items.statement: Company on track to prepay Rs 300 crores of NCD long-term debt in August from QIP proceeds
items.quote: We are on track to prepay as we had mentioned earlier. We have earmarked Rs 300 crores out of the QIP raise that we had done and that is something that we would prepay during this particular month. We are on track for it. And this prepayment is happening towards NCD which is a long-term debt.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded to 28% from 19% YoY driven by licensing income mix and formulation growth
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter was at Rs. 83 crores compared to Rs. 50 crores in Q1, again, a strong growth of 66% YoY and EBITDA margins were also up at 28% from 19% during the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Secured pre-launch order for NDA molecule #1 with breakthrough designation; supplies over current and subsequent quarters
items.quote: We have already secured a pre-launch order in this quarter for which the supplies will be done over the current quarter and subsequent quarters.

items.statement: Signed CDMO deal with Unicycive Therapeutics for Oxylanthanum Carbonate with US$ 10 million milestones; dedicated facility to be funded by customer
items.quote: We are delighted to announce a key CDMO signed during the quarter with Unicycive Therapeutics for Oxylanthanum Carbonate. We will be supplying to them the finished formulation along with our own API. We will be receiving US$ 10 million milestones for this deal.

items.statement: Licensing revenue in Q1 FY25 was 50:50 mix of existing contract milestones and new contract signings
items.quote: currently in this quarter, it's a mix of both; it's a ratio of maybe around 50:50.

items.statement: New microbial fermentation facility for Albumin expected to complete in Q3 FY25
items.quote: the new facility for large scale Microbial Fermentation, the project is going well on track, and we are expecting to complete the project in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: ANVISA Brazil GMP audit for 29 products in Unit-II successfully completed in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Q1, we could finish the ANVISA Brazil GMP audit for almost 29 products in Unit-II and the audit was successfully completed.

items.statement: USFDA formulation facility review ongoing after appointing subject experts; expected to complete in Q3 FY25
items.quote: we have finished the meeting with the USFDA, and they have suggested us to appoint some subject experts for which the appointment is completed, and the review has started, and we are expecting to complete the review in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Pemetrexed injection sold >1,000 vials in US market; K Code reimbursement approval expected this quarter
items.quote: Post launch currently Amneal has already sold more than 1,000 vials currently in US market and they are waiting for K Code which is again very important for insurance reimbursement which is expected to come in this quarter.

items.statement: UDCA (Ursodeoxycholic Acid) European CEP received in Q1 FY25; expects large volume export growth in coming quarters
items.quote: With the approval of CEP, it opens a big opportunity for Shilpa Medicare in export markets, and in the quarters to come, we are confident that this molecule is expected to grow in export market in a large volume.

items.statement: Two new oncology molecules (Abiraterone, Methotrexate) US DMF and EU CEP filing planned Q3 FY25; plant scale-up and validation initiated
items.quote: two new oncology molecules, which is Abiretarone and Methotrexate, for which US DMF and European CEP is planned to be filed in Q3 FY25. And two new molecules plant scale up and validations in the oncology segments are already initiated and expected to complete in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Liraglutide plant validation completed; DMF filing expected Q3 FY25; formulation scale-up planned Q3 FY25
items.quote: I am happy to share our first GLP-I product, which is Liraglutide, for which the plant validation was successfully completed, which is a very complex API and the DMF for the same is expected to be filed in Q3.

items.statement: Semaglutide large-scale development completed; plant validation and DMF readiness targeted this financial year
items.quote: Semaglutide, which is again a second molecule in the peptide space, the large-scale development is finished and now our target is to finish the plant validation and make drug master file ready in this financial year.

items.statement: Aflibercept client scale-up batches ongoing; Phase-III human studies expected to start Q3 FY25; European scientific advice positive
items.quote: currently our client scales up batches are ongoing, and we are expecting to start the Phase-III human studies for the same product in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Albumin Phase-I human study completed; Phase-III studies for India/emerging markets and Europe to run in parallel starting Q4 FY25
items.quote: we are expecting to start the Phase-III human study in Q4 FY25 and the study duration is for one year

items.statement: Albumin excipient grade US DMF filed; commercial sales to begin as clients qualify the product
items.quote: the US DMF filing for Albumin for the excipient grade was successfully filed which gives us more confidence on the quality of our product with not only manufacturing but also with the dossier quality.

items.statement: Nilotinib European regulatory review completed; launch expected Q3 FY25 with #1 European oncology generic partner
items.quote: I am happy to share that our regulatory review for the same product is completed and the launch for the same product is expected in Q3 and for this product Company has partnered with the #1 Company in the generic space in oncology selling in Europe.

items.statement: First transdermal patch product filing in Europe expected Q2 FY25; two new transdermal patch deals signed in Q1 FY25
items.quote: our first product will be filed in September of this financial year, for which the complex clinical studies are completed and is successfully passing, and the product is expected to be filed in Europe in Q2 FY25.

items.statement: SMLNUD07 (NAFLD) Phase-III expected to complete Q2 FY25; India filing planned Q3 FY25
items.quote: Currently, the Phase-III studies are expected to complete in Q2 FY25 and we are expecting to file this product in Q3 FY25 in India

items.statement: SMLTOP09 (Androgenic Alopecia) Phase-III study expected to start Q3 FY25 after DCGI application
items.quote: for the Phase-III studies we have applied in DCGI, and we are expecting to start the Phase-III study in Q3 FY25.

items.statement: Second NDA molecule approval expected Q2/Q3 FY25; oncology oral liquid NDA approval expected Q4 FY25
items.quote: the second most important NDA molecule which Company had filed in the last financial year, we are likely to get approval for the same product in Q2/Q3 of FY25. Now, the third update is, there is one more NDA molecule which is the oncology oral liquid, for which our partner had filed this product in the US, which is in the oncology space specially in the oral liquid it is the first-of-its-kind US N

items.statement: New US MNC client secured for specialty polymers; initial sample order completed Q1, pilot quantity supplies expected Q2/Q3 FY25
items.quote: In Q1, we are happy to share that we could crack one more US MNC client, for which the initial sample order was successfully completed in Q1, and for which the order is already received for the pilot quantity, for which the supplies are expected to complete in Q2/Q3.

items.statement: Korean CDMO client GMP audit passed; confirmed as primary supplier for Phase-I/II supplies
items.quote: the Company could successfully finish the audit and now we are confirmed as a primary supplier currently for the client for the Phase-I and Phase-II supplies.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex spend Rs 58 crores including advances; full year capex guidance Rs 125 crores
items.quote: Our CAPEX for the 1st Quarter was Rs. 58 crores, which was again mainly driven by our investment in our Albumin facility that we are setting up.

items.statement: Tax rate for FY25 expected around 35%; Q1 higher due to intercompany interest structure being corrected
items.quote: Typically, our tax rates are in the region of about 35%-odd. For the quarter it has been on a bit higher side mainly on account of intercompany interest which has been there where the income is getting accrued in a higher tax Company as compared to the expenditure getting booked in a lower tax Company.

name: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd

items.statement: Overall consumption environment remained weak; apparel market impacted by subdued wedding season and prolonged heat wave reducing consumer activities
items.quote: As we look back at the first quarter of this fiscal, the overall consumption environment has remained weak. The apparel market, in particular, was further impacted by a subdued wedding season, prolonged heat wave, all of which have contributed to reduced consumer activities.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin expanded to 11.8% with EBITDA up 15% YoY; Lifestyle and Pantaloons saw margin expansion from gross margin improvement and cost control
items.quote: Company achieved consolidated EBITDA of INR406 crores with 11.8% margin. EBITDA increased 15% year-on-year in absolute terms. Both our established businesses, that is Lifestyle and Pantaloons witnessed margin expansion led by gross margin improvement and effective cost control measures.

items.statement: Revenue grew 7% YoY to INR3,428 crores; demerged ABFRL grew 26% YoY; ethnic and digital-first portfolio more than doubled revenues
items.quote: Our company delivered revenue of INR3,428 crores in this quarter, reflecting a growth of 7% over last year. The demerged ABFRL grew 26% Y-o-Y this quarter. Both our ethnic and digital-first portfolio together more than doubled their revenues led by organic as well as inorganic growth.

items.statement: TCNS merger approved by NCLT, awaiting court order; demerger filed with stock exchanges, targeting completion by end of FY25
items.quote: The amalgamation of TCNS with ABFRL is on track as the honourable NCLT has approved the merger. We are awaiting the court order and then we will work towards making this scheme effective. For demerger, we have filed the application with the stock exchanges and hopefully we'll be able to complete it within the timeline indicated earlier, that is by end of fiscal year '25.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands EBITDA margin expanded 50 bps to 18.8% led by cost optimization and better discount control
items.quote: Quarter revenue for the brand stood at INR1,482 crores. EBITDA margin expanded by 50 basis points to reach 18.8%, led by sustained cost optimization and better discount control.

items.statement: Pantaloons EBITDA margin expanded 470 bps to 17.6% driven by markdown management, cost control, and improved gross margins
items.quote: Pantaloons revenue grew by 5% Y-o-Y to INR1,100 crores Retail's like-to-like growth for the quarter was 2%. EBITDA margin expanded by 470 basis points to reach 17.6% led by markdown management and cost control measures.

items.statement: TMRW portfolio grew 2x YoY; added minority investment in Wrogn; portfolio includes large category-leading and mid-size emerging brands
items.quote: TMRW portfolio grew to 2x of last year as the brands continued to benefit from operational and business model announcements provided by the center of excellence. TMRW expanded its portfolio with minority investment in Wrogn.

items.statement: Anticipate improved demand environment during upcoming wedding and festive seasons; greater momentum shift expected in second half of the year
items.quote: As we look ahead, we anticipate an improved demand environment during the upcoming wedding and festive seasons that will hold us in a much stronger position to capture the opportunity in the market.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands same-store growth was low-single-digit negative primarily impacted by reduced wedding days and consumption occasions
items.quote: First question, low-single-digit negative, okay, for the quarter. Primarily impacted by wedding days. While definitely our suits and blazers business and categories which are more impacted by weddings, had that impact more. But overall itself consumption o ccasions had reduced

items.statement: Pantaloons margin improvement driven by gross margin enhancement from better quality product, intake margin, inventory management, lower markdowns, and higher private label share; cost rationalization marginal
items.quote: The bigger improvement in Pantaloons has happened through gross margin enhancement, through better quality product, better intake mar gin, superior inventory management leading to lower markdown and discounting and all this happening and increasing the share of private

items.statement: Consolidated PAT negative INR215 crores due to continued investment in TMRW and ethnic businesses; losses increased sequentially from TCNS and TMRW
items.quote: Company's consolidated PAT was negative INR215 crores, majorly on account of continued investment in TMRW and ethnic businesses.

items.statement: TCNS losses being wound down; most deep correction behind; expect TCNS EBITDA breakeven in H2 FY25; Tasva losses to continue for another year; designer labels profitable
items.quote: As far as TCNS is concerned, I think most of the big deep correction that we are doing in that business, is mostly behind us, maybe a quarter more or something. It's a business which in the second half of the year, we'll definitely see a much better and positive bottom line apart from an improved traction Aditya Birla Fashion and in top line

items.statement: Net debt approximately INR3,500 crores at end of Q1 FY25; equity raise planned post demerger to fund growth
items.quote: In 3 months, you want me to update. Okay, INR3,500 crores approximately.

items.statement: Bangladesh unrest not material; only 2-3% of overall sourcing from Bangladesh; no significant supply chain disruption
items.quote: No, it's not material. It's between 2% to 3% of our sourcing comes from there on an overall basis. So there might be individual business, some segment, a little bit of it. But at overall level, it's not significant for us.

items.statement: TCNS EBO count reduced to ~550-600 from 670-680; network rationalization largely complete; old inventory correction mostly done
items.quote: Yes. I think the number is in the range of 550 or something. Just around that. Closer to 600.

items.statement: TCNS gross margins expected to return to 65-67% range as old inventory cleared; EBITDA margin recovery depends on retail productivity improvement targeting FY26
items.quote: We would get to that because old inventory is behind us, new inventory is working well. The pricing power stays with the brand. So we expect the gross margins to the range that we had mentioned. I think EBITDA margin will be a function of retail productivity. And that's a project that is currently on way.

items.statement: TMRW portfolio at ~INR800 crores NSV run rate (INR1,000+ crores GMV); top 3 brands (Indian Garage, Bewakoof, USPL/Wrogn) to drive scale; acquisition engine paused to focus on profitability
items.quote: Just 3 of the big brands, which is The Indian Garage, Bewakoof, and the USPL, which is currently a minority investment, those 3 will be close to INR800 crores to INR900 crores and rest of the business would be close to INR200 crores. So that's the potential of just this portfolio.

items.statement: TMRW capital raise targeted ideally by end of FY25, but H1 FY26 also acceptable; acquisitions paused until fundraise completes
items.quote: Ideally would be end of this year, but first half of next year is also fine for us. Till then, therefore, our acquisitions as far as TMRW is concerned, will have to wait until the fundraise actually comes through.

items.statement: Value retail segment showing green shoots; lower price points performing better across Pantaloons and Peter England; Style Up traction strong though small
items.quote: Yes, yes, absolutely. And it's reflected in the numbers that you've seen and reported also. Style Up is still too small, but we are very excited by the traction that it's got. Pantaloons you have seen on a large scale is organic performance is looking much stronger.

items.statement: Inventory levels lower across all businesses; improved quality and freshness; increased product drop frequency; markdown needs reduced
items.quote: Across all businesses, our inventory is lower. In fact, wherever we are fixing the business also, a large part of that fix involves not just correcting for the inventory that is excess, but also Aditya Birla Fashion and ensuring and putting in systems that you don't fall into that again

items.statement: Real estate slightly easier with some softening from peak 2 years ago; talent market remains challenging
items.quote: Ashish, hard to answer directly, but simple answer is, yes, real estate does become slightly easier. I wouldn't say it's become dramatically easier. But yes, there are opportunities in real estate. But then you have to assess it against market realities. So talent, I think, is a different ball game altogether.

items.statement: Reebok at ~INR400 crores revenue with 170 stores; significant headroom for growth across retail, MBO, and e-commerce; targeting scale of INR1,500+ crores brands
items.quote: See, as you know, on Reebok, we have catching up to do. So there is a lot of headroom for growth. There are at least 3 brands in the business, which are INR1,500 crores plus in the segment. So we have catching up to do and we are doing that.

items.statement: Lifestyle Brands growth impacted by weak wedding season; premium brands suffer more on special occasions; Pantaloons caters to more regular occasions with 2% L2L growth
items.quote: The larger phenomenon in the market is that the premium brands are particularly bought for special locations, wedding being a very large part of it, but all other special occasions. This quarter being particularly slow either on festivals or in weddings, the premium brand demand has suffered more on a like-to-like basis as well in absolute terms.

items.statement: Athleisure category undergoing base correction post-COVID oversupply; worst may be behind but recovery timing uncertain; correction ongoing for 1-1.5 years across industry
items.quote: that's a more longer-term phenomenon. It's a base correction happening across the industry. Post COVID, there was a resurgence in the market, multiple brands, retail formats, from sportswear to casual brands to department store private labels. Almost everybody has created large range around it. Consumer also created and the demand equations were also higher. As recovery has happened, I think that

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance for FY25 maintained at 12% to 14% band
items.quote: Overall, we are in that band of 12% to 14%, which we have been guiding on the EBITDA margins, while continuing to grow our volumes, investing back in brand, a lot of digitization and transformation efforts which the company is embarking on.

items.statement: Annual capex guidance of INR 25 crore for lubricant business
items.quote: On a yearly basis, we have given a capex guidance of around INR 25 crore which is largely to get some filling lines and some auxillary.

items.statement: Core lubricant volumes grew 5.7% YoY to 37,000 kl in Q1 FY25, 2x industry growth of 3-4%
items.quote: Core volumes for Q1 FY '25 was INR 37,000 kl with a growth of 5.7% year -on-year. The factory fill segment was the only segment which probably saw some declin e around 10%, 11% due to a decline in production by some OEMs, which clearly is not in our control, but impacting our volumes slightly. Excluding factory fill, our growth is 2x of the

items.statement: AdBlue volumes grew 26% YoY to 38,000 kl in Q1 FY25
items.quote: AdBlue volume for the quarter has been 38,000 kl, which is roughly 26% growth over the last year same quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin improved ~200 bps YoY and ~50 bps QoQ; EBITDA grew 25% YoY to INR 116 crore
items.quote: You will also see from the result that we have grown our gross margin by nearly 200 basis points Y-o-Y over last year June quarter and eve n from March quarter, we have grown our gross margins by another 50 basis points nearly so that has translated into excellent EBITDA growth of 25% and profit after tax of 29% nearly

items.statement: EBITDA margin 13.1% in Q1 FY25 vs 13.5% in Q3/Q4 FY24 due to higher brand investment and freight/OEM royalties
items.quote: I think we spoke about EBITDA margins , while the gross margins have seen an im provement, we have invested back in the brand mo re because this being the IPL quarter as well and also, there has been increase in freight and some of the OEM royalties in line with our volume growth so that's the primary reason

items.statement: Exports now 6-7% of volumes, up from 4-5% three years ago, driven by OEM co-branded and Gulf branded products
items.quote: Yes, we used to be around 4%, 5%, if I recall 3 years ago, but now it has gone to 6%, 7% of our volumes, and we are seeing good traction in terms of export opportunities, especially with some of the OEM-related products, where the more the vehicles are exported by our OEMs, we on the back of that increase are also increasing our supplies to those geographies in terms of lubricant.

items.statement: Small retail price increase taken in mid-May after crude rose above $90; base oil follows with 1-2 month lag
items.quote: Yes,we took a small price increase in retail in mid-May. Obviously, it takes some time to realize the price increase,I think all the participants will recall that crude went above $90 in April and that's where base oil also follows with a lag of one month or so, and the price increase was taken in mid-May.

items.statement: If crude sustains below $80, input cost reduction may allow margin improvement or scheme adjustments
items.quote: As I mentioned in one of the previous questions that if the crude sustains for a reasonable period below $80 and all, there can be recalibration in some of the schemes and all, but that input cost also will come down with the lag base oil also reacts so we'll keep managing our margins to see that overall, we deliver what we are guiding.

items.statement: Premiumization drive across retail, OEM and industrial segments; premium products growing at 2x normal products
items.quote: Our endeavor is to certainly take up so if we are growing x in the normal products, we would like to grow at least 2x in these products. That's the norm.

items.statement: Distribution grew double-digit in Q1; commercial and personal mobility segments stood out
items.quote: We have seen our distribution also go up by double digit in this quarter and segments like commercial and personal mobility to stand out in terms of distribution growth this quarter.

items.statement: EV fluids supplied to 7-8 OEMs, targeting another 7-8 OEMs; volumes currently very small
items.quote: EVs, again, a very small segment in terms of volume so we are working. We've got about 7, 8 OEMs, looking to add another 7, 8 OEMs, it's not going to be major volum es, but we are there,I guess, for us, it is now just getting in with the OEM

items.statement: Sufficient blending capacity for next 2-3 years if plants run third shift; capex focused on filling lines and storage
items.quote: We have sufficient capacity for next 2, 3 years. If we run our plants on a third shift basis, especially from the blending side, so we may have to continue to add filling lines and some of the augmentation of storage area et cetera.

items.statement: EV investments total INR 150 crore across Tirex (51%), ElectreeFi (26%), Indra Technologies (7.5%)
items.quote: On the EV investment side, we have invested close to INR 150 crore in all the 3 investments put together and out of this Tirex transmission, which is a DC fast charger company, we have 51% stake, ElectreeFi, which is a software as a service company, we have 26% stake and Indra Technologies, which is a UK-based company manufacturing slow AC home chargers there, we have 7.5% stake from India balance

items.statement: AdBlue realization ~INR 50/litre with mid-single-digit margins; company holds ~20% market share
items.quote: Revenues are a function of the market. But on a ballpark basis, you can take INR 50 on an average realization and mid -single-digit margin profile is what we would say, for your understanding and competition.

items.statement: Cash and equivalents ~INR 850 crore at end of June; net cash ~INR 450 crore after short-term borrowings
items.quote: We continue to generate healthy cash and at the end of June, we are carrying nearly INR 850 crore of cash and our net cash also has gone up in terms of after removing some short-term borrowings, that is also now upwards of INR 450 crore.

items.statement: Final dividend of INR 20 per share approved, total FY24 dividend INR 36 including interim INR 16; AGM on 12th September
items.quote: You will all recall that the board had announced a final dividend of INR 20 in our earlier board meeting, which will be paid now after AGM, which is scheduled on 12th of September, so the dividend payout with the earlier interim dividend of INR 16 stands at INR 36 for the last year.

items.statement: AdBlue consumption mandatory for BS-VI diesel vehicles (~4% of diesel volume); no regulatory change expected to significantly alter volumes
items.quote: If you use 100 liters of diesel around 4% of AdBlue has to be used to meet these norms so this is a technical requirement for meeting the BS-VI standards in the industry.

items.statement: Industrial lubricants market share below 5%; growing double-digit due to low base and focus on product, service, technology
items.quote: We have an industrial business, which we sell direct to larger industries like JSW and steel plants, cement plants, thermal users. We have a distributor network which supplies industrial distributors, they are called and his is an area where our market share is below 5%. Just to clarify, our market share is below 5%. We know, obviously, as you know, industrial business and all these plants are goi

items.statement: Data center liquid cooling opportunity theoretical max 14 million litres (1% of non-process oil market) by 2025; product development underway, commercialization in few quarters
items.quote: If everything is to convert, it will be 14 million liters, which is not even 1% of this market outside the process oil which I give you, so if you look at that and the conversion has to happen only once data centers go to this new structure because even the high-power density servers, high compute applications, which will come in, this is a very good technology to help that, cooling off that high

items.statement: APT strategy: Accelerate (grow 2-3x industry), Premiumize (improve product mix), Transform (digital, EV charging, culture)
items.quote: we have internal ly spoken about a thing called Unlock 2.0, which is Accelerate, Premiumize and Transform. Acceleration for us means obviously, growing ahead of the industry in the core business as you look at the economy and really a lot happening around us, manufacturing led economy, it's a consumption economy. We continue that mantra

items.statement: Management expects to beat FY24 revenue growth of 10.4% in FY25 without price increases
items.quote: I think FY25, I told you last time we will try and beat the FY24 number. This quarter is 11.3, its better than 10.4%. I have a feeling we will continue to do better and then definitely beat 10.4% of last year.

items.statement: Long-term sustainable EBITDA margin guided around 27% due to ongoing investments
items.quote: On a longer term , we said in the last call around 27% kind of margins because we also are doing lot of investment s, we are going deeper, we are spending more and lot of new investments are required which will give obviously top line in a longer period

items.statement: Planning to establish 20 new labs primarily in Tier-3 and Tier-4 towns of North and East
items.quote: We are establishing 20 new labs to broaden our reach with plans to add more labs as the year progresses.

items.statement: Suburban integration progressing; full test menu now available through Suburban, IT integration ongoing
items.quote: From a test perspective, now the whole test menu, which Dr. Lal PathLabs operates is today available through Suburban as well. But having said that, there are certain background integration, IT integration work, which is still happening to make it even more seamless.

items.statement: Revenue grew 11.3% YoY to Rs. 602 crore in Q1 FY25 driven by patient and sample volume growth
items.quote: In Q1 FY25, we achieved a revenue of Rs. 602 crore, representing a 11.3% growth over Q1 last year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 28.2% in Q1 FY25, up from 27% in Q1 FY24; PAT margin at 17.9%
items.quote: EBITDA for Q1 FY25 came in at Rs. 170 crore v/s Rs. 146 crore in Q1 FY24, registered a growth of 16.2% with the EBITDA margin of 28.2%.

items.statement: No price increase taken since February 2023; revenue per patient growth driven by mix improvement
items.quote: We took last price increase, that was in February 2023, and we completed one full year of cycle of that in Feb '24 and we have not taken any price increase and neither we have intent to take as of now.

items.statement: Specialized tests contribute ~23% of revenue, up 1-1.5 percentage points YoY; Swasthfit contributes ~25% of revenue
items.quote: The specialized portfolio is again the way we define it, because specialized portfolio definition can vary from organization to organization, the way we define it, it currently contributes about 23% of our revenue v/s let's say similar period last year, the contribution would have grown by about 1-1.5% points.

items.statement: Patient volume grew 5.5% YoY and sample volume grew 9.6% YoY in Q1 FY25; patient visits up 10.4% QoQ
items.quote: Patient volume growth for Q1 FY25 is 5.5% and sample volume growth is 9.6% over Q1 Classification: Restricted FY24. Notably, we saw a 10.4% increase in patient numbers in Q1 FY25 as compared to Q4 FY24

items.statement: Swasthfit driven by preventive wellness awareness, channel expansion, and clinician prescription of packages; predominantly retail product
items.quote: First and foremost, there is this whole awareness amongst the public regarding doing preventive testing. The whole area in the metro cities as well as kind of approach that we put on online, etc., so there is a slice of that preventive wellness market that we see is helping Swasthfit growth.

items.statement: Unhealthy competitive practices like predatory pricing have eased; competition remains but has become healthier
items.quote: I think the spend to acquire customers, spend to actually just be visible anywhere and everywhere, that too has come down. I think the other intensity in terms of predatory pricing, this kind of promotion, this Rs. 199, Rs. 99 tests and all, all that actually also has gone away.

items.statement: Net cash and equivalents at Rs. 1,044 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Net cash and equivalents as on June 30th, 2024 is Rs. 1,044 crore.

items.statement: Board approved interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share for FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to announce that the board of directors has approved an interim dividend of Rs. 6 per share for FY25.

items.statement: Priority #1 for cash deployment is strategic acquisitions in South and West regions; Suburban acquisition in West already done
items.quote: Our priority #1 is to look for strategic assets, inorganic which are in South and West Region, in West we have done Suburban. If you look at contribution wise, region wise obviously South is still very weak. We would want to fill that gap.

items.statement: Suburban revenue grew ~8% YoY with EBITDA margin ~14%; core DLPL business grew ~13%
items.quote: Suburban revenue growth for this quarter is about 8% and EBITDA is about 14%.

items.statement: Investing in frontline manpower, sales and marketing expansion as part of growth investments
items.quote: And lastly, some of it will also go into our frontline, manpower, expansion in sales and marketing kind of areas.

items.statement: Effective tax rate of ~28% in Q1 impacted by deferred tax and Suburban depreciation; annualized rate unchanged
items.quote: There is the deferred tax and Suburban depreciation, which obviously has impacted. There is some adjustment on account of deferred tax. But on an average, this tax rate is not changing, if you will see annualized basis, I don't think there is a change in tax rate.

items.statement: Bundle testing packages discounted at 20-30% off MRP; test per patient not a specific operational target
items.quote: Generally, I mean these packages are discounted at a 20%-30% kind of discount on MRP and depending on the packages.

items.statement: Management expects next major growth inflection when new capacities come online in 2-3 years; near-term growth will be normal, double-digit year-on-year
items.quote: The next big inflection point will come when our capac ities come online. Until then, we will grow in line with the market and in line with our own efforts that we are putting in in terms of throughput maximization as well as quality of revenue

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex of INR 2.8 billion spent on Bangalore land purchase, maintenance, biomedical upgrades, interior transformation; full-year capex projected at INR 1500-1600 crore run rate for next 3 years
items.quote: We have incurred a capital outlay of INR 2.8 bill ion directed towards purchase of land in Bangalore for Greenfield expansion, regular maintenance, biomedical upgrades, and interior 3 transformation work within existing hospitals.

items.statement: Kolkata Greenfield first phase estimated at INR 950-1000 crore for 350 beds plus infrastructure for 1000 beds; Bangalore land cost ~INR 500 crore; construction start Kolkata end of Q3 FY25, Bangalore couple months later
items.quote: For the Kolkata Greenfield one, the first phase project estimate is almost around INR 1000 crores, which includes the building of around 350 beds in the first phase and there will be a lot of infrastructure development for the entire for the 1000 beds as well, but the first phase will cost around INR 950 crores. For the Bangalore land, cost will be around INR 500 crores.

items.statement: New Cayman hospital inaugurated July 2024 with 50 beds, daycare-focused; patient inflow expected before end of Q2 FY25; existing Cayman facility at saturation, new facility to unlock next growth wave
items.quote: We're delighted to share that our new hospital in Camana Bay was inaugurated in July, with patient inflow expected to start before the end of the second quarter.

items.statement: Kolkata Rajarhat Greenfield: 350 beds phase 1, up to 600 beds total in 2 phases; Bangalore: annex to cardiac building for advanced valve/aneurysm surgery, plus 1.5 acre HSR Layout land for ~200 bed greenfield extension
items.quote: For Kolkata, we have got land in Raja rhat. This is a new suburb of the city and there we bought a very large piece of land. We will make a very large hospital over there in faces. Indicatively, this could go up to about 600 beds but we will do it in 2 phases and plan the action accordingly.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 24.4% in Q1 FY25 vs 23.2% Q1 FY24; India EBITDA margin improved from 18.3% to 19.4% YoY; margin expansion driven by quality of revenue, bed mix upgrade, digital throughput
items.quote: Narayana Hrudayalaya generated a consolidated EBITDA of INR 3,274 million at a margin of 24.4% against 23.2% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 consolidated revenue INR 13,410 million, up 8.7% YoY, 4.8% QoQ despite seasonal weakness (summer, Eid, elections); HCCI revenue USD 32 million, up 4.8% YoY, 5.8% QoQ
items.quote: Consolidated revenue for the quarters to that INR 13,4 10 million reflecting a growth of 8.7% year-on-year and 4.8% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: India inpatient volumes flat last 3 quarters due to election impact, bed reconfiguration, payer mix shift; outpatient volumes growing; management expects normal double-digit revenue growth until new capacity comes online in 2-3 years
items.quote: The current growth will be normal growth and we will get the next point of inflection when our new capacities kick in, in few years from now.

items.statement: Cayman existing facility at saturation with mid-single digit growth; inpatient volumes declined -7% YoY, outpatient grew 6.5% YoY; new facility needed for next growth leap
items.quote: we have sort of reached a point of where we will not see double digit growth with just the existing facility and that's why about t wo and a half, three years ago, we started planning the new facility

items.statement: Not aggressive on pricing; peg services at slight discount to market; normalized prices between domestic and international patients; focus on quality of revenue over volume
items.quote: We've never in the recent, I mean, ever since a fe w years before COVID we have normalized the prices between domestic and international patients.

items.statement: International patients 7.6% of Q1 FY25 revenue, largely from Bangladesh; management consciously reducing reliance on medical tourism, expecting share to trend to zero over 5 years
items.quote: Consciously as a company we're moving away from a reliance on international medical tourism and more towards domestic patient s. So, this is the number over five years, we expect to go down to zero.

items.statement: Debtor days deteriorated 7-8 days QoQ due to election impact and government budget cycles; expected to recover next quarter; payable days currently elevated due to ERP migration, targeting 60-90 days
items.quote: Between Q4 of last year to Q1 of this year, we have deteriorated by about 7-8 days, which we will catch up in the next quarter.

items.statement: Payable days target 60-90 days; currently higher due to ERP migration lag; will normalize as migration completes
items.quote: Between 60-90 days is what we have negotiated with the payer. So, we will go back to those levels.

items.statement: Group cash and liquid investments INR 13.2 billion vs gross borrowing INR 14.75 billion; net debt INR 1.55 billion; net debt/equity 0.05; 80% of future capex to be debt-funded, leverage will increase
items.quote: The balance sheet and liquidity profile at the group level remains strong with group cash and liquid investments of over INR 13.2 billion against the gross borrowing of INR 14.75 billion, resulting in the net debt position of INR 1.55 billion as of 30th June 2024.

items.statement: No equity raise planned currently; sufficient cash and borrowing capacity; equity route only if ambitions exceed cash flow and borrowing capacity
items.quote: It's not something that we need to look at right now, given how under levered we are and how much cash we still have on the books.

items.statement: EWS bed reservation applies to 3 hospitals: Dharamshila Delhi (10%), SRCC Mumbai (10% Charity Commission), Guwahati (Assam scheme); small proportion of total beds
items.quote: That requirement only applies in some variation or the other to three of our hospitals. One is our Dharamshila hospital in East Delhi, where 10% of the beds need to be reserved for EWS category of patient.

items.statement: ARPOB annualized: India Q1 FY25 INR 15 million vs INR 13.6 million YoY; North region ARPOB ~INR 16.6 million annualized; management will share volume numbers and ARPOB calculation
items.quote: So, Q1 here it is 15 Mn and last year it was 13.6 Mn.

items.statement: Integrated Care revenue crossed INR 80 million in Q1 FY25, highest so far, with 51,000+ patient transactions across 8 clinics; cash burn continues as long-term venture
items.quote: Revenue for the quarter has crossed INR 80 million, which is the highest so far with more than 51,000 patient transaction across 8 clinics.

items.statement: Launched Narayana Health Insurance in Mysore (Aditi product: INR 1 crore surgery cover for ~INR 10,000 family of 4); INR 100 crore capital committed; narrow network, underwriting at acceptance, free physical exam; breakeven timeline prematu
items.quote: I'm pleased let you know that we launched Na rayana Health Insurance in Mysore ass we have said in late June with our first product it's called Aditi, the headline feature which is providing 1 crore cover for surgeries for a price of about ₹10,000 for a family of four.

items.statement: Administrators assessed on 80-20 fixed-variable pay structure tied to financial parameters, cost control, digitization, length of stay reduction, throughput improvement
items.quote: At the senior levels, they have a 80-20 fixed to variable pay structure which incentives them towards that.

items.statement: Digital initiatives: AI auto discharge summaries, NAMAH app AI alerts, Virtual Tumor Board, revamped digital appointment system (60%+ consultations digital), ATHMA in ER reduced ALOS by 50%
items.quote: Deployment of Athma in Emergency Department has reduced the ALOS by 50% in the emergency room by digitizing all the time-consuming documentation process.

items.statement: Lease liability: equipment finance leases unwinding as tenure completed (biomedical equipment); rental expense down from INR 235 cr to INR 195 cr YoY; most unwinding done, slight further decline then normalize; new equipment leases will inc
items.quote: Yes, correct. We have paid those. We have completed the lease tenure and completed the payouts. We own these assets now and that is why the unwinding of the lease charges have happened.

items.statement: Cayman new facility will have initial operational losses and margin dilution due to high fixed costs; quantum not quantified; existing facility occupancy to increase meaningfully once new facility operational as they function as two campuse
items.quote: Initially there will be obviously, certainly margin dilution and operational losses. We are not in a position to, you know to give out a particular number or a hard value to quantify that.

items.statement: Tax rate steady state ~13% (Q1 FY25); FY24 11.13% included one-time deferred tax credit from regime change; rate varies with India/Cayman profit mix
items.quote: If you see, last year in the 1st quarter was 10.6pc. 2nd and 3rd quarters were 8.7 and 9.8. For the full year, last year we were at 11.13pc. That was the effect of the deferred tax credit that came in in last year.

items.statement: IndAS 116 impact Q1 FY25: EBITDA increased by INR 148.7 million, PAT decreased by INR 19 million on like-to-like basis
items.quote: Our EBITDA will increase by, because of IndAS our EBITDA has increased by INR 148.7 million, and our PAT has decreased by INR 19 million for Q1 FY25 on a like to like basis.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 6-8% for FY25
items.quote: Yes, fixed rate percent. Yes, that remains. That remains.

items.statement: EBITDA per metric ton guidance maintained at INR20,500-21,500 for FY25
items.value: INR20,500 to INR21,500 per metric tonne
items.quote: We increased the guidance last quarter to INR20,500 to 21,500 per metric tonne. So the industry builds on that as a volume growth plus increase in EBITDA means that we have more amount of specialties that should contribute, which we said should happen from H2, that the rational, we increased it. And we continue with the same guidance.

items.statement: Volume growth of 8% YoY and QoQ in Q1 FY25 across all regions and segments
items.quote: While overall volume growth stood at 8%, sequentially as we ll as year-on-year, we saw growth in our EBITDA

items.statement: India grew 2% in Q1 with strong May-June after slow April; rural demand recovery expected
items.quote: Starting with India, which grew by 2% in this quarter. While this happen to be relatively slower compared to double-digit growth we have seen in the last 4 years, this comes on the back of a relatively slower April that we had before for an extremely strong May and June.

items.statement: Rest of World grew 24.5% in Q1 driven by Europe and Latin America; strong double-digit growth expected
items.quote: This quarter saw our company growing by 24.5% in rest of the world markets driven by strong growth seen in Europe and Latin America. We strongly believe the momentum in masstige categories should translate to strong double-digit growth for these markets.

items.statement: EBITDA per metric ton at INR20,197 in Q1, slightly below guided range of INR20,500-21,500
items.quote: the EBITDA for per metric ton came in at INR20,197 per metric ton, slightly below the guided band of INR20,500 to INR21,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Higher supply chain costs across all locations caused EBITDA per ton to miss guided range
items.quote: Higher supply chain costs across all locations contributed towards this being lower than the guided range of INR20,500 per metric ton.

items.statement: Specialty ingredients contribution improvement expected from H2 to drive EBITDA per ton to higher end of guidance
items.quote: we expect the speciality ingredients to start catching up from the H2 of this year. So we continue to remain consistent on that. And we do hope that once that happens, we should see the EBITDA per metric ton also trending towards the higher end of the guide.

items.statement: Surfactants grew 5.4% and specialties grew 13.3% in Q1; specialty growth partly from restocking (~40%)
items.quote: Even segmentally while our performance of surfactants grew at 5.4%, specialties driven by masstige recorded 13.3% growth.

items.statement: ~40% of specialty growth attributed to restocking; balance from new business wins
items.quote: I think about 40% of this can be attributed to the stocking of -- the restocking, as I can call it. The balance is in terms of certain geographies where we also got some newer businesses.

items.statement: Specialty capacity expansion under implementation, targeting commissioning by end of FY25; more on drawing board
items.quote: So there is one which is already under implementation and execution. I think we're looking at getting it commissioned by end of this financial year. And there is something more that is on the drawing board which we are working on.

items.statement: Capacity expansion across mild surfactants, non-toxic preservatives, high-end emollients and emulsifiers via debottlenecking and brownfield investments
items.quote: it can be effective, which one it will be. Because many of the high-end formulations will require both mild surfactants and non-toxic preservatives. And high-end emollients, okay, and emulsifiers. So this is something that will be across. So we may not be able to very clearly demarcate to say as to which will be the sort of capacity that will get set up. Because some of them will be debottling, so

items.statement: Lauryl alcohol prices up ~10% QoQ in Q1 and ~30% in last month; palm, soya, oil complex all up
items.quote: See lauryl-alcohol prices have been -- it's been -- it is only increasing, in fact, increased by about 10% compared to the previous quarter in this quarter. But if you see the last one month, it has gone up significantly, aided by the increase in the oil price. So it's like -- it's going to be another about 30% in just about 30 days.

items.statement: Freight cost increases passed on to customers with lag; DDP shipments lower in Q1 reducing other expenses
items.quote: So typically, there are some -- the DDP shipments were lower within this quarter, then the revenue, the DDP costs are much higher than CIF freight costs. So that can be the only explanation for that, nothing else.

items.statement: Logistics cost pass-through ongoing; shipping companies indicate stabilization from October
items.quote: I only -- as I said earlier, that in October, the shipping companies tell us that things would start stabilizing. So till that time, we would like to find ways to ensure that we can engage with the customers and that we can judiciously pass on the increases.

items.statement: Raw material arrivals severely impacted by Red Sea crisis; containers arriving 30-40 days late
items.quote: Because of the red issue, the incoming raw materials were severely impacted. In fact, we have containers coming almost 30, 40 days after the schedule date of our arrival.

items.statement: Container unavailability, port congestion, elongated lead times and rationalized raw material availability impacted volumes
items.quote: Unavailability of containers, port congestion and some of the major ports in the world, combined with higher lead times and rationalized availability of raw materials, adversely impacted the volumes in this quarter.

items.statement: Premium specialty growth driven by preservatives, mild surfactants, non-toxic preservatives and new product launches
items.quote: Actually, it's a combination. It's not just one of it. So we have preservatives. We have mild surfactants. We have our non-toxic preservatives, okay? And also some of the new products that we launched; we are seeing some early victories.

items.statement: Premium specialty products include high-end cleansing bars, solid shampoo bars, moisturizing creams, safe preservatives, natural ingredients
items.quote: No, you're talking about say, high-end cleansing solutions. We're looking at high-end cleansing bars, you're looking at, say, solid format shampoo bars. We're looking at high-end skin moisturizing creams, which require better emollients and high-end emollients. We're looking at certain formulations that require safe preservatives, natural ingredients or ingredients with more naturalized index and

items.statement: Customer projects for premium specialties suspended during destocking now recommencing; expected to aid H2 specialty volumes
items.quote: What had happened, Sanjesh, was only about last 12, 15 months, because of the cutback in demand that happened in the U.S. and Europe, the destocking and all that led to many of our customers where we have started certain projects in pipeline for our new products, they have suspended work on this because they were finding that the demand itself has gone to -- so that has started, that has recommenc

items.statement: FMCG customers taking price cuts, grammage increases, buy-one-get-one offers; volume-led growth returning
items.quote: all the FMCG companies have started taking price cuts, various prices only over the last -- probably most of it happened in the last quarter, very significantly. So now that should start sanctioning demand because good demand from both rural and urban, okay?

items.statement: No business impact from Unilever reducing palm oil content; Galaxy supplies syndet soaps not traditional soaps
items.quote: So we don't cater into soaps. What we do is -- Syndet soap is a specialty for us, which is synthetic detergent soap. So it has nothing to do with what Unilever announced in terms of reducing the farm content by 25%. So there is no connection with our business.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis causing longer routes via Cape of Good Hope, container shortages, port congestion, freight rate increases
items.quote: This is essentially the Red Sea crisis started in November when we had skipped going through the Red Sea. So we skipped Suez Canal there to go through the Cape of Good Hope. So we have ships taking more time to get to their destination. So cont ainers also took more time to come

items.statement: Supply chain deterioration is key risk; if situation doesn't worsen, volume growth momentum should sustain
items.quote: The supply chain situation, though not improving, at least should not deteriorate. If it doesn't deteriorate today, we don't see any reason why we can't have a good volume growth next quarter as well.

items.statement: Feedstock price volatility risk; robust raw material management framework in place to manage open positions
items.quote: That's why it's very critical where we need to have a very robust raw material management framework in place, which we have. So we're ensuring that we have the right buying down, the timing of the buying and the quantum of buying to take care of this price volatility.

items.statement: FY25 revenue expected similar to FY24 level
items.quote: on an overall year basis -- FY '25 basis, we are fairly hopeful and comfortable that we should be able to do a similar level as FY '24 on an annual basis

items.statement: PAT margin target 7-7.5% short-to-midterm
items.quote: we will have a PAT margin in the range of 7% to 7.5% on a short-to-midterm perspective

items.statement: Core EBITDA margin expected at FY23-24 level for FY25, may dip few bps in FY26
items.quote: for this particular year and most of the next year, we should be within the range of 6.5% to 7%, 7.5%

items.statement: Order book INR 26,000 cr as of 30 June 2024, 51% competitive, 91% domestic
items.quote: The order book of the company as at 30 June 2024 stood at about INR 26,000 crores, wherein about 51% orders are on competitive basis and balance on nomination. In terms of the domestic international split, it is about 91:9

items.statement: Q1 order inflow INR 1,000 cr; expect INR 4,000-5,000 cr by Q2; full year target INR 10,000-12,000 cr
items.quote: order inflow that we've had in Q1 is about INR 1,000 crores. We hope to get another INR 4,000 crores to INR 5,000 crores by Q2. And overall as we have been maintaining, we should be getting order book in the range of INR 10,000 crores to INR 12,000 crores for the full year

items.statement: Bid pipeline INR 20,000-25,000 cr in Q1; INR 15,000-18,000 cr opened, 50-50 rail-road mix
items.quote: we have bid to the extent of about INR 20,000 crores to INR 25,000 crores. And wherein the indicative bids that have been opened until now, approximately out of that INR 25,000 crores is around INR 15,000 crores to INR 18,000 crores

items.statement: Q2 expected mild due to monsoon; post-election tendering pickup expected in rail and highway
items.quote: we do expect Q2 to be mild because of the monsoon and extraneous factors. But on an overall year basis -- FY '25 basis, we are fairly hopeful and comfortable that we should be able to do a similar level as FY '24 on an annual basis

items.statement: May take margin hit on competitive bids but avoid loss-making projects; industry average ~5%
items.quote: industry average typically right now is in the range of about 5%. And let us see how we are able to secure around it

items.statement: Targeting niche complex projects (tunnels, bridges) to maintain margins; using tie-ups
items.quote: there are certain projects where there are niche areas such as tunnels, bridges and some complexities. Where we feel the competition is going to be less, especially if the size of those opportunities are large

items.statement: Government stopped nomination-based orders in railways; only competitive bidding going forward
items.quote: as a matter of principle, government has stopped giving any business on nomination in railway sector. And that's been stopped for quite a while now

items.statement: Targeting railway EPC, road EPC, and PPP projects in roads

items.quote: typically, we would be probably in the range of 8.2%-8.25%. We would be looking at an incremental cost of that.

items.quote: The mix of home loans versus non-home loans stood at 75% and 25% respectively.

items.statement: Write-offs at INR7-9 crores in Q1 FY25
