items.statement: Plan 75 new branches over next couple of years: 25 in existing locations, 50 in deeper impact strategy
items.quote: As we go ahead, next couple of years, we will keep introducing 75 new branches. 25 of those will come in the existing locations. And 50 will come in the deeper impact strategy that I spoke about.

items.statement: Incremental ticket size: home loans INR13 lakhs, non-home loans INR8.2 lakhs
items.quote: Housing loan incremental ticket size is 13 lakhs and non-housing stands at 8.2 lakhs.

items.statement: Sourcing mix: 55% in-house, 35% corporate DSA, 45% overall external channels
items.quote: the breakdown of the sourcing mix stands at broadly 45% comes from overall external channels. The corporate DSA contributes about 35% and the balance 55% is all in-house.

items.statement: Dr. Punita Kumar Sinha inducted as independent director effective 7 Aug 2024, subject to AGM approval
items.quote: Dr. Punita Kumar Sinha has been inducted as an independent director on our board with effect from 7th August 2024, subject to approval of the AGM.

items.statement: ROE at 4.1% pre-IPO proceeds; 15.9% post-IPO proceeds
items.quote: Our ROE, post receipt of IPO proceeds stands at 15.9%.

items.statement: Management cannot forecast future quarterly performance or simulate Q1 to Q4 trends
items.quote: From Q1 to Q4 last year, what you saw, whether you can use that as a yardstick to project you into Q4 this year. Unfortunately, my capabilities and knowledge do not lie in that area, I'm not able to help you there.

items.statement: Registered investors grew 51% from 12.1 crore to 18.4 crore UCC
items.quote: When I joined BSE, registered investors based on Unique Client Code UCC, stood at INR 12.1 crores, which has increased to INR 18.4 crores as on date, a growth of 51%.

items.statement: Cash segment average daily turnover more than doubled to INR 9,006 crores
items.quote: BSE's average daily turnover in the cash segment for Q1 FY 2025 stands at INR 9,006 crores as compared to INR 4,025 crores in the same quarter last year on account of a buoyant market.

items.statement: Sensex derivatives hit record 54 crore contracts traded with notional turnover of INR 432 lakh crores
items.quote: It also gives me great pleasure to inform you that Sensex derivatives continues to grow and broke its record on 26 July 2024, at more than 54 crores contracts traded representing a notional turnover of INR 432 lakh crores.

items.statement: Bankex derivatives hit record 25.9 crore contracts traded with notional turnover of INR 230 lakh crores
items.quote: The Bankex contracts have also generated significant interest since its expiry date changed to Monday from October 16, 2023, by creating a new record on 29th July 2024, with 25.9 crores contract traded representing a notional turnover of INR 230 lakh crores.

items.statement: Single stock derivatives launched July 2024 with 155 members in futures and 35 in options
items.quote: BSE forayed into single stock derivatives space with effect from 1st July 2024, with a mid-month expiry for the second Thursday of the month. So far, 155 members have participated in single stock futures and 35 single stock options.

items.statement: Net profit attributable to shareholders INR 265 crores up 253% YoY excluding CDSL stake sale
items.quote: The net profit attributable to shareholders as the company stands at INR 265 crores, up from INR 75.1 crores, excluding CDSL Stake Sale, a growth of 253%.

items.statement: Redesigning derivatives charge structure to uniform per-unit pricing per SEBI 'true to label' circular
items.quote: BSE is also in the process of redesigning the existing charge structure which will be uniform for all the members in the equity derivatives segment to confirm the SEBI circular stating the market infrastructure institutions have to be true to label.

items.statement: Regulatory charge INR 1,200 per crore, clearing and settlement charge INR 1,200-1,300 per crore on premium turnover
items.quote: See around INR 1,200 crores to INR 1,300 per crores, INR 1,200 crores is the regulatory charge. That is very clear. INR 1,300 to INR 1,200 is the clearing and settlement charges that we pay.

items.statement: SEBI consultation papers on derivatives framework, interest income on collateral, and MII charges under review; feedback deadline August 20, 2024
items.quote: SEBI has constituted the expert working group on the topic, which you mentioned about derivatives, which confabulated and gave their thoughts to the regulators which was discussed in committee called Secondary Markets Advisory Committee and the public consultation paper has been published by SEBI, requesting for views from the market till August 20, 2024.

items.statement: No regulatory target set for F&O SGF contribution yet; regulator reviewing adequacy based on risk analysis
items.quote: I would like to clarify to you that we do not, at this point of time, have any regulatory targets stipulated to us in terms of SGF requirement, from F&O. That is a first clarification.

items.statement: Treasury income on clearing funds INR 62 crores; only excess unutilized collateral may need interest pass-through per consultation paper
items.quote: The total number is INR 62 crores, which is coming out of the treasury income of ICCL. That is the number I can say.

items.statement: Submitted representations to SEBI on turnover fee matter; awaiting response, provision already made in prior quarter
items.quote: We always do what we promise to do and keeping up our promise, we have had detailed discussions and we have submitted our submissions to the kind review of the regulators.

items.statement: Investing in StAR MF scalability and functionality; launching StAR MF 2.0 this quarter
items.quote: Given the growth, we are going to continue investing in StAR MF and improve it in terms of scalability, functionality, order processing and introduce a new platform called StAR MF 2.0 this quarter.

items.statement: 430+ members trading BSE derivatives representing 47 lakh active clients since relaunch
items.quote: Since relaunch, more than 430 members have traded the BSE derivatives representing around 47 lakh active clients.

items.statement: Currency segment SGF surplus exists; reversal requires regulatory discussion
items.quote: The fact that the regulatory -- the earlier regulatory clarification has resulted in not being any volumes in currency segment, and therefore, the need for the settlement guarantee fund coming down is well known and highly appreciated. But to take back that money and reuse it elsewhere as part of settlement guarantee fund would require regulatory discussions.

items.statement: Regulatory changes may impact derivatives volumes but also create new opportunities; BSE will adapt and restrategize
items.quote: Every emerging regulatory and business environment is new, and therefore, the regulatory changes when they impact existing paradigm invokes a sense of concern at times. But what we need to notice, they also provide newer opportunities.

items.statement: Primary market capital raising INR 7.7 lakh crores via equity, debt, bonds, commercial papers
items.quote: BSE platforms continue to remind the preferred choice by Indian companies to raise capital by enabling issuers to raise INR 7.7 lakh crores by means of equity, debt, bonds, commercial papers, et cetera.

items.statement: StAR MF revenue up 101% YoY to INR 48 crores
items.quote: BSE StAR MF delivered yet another year of record revenues and performance, up 101% year-on-year to reach INR 48 crores.

items.statement: Clearing and settlement operational revenue up 40% to INR 33.8 crores
items.quote: The clearing and settlement operational revenues increased by 40% to INR 33.8 crores from INR 24.1 crores.

items.statement: Treasury income from clearing and settlement funds up 179% to INR 62 crores
items.quote: Treasury income from clearing and settlement funds has increased by 179% to INR 62 crores from INR 22.2 crores.

items.statement: Investment income up 43% to INR 62.9 crores
items.quote: Investment income increased by 43% to INR 62.9 crores from INR 44 crores.

items.statement: CloudTech expected to contribute 20-30% of total revenue
items.quote: But at the same time, if you look at the overall sector, we have CloudTech business between 20% to 30% of total revenue count.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 14.85% in Q1 FY25, up 329 bps QoQ
items.quote: Additionally, our EBITDA margin for Q1 FY25 stands at an impressive 14.85%, marking a substantial enhancement of 329 basis points from the previous quarter.

items.statement: Total addressable market over a trillion dollars growing at double-digit CAGR
items.quote: So, this total addressable market is over a trillion-dollar industry, okay. Considering that, there is lot of potential within India as well as in the international market.

items.statement: Six platforms across MadTech and CloudTech driving diversification
items.quote: So, under the umbrella, like I said, we have two major sub segments, MadTech and CloudTech. Definitely that's one side of the diversifications what we have built.

items.statement: Himalaya campaign reached 134 million audiences in 60 days
items.quote: The company spearhead a groundbreaking influencer campaign for Himalaya Turmeric Face Care range, reaching an impressive 134 million, that is 13.4 crore audiences with just 60 days averaging around 22 million per day.

items.statement: Happilo campaign on Zomato achieved over 100K coupon redemptions
items.quote: Vertoz also executed a highly successful campaign on Zomato for Happilo, a leading health food brand, resulting in over 100K coupons redemption.

items.statement: IncrementX partnered with Loop Media for CTV and DOOH monetization
items.quote: Moreover, Vertoz's IncrementX division partnered with Loop Media to elevate monetization for connected TV, CTV, digital out of home advertising.

items.statement: Investments primarily in intangible tech products and media platforms
items.quote: So being as a technology company, most of our investments are in the intangible, which is in tech products, intangible products, but consisting of the media properties and the platforms what we have built.

items.statement: Very minuscule debt, funded mainly through internal accruals
items.quote: There is a very minuscule amount of the debt. It's usually the accrued earnings what we have.

items.statement: Revenue grew 77.40% YoY to Rs 60.17 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We are pleased to report that our revenue for Q1 Financial Year '25 soared to Rs. 60.17 crore reflecting an exceptional growth of 77.40% year-on-year over year.

items.statement: PAT increased 61.94% YoY to Rs 5.74 crore in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our profit after tax, PAT, for quarter one Financial Year '2025 reached Rs. 5.74 crore, representing a remarkable 61.94% year-over-year increase.

items.statement: Expanding US presence to capture larger market share
items.quote: Particularly, our expansion efforts in the United States have been significant, aiming to capture a large share of this crucial market and unlock new growth opportunities.

items.statement: Focus on self-improvement rather than external competitors
items.quote: So generally, we always believe that our biggest competition is we ourselves where we have to keep expanding our site.

items.statement: Thanked team for untiring efforts and hard work
items.quote: I thank the entire team of Vertoz for this untiring efforts, hard work, and dedication, digitized the company forward through the various market conditions.

items.statement: FY25 budgeted capex over ₹4,500 crores, with ₹3,000 crores (66%) for growth capex in new businesses
items.quote: On the capex front, we continue to focus on growth capex for FY'25 budgeted capital expenditure is over ₹4,500 crores, of which growth capex in new businesses is planned at ₹3,000 crores, which is 66% of the total capital expenditure.

items.statement: UltraTech added 8.7 million tons capacity in Q1 FY25, reaching 155 million tons total capacity
items.quote: For this year, out of plan ned 16 million tons capacity, we have already added 8.7 million tons in Q1 FY '25, crossing milestone of 150 million tons per annum, reaching a total capacity with the domestic and overseas totaling to 155 million tons per annum

items.statement: Paints capex ₹10,139 crores excludes working capital
items.quote: Yes. Navin. So, ₹10,139 crores, I think is the number is the capex only, which, of course, includes the IDC, the tinting machines, the IT system, everything. Working capital is not included. Okay.

items.statement: Birla Pivot quarterly revenue run rate over ₹550 crores with increasing buyer trends
items.quote: Revenue of our B2B e -commerce business, Birla Pivot is gradually ramping up. The current quarterly run rate of revenue is over ₹550 crores with increasing trends in total number of buyers.

items.statement: Birla Pivot targets $1 billion revenue in three years
items.quote: Our aspiration that we had announced in the last quarte r was to reach $1 billion in three years' time span. Our internal markets are pointing towards that, and we are in the right direction in achieving that goal

items.statement: Renewable energy capacity to double from 1 GW to 2 GW by end of FY25, then add 1 GW annually for 2-3 years
items.quote: So, I think we have earlier also shared this that firstly, we aim to double the capacity by this financial year, okay? And the projects are already under implementation. So from 1 -GW to 2-GW in this financial year, and then our aim is to add maybe 1-gigawatt every year for next 2, 3 years, depending upon the tenders or the bids, which we can successfully bid for.

items.statement: Birla Opus commercial production started at 3 plants in April 2024, Chamarajanagar trial run started, Mahad in Q3 and Kharagpur in Q4 FY25
items.quote: Paints business under brand Birla Opus has started its commercial production at 3 plants in April 2024 and more than 80% ra nge of 145 planned products have been placed in the distribution channels. Construction at other two plants is progressing as per plans and remains and exp

items.quote: Our CSF volumes stood at highest levels of quarterly number of 200 tons and revenue stood at highest levels since past 7 quarters.

items.quote: Improved caustic reductions, coupled with uptick in demand and realization for chlorine derivati ves had led to improvement in eco realizations, which stood at ₹32,529 for Q1 FY '25, highest since Q2 FY '24.

items.quote: Chlorine is a somewhat different story because chlorine is more domestic. As you know, one of our competitors have guided significant capacity in Gujarat, without an integration. So chlorine for sure is under downward pressure. So, ECU could be flat to slightly rise.

items.statement: Specialty chemicals now contribute 30% of chemical business revenue, highest ever sales volume and revenue
items.quote: We have clocked highest ever sales volume and revenue for the specialty chemical business, which now contributes 30% to the chemical business revenue.

items.statement: UltraTech approved purchase of 32.72% equity stake in India Cements at ₹390/share for ₹3,954 crores, triggering mandatory open offer
items.quote: UltraTech will pay ₹3,954 crores at ₹390 per share for by this 32.72% stake in ICL from the promoter and their associates. This has triggered a mandatory open offer at ₹390 per share, which would be done after obtaining all regulatory approvals.

items.statement: Q1 operating cash flows much higher than EBITDA due to working capital management, but will reverse in Q2
items.quote: In this quarter, Q1 specifically, our operating cash flows are much higher than the EBITDA for the quarter because of the working capital management. Of course, that is not a permanent kind of thing. It will get reversed in the Q2.

items.statement: VSF margins expected to remain range-bound
items.quote: Range bound, that is what the best assessment.

items.statement: Birla Opus in investment mode, losses to continue in FY25, targeting profitability after third year of full operation
items.quote: So we are in investment mode. And like we said, we are looking at a three-year picture, where after the third year of full operation, we will be positive. So I think that's what we should continuously aim for.

items.statement: Birla Pivot gross margins 1.5-4% across categories, losses not very large as business scales
items.quote: You see, the gross margins, as we have earlier said, will be in the range of about 1.5% to 4% in different product categories, okay. So that is the situation as far as gross margins are concerned. But yes, since the team building, and the business investment activity is going on so initially, there are losses, not very large numbers to be I mean, discussed to you.

items.statement: Aditya Birla Capital lending portfolio surpassed ₹125,000 crores and AUM surpassed ₹500,000 crores
items.quote: Total lending portfolio and average assets under management have also surpassed milestones of ₹125,000 crores and ₹5,00,000 crores, respectively, in the current quarter.

items.statement: Aditya Birla Capital launched ABCD digital platform with 20+ products, over 1,500 branches across businesses
items.quote: While the company continues to expand its physical footprint, a total of over 1,500 branches across businesses, the endeavour remains on digital first approach, under this line, Aditya Birla Capital has commercially launched its B2C platform, the Aditya Birla Capital Digital, ABCD, offering over 20 products and services catering to each facet of financing solutions such as payments, loans, insuran

items.statement: Geopolitical conflicts in Middle East and Ukraine remain major risks, inflation persistence leading to high interest rates
items.quote: Conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine remain major risk, inflation persistence is leading to continued high interest rates by major central banks.

items.statement: Chemicals outlook depends on Chinese consumer demand and global supply chain stability amid Middle East crises
items.quote: With the disclaimer that a lot will depend upon what happens with the Chinese consumer and nothing funny should happen either in the global supply chain because of the crises in the Middle East.

items.statement: Birla Opus dealer adoption strong, over 102 depots operational covering pan-India including North-east, targeting 50,000 active dealers by year-end
items.quote: We had talked about reaching 150 depots by the end of the year. We are already beyond 102. We have talked about reaching 50,000 dealers. We are in sync with the plan to hit 50,000 active dealers by the end of the year

items.statement: Birla Opus retail sellout exceptional, inventory at stores small part of sold volume, tinting machine data provides real-time demand insights
items.quote: Our retail audit of stores where we have gone and seen stocks sold till date and taken inventory of stocks lying in the store, suggest that the inventory lying in the store is a small part of what we have sold till now, which means majority of it has been sold out.

items.statement: Hydrogen sales approximately 10-25% of production, rest captive consumption or process venting
items.quote: I think you can r oughly assume that approximately 10% to a quarter of our hydrogen is towards external sales. And rest is towards either captive consumption or maintaining process stability

items.statement: Chlorine derivatives split: 40% water treatment, 30-35% industrial, 25% plasticizers/PVC additives, 10-15% specialty (refrigerants, pharma, agrochemicals)
items.quote: So I'll give you a rough assumption breakout, right? So assume around 40% for water treatment. Between 30%, 35% for what we would call the industrial users. We have about a quarter in plasticizers and PVC additives. And then maybe close to 10%, 15% in real ly speciality things like refrigerants, pharma, agrochemicals

items.statement: Paints trial production revenue goes to CWIP for 3-4 months per plant, commercial revenue only post-capitalization
items.quote: Every plant, which is launched will have a 3 -month period of trial production average. I'm just giving average. So that is the only number that we have to see. So the three plants, which were 30th of April that was announced, most of their production, which has happened after 30th of April are on commercial production, their sale has already started to take place in quarter 2 and quarter 3. Chama

items.statement: Net debt increased ₹330 crores sequentially despite ₹1,000 crores capex spend due to strong working capital cash generation
items.quote: Yes. So, working capital management of our existing business has been able to generate some cash flows. So that has, I mean, led to the lower bad debt increases, okay? So, in this quarter, Q1 specifically, our operating cash flows are much higher than the EBITDA for the quarter because of the working capital management.

items.statement: Birla Opus targeting high single-digit market share exit by FY25 end
items.quote: And you're still maintaining the high single -digit market share exit target, right, for FY '25

items.statement: Underlying volume growth of 9.6% in Q1 FY25; C&B grew 8%, B2B grew 18%
items.quote: For the quarter, we reported underlying volume growth of 9.6% with Consumer and Bazaar (C&B) businesses growing UVG by 8%, whereas our Business to Business (B2B) businesses reported strong UVG of 18%, driven by both domestic and export segments.

items.statement: VAM consumption price averaged $1,022/ton in Q1 FY25 vs $1,137/ton in Q1 FY24
items.quote: VAM consumption in the quarter was $1,022 a ton versus $1,137 in the same period last year.

items.statement: Working capital in absolute terms lower than March 2024, resulting in strong cash flows
items.quote: The working capital situation remained healthy, and in absolute terms, was lower than March '24, which resulted in strong cash flows.

items.statement: Kerala market soft with demand issues; magnitude may differ by company
items.quote: Yes, Kerala vis-à-vis other markets has been soft. There is clearly an issue of demand in Kerala vis-à-vis the normal buoyant conditions.

items.statement: Exterior new product piloted; in Southern Europe such products are 15-20% of exteriors market
items.quote: If you look at markets like Southern Europe, whether you look at France or you look at Italy or you look at Spain, this is like up to 15% to 20% of the exteriors market.

items.statement: No significant pricing rollbacks in Q1; further cuts depend on input price reductions
items.quote: As of now, in the first quarter, we have not taken any significant pricing rollbacks. What you are seeing is really the impact of what we have done over the course of all of last year.

items.statement: Current VAM price fluctuating between $850 and $1,000 per ton due to force majeure at a major producer
items.quote: Currently, the VAM price is fluctuating because one of the big guys had a force majeure, so on. I would say it's between $850 and $1,000 depending on where you are.

items.statement: Rural (Emerging India) growth outpacing urban for 8th consecutive quarter; 14,000 Pidilite Ki Duniyas covering 28,000 villages
items.quote: And now you would see this is the eighth quarter where we have had double-digit growth in rural India. So as far as we are concerned, all the efforts and the focus that we have put in, I mean, to give you a little statistics, we now have 14,000 Pidilite Ki Duniyas, where now currently in a situation where villages below 10,000, we are now covering about 28,000 villages directly.

items.statement: Capex to be 3-5% of sales annually while maintaining double-digit growth ambition; asset turnover to normalize over 2-3 years
items.quote: We are now in a stable equilibrium place, where you will find us spend capex between 3% to 5% of sales every year as long as we maintain our double-digit growth ambition.

items.statement: Capacity utilization between 70-75%; 20 plants undergoing brownfield expansion
items.quote: To give you back of the envelope, we remain between 70 and 75. The moment, we crossed 75, we start looking at fresh capacity. So as we speak, actually 20 of our current plants are undergoing some form of brownfield expansion.

items.statement: Value and volume growth expected to converge by Q2, definitely by H2 if pricing stable and no raw material volatility
items.quote: As far as pricing is concerned, if we keep pricing at the current levels, and we don't have any massive volatility or major volatility in raw materials, starting the second quarter, but definitely by the second half, you will see value and volume converge.

items.statement: Paints foray progressing organically; will assess after one festive season; happy with progress so far
items.quote: As we said, Latika last time, give us a little more time on paints because company with our sales and distribution network and reach just through a channel field, you will always see good results in the first 6 months. I would be best equipped to answer this question after these markets have gone through one festive season and we see where we settle.

items.statement: Domestic subsidiary revenues flat in Q1 due to heat wave and elections; expected to normalize by H2
items.quote: See, as far as domestic subsidiaries are concerned, again, this is because of massive, more of the heat wave and some part of the election. But frankly, by the second half, you will see them all normalize because demand conditions will continuously improve.

items.statement: EBITDA margin likely at higher end of 20-24% range for rest of year if input costs remain benign; will invest more aggressively if stability continues
items.quote: As of now, as we said, we will be in the 20% to 24% range, probably a little more at the higher end. But as we see signs of stability, we will invest back more aggressively for growth.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted from 80% core / 20% growth+pioneer to 55% core / 45% growth+pioneer over last 7-8 years
items.quote: See, I would say when we started on this journey, Percy, we were 80-20, 80 was core and 20 was growth and pioneer. We are now close to 55-45.

items.statement: International exports (Africa, Middle East, Indian subcontinent) growing in strong double-digits consistently for 3 years; 2 factories in Africa
items.quote: Africa is growing substantially for us. In fact, now on a consistent basis over the last 3 years would have been a fast-growing geography. That is also true for the Middle East. So slowly and steadily in our neighbouring Indian subcontinent, the Middle East and Africa, we continue to grow in strong double-digit numbers.

items.statement: Core demand environment remains confident; real festive demand indicators emerge in September; Q2 small due to monsoon
items.quote: The basic indicators of good festive demand and where the new normal only emerges in September. We are all optimistic because there is no reason to see that demand should not be good given what we have seen in the first quarter. But having said that, if you ask me, where is my degree of confidence? I mean, I think we should ask the same question at the end of September.

items.statement: Advertising and sales promotion expenses increased in Q4 FY24 and continued in Q1 FY25; not managed quarter-to-quarter but planned for longer period
items.quote: One of the biggest chunks of this other expenses will be advertising and sales promotion expenses, which is something that we are continuing to dial-up as we see opportunities to build our brands and categories.

items.statement: 90% of rural growth is same-store growth; new outlets contribute <10%; massive penetration and range expansion opportunity in existing accounts
items.quote: See, firstly, Rishi, just let me clarify, 90% of our growth is same-store growth. The new outlets, etc. is less than 10%. So we still have a massive opportunity in penetration in existing markets with existing stores.

items.statement: VAM prices near bottom; largest producer declared force majeure at current levels; comfortable with 20-24% EBITDA band at current VAM prices
items.quote: In fact, the largest one of them actually declared a force majeure in its U.S. and Mexico plants because they found these levels itself not satisfactory. So I would say we are very near the bottom. This is very near the bottom. And as far as price is concerned, if it remains at this level, we are very comfortable with our 20% to 24% range.

items.statement: Real estate cycle benefits for core categories typically appear in years 3-4; currently in year 2; some waterproofing benefit now, multiplier expected end of this year/beginning next year
items.quote: Normally, what we have observed in the past when real estate is taken off, its year 3 and 4 that give you a multiplier much stronger than years 1 and 2. So I suspect starting maybe the end of this year, beginning of next year, you will start seeing the multiplier as long as real estate continues to boom.

items.statement: Tied up with Chinese/German company for electronic adhesives in early stages; constantly adding to B2B portfolio for EV/electronics demand
items.quote: We have tied up with a Chinese/German company in the area of electronic adhesives, which is just beginning off, we are in the initial stages.

items.statement: Targeting profitable double-digit underlying volume growth for full year FY25 barring black-swan events; Q1 UVG 9.6% close to target
items.quote: See, again, barring any black-swan events, that's our clear objective. I mean, we have clearly maintained that for us, success is profitable double digit.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin fell 200 bps sequentially to 14.4% in Q1 FY25 due to raw material cost pressures
items.quote: The consolidated EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 9.1 billion, a margin of 14.4% compared to 16.4% in the last quarter.

items.statement: India EBITDA margin declined to 13.8% from 15.6% sequentially due to rising raw material costs
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter stood at a margin of 13.8% compared to 15.6% in the last quarter, given the pressure from rising raw materials.

items.statement: Europe EBITDA margin improved to 13.7% from 13.4% year-on-year despite raw material pressure
items.quote: The EBITDA for the quarter at E UR 20 million was a margin performance of 13.7% compared to 13.4% for the same period last

items.statement: Expect raw material cost to increase by mid-single digits in Q2 FY25 sequentially
items.quote: We expect the raw material cost to go up further by mid-single digits in Q2 on a sequential basis.

items.statement: Expect mid to high single digit top line growth in Europe in Q2 FY25 year-on-year
items.quote: Next quarter, as of now, our expectation would be a mid to high single digit top line growth.

items.statement: Long-term target remains higher than 15% EBITDA margin

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue Rs 84.82 crore, up 11.8% YoY, highest quarterly revenue ever despite heat waves, labour shortages, elections
items.quote: During Quarter 1 FY25, Duroply has reported a revenue of Rs. 84.82 crores, an increase of 11.8% from the same period last year, up 0.4% from Q4 FY24. This also marks our all-time highest quarterly revenue.

items.statement: Expect growth rate to increase in upcoming quarters driven by urbanization and interior spending
items.quote: This bodes well for the upcoming quarters and we expect our growth rate to further increase.

items.statement: Organised sector 25% of Rs 30,000 crore industry; ample room for all to grow
items.quote: See, our industry is estimated at 25 to 30,000 crores. Let's just take 30,000 crores as an industry side. The organized sector has a 25% market share. 75% lies with the unorganized sector. Whatever the competition be, with the income levels going up, I think there's enough space for everyone to grow and grow rapidly in this market environment.

items.statement: Industry facing severe timber shortage and inflationary pressure on raw materials
items.quote: This is at a time when the industry is facing severe raw material shortages and inflationary pressure.

items.statement: Timber shortage pressuring gross margins across industry
items.quote: Our industry is going through a tremendous shortage of timber. I think if you look at the other players and the results that have come out, gross profit margins, there's a lot of pressure on them.

items.statement: Employee cost rose to 11.2% of sales in Q1 FY25 from 10% in FY24 due to team expansion investment
items.quote: The company saw a significant increase in its employee expenses which stood 11.2% of sales as compared to 10% for the entire previous financial year. The company is looking to invest in expanding its team across India to better cater to its demands.

items.statement: Plan to raise working capital debt in near future alongside internal accruals
items.quote: So internal accruals, working capital debt, our balance sheet is now strengthened. So there is scope of raising some working capital debt in the near future and of course, definitely internal accruals.

items.statement: Higher cost inventory from previous year consumed in Q1, limiting margin improvement
items.quote: We've not fully realized the improvement in our gross profit margins because we also were holding higher cost inventory from the previous financial year which has been consumed this year.

items.statement: Volume growth guidance maintained at 10-20% for FY25
items.quote: We maintain the guidance of 10% to 20% as of now.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg margin guidance maintained; visible improvement expected in 1.5-2 years
items.quote: We would like to maintain the guidance that most of our EBITDA growths will be driven by volume growth and not really by margin improvement after maybe 1.5 years or 2 years-or-so, I think that's the time we will start improving the margin profile as such.

items.statement: PBT guidance of Rs 320-350 crore for FY25 considered reasonable
items.quote: PBT of Rs. 320 crores to Rs. 350 crores sound reasonable as of now.

items.statement: Consolidated tax rate guidance of 13-14% for FY25
items.quote: At a consol level, around 13.5%, 14%.

items.statement: India retail branded business revenue target of Rs 300 crore for FY25
items.quote: Yes. So, yes, 300 is the number that we are looking at, which will mean that almost 50% growth over last year.

items.statement: Overall India business revenue target of Rs 400 crore for FY25
items.quote: At an overall level, the India business should cross Rs. 400 crores.

items.statement: India branded business EBITDA margin target of 7-8% for FY25
items.quote: Last time itself, we said that we had broken even, and we probably will be looking to get to a 7% to 8% EBITDA margins for the branded business.

items.statement: Clients placing only short-term orders due to high coffee prices; long-term contract revival not yet strong
items.quote: Most of the clients are into hand to mouth kind of a situation. So, the orders are really coming not in the long term, but in a very, very short-term manner.

items.statement: Q1 volume growth of 15-16% YoY in line with guidance
items.quote: We are experiencing last quarter around 15% to 16% volume growth, which is in line with the guidance that we have been giving.

items.statement: Per kg EBITDA margins intact; optical margin compression due to high coffee prices
items.quote: The margins never contracted. Optically, it gets contracted because we would work on a per kilo EBITDA margin, which means that if the coffee prices go up, in relation to top line, the margins may look depleted, but that's not the case.

items.statement: Freeze-dried margins 30-40% higher than spray-dried margins
items.quote: The freeze-dried margins, as we have told earlier, is approximately 30%, 40% higher than the spray-dried margins.

items.statement: Long-term contract revival not yet visible; clients in wait-and-watch mode
items.quote: As of now, we are not seeing so much of revival of long-term contracts because coffee prices are still high.

items.statement: Vietnam freeze-dried capacity of 6,000 tons on track for September-October 2024 start-up
items.quote: Yes, we are on track. September, October, we should be up and running.

items.statement: Vietnam project cost $50 million; $47 million incurred; balance in next couple of months
items.quote: Total schedule is about 50 million, total implementation of the project cost. And this predominantly, as part of the loan, has been revised in last financial year itself. And we have incurred almost around 47 million so far, and the balance amount is going to be incurred in another couple of months.

items.statement: India spray-dried capacity 15,000 tons not yet added; Vietnam line 1 at full capacity, line 2 at ~50%
items.quote: The first line is running at full capacity. The second one probably at around 50% of the capacity.

items.statement: India food & beverage capacity utilization only 5-10%; rest running near full
items.quote: So, while there is a certain sales that is happening, but the capacity utilization is not very high. So, it will not be more than 5% to 10% of the capacity. Rest of the capacity, we were running almost full.

items.statement: B2B pricing on cost-plus model linked to green coffee prices; B2C pricing based on market index with ~30% price increases
items.quote: Here, we can't work on cost-plus. Generally, because we are a fighter, we are a competitor to the largest player, we maintain a pricing index of the market. So, that's how we increase prices, and we have seen 30%-or-so price

items.statement: Freeze-dried ~25% of consolidated volumes; small packs 20-25% of units; specialty coffee >5% of portfolio
items.quote: So, let's say I don't spell out the exact numbers, so 25% of the total volumes will be spray-dried volumes.

items.statement: Adding 10-15 new clients annually; 4-5 drop off; focus on quality clients building brands
items.quote: On a very, very broad basis, in any year, we would add 10 to 15 new clients. There will be 4 to 5 clients who drop-off also.

items.statement: Wallet share target 20-25% for clients currently at 5-10%; max 35-40% for top clients
items.quote: Our endeavor is to kind of get into more of a 20%, 25% wallet share for those clients.

items.statement: Geographic revenue split: Asia 40%, East Europe 20-25%, West Europe/UK 15%, US 10-15%, rest RoW
items.quote: Let's say, out of our total business approximately, everything put together, 40% comes from the Asian markets and then around 20% to 25% from East European markets.

items.statement: Gross debt Rs 1,885 crore (June 2024): WC debt Rs 1,200 crore, term debt Rs 675 crore; WC debt up from Rs 1,000 crore in March
items.quote: Rs. 1,200 crore is the working capital debt and Rs. 675 crore is the term loan debt. Total on 30th June, it was Rs. 1,885 crores as against, earlier working capital debt of Rs. 1,000 crores and almost around Rs. 700 crores, which is around Rs. 1,620 crores.

items.statement: Inventory days elevated ~180 days due to Brazil sourcing logistics; expected to improve by Q4 if coffee prices soften
items.quote: So, until then, we will have to stay put with these kind of working capital cycles.

items.statement: Year-end debt target Rs 2,200 crore at current prices; could drop by few hundred crores if prices correct post Nov-Dec
items.quote: We are looking to end the year at around Rs. 2,200 crores from Rs. 1,800 crores. But let's say, if the prices do drop after November, December, then this could come down by a couple of hundred crores.

items.statement: Working capital cost of funds 6.5% till June; risen to 8.25% from July on Rs 1,200 crore WC debt
items.quote: 8.25% is the current cost of funds towards working capital, that is from July onwards.

items.statement: Refinancing under review; no decision yet due to volatile global interest rates
items.quote: We are still under review. There is a lot of background working that has to be done. So, we are constantly reviewing it because what is happening is that the interest rate scenario across the world is changing by the minute.

items.statement: EUDR compliance not a risk for instant coffee; green coffee largely shade-grown and compliant
items.quote: Instant Coffee does not kind of come under this ambit. So, I don't think as of now, there is no risk that we see on this track.

items.statement: Coffee price volatility high; Brazil crop good but Vietnam El Nino shortages keeping prices elevated; next trigger Nov-Dec harvest
items.quote: Brazil, and last time we had discussed that Brazil seems to be having good crops, it had a good crop, but simultaneously, there were news, and the market suggested that Vietnam had El Nino effect and they had certain crop shortages.

items.statement: Global B2B market share estimated 6-7% at 40k tons; targeting 12-13% by FY28 at 17-18% CAGR
items.quote: We probably will end up at around 12%, 13% by '27-'28.

items.statement: Best-ever Q1 revenue of INR 784 crore driven by higher volumes in most front-ends and rail; exports flattish due to geopolitical issues
items.quote: So the -- opening remarks, as we concluded our meeting yesterday, we had the best-ever June quarter revenues of INR 784 crores, so best ever first quarter. It was driven by higher volume in most of the front-ends and better in rail. Intercompany sales which is exports, was flattish. And we still have those geopolitical situation around us.

items.statement: PBT margin declined to 16.6% from 17.1% YoY due to higher energy and transportation costs
items.quote: PBT margins were at 16.6% compared to 17.1% in the previous year period. So that was a deterioration, while the sales were up, and energy cost and transportation because everything is going up.

items.quote: Yes. So wind is like -- wind consumes 1 meter bearing kind of -- it consumes 300 mm, 400 mm, but right up to 1 m. And as we start installing 5-megawatt windmills in India, it will need 1.5 meter or so, but the critical mass, and that will mandate everybody to invest locally more and more as that comes up.

items.quote: So gratuity, last quarter was there, this quarter was not there. That is the short answer.

items.quote: But the immediate geopolitical situation hopefully gets corrected, which is important for the nation and everybody involved in the manufacturing and selling business in India. Obviously, it can have a great -- different effect if somebody wins and wants to infuse lot of

items.statement: Maintains FY25 revenue growth guidance of 15-20% and EBITDA margin guidance of 25-26%
items.quote: We maintain our guidance that we expect to achieve a 50% to 51% gross margin, 25% to 26% EBITDA margin and these variations quarter-on-quarter will keep on happening depending on the product mix. But we maintained our earlier guidance of maintaining a 25% to 26% margin.

items.statement: Will review growth guidance after Q2 FY25 based on Kharif season progress
items.quote: We shall, however, closely monitor the emerging business scenarios and review our growth guidance after Q2FY25.

items.statement: Effective tax rate for FY25 expected at 22-23% due to SEZ tax exemption change
items.quote: The ETR for FY25 is expected to be around 22% to 23% due to the tax exemption of our second SEZ at Jambusar moving from 100% to 50%.

items.statement: Global agri input industry facing challenges from weather, destocking, commodity prices; initial signs of improvement
items.quote: The global agri input industry is passing through a challenging time due to extreme weather events, inventory destocking, commodity prices, and more. items.statement: Capex plan of Rs 800-900 crore for FY25; includes capacity optimization and new capacities
items.quote: We have a plan of close to Rs. 800 crore – Rs. 900 crore CAPEX this year and we are moving in that direction.

items.statement: Optimizing existing plant capacities and improving throughput to commercialize new products without heavy investment
items.quote: Apart from fresh CAPEX and building new capacities, we are also, as we have alluded to in the past, optimizing plant capacities and improving throughput by adopting various technologies and that also gives us good room to maximize the capacity utilization because so many new products are now getting commercialized.

items.statement: Plant Health Care (PHC) acquisition on track for court approvals; expected completion in current quarter
items.quote: We are on track with obtaining the requisite court mandated approvals and hope to complete this process in the current quarter.

items.statement: Commercialized 2 new molecules in Q1 FY25; targeting 6-7 more for the year
items.quote: For the current fiscal, we have already commercialized two new molecules in Q1 and are looking to commercialize another 6 to 7 molecules for the sustained growth trend.

items.quote: The trade working capital in terms of Days of Sales reduced to 55 days versus 83 days as on 30 June 2023. Inventory levels also reduced in terms of Days of Sales from 73 days as on 30 June 2023 to approximately 50 days.

items.statement: Board will evaluate returning surplus cash (Rs 4,000+ crore) via buyback or other means at appropriate time
items.quote: But yes, at an appropriate time, the board will obviously take a view on both the cash situation and also the growth opportunities that would be in front of us and we will act accordingly.

items.quote: We have further strengthened our Board with induction of a global Agchem industry veteran, Mr. Rafael Del Rio, who had an illustrious long career. His experience is perfectly aligned to our long-term strategic goals and vision of expanding our global footprint.

items.quote: Out of the new inquiries, at least 50% of them come from the non-Agchem segment, which is also helping us diversify into adjacencies.

items.quote: In a positive development, we started operations at the Hyderabad Research facility, while the GMP Kilolab in Lodi is nearing completion, we are moving on to the certification.

items.quote: Yes, on a blended basis, the margin expansion is driven not only from CSM products, particularly new products, but also from product mix at our domestic market, including biologicals. items.quote: We would like to shape up and our vision is to be a INR300 crores company in five years' time.

items.quote: We also mentioned that our utilization of the quartz sink capacity has grown from 60% to 70% right now.

items.quote: So, the premium launches at ₹30 and ₹40, they have just been launched and it will take a couple of months to really scale up , rather a couple of quarters to scale up all India.

items.statement: Targets mid-teen EBITDA margins by end of FY26
items.quote: So that holds right 15%, 16% margins by FY '26 margins? Dilip Banthiya: Yes

items.statement: Aims to be almost debt-free by FY26 then return cash to shareholders
items.quote: We reiterate our commitment to be almost debt-free by FY '26 and thereafter focus on returning cash to the shareholders.

items.statement: Expects annual price increase impact of 150-170 bps for full year
items.quote: And we expect the price increase for the whole year to remain between 150 basis points to 170 basis points.

items.statement: Regular category volume growth guided at 4-5%
items.quote: However, we see that we will be on a muted growth. And overall, we guided that 4% to 5% growth, which we aspire from the regular category.

items.statement: Ad spend guided at 7-8% of IMFL revenue annually; Q1 was aberration
items.quote: First of all, the ad spend that we have always guided would be around 7% to 8% [of our IMFL revenue] annually. The first quarter this year is an aberration.

items.statement: Industry lost 3-4% volume due to election-related excise policy delays in Q1
items.quote: Yes. I think it would be , it is just an estimate, but I think it should be close to about 3% to 4%.

items.statement: Expects margin expansion trajectory to continue with stable raw material basket and premiumization
items.quote: As the year progresses, we expect the broader raw material basket to remain stable. Coupled with ongoing premiumization, we anticipate staying on track with our margin expansion trajectory.

items.statement: Prestige & Above volume grew 14.3% YoY; value grew 19.1%; P&A share 43.4% of IMFL volume
items.quote: Prestige & Above category volume grew by 14.3%. In value terms, the Prestige & Above category registered 19.1% growth. Prestige & Above category accounts for 43.4% of IMFL volume compared to 36.5% in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Magic Moments Vodka sold 1.9 million cases in Q1 FY25; crossed INR 300 cr sales value
items.quote: Magic Moments Vodka continued its growth momentum and recorded 1.9 million cases sales in Q1 FY '25 and cross ed sales value of INR 300 crores for the current quarter.

items.statement: Price increases contributed 170 bps YoY and 55 bps QoQ to IMFL sales value in Q1
items.quote: Y-o-Y basis, there was 170 basis points impact due 4 | P a g e Q1 FY2025 Earnings Call Transcript to price increase in Q1 of FY '25 on our IMFL sales value. On quarter- on-quarter basis, impact of price increases was 55 basis

items.statement: Broken rice prices peaked around INR 28,000; softened in April-May but rose after MSP hike; FCI allocation decision awaited
items.quote: So actually, Himanshu, th ese prices, which had risen up to INR28,000 or so the broken rice and have seen some softening in the April and middle of May. But after th at government has taken one decision of increasing the MSP, again, the sentiment went toward the little price increase.

items.statement: Glass prices saw steep inflation last year (~INR 9,000-10,000/tonne); some softening expected from Q2
items.quote: Last year, we had seen a steep inflation and it was to the tune of something around INR 9,000 to INR 10,000 per tonne . But after that, the gas price and the other input cost price have come down. So, some softening from Q2 onwards, we can see in this.

items.statement: Net debt increased due to cyclical inventory build-up and higher receivables in certain states
items.quote: The increase in net debt over March '24 is primarily due to the cyclical building up of inventory at the plants and higher receivables in certain states.

items.statement: Telangana receivables coming slowly but regularly; supply linked to payments
items.quote: The payments in Telangana are coming on a slower pace. But payments are coming, that's most important. The government agrees that payments will be released to also build up their margins and their stock supply. So, I think we have been getting payments on a very frequent basis. And accordingly, we are supplying based on payments.

items.statement: Focus on improving profitability, cash flow generation and efficient working capital management to reduce debt
items.quote: Going forward, our focus will be on improving our profitability along with the cashflow generation and more efficient working capital management, resulting in debt reduction.

items.statement: Government restricting surrogate advertising; Radico will comply and shift to innovative on-ground marketing
items.quote: First of all, we must state that the government has not said that you cannot advertise. Actually they are talking about advertisement of surrogate brands, which the objective is to prevent misleading ads. However, the government is talking about brand extensions, which can be advertised with the same brand name and you must have a revenue model for it, which is quite justified and logical.

items.statement: Some states planning duty rationalization which is positive for industry
items.quote: In fact, there are few other states, which are planning to rationalize the duty. So, if that happens, it is very good for the industry. So, I think if the governments are now quite proactive and they feel that if it's highly taxed, then it leads to less of sales, etc . So, in fact, they are talking of duty rationalization in states, which is a very good sign for the industry.

items.statement: Launched four luxury brands in Q1: Rampur Asava (INR 10,000), Sangam World Malt (INR 4,000-7,500), Jaisalmer Gold Edition (INR 4,000-7,000), 1999 Spirit of Victory
items.quote: During the quarter, we launched Rampur Asava, Sangam World Malt and Jaisalmer Gold Edition in India, enhancing the experience for connoisseurs of luxury brands. We will expand the distribution of these brands throughout the year, including the canteen stor e department.

items.statement: Regional players launching in P&A and below, not in luxury; organized peers ahead in luxury; two large competitors announced backward integration plans
items.quote: See, I'll tell you there are two situations. One, regional players are introducing new brands in P&A and below, actually, not in P&A. P&A upwards only organized companies are creating brands and we are ahead of others. As far as the regional players creating brands in the luxury segment is concerned. today, it's a nonissue right now and we are not too worried about it.

items.statement: Rampur Single Malt volume tripled last year; expects 25-30% jump this year
items.quote: Globally, in India, we are also doing, last year also, we tripled our volume. And this year, again, we will see 25%, 30% jump in our last year volume on the Rampur.

items.statement: Food grain inflation worst over; government holding large rice stocks; expects same or softening ahead
items.quote: I think the food grain inflation, I think the worst is over because the government is sitting on a lot of stock of rice, which they ha ve to dispose. So, I think as far as the industry goes, I think we've seen the worst of the inflation. And I think now onwards, it will be the same or it will soften.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM fell from above Rs 26,000 crore to Rs 12,162 crore as of August 5; over a million customer accounts closed and jewellery returned
items.quote: So, the gold loan AUM which was a little above Rs. 26,000 crore has fallen to Rs. 12,162 crores, so it is less than half. More than a million customer accounts have closed their accounts and safely taken their jewellery.

items.statement: Repaid Rs 15,700 crore to all lenders since embargo; raised Rs 2,886 crore via term loans, bonds, refinance and ECB; assigned Rs 1,769 crore of other loans
items.quote: We additionally also repaid to our capital market lenders close to around Rs. 2,239 crores. So, in aggregate the entire repayments since the embargo to all our lenders have been around Rs. 15,700 crores. In addition to that, we also raised funds in aggregate to around Rs. 2,886 crores through term loan, bond, refinance. And also assigned around Rs. 1,769 crores of other loans.

items.statement: Expect RBI to lift gold loan restrictions at an early date but cannot give certainty; committed to full compliance and stronger systems
items.quote: We expect that RBI will lift the restrictions in a short time from now. The RBI processes are involved and therefore we cannot have any certainty of when this will happen. But we anticipate that to happen at an early date.

items.statement: Consolidated gross NPA 2.2%, net NPA 1.1%; provision coverage ratio 128% under IndAS ECL
items.quote: Our gross NPA stood at around 2.2% and net NPA was around 1.1%, which is up by around 40 basis point and 4 basis points respectively when compared to the same period last year. With the implementation of the expected credit loss under IndAS, provision coverage ratio on NPAs stands at 128%.

items.statement: Consolidated loan AUM grew 2% Y-o-Y but degrew 12% Q-o-Q to Rs 69,610 crore; core loan AUM 97% of total at Rs 67,853 crore
items.quote: a consol basis, we degrew by around 12% on quarter-on-quarter basis, touching AUM of around Rs. 69,610 crores. If I further dissect the AUM on our core products, which is largely Microfinance, Gold loan, Home loan, Digital finance and LAP, there we grew Y-o-Y by around 4%, and degrew by around 12% on quarter-on-quarter basis to Rs. 67,853 crores. The core loan AUM now in comparison is 97% of the o

items.statement: Quarterly average cost of borrowing decreased 2 bps Q-o-Q, up 2 bps Y-o-Y
items.quote: Our quarterly average cost of borrowing decreased by 2 basis points on Q-on-Q basis and is up by 2 basis points Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Hired CXO-level executives and strengthening assurance organization (risk, audit, compliance) at mid and low levels
items.quote: We have hired a few people at the CXO level, and we are in the process of hiring few more to strengthen our senior management team and also the entire assurance organizations. So, that means that even at the mid-level and low-level we are enhancing the resources.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents including committed credit lines at Rs 6,853 crore; positive ALM with inflows exceeding outflows across all buckets
items.quote: Our cash and cash equivalents including committing credit lines from banks and institutions was around Rs. 6,853 crores adequate to meet not just some near-term liabilities but also to support growth in some of the other businesses which continue to operate. We have a positive ALM whereby inflows cover exceeds the outflows across all buckets.

items.statement: Net gearing 2.8x after May 2024 capital infusion; CRAR: NBFC 27.8%, HFC 46.5%, Samasta 27% — all well above 15% regulatory minimum
items.quote: With the infusion of capital that we raised in the month of May of '24, our net gearing stands around 2.8x. Supported by that, our capability NBFC entities stood at around 27.8%, for HFC it was 46.5%, and for Samasta it was 27%. Each of them much higher than the minimum threshold of 15% laid down by the regulator.

items.statement: Consolidated PAT Rs 338 crore, down 28% Y-o-Y and 21% Q-o-Q; pre-provision operating profit Rs 647 crore, down 18% Y-o-Y and 35% Q-o-Q
items.quote: consolidated level for the quarter Q1 FY ‘25, the profit after tax before non -controlling interest was Rs. 338 crores, down by 28% Y-o-Y and down 21 % on quarter-on-quarter basis, for reasons that Nirmal high lighted earlier. We recorded pre -provision operating profit of Rs. 647 crores, down 18% Y-o-Y and down 35% on quarter-on-quarter basis

items.statement: Gold prices firm during suspension; off-book (assigned + co-lending) at 35% of AUM; assigned book Rs 14,609 crore down 17% Y-o-Y, co-lending Rs 9,532 crore up 6% Y-o-Y
items.quote: In line with our capital optimization strategy, we have done DAs and co-lending in some of our other businesses, and our off book stands at around 35%, which is the aggregate of assigned and co-lending book as of 30th June. The assigned book stood at around Rs. 14,609 crores, which is down by 17% Y-o-Y, and 11% Q-on-Q. And the co-lending assets stands at around Rs. 9,532 crores, which is up 6% Y-o

items.statement: RBI action on gold loans was industry-wide practice; after RBI circular, all players stopped cash disbursals above Rs 20,000 creating level playing field
items.quote: Supposing you are disbursing cash more than Rs. 20,000, everybody else is doing it. Now if I follow very strictly the guideline and this thing, then I will lose all the customers because customers will walk to the other gold loan branch and say, big deal, you are not giving it, I am getting from somewhere else. But what has happened is that after the action taken on us and then there was another c

items.statement: ROE 10.3% annualized, ROA 2.3%; basic EPS Rs 7.2 for the quarter
items.quote: Our overall annualized ROE stood at around 10.3% while ROA was around 2.3%. The basic earnings per share for the quarter was around Rs. 7.2.

items.statement: CRE portfolio tapering off and becoming insignificant; increased ECL provisioning for Stage-2 and Stage-3 on CRE and capital market books per auditor recommendation
items.quote: CRE portfolio, I mean, the book is just like sort of tapering off and will become very insignificant just like our capital market. But for the time being, as recommended by auditors, we will increase the provisioning.

items.statement: Home loan business saw slack quarter but government allocated significantly higher resources for affordable housing; expect stronger growth ahead
items.quote: Our home loan business has seen a slack quarter in April to June. But the government has come out with very strong support and impetus for this business. They allocated significantly higher resources for affordable housing. So, we expect that this business, which had a relatively slow growth rate in last one or two years, will also have stronger growth.

items.statement: Liquidity concerns in MFI easing slowly; growth impacted by conscious compliance strategy and industry trends
items.quote: As of now, so I think liquidity concerns are easing slowly. But the growth is impacted also by our conscious strategy on compliance, as well as the industry trends.

items.statement: Management declines to give volume guidance for the year, will wait at least one more quarter due to logistics uncertainty
items.quote: targeted volume growth year-over-year target and the opportunity remains the same. But in all honesty, we want to wait and watch at least for one more quarter before we give you a clear volume guidance, at least for this year

items.statement: Logistics issues and container shortage caused ~10,000-11,000 tonne volume drop in Q1; customers on wait-and-watch for new conversions
items.quote: this saw about 4,000 tonnes to 5,000 tonnes of orders that just will get shipped next quarter. That's an annual order that moves, over the last two, three years it was generally being invoiced in the first quarter, I think it will happen in the second quarter.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA Rs 372.32 cr, PAT Rs 259.58 cr; margins strong despite volume drop due to better product mix
items.quote: Total production was 68,000 tonnes and that translated into a revenue of Rs. 1,000 crores, Rs. 1,004 crores. An EBITDA of Rs. 372.32 crores , and a profit after tax of Rs. 259.58 crores. So, from a margin standpoint, this quarter has been great.

items.statement: Total FY25 capex ~Rs 250 cr: Rs 65 cr for composite mill liner Brownfield, Rs 150 cr for grinding media phase 1, Rs 35 cr captive power
items.quote: A large part about CAPEX, the plan for capital outlay this year, we are doing about Rs. 35 crores on captive power, there's Rs. 65 crores on the mill liner composite facility , and money that we are spend on the first phase of the grinding media, which is about Rs. 150 crores. So, total as we speak , our outlay remains at about Rs. 250 crores

items.statement: Adding 20,000 tonnes composite/rubber mill liner capacity via Brownfield at Kerala GIDC; commissioning by end of CY2024
items.quote: We expect about 20,000 tonnes of additional capacity in this configuration to be available to us. Of course, mill liner sales and penetration and all of that we have discussed at length in the past few quarters.

items.statement: Freight cost to Latin America rose from $100 to $400 per tonne; freight is full pass-through on cost-plus model
items.quote: the freight cost for sending a container from here to say Latin America, which was about $100, has gone up now to $400 per tonne. And more importantly, the container availability is just not there

items.statement: Higher casting mix in Q1 drove better realization and margins despite lower volumes
items.quote: Overall, if you have seen the numbers, the product mix is better where there is higher casting, higher priced product . A nd you ar e right , that is reflected in the higher selling price, yes , higher realization.

items.statement: New customer conversions slowed due to shipping cost unpredictability and supply chain timeline uncertainty; existing customers continuing
items.quote: customers all of a sudden have gone back to what we saw post COVID which is on a wait and watch, as far a s new conversions are concerned . T hey want to be sure that price remains predictable, and the curr ent shipping regime does not allow for that.

items.statement: Receivables up Rs 66 cr to Rs 77 cr; raw material inventory 31 to 52 days; stock 69 to 79 days; attributed to seasonality and transit delays
items.quote: Working capital has been a little higher , receivables have moved from Rs. 66 crores to Rs. 77 crores, I think it is just our timing adjustment because we had poor sales reflecting a higher number of absolute receivables, otherwise it's at par with regular.

items.statement: Net cash ~Rs 3,500 cr before buyback and dividend payout
items.quote: Our net cash stands at about Rs. 3,500 crores, that will get adjusted for the buyback cash and the dividend that has to flow out from that.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 500 cr buyback; execution in next few days/weeks
items.quote: We have also done a buyback; Board approved a buyback of Rs. 500 crores. So, that should be getting through in the next few days , next few weeks.

items.statement: Brazil dumping duty (6.3%) terminated; countervailing duty (6.5%) under sunset review, outcome in 2-3 months; Canada duties settled at minimum price level
items.quote: Brazil dumping is already terminated. The countervailing duty part, which is 6.5%, that's under the sunset review, and we hope to hear in next two months on the outcome of that, two to three months.

items.statement: Supply chain transit time extended from 30-40 days to 2-3 months due to Red Sea crisis; ~5,000-6,000 tonnes orders could not ship in Q1
items.quote: What we used to do in 30- 40 days is now taking more than two, two and a half to even three m onths. So, that's indeed a challenge which we are trying to circumvent.

items.statement: Magotteaux at full chrome capacity utilization for years; no direct competitor offers comparable composite/rubber liner design and solution
items.quote: as far as their chrome capacity is concerned , a s we understand, they are capacity constraint, they are fully utilized for last few years. So, there is only so much that they are able to do.

items.statement: Mining addressable market >3M tonnes annually; high chrome penetration only ~25% of 1.5-2M tonnes focused metals market
items.quote: Addressable market if I just look at the three metals where I am focused could be 2 million or a little more than that. Out of that, today, hardly 25 -odd-percentage serviced by high chrome solution players like me

items.statement: Logistics uncertainty structural vs cyclical debated; evaluating long-term options including overseas manufacturing but no decision; India remains primary base
items.quote: we are seriously evaluating various options. So, please give us some more time and we will come back to you, maybe in a couple of months, that's all. Warehousing alone may or may not be a solution.

items.statement: Welcast delisting attempt failed; status quo maintained; minimal sourcing continues; evaluating bank suggestions for alternative structure
items.quote: As we speak, yes, we attempted for delisting, but somehow it di d not succeed. So, as it stands now, it is status quo. We have not taken any other call.

items.statement: Company on track to achieve volume guidance for FY25
items.quote: I am delighted to share that the Company is on track to achieve the volume guidance given at the beginning of the year.

items.statement: Pellet realization increased 3% YoY and 4% QoQ to Rs 10,500 per ton
items.quote: The realization of iron ore pellet increased by 3% and 4% respectively on Y-o-Y and quarter-on-quarter basis to Rs. 10,500 a ton.

items.statement: EBITDA margin increased significantly to 30% from 23% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA margin increased significantly to 30% as compared to 23% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: Mining capacity expansion approvals expected by December 2024; pellet capacity expansion on schedule for June 2026 commissioning
items.quote: Basically, approvals are expected to be placed by December 2024. The project of increasing pellet capacity from 2.7 to 4.7 is running on schedule and same is expected to be commissioned by June 2026.

items.statement: Integrated steel plant 2 million ton capacity: environmental approval process expected to complete by December 2024; project takes 36 months from ground breaking
items.quote: Environment impact assessment study is now finalized and being filed with MOEF for final presentation. The process is expected to be completed by December '24. After receipt of environmental approval, consent to set up the steel state pollution authorities, the implementation shall start after the mining lease for the project land is executed with the state government authorities. The project will

items.statement: 20 MW captive solar plant completed; additional 70 MW solar project planned for Q1 FY26 commissioning
items.quote: 20 MW captive solar power plant for meeting the power requirement of the Rolling Mill and Fabrication Division has been completed and synchronized. Further, GPIL has planned to set up an additional 70 MW solar power project to meet the power requirement of the upcoming pellet plant, which we expect to commission by Q1 FY26, coinciding with the commissioning of pellet plant.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 75 crore investment for energy efficiency project generating 11 MW additional power with 2-year payback and Rs 38 crore annual savings
items.quote: The Board has approved an investment of Rs. 75 crores for this energy efficiency project which will generate an additional power of 11 MW without requiring any additional fuel. The project expected payback for this project is about 2 years, with cost saving of Rs. 38 crores per annum and this is expected to result in additional carbon reduction intensity by 2,59,415 tons.

items.statement: Completed buyback of 21.5 lakh shares at Rs 1,400 per share in July 2024; approved special dividend of 25% on face value of Rs 5; approved share split from Rs 5 to Re 1 face value
items.quote: The Company has recently completed the buyback of 21.5 lakh shares at a price of Rs. 1,400 per share in July 24. The Board has further approved a special dividend of 25% on face value of Rs. 5 each on the occasion of 25th Anniversary of GPIL will falls on 21st of September 2024. The Board has further approved the split of equity share from face value of Rs. 5 to Re. 1 each.

items.statement: WSA forecasts India steel demand growth of 8.2% in 2024 and 2025 to 144 million ton and 156 million ton respectively
items.quote: WSA forecast India steel demand to increase by 8.2% in 24 and 25 to 144 million ton and 156 million ton respectively.

items.statement: Domestic pellet prices strong due to regional shortage; delta of $20 premium over export market; no exports in last three months
items.quote: For today example also there is a delta of $20 more by selling domestic compared to the national market. So, we have not in the national market at all from last three months and going forward, we don't think so we will be in a position to even think of export. Domestic is quite strong right now in terms of iron ore.

items.statement: Billet prices corrected ~10% from last quarter to ~Rs 39,000 as of August 8
items.quote: See as of now as of on 8th of August, so prices are down by almost 10% compared to last quarter. So, on absolute number there is about 44,500, billet is about 39,000 mark-to- market. So, there is a correction of almost 10%.

items.statement: Average landed imported coal cost in Q1 was Rs 11,500 per ton; Q2 expected at similar levels

Abhishek Agrawal: Q2 is more or less same because we do a lot of planning in terms of, we maintain an inventory of two months. Q2 looks on the similar level, there might be slight change in Q3 with the current international

items.statement: Monthly coal consumption 90,000-1 lakh tons; 50% imported (flat), 50% domestic (cost reducing in Q2)
items.quote: Monthly, we consume about 90,000 to 1 lakhs on monthly basis in units. So, 50% is in imported coal which will remain flat and the other 50% is domestic, there will be a reduction in that cost.

items.statement: Current solar capacity 165 MW; adding 70 MW solar and 10-11 MW waste gas power; average power cost Rs 3.5/unit currently, targeting Rs 3.1/unit
items.quote: different understanding. Our current solar capacity stands at about 145 MW, which is already operational and. Dinesh Gandhi: Now it is 165. Abhishek Agrawal: And another 70 will be in pipeline.
