So, if you want to know the average power cost till date,

items.statement: Pellet production guidance lowered from 2.6 to 2.45 million tons for FY25 due to planned shutdown in Q2
items.quote: Yes. So, there is an annual shutdown plant for one or two plants which will take about 50 years of operation that happens every 4-5 years in cycle. So, that is why we have lowered the guidance in this financial year from 2.6 to 2.45.

items.statement: Supreme Court ruling allows states to levy tax on mineral rights; Jharkhand imposed Rs 100/ton tax; company cannot comment on potential Chhattisgarh impact
items.quote: We should be, to be honest, something we never would like to, but we really can't comment because it is a state matter. It is up to the state government, Jharkhand just passed in the assembly to impose Rs. 100 tax on the mine industry. So, we really can't comment. Hopefully, nothing imposes but if there is an imposition, we have to comply.

items.statement: Increased stake in Alok Ferro Alloys from 78% to 88.34% direct (97.62% including Hira Ferro Alloys)
items.quote: As a part of the group simplification structure, the Company has further increased its stake in Alok Ferro Alloys from 78% to 88.34%. This is direct effect and 97.62% along with this thing held through Hira Ferro Alloys Limited.

items.statement: Raipur Infrastructure JV (non-operational) being wound up; Chhattisgarh Captive Coal Mining JV (non-operational) held for potential recovery; Chhattisgarh Ispat Bhumi is non-profit industrial area management JV
items.quote: Now, Raipur Infrastructure, there are three partners, Sada Energy, Godawari Power and there is a Company called Vanda Global. We are in the process of winding up this Company or distributing whatever surplus funds are there. This JV is not operating, it is nonoperational company, and we are in process of winding it up. In regard to Chhattisgarh Captive Coal Mining, a similar process is being updat

items.statement: Net cash balance of Rs 1,261 crore as on June 30, 2024
items.quote: GPIL had a healthy balance sheet with net balance as on 30th June was Rs. 1,261 crores.

items.statement: Carbon intensity reduced from 2.75 tons CO2 per ton steel in FY22 to 2.43 tons in Q1 FY25; targeting net zero by 2035
items.quote: GPIL has been working towards the Net Zero Carbon Emission, has now let down a clear target of becoming Net-Zero emission by 2015. Last two years, the Company is focusing on maintaining the increased power requirement through capital solar project, which has resulted in carbon reduction from 2.75 tons CO2 per ton of steel in FY22 to 2.43 ton in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Mining and environmental approvals delayed due to elections; confident of approvals by Q3 FY25 but dependent on MOEF and state processes
items.quote: It takes it so long as if we go to MOEF and then to EC from there and it will be taken by the state board. So, the subsidiary side, so many players and due to last month, there was election so getting slightly delayed, but which is we really can't. We are trying our best to move as fast as possible. So, we confidently as committed by Q3, we should have the approvals in place.

items.statement: Structural steel to be supplied to Indian Railways, Power, Discoms; applied for approved vendor status; rolling mill already registered with Railways
items.quote: The structural steel will be partially used for captive manufacturing of galvanized fabricated products for supply to various agencies like Indian Railway, Power, Discom, etc., for which Company has applied to these agencies for approval as the approved vendor for this supply of galvanized product made by the captive rolling mill as well as the steel billets from GPIL existing manufacturing facili

items.statement: Boria Tibu mine to remain non-operational until beneficiation plant ready; targeting commissioning aligned with new steel plant in FY28-29
items.quote: See, as we mentioned last time as well we are working on joining the beneficiation plant inside the mines and start the mine eventually because today mining and bringing the quality of work we are getting, it is not commercially viable. So, we are working on the beneficial plant. We have started working on the desired approval. So, fully I think my once the new steel plant which gets commissioned

items.statement: Q2 FY24 adjusted EBITDA margin 16.5%, up from 14.4% in Q1 and 14.7% a year ago
items.quote: The adjusted EBITDA was 16.5% compared to 14.4% last quarter and 14.7% in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Management targets sustaining adjusted EBITDA in the high 15s to early 16s percent range
items.quote: So, we hope to sustain our margin levels at reasonably in the high 15s or early 16s, kind of levels.

items.statement: Seeing early signs of deal activity across sectors and geographies; optimistic on H2 market sentiment
items.quote: So overall, we are optimistic of the market sentiment improving in the second half of the calendar year. We are seeing early signs of deal activity in the market.

items.statement: Discretionary spend revival unlikely in CY24; budget cycles for next year may drive growth in Q1 CY25
items.quote: Looking at massive or significant increase in discretionary spend this year is a little unrealistic. What we are seeing is where there were project decisions that were pending that were put on hold or people were unsure and were undecided, some of those have opened up, and those are things that we are capturing.

items.statement: Active pipeline with Microsoft Fabric: more than a dozen joint opportunities, one win last quarter, targeting a couple more this quarter
items.quote: We have an active pipeline and I think to define it as a percentage of what our total pipeline is. I don't have those numbers handy, but just to give you a sense, we are talking more than a dozen opportunities in pipe together with Microsoft, where we are jointly going to the customers and providing them a proactive pitch on how they could leverage Fabric.

items.statement: Added more than two dozen new logos company-wide; two new logos from Blackstone portfolio
items.quote: Overall, the Company has added a significant number of logos. We've added more than 2 dozen logos across the Company. And I think we've also added, if I'm not wrong, 2 new logos from a Blackstone portfolio perspective.

items.statement: Top 10 clients contribute ~22% of revenue; top client 5.2%, slight quarterly fluctuation
items.quote: Our top 10 clients are giving us close to 22% of revenues with our top client giving 5.2% in this quarter which is slightly lower than last quarter, but that's mostly a quarterly fluctuation kind of a thing with a minor reduction.

items.statement: Utilization improved to 81-82% from ~76% three quarters ago
items.quote: Our utilization has consistently gone up. There has been a lot of operational rigor and focus on improving utilizations and that number has gone up consistently, quarter-on-quarter. We moved from approximately 76% utilization as of about 3 quarters ago to approximately 81% or 82% utilization.

items.statement: Days sales outstanding at 60 days, within the 60-64 day range
items.quote: Days of sales outstanding has largely been in the range as we have operated between 60 to 64 days. This quarter, we have ended at 60 days and that way our c ollection cycles are running fairly

items.statement: Forward cover of $37.46 million at avg INR 84.5/USD and EUR 2.3 million at avg INR 93.7/EUR
items.quote: As at the year-end, we have a forward cover of $ 37.46 million with average rate of INR 84.5/- and Euro cover of 2.3 million with average rate of INR 93.7/-.

items.statement: Velotio integration operationally complete; merger process pending; OCPS redemption after 2 years; funding via stock swap possible
items.quote: There are optionally convertible preference shares in Velotio which we need to acquire. So, that process will happen. I mean, we will be doing through merger process, which is yet to be initiated. The acquisition will be done based on the performance of Velotio. Those are redeemable after another 2 years.

items.statement: Actively evaluating acquisitions; no fixed size; Blackstone backing provides funding flexibility
items.quote: we are constantly looking, we are open., Yes, there was a sense of that we'll digest Velotio and then move forward. Velotio part, I think we are mostly done. Of course, still the formal process of merger, etc., will take some time. But operationally, we are working well together. So, that part is done. So we'll continue to look for and on the size again, we want it to be meaningful, but again, we

items.statement: Billing rates maintained within same range; no sacrifice for new clients
items.quote: No, not so far. Vinay, thankfully, we have managed to keep our billing rates more or less secure but depending on nature of deals and all whatever we used to do earlier, we're operating within the same range.

items.statement: Launched AI-enabled partner onboarding solution at Boomi World and AI-enabled end-to-end Power BI solutions with migration accelerators
items.quote: From an offering and positioning perspective, we launched an AI-enabled partner onboarding solution at Boomi World 2024, and it is available on our website, and we are also seeing some follow-on activity through that launch. We have also recently launched an AI-enabled end-to-end Power BI solutions, including accelerators for migrating from other BI platforms to Power BI.

items.statement: Revenue INR 4,320 million ($51.8M), up 6.2% YoY; H1 revenue INR 8,487M ($102M), up 4.7% YoY
items.quote: We ended the quarter at INR 4,320 million or INR 432 crores of revenue. In U.S. dollars that translates to $51.8 million, which translates to a year-on-year growth of about 6.2%.

items.statement: Gross margin 35.5% vs 33.7% last quarter and 34.8% a year ago
items.quote: The gross margin was 35.5% compared to 33.7% last quarter and 34.8% same quarter last year.

items.statement: Uncertainty from US elections and Middle East situation could affect sentiment and budgets
items.quote: Very clearly, we'll watch out for the elections in the U.S. and kind of developing situation in the Middle East because those could cause some uncertainty.

items.statement: Annual salary increments rolled out in Q2; hiring in BPM segment to service demand
items.quote: We have given pay hikes during the quarter to our employees, this is the annual salary increment that we usually roll out. And we have absorbed that impact and there were normal operating benefits that we got of about another about 3% to 4%, resulting in the final EBITDA of about INR 714 million or INR 71 crores, which is 16.5%.

items.statement: Acquisition funding options open including stock swap; Blackstone backing provides flexibility
items.quote: This could be a stock swap in which pursuant to those preference shares, R Systems shares may be issued. subject to our shareholders' approval in due course of time.

items.statement: Tax expense increased due to INR 6.2 crore provision on dividends from subsidiary; eligible for offset upon dividend declaration
items.quote: Our tax expense was INR 21.9 crores this quarter as against INR 8.9 crores last quarter. Increased tax expense is mainly due to tax provision of INR 6.2 crores against dividends received from subsidiary company. The Company would be eligible to offset this upon dividend declaration.

items.statement: TCV/ACV disclosure targeted in 1-2 quarters once internal processes aligned
items.quote: Sure. I think Vinay, that has been an old ask. So, I think probably we need another 1 or 2 quarters, to get it in final shape for getting it aligned with other companies as well. So, maybe we'll need another 1 or 2 quarters before we start doing that.

items.statement: Management expects continued quarter-on-quarter improvement but cannot provide visibility due to challenging conditions
items.quote: We have been improving quarter-on-quarter, let's see how does it work out.

items.statement: Domestic demand increase ahead of festival season is lower than expected
items.quote: We are witnessing a lower-than-expected increase in demand ahead of the festival season.

items.statement: Gross margin improved to 44%, up 4% quarter-on-quarter
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 44%, which is higher by 4% on a quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Home textile exports growing 5-10%
items.quote: Exports, if I say, it's about 5%, 10% growth in export numbers.

items.statement: Dropped planned INR 800-900 crore project due to lack of market visibility; only routine capex continuing
items.quote: We have already dropped that because it was INR 800-900 crores project. And since the visibility of the textile market is not there, and we may think of something else, we keep on evaluating.

items.statement: No new plant being set up; only routine maintenance capex ongoing
items.quote: No new plant is being put up right now.

items.statement: Geopolitical tensions causing volatility in raw material prices and rising energy costs
items.quote: Geopolitical tensions have disrupted the global supply chain and caused significant volatility in raw material prices impacting the man-made fiber industry.

items.statement: Exports constitute about one-third of business; high ocean freights and geopolitical challenges affecting export markets
items.quote: For exports, we are about 1/3 always in the exports. So ocean freights are very high. There are so many geo-political challenges.

items.statement: Long-term debt reduced by INR 22 crores and working capital borrowing reduced by INR 27 crores; debt-to-equity at 0.81
items.quote: Total long-term debt further reduced by INR 22 crores and working capital borrowing also reduced by INR 27 crores in Q1 FY25. Our debt-to-equity is maintained constantly below 1, around 0.81 as of now.

items.statement: Launching 12 new home textile collections annually; maintaining 50-60 collections in market with 5-year lifecycle
items.quote: We have already launched 36 collections and every year we are launching 12 new collections. So this year also, we will be launching 12 new collections and normally one collection has a life cycle of 5 years.

items.statement: No subsidy on green fiber unit; plant already operational and preferred for sustainability
items.quote: No, there is no subsidy on green fiber, except that it is preferred fiber because of sustainability. So that is already there. Plant is already working.

items.statement: Short-term outlook hazy due to geopolitical tensions, Red Sea crisis, Bangladesh turmoil, and recession fears in USA
items.quote: At present the outlook for the short term is little h azy. As I mentioned i n my opening remarks, there are a lot of geopolitical tensions are going on

items.statement: EBITDA improved to INR 25 crores from INR 13 crores in Q4 FY24
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was INR 25 crores as against INR 13 crores in Q4 FY24.

items.statement: Bangladesh is an important export market for cotton and cotton blended melange; factories normalizing there
items.quote: As I mentioned say in export markets, say in cotton and cotton blended melange, Bangladesh is one of our important market.

items.statement: Working capital borrowing reduced by INR 27 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Total long-term debt further reduced by INR 22 crores and working capital borrowing also reduced by INR 27 crores in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Management targets at least Rs 8,500 crore of sales for FY25.
items.quote: in this year we would be targeting a sale of at least about 8,500 crores and that's what we would continue to aim for.

items.statement: Management expects at least 6 million sq ft of launches in the remaining three quarters of FY25, taking full-year launches to about 9 million sq ft.
items.quote: remaining three quarters we should be able to do at least 6 million square feet. There is an upside potential to this definitely, but this is the number that we think we can surely do.

items.statement: Unsold inventory stands at 9.24 million sq ft; residential launch pipeline of 17.9 million sq ft across 16 projects in 7 cities to be launched over next six to eight quarters.
items.quote: currently we have 9.24 million square feet of unsold inventory. This gives us a great visibility for our teams to work on sales for the remaining years in addition to the planned launches for the next nine months.

items.statement: Future project pipeline from existing land bank and new deals estimated at 25-30 million sq ft, largely in Bangalore, with potential in Mumbai and Noida over 1.5-3 years.
items.quote: The current potential of these projects is about 30 million square feet. We will share the details of these projects as we move into forthcoming projects from time-to-time. The expected timeline to br ing these projects into launch stage is between one and a half to three

items.statement: Demand outlook steady across operating cities with supply catching up; NCR contributed 45.5% of Q1 sales value (Rs 852 cr) for the first time, overtaking Bangalore.
items.quote: The demand outlook in all our operating cities continues to be steady with supply catching up to the demand.

items.statement: Q1 saw highest-ever price realization due to shift toward high-ticket launches (>Rs 5 cr); remaining 18 million sq ft pipeline skewed to mid-income apartments of 1,800-2,000 sq ft.
items.quote: SOBHA's overall price realization in Q1 FY25 was the highest ever. This is because of the significant shift in our product mix aided by the recent launches.

items.statement: Project-level EBITDA margins on sales done in FY23, FY24 and Q1 FY25 exceed 30%; reported margins to improve steadily from next quarter and more meaningfully from FY26 as higher-margin revenue is recognized.
items.quote: our EBITDA margins at project level should be more than 30%. So, hence they will recover as we recognize these revenues in the coming years.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 44.5 cr incurred in Q1; Rs 161 cr invested in growth (likely land/development).
items.quote: We have invested in CAPEX close to 44.5 crores while higher due to start of construction of recently launched projects. During the quarter we have invested 161 crores in line with our growth focus.

items.statement: Quarterly collections hit record Rs 1,546 cr (real estate Rs 1,392 cr); net operating cash flow Rs 327 cr, up 68% YoY.
items.quote: Total collection from all the business amounted to Rs.1,546 crores in this quarter. Of this, about 1,392 crores were contributed by real estate businesses marking it the highest ever quarterly achievement as well as in our operating history.

items.statement: 15th consecutive quarter of net debt reduction; net debt down Rs 74 cr to ~Rs 1,200 cr; debt-equity 0.47x; post-rights net debt seen ~Rs 300 cr.
items.quote: These are 15 consecutive quarters of debt reduction. We reduced our net debt by 74 crores in the quarter and now our debt-equity is 0.47.

items.statement: Rights issue raised Rs 2,000 cr (1.21 mn shares at Rs 1,651, 1.39x subscribed); first tranche Rs 1,000 cr received; remaining tranches within 18 months.
items.quote: As you are aware, recently we have raised 2,000 crores through the capital market. We have issued 1.21 million shares at the rate Rs.1,651 per share and the rights issue was subscribed 1.39 times.

items.statement: GIFT City realizations risen from ~Rs 6,500 to ~Rs 10,000 over 4-5 years; new project launched at ~Rs 12,000/sq ft with strong traction.
items.quote: In the past four to five years particularly, we have seen an increase in the realization from earlier 6,500 to close to about 10,000. So, the new project that we launched is at about 12,000 and we are seeing decent traction.

items.statement: Completed 0.92 mn sq ft (564 units) in Q1; on track for ~5 mn sq ft deliveries in FY25 vs ~4 mn sq ft in FY24.
items.quote: we are on track to complete about 5 million square feet versus about 4 million square feet in the previous financial year.

items.statement: SOBHA share of forthcoming 18 mn sq ft pipeline estimated at 76-80%; JD partner share 20-24%.
items.quote: overall SOBHA share would be about in the range of 76% to 80%.

items.statement: RERA account restrictions limit cash extraction from owned-land projects, keeping gross debt ~Rs 2,000 cr despite strong collections.
items.quote: for owned land projects, it's far lower that we can take out. So, hence what number that you are seeing in terms of the cash that's lying in the books, that will be largely towards in the RERA accounts.

items.statement: Revenue recognition lagged in Q1 due to OC delays (partly election-related); expected to normalize from Q2 as OCs received post-quarter.
items.quote: delays in obtaining OCs have affected our revenue recognition and hence, going forward, the revenue recognition would be in a little lagged manner for the remainder of the financial year.

items.statement: Estimated margin cash flow from residential business Rs 16,200 cr (Rs 9,994 cr ongoing + Rs 6,210 cr forthcoming) for sales and marketing expense.
items.quote: we have an estimated margin cash flow of Rs.16,200 crores to be realized for sale s and marketing expense. Of this, Rs.9,994 crores is expected to come from our ongoing project s and balance 6,210 crores from our forthcoming projects

items.statement: Promoter holding increased ~0.5% in rights issue; no management changes mentioned.
items.quote: the promoters' share has gone up by about 0.5%.

items.statement: Contract revenue steady; management to de-emphasize civil contracts to focus resources on real estate and backward-integrated model.
items.quote: Our contract revenue is steady for the quarter and going forward we would deemphasize on civil contracts projects owing to the increase in scale of our operations in real estate.

items.statement: Operating environment stable with early signs of rural consumption uptick expected to boost overall consumption in coming quarters
items.quote: The operating environment in Q 1 remains stable and largely consistent with the preceding quarters. We are yet to witness significant improvement in consumption, though there are early signs of positive indicators. An uptick in rural consumption is engaging and is expected to provide an impetus to overall consumption in coming quarters.

items.statement: No price increase expected in current financial year due to stable input costs
items.quote: So, the input cost has been largely stable, in fact the cotton prices are quite stable on the lower side, so we don't see any input cost, especially in the fabric and yarn creating a pressure that can lead us to any price increase. So, current financial year, as of now, there is every reason to believe that there will be no price increase in the current financial year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin at 19% in Q1; annual operating margin expected within 18-21% range
items.quote: EBITDA margin was 19% with stable raw material costs. Margins have remained healthy, though there was marketing spends for the cricketing season in the Q1.

items.statement: Marketing spend to remain at 4-5% of net revenue annually; EBITDA margin expected 18-21% for the year
items.quote: So, typically on the marketing side, we spend around 4% to 5% of our net revenue, and that's what will continue. So, that's on an annual basis, in a quarterly level there can be some variation, but overall, for the year, it will get 4% to 5% levels. And the overall operating margin at EBITDA level, we have done around 19% current quarter, it should be largely there, within the 18% to 21% even at t

items.statement: Orissa plant nearing completion with initial production expected in Q4 FY25; no backward integration capex this year
items.quote: While the Orissa plant is nearing completion, and we should be getting into initial production days in the last quarter of this year.

items.statement: Current planned capacity 200 million pieces; total capacity 260 million with outsourcing; Odisha and Mysore units coming up
items.quote: So, currently, our planned capacity is around 200 million pieces, and our current expansion plan with increase in efficiency, we do not have immediate plans of any additional manufacturing facility. While the Orissa plant is nearing completion, and we should be getting into initial production days in the last quarter of this year.

items.statement: Manufacturing capacity 200 million pieces in-house, 60 million outsourced for total 260 million
items.quote: Manufacturing capacity, we currently have a capacity for around 200 million pieces, and with outsourcing we can go up to 260 and we are continuously working on expansion.

items.statement: Distributor inventory days reduced by over 6 days overall, over 10 days for athleisure since auto-replenishment started
items.quote: From the time we have started auto replenishment as a process for primary billing to our distributors, our inventory levels have now come down by about little over six days at an overall level. Of course, it's a lot more pronounced for the athleisure, more than 10 days of inventory has been reduced at the distributor level.

items.statement: Channel inventory at ~20 million pieces; inventory days down but absolute levels similar due to Q1 seasonality
items.quote: There's not been much of a decrease from an absolute point of view, however Q1 typically is a high contributing quarter for us. From that standpoint, the number of days of inventory has come down, whereas the absolute inventory holding will remain more or less similar to what I had mentioned earlier.

items.statement: Inventory days improved to 72 from 93 at end of FY24; working capital days at 73
items.quote: Inventory days was 72 as against 93 days in end of FY 24. Focus on healthier inventory in the distribution network has resulted in maintaining optimum inventory levels. Working capital days was 73 days, and it was in line with PAT in the end of FY24.

items.statement: Company remains debt-free
items.quote: We continue to remain debt free.

items.statement: Input costs stable; cotton prices on lower side; no price increase expected in FY25
items.quote: So, the input cost has been largely stable, in fact the cotton prices are quite stable on the lower side, so we don't see any input cost, especially in the fabric and yarn creating a pressure that can lead us to any price increase.

items.statement: Realization improved ~1% due to category mix and premium ranges outperforming mid-premium
items.quote: We have seen both. It is a function of category mix, and also within categories, we have seen the premium ranges perform better than the mid premium ranges.

items.statement: E-commerce grew 32% in Q1; D2C margins slightly lower than B2B due to marketing and delivery costs
items.quote: The e-commerce channel had a growth of 32% in Q 1, reflecting evolving consumer purchasing preferences and the commitment to cloistering our online presence.

items.statement: E-commerce margins comparable to offline overall; D2C slightly lower than B2B
items.quote: E-commerce as a whole, the margins are more or less comparable with the offline business, whereas within the e-commerce, D2C have slightly lesser margins because the spends in marketing, even the delivery cost are slightly higher, but largely they are comparable.

items.statement: Tier 3/4 towns growing faster than metros and Tier 1/2; growth consistent across North, South, East, West
items.quote: We are definitely seeing better growth rates in smaller town when compared to metros, and this is in fact inversely proportional to the size of the town. So, tier three and tier four towns are seeing better growth rates when compared to metros, tier ones and Tier-2s.

items.statement: Metros and Tier 1 contribute ~50% of business; Tier 2+ contribute late 40s%
items.quote: So, metros and tier one, the way we classify it, contribute to little over a 50% of our business and Tier-2 downwards are in the late 40s in terms of.

items.statement: Price gap with competitors reduced as Jockey held prices for 24 months; no sub-brand planned but value products launched under Jockey
items.quote: Firstly, in the last couple of years, if at all, from what we study of competition and who we consider our target audience, the available brand and Jockey, the gap is only reduced because J ockey has stuck to its prices for the last 24 months. T he last price increase that was initiated by the brand was back in July 22 and we are exactly about two years since we have touched our prices

items.statement: No plan for sub-brand; value price points addressed under Jockey brand with new athleisure products
items.quote: As far as the second question is concerned, there is no plan for the launch of a sub brand at least. But of course, if there is an opportunity for us to hit value price points with our products without compromising on quality or consumer experience t hat is something we strive to do . With some level of input cost reductions that have been favorable to the brand there have been a few products stra

items.statement: International expansion planned for medium term; focusing on select geographies with market understanding first
items.quote: We are looking to consolidate our international presence. There are a few markets which lend itself to the products that we make here for India and become a natural extension in terms of placing us there. There is specific focus towards those geographies, I believe in the coming years we should see some level of focused approach towards our international business.

items.statement: Interim dividend of Rs.300 declared; dividend policy remains 50% of PAT; future payouts depend on cash balance and capex needs
items.quote: Our dividend distribution policy remains the same. So, we plan to pay 50% of our PAT as a policy.

items.statement: Employee count down ~16% YoY due to unfilled attrition; productivity up 12-13%; subcontractor cost halved due to inventory optimization
items.quote: We are trying, so it's a combination, you are right we are more productive, productivity has improved by more than 12%, 13% that means the outputs have increased. We have not reduced manpower; we are now normal attrition.

items.statement: Sales volumes 57.4 million pieces, up 2.6% YoY; revenue Rs.12,775 million, up 3.9% YoY; PAT Rs.1,652 million, up 4.3% YoY
items.quote: So, to take you through the highlights of key Financial Highlights in Q1, we recorded sales volumes of 57 .4 million pieces, a growth of 2.6% year -on-year. Revenue in quarter one was Rs.12,775 million, which was a growth of 3.9% year-on-year. EBITDA for the period was Rs.2433 million, which was a growth of 2% over the last quarter. EBITDA margin was 19% with stable raw material costs. Margins hav

items.statement: $1 billion revenue target by FY26 likely tough; recasting 3-5 year plan for realistic trajectory
items.quote: Gaurav, you are right it may be tough to achieve the target at that speed, because this was, we projected this number way back then we had the volatility during the pandemic, and then we had the last year a challenging year for retail across brands. So, we have to consider all this, and then we need to recast the numbers and look at a more realistic trajectory for us. And we are actually working o

items.statement: Bangladesh sourcing minimal (~few thousand pieces/month); healthy inventory and multi-vendor strategy mitigate disruption risk
items.quote: No, because we import very small quantity few 1000 pieces per month from Bangladesh. And those SKUs are actually having very healthy inventory in our warehouses. And today, I got an update that factory which is actually supplying for this is back in operation, so we don't foresee any risk at all.

items.statement: Secondary and tertiary demand ahead of primary; expect primaries and secondaries to align in couple of quarters if demand sustains
items.quote: In quarter one, we have seen secondary and tertiary numbers to be ahead of primary. That's a reflection of the inventory holding in the value chain. So, we have seen better secondar ies and primaries when compared to what we have reported as primary. And, I repeat myself if the demand continues the way it is, if quarter one is any reflection of what we expect in the future, then it will take us an

items.statement: Accessories portfolio (socks, towels, caps, etc.) contributes high single digits; independent sales vertical created
items.quote: Even the current portfolio of accessories that we hold is quite substantial, and hence we move to have an independent sales vertical addressing only this vertical. Within accessories today, we include our categories like socks, towels, caps, handkerchiefs and face masks which has little relevance today, but forms a part of our portfolio.

items.statement: Exclusive brand store expansion target 150-180 stores/year; modern retail expansion dependent on partner plans
items.quote: We also categorize our exclusive brand stores under modern retail, there it's a stated strategy that we look to expand anywhere between 150 to 180 stores every year. That's the plan we have for this year as well.

items.statement: Management expects double-digit EBITDA margin and healthy, substantial topline growth for FY25, targeting around Rs 2,000 crore revenue.
items.quote: But certainly we should be going into the double digits for the EBITDA margin and growth of topline also will be healthy and substantial as we had guided for the year. So, we are on target for that, to get to that around 2,000 mark.

items.statement: Global industrial growth stable but hampered by weaker demand; US demand resilient, China stagnant, Europe soft, Latin America returning to normalcy.
items.quote: Global industrial growth was stable but remained hampered by weaker global demand in many of our markets. Regional demand remains resilient in USA. China seems to be stagnant and struggling with its local economic weakness. Softness in Europe is more than evident as you know.

items.statement: Blends revenue grew 13.4% QoQ; management expects this momentum to continue through the year, strengthening overall revenues.
items.quote: The revenue from blends have grown at a rate of 13.4% as compared to last quarter. We expect that this momentum continues during the year, resulting in strengthening the overall revenues.

items.statement: Anti-dumping action initiated by US and European manufacturers against Chinese Vanillin dumping; US action likely before EU, timeframe 2-6 months; already seeing positive impact as buyers develop alternative supply.
items.quote: the initiation of anti -dumping action by local manufacturers in US and Europe against the dumping and predatory pricing by Chinese manufacturers is likely to have a positive impact on our business whe never this anti-dumping regulation is promulgated by the US and European governments

items.statement: New Methyl Vanillin campaign commenced end of May, achieving process stability and product quality; validation ongoing with encouraging customer response.
items.quote: The new campaign of Methyl Vanillin was commenced as we had declared in the last investor call also by the end of May. This new campaign has resulted in process stability as well as quality of the product.

items.statement: Acquired Vitafor Invest NV, Belgium on June 11, 2024; manufacturing near Antwerp, caters to animal feed, nutritional products, hygiene and disinfectants; synergy with blends business geographically and product-wise.
items.quote: As you are aware, we acquired Vitafor Invest NV, Belgium on June 11, 2024. This acquisition paves way to the group to extend its blends and related businesses in Northern Africa and other East European markets through the Vitafor subsidiary network.

items.statement: Finance cost increased due to Rs 6.5 crore foreign exchange loss from currency depreciation in some geographies, not due to higher borrowing costs.
items.quote: The interest portion includes foreign exchange and you can go and see in my results, you will see that finance cost includes consolidated around Rs. 6.5 crores of foreign exchange. And that has moved the increases.

items.statement: Overall borrowing costs have not increased; finance cost rise driven by foreign exchange volatility, not interest rate hikes.
items.quote: The borrowing costs have not increased. Do you see there has been a foreign exchange hit in some of our geographies on finance cost because of the depreciation of their currencies.

items.statement: Vitafor acquisition current run rate ~1 million Euros/month topline with low EBITDA margin; expected to improve to levels seen in other geographies over next few quarters.
items.quote: I think currently the run rate is abo ut a million Euros a month, topline and low EBITDA margin. I think that will improve as we go along in the next few quarters to more like what we see in the other geographies

items.statement: Tax expense at 47% in Q1 due to conservative no deferred tax on Europe loss; full-year effective tax rate expected 25-30%.
items.quote: Overall, tax expense should be in the range of 25% to 30%.

items.statement: Operating efficiency improvement program underway, expected to yield a few percentage points improvement to support full-year guidance.
items.quote: Also on the operating side, operating efficiencies, we are working on a program to improve the operating efficiencies, which should give us a few percentage points improvement.

items.statement: Lockheed Martin commercial battery commissioning this year; substantial potential in 2-3 years but too early to estimate near-term contribution.
items.quote: Martin is actually, they are commissioning their first commercial battery, which will happen during this year. Thereafter, they will look at commercializing, in a sense, try and scale it up. I think it's too early in the day to estimate what that business will look like in the near future

items.statement: Targets 4 MMT+ crude oil and 5 BCM gas within next 2-3 years; plans 78 wells in FY25 and 100 wells in FY26/FY27
items.quote: we can very much assure you that the trajectory we have projected in the last year is, in fact, and we have been moving in that trajectory only.

items.statement: Expects $0.25/MMBtu increase in APM gas price from April 2025
items.quote: as per the guidelines that will be increasing by $0.25 from first April '25.

items.statement: Capex for FY25: Oil India INR6,880 crore, NRL INR9,650 crore
items.quote: For Oil India, it is -- '24, '25, it is INR6,880 crores. That is the Cap ex. The NRL '24, '25 is available, INR9,650 crores.

items.statement: NRL expansion project cost INR28,000 crore, 65% physical progress, completion by December 2025; INR19,000 crore already invested
items.quote: this cost for this NRL is -- this is INR28,000 crores. Currently, the physical progress is 65%. And we are expecting that the completion will be by end 2025, that is December 2025.

items.statement: NRL expansion to add 2 MMSCMD gas demand; first year ramp-up 50-60%, reaching 100% by FY27
items.quote: For NRL, it will be close to, once the expansion is received and the production would be 2 MMSCMD for expanded capability.

items.statement: Indradhanush Gas Grid first sales expected by December 2024; north bank connection near Tezpur completed via micro tunneling
items.quote: This pipeline, we are expecting the first sales by December this year.

items.statement: Gas production affected by cyclic demand and offtaker constraints; North East Gas Grid completion by end of 2024 to enable 5 BCM gas production
items.quote: once we -- and North East Gas Grid is in place, which we are expecting by end of this year, there will be no interruption in gas production, and we'll be able to increase our gas production to the 5 BCM level

items.statement: Average crude oil realization Q1 FY25 USD 84.89/bbl (+10.46% YoY); gas price unchanged at USD 6.5/MMBtu
items.quote: average crude oil price realization for Q1 FY '25 is USD 84.89 per barrel, vis -a-vis, USD 76.85 per barrel for Q1 of FY '24, increased by 10.46%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin Q1 FY25 43.79% vs 53.49% YoY; decline due to SAED increase from USD2.59 to USD10.27/bbl and INR204 crore GST on royalty provision
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Q1 FY '25 is 43.79%, vis -a-vis, 53.49% for Q1 FY '24. The reduction in EBITDA margin is mainly due to the increase in SAED from USD2.59 per barrel in Q1 FY '24 to USD10.27 per barrel in Q1 FY '25

items.statement: GST on royalty provision INR3,300 crore total; Supreme Court 9-judge bench ruling on MMDR Act does not directly apply; separate judgment needed

items.statement: Adjusted ROCE over 20% sustained long-term; PAT margin 17% in Q1 FY25 vs 10% YoY
items.quote: The adjusted ROCE of the business is over 20%-plus over the period, and the same will be sustained in a long-term basis.

items.statement: GTRE/DRDO engine program confidential; platforms not disclosed; qualification timelines for Rolls-Royce/Siemens parts by CY25, revenue from FY26
items.quote: Those qualifications will be done by calendar year '25 and the revenue you can see from FY '26 for these components.

items.statement: Targeting INR 1,000 crore revenue in FY25 with 18% EBITDA margin; Q1 behind but confident to get close
items.quote: That's the objective, Prathik. Q1, we are a little behind. We are hopeful we can make it up. The whole idea is if you aim big, you will get close to the target. So it's an aggressive goal but as of now, at the end of Q1, we are confident that we'll get close to it, if not at it.

items.statement: Revenue gap of INR 150 crore to reach INR 1,000 crore target including Augmento; weighted pipeline INR 50 crore
items.quote: If I look at our pipeline today, Vikas and our order book, we have from a INR 1,000 crores, we have a gap of INR 150 crores. This is including Augmento.

items.statement: Augmento did INR 45 crore last year; targeting 33% YoY growth; two large Hi-tech clients (Fortune 100 and Fortune 5000) for wallet share expansion
items.quote: Augmento has 2 fairly large customers. One is a Fortune 100 company, the other is a Fortune 5,000 company, and which are both Hi-tech, lots of technology spend. And we are very confident that we can increase our share of wallet in both these accounts

items.statement: Future acquisitions limited to small capability players due to capital constraints; no big plays planned
items.quote: We're always talking to potential targets, hopeful something will come out. But, you know, we don't have that much money with us now to make a big play. So it will be a if whatever we do will be a small capability player. Nothing else.

items.statement: Focusing on 4 high-growth verticals: Fintech, Hi-Tech Media & Utilities, Transport & Logistics, Retail E-commerce; first three seeing high tech spend
items.quote: We have reorganized our business into 4 high growth business units, making us more market facing and customer focused. These business units are Fintec h, Hi -tech Media and Utilities, Transport and Logistics and Retail e - commerce

items.statement: Fintech remains hot in payment tech, credit tech, regulatory tech; India funding tremendous but startup payment risk exists
items.quote: Fintech should not be confused with BFSI. The trend in BFSI is an improvement. Fintech has always been hot because those are the disruptors in the BFSI industry. These are organizations, which are focused on credit tech. These are organizations that are focused on payment tech as well as regulatory tech, our focus is there.

items.statement: Healthtech/MedTech parked; not focusing excessively after previous attempt didn't work out
items.quote: Correct. That didn't work out. And, I think this is a sector, which we are sort of parked, not going to focus on it excessively for now.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 17.43%; targeting 18% for FY25; Augmento expected to deliver 20%+ margin
items.quote: The EBITDA stood at INR 35 crores, which grew by around 1% YoY and 5% QoQ, with the EBITDA margins being at 17.43%.

items.statement: Confident of maintaining 18% EBITDA target despite 3 new sales hires in June; Augmento's higher margin to offset costs
items.quote: Yes. You're looking at it correctly because we're hopeful Augmento will give us a better EBITDA than the company wide.

items.statement: Utilization at 85% (excl. training), maxed out; only 100-200 bps variation expected
items.quote: I think this is pretty much maxed out. Maybe 100-200 basis points in either direction is probably what you will see, but 85% is pretty much where we will remain.

items.statement: Main billing rate improvement lever is INR/USD currency benefit; no other pricing tailwinds mentioned
items.quote: One big area they'll come from is our finance minister, if the rupee dollar benefits.

items.statement: 15 clients >$1M revenue, 9 clients $500K-$1M; added Fortune 100 Hi-tech client in California and Fintech credit tech client in US
items.quote: I'm happy to inform that we have bagged a high-tech company in California as our customer, a Fortune 100 company and also a Fintech U.S. Customer in the credit tech space, which we have been targeting for the last 15 years has finally opened up.

items.statement: US revenue focus: targeting 45-75% mix (currently 42%); hired 3 US salespeople (1 in CA 7 months ago, 2 in June), 1 UK hire from Accenture
items.quote: In terms of U.S. revenue, all our focus, all our investment is happening in the U.S. market towards the objective of getting 45-75 because that's our biggest market, that's the most lucrative market, and that's the most forgiving, rewarding market, call it in any way, and the deepest market.

items.statement: Hired 3 US salespeople (California, New York) and 1 UK senior from Accenture in June/July; CA hire brought Fortune 100 Hi-tech deal after 7 months
items.quote: We have hired 3 new sales guys in the U.S. 1 is the guy who brought this Hi-tech company and this was 7 months ago, and 2 have joined in the month of June. They have joined in the month of June. So very recent hires, 1 in California, 1 in New York. And then we've got one guy who's joined us, another senior person who's joined us in the UK. He comes to us from Sweden. He was with Accenture there an

items.statement: Revenue split: Digital engineering 45%, QA/testing 15%, balance data & infrastructure; white spaces in cyber security, digital product engineering, data analytics
items.quote: So Amit, digital engineering, which is a product capability, that shows almost 45% of our revenues. The QA and the testing, that's about 15% and the balance comes between data and infrastructure.

items.statement: Sales approach is business-outcome led, not technology-led; operate in 3 Fintech sub-verticals: payment tech, regulatory tech, credit tech
items.quote: Honestly, the focus is not that so much. The focus really is how can we Amit, the way we sell is not technology focused, we sell business focused. In other words, take the case of Fintech. We go to potential customers or prospects in Fintech and the way we approach them is we say, look, in the last 3 years or 4 years, we have solved these business challenges.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue INR 201 crore (+10% YoY, +3% QoQ); EBITDA INR 35 crore (+1% YoY, +5% QoQ); PAT INR 26 crore (+2% YoY, +10.3% QoQ)
items.quote: For the first quarter of FY25, revenues were reported at around INR 201 crores, representing a growth of around 10% YoY and 3% QoQ. The EBITDA stood at INR 35 crores, which grew by around 1% YoY and 5% QoQ, with the EBITDA margins being at 17.43%. Net profit for the quarter was around INR 26 crores, which grew by around 2% YoY and 10.3% QoQ, with the profit after tax margins reported at 12.73%.

items.statement: Geography split: Americas 42%, Europe 24%, APAC/others 34%; Onsite 45%, Offshore 55%
items.quote: For the revenue split by geography, in the current quarter of FY25, the Americas contributed 42% of our total revenues. Europe contributed 24%, while the remaining 34% came from Asia Pacific and other regions. The on -site revenue mix was 45% and the offshore was 55%.

items.statement: Vertical split: Hi-Tech Media & Utilities 42%, Fintech 31%, Transport & Logistics 16%, Retail E-commerce 11%
items.quote: The revenue split across our verticals for Q1 FY25 is as follows. Fintech contributed about 31%, Hi -Tech, Media and Utilities a round 42%, Transport and Logistics contributed 16% and Retail e -commerce contributed 11%.

items.statement: Positioned as Tier 3 IT services co targeting Tier 2 by 2030; nimbler than Tier 1/2 to beat market avg growth via high-growth vertical bets and partner ecosystem
items.quote: I would classify ourselves as a Tier 3 technology services company, not a Tier 1 for sure and neither a Tier 2. Our aspirations are to get to a Tier 2 by 2030.

items.statement: Partner ecosystem strategy: targeting early partnerships with emerging 'future star' tech companies (e.g., Snowflake-like) for SI revenue; current hyper-scaler partnerships (Salesforce, ServiceNow) yield no deals as late entrants
items.quote: What we are missing is, a new star partnering with them early so that we can ride onto their or hang onto their coat tails.

items.statement: Board proposed 1:4 bonus shares to commemorate 25th anniversary
items.quote: Lastly, I'm pleased to inform you that to commemorate our company's 25th anniversary, the Board of Directors have proposed issuance of bonus shares in the ratio of 1:4 to all

items.statement: Fintech startup client concentration risk: payments dependent on funding cycles; must stay on top of collections
items.quote: What we have to be careful about is, and this is a fine line that we have to ride is, since a lot of these are startups, we have to be careful that w e don't get stuck with them. When we provide technology services to them, payments we've got to stay on top of payments as well as their funding because they are based on their spending is based on their funding patterns. That's the risk there

items.statement: Institutional investor interest low (FII ~4%, no large MFs); structured IR outreach planned with Mumbai focus
items.quote: not much interest from institutional investors, only thing that we see is a Saksoft Ltd 16 08.08.2024 Earnings Conference Call lot of calls. We have a call scheduled in September with HDFC Securities. They have shown some interest. Last month, we had a call with Kotak Securities. They had shown a lot of interest and lot of their clients; especially PMS clients were on the call. As of today, we hav

items.statement: Target Jeevansathi breakeven in FY25 with high growth; target Shiksha breakeven or profit in FY25; continue investing in 99acres even if losses persist
items.quote: In Jeevansathi we are targeting breakeven this year. So we would like to get as close to breakeven as possible. At the same time, we're targeting high growth because we've started monetizing more aggressively.

items.statement: Continue investing in recruitment verticals (JobHai, AmbitionBox, iimjobs, hirist, Naukri Gulf) and Naukri marketing despite slow growth
items.quote: Even in recruitment, we will continue, we continue to invest in our JobHai business. We continue to invest behind the AmbitionBox platform. We continue to invest behind iimjob and hirist.

items.statement: Standalone operating margin 36% in Q1FY25; recruitment operating margin 54% in Q1FY25
items.quote: Operating profits at a standalone level grew by 9% Y-o-Y to Rs. 227 crores, and the operating margin was 36%.

items.statement: Recruitment operating profit down 3% YoY to Rs. 255 crore, margin 54% due to IPL campaigns and strategic investments
items.quote: Consequently, the operating profits were lower by 3% Y-o-Y to Rs. 255 crores and the operating profit margin was 54%.

items.statement: 99acres operating losses reduced 39% YoY to Rs. 14 crore; cash losses down 54% YoY to Rs. 19 crore
items.quote: Operating losses reduced by 39% to Rs. 14 crores and cash losses from operations were Rs. 19 crores, Y-o-Y reduction of 54%.

items.statement: Jeevansathi operating losses reduced 88% YoY to Rs. 2 crore; cash loss Rs. 4 crore, down 79% YoY
items.quote: Operating losses were reduced by 88% Y-o-Y to Rs. 2 crores. Cash loss was Rs. 4 crores, a Y-o-Y improvement of 79%.

items.statement: Shiksha operating profit Rs. 4 crore vs loss of Rs. 1 crore YoY; cash generation Rs. 7 crore vs Rs. 30 lakh YoY
items.quote: We made an operating profit of Rs. 4 crores last quarter versus a loss of Rs. 1 crore in the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Non-IT recruitment billings grew 14% YoY driven by healthcare, infrastructure, transport, real estate, media & telecom
items.quote: Growth momentum in the Non-IT segment continued, with billings growing at 14% year on year. This was largely driven by sectors such as healthcare and life sciences, infrastructure, transport, real estate and media & telecom.

items.statement: IT recruitment billings growth moderated to mid-single digits; consultant segment low single-digit growth after four quarters of decline
items.quote: Billings growth in the IT segment also continued this quarter. Though the growth rate was actually moderated compared to the previous quarters and was in mid-single digits.

items.statement: Niche verticals strong: iimjobs 26%, NaukriGulf 25%, Naukri Fast Forward 29% YoY billings growth
items.quote: Our niche and adjacent business verticals, including iimjobs, NaukriGulf, and Naukri Fast Forward also maintained healthy billings growth with Y-o-Y increases of 26%, 25%, and 29%, respectively.

items.statement: 99acres traffic up 23% YoY, daily active users up 33% YoY; new project sales flat sequentially, up ~10% YoY in top 8 cities
items.quote: Overall traffic on the user side in 99acres grew by 23% Y-o-Y, driven by growth in new projects and resale traffic. Our daily active users on the app grew by 33% Y-o-Y in Q1.

items.statement: Jeevansathi billings and revenue grew 35% YoY to Rs. 25 crore and Rs. 26 crore; acceptances and two-way chats show healthy growth
items.quote: In Jeevansathi, the momentum continued in billings growth. Billings grew by 35% to Rs. 25 crores, and revenue also grew by 35% to Rs. 26 crores.

items.statement: Standalone billings Rs. 579 crore (+11% YoY), revenue Rs. 639 crore (+9% YoY); including subsidiaries billings Rs. 596 crore, revenue Rs. 655 crore
items.quote: In Q1FY25, our standalone billings were Rs. 579 crores, a Y-o-Y growth of 11% and revenue was Rs. 639 crores, a Y-o-Y growth of 9%.

items.statement: Recruitment billings Rs. 431 crore (+9% YoY), revenue Rs. 472 crore (+6% YoY); cash from operations Rs. 190 crore
items.quote: In Q1FY25, recruitment billings grew by 9% to Rs. 431 crore, and revenue grew by 6% to Rs. 472 crore.

items.statement: 99acres billings Rs. 81 crore (+10% YoY), revenue Rs. 99 crore (+20% YoY); broker billings growing faster than developer
items.quote: In 99acres, billing growth moderated to 10% to Rs. 81 crores, while revenue grew by 20% to Rs. 99 crores.

items.statement: Jeevansathi billings Rs. 25 crore (+35% YoY), revenue Rs. 26 crore (+35% YoY)
items.quote: Billings grew by 35% to Rs. 25 crores, and revenue also grew by 35% to Rs. 26 crores.

items.statement: Shiksha billings Rs. 42 crore (+25% YoY), revenue Rs. 42 crore (+18% YoY)
items.quote: In Q1FY25, billings grew by 25% to Rs. 42 crores while revenue grew by 18% to Rs. 42 crores.

items.statement: Cash balance Rs. 4,255 crore (including wholly owned subsidiaries) as of June 24, 2024; headcount 5,817
items.quote: The cash balance of InfoEdge (including wholly owned subsidiaries) at the end of June 24th stood at Rs. 4,255 crores, and the headcount as of June 24 end was 5,817.

items.statement: Gestation projects (JobHai, AmbitionBox, iimjobs, hirist) costing Rs. 20-25 crore per quarter in P&L drag
items.quote: In the range, you said, Rs. 20-25 crores a quarter, around that much.

items.statement: 99acres advertising spend higher than last year; manpower costs under control
items.quote: We are actually spending more than we spent last year. I don't know exactly how much. Right now, as we speak, we have a higher budget than we spent last year.

items.statement: Naukri advertising spend significantly higher in FY25 vs FY24 due to IPL in Q1; Q2-Q3 lean quarters for advertising
items.quote: In general, we will spend a lot more on advertising this year than we spent last year on Naukri.

items.statement: Non-IT pricing more modest than IT due to different hiring volumes; aggressive pricing for SME segment
items.quote: Our pricing in non-IT is more modest compared to IT because of the different hiring needs of customers of every company and IT companies hire in large numbers while here they don't hire that many people.

items.statement: 99acres listing realization increasing YoY and QoQ driven by premiumization through product upgrades
items.quote: Our listing realization continued to increase Y-o-Y and Q-o-Q as well driven by successful premiumization through product upgrades.

items.statement: JobHai freemium model targeting 1M customers in 5-7 years; blue collar market 4-8x white collar volume but lower ARPU
items.quote: If, JobHai has to be successful, then we would want JobHai to work with a million customers, 5-7 years from now. It should be the platform of choice for SMEs, as well, not just enterprises.

items.statement: Jeevansathi launched super interest and handpicked matches features gaining traction; chat remains free
items.quote: We made several features on the app free a couple of years ago and now we are back to focusing on monetization with new features launched in Q1, such as super interest and handpicked matches gaining good traction.

items.statement: 99acres focusing on channel partner growth (90% of NCR homes via brokers); developing better developer offerings
items.quote: In the north, for example, in NCR, maybe 90% of all homes are sold through channel partners. In a city like Bangalore, maybe 40-50% of all homes are sold through channel partners.

items.statement: Naukri expanded to 70+ cities, targeting 100 cities in 2 years; opened new offices in NCR (Ghaziabad, Faridabad, Greater Noida, Manesar)
items.quote: Our goal is to get to 100 cities in a couple of years. We perhaps are already in more than 70 cities.

items.statement: Naukri works with 120,000+ customers; targeting 200,000-250,000 in 5-6 years; JobHai targeting 1M customers
items.quote: Naukri today works with over 120,000 customers. If you do a good job, you may end up working with 200,000 - 250,000 customers in the next 5-6 years.

items.statement: 99acres competing with Facebook and Google for user engagement; need superior offerings
items.quote: We actually are not competing with the real estate portals. We end up competing with Facebook and Google and there we need superior offerings to get people to engage with the platform a lot more.

items.statement: Jeevansathi competition intensity similar to last year; no change
items.quote: Competition intensity remained similar to last year. There was no change on that front.

items.statement: No further updates on Google in-app billing issue; all okay currently
items.quote: There are no further updates. I mean, all is okay on that front right now. Nothing to worry about at this point in time.

items.statement: GreytHR: allowed Apex Digital to buy out early investors; no longer strategic, now financial investment; hope for IPO in few years
items.quote: When we went into GreytHR, in our heads it was quasi strategic. But over time, we've realized that we would rather invest more in sourcing and recruitment and automation then in getting into an HR services play.

items.statement: AIF funds (12+2 year duration) early for exits; first fund 2019, exits expected 2027-28; patient capital approach
items.quote: Our first fund, our first AIF was 2019. So if you start looking at getting your exits eight years or nine years out, then you're talking about 2027-28.

items.statement: No plan to exit Zomato or Policybazaar holdings; board discusses constantly but taking long-term view for value creation
items.quote: As of now, there is no plan to exit.

items.statement: IT hiring uncertain: July Jobspeak +12% YoY but sustainability unclear; US recession risk; attrition ticking up
items.quote: The July 2024 Jobspeak report has also been very encouraging. The Jobspeak index grew by 12% Y-o-Y in July and M-o-M grew by 11%. Let's see how this plays out over the next couple of months.

items.statement: 99acres growth moderated in June due to election uncertainty; state government changes delay project approvals
items.quote: The business took a hit in June. Maybe again, it had to do with some uncertainty around the elections. And often when state governments change and all these things happen in real estate some of the projects get delayed.

items.statement: Revenue growth target of at least 20% for FY25 maintained but with cautious optimism
items.quote: I would still do not want to jump into any change in numbers, but we are quite cautious and we keep ourselves cautiously optimistic on this year's performance.

items.statement: Order book additions expected to be higher than previous year
items.quote: we definitely would like to achieve a number which will be higher than the previous year's addition into the thing.

items.statement: Aerospace revenue growth target of 30-35% for FY25
items.quote: For this year, for Aerospace, we are looking at between 30% to 35% growth as it stands today.

items.statement: Swedish subsidiary EBITDA margin expected to reach 12-13% from next financial year
items.quote: we have worked, and we have acquired 2 key business wins for our Swedish subsidiary, which will enable us to go back to 12% to 13% EBITDA starting from next financial year.

items.statement: Medium-term target of 20% EBITDA margin
items.quote: we clearly understand that while we have set ourselves target on working towards 20% margin expansion, we very clearly understand that these are not going to come very easy.

items.statement: Non-auto, tech-agnostic and xEV business expected to grow at 40-50% CAGR for next 2-3 years
items.quote: we are looking at a CAGR growth in this by about 40% to 50%.

items.statement: Aerospace and Defense sector expected 40-50% CAGR for next 2-3 years
items.quote: We are looking at about 40% to 50% CAGR growth in this sector for the next 2 to 3 years.

items.statement: Capex of approximately Rs 4,500 million planned for FY25
items.quote: We are looking at a CAPEX of approximately Rs. Rs. 4,500 million during FY '25.

items.statement: 40-45% of capex allocated to tech-agnostic and non-automotive segments
items.quote: 40% to 45% of our CAPEX is expected to go towards tech -agnostic and non -automotive segments.

items.statement: Special process facility for aerospace approved with Rs 30 crore investment, operational by mid-FY26
items.quote: this would have an overall investment of about Rs. 30 crores.

items.statement: MOU signed with Karnataka government for 55 acres land for future greenfield expansion
items.quote: we have recently signed an MOU with the government of Karnataka to acquire 55 acres of land. Over the years, we will be looking at greenfield expansion in the area of our current expertise in this piece of land.

items.statement: Current plant utilization at 65-70%, peak utilization around 80%
items.quote: Our current facilities are working between 65% and 70% utilization across our plants. And in our industry, peak utilization can reach to up to around 80% in the best-case scenario

items.statement: New 4,000-ton press to be fully commissioned by end of H1 FY25
items.quote: The new 4,000 -ton press, which is being commissioned and which will be fully commissioned by the end of H1

items.statement: Order book stood at Rs 16.9 billion as of June 2024, 63% international, 37% domestic
items.quote: In terms of order book, it stood at Rs. 16.9 billion as of June '24. Out of which, 63% of orders are from international business and the rest 37% are domestic orders.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded by ~2 percentage points to 41.8% in Q1 FY25 due to favorable product mix
items.quote: During this quarter, the gross margin grew from 39.9% in Q1 of FY '24 to 41.8% in the Q1 of FY '25.

items.statement: EBITDA margin stable at 17% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins were stable at 17% levels.

items.statement: MMRFIC radar business expected to have EBITDA margins upwards of 50%
items.quote: the average, the EBITDA numbers on this business would be upwards of 50%.

items.statement: Domestic 2-wheeler demand strong driven by rural economy and positive monsoon
items.quote: notable growth in 2-wheeler segment has been driven by driving rural economy and its positive monsoon effects.

items.statement: PV segment: SUVs doing well but small car demand lower with heightened inventory
items.quote: On the PV side, SUVs continue to do well. However, demand for small cars is on the lower side. The industry is also seeing heightened levels of inventory.

items.statement: International business growth fueled by client additions, wallet share expansion and orders moving to commercial production
items.quote: the growth has been fueled by multiple levers, including client additions, valid share expansion and some of the orders moving to commercial production.

items.statement: Emerging sectors (non-auto, tech-agnostic, xEV) grew 34% YoY in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Together, these segments have expanded by 34% on a year-on-year basis during this quarter.

items.statement: Auto tech-agnostic products revenue Rs 712 million, up 68% YoY
items.quote: We have registered a top line of Rs. 712 million in auto tech-agnostic products with a year-on-year growth of 68%.

items.statement: xEV business grew 29% YoY to Rs 421 million despite losing a key 2-wheeler EV customer
items.quote: Our xEV business grew by 29% on a year-on-year basis to Rs. 421 million despite the fact that one of key customers in the 2-wheeler segment, we have reduced considerable business.

items.statement: Non-auto segment grew 16% YoY, all subsegments except Agri saw strong double-digit growth
items.quote: Non-auto side, which is another part of our emerging new age business grew by 16% as compared to Q1 FY '24. All non-auto subsegments with the exception of Agri saw a strong double-digit growth.

items.statement: Aerospace and Defense revenue Rs 256 million, up 28% YoY despite order delays from key customer
items.quote: The Aerospace and Defense segment delivered a top line of Rs. 256 million, with a 28% year -on-year growth despite some delays in our orders from a key customer.

items.statement: Off-road segment revenue Rs 302 million, working closely with customers to increase wallet share
items.quote: For the off -road segment, where our end market is North America, we have c locked revenue of Rs. 302 million during this quarter. We are working very closely with our customers to increase wallet share in this segment.

items.statement: Auto ICE segment grew 7.2% YoY driven by solid 2-wheeler growth and increased content per vehicle
items.quote: In the Auto ICE segment, we grew our revenues by 7.2% during the quarter, primarily on account of solid growth on the 2-wheeler side.

items.statement: Added aerospace customers Saab and Triumph Aerospace to broaden clientele
items.quote: To broaden our clientele in this space, we have added customers like Saab and Triumph Aerospace .

items.statement: Lost significant business from one 2-wheeler EV customer due to model change and commercial disagreements
items.quote: one of our customers whom we were supplying some quantity, I am talking about an EV customer, and they had a model change. And due to various factors, which includes commercial also, we could not participate in the newer program

items.statement: Swedish subsidiary won 2 key engine programs from Volvo after existing supplier went out of business
items.quote: we have acquired 2 key business wins for our Swedish subsidiary, which will enable us to go back to 12% to 13% EBITDA starting from next financial year. So, we have had 2 very clear-cut order wins on 2 engine programs

items.statement: Acquiring orders in ultra-high-precision component machining for semiconductor machines manufacturing
items.quote: we have been able to acquire some good amount of orders into this space as well.

items.statement: Higher international freight costs impacted logistics expenses in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Further, during the quarter, we faced some issues on the logistics side leading to higher spend on the international freight costs.

items.statement: Annual salary hikes in Q1 increased employee expenses YoY and QoQ
items.quote: We had an annual salary hikes, which kicks in every year in the 1st Quarter of the year. As a result, we see an increase in the employee expenses on both a year-on-year and quarter-on-quarter basis.

items.statement: Standalone product sales grew ~17% YoY in Q1 FY25 vs consolidated 13% growth
items.quote: on a stand-alone basis, Sansera has grown by almost 16.8%, almost 17% on our product sales.

items.statement: Aluminum forging production reaching ~1.5 million parts in FY25
items.quote: This year, we will be doing almost close to 1.5 million aluminum parts, which is quite a good progress given the fact that this has been only about 2.5, 3 years of this thing.

items.statement: International business outlook for H2 FY25 looks slightly worrisome
items.quote: international business is looking in the second half of this year, especially the international business looks to be slightly worrisome.

items.statement: EV adoption slowdown in Western markets (Europe and US) with some OEMs shifting focus back to ICE
items.quote: there has been some concerns on the rate of adoption of EV and the expansion of EV in the western market, both in Europe as well as in U.S., we can see a slowdown in the sales as well as overall when companies had announced that their focus is largely on EV and no ICE focus. But that has definitely shifted now.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue expected flat to down 2-3% YoY; Q2 sequentially flat, H2 higher than H1, Q4 highest run rate
items.quote: for the full year, like I said, it could be flat to maybe minus 2%, 3% or something like that.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin target 18%; long-term target remains 20%
items.quote: But 18% is what I'm looking at for this full year. But my longer-term stand on the 20% margin remains

items.statement: Early signals of slowdown in US construction equipment; Europe also soft in construction equipment; large ag slowdown in US and Europe with inventory correction
items.quote: There are some early signals of slowdown in U.S. construction equipment end market. Europe, as alluded earlier as well, is also witnessing softness in construction equipment end market.

items.statement: Aftermarket inventory correction appears over, demand bouncing back gradually; small ag steady on reduced base; India domestic tractor market steady
items.quote: Aftermarket, which overall declined 30% for Uniparts in FY'24 owing to dual impact of softness aggravated by inventory correction, is bouncing back gradually as inventory correction cycle appears to be over for now.

items.statement: New awards pipeline encouraging with traction in PMP, large ag assembly, ag machinery in India, high-horsepower 3PL, geographical expansion in below 70-hp tractors; end market softness may affect implementation timelines
items.quote: New awards pipeline remains encouraging with added traction in all product verticals including PMP, large agricultural equipment assembly, agriculture machinery in India, high-horsepower 3PL as well as further geographical expansion in below 70-horsepower tractors.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 reported EBITDA INR46 cr, margin 17.6%; operating leverage impact due to volume decline
items.quote: Reported EBITDA for Q1 was INR46 crores, which is a quarter-on-quarter change of minus 10.6%, and year-on-year change of minus 23.6%, while reported EBITDA margin was at 17.6% for the quarter.

items.statement: FY25 capex outlook INR35-40 cr; Q1 capex ~INR8.3 cr; capacity sufficient for current demand, capex only for specific new projects
items.quote: I think the capex outlook is going to be between INR35 crores to INR40 crores. This quarter, was about INR8 crores or so.

items.statement: Overall capacity utilization 55-60%; factories flexible across 3PL and PMP with common processes; no product-specific dedicated capacity
items.quote: the capacity utilization overall is in the range of 55% to 60%, currently. It is not product-specific. Pretty much all our factories, except the U.S. one, which produces only PMP. All our India factories produce both 3PL and PMP.

items.statement: Medium-term target: 15-18% sales CAGR and 20%+ EBITDA margin on blended basis over next 3-4 years
items.quote: we feel on a medium to long-term range we should continue to grow on an average 15% to 18% on sales, and 20% plus on the EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Total capex for Roorkee pipe plant plus debottlenecking ~Rs 170-180 crore; ~40% spent, balance over next 9 months
items.quote: total will be somewhere around that range only, given the fact that the land was procured last year.

items.statement: Roorkee pipe plant commercial operations expected by Q3 FY25; current capacity sufficient for FY25 volume growth
items.quote: The construction of our Roorkee facility is progressing as planned, with commercial operations expected to commence by Q3FY25.

items.statement: Sanitaryware capacity utilisation 86%, faucet 58.5% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our capacity utilization in Q1 FY25 for sanitaryware was about 86%, and for faucet it was about 58.5%.

items.statement: Secondary sales improved in late June and July; expect momentum through festive season in H2
items.quote: Early market inputs suggest secondary sales have seen noticeable upticks since late June and we anticipate further momentum building up through the festive season.

items.statement: Bathware Q1 EBITDA margin 12.9% (Rs 42 cr on Rs 326 cr); margin drop due to lower revenue, fixed cost absorption
items.quote: the margin reduction is solely a loss of gross margin because of lower revenue, which we recorded in the quarter 1.

items.statement: Pipes Q1 EBITDA margin 6.7% (Rs 11 cr on Rs 163 cr); full-year double-digit EBITDA growth guided
items.quote: We have not degrown, but we are at the same, it's at 6.7%. But as far as the guidance for the whole year is there because Q3 and Q4 for this business are at its peak.

items.statement: Consumer Appliances Q1 EBITDA margin 2.7% (Rs 3 cr on Rs 111 cr); improved via cost optimisation and exiting furniture retail
items.quote: Our consumer Appliances business delivered INR111 crore in revenue with an EBITDA of INR3 crore at a 2.7% EBITDA margin reflecting the positive impact of cost optimization and exiting our loss-making retail furniture business.

items.statement: Sales-force consolidation expected to add 100+ bps to Bathware EBITDA margin annually
items.quote: We believe that it is going to help us increase our margins by 100 basis points plus on an annual basis.

items.statement: Bathware premium/economy split shifted to 48% premium / 52% economy in Q1 FY25 vs 53%/47% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: In Q1FY25, it was 52% for economy and 48% for premium. In Q1FY24, it was 47% for economy, and 53% for premium for us.

items.statement: Net debt rose ~Rs 100 cr QoQ due to stuck inventory and Roorkee capex; rights issue proceeds primarily for debt repayment
items.quote: First, I think the main reason debt has increased is, we couldn't reduce the level of working capital because of the slowness in the market and some of the inventories is stuck with us right now.

items.statement: Board approved rights issue up to Rs 205 cr for liquidity and substantial debt repayment
items.quote: the Board has approved the raising of funds through issuance and allotment of equity shares of the Company of face value Rs. 2 each (Rupee Two Only) for an aggregate amount not exceeding Rs. 205 crore on rights issue

items.statement: Bathware sales force reduced ~25% (on-roll and off-roll) in Q1 via faucet-sanitaryware team merger; no further restructuring planned
items.quote: we have impacted nearly 25% of our sales force in this quarter based on our decision to consolidate and synergize between our sanitaryware and faucet verticals

items.statement: July secondary sales positive across market and for company; dealer inventory high, may clear in 2-3 months
items.quote: secondaries sales have been positive in July. We've seen some positive momentum on the secondary basis, yes across the market.

items.statement: Consumer Appliances category review ongoing; may exit loss-making categories eroding kitchen margins
items.quote: we are evaluating the product categories in which we are operating. And we don't foresee any strategic future in terms of the categories, we'll come back to investors and share, if we are making a transition within the organization and evacuating those categories.

items.statement: Consolidated Q1 revenue Rs 600 cr, EBITDA Rs 55 cr, margin 9.2%
items.value: Rs 600 cr revenue, Rs 55 cr EBITDA, 9.2% margin
items.quote: Our consolidated revenue for the quarter reached Rs. 600 crore, EBITDA stood at Rs. 55 crore with margins at 9.2%.

items.statement: China import dependence for Bathware reduced from 17-18% to ~3% over last 2 years via in-sourcing
items.quote: It will be like low-single digits, like 3%. Sandeep Sikka: I mean we started off, this used to be 17% to 18%. And from the last 2 years, we are reducing this

items.statement: Core revenue growth guidance of 14-18% for FY25, EBITDA margin target 23-24%
items.quote: We would be talking around 14% to 18% of growth on core revenues, and this excludes sale of compost, RDF because those are something that we will expect a sharp change in the second half of the year.

items.statement: EBITDA margin of 23.8% in Q1FY25, guided 23-24% as base going forward
items.quote: Over the last 2 quarters, we have demonstrated steady improvement in the reported margin, which now stands at 23.8%. And we believe this range of 23% to 24% will serve as a base going forward.

items.statement: One large C&T contract likely to close in Q2FY25, Chennai processing project bid submission later this month
items.quote: One of the projects is likely to close in this quarter, at least one large C&T contract is likely to close.

items.statement: Capex for vehicle scrapping and tire recycling Rs.20-28 crores plus Rs.8 crores incremental
items.quote: The investment will be in line with what we have announced. It would be around Rs.20 crores to Rs.28 crores for both the projects and maybe an incremental Rs.8 crores to scale up the entity.

items.statement: WTE plant PLF reached ~89% in Q1FY25 vs ~71% in Q4FY24
items.quote: We are proud to announce a remarkable achievement with our Waste-to-Energy plant's Plant Load Factor reaching ~89% during the recently ended quarter.

items.statement: Managed ~1.18 million tons waste in Q1FY25, 6% YoY increase despite completed projects
items.quote: During this period, we successfully managed ~1.18 million tons of waste reflecting a notable 6% year-on-year increase despite completion of Mangalore C&T and Greater Noida Biomining project last year.

items.statement: RDF sales ~34,000 tons in Q1FY25, 23% YoY growth, high calorific value as coal substitute
items.quote: We also achieved a record sale of about 34,000 tons of RDF in Q1 of FY '25, marking a strong 23% year-on-year growth.
