items.statement: DSOs improved to 79 days adjusted for collections vs 115 days reported at quarter end
items.quote: We are pleased to report that adjusted for the collections received to date, our DSOs now stand at 79 as compared to 115 as reported at the end of the quarter.

items.statement: Gross debt ~Rs.389 crores, cash ~Rs.80 crores, net debt ~Rs.308 crores, net debt-to-equity 0.4x
items.quote: As of June 2024, the group's gross debt stands at ~Rs.389 crores with cash and bank balance of approximately Rs.80 crores, this results in a net debt of around Rs.308 crores.

items.statement: MoEFCC draft guidelines propose 20% recycled materials usage in construction projects, positive for C&D waste
items.quote: The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change recently issued draft guidelines for public consultation, supposing that property developers and infrastructure companies used 20% recycled materials in their projects, a strong positive for this area of waste management going forward.

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted to 59% C&T, 26% MSW processing, 15% Others & Contracts in Q1FY25
items.quote: In Q1FY25, the total contract revenue amounted to Rs.35 crores, which is down from Rs.49 crores compared to the same period last year and Rs.22 crores in the Q4 of '24.

items.statement: C&D waste opportunity estimated at Rs.5,000 crores (150M tons/year India, half addressed)
items.quote: Their estimate is that about 150 million tons of C&D waste is generated in India every year. So even if half of it is done, I think it should be Rs.5,000 crores opportunity.

items.statement: Vehicle scrapping and tire recycling opportunity estimated up to Rs.10,000 crores over years
items.quote: There are no official studies for this thing, but we think it is again going to be going forward because we are talking about passenger vehicles and HCV trucks. So that thing is going to be as big as Rs.10,000 crores over the years.

items.statement: C&D project in Mumbai launched Aug 14, annualized revenue ~Rs.30 crores first full year
items.quote: So on an annualized basis, in the first full year of operations, we will have a revenue of about Rs.30 crores per year.

items.statement: C&D project margins expected slightly better than existing weighted average margins
items.quote: We should doing slightly better than our existing margins that have been reported on a weighted average because that's a percent of processing involved and there's also Collection & Transportation.

items.statement: Vehicle scrapping/tire recycling EBITDA margins expected 8-12% range
items.quote: Looking at the kind of competition or looking at the kind of margins which the current companies are making, that's in the range of about 8% to 12% of EBITDA margin.

items.statement: Rs.25 crores capital grant received from WTE client applied to project debt
items.quote: During the quarter, the company has received a Rs.25 crores capital grant from the W TE client, which was applied towards the project debt

items.statement: Workforce ~10,452 employees, gender diversity 2-4%, attrition low, 1,875 training hours in Q1FY25
items.quote: Socially, we engage actively with our employees and communities, boasting a diverse workforce of about 10,452 employees with gender diversity between 2% to 4% across sites.

items.statement: Debtor days stressed due to municipal election cycles, expected to normalize to 70-90 days post elections
items.quote: Once the elections at various municipalities get completed, then this will again go back to our historical average about 70 to 90 days.

items.statement: Integrated C&D contracts (C&T + processing) provide moat vs MSW where contracts are separate
items.quote: Our moat basically is that a typical Construction & Debris project, and that's the trend that we have seen across cities, is that these are integrated contracts.

items.statement: Land purchase for vehicle scrapping/tire recycling at MIDC Industrial Park near Mumbai, deal closing shortly
items.quote: We are looking at MIDC Industrial Park, in and around Mumbai. We had zeroed down o n three or four locations. And very shortly, we should be closing the deal with one of

items.statement: Vehicle scrapping policy implementation expected to drive adoption, starting with metro/Tier 1 cities
items.quote: But we expect and especially when it comes to adoption of regulation, we have seen that the big metro cities and Tier 1 cities are the first ones to adopt. So that's where we think -- that's the direction it will take.

items.statement: Tax rate ~25% for all companies except one processing company shifting in 2028
items.quote: Now new adjusted tax rate about 25%. So the company has shifted all its historical companies and subsidiaries to new tax regime. So a 25% tax rate, it will be applicable for all our companies, except for one processing company, which will shift to the new tax regime in 2028.

items.statement: Company could be debt-free in 4 years on steady state without new contracts
items.quote: Going forward, on a steady state of affairs, if the company doesn't bag any contracts and we have a decent cash flow, we would completely be debt-free in the next four years' time frame.

items.statement: C&D processing uses CD E Asia equipment for dry/wet processing, different from traditional MSW processing
items.quote: So this is a different type of processing as in that there are two parts of processing here, dry and wet processing. So you require different kinds of crushers and equipment. That is something that we have procured from a leading international firm called CD E Asia.

items.statement: EBITDA to cash conversion ~88% normally, Q1FY25 CFO ~Rs.18 crores due to stressed receivables
items.quote: So normally, we have a EBITDA to cash conversion of around 88%.

items.statement: Aggressively developing outdoor lighting (landscape, facade) and home segment (decorative, semi-decorative technical lighting) with worldwide patent on technology; also targeting trade segment with screw-less, fast-assembly products
items.quote: Currently we are working very aggressively on outdoor profile. Outdoor is a very huge market till India is concerned and India, Middle East and Europe is concerned. And we are working on landscape and we are working on facade lighting, building facades.

items.statement: Introduced technical lighting in home segment, now expanding into decorative and semi-decorative technical lighting for stronger foothold
items.quote: In home segment, we are working very, very aggressively. We introduced technical lighting. Now we are going in a segment of decorative lighting and semi -decorative technical lighting, which gives us a very, very strong foothold in home segment.

items.statement: Entering trade segment with differentiated screw-less products, exclusive designs, and fast assembly (10-25 seconds) to reduce cost and create differentiation in price-sensitive market
items.quote: We are working on a very different level wherein we are introducing products which are screw-less. We are introducing products with very different materials, unlike what is used in trade. We are introducing a lot of exclusive designs and technology in trade.

items.statement: Debt increased significantly; receivables from Middle East and Southeast Asia channel partners delayed but assured to be cleared by September-October; INR6 crores already collected in home lighting
items.quote: Yes, the debt has gone very high. We are working with a few channel partners, especially in the Middle East and in Southeast Asia. Now with channel partners, when it comes to home segment, we are not doing direct business in Middle East and in Southeast Asia.

items.statement: CFO confirms INR6 crores collected towards home lighting vs previous quarter; retail lighting collections also being followed aggressively; most over-6-month receivables expected by September-October end
items.quote: So if you see, as compared to previous quarter, we have collected almost INR6 crores towards the home lighting. And in retail lighting also, we are following up very aggressively. So by September or October end, we will be able to receive most of the amount, which is above six months.

items.statement: Currently managing working capital without problems; may face stress once outdoor portfolio launches and might need to raise limits
items.quote: Till date, we still don't have problems and we are surviving and we are able to manage it. Once the outdoor portfolio is done, we might have a stress and we might have to raise or increase our limits.

items.statement: Dividend policy to be announced; dividend expected to be declared at next meeting
items.quote: Dividend here, we will announce. Of course, we will come out with the dividend policy and we will give the dividend. I think next meeting we will announce the dividend for sure.

items.statement: Domestic home segment routed through 30-35 channel partners (target 50); each partner potential INR1-5 crores annually; experience centers in Andheri, factory, Bangalore, Lower Parel, with Delhi and Pune finalized; partner centers in Hydera
items.quote: All put together, we have 35 channel partners right now. Between 30 to 35, I don't know the exact numbers. And this year we are planning to increase it to 50 channel partners. Till date, average channel partner's potential with us was somewhere between 50 lakhs to 1 crore. Their potential can increase up to 5 crores in local, I am talking about India.

items.statement: Middle East home channel: tie-ups with three companies; one opened experience center in Saudi Arabia last month, second planned in Dubai; Saudi market growing significantly
items.quote: Till Middle East is concerned, we have tie up with three companies. And one of the companies have been very keen and they have opened experience center in Saudi. It has just opened last month. And Saudi, the way India is growing, Saudi is growing in a very big way.

items.statement: No railway orders secured this quarter; railway tendering system in turmoil with quality concerns and vendor due diligence; approved vendor status achieved with private players (Bombardier, Alstom) but factory visits and traction taking tim
items.quote: No, railway currently we are not able to secure any orders. Railway, there are two systems where railway works. One is there are private players, companies like Bombardier or Alstom who buys lights and who installs in the boogies and supplies it to railway.

items.statement: Airport orders: Mumbai Airport INR7-8 crores (Phase 1 of 4 phases, full completion expected by Dec/Feb); Guwahati Airport Phase 1 received; Indore Airport order received; approved by Airport Authority of India; working closely with Adani (2
items.quote: Guwahati was received before Mumbai. Both are phase 1. This is not a complete order. Okay. We have received in Mumbai there are 4 phases. And this is the first order what we have received. The government of India is supposed to complete it by this. They were supposed to complete it by August. But I don't think so it is happening for them. So probably by December or by Feb.

items.statement: Government projects: working with Ahmedabad Tourism (large inquiries concluding next month), Surat Municipal Corporation (designing street light, conclusion in 6 months), Central Vista/Secretariat orders via L&T; government share increasing
items.quote: We are working with Ahmedabad Tourism in a very big way. There are some huge inquiries and they should be concluded by next month. We are expecting. It is a very large value for a company like us. We are working very closely with Surat SMC, Municipal Corporation.

items.statement: Confident on sustaining top-line growth and expanded margins over 3-5 year horizon across four verticals (trade, outdoor, home, retail) with patents and technology investments; visibility good for 2-3 years; acknowledges possible 1-2 quarte
items.quote: As a company, what we are looking at is three years and five years bandwidth. Okay. The investments what currently we are doing in three major verticals. And we've got patents and we are working on different technologies in trade, in outdoor and in home. And of course, retail also.

items.statement: Home segment revenue cyclical (spikes with large builder projects); Q1 home revenue declined from INR6 crores to INR2 crores due to project timing; not a benchmark; similar lumpiness expected in infra segment
items.quote: See, you have to understand. There is a builder. I will just give you an example. Loda or DLS is coming out with a township. And you get the order. Then you will see a spike in one quarter. Which is a very normal thing. But it is not that DLS completed one project and he will come out with immediately a second project.

items.statement: Stock price decline (150 to 86-87 over two months) attributed to profit booking by long-term investors; management focused on business growth, not daily stock tracking
items.quote: No, it is you, investors. I should at this is one question which I have to ask rather than you asking me. Sorry, this is not my job to track day to day what is happening. Of course, it is. We are growing and we were expecting the market to react positively. But I think people are encashing profit and there are investors in the company for a very long time.

items.statement: Expects high-teen to 20% year-on-year revenue growth for FY26 and FY27 based on awarded programs and advanced negotiations
items.quote: down the line, if you ask me, for FY 26, FY 27, definitely we are expecting high teen to 20% growth, year on year.

items.statement: European bearing ring demand fell 30-35% in Q1 FY25 vs Q4 FY24 due to geopolitical factors and container shortages
items.quote: the bearing ring segment and particularly in the overseas market, again, drill it down to the European market. It has affected more than, 30 to 35% in this current quarter, that is June 24th compared to March 24th

items.statement: Expects gradual recovery in European demand from Q3 FY25, stabilising by end of fiscal
items.quote: we expect very frankly not expecting much of the recovery in the current quarter that is second quarter. But from the third quarter onwards we expect bit of the recovery and maybe it would be stabilized by the end of the fiscal.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 24.2%, up from 23.8% in Q4 FY24, aided by 11.5 MW solar plant operationalisation
items.quote: the company has recorded 76.4 crore EBITDA for the first quarter of FY 25, which is somewhere about 24.2%. And it was almost the same amount, 76 crore, which is a percentage of Rs 23.8% in the last quarter of the previous quarter.

items.statement: FY25 capex guided at Rs 40-45 crore, including Rs 27 crore for 12 MW solar plant and balance for forging presses and value-added processes
items.quote: CapEx broadly, as I told you, we did somewhere about ten odd crores. And considering my remaining CapEx for solar and all this thing, we would be ending in between 40, 40 to 45 crores.

items.statement: FY26 capex expected in similar range of Rs 40-50 crore
items.quote: Again, more or less not significant. Again, it would be in the range of 40 to 50 crores.

items.statement: 12 MW solar plant under execution with initial approvals, expected commissioning by March 2025
items.quote: Company is planning for 12 megawatt solar, It has already been initiated and we got initial approval. And, we expect that this 12 megawatt solar plant would be operationalized or commissioned before the end of this fiscal, that is March 25th.

items.statement: Current renewable capacity ~30 MW (20 MW solar + wind) covering ~30% of power cost; post 12 MW addition will cover 37-40%
items.quote: broadly after adding up this 12%, we, 12 megawatt, we would be somewhere about, 35 to 38% of my overall, this one, because we had certain other windmills also and all put together as of now, it is giving me a cost saving of somewhere about 30%

items.statement: New European auto component customer ramped from Rs 14 crore to Rs 22 crore quarterly; 2-3 more customers to start in next 2-3 months
items.quote: Let me tell you one European customer what it was there in FY, last quarter of this one FY 24, it was somewhere about say, 14 crore, of quarterly business. And in this particular quarter, June 24, it has increased to 22 crore, revenue.

items.statement: US-based customer started in May 2024 (delayed from Feb-Mar), expected to pick up in Q2 and Q3 FY25
items.quote: another couple of, one one main US based customers, which are initially it was supposed to be started in the Feb March 24th, but fortunately it has started in the month of May 24th onwards and we expect that to be picked up in the second quarter and third quarter.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue mix: bearing rings 46% (Rs 131 crore), auto components 54% (Rs 153 crore); bearing rings domestic up 15-18% QoQ
items.quote: bearing ring number for this quarter. it was 131 crore and auto component business, it is. Or rather, it was 153 crore.

items.statement: End-user segment mix: passenger vehicles ~40%, EV/hybrid ~10-12%, HCV/commercial and industrial ~50%
items.quote: broadly 40% into the passenger segment, 10 to 12% into the EV hybrid and remaining into HCB and commercial industrial applications.

items.statement: Added new auto component customers in Europe and US; domestic bearing ring revenue grew 15-18% QoQ
items.quote: we have added a couple of new customers in Europe and in the US also something what it has been, you know, started to the first quarter

items.statement: Europe currently 16-17% of revenue, targeting 20% by end of FY25 as bearing ring recovery and new auto customers ramp
items.quote: by end of this fiscal, we are expecting at least 20% from my, European business

items.statement: Sea freight rates elevated due to geopolitical factors; expects normalization from Q3 FY25 (Oct-Nov)
items.quote: Not for this quarter, maybe down the line October, November or so it may because there are certain other, you know, factors, you know, with the US market business and with 13 other countries, China, US composition, the the traffic has been diverted.

items.statement: Customers deferring shipments 15-45 days due to container shortages and high freight costs
items.quote: customers are also deferring certain you know, these small, lifting maybe a half container load they are waiting that let us have an entire container load. Let's postpone our lifting or shipment maybe for, 15, 30 days, 45 days or something like that.

items.statement: Net cash position of Rs 195-200 crore as of call date; zero long-term debt
items.quote: if you ask me, as on date, I am sitting on a, net cash or you can say, or including all my, this thing is it is touching somewhere about 195 to 200 crores

items.statement: Right of recompense (ROR) of ~Rs 32 crore provided in Q4 FY24; further charge possible as bankers finalize
items.quote: Again, the same matter is there with the bankers and in last consortium meeting with our bankers, they are working on it. They are processing not because there are six nationalized banks. So maybe down the line they have asked maybe 40 to 45 days to again revert.

items.statement: Chinese competition exists but customers prioritize precision, supply chain reliability and one-stop solutions over price
items.quote: our customers, you know, those are very much clear or rather, their requirement of the component is highly precision components. And they are ready to pay the, you know, the, best, competitive price without, compromising on the quality front

items.statement: Sales volume 11,000 MT in Q1 FY25 vs 9,900 MT in Q4 FY24 and 10,000 MT in Q1 FY24; marginal tonnage growth offset by commodity price decline
items.quote: In terms of, you know, let me tell you the quantum of my this one, the sales, what it is there in the first quarter, it is somewhere about 11,000 metric ton what we have sold and which was 9900 metric ton, in the quarter 20, last quarter of FY 24

items.statement: Geopolitical factors and container shortages creating hurdles for European exports for last 15-24 months
items.quote: Demand slowdown, particularly in and apart from that this geopolitical reasons what it is there for last almost 15-18 months or 24 months. That is something creating hurdle.

items.statement: Auto component revenue target 45-50% of total by end of FY25 (from ~54% in Q1) as bearing rings recover in H2
items.quote: broadly, our target auto component business would be touching 45 to 50 percentage something by the end of this current fiscal of our overall contribution.

items.statement: CMC revenue target of INR1,000 crore by FY27 will be surpassed with new LOI and capex
items.quote: Earlier, we had talked about by FY '27, we'll touch INR1,000 crores of revenue. I think we will surpass that. With this new announcement and with the orders and the LOIs we've signed, we'll definitely surpass that number by FY '27. It will be over and above that INR1,000 crores.

items.statement: Fifth LOI signed with agrochemical innovator for 5-year advanced intermediate supply
items.quote: We have recently signed a new letter of intent with an agrochemical innovator for an advanced intermediate for a new active ingredient. This LOI covers a period of 5 years.

items.statement: CMC pipeline has 12-15 additional products in development
items.quote: I would guess, at least another 12 to 15 products in the pipeline.

items.statement: Board approved INR160 crore capex to expand CMC capacity at Berigai including next MPB infrastructure
items.quote: The Board has also approved an investment of about INR160 crores to increase the production capacity of the Custom Manufactured Chemicals Division at Berigai.

items.statement: CMC Phase 2 expansion expected to commission by end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: Phase 2 of our CMC expansion is progressing well and is expected to get commissioned by the end of Q2 FY '25.

items.statement: Phase 3 CMC civil infrastructure being built to accelerate future capacity addition
items.quote: A portion of this investment will go towards creating the infrastructure for the next multi-purpose production block.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA INR124 crore at 11% margin; gross margin improved QoQ from 31% to 40%
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we reported an EBITDA of INR124 crores with an EBITDA margin of 11%. Our finance cost for the quarter stood at INR59 crores and the net profit for the quarter was at INR24 crores.

items.statement: Paste PVC unit contribution INR21,000/ton vs Suspension PVC INR14,500/ton in Q1
items.quote: The unit contribution in the last quarter, that is in, Q1 paste PVC is around INR21,000 per ton as against the suspension PVC was around INR14,500 per ton.

items.statement: Provisional anti-dumping duty on Paste PVC from 5 countries announced June 2024; new petition filed for EU and Japan
items.quote: based on the preliminary findings, provisional anti-dumping duties were announced in June 2024 for a period of 6 months on import of Paste PVC from producers in c ountries such as Norway, Thailand, Malaysia, Taiwan and China

items.statement: Suspension PVC anti-dumping investigation ongoing against all major exporters; decision expected by Q3 FY25
items.quote: Suspension is in advanced stage. The petition has been filed, investigation initiate d, and we expect that maybe by Q3, we should see a decision on that

items.statement: Domestic PVC demand strong driven by infrastructure and construction; destocking easing in FY25
items.quote: Domestic demand continues to remain strong. India's infrastructure missions to provide access to clean water and improve irrigation are critical projects that are bolstering this growth.

items.statement: Net debt INR560-570 crore with cash balance ~INR800 crore
items.quote: Current net debt is around INR560 crores. We are carrying a cash of around INR800 crores, that is around INR570 crores of net debt.

items.statement: Specialty Chemicals volumes up 44% YoY driven by new Paste PVC capacity commissioned in Q4 FY24
items.quote: The Specialty Chemicals Division's volumes increased by 44% on a year-on-year basis, mainly due to the commissioning of the new Paste PVC capacity in the last quarter of the previous year.

items.statement: Paste PVC price improvement ~$150/ton seen but partially reversed due to EU imports and freight normalization
items.quote: We have seen an improvement of around $150 or so on prices that did happen. Some part of it would have been due to the container fre ight rate movement as

items.statement: VCM prices track PVC with 4-6 week lag; input-output ratio ~1.003 ton VCM per ton SPVC
items.quote: Practically 1 ton of VCM per ton of suspension PVC, it should be in the third decimal maybe around 1.003 or so.

items.statement: CMC contracts typically 3-5 years with price formulas; some have volume commitments, others flexible in multipurpose blocks
items.quote: The time period of those are typically anywhere between 3 to 5 years. And it may have a component related to the price structure or price formula. In some cases, there may also be some volume agreements or volume arrangements.

items.statement: LOI 5 adds INR300 crore cumulative revenue potential and INR125 crore annualized at steady state
items.quote: The 5th LOI will add INR300 crores to that. On an annualized basis on a steady state, this LOI still add around INR125 crores.

items.statement: Phase 3 CMC capacity commissioning timeline ~12 months from now, can accelerate based on pipeline
items.quote: I would say maybe another 12 months from where we are now, but we could do it much faster. It all depends on how the pipeline is.

items.statement: PVC prices dropped in July 2024; may impact Q2 performance but import measures expected to help later in year
items.quote: While Q1 performance was a positive start to the year, prices of PVC have again dropped in July. While this may impact Q2 performance, we believe that various measures being taken to stem the flow of low-cost imports into India, will bear fruit later in the year.

items.statement: Custom manufacturing currently a drag on EBITDA/kg but will improve as volumes ramp up
items.quote: Definitely, the Custom Manufactured Chemicals Business will move the needle as we go forward, especially given the very exciting growth possibilities that we have. So that is going to weigh in as we move along.

items.statement: Phase 1 and 2 CMC capacities fully utilized based on 5 LOIs; Phase 3 civil works underway for next block
items.quote: Based on LOIs that they received, the Phase 1 and 2 capacities will be fully utilized. And in Pha se 3 that we are planning, even part of that will also get utilized based on that

items.statement: Caustic soda prices moved up slightly in Q1; chloromethane prices improving from July
items.quote: from July, we are also seeing a good move up in a couple of the chlorometh ane products. Their prices have moved up a bit

items.statement: Custom manufacturing dispatches now evenly paced vs bunched in Q4 FY24
items.quote: This year, the Custom Manufacturing dispatches are reasonably evenly paced. So that is the difference that we are seeing. It is not a drop.

items.statement: R&D Phase 2 and pilot plant expansion commissioned; dedicated labs for hazardous chemistries added
items.quote: The second phase of the R&D was commissioned a couple of quarters back. And similarly, we have already commissioned the next phase of our pilot plant expansion.

items.statement: Suspension PVC revenue stable YoY, up 8% QoQ; positive profit swing from higher PVC prices and lower feedstock costs
items.quote: Suspension PVC revenue has been stable in Q1 FY '25 as compared to the corresponding period last year, while it has improved by 8% sequentially. We wi tnessed a positive swing in profits in the current quarter on account of both improved prices of suspension PVC and lower feedstock prices

items.statement: Management guides for 25% revenue growth in FY25 and expects to achieve historical pharma EBITDA margin of 23% this financial year.
items.quote: Looking at our current order book, I am confident that we will comfortably meet our 25% growth guidance for the year.

items.statement: Management expects EBITDA margin to exceed 20% in Q3 and Q4 FY25, driven by operational leverage and gross margin improvement.
items.quote: So, a similar kind of revenue topline figures, we will achieve those additional 200 basis point operational leverage. Apart from that, we already improved 200 basis points in terms of gross margin. So, that add-up will definitely reach us more than 20% margin in this financial year only, hopefully, we will achieve in Q3 and Q4.

items.statement: Ankleshwar project Blocks 2 and 3 on track for completion by end of Q2 FY25; 16 MW solar captive power plant expected to be completed by end of Q2 FY25 with energy savings from Q3 FY25.
items.quote: For Ankleshwar project, we are on track to complete the remaining 2 blocks by end of quarter Q2 FY '25. In line with our commitment to combat global warming under the United Nation Global Compact Pledge, we have initiated a 16-megawatt solar CAPEX captive power plant project. This project will meet most of our energy needs, leading to reduce carbon emission and lower energy cost. We anticipate com

items.statement: Electrolyte additives capacity expansion for VC and FEC up to 2,000 metric tonnes on track for completion by end of FY25.
items.quote: As Naresh ji mentioned, we have also started CAPEX for electrolyte additives, which is on track completion by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Near finalization of a new CDMO contract with a large European originator for Ankleshwar Blocks 2 and 3; validation batches planned next quarter.
items.quote: We are in an active discussion, I think not active discussion but almost a finalization of signing one more contract as a CDMO with one of big originator based in Europe, samples, everything is done, now validation batches will be planned in next quarter.

items.statement: Gross margin expanded 210 bps sequentially to 42.1% in Q1 FY25 as raw material prices stabilized and company moves back to old pricing formula with long-term customers.
items.quote: As expected, RM prices have stabilized, and we are slowly moving back to old pricing formula with most of the long-term customer, and therefore, there was a good expansion of around 210 basis points in gross margin in Q1 FY '25 sequentially.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 16.7% in Q1 FY25 from 22.1% YoY due to lower gross margin YoY, higher employee costs from increments and new hires, and seasonal low revenue quarter.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 29.5 crores at 13.2% decrease year-on-year with EBITDA margin at 16.7% down from 22.1% in the same period last year.

items.statement: Advanced pharmaceutical intermediate business grew 16.6% YoY driven by strong CDMO and core product performance; specialty chemicals grew 10% YoY led by commodity chemicals, partially offset by subdued Baba Fine Chemicals.
items.quote: Our advanced pharmaceutical intermediate business reported revenue of Rs. 135 crores for the quarter, reflecting strong robust 16.6% Y-o-Y growth. This increase was driven by strong performance in both CDMO as well as the core product business.

items.statement: Semiconductor demand weak currently but expected to normalize by end of year; battery chemical sector evolving rapidly with capacity building for electrolyte additives and collaboration with global player for electrolyte solution capacity i
items.quote: In the semiconductor sector, despite the current demand is weak, the discussions with customers suggest that this is a short-term issue and demand is expected to normalize by the end of the year.

items.statement: Revenue growth of 15% YoY driven entirely by 18% volume growth, offset by 3% price decline; Q1 historically lowest quarter with sequential growth expected through Q4.
items.quote: So, we have got this 15% hike completely on a volume side that is 18% growth on volume side.

items.statement: Successfully completed PMDA inspection in Japan with no critical or major observations, potentially the only Indian chemical company with both US FDA and PMDA approvals in intermediates, opening opportunities in Japan.
items.quote: Additionally, we successfully conclude the Good Manufacturing Practice inspection by the Pharmaceutical and Medical Device Agency, PMDA in Japan with no critical or major observation. To our knowledge, we may be the only chemical company in India to have successfully completed both US FDA and PMDA inspection in the Intermediate space.

items.statement: Apixaban orders started gradually across customers with peak sales expected in FY26; Rivaroxaban also expected to peak in FY26.
items.quote: Apixaban, your understanding is correct. Rivaroxaban is still we have to wait because it has still time. But we are moderately selling Rivaroxaban as well, but not at the peak right now.

items.statement: Ankleshwar asset turn expected >3x, potentially >4x with CDMO contracts; full utilization could support Rs. 1,200+ crores topline on Rs. 300 crores capex.
items.quote: So, asset turn for Ankleshwar unit definitely will be more than 3x. But because of we have some good CDMO contracts already in place, it can go more than 4x also.

items.statement: Freight costs and extended delivery times increased due to geopolitical instability but managed through early booking; no sales lost, only incremental shipment cost impact on margins.
items.quote: It is not that great impact on our sales because we have an order in hand for longer period. So, we planned very strategically about the shipment as well. And accordingly, we booked our containers and all. But yes, it has impacted on the cost of the shipment, it is little bit incremental.

items.statement: All debt retired from QIP proceeds; net cash on hand ~Rs. 385 crores as of June; finance costs expected to decline sharply with significant debt repayment.
items.quote: So, as on June, net cash on hand is around Rs. 385 crores.

items.statement: QIP proceeds used to retire all debt; company now net cash positive.
items.quote: From QIP proceeds we have retired all the debt for the company, right? Abhishek Patel: Yes.

items.statement: Other expenses guided at 15-17% of total sales; expected to improve with operating leverage as revenue grows quarter-on-quarter.
items.quote: So, in this case, our other expenses should be ranging between 15% to 17% of the total sales. And as we grow quarter-on-quarter, with better topline, we will have a better leverage, and we will have a savings in this area.

items.statement: Fermion contract validation batches sent; qualification across 84 countries targeted this year with gradual ramp-up Q2-Q4 FY25 and full ramp-up FY26.
items.quote: We have already sent validation batches for the qualification at customer end. And by starting from Q2, Q3, Q4, it will gradually increasing, and it will fully ramp up in FY26 up to the maximum level.

items.statement: Enchem AMI Organics step-down subsidiary established for electrolyte manufacturing in India exclusively for Korean parent; JV terms finalization ongoing with regulatory complexities.
items.quote: Enchem AMI Organic is a subsidiary for making toll manufacturing for electrolyte in India, exclusively for the parent company in Korea. And right now, we are in discussion of finalizations of the JV terms and conditions.

items.statement: Baba Fine Chemicals revenue ~Rs. 5 crores/quarter impacted by Heraeus customer headwinds and ownership change compliance; recovery expected H2 FY25 with new customer collaborations in Korea and Japan.
items.quote: For the past 2 to 3 quarters, BFC has been operating around Rs. 5 crores revenue per quarter affected by business integration and demand issue from our client side. We expect a recovery to begin in second half of the year.

items.statement: Employee costs increased due to annual increments and new hires for Ankleshwar plant.
items.quote: Second is increase in employee costs, higher expenses this quarter resulted from annual increments and new hires for the Ankleshwar Plant.

items.statement: Chinese oversupply pressures pricing in advanced pharma intermediates and commodity chemicals; specialty players with technology-driven processes less impacted.
items.quote: The competitive threat from China's manufacturing capability remains significant, and I expect certain segments of the chemical sector to stay under pressure. However, Specialty players, those relying on a technology-driven processes and niche products are less impacted by current market challenges.

items.statement: Exports face longer lead times and higher freight rates; managed through strategic shipment planning and early container booking; no supply restrictions.
items.quote: Geopolitical instability worldwide has led to extended delivery times and higher freight rates over the past quarter, although input prices have stabilized, they remain low, continuing to exert pressure on the pricing of finished goods.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of ~15% average with blended EBITDA margin of 20-21%
items.quote: We have already given the guidance that the revenue growth should be around 15% on an average with an blended EBITDA margin of about 20% to 21%.

items.statement: Copper and gold outlook positive with projects coming online; market growing 2-3%, liner business ~5%
items.quote: But from this first half we see good headwinds over there. Projects are now coming on online and going forward both for the current financial year and the next year we think copper can be -- outlook is pretty good.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 group EBITDA margin 21%, operating EBITDA margin 19% vs 15% YoY; consumables 21% vs 16% YoY
items.quote: The total group revenues for Q1 of FY 2025 stood at INR352 crores with an EBITDA of INR76 crores, that is at an EBITDA margins of 21%.

items.statement: Group order book INR560 crores at June 2024 end vs INR520 crores June 2023, excluding long-term orders like NMDC
items.quote: We also have a strong order book at a group level of INR560 crores as at June 2024 end, vis -a-vis an order book of INR520 crores as of June 2023, without considering the long term orders like NMDC in Tega McNally.

items.statement: Chile project construction started, commercial production targeted by June 2025; additional 51,000 sqm land acquired for future expansion
items.quote: We intend to start the commercial production for the new facility by June of 2025. The Chile project will assist us in consolidating the existing facilities and adding new capacity.

items.statement: Heightened shipping costs will be passed on to customers in most cases; logistics cost increase minimal due to pass-through
items.quote: The impact of heightened shipping costs will be passed on to the customers in most of the cases.

items.statement: Supply chain more vigilant with better planning for raw materials and customer deliveries; inventory built up
items.quote: Our supply chain is more vigilant with better planning for both raw material, as well as customer deliveries. We have built up the inventory and are in constant communication with all our customers.

items.statement: European order executing well for 6+ months, generating ~INR10 crores monthly cash flow over 5+1 year term
items.quote: This order, particularly on an average, generates about INR10 crores of cash flow per month, which is on a steady state basis and keeps continuing accruing us over the period of five plus one, that is six years.

items.statement: Metso is major global competitor; Tega products equal or superior, leading in DynaPrime; continuous R&D investment to stay ahead
items.quote: Metso is our major competitor globally. And our product, both from quality and other aspects of deliverance of value to the customer is in no way second to anyone, okay? And on some of the fronts, including DynaPrime, we are the leaders in that segment.

items.statement: All regulatory approvals including construction received for Chile project
items.quote: We have received all regulatory approvals including construction for the Chile project and have started the construction activity.

items.statement: 75% revenue from exports, 25% domestic (includes 100% of McNally revenue)
items.quote: 75% is my exports on this thing and 25% is domestic sales. In that domestic sales, McNally is -- the entire McNally 100% revenue is a part of that domestic sales.

items.statement: Logistics cost pass-through to customers with small time lag; no significant increase in logistics cost
items.quote: The logistics cost is basically is -- we do not have too much of increase in the logistics cost because we pass on the logistics cost to our customers because small time lag.

items.statement: Open to acquisitions at right strategic value fitment for capability, technology or geographical expansion
items.quote: We are open for any acquisition which comes, but then it has to be at the right value for us. If it's the right value fitment, we are definitely open and we will explore that if it's a strategic fit for us.

items.statement: Shipping routes via Red Sea remain challenging with port congestion and container delays; proactive measures in place from COVID experience
items.quote: From a logistics point of view, the shipping routes continue to be a challenge with shipping lines evading the conflict stricken Red Sea, congestion at major ports along these alternative routes has escalated, delaying the container turnaround times.

items.statement: High employee engagement drives customer satisfaction; team feels engaged and committed globally
items.quote: I believe that high employee engagement leads to improved customer satisfaction, that in turn leads to bett er business results. Our employees across the globe feel engaged and

items.statement: Equipment business revenue delayed due to payment receipts, inspection reports, dispatch clearance certificates; expected to regularize in Q2
items.quote: The equipment business performance was lower in the current quarter due to delay in receipt of payments, inspection reports and certain dispatch clearance certificates fr om few customers, which is expected to be regularized in Q2 of the current financial year

items.statement: Tega McNally consortium won NMDC order: INR872 crores total (INR120 crores Tega McNally share) for 7MTPA iron ore plant over 26 months
items.quote: Tega McNally has formed a consortium for designing and commissioning of a new 7 million ton per annum iron ore scre ening and beneficiation plant at Donimalai for NMDC Limited. The total contract value including taxes is INR872 crores with Tega McNally ’s share being INR120 crores and is to be executed over a period of 26 months

items.statement: Solar installations at Samali, Kalyani, Dahej plants totaling 1600-1700 kWh; no specific cost savings quantified yet
items.quote: Totally, if you see it's about 1600 to 1700 kilowatt hours of solar power, what we intend to harness.

items.statement: Tega McNally integration milestones and synergy targets progressing as per plan; 18-24 month integration timeline on track
items.quote: The integration milestones and the synergy targets are progressing as per the integration plan and we are satisfied with the progress made till date.

items.statement: Capex guidance for FY25 is INR 45-50 crores
items.quote: Our capex, if I look at the years gone by was focused largely on digitization and innovations. While that continues, we'll also keep investing on areas like R&D, etc. But we expect the year to end somewhere between INR 45 crores to INR 50 crores.

items.statement: Demand sentiment muted due to high food inflation; no material change expected in short term
items.quote: As we look at the period ahead, we do not see the demand sentiment changing materially in the short term. I think the food inflation being persistently high has dampened sentiment, the demand sentiment, consumer sentiment.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin at lifetime high 11.5% in Q1 FY25, up 166 bps YoY
items.quote: Adjusted EBITDA margins at 11.5% grew 166 basis points year on year.

items.statement: PBT margin pre-ESOP at 9.1%, up 219 bps YoY; PAT margin at 6.8%, up 186 bps YoY
items.quote: PBT margins pre-ESOP grew 219 basis points to 9.1% and PAT margins expanded 186 basis points to 6.8%.

items.statement: Service AMC volumes growing; revenue recognition lags 3-4 quarters due to 18-20 month amortization
items.quote: The second is that, as you can imagine, AMCs have a fairly long tenure. The average tenure is anywhere between 18 to 20 months. So, hence, the amortization happens over a fairly long Q1 FY25 Earnings Conference Call August 09, 2024 period of time. And hence, it will take three to four quarters for this to start getting reflected in the reported

items.statement: Commodity prices (polymers) rose in June; monitoring if trend sustains
items.quote: we've seen in the month of June in particular are in the case of certain commodities like polymers, we've seen prices go up. It's still Q1 FY25 Earnings Conference Call August 09, 2024 at a stage where we are in a bit of a wait-and-watch mode to see whether this sustains or not

items.statement: Vacuum cleaner ASPs rising significantly due to shift to convenient cleaning (robotics, upright) at ~4x conventional ASP
items.quote: And as you can imagine, the convenient cleaning segment comes at almost a 4X ASP higher than the conventional cleaning ASPs. So as the category mix evolves and moves towards convenient cleaning, both robotics and upright vacuum cleaner, we are seeing the ASPs improve.

items.statement: Water purifier ASPs up but range-bound; both premium and economy segments growing
items.quote: Equally, in water, there will be both the bookends growing. We will grow the premium segment through innovations and through point-of-sale innovations and interventions. There will also be a lot of effort in driving penetration. So I would say the ASPs will be, I think, up, but will be range-bound in the case of water.

items.statement: Market share gain in water purifiers vs same time last year, driven by premium segment
items.quote: Yes, pretty static report that we have seen a market share gain in water purifiers versus same time last year. And I think the good news is that we are beginning to see the impact of our premium innovations kick in.

items.statement: All regions grew double-digit; Tier-2/3 towns grew faster than Tier-1 metros
items.quote: is that our revenue growth across regions was in double-digit and all regions grew well. And there was no specific reason that was an outlier when it came to growth. In terms of town-wise growth, again, all town tiers grew, but what was an interesting sort of nuance was that our Tier-2 and Tier-3 towns grew faster than the tier-1 towns in metros

items.statement: >75% of economy water purifier buyers are first-time users
items.quote: And I think the good news and encouraging part is that more than 75% of customers who enter, who buy economy products, are first-time users.

items.statement: Welcomes competition including MNC entrant; believes category needs more innovation to unlock penetration
items.quote: I think on competition, I think this category needs more competition, it needs more innovation it needs more excitement to drive growth and to get consumers to re-evaluate this category to enter it. So we welcome all competition including the ones that you referred to.

items.statement: Existing manufacturing capacity adequate for current volume growth; no significant capex needed
items.quote: Even if I look at the volume growth that we've had, it's not required any significant investments on the manufacturing side. Our capacities are adequate to cater to it.

items.statement: Service revenue amortized over 18-20 months; costs incurred upfront causing margin compression in Q2
items.quote: Typically, in our case, the average tenure of an AMC ranges anywhere between 18 months to 20 months. Hence, what happens is that the AMC that you sell, for example, in a particular quarter, the revenue of that gets amortized over 18 months to 20 months. However, the cost for acquiring that AMC, that cost entirely comes upfront.

items.statement: Water purifier category penetration only ~6% in India; TAM expected to reach INR 23,000-24,000 crores in 5-6 years
items.quote: The expectation is that the categories in which we operate will anyway be between INR 23,000 to INR 24,000 crores in five to six years' time.

items.statement: RO segment growing faster than UV due to inconsistent source water quality
items.quote: So, Sri, I think clearly given the deteriorating water quality across the country, we are seeing the RO segment grow faster.

items.statement: High food inflation dampening consumer sentiment; demand environment could be brighter
items.quote: I think the food inflation being persistently high has dampened sentiment, the demand sentiment, consumer sentiment. That said, I think we have strong set of plans that we have deployed already.

items.statement: Rental model in pilot phase; not scaled up yet; prioritization decision pending
items.quote: Rental, as we've been saying, in our earlier calls as well, remains an area of opportunity that we are watching closely. And it's an area where we believe we have a right to win. We have not scaled up a rental project yet. It is in pilot, we are looking at it closely.

items.statement: Bundled AMC proportion at sale is very low; customers prefer to defer AMC decision
items.quote: The proportion of bundled AMCs upfront is very, very low. And I think if you think about the point I made earlier that one of the barriers that the customers face very often in the category, especially new entrants, is what they believe is a high cost of product and high cost of service.

items.statement: NPS at lifetime high in Q1; significant complaints closed within one hour
items.quote: Our NPS has never been higher. Our lifetime high NPS is what we reached in Q1 well above what we had in Q1 at the same time last year or indeed above the recent year of Q4, number one. Number two, we are seeing a significant number of complaints getting closed within one hour of either the customer facing the complaint or the customer's desired time of resolution.

items.statement: Management expects volumes to improve from Q1 but will wait another quarter to give proper guidance; growth slightly lower than earlier targets
items.quote: It will definitely be better than Q1, but still because of global uncertainties, demand in US and Europe is still subdued. So, we haven't been able to get a clear picture of how much we will be growing.

items.statement: Rail EBITDA/TEU at Rs 9,400; margin slipped due to lower volumes and double stack percentage down 2%
items.quote: The EBITDA margin has slipped a little bit because of the low volumes and our double stack percentage has gone down by say 2% this quarter so that reflects on the EBITDA margin

items.statement: CFS EBITDA per TEU improved to Rs 1,350-1,375 from Rs 540 last quarter
items.quote: CFS has maintained the same volume. And I mean the margins on CFS, if you compare them from the last quarter, which was from three digits have gone up to Rs.1,350 - Rs.1,375, last quarter it was Rs.540 only.

items.statement: EXIM growth expected to continue but pace uncertain; will clarify by end of quarter whether single or double digit
items.quote: I think the EXIM growth will continue. How much? That is to be seen. We cannot make any forward announcements or looking at what is happening everywhere. We will continue to grow.

items.statement: Overall India EXIM volume expected to grow at 5-6% level
items.quote: Overall, I think India is expected to grow at 5% - 6% level in terms of EXIM volume.

items.statement: Waste paper volumes down 30% at Kashipur and 10% at Ludhiana; bookings improving in July-August
items.value: 30% drop in Kashipur, 10% drop in Ludhiana
items.quote: Kashipur, 85% of the waste paper is import. So, there has been close to 30% drop in Kashipur. And in Ludhiana we have 20% of our import volumes and there has been almost 10% Gateway Distriparks Limited & drop in the import waste

items.statement: Jaipur terminal expected operational in 12-15 months; litigation ongoing but backup plan exists
items.quote: According to our present estimates, we will be operational in about 12-months from now.

items.statement: New northern terminal land identified; will be full-fledged ICD at one of their hubs
items.quote: It will be in north of India. So, it is yet to crystallize, I mean we have identified the land and once we have a deal and we acquire the land that will be the appropriate time to inform the location.

items.statement: Double stack percentage fell from 39% average last year to 33% in Q1; recovery to 40%+ will directly improve EBITDA
items.quote: So, last year we averaged at about 39%, but this quarter, we were at 33%. As and when the volume cut back and the imbalance within the ports also like Mundra, Pipavav, JNPT our volumes, some were import-heavy, some were export-heavy.

items.statement: Road has advantage with 10% busy season surcharge; passed on to customers but hope for revision
items.quote: So, little bit, road does have an advantage with the 10% busy season surcharge that came in. Although we passed it on, w e had no choice but to pass it on to our customers and that's been fully implemented now

items.statement: Lost market share YoY in Uttarakhand (25%) and Ludhiana (22.5% from 28%) due to pricing competition on low-value commodities
items.quote: Between Q4 and Q1, we are at the same market share that we had, but it's on a YoY basis we have lost market share in places like Uttarakhand and Ludhiana which we have mentioned in the last few quarters due to pricing competition.

items.statement: Faridabad double stacking completion in couple of months will help regain volumes lost to competitor
items.quote: One big factor is one location which has been connected on double stack and that's why the leader in our sector is gaining from that. As soon as Faridabad, which we just mentioned, is nearing completion, once that is operational, we will get quite a good s hare back what we have lost because of the double stacking advantage and to our competitor

items.statement: Low-value commodities (waste paper ~20%, scrap ~5%) constitute ~25% of volumes; concentrated in Kashipur (80%) and Ludhiana (20-25%)
items.quote: So, if you look at the low value commodities, we need to see a split into import and export. So, what we are talking about is that due to the dip in imports on the low value, so basically one is waste paper that constitutes about 20% of the overall volumes.

items.statement: DFC western corridor completion guided for December 2025; 93% complete up to Vaitarna
items.quote: DFC is giving us guidance of December 2025. And again, the status is the same that 93% of the total WDFC has completed up to Vaitarna and the last leg of 100 kilometers is still going to take a lot of time.

items.statement: Evaluating sale of all five CFS locations together; not piecemeal; Nhava Sheva property expected to fetch good valuation
items.quote: I don't think it will be a piecemeal affair. We let go all the five locations at a proper valuation.

items.statement: Stake in Snowman increased to 46.4%; can acquire up to 5% per year under creeping acquisition; may cross 50% this FY
items.quote: See, we are all owed to acquire 5% under creeping acquisition rules. So, last year we acquired 5%, this year we have acquired a little over 1% and we are at 46.4% now and if we complete the full 5% acquisition in this financial year, so we should be ending up little over 50

items.statement: Snowman 5PL vertical targets 25%+ YoY growth; new ice cream/dairy client to contribute Rs 15-18 cr/quarter from August
items.quote: So, as we explained last time, we have expectations of more than 25% year-on-year growth on this particular vertical to distribute which is the 5PL vertical.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing business expects 12-15% growth this year with new facilities in Lucknow and Kolkata
items.quote: considering the new facilities which are going to be functional in next month, Lucknow and after that Kolkata, and also some of the lease capacities which we are yet to fully utilize, considering all these, we expect around 12% to 15% growth in warehousing business this year.

items.statement: Snowman Q1 margins impacted by Rs 2-2.5 cr one-off costs; Q4 had provision reversals; underlying margins stable
items.quote: So, there are two reasons. One is, there has been some one -off cost which we accounted in this particular quarter, which were one-time cost and we had to take that in repairs and maintenance and some of the accounting

items.statement: Tax rate to stay at 6-7% for next two years
items.quote: Yes, it will stay like this for the next two years at least.

items.statement: Net debt at Rs 245 crores (lowest); gross debt Rs 310 crores; down significantly from Rs 800 crores peak
items.quote: Our debt situation is very good right now. I mean we at our lowest net debt to INR 245 crores compared to which was at one-time INR 800 crores or something and even from last quarter last year, if you see it has come down significantly.

items.statement: Capex this quarter not significant; full year plans include Jaipur and new northern terminal
items.quote: not significant CAPEX this quarter, but for the overall year, we still have plans like we have been announcing for one new terminal is in immediate site, plus some balance on Jaipur land.

items.statement: Kashipur long-term target 5,000-6,000 TEUs/month in 5 years; Jaipur target 3,000 TEUs/month in 3 years
items.quote: longer term what we were saying in five years we should be doing 5,000 - 6,000 from this location that will remain the same.

items.statement: NCR market ~2.9 lakh TEUs/quarter; Ludhiana ~65,000 TEUs/quarter (down from 80,000 Q4); Uttarakhand 20,000-25,000 TEUs/quarter
items.quote: roughly if you look at NCR, it was about 2.9 lakhs for the quarter, this is the whole volume of NCR. And if we look at it Q1 last year, it was a very similar figure. So, less than a pe rcent variance. And Q4 was slightly higher; it was crossing 3 lakhs

items.statement: Global uncertainties (Red Sea, port congestion, US/Europe demand) affecting visibility; election and budget policy changes added to Q1 weakness
items.quote: overall that red sea impact still continues, there has a lot of port congestion at various international ports, vessel schedule has been erratic over the last few months. But slightly we have seen some improvement towards June, July is also looking slightly better.

items.statement: CFS revenue impacted by Rs 8.43 cr accounting change (discounts netted from revenue); no impact on EBITDA/TEU
items.quote: This is basically a business model done with consolidators, but it was discount being passed on was actually earlier being counted in the revenue. But as per the accounting standard now, that comes under gross revenue, but under net revenue we have to remove this discount.

items.statement: Acquired 2.2 acres of land in Mumbai Oshiwara from MHADA for Rs. 125.11 crores to build a ~500 bed super specialty hospital.
items.quote: We are extremely pleased to acquire 2.2 acres of prime land in Mumbai Oshiwara in an auction from Maharashtra Housing and Area Development Authority (MHADA). This is an important milestone in Medanta's growth journey, as we plan to establish a state of the art ~500 bed super specialty hospital in Oshiwara.

items.statement: Board approved construction of service apartment guest house at Gurugram campus with investment of approximately Rs. 250 crores.
items.quote: have secured Board approval to construct the service apartment guest house on the Medanta Medicity GurugramGurugram campus. This project, with an investment of approximately Rs. 250 crores, will cater to the growing demand from international as well as out of town domestic patients

items.statement: Added 49 census beds in Gurugram mother and child department and 18 new dialysis beds at Patna unit.
items.quote: We have added 49 census beds in Gurugram in our mother and child department, as Dr. Trehan already mentioned. Furthermore, we have added 18 new dialysis beds at our Patna unit, as the demand for our nephrology services in the region continues to remain strong.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin declined to 23.6% due to employee cost increments and sluggish Lucknow growth; mature hospitals EBITDA grew 11.6%.
items.quote: EBITDA for the quarter was Rs. 2,082 million, an increase of 4.5% year-on-year basis, with an EBITDA margin of 23.6%. Our margins have declined primarily due to increase in employee cost on account of annual increments and some sluggish growth in our Lucknow unit.

items.statement: Outpatient pharmacy revenue increased 25.6% YoY from Rs. 266 million to Rs. 334 million.
items.quote: Our outpatient pharmacy business revenue increased by 25.6% from Rs. 266 million in Q1 FY24 to Rs. 334 million in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: International patient revenue was Rs. 475 million (~6% of total revenue), flat YoY vs Rs. 477 million.
items.quote: During the quarter, revenue from international patients was Rs. 475 million, compared to Rs. 477 million in the same quarter last year. This accounts for approximately 6% of the total revenue.

items.statement: Started treating Ayushman Bharat patients in Lucknow; applied for CGHS and other government scheme empanelment.
items.quote: indicated in our earlier calls, with the increased bed capacity, we have already signed up and started treating patients in Ayushman Bharat Scheme. Furthermore, we have applied for empanelment with the CGHS and other government schemes

items.statement: Planned equipment investments in Lucknow include new biplane Cath Lab and Da Vinci Xi surgical robot; additional investments in Indore and Ranchi.
items.quote: We will be putting in a new Cath Lab, we already have two Cath Labs, we will be adding in our third Cath Lab, in fact it's a biplane Cath Lab, so it's a pretty high end machine. We will be adding in a Da Vinci Xi surgical robot that should come onboard in next several weeks.

items.statement: Manpower cost increases budgeted for the year due to talent competition; clinical talent additions to continue impacting costs.
items.quote: We do anticipate and have budgeted a certain increase in the manpower cost on an overall basis, as well as some maybe on a percentage of revenue basis, just because we feel that there will be increasing intensity for high quality talent given all the various hospitals and all the excitement and investment going into hospitals and healthcare.

items.statement: Operating leverage expected to improve developing hospital margins as volumes recover; scheme patients viewed as margin-accretive due to low marginal cost.
items.quote: Overall, our belief is that because the marginal cost to serve every incremental patient for us is significantly lower. We generally believe that increased volume, even at lower realizations is margin accretive, and we have seen that play out again and agai n, year-over-year in our GurugramGurugram facility

items.statement: Lucknow performance below expectations; management not satisfied but cautions against using last year's high baseline (seasonal dengue, lower bed count).
items.quote: we are by no means satisfied with this performance. But I would caution if we put a baseline of saying, you will be at 75% let's not forget that we have increased Global Health Limited – Medanta August 09, 2024 bed capacity and some of the performance, which you saw last year were really, really I would say above normal performance

items.statement: No financial guidance provided; management refuses to give specific projections for mature or developing hospitals.
items.quote: As we have stated multiple times, we don't give any future projections or any expectations with respect to the specific numbers on either of our developing or matured hospitals.

items.statement: FY25 consolidated revenue growth guidance 20-25% YoY and EBITDA margin 20-22%
items.quote: We are on the track to achieve FY25 guidance of consolidated revenue growth of 20 %-25% year-on-year and EBITDA margin in the range of 20 %-22%.

items.statement: Block 1 of 2 lakh sq ft commercialized in May 2024; Block 2 of 2 lakh sq ft expected by March 2025
items.value: 5 lakh sq ft total greenfield expansion
items.quote: Block 1 of 2 lakh square feet in May 2024. This is just one part of our overall green field expansion project of 5 lakh square feet. Block 2 of another 2 lakh square feet is expected to be completed by March 2025

items.statement: Block 1 operational for LED home lighting, solar panels, systems and new categories; Block 2 civil construction ongoing
items.value: 2 lakh sq ft operational; 2 lakh sq ft under construction
items.quote: Block one of our new integrated facility, nearly 2 lakh square feet, is commercialized in May 2024. This facility will be used for the manufacturing of LED home lighting, solar panels, systems, and other new categories of products.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin 13% impacted by new facility costs, USA subsidiary start-up and higher employee costs; expected to stabilize by H2 FY25
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was at 13%, which was impacted by the higher employee benefit cost, operational cost for the new facility and starting of our USA subsidiary.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue up 17% YoY and 34% QoQ across all three verticals; domestic lighting market flat, Gulf exports aided product display
items.quote: For instance, if you look at our revenues, Q1 FY25, it was up 17% year -on-year and 34% quarter-on-quarter. This was an account of all our three vertical business we are doing.

items.statement: Hearables and Wearables sales commenced in Q1 with prestigious clients onboarded; categorized under product display segment for now
items.quote: Coming to the Hearables and Wearables segment, I am happy to inform you that our sales have commenced in quarter 1 and we have successfully on boarded few prestigious clients in this segment.

items.statement: US subsidiary started ESCO and solar product business; initial orders executed with bought-out items impacting margins
items.quote: Yes, if you talk of the business that has come into the direct, I mean, into the subsidiary that is there in the U.S., which is new. So that is the category that we have started in this subsidiary.

items.statement: Main customer Signify was slow last quarter; now things improved across sectors; RV business turnaround expected by H2 FY25
items.quote: Our main customers, the Signify were a little slow. And the overall business, that was a degrowth. So similarly, in the inshore lighting, the main reliance and others were little, but they were revamping their things. So but now the things are almost improved at all the sectors.

items.statement: Exports from India ~INR 12-13 crore in Q1 FY25 with good jump QoQ; UAE exports started, Saudi market potential
items.quote: And I'm just looking for the number right now, it's somewhere close to around INR12 crores to INR13 crores that we posted in that, the export business from India.

items.statement: Debt-free balance sheet maintained; IPO debt repayment completed immediately after IPO
items.quote: Our financial position continued to remain strong with a debt -free balance sheet, well -funded capex cycle and healthy return ratio.

items.statement: More than half of IPO proceeds deployed; on track to deploy rest within set timeline
items.quote: We have now deployed more than half of the IPO fund and are on course to complete, deploying the rest within the timeline we set for ourselves.

items.statement: Target ROCE 30-35% for Hearables and Wearables business once fully established
items.quote: So in that case if you look at the ROCE going forward once this business is fully established our target is to stay in the range of 30% to 35% when it comes to the return on capital employed and that is what we are targeting with this particular business as well

items.statement: Pre-IPO ROCE consistently 30-35%; FY24 ROCE decline due to capex investments; expected to return to 30-35% as new factories ramp
items.quote: But if you look at pre-IPO proceeds before we started making all these investments, our ROCE has always been consistent in the line of 30% to 35%. And going forward, once the expenditure that we have made in the new factories and the expenses that we are currently doing, it is going to give the returns in the near future.

items.statement: Fine Technologies merged into Royalux Lighting recently
items.quote: Yes. So we've merged Fine Technologies into Royalux Lighting. So that is something that we've done recently.

items.statement: Full backward integration in-house: metal, plastic, CNC, moulds, powder coating, tool designing and tool making
items.quote: Yes. We are doing metal, plastic, even doing CNC, even doing our mo ulds. A month and a half before all that, all the investors they visited our facility, they have seen that everything is somewhere under installation, some machines are already installed, including the powder coating and all, everything we are doing in -house. Even the tool designing, tool making is also we are doing in-house.

items.statement: Standalone margins normalized at current ~11% EBITDA after price corrections last year due to muted demand; Q4 FY24 to Q1 FY25 margins steady and growing
items.quote: So we believe that if you look at the standalone numbers, where we are today, this is the margin range for this business. Because last year due to that, muted supply, there was a lot of panic, I would say in the industry, because the demand certainly, was nose diving.

items.statement: Gross margin volatility 36-46% driven by US subsidiary bought-out items and minimum wage increase; temporary phase expected to normalize
items.quote: This year, first quarter the only reason for this sort of decline is the kind of business that we did in the first quarter in the US subsidiary. Like I told in the previous question also that because of the constraint in time and we wanted to establish that relationship with the client.

items.statement: Consistently ahead of peers due to new product lines and backward integration setup; industry saw big decline in FY24 while IKIO remained consistent
items.quote: Even if you look at last year, if you compare our peers to us, we've sort of much ahead of everyone. Yes, so that was only due to the fact that, we constantly bring in new products, we constantly, work on new product lines, not just the new products, but even product categories or product lines.

items.statement: New verticals require team setup and product development expenditure; shorter timeline due to existing electronics design and manufacturing expertise
items.quote: Initially, the costs are generally very high when it comes to establishing the team, development of the product, the sample, a lot of cost is involved a nd by the time you start reaping the benefits . And for us I think we feel that because the kind of business that we've been doing since a very long time which is into lighting and electronics. So we feel that time for us is going to be fairly sho

items.statement: RV business inventory clearances continuing quarter on quarter in energy solutions segment
items.quote: In the segment of energy solution and others, we are witnessing continued pickup in inventory clearances quarter on quarter.

items.statement: Government sudden minimum wage increase impacted gross margin in last quarter
items.quote: What happened is actually, in the last quarter, the government suddenly increased the minimum wages also but because of that also gross margin.

items.statement: Other income increased YoY due to FD income from unutilized IPO proceeds and forex capital gains
items.quote: So other income is , one is our normal income from FDs of the unutilized proceeds from the IPO. And then there is some forex capital gain also, currency, there is something that also we got.

items.statement: Management expects 30-40% top-line CAGR over the next three years
items.quote: If you want to know, then the company will grow at a pace of 30% to 40% per annum in the next coming three years.

items.statement: Revenue growth of at least 30% expected from new flagship showroom
items.quote: We are expecting revenue growth of at least 30% from the new store.

items.statement: Current capex sufficient for flagship showroom; further capex to be decided later
items.quote: The current capex is whatever the company is holding. It is going to work with the current capex for the next coming up showroom. And the further requirement of capital would be decided by the management on a later scale.

items.statement: New 10,000 sq ft flagship showroom in Sowcarpet opening in 9-12 months (Jan-Apr FY26)
items.quote: We will be recalibrating our revenue distribution, focusing entirely onto the B2C segment in our new showroom to enhance our market position and better serve our customers.

items.statement: Plan to open five to six showrooms in two years after flagship launch
items.quote: Initially, our flagship showroom would be opening in another 9 to 12 months. And further from there for the coming two years, we have an expansion plan of geographical expansion here around five to six showrooms in the coming years.

items.statement: EBITDA margin currently around 5.5%; expected to rise as B2C mix increases (B2B ~4%, B2C ~8-9%)
items.quote: The current EBITDA margin is around 5.5% and it is since we are expanding into the retail segment for the coming years, the margin would be surely increasing because the difference between the B2B and B2C segment the margins are around for B2B segment it is around 4% and for B2C it is around 8% to 9%.

items.statement: Retail (B2C) to contribute ~25% of top line after new showroom opens
items.quote: Among that 25% of the top line would be in retail in the coming years after the opening of showroom.

items.statement: Custom duty cut on gold/silver (15% to 6%) and platinum (12.5% to 6.4%) lowers procurement costs; benefit passed to customers immediately
items.quote: Yes, obviously. It is the price is amended immediately from the time of his amendment, the prices of the gold and silver has been reduced. And from the same period, it has been transferred to the clients also because the prices immediately changes, and it gets affected to the market immediately.

items.statement: Shift to lightweight, budget jewellery due to rising gold prices; new designs added daily
items.quote: Since the gold prices have been appreciating, everybody prefers to buy a lightweight jewellery, a budgeted jewellery. So we have been manufacturing that too. And we are, on a daily basis, making researchers to make products more attractive and more reachable.

items.statement: B2B client base includes major multi-store jewellers and generational jewellers across South India
items.quote: We are working with all the major jewellers who are famous and who are operating in multi-stores. Those players who are having familiar name, Pan India. And a few traditional jewelers who are having a very famous and who have been working with us from past four decades, five decades.

items.statement: No exports currently; working on plans to enter export market
items.quote: The company has been currently we do not engage in exports, but the company has further plans of making. We are working on going expansion towards the export market.

items.statement: Current working capital sufficient for flagship showroom; further funding to be decided later
items.quote: Currently, the current stocks and the current working capital will be enough sufficient for the opening of this initial flagship showroom. On a later scale, when there are further expansions, the management will be deciding on getting the source of funds for expansion.

items.statement: Sanctioned loan limit INR 38 cr; utilisation INR 17-18 cr last quarter
items.value: INR 38 crores sanctioned; INR 17 to INR 18 crores utilised
items.quote: I am sorry. It is a limit that is sanctioned for INR38 crores, but the company has been last quarterly utilizing it to the extent of INR17 to INR18 crores.

items.statement: Focus shifting to high-value temple jewellery, diamond and polki jewellery in new showroom
items.quote: Since we are going to add all the premium products along with the diamond jewellery and polki jewellery of the new showroom, so the margins are going to be higher.

items.statement: Organised sector share rose from 17% (2019) to 34% now; duty cut to accelerate shift
items.quote: If you take a data wise, if you say it was around 17% was with the organized sector in 2019. Now it has been improved to 34%. And after the reduction of duty, it is going to be a very plus point for the organized sector

items.statement: Primary raw material is fine gold; pilferage/wastage 0.8-2% during manufacturing
items.quote: It is around, say, 0.8 to 2%.

items.statement: Artisan relationships span 25-40 years across India; design library >5 lakh unique designs
items.quote: We have been working with artisans who are along with us from last 40 years, 30 years, 25 years, who are working with the company and providing us the best quality craftsmanship for the company and for its customers.

items.statement: No split or bonus decided yet; management will decide later
items.quote: That management has to decide. Till now, nothing of that sort has been decided. Later on, anything which will be decided will be surely posted.

items.statement: Gold price rise seen as positive; no demand concern as gold viewed as investment
items.quote: No, no issue at all. Since the prices have been increasing and it is providing a better return opportunity for all the investors who have invested in gold in regular interval. So, everybody is optimistic about gold in near future also.

items.statement: Targets ~19.5% EBITDA margin for Q2-Q4 FY25
items.quote: However, we remain quite confident in our ability to achieve about 19.5% EBITDA margin mark in the fo llowing three

items.statement: Targets 4.5-5% revenue contribution from steel bottles and houseware in FY25
items.quote: Overall, we are targeting around 4.5% to 5% contribution coming from steel bottles and steel bottles and household as a category both put together around 4.5% to 5% of the overall revenue.

items.statement: Pen demand picked up in second half of Q1 after elections; own brands grew 7% YoY domestically
items.quote: Overall, demand picked up in the second half of quarter post the peak of elections. Despite facing such challenges in the demand environment our own brands grew by 7% year -on-year in the domestic market signifying their resilience and wider market

items.statement: Creative segment grew 21.4% YoY to INR 37 crores in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Creative as a segment increased in Q1 25 by 21.4% year-on-year with the revenue clocking in at INR37 crores.

items.statement: Steel bottles grew 116% YoY to INR 8 crores with growing order book
items.quote: Steel bottles has gathered the momentum registering a 116% year-on-year increase to INR8 crores. Aggressive scaling, robust enquiries and a growing order book in the category provide an exciting outlook for this segment.

items.statement: Overall ASP increased to INR 5.29 in Q1 FY25 from INR 5.27 in Q1 FY24
