items.quote: Despite certain challenges, our ASP for the overall business increased from INR 5.27 in Q1 24 and INR 5.17 in Q4 24 to current INR 5.29 in Q1 25, a testament of our focus on premiumization strategy.

items.statement: Own brand sales mix improved to 87% in Q1 FY25 from 83% in Q1 FY24
items.quote: Contribution of our own brand sales to overall mix improved to 87% in Q1 25 from 83% Q124 with overall own brand sales growing by 5% on year-on-year basis to INR215 crores.

items.statement: Export own brand sales declined 9% due to Red Sea freight issues; export OEM grew 10%
items.quote: Persistent geopolitical issues around the Red Sea have raised freight costs and created a shortage of shipping containers, bottlenecking supply to the export markets thus affecting overseas own brand sales although demand remains intact. However, we received a very encouraging update from export OEM segment which is on a gradual, but a definite path of recovery, increasing by 10% in the current qu

items.statement: Domestic OEM demand subdued, expected to remain at Q1 levels; to be offset by own brand growth
items.quote: Domestic OEM face a subdued demand and is expected to remain at current quarterly levels whi ch we propose to make up from our own brand sales in domestic market

items.statement: Capex plans on track; creative manufacturing lines ordered, targeting 75% in-house by end of FY25 or early FY26
items.quote: So, as we mentioned that, the capex plan is already on and, everything is in time as per the schedule. And, once the capex, similarly, even for the creative, all the manufacturing lines have been already ordered and set up. So, I think by the end of t he year or early next year we should be making , up to 75% of our total business. What we get from creative would be manufactured in-house

items.statement: Added 20+ distributors and 15 salesmen for steel bottles; entered Reliance and other modern trade
items.quote: Yes. So, in domestic market for steel bottles, we have already appointed 20 plus distributors and we have also recruited around 15 salesmen. And other than that, we have also set up a separate department to cater to modern trade and we have already, got into Reliance and other departmental stores.

items.statement: GST demands mostly replied/settled; two under appeal but liability not substantial
items.quote: Almost all of the GST demands have been replied to or have been settled. So, we don't see a liability out here at our end because... Vimalchand Rathod: There will be some liability. Because it is an appeal. So, as soon as the appeal is settled, then we will know the exact -- But it will not be

items.statement: Steel sourced from India and importers from Korea, Vietnam, China; BIS standards to reduce imports over time
items.quote: And as BIS standards will become more stringent these imports will reduce going on and on. And also from our part, we are having a combi nation of sourcing from steel from India as well as a couple of importers which import from various countries like Korea, Vietnam and other countries and China for us

items.statement: Alpesh Porwal appointed as new CFO with two decades experience; Mayur Gala ceased as CFO and KMP
items.quote: It gives me immense pleasure to welcome Mr. Alpesh Porwal as the new Chief Financial Officer of the company. He has two decades of experience across various functional areas and will provide us with invaluable insights. Mr. Alpesh Porwal succeeds the outgoing Mr. Mayur Gala, who ceases to be the Chief Financial Officer and KMP.

items.statement: Monthly revenue run rate: April INR 61.57 cr, May INR 93 cr, June INR 98 cr, July similar to June
items.quote: Just to add, on the April number was about INR61.57 crores, which moved to about INR93 crores in May and INR98 crores in June.

items.statement: Red Sea geopolitical issues raising freight costs 3-5x and container shortages impacting export own brand sales
items.quote: Persistent geopolitical issues around the Red Sea have raised freight costs and created a shortage of shipping containers, bottlenecking supply to the export markets thus affecting overseas own brand sales although demand remains intact.

items.statement: Re-entered INR 5 price point using existing moulds/machinery; no significant capex needed
items.quote: we received good initial marke t feedback on the relaunch of INR5 MRP products and we remain intact on focusing on this segment as we can leverage our past investments into moulds and machinery to grow this segment without any significant need of additional capex

items.statement: Zoox premium pen brand currently limited to A-class counters; will expand to B/C class in Q3-Q4
items.quote: So, Zoox purposely we haven't launched pan India. We have launched only in few selected outlets because being a little expensive premium plastic pens. So we were focusing on only A class counters. We haven't reached out to B and C class counters. So maybe going forward, we would be entering into those B and C categories as well.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant under construction with three tube mills, slitting line, galvanizing unit; 10,000 tonnes capacity similar to Maharashtra plant
items.quote: At the moment, after the land being purchased, the plant is under process. We have erected two tube mills, three tube mills we are installing in that area with Slitting line and galvanized unit.

items.statement: Hyderabad added second galvanizing line for crash barrier production; achieved 1,200 tonnes dispatch last month vs 500 tonnes earlier
items.quote: Just last month, we have achieved the target of 1200 tonnes of dispatch of galvanized product called crash barrier or highway guardrail, before that it is used to be only 500 tonnes.

items.statement: Orders placed for Octagon Pole and High Mast Pole machinery to be installed at Jharsuguda
items.quote: we are in way of achieving the machineries for those products are also being placed, orders of those machines have been placed and they shall also be getting installed in Jharsuguda location in its view.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant trial run or production targeted for Q2 FY25
items.quote: we had given a timeline of somewhere 2nd Quarter and 2nd Quarter for the plant to start its trial run or its production and we are well on our way to achieve that target.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant production expected by September or October 2024; GI plant ~50% complete; one month delay due to heavy rain
items.quote: I feel we are going to be in the production in the month of September, it may go up to October, but not beyond that.

items.statement: Monopole machinery delivery expected August or September 2024
items.quote: The machineries like monopole and all will be finalized, and that machine will come in the month of August or September, I think so.

items.statement: Expect increase in production, sales, and profit visible in October-November 2024
items.quote: All these things are happening now which you can watch very easily in the month of October and November, you can watch increase in production, increase in sales, and increase in profit.

items.statement: Profit decline due to steel price correction post-COVID; prices back to pre-COVID levels; volume stable
items.quote: This decline of the profit is a cycle of steel which was expected after the revise of steel prices due to covid. The ripple effect of covid has taken its own due course to settle up.

items.statement: Quantity sold Q1 FY25 36,747 tonnes vs 38,129 tonnes Q4 FY24; revenue impact from price decline not volume
items.quote: Last quarter in 2023-24, the quantity was 38,129 and 2024-25, it is 36,747, so quantity wise it is not decreased, because of the pricing goes down, that's why sale is effected in the terms of amount.

items.statement: IPO proceeds (Rs 72.17 cr) mostly used for raw material procurement; ~Rs 3 cr remaining in FD
items.quote: This working capital is only utilized in our procurement of raw material which was the reason why we raised IPO. It was mentioned as well and that's exactly were the fund has been utilized. Most of the fund is utilized there. I think we have very little, which is in the form of FD. I am not sure about the exact number it should be around 3 crores.

items.statement: IPO funds reduced working capital debt; CC/OD interest cost under control; interest expense to decrease significantly
items.quote: I believe with the IPO being successful, the money has been raised for working capital. So, now we have been able to manage our debt significantly effectively so that has been taken care and so our bank interest for the working capital which is a CC or OD limit that has been under control which was our target.

items.statement: Long-term assets funded via internal accruals and term loans, not IPO proceeds
items.quote: No not for the long-term assets. It has been done through our internal approval and also the term loan that we had taken from the bank.

items.statement: Total installed capacity 221,000 metric tonnes per annum across two units each in Telangana and Maharashtra
items.quote: VSTL has two manufacturing units each in Telangana and Maharashtra with the total installed capacity of 221,000 metric tonnes per annum.

items.statement: Jharsuguda plant capacity 10,000 tonnes similar to Maharashtra plant
items.quote: The installed capacity of Jharsuguda plant is similar to what we have in the western region of India in Maharashtra, which are 10,000 tonnes.

items.statement: Crash barrier (highway guardrail) production ramped up; new products Octagon Pole and High Mast Pole planned for Jharsuguda
items.quote: during IPO, we had promised that once we established ourselves in crash barriers, we will go ahead and introduce other products as well such as Octagon Pole, High Mast Pole and we are in way of achieving the machineries for those products are also being placed

items.statement: IPO in February 2024 raised Rs 72.17 crores on BSE and NSE
items.quote: in February 2024, VSTL made a stellar debut on BSE and NSE raising Rs. 72.17 crores from the IPO.

items.statement: Stock placed under SEBI surveillance; management attributes price decline to surveillance
items.quote: Because they have put this share in surveillance, SEBI has put this share in surveillance that's why it is down.

items.statement: Jharsuguda project faced labor shortage during elections and heavy rain delays
items.quote: Two months later, elections came up, and since the laborers were from Bihar, they couldn't come. Then it rained for two months. Despite all these challenges, we continued to work with full determination.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance of 12-14% for FY25
items.quote: We are still, I would say, on track to do a $12%-14% kind of growth number. We did guide for, did not guide for 15%, we guided for 12-14%. We are still on track.

items.statement: Howrah Hospital occupancy expected to exceed 50% in Q2 and meet annual guidance
items.quote: At this point also in quarter 2 we are tracking a figure of more than 50%. So we are fairly confident that on an overall year-ending basis we will be tracking a guidance figure on this.

items.statement: Raipur hospital commissioning by February 2025 adding 155 beds
items.quote: We are coming up with our fifth hospital in Raipur. This should be commissioned by February of 2025. With this, we will be adding another 155 odd beds to our portfolio.

items.statement: Ranchi hospital under construction, expected to commence in FY27
items.quote: We are potentially looking at that starting commencing in FY '27.

items.statement: Raipur capex spent INR5-7 crores in CWIP; Ranchi only security deposit spent
items.quote: In Raipur, we have spent almost INR5 to INR7 crores in capital works in progress and the equipment ordering process, the major chunk of our expenses already started.

items.statement: Initial cash loss for new hospitals estimated at INR5-7 crores
items.quote: It would be around INR5 to INR10 crores in the initial period. For the initial period where we will be likely to sustain cash loss that will be the INR5 to INR7 crores mark.

items.statement: Target to become 1,000-bed hospital chain in 2-3 years
items.quote: I am excited to share our ambitious goal of becoming a 1,000-bed hospital chain within the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Dum Dum ALOS reduced to 4.74 days from 5.19 YoY; Salt Lake ALOS reduced to 2.78 days from 3.32 QoQ
items.quote: Dum Dum Hospital has recorded an ARPOB of approximately INR.40,000 for the quarter. In line with our intent to reduce the average length of stay of this hospital, the ALOS has reduced to 4.74 days compared to 5.19 days of the previous year.

items.statement: Company ARPOB at INR36,500; Salt Lake ARPOB rose to ~INR40,000; Dum Dum ARPOB ~INR40,000; Howrah ARPOB rose to ~INR33,000 from INR26,000
items.quote: Notably, our ARPOB stands at 36,500, aligning with our commitment to serving the aspiring population of the society with higher disposable income in the middle to high-income segment.

items.statement: Company bed occupancy at 53%; ALOS 3.62 days vs 4.0 YoY
items.quote: The company-level bed occupancy currently stands at around 53%, with an ALOS of 3.62 days compared to 4.0 on a YoY basis.

items.statement: Q1 revenue grew 1.7% YoY to INR97.8 crores despite seasonally weak quarter and election overhang
items.quote: Revenues for Q1 FY25 witnessed a 1.7% year-on-year growth, totalling to INR97.8 crores with total income of INR100.1 crores, up by 2.5% year-on-year.

items.statement: Q2 monthly revenue run rate tracking ~INR37 crores in July
items.quote: We are right now on a monthly run rate of almost INR 36-37 crores in terms of revenues in Q2.

items.statement: EBITDA INR20.2 crores at 20.2% margin; PAT INR10 crores at 10% margin; finance costs down 57%
items.quote: EBITDA for the year amounted to INR20.2 crores, with an EBITDA margin of 20.2%. Profit after tax for the quarter stood at INR10 crores with a 10% PAT margin. Finance costs have come down by 57% on account of reduction in debt.

items.statement: ARPOB increase driven by case mix change, TPA and cash price hikes, and new specialities like robotics and oncology
items.quote: There was a slight price correction in the beginning of the financial year for cash patients, but that was a very small component. Apart from that, insurance companies as and when the term or their term of contract expires and renews, there is a price correction there as well.

items.statement: Employee cost up due to annual salary increments; medicine cost down due to case mix; doctor fees and robot vendor payouts up
items.quote: Yes so the employee cost has gone up due to the annual increase in the salaries for the employees which happens every April. If you see in terms of the cost structure due to the change in case mix, the medicine cost or the cost of material consumed has come down, whereas other expenses have slightly gone up because the doctor expenses has gone up.

items.statement: ~95% of patient business from cash and insurance; ~5-7% of Agartala patients from Bangladesh

items.statement: New R&D centre opened in Japan with Japanese design engineers for closer OEM collaboration
items.quote: During the quarter, we opened a new R&D centre in Japan and also expanded our design team. This will enable closer collaboration with our Japanese customers.

items.statement: No PLI benefits currently availed, will examine if government opportunity arises
items.quote: We currently don't have any PLI benefit or scheme that we are availing. If there is any opportunity that comes by from government, we will examine it -- at this point of time, we don't have it.

items.statement: Hub motor volumes to start in FY25 and grow further in FY26 after Gogoro price reduction and new battery launch
items.quote: FY '25 will start with the volume and it will be go further by 2026, FY '26.

items.statement: INR35 crores already invested in hub motor segment
items.quote: INR35 crores, approximately.

items.statement: 4-wheeler margins expected to remain similar to current levels initially, with efforts to improve
items.quote: So margins would remain approximately at similar levels for 4-wheelers. The industry margins are the same. However, our efforts will be to make it better. That will be our direction because most of the facilities do exist in the organization. But currently, for guidance purposes, the margins are similar to the current level.

items.statement: All current order book is for LED products only
items.quote: All order book as of now is LED only.

items.statement: 4-wheeler revenue currently less than 1%, target to reach significant double-digit level in 5 years
items.quote: At this moment, for all guidance you take, it is even less than 1%. Our direction is to take it to a significant level in coming 5 years.

items.statement: Margin improvement in Q1 FY25 vs Q4 due to raw material mix shift from rice to maize and good Rabi crop in East India
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we saw a margin improvement compared to Q4 due to a change in raw material mix away from rice and to maize, and due to a good Rabi crop in East India.

items.statement: Procured additional maize inventory to control raw material costs in East India
items.quote: In this period, we also managed to procure additional inventory of maize, which is helping us keep RM costs under some control in the East.

items.statement: Promising margin recovery expected towards end of Q3 with good monsoons, normal paddy crop, and increased maize cultivation
items.quote: However, a more promising recovery in margin is expected towards the end of Q3 with good monsoons, expectations of a normal paddy crop and a significant increase in maize cultivation across the country.

items.statement: Average commodity cycle margin is Rs. 7 per liter with volatility; actively hedging maize positions with traders and stockists
items.quote: As mentioned previously, our average commodity cycle margins is in the range of Rs. 7 per liter with periods of volatility in margins during the course of the cycle.

items.statement: Expect profitability and productivity improvement of 15-20% in next 2 quarters with maize operations
items.quote: We hope to improve our profitability and productivity, which should increase our profitability by about 15% to 20% in the next 2 quarters.

items.statement: UP distillery CAPEX of Rs. 120 crores for 80 KL capacity with molasses and grain flexibility; construction starts post-monsoon, completion in 14-16 months
items.quote: The CAPEX of this facility is expected to be around Rs. 120 crores.

items.statement: Prestige & Above segment volume 0.19 million cases, up 292% YoY and 50% QoQ; entered Goa taking total states to 7
items.quote: For the quarter gone by, we witnessed a sales volume of 0.19 million cases with a growth of 292% year-on-year and 50% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Regular & Others segment volume 3.95 million cases, up 13% YoY and 15% QoQ; EBITDA Rs. 430 million, up 47% QoQ
items.quote: This segment continues to perform well for the Company with a total volume of 3.95 million and a growth of 13% year-on-year and 15% quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Launched GR8 Times in UP, Brothers & Co. whisky in UP, NOT OUT RTD in Delhi; Mountain Oak and Snoski Vodka expanding to new states
items.quote: we launched GR8 Times brand in UP. The state has the largest salience of Regular & Others category in India, and we're excited about the prospects of the state, ba cked by our own production premises in Lakhimpur, Central UP

items.statement: Net revenue Rs. 642 crores, up 13% YoY and 6% QoQ; EBITDA margin 8% vs 4% in Q4; net debt Rs. 331 crores, up 35% QoQ and 31% YoY
items.quote: As a result of the above, the EBITDA margin is at 8%, which for Q4 was at 4%.

items.statement: Bottle costs reducing by Rs. 0.17 per bottle effective August 2024, mitigating packing cost pressures in Q1
items.quote: with bottle costs reducing by Rs. 0.17 per bottle effective August '24, the same will be mitigated.

items.statement: Distribution strategy: 7 states for mainstream brands, luxury-only states like Goa; focus on strengthening route-to-market in existing 7 states this year
items.quote: at this point of time, this year, we are expecting that we will more or less remain with these 7 states. And towards the end of the financial year, we will start speeding work on a couple of states which will go through their initial phases in the coming years.

items.statement: Target: 20% of consumer business from Prestige & Above in about a year, but difficult to project due to Regular & Others growth in UP
items.quote: Maybe about a year or so, I have said that our target is 20% of o ur consumer business should come from Prestige & Above

items.statement: Subsidiary loss of Rs. 54 lakhs is a one-time debtor write-off of Rs. 45 lakhs; not included in Prestige & Above EBITDA
items.quote: the loss is Rs. 54 lakhs, not Rs. 5 crores, and it's a onetime write-off that we had to do. We are chasing for the money, it's a debtor's write-off that we had to do of around about Rs. 45 lakhs.

items.statement: UP distillery capacity 80 KL, dual feed (molasses/grain); Bengal and Jharkhand plants debottlenecking at Rs. 5-7 crores to improve maize throughput, completion in 2 quarters
items.quote: Debottlenecking is not an expensive process, Rs. 5 crores, Rs. 7 crores for our Bengal and Jharkhand plants.

items.statement: Bulk business margins at bottom (Rs. 2.2/liter); recovery from Q3 with Kharif crop; full recovery to Rs. 10+ in 24 months as maize supply increases
items.quote: I believe that it will take 2 Kharif crops and 2 Rabi crops, so about 24 months from now for there to be sufficient supply of ma ize in the country

items.statement: Rice procurement at Rs. 26-27/kg; maize at Rs. 22-23/kg due to Rabi crop in East India
items.quote: It's in the range of Rs. 26 to Rs. 27 per kilo.

items.statement: Target capacity utilization: 90%+ with maize, 95%+ with rice; current lower throughput due to maize bottlenecks, not yield
items.quote: The target is to go to 90-plus with maize and 95-plus with rice.

items.statement: Rajasthan market share: CL 29%, RML 68%, collective 35.5%; RML share grew from 57% to 68% after government released control
items.quote: Our CL market share in the last quarter has been 29% and the RML market share has been 68%, with a collective market share of 35.5%.

items.statement: Prestige & Above loss peak of Rs. 25 crores tapering; FY25 loss < Rs. 15 crores; FY26 recalibration based on growth opportunities
items.quote: My sense is that this year, it will be less than Rs. 15 crores loss. And I think, next year, we have to recalibrate towards the end of this year, depending on what are the growth opportunities in existing and in new states.

items.statement: FCI policy change stopped rice allocation to distilleries; government not reversing policy; OMC prices revised with MSP changes
items.quote: the government has now created a policy, well, not now, but last year, where the FCI rice surplus stock will not be given to distilleries.

items.statement: Maize cultivation area up ~20% in current Kharif; expecting further growth; 24 months for sufficient maize supply
items.quote: We are seeing in the current year, almost close to 20% increase in area under cultivation for maize.

items.statement: Single malt whisky launch planned; innovations across categories but confidential until launch
items.quote: the next is a single-malt whisky and we have a few others that are indicated on our corporate presentation.

items.statement: Sales team ~100 direct + indirect; gradual increase with penetration, no major change this year as no new states planned
items.quote: Our current strength should be about 100 all direct people and a little more than that indirect people who are helping sell out, that is the current strength, yes.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost Q1 FY25 Rs. 48 crores; savings observed
items.quote: the power and fuel cost for Q1 FY '25 was Rs. 48 crores.

items.statement: Ethanol pricing: rice ethanol Rs. 64/liter, maize ethanol Rs. 72/liter; conversion costs differ but selling price compensates
items.value: Rs. 64. Maize ethanol sells at Rs. 72
items.quote: Rice ethanol sells at Rs. 64. Maize ethanol sells at Rs. 72.

items.statement: Industry-wide maize demand may prolong pricing pressure; working with government and OMCs to ease situation
items.quote: Yes, there are efforts being made with the government, with the oil companies to find ways to ease the situation.

items.statement: FY25 volume growth target 15-18% over FY24 base of ~60 lakh units
items.quote: Last year we made a volume of approximately 60 lakhs. So, this year in the same ratio, in our same, which would be approximately 15 % to 18%, should grow as well.

items.statement: FY25 revenue growth target 15-18% with EBITDA margin 27-28% post-Ind AS
items.quote: Approximately, as just I answered earlier question, 15 %, 16% to 18%. And by this, we are maintaining our gross margin and watching very close, monitoring the gross margin.And then we should be able to back on our EBITDA margin, pre-India, approximately 17%, 18%, which post-India, you can take 27%, 28%.

items.statement: FY25 same-store sales growth target 4-5%
items.quote: So, this year also, out of this 15%, 16% overall growth, 4% to 5%, we can say, would be expecting from the same-store sales growth and balance is coming from the new stores as well as slight increase in the e-commerce shares.

items.statement: FY25 store opening target 70-85 new stores (11 opened in Q1)
items.quote: Approximately 70 to 80 stores we are targeting. First quarter was slightly on the lower side due to properties.So, 11 has already been opened. So, at the end of the year, we should be ending at approximately 70 new stores for the financial year.

items.statement: FY25 store opening target revised to 80-85 stores
items.quote: We plan to open like 80 to 85 stores in the current financial year. And in the first quarter, we have opened at 11 stores. So, rest will be coming in the next coming quarters.

items.statement: FY25 franchisee store additions 20-25; rest company-owned
items.quote: So, it will be again Coco stores will be between 20 to 25 and rest will be the company stores. Okay.

items.statement: Q2 expected marginal growth similar to Q1; major rebound from Q3 festive/wedding season
items.quote: Yes. There will be marginal growth. It will be something like Q1.So, that's why we are saying that a major change will be coming from the Q3 onwards only.

items.statement: Wedding season contributes 20-25% of sales; Q3/Q4 expected strong due to wedding dates
items.quote: So, the three categories, suit, blazers and the waist warts, which are directly related to wedding, contribute 15% of the Cant abil sales. But yes, we cannot ignore the shirts and the trousers for the wedding season sales also. So, in the range of 20% to 25%, we can easily say the wedding season contributes.

items.statement: Larger family stores have lower per sq ft rental (INR122 vs INR128) and better profitability despite lower per sq ft sales
items.quote: Rental per square feet is going down. Like, we have an average rental per square feet of INR128 last to last year. And last year, our average rental per square feet came down to INR122.

items.statement: Ladies wear contribution to rise from 10% to 15% in 2 years; kids wear to double from 2.5%
items.quote: Yes, our contribution from the ladies category was 10%. So, from the 2 years, it will come to 15% and kids category can double up because it's a very small 2.5%. So, kids category contribution can double in next 2 years.

items.statement: Footwear sales target INR10 cr in FY25 (up from INR2.6 cr); now in 90 stores vs 60
items.quote: Footwear stores, last year we did was INR2.6 crores and this year we are targeting the footwear sales of INR10 crores. Till last year, we put footwear into the 60 stores. Now, we have put it into the 90 stores in the company.

items.statement: Active/athleisure category launched last year; non-apparel accessories 5% of business
items.quote: We have been into the active year. In the last year only, we have introduced the active year and the Athleisure category. So, our per square feet sale was INR800 last year and we are targeting 5% increase in the per square feet sales.So, that was for the same stores, I mean.And we know apparel business accessories contribution in the total business is 5%.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 same-store sales growth positive at 1.2%; volume growth 18.5%
items.quote: FY25 has started on a positive note with the company delivering a double-digit volume growth of 18.5%. The company also achieved a positive SS G.

items.statement: E-commerce revenue INR7.13 cr in Q1 FY25 (+10% YoY); Q4 FY24 ~INR9 cr
items.quote: So, this year, out of this total revenue, we have a INR7.13 crores of the slight increase of 10%. Last year, it was approximately 6.5. This year in this quarter it has been done INR7 crores.

items.statement: Target 5% increase in per sq ft sales for same stores (from INR800 base)
items.quote: So, our per square feet sale was INR800 last year and we are targeting 5% increase in the per square feet sales.So, that was for the same stores, I mean.

items.statement: Customer demographic 20-45 years; 50% repeat customers (up from 44% three years ago)
items.quote: Demography is like a bigger range. So, we have a demographic something between 20 to 45 because we are majorly into the basic fashion. S o, all kind of customers come to us.It's young customers also coming to us and the middle-aged customer also coming to us. So, it's a bigger bracket of the age group

items.statement: Repeat customer rate 50% (up from 44% three years ago) showing brand acceptance
items.quote: Earlier, my number was 3 years back was 44% repeat. Then 2 -2% everyone repeat. So, it's a good chance that's a new expansion.I mean new customer is adding as well as new repeat is in. So, that is what the as far as reason is concerned brand for the Cantabil is quite acceptable.

items.statement: Average selling price ~INR1,040 positioning mid-premium between value (INR500-600) and premium (INR1,800)
items.quote: Yes. We feel like our average selling price for a product is around INR1040.So, we are neither in the value format nor in the premium segment. So, we call our asset the mid -premium segment because ASP in the value segment is around INR500-INR600 and the premium segment ASP of the product is around INR1800.

items.statement: Depreciation increase due to Ind AS 116 from 84-85 new company-owned stores opened last year
items.quote: As far as depreciation is concerned, this depreciation is mainly on account of Ind AS 116, because last year we opened more stores, company-owned stores. Earlier we were maintaining approximately 50 to 55 company-owned stores. Now, last year we opened 85 company, 84, in fact , company-owned stores.

items.statement: Board approved Walker Chandiok & Co LLP as statutory auditors
items.quote: With the approval of the board, we appointed, the board has Cantabil Retail India Limited August14, 2024 approved Walker Chandiok & Co LLP as our statutory

items.statement: No near-term South India expansion planned; maybe after 2 years
items.quote: Yes, in the near future, we are not planning to go to the South India. Maybe after 2 years, we plan to go to South India. So, right now, we are planning to expand in the current

items.statement: Same-store sales calculation uses pro-rata basis for stores opened within last 2 years
items.quote: So, same -store sales growth is purely on the pro -data basis. The stores which opened in between the last 2 years, if a store has been opened in last 2 years, June, so it worked for the 9 months. So, this year also we calculate for the 9 months only.

items.statement: EBITDA margin target of 12.5% to be achieved in staggered way within FY25
items.quote: So yes, Deepak, certainly, that is the endeavor in which we all are working. So yes, the number which we mentioned, 12.5%, we should be able to achieve it in a staggered way within this financial years.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 10.9%, up from 9.5% in Q4 FY24
items.quote: So if you see Q -o-Q margin, so last year, in quarter 4, we had an EBITDA of 9.5% for Texmaco Rail stand -alone, whereas if you see our Q1 results, in spite of there is a dip in turnover, the EBITDA has gone up. So in Q4 -- sorry, Q1 this year, we have reported an EBITDA of 11% -- close to 11%.

items.statement: Order book stands at INR7,500 crores with 60% from freight car business, 88% of which from Indian Railways
items.quote: Looking forward, our order book is very healthy, which stands at -- in the range of INR7,500 crores, of which freight car business contributes 60%. Of this 60%, 88% is from the Indian Railways.

items.statement: Jindal Rail acquisition for INR615 crores at 8.1x multiple, expected to close in 3-4 weeks
items.quote: You have also noticed that we have made a significant achievement in the quarter by acquiring 100% of Jindal Rail and Infrastructure Limited for a consideration of INR615 crores and that happened in July 2024. We hope to close the entire transaction by within the next of 3 to 4 weeks' time.

items.statement: Foundries at Belgharia and Raipur produced 9,474 metric tons, near full capacity after debottlenecking
items.quote: Now I must tell you here that we are almost reached to the capacity. We have reached the capacity, we have debottlenecked and that's the best that we could ever happen that's Texmaco Rail & happening in the foundry business.

items.statement: Jindal Rail capacity assessed at 2,200 wagons/year, can be improved 60-70% without capex
items.quote: I mean as per the railway capacity, I think they were in last assessed capacity a couple of years back, which Railway did was around 2,200. And but it is not a limitation to do more. And on a typical month, they have already crossed more than 200 wagons. So I mean, from a specialized in a combination perspective, I think that capacity can be even 60% to 70% improved without any further capex.

items.statement: Texmaco standalone monthly wagon capacity over 1,000 units for commodity types
items.quote: In general, the capacity, which is the commodity type of box and DCM kind of a wagon. So your company will be having a capacity more than 1,000 wagons a month.

items.statement: Company capable of manufacturing double-stack container wagons, supplying in current quarter
items.quote: Your company is already equipped to manufacture those wagons, and in fact, in the coming quarter, we will be supplying few such rigs to one of our customer.

items.statement: Jindal Rail acquisition brings new wagon designs including double-stack capabilities
items.quote: this just didn't come nearly with capacity. It came with good manpower, very strong design capabilities of that company. Some of our learned investors, a little while ago asked about certain double stack. So these are all various new designs, which are available with -- which were available with Jindal, which is now getting passed on to us

items.statement: Railway orders covered by PVC clauses; private orders mostly protected via contract terms
items.quote: So for Texmaco, suppose we have -- I mean, as of now, 60% of our order book is railway and in terms of our turnover. So it's more than 80% -- 85% is our railway contracts. And it is covered under PVC. In private, of course, it depends on customers, I mean the type of product, whatever, but mostly, we try to take care of our interest in terms -- when we take the order in terms of the contracts.

items.statement: Acquired 100% of Jindal Rail for INR615 crores; will become 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail
items.quote: So initially, yes, we will be acquiring 100% stake of Jindal Rail, and it will become a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco Rail. So we have signed the definitive agreement on 25th of July, and we expect the closing to happen within next few weeks' time.

items.statement: Jindal Rail acquisition to remain part of Texmaco Rail post demerger
items.quote: No. So this will be a 100% subsidiary of Texmaco. This will be a part of Mother Texmaco Rail.

items.statement: 51% stake in Saira Asia for passenger mobility components; European designs for Vande Bharat type trains
items.quote: And Saira is actually a European company, which also holds a strong modern designs. And I think it is going to help us a lot in moving towards the field of passenger mobility. We just don't want to jump into it. We are very carefully moving into it so that we don't get into any unwanted risky situation.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 wagon sales 1,967 units, up 48% YoY; revenue INR891.7 crores, up 35.8% YoY
items.quote: During this period, we recorded our revenue from operations, which runs INR891.7 crores, showing a growth of 35.8% compared to Q1 same period last year, which is Q1 financial year 2023 -'24. This growth was primarily driven by upsize in wagon sales to both Indian Railways, private sectors and also the export with our capabilities to produce them in this period of time. We sold 1,967 units, reflect

items.statement: Foundry production 9,474 metric tons, up 4.4% YoY
items.quote: In combination, our foundries produced and let up to the challenge of making 9,474 metric tons of costings for Railways and other components, which shows a growth of 4.4% from last year.

items.statement: Current run rate 750+ wagons/month for Texmaco units; expected to increase in coming quarters
items.quote: To answer you the first part, I mean, we are already on the run rate 750 plus in terms of Texmaco units are concerned. And we feel that will be better off and as per plan, we'll be able to maintain in the next coming quarters, we will increase the number.

items.statement: Order book deliverable up to September 2025, some contracts may extend 1-2 months beyond
items.quote: As of now, whatever we have the contract in terms of rate rolling stock, it spreads over up to September 2025. And a few of those are, of course, may go up to another 1 or 2 months contracts.

items.statement: Rail Infra & Green Energy segment (Kalindee) reported INR10.1 crore EBIT loss due to legacy contracts
items.quote: Yes, you see our rail inf ra and green energy, which is mainly Kalindee Hydromechanical and Bridge. They had reported a loss of INR10.1 crores over EBIT. The main reason of it is that yes, there are a few legacy contracts which are being continued, which management has full focus on how do we close this contract, either close and complete or how can we short -close this contract.

items.statement: Demerger delayed due to bank clearances and legal issues; NCLT process takes 9-12 months after filing
items.quote: In any case, an NCLT process takes about 9 months to 12 months. And we have to go and apply which we haven't done because, as I said, that there are a few internal things which we are trying to sort out. So you can take that kind of a time span. It's very difficult to give a specific one. But normally, that's what it takes, as you know very well.

items.statement: Foundry products have AAR quality acceptance enabling exports to US rail industry
items.quote: As you may recall, our stream foundries are one of the leading foundries in India whose products has achieved quality acceptance by the Association of American Railroads, which is a very rare achievement and that's the reason why we can freely export to -- for use in the American rail industries.

items.statement: Geopolitical factors driving strong demand for foundry exports to US market
items.quote: So we have a great demand from -- because of various geopolitical reasons. And last but not the least, I think you only have mentioned that we want to make our own strategic plans towards moving from freight to customer mobility.

items.statement: Pursuing claims on legacy Kalindee contracts; government payment processes slow
items.quote: I'd like to add Hemant on to your comments by saying that most of these contracts there are a huge amount of potential claims, which we have not yet got paid. So we are also very actively pursuing our efforts, efforts to realize this claim. And as you know that with the government complaints, it takes a long time to redo the change to reclaim and get the money.

items.statement: Strong, energetic team focused on achieving targets and optimizing product mix
items.quote: Only one point that I would like to mention is that I would like all of you to ensure that we have a very strong vibrating, energetic team and which is the team very focused to achieve the target.

items.statement: No plans to sell land parcels; acquired Jindal Rail includes extra land parcel
items.quote: So Mrs. Shah, right now, there is no thought on selling of any of our land, which we have. In fact, in our opening remarks and few of the conversation, you must have heard that we have -- we are in the process of acquiring some of the -- one of the company Jindal Rail, wherein there is some extra parcel of land. So right now, we do not have any thought on selling any of the land parcel.

items.statement: Management refrains from giving 3-5 year financial outlook due to regulatory restrictions
items.quote: Absolutely, so commenting on any forward-looking statement we would like to refrain. Sorry, so we wouldn't like to duck on this question, please. And I fully understand and we appreciate. I would -- we hope that you also appreciate that, yes, we are on our investor call, and we are barred to give a forward-looking statement over here.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance revised to flat to minus 10% due to elections, heat, monsoon and land acquisition delays
items.quote: Given the con ditions -- and some of them are expected things. So the guidance for the FY '25 would not be what we expected earlier would be may be at flat or maybe around 10% downwards

items.statement: FY25 standalone EBITDA margin guidance maintained at around 12.5%
items.quote: Yes. Yes. EBITDA margins would be around 12.5%.

items.statement: FY26 revenue growth guidance of around 15% with potential upside to 20%
items.quote: FY '26 guidance would be around 15%. See, we expect 15% because the projects which we are expecting -- we are expecting quite a few projects appointed date during the current financial year even during the second quarter.

items.statement: Unexecuted order book Rs 14,100 cr as of June 2024; including 2 new EPC contracts total Rs 19,098 cr (2.5x FY24 revenue)
items.quote: As of 30th June 2024, the company's unexecuted order book stands at Rs. 14,100 crores which does not include the contract value of 2 EPC contracts recently secured for an aggregate value of Rs. 4,994 Crores. Upon inclusion of these 2 EPC projects, our unexecuted order book would be over Rs. 19,098 Crores which is 2.5 times of FY 24 Revenue.

items.statement: FY25 order inflow guidance Rs 13,000-15,000 cr (Rs 5,000 cr already secured, expect Rs 8,000-10,000 cr more)
items.quote: We already secured INR5,000 crores worth of new orders during the current financial year, and we expect to secure another INR8,000 crores to INR10,000 crores. So it will be around -- between INR13,000 crores to INR15,000 crores new orders during the FY '25.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 standalone EBITDA margin 34% includes Rs 435 cr arbitration/bonus; core margin ~12.5%
items.quote: So, the 34% is inclusive of INR435 crores amount received on account of arbitration and bonus in this quarter. Otherwise, the EBITDA margin will be maintained around 12.5%.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance Rs 80-100 cr (vs Rs 46 cr FY24); Q1 capex Rs 3 cr
items.quote: Capex last year was INR46 crores. But this year, we are expecting around INR80 crores to INR100 crores.

items.statement: Three HAM projects (Western Bhopal Bypass, Varanasi-Kolkata Pkg 6, Gwalior Bridge) expected appointed dates first week of October; revenue from Q3
items.quote: appointed dates for all these three projects we expect in the first week of October as the land is expected to be possessed before end of September, the required land, more than 80%. So, these three projects, we expect appointed dates in the first week of October. And the revenue, maybe initial revenues would be booked during the Q3 of the current financial year.

items.statement: NHAI floated tenders for 100+ projects worth >Rs 1,00,023 cr (30 EPC, 70+ HAM); 10 BOT-toll projects also available
items.quote: NHAI has floated tenders and NIT for more than 100 projects. Around 30 projects on EPC and more than 70 projects on a HAM basis. The total value of these projects will be more than INR1,00,023 crores.

items.statement: Net working capital cycle 121 days as of June 2024; target ~100 days by year-end as debtors realize
items.quote: Working capital days should be around 100 days, because at this time, it has increased from 102 to 121 because of the increase in the debtors.

items.statement: Standalone net debt/equity 0.07x (net worth Rs 5,203 cr, debt Rs 389 cr, cash Rs 486 cr); Consolidated net debt/equity 1.43x (net worth Rs 5,761 cr, debt Rs 8,258 cr, cash Rs 1,501 cr)
items.quote: Our net worth on standalone basis is Rs. 5,203 crores as on 30th June 2024, whereas total standalone debt is Rs. 389 crore. The total cash and bank balance as on 30th June 2024 is Rs. 486 crores. We have a net surplus of Rs. 97 crore. This translates to net debt to equity of 0.07 times. On Consolidated Basis, our net worth is Rs. 5,761 crores whereas total debt is Rs. 8258 crores as on 30 th June

items.statement: HAM equity requirement Rs 3,092 cr total; Rs 2,079 cr invested by June 2024; balance Rs 1,013 cr over 2-3 years (FY25 Rs 587 cr, FY26 Rs 290 cr, FY27 Rs 140 cr) from internal accruals
items.quote: Actually, out of the INR3,092 crores equity required for completing the projects, we have already infused INR2,079 crores till June 2024. And remaining INR1,013 crores is required in FY '25, around INR587 crores; FY '26 is INR290 crores; and FY '27 is INR140 crores.

items.statement: Asset monetization Phase 1 (6 HAM + 1 BOT, value ~Rs 1,789 cr) CPs by Dec 2024, payment by Mar 2025; Phase 2 by Sep 2025
items.quote: CPs of Phase-l is expected by Dec 24 & payment by end of March 25 and Phase-II by Sep 25 in case we receive the NOC from NHAI

items.statement: Snowman warehousing business expects 12-15% growth in FY25 with new facilities in Lucknow and Kolkata
items.quote: Considering the new facilities which are going to be functional in next month, Lucknow and after that Kolkata, and also some of the lease capacities which we are yet to fully utilize, considering all these, we expect around 12% to 15% growth in warehousing business this year.

items.statement: Snowman warehousing realization up 2.5% YoY; expects another 1% increase next quarter
items.quote: Also, warehousing realization has gone up by 2.5% as compared to last year and we expect it to go by another 1% in the next quarter because some of the price corrections have happened now, which will start yielding in the coming quarter.

items.statement: New 5PL client from ice cream/dairy industry signed; expected to contribute Rs 15-18 crores/quarter from Q2
items.quote: It is from ice cream and dairy industry, and this is expected to contribute anywhere between 15 to 18 crores a quarter.

items.statement: Rail busy season surcharge of 10% passed on to customers; hope for revision to improve competitiveness vs road
items.quote: So, little bit, road does have an advantage with the 10% busy season surcharge that came in. Although we passed it on, we had no choice but to pass i t on to our customers and that's been fully implemented now. But maybe hopefully this can be revised in the near future and then can get a better pricing to make it more competitive

items.statement: DFC Western corridor 93% complete; last 100 km to Vaitarna will take time; commissioning guidance December 2025
items.quote: DFC is giving us guidance for December 2025. And again, the status is the same that 93% of the total WDFC has completed up to Vaitarna and the last leg of 100 kilometers is still going to take a lot of time.

items.statement: EXIM imbalance persists at port level (Mundra imports down, Pipavav imports up) affecting double stacking despite overall 52:48 import:export ratio
items.quote: Yes, but then if you look at within the ports what used to be there like Mundra imports have gone down, Pipavav imports have gone up, so within that there is imbalance. So, for a train running perspective, it is still an imbalance in certain markets.

items.statement: CFS business faces intense competition with no players exiting; management wants to exit but not in a hurry
items.quote: we would definitely want to get out of the CFS business because even though the margins have increased in the first quarter compared to last q uarter of the year, but at the same time, we don't see any uptick on the CFS business because the competition is so intense and there is hardly anyone who has moved out of this business

items.statement: Accounting policy change: consolidator discounts now netted from revenue (Rs 8.43 cr impact); no impact on EBITDA per TEU
items.quote: This is basically a business model done with consolidators, but it was discount being passed on was actually earlier being counted in the revenue. But as per the accounting standard now, that comes under gross revenue, but under net revenue we have to remove this discount. So, it was like a pass-through almost. So, it's gone away from this quarter on.

items.statement: Fair value disclosure will be included in the Annual Report as statutorily required
items.quote: Yes, the fair value disclosure will be in our Annual Report, as it is statutorily required to be.

items.statement: Consistent interest seen for relicensing Morgan Stanley space at NKP
items.quote: The Company has seen consistent interest for relicensing the space currently occupied by Morgan Stanley.

items.statement: EBITDA margins approximately 77% for Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margins are approximately 77%.

items.statement: Morgan Stanley to vacate 13,000 sq ft in Q3 FY25 and 122,000 sq ft in Q4 FY25 at NKP
items.quote: Morgan Stanley has given notices at the end of July and in August 2024 to vacate approximately 13,000 square feet in Q3 FY 25, and approximately 122,000 square feet in Quarter 4 FY 25, at NKP, respectively.

items.statement: Current licensing rates just north of Rs. 160 per sq ft per month on 80% efficiency basis with roughly three months rent free
items.value: Rs. 160 per sq ft per month
items.quote: They are just north of approximately Rs. 160 per square foot per month on an 80% efficiency basis, with roughly three months of rent free.

items.statement: Carpet area equivalent rate is Rs. 200 plus CAM plus GST
items.quote: No, that's our chargeable area. The carpet area equivalent is Rs. 200.

items.statement: Current interest rate is 8.54% based on monthly T-bill
items.quote: Current rate is 8.54%.

items.statement: Tax rate applicable from FY25 is 34.94% vs 29.12% earlier due to turnover exceeding Rs. 400 crores in FY23
items.quote: the tax rate applicable from the current year, that is FY 2024-25 will be 34.94% as against 29.12% earlier under the old regime, as the Company's turnover has exceeded Rs. 400 crores in FY 2022-23

items.statement: Discussions and consultations on potential restructuring or value accretive measures continue with concerned parties
items.quote: With reference to the potential restructuring or other possible value accretive measures, discussions and consultations with concerned parties continues.

items.statement: Average occupancy rate stable at 99.8% for Q1 FY25 with NKP at 100% occupancy
items.quote: the average occupancy rate for the Company as a whole, that is Nirlon Knowledge Park and Nirlon House combined was stable at 99.8% for the 1st Quarter, and NKP remained 100% occupied.

items.statement: Nirlon House sale process ongoing with regulatory bodies due to strata ownership structure
items.quote: That is under discussion with various regulatory bodies etc., because of the profile of the ownership and the nature of the ownership, which is basically strata, as well as the ownership within Nirlon.

items.statement: Domestic tire volume expected to grow mid-single digits in FY25; replacement market healthy due to infrastructure investment
items.quote: The domestic tire volume is expected to have a moderate growth of around the mid -single digits in FY'25. The replacement market, which contributes significantly to the tire industry volumes is also anticipated to remain healthy.

items.statement: Selling prices maintained despite aggressive dumping from China; raw material costs expected to give relief in second half of quarter
items.quote: We maintained our pricing. We did not yield to the pressure on pricing. There were some small aberrations in the input cost.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined to 11% in Q1FY25 from 12.5% in Q4FY24 due to front-loaded employee costs and market conditions; expected to improve with capacity utilization ramp-up
items.quote: EBITDA margins for Q1FY'25 stood at 11% as compared to 12.5% in Q4 FY '24. There is one item called employee expenses, this have increased sequentially largely due to the annual revision in salary along with retiral provisions.

items.statement: Dahej capacity expansion at 10-15% completion; Board approved in March; adding 20% to existing capacity; product split not disclosed
items.quote: So we got the approval from the Board in March and I think if I want to put a percentage, probably 10% to 15%.

items.statement: Current utilization ~70% overall; peak utilization expected in 1-1.5 years; expansion targets products at 90-95% utilization
items.quote: About 70% utilization. Peak utilization is not putting a finger, Aditya, on a specific quarter or a month. But we're quite positive this will keep getting ramped up from quarter-to-quarter.

items.statement: Export volume mix 34% in Q1FY25 (up from 32%); revenue mix 34%; growth from Asia, Europe, and US despite container shortages and freight costs
items.quote: So the export is around 34%. I think if I recall, earlier it was 32%, it's about 34% now. And from a market development point, this growth is coming not only from Asia, but also from Europe also to a certain extent.

items.statement: Green energy (solar, wind, cogeneration) at 60-70% of Dahej power; expected to reach 75%+ at full utilization; turbine commissioned, savings from Q2
items.quote: So if you put both together, we should be in the range of 60% to 70% in Dahej, and this should go up with full utilization. As utilization ramps up, I would expect this to go to at least 75 and more.

items.statement: Value-added portfolio expansion underway; results in medium term; localized an imported accelerator product; more products in pipeline
items.quote: We are building up alternative plans to improve our value-added portfolio. We are working on our growth plans on that also. That's what is going on. The results will not be seen immediately, but in the medium term, you can see those results being getting reflected in the operational performance.

items.statement: Antidumping duty study ongoing; no concrete decision yet; will explore if valid case emerges
items.quote: Study is going on. At this moment, we are evaluating various options. And at an appropriate time if we feel there is a m erit -- there's a valid case in this as per the merits, we may explore that option

items.statement: Manufacturing cost comparable to China Sunsine; their pricing advantage from export subsidies; NOCIL has supply reliability and faster turnaround edge
items.quote: So what we have seen is we're quite comparable as far as our -- if you do a comparison with China Sunsine across the product category, it is largely the delta on the export subsidy that tends to kind of give them that additional pricing power.

items.statement: Sales volume index at 144 (base Q1FY20=100); 4% QoQ volume growth; 8% YoY volume growth
items.quote: On the sales volume front, the volumes for Q1FY '25 is at 144 taking a base of Q1FY '20 as 100.

items.statement: Employee cost front-loading: 65% in Q1, remaining 35% spread over Q2-Q4; actuarial valuation for retiral provisions drives pattern
items.quote: So if you see last year, and the last two years, if you see, 65% gets loaded in the first quarter, then you have 30% or 32% gets distributed over the next three quarters.

items.statement: Chinese domestic demand stable, not improving; European market slight improvement but not significant; geopolitical and container challenges persist
items.quote: Yes, so the Chinese market is kind of -- we don't see any significant improvement kind of like more or less stable is what we see. European market, there has been a slight improvement, but clearly not something significant that to, but there is a slight improvement.

items.statement: Green chemicals pipeline in testing/approval stages; related to rubber applications; lower energy-intensive products
items.quote: Yes. So there are quite a few greener, more lower energy -intensive products that we are continuously working on, there are quite a few in the pipeline, but they take their time and they are in different stages of testing and approvals.

items.statement: Management expects minor sales volume growth for FY25 despite Q1 strength
items.quote: Despite the strong performance in Q1, we are witnessing macro challenges accentuated by recessionary fears in USA, Geopolitical sanctions and inflationary raw material scenario coupled with high freight costs are there. This will result in a tepid demand environment for the remainder of the year. However, we believe we will be able to achieve a minor sales volume growth in this financial year.

items.statement: Demand slowing down in Q1; tepid environment expected for remainder of FY25
items.quote: Yes, we are seeing demand slowing down and that's why we are saying that despite this quarter, by the remainder of the year, we will only be able to get a minor growth.

items.statement: Board approved new capex of up to INR1,300 crores for 35,000 MTPA OTR capacity at Bhuj in phases
items.quote: Accordingly, we are embarking on a new capex spend of up to INR1,300 crores for 35,000 metric ton per annum at Bhuj. This will be executed in various phases.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance of INR600-700 crores; Q1 spend was INR200 crores
items.quote: Full year would be between INR600 crores to INR700 crores.

items.statement: Advanced carbon black project of 30,000 MTPA progressing on schedule for H1 FY25 commissioning
items.quote: We are working on advanced carbon black project with a capacity of 30,000 metric tons. This project is progressing well and is as per schedule.

items.statement: New mould manufacturing plant at Bhuj commenced operations for internal consumption
items.quote: Further, we have commenced the operations of our new mould manufacturing plant at Bhuj. Please note this plant will provide us mould for our internal consumption and help better our quality levels.

items.statement: Channel inventory increasing due to Q1 stocking; OEM demand softer
items.quote: It is increasing. Channel inventory is increasing, and OEMs demand is softer also.

items.statement: Targeting full-year EBITDA margin around 24.8% despite cost pressures
items.quote: Last year, full year, our EBITDA margin was around 24.8%, and we will be striving for the same range for the whole of the year.

items.statement: Raw material costs expected to increase 2-3%; freight costs to rise to 8-9% of revenue in Q2
items.quote: Commodity prices are also going up. So raw material, approximately 2% to 3%, will increase the raw material cost.

items.statement: No price hikes taken yet; weak demand limiting pass-through ability
items.quote: No, till now, we have not been able to take any price hike. Going forward, the market demand is a little weak. Hence, we are trying to see what we can do and what we can pass on. But so far, we have not taken anything.

items.statement: Q1 EUR/INR rate 92; Q2 hedge rate around 92.5
items.quote: So this quarter was INR92 euro and next hedging is around 92.5 we can say for next quarter.

items.statement: Forex gain of INR52 crores on sales; INR11 crores on expenses in Q1
items.quote: On sales it is INR52 crores, which is we have disclosed in our presentation. On other expenses, it is about INR11 crores.

items.statement: India market share in agri estimated at 6-7%; outlook remains positive
items.quote: Very difficult to give you an exact number, but between 6% to 7%.

items.statement: Expect to maintain market share despite demand slowdown
items.quote: No, we will be maintaining.

items.statement: Gross debt INR2,771 crores; cash INR2,946 crores; net cash ~INR175 crores as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: Our gross debt stood at INR2,771 crores at the end of 30th June '24. Our cash and cash equivalents were INR2,946 crores. Accordingly, we have a net cash of approximately INR175 crores.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR4 per equity share declared
items.quote: The Board of Directors has declared an interim dividend of INR4 per equity share.

items.statement: Natural rubber sourced from Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia, Africa, Vietnam based on best deal
items.quote: Yes. From all Thailand, Indonesia, Malaysia as well as African countries, Vietnam. So wherever we get the best deal, we buy from there.

items.statement: Macro challenges: US recession fears, geopolitical sanctions, inflationary raw materials, high freight costs
items.quote: Despite the strong performance in Q1, we are witnessing macro challenges accentuated by recessionary fears in USA, Geopolitical sanctions and inflationary raw material scenario coupled with high freight costs are there.

items.statement: Joined Global Platform for Sustainable Natural Rubber (GPSNR) for EUDR compliance and sustainability reporting
items.quote: Further, in order to promote sustainable practices beyond our manufacturing units, BKT recently announced its membership to the Global Platform for Sustainable Natural Rubber or the GPSNR.

items.statement: Guided mid-double-digit volume growth for FY25 and revenue growth ~300 bps above volume growth
items.quote: Yes. Like we mentioned, mid-double-digit growth is what we are looking at. That is the guidance that we are providing.

items.statement: Expect to become net debt free during FY25, sooner than earlier March 2025 target
items.quote: We are on track. In fact, our earlier commentary suggests that we would have been net debt free by March 2025. But I do expect given the current trajectory, it would be even sooner than that.

items.statement: Adjusted EBITDA margin base of 14.5% in Q1 FY25, expected to expand further with volume growth and policy benefits
items.quote: Yes. You should consider the new base, if you ask me, is 14.5%. Right. Adjusted for the subsidy, you're looking at an EBITDA margin of 14.5%. That will be your base.

items.statement: Flandy contribution margins stronger than company weighted average, will drive margin expansion as it grows
items.quote: Given the fact that it is on the premium end of the portfolio of the spectrum, our contribution margins are actually better in Flandy as compared to the weighted average for the company as a whole.

items.statement: Q1 volume growth 0.9% YoY impacted by election disruptions; Southern IMFL industry de-grew 0.1% YoY
items.quote: While volume growth was 0.9% YoY, our EBITDA growth stood at 30.8% YoY. This significant growth in EBITDA has been on account of cost optimization initiatives and increasing share of premium products in the portfolio.

items.statement: Seeing good demand in Q2 post elections; confident of resuming industry-beating growth
items.quote: We are seeing good demand in Q2 and the guidance which we have given for the volume growth which will be in the double-digit volume growth that we are very confident we will be able to achieve.

items.statement: ENA costs reduced ~Rs 2/litre in Q1; glass and packing material costs softened; maintained gross margins QoQ despite NSR reduction
items.quote: Despite the highly volatile and inflationary trends in ENA, we have done a great job in our procurement efforts and have seen ENA costs come down by almost Rs. 2 per litre in Q1.

items.statement: Premium share increasing; 85%+ volumes from Prestige & Above segment; Flandy achieved 20% share of Flandy volumes in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh
items.quote: 85% plus of our volumes are actually driven by P&A. From that perspective, it was kind of a similar range in terms of growth for both.

items.statement: Green Apple Flandy launch successful; luxury product launch planned in next couple of months; non-brandy premium pipeline for Pan-India expansion
items.quote: Very soon you should be seeing a luxury product coming out of our stables, over the next couple of months itself.

items.statement: Flandy attracting non-brandy drinkers and women; trials from flavoured spirits consumers; 10% of Mansion House volumes in first year
items.quote: We have approximately 10% of the sales coming of Mansion House Brandy, which is the mother brand, which in the first year of launch, is fairly respectable.

items.statement: Free cash flow from net debt free status to be deployed in strategic initiatives including new products and categories
items.quote: What that will effectively do is that, the company will be generating a significant amount of cash, almost the EBITDA will largely translate into a free cash flow, which then we can prudently deploy into various strategic initiatives.

items.statement: Gross debt reduced Rs 22.3 crore; net debt Rs 42.6 crore; prepaid Rs 20 crore Kotak term loan in Q1
items.quote: On the debt front, we reduced our gross debt by Rs. 22.3 crore and have now brought down our net debt to Rs. 42.6 crore. Furthermore, due to strong cash flows, we prepaid Rs. 20 crore of Kotak term loan in the quarter.

items.statement: Marketing spend cut in Q1 due to election disruption expectations; A&SP spend to increase to 2.5-3% of sales over 2-3 years
items.quote: Our range let's say of 2-3 year perspective would be more in the range of 2.5%-3% of sales.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh excise policy expected effective Oct 1; Telangana policy also awaited; both expected progressive based on CM's prior regime
items.quote: What we have understood from reports is that in Andhra Pradesh, they expect to announce the excise policy to be effective from October 1.

items.statement: Q1 FY25: Revenue growth 3% YoY, NSR Rs 1,252/case, EBITDA Rs 50 crore (highest ever Q1), PAT Rs 40.1 crore, PAT margin 12.7%
items.quote: During the first quarter, we have recorded a revenue growth of 3% YoY, predominantly on account of disruptions due to elections. The NSR per case came in at Rs. 1,252 per case during Q1 2025 relative to Rs. 1,249 in the corresponding period of last year.

items.statement: Rs 200 crore tax credit available at start of FY25; no tax payment expected in FY25; tax incidence from Q1 FY26
items.quote: We had around Rs. 200 crore of tax credit available as at the beginning of the year. We are hopeful that this year we will not need to pay any tax and our tax incidence will start from next year.

items.statement: Flandy competes with flavoured vodka category; priced alongside flavoured vodka; flavoured spirits industry growing overall
items.quote: Usually we are priced along with the flavoured vodka. When we look at our market share or tactical analysis which we do, we look at flavoured vodka category as well.

items.statement: Policy announcements in two key southern states pending; volume growth dependent on favourable excise policies
items.quote: Of course, we are waiting for certain policy decisions as I mentioned in two of the southern states. Once they come, that will also set the direction since they are both important markets for us.

items.statement: Board approved Rs 100 crore buyback of up to 50 lakh shares at Rs 200 per share, record date Aug 13, 2024
items.quote: The Board of Directors have approved a share buyback of Rs.100 crores. This buyback will involve repurchasing up to 50 lakh shares at a price of Rs.200 per share, representing approximately 2.2% of the total paid up equity capital of the company.

items.statement: Export stationery expected to grow double digits on previous year reported numbers
items.quote: No, no, double digit is very sure of, for us, to grow in this year.

items.statement: Domestic stationery internal guidance of 14-15% growth for full financial year
items.quote: So from our internal guidance point of view, we should be growing to around 14% to 15% in the whole financial year.

items.statement: Publication business maximum 5% growth for full year due to no curriculum change and product redesigning
items.quote: Yes, maximum because of no curriculum change and this redesigning of products, maximum we'll be able to see 5%.

items.statement: Stationery EBITDA margin improvement of at least 100 basis points; publishing margins to remain same
items.quote: So having restated earlier years number also, so if you combine both business earlier though, it was a separate activity, and we were merging. So, the number that used to come after merging, the margin will improve a little bit. But because the sales growth is limited, we believe that the inflationary cost pressures would be there. And therefore, the net margin, if you combine both businesses toge

items.statement: Publication volume grew ~2% but realization fell due to curriculum reduction and product redesign
items.quote: So again, in volume wise, we have grown by around hardly, it is a marginal growth of 2% in terms of volume, but realization -wise, it reduced.

items.statement: Domestic stationery volume grew ~4% but realization fell due to raw material price reduction passed to customers
items.quote: In reality, volume-wise, it has increased, but it is so dynamic that because of the raw material prices went down and to be with the market, we had to reduce our price of the products. So realization reduced. So in reality, volume -wise, we have grown by around 4% in first quarter.

items.statement: Paper prices corrected 12-13% from Sep 2023 to Jan 2024, forcing product price reductions
items.quote: So whatever inventory that was manufactured, there the price of paper corrected by almost 12% to 1 3%, and that we had to reduce the final product price to remain in line with the competition.

items.statement: Paper prices stable recently; attempted increase last month failed due to no takers
items.quote: No, no. They did try to increase last month, but there were no takers, so they had to again fall back to the same price.

items.statement: CBSE textbook market opportunity Rs 4,000 crore today, expected to grow to Rs 8,000-9,000 crore in 5-6 years
items.quote: So all put together opportunity for CBSE textbook business only, which is INRs.4,000-odd crores today is likely to grow to Rs.8,000 crores to Rs.9,000 crores in 5 to 6 years.

items.statement: Navneet reaches ~10,000 of 26,000-46,000 CBSE schools; fully penetrated in 38,000-40,000 private schools in Gujarat and Maharashtra
items.quote: Altogether out of 26,000 and 46,000 schools, which are using the CBSE publications, we would be reaching hardly to 10,000-odd.

items.statement: Publication revenue Rs 417 crore: Rs 384 crore supplementary, Rs 26 crore textbooks, Rs 7 crore non-curriculum
items.quote: So as far as out of Rs.417 crores, the non-curriculum is just Rs.7 crores, the balance is all curriculum. And within curriculum, supplementary book products is, to be precise, Rs.384 crores and the non-textbook business is Rs.26 crores.

items.statement: Curriculum change for grades 1-2 in Maharashtra and Gujarat expected next academic year, continuing for 4 years
items.quote: Curriculum, both in Maharashtra and Gujarat, part of the curriculum will start changing for a few of the periods and that will then continue for 4 years.

items.statement: Internal discussion ongoing on merging Indiannica subsidiary into parent; no clear timeline yet
items.quote: Yes, that discussion is on internally, but I do not have clear date or time line to mention that.

items.statement: Sales return provisions: Rs 30 crore publication, Rs 3 crore each for exports and domestic stationery in Q1
items.quote: So we have provided around Rs.30 crores in publication business and around Rs.3 crores each in exports and domestic business -- domestic stationary business.

items.statement: Last year Q1 publication sales return provision Rs 32 crore, actual returns Rs 37 crore received in Q2
items.quote: So provision for Q1 was around Rs.32 crores, and we got the return of around Rs.37 crores.

items.statement: Marketing team of 400+ people across India for school canvassing; segregated teams for SSC vs CBSE/ICSE schools
items.quote: So we have a huge fleet of people, more than 400 across India, including Maharashtra, Gujarat, they visit schools on a day-to-day basis and see to it that our books gets recommended.

items.statement: Navneet CBSE textbook business profitable at Rs 26 crore quarterly due to shared sales force; Indiannica still loss-making at Rs 50-65 crore sales
items.quote: At Navneet, with this Rs.26 crores, then yearly maybe Rs.40-odd crores, it will be profitable, reason beingmost of our present team only is selling these products, so the biggest expenditure in CBSE business has been the sales team, which goes all India. That is not there at Navneet.

items.statement: Curriculum change dependent on government action; risk of delay if new government cancels prepared changes
items.quote: Of course, I can't guarantee, but the preparation at the education department has started. Now suddenly, the new government comes and says, we don't want to replace even though curriculum is ready, then it's not in our hands.

items.statement: SFA edtech investment making losses but building strong foundation; confident of future returns despite possible revaluation
items.quote: we are not really worried for next 1 or 2 years for them to make losses, but they are making their foundation very, very strong. So be cause of the accounting policies and standards, we may had to revalue the assets for some of the other reasons. But I'm personally very, very hopeful -- confident of that business giving us really good returns in the future

items.statement: Export stationery revenue Rs 241 crore vs Rs 214 crore YoY; regained business lost to anti-dumping duties by moving production
items.quote: So as you might have seen, the Q1 '25 revenue is Rs.241 crores compared to Rs.214 crores corresponding period. This performance reflects our strategic efforts to broaden our product portfolio and extend our market reach.

items.statement: No major technology investment in blockchain, metaverse or 3D/4D animation; digital investment as per customer need only
items.quote: New -age, of course, we are adding more and more features in the product by using different, different newer technologies, but that's really not a big investment and particularly the blockchain or 3D or 4D animations, all that is really not required in this.

items.statement: CBSE textbook market dominated by 7-9 large publishers in North India; Navneet has blended print-digital advantage
items.quote: Finally, we have seen that around 7 to 8 publishers only have been doing quite big, good revenue because of the consistent content quality and, therefore, we'll have to fight with these 8, 9 publishers who are quite big enough.

items.statement: FY25 revenue guidance of INR7,000-8,000 crores with 2.5% EBITDA margin; FY26 target INR13,000-14,000 crores; FY27 target INR18,000-20,000 crores
items.quote: So, if you look at FY25, we are looking at around INR7000 to INR8,000 crores of revenue, right, which will translate into like 1.3 million ton of steel business put together. And margin should be around 2.5%.

items.statement: FY27 revenue target INR18,000-20,000 crores split equally across three business segments at INR6,000 crores each
items.quote: If you look at the split also of INR18,000 crores revenue guidance, which we have given for FY27, it's also like we have divided it equally, like INR60-INR60 billion.

items.statement: Service center capex of INR20-25 crores per unit plus INR10-15 crores working capital; total INR2,500 crores gross block for 100 centers by 2030
items.quote: If I do 100 in next seven years, so INR2,500 crores will be the total gross block which we will be spending.

items.statement: Two service centers operational; three more starting in next 2-3 months (two in India, one in Dubai); 15 new locations over next 12 months; target 101 service centers by 2030
items.quote: Two new service centers in India will be starting in next two to three months. The construction work is underway and we will be starting those service centers in the next two to three months. And fifth service center we are starting in Dubai.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 revenue INR1,150 crores: metal trading INR500-600 crores, service centers INR400 crores, B2C distribution INR200 crores
items.quote: Right. So, if I have to break up my INR1,200 crores revenue, which I did in Q1, 1,150 crores, right, I would say that out of this, INR500, INR600 crores will be metal trading, INR400 crores will be service center business and the rest 200 crores worth will be the distribution business.

items.statement: Metal trading margins 1.5-2% with zero to 10 days working capital; service centers 4-5% EBITDA margin with 15-25 days inventory; B2C distribution blended 2.5-3% margin with 15-20 days inventory
items.quote: Here the margins are between 1.5-2% based on what kind of [inaudible 10:08] we source. And the working capital which is required here is around zero to 10 days.

items.statement: India steel capacity to increase 50% from Dec 2023 to Dec 2025; target 300 million tons by 2030 creates need for large-scale traders
items.quote: But if you see from December 2023 till December 2025, India's steel capacity is going to go up by 50%.

items.statement: Metal trading zero to 10 days net working capital; service centers 15-25 days inventory; B2C distribution 15-20 days; blended average 20 days working capital at scale
items.quote: The net working capital here will be zero to 10 days here. Average you can take five days with a margin of 1.5-2%.

items.statement: Business equity funded; no debt currently; may need INR1,000-300 crores short-term bank limits at INR50,000 crores revenue scale
items.quote: Now, everything is equity funded. When I will be doing INR50,000 crores of revenue, then I may need INR1,000 crores, INR300 crores of short-term bank limits.

items.statement: Raised INR1,300 crores via listed shell: INR350 crores from promoters, INR900 crores from investors; no further equity needed for INR50,000 crores revenue target
items.quote: When we raised INR350 crores from the promoters and INR900 crores from the investors, so with INR1,300 crores money in the kitty, then I went to the steel traders and steel manufacturers.

items.statement: Metal trading: JSW Steel, NMDC Steel, Jindal Steel and Power, Steel Authority; service centers targeting OEMs like Havells; B2C leveraging APL Apollo's 800 distributors
items.quote: So today we are doing business with JSW Steel, NMDC Steel, Jindal Steel and Power, Steel Authority as well, and some imports which we are doing in SG Mart.

items.statement: Industry grew 13.33% in Q1 FY25; GDP Rs 72,758 crore
