items.statement: GWP Rs 11,788 crore in Q1 FY25; net earned premium Rs 8,503 crore, up 7.37% YoY
items.quote: The company's GWP for the quarter ended 30th June 24 was Rs. 11,788 crores. Our net earned premium for the quarter ended 30th June 2024 was rupees Rs. 8503 crores, registering a growth of 7.37% year on year.

items.statement: Market share 14.67% as of June 30, 2024; remain market leader
items.quote: Our market share stands at 14.67% as on 30th June 2024 and we continue to be market leader despite the highly competitive environment.

items.statement: Retail health price increase ~25% rolled out last year; further zoning and regulatory hikes this year
items.quote: So, coming to specifics in retail health, there has been a price increase of close to 25 odd percent, which we rolled out last year and this year also because of some zoning related changes, there has been price increase in some zones which has been rolled out.

items.statement: Motor TP no price increase in last 3 years; motor OD price increases rolled out, especially commercial vehicles
items.quote: Coming to motor because there has been no price increase on the motor third party front, we have rolled out some price increases on the motor own damage front in order to cushion the impact so that has been done and that has been done across segments, particularly on the commercial vehicle side.

items.statement: Group health pricing on case-to-case basis; walking away where price not viable
items.quote: On group health, pricing is done on a case-to-case basis depending on how the behavior of the group works and as Mrs. Sushma mentioned earlier, the pricing has been made much more prudent and wherever the price we want is not available, we are happy to walk away.

items.statement: Must comply with master circular changes by 30 Sep 2024; pricing adjustments in ~15% of premium
items.quote: And then now after the master circular, which has come in, there are some 5-6 changes which are introduced and mandated by the regulator for which we have to be compliant by 30th of September'24 to take care of that in some of our products which we had not touched the pricing for maybe over five years or so and which products are actually not very, I would put it this way that they form part of al

items.statement: Focus on retail segment, under-penetrated areas: rural, livestock, tier 2/3 cities, microinsurance, MSME, women, millennials, Gen Z
items.quote: As per our benchmarks by under penetrated areas, we consider potential in the rural sector, livestock insurance tier two and three cities, microinsurance products for low-income groups, MSME sector, women centric products, targeting millennials and the Gen Z.

items.statement: Product mix: Fire 16%, Marine 2%, Motor 22%, Health & PA 50%, Others 10%
items.quote: Our product mix for Fire is at 16%, Marine is 2%, Motor 22%, Health & PA 50% and others at 10%.

items.statement: Launched surety bonds (bid and performance bonds) to support infrastructure
items.quote: The company has a well-diversified portfolio of products, including the recent launches of surety bonds. In fact, New India is one of the few insurers issuing both bid bonds as well as performance bonds, which will support infrastructure growth in the country.

items.statement: Investing heavily in systems, processes, skill development; inducted risk engineers, automobile engineers, doctors
items.quote: We are improvising heavily on our systems and processes. We are investing a lot into skill set development of our employees in order to be able to address issues, you know quickly bring around faster turnaround times in terms of claim service.

items.statement: Premium split 90% domestic, 10% foreign; international operations in 25 developed countries, self-sustaining
items.quote: Yeah. So, our overall premium consists of 10% foreign and 90% domestic.

items.statement: Solvency ratio 1.83x, comfortably above 1.50x threshold
items.quote: The solvency ratio remains comfortably above the threshold of 1.50 times and we are currently at 1.83 times.

items.statement: Investment income weaker YoY due to less equity sold and lower dividend received in Q1
items.quote: Actually, in the first quarter or that profit on sale, we have not sold much equity. Due to that dividend, we received in the first quarter. In the after first quarter also. So we sold less equity after the first quarter and our due to that we realized less profit on sales of equity.

items.statement: Government health scheme loss ratios seasonal; expected to stabilize by year-end
items.quote: Actually, the policy which is there is for a year and in usually in all such policies as the awareness increases and as we encounter different seasons, the claims do change in the numbers and the exposure that is there changes in the time of the year that we talk about; so, usually all such policies they stabilize by end of the year.

items.statement: Medical inflation remains high post-COVID; modern treatments adding cost pressure
items.quote: But at the same time, another challenge or a problem that we encounter all along is the high medical inflation. So, initially it was felt that after COVID the medical inflation would come down, but it has sadly not come down and then to add to it, we also have lot of modern treatments coming up, which are actually quite costly.

items.statement: Recruited large number of doctors; inducted risk engineers, automobile engineers for better risk selection
items.quote: We have inducted a lot of risk engineers, automobile engineers, we have inducted doctors into our workforce and they are working tirelessly and gaining experience each day as we go.

items.statement: Net worth Rs 21,343 crore; net worth including fair value Rs 47,703 crore; investment assets Rs 98,770 crore
items.quote: As on 30th June 2024, the company has a net worth of rupees Rs. 21,343 crores and investment assets standing at rupees Rs. 98,770 crores. The company's net worth including the fair value change account increased from rupees Rs. 44,704 crores in March 24 to rupees Rs.47,703 crores in June 24.

items.statement: Domestic revenue growth guidance of 17% for FY25 maintained
items.quote: Overall FY '25, 17% guidance on growth of domestic market remains. We will achieve that.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin guidance of 15% for domestic business maintained
items.quote: No, no, we maintain our guidance of that 15% because there are lot of other penetration in the new market, other thing will come. So, right now we are holding on to that guidance of 15% on Indian market.

items.statement: Target to increase India revenue share to 70-75% in 3-5 years
items.quote: So, since we are around 60% currently, we have a target of taking it to 70%-75%.

items.statement: Export revenue growth target of 4-5% annually
items.quote: But that will be only compensating our less revenues from Europe and other where it is not growing. So, the export will continuously focus, but we will see that at least we grow by 4% to 5% every year on our export sales.

items.statement: Consolidated revenue target to double in 5 years
items.quote: In five years from now we are doubling. We are doubling top line for sure.

items.statement: Completed Rs 175 crore CAPEX across three Indian manufacturing units
items.quote: We have successfully completed our CAPEX of around 175 crore, which was announced for all three manufacturing units in India.

items.statement: Inaugurated casting flux granules unit at Visakhapatnam with 18,000 MT annual capacity
items.quote: We recently inaugurated state-of-the-art casting flux granules production unit at Visakhapatnam with an annual capacity of 18,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Launched Magnesia Carbon production line with initial 9,000 MT capacity, targeting Rs 100 crore revenue
items.quote: We also launched a new Magnesia Carbon production line, part of our Phase-3 expansion. The facility with an initial capacity of 9,000 metric tons annual will enhance performance, longevity and reliability in high temperature application. This will allow us to generate a revenue of Rs 100 crores.

items.statement: Magnesia Carbon capacity to expand to 24,000 MT by FY26 Q2 with additional Rs 3 crore
items.quote: Plant capacity will be enhanced to 24,000 tons per annum in a year time with further capital outlay of around 3 crores.

items.statement: Odisha land allotment expected within a month for new manufacturing unit
items.quote: Yes, the land allotment is almost nearing because after this election results and everything is over, a new government has come in place. So, we are going to get that within a month's time also.

items.statement: Domestic capacity utilization at 65-70% overall (excluding new Vizag plant)
items.quote: Utilization level is in the range of 65% to 70%, overall basis I am talking about, not product to product.

items.statement: Peak revenue from new flux and Magnesia Carbon lines estimated at Rs 180 crore at full utilization
items.quote: Peak revenue we have already indicated that once when you reach 100% CU capacity utilization of flux plant, that's going to be around 80 crore and Magnesium-Carbon with some debottlenecking and other thing once when we reach, it will be 100 crore. So, it will be totally both the new lines will add 180 crore when we reach full capacity.

items.statement: Domestic steel demand projected at 6-8% growth, driving refractory demand
items.quote: So, steel growth and cement growth are projected, though it has not happened in the same rate in the first quarter, but we are expecting it to pick up, 6% to 8% growth in steel. So, to that extent, our refractory demand also will raise.

items.statement: European steel demand recovery expected from calendar Q4 2024
items.quote: So, I think then German companies will start being good. So, I think, calendar year, if I talk about, then from quarter four onwards, I think demand is expected to pick up in the European steel market.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin at 12.6% in Q1 FY25, down 11% YoY due to high employee cost, restructuring, and freight
items.quote: EBITDA margin for Quarter 1, FY '25 stood at 12.6%. PAT for the quarter was at 24.7 crore, down by 17% year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Standalone EBITDA margin at 17.9% in Q1 FY25, down 4% YoY but up 18% QoQ
items.quote: EBITDA for Quarter 1, FY '25 stood at 44.4 crores, down by 4% on year-on-year basis, and up by 18% on Q-on-Q basis. EBITDA margins for Q1 stood at 17.9%.

items.statement: Freight cost impact of Rs 6 crore in Q1 FY25 due to Red Sea crisis
items.quote: So, due to freight, the impact is around Rs. 6 crore.

items.statement: Entered non-ferrous refractory segment with alumina bricks and castables for cement, glass, coke; supplied trial orders to top 2 cement producers
items.quote: Predominantly, it is led by cement now. At the moment, we have already got kind of India's number one and number two cement producers have already given some trial orders and we have already supplied. And to the extent I can say, like around alumina bricks which we are supplying to the tune of 8 crores, the first time we have taken the order and also some castables, monolithic refractories.

items.statement: R&D focus on refractory recycling to reduce input costs and technology transfer from Sheffield Refractories
items.quote: One of key developments will be the initiation of refractory recycling which will significantly reduce input costs and contribute positively to our bottom line. This focus on innovation and cost efficiency is expected to deliver substantial benefits as we move forward, reinforcing our commitment to sustainable growth and profitability.

items.statement: Added new customers in mini steel plant (ESM) segment; increasing share of spend with integrated steel plants
items.quote: Yes, you see, we have added a few, you know, the mini steel plant and particularly with our cost-effective products of this, we name it as electro steel casting, electrical steel making (ESM) sector, where we are fast growing and adding new accounts. But coming to integrated steel plants, it is more of an increase in share of spend than addition of new customers.

items.statement: Mini steel plants contribute ~25% of domestic revenue
items.quote: So, if I talk about domestic kilns, then it would be almost 25%, share of domestic business.

items.statement: Cautious on Liberty Steel Group exposure; provisions taken in December quarter; ArcelorMittal exposure stable
items.quote: In terms of other customers, yes, we are very cautious with respect to Liberty Group, and because of the last quarter we had, in December quarter we had provisions. So, we are very, very cautious on that group, and we have taken the actions in terms of deliveries and payment terms and other things.

items.statement: Export revenue declined 6% YoY to Rs 80.2 crore in Q1 FY25; Europe slowdown primary driver
items.quote: Export business stood at 80.2 crores, saw a decline of 6% on a year-on-year basis.

items.statement: Sheffield Refractories running at ~Rs 45-50 crore quarterly revenue run rate
items.quote: So, Sheffield is now 45-50 crores roughly on a quarterly basis.

items.statement: Company remains net debt-free with Rs 213.4 crore cash and equivalents on consolidated basis
items.quote: With respect to liquidity positions, we remain net debt-free with a strong balance sheet. Cash and cash equivalents stood at 213.4 crore on consol basis as on 30th June 2024.

items.statement: Actively pursuing inorganic growth in India and overseas; no concrete deals to announce
items.quote: Yes, see, we are definitely actively looking forward to our inorganic growth, both in India as well as outside. And as of now, we do not have anything concrete to share with you, but the work is on progress.

items.statement: Red Sea crisis causing freight rate surge from $2,000 to $6,000 impacting export margins and customer deliveries
items.quote: Because of the uncertainty into the freight market, as you know, because of the Red Sea, the freight has gone up from $2,000 to $6,000 in some sectors. So, we can cause a lot of dent in our profitability.

items.statement: Revenue growth forecast for FY25 revised to 30-35% from earlier 35-40% due to delayed acquisition closures
items.quote: Basis, my estimate of the first week of April, we had said 35% to 40% in terms of forecast for the revenue growth, but now it is 30% to 35%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin forecast maintained at 20-22% for medium term despite Q2 headwinds from salary hikes and fewer working days
items.quote: We cont inue to maintain our forecast on EBITDA of between 20% to 22% in the medium term

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 23.9% of total income; operating margin (excl. other income) at 19.8%
items.quote: We reported an EBITDA of ₹ 117 crores, which is 23.9% of total income and has shown a growth of 13.3% Y -o-Y and 7.8% Q -o-Q.

items.statement: Salary increases effective July 1 to impact margins by 250-280 bps in Q2
items.quote: Effective 1st July, in line with our regular appraisal cycle, we have rolled out our yearly pay increases, which will have an impact of about 250 to 280 basis points on our margins.

items.statement: Generative AI Business Services (GBS) revenue $855K in Q1; 50+ customer conversations and 15 PoCs completed
items.quote: Our new Gen AI business unit has got off to a flying start, with reported revenues of $855,000 during the quarter.

items.statement: Active customers increased to 279; average revenue per customer $840K; $1M+ customers up to 58; 65 billion-dollar corporation clients
items.quote: We have 279 active customers and the average revenue per customer has increased to US $840,000 which is a testament to this strategy of land and expand that we've adopted.

items.statement: PureSoftware selected by leading American multinational investment bank for digital transformation; Arttha platform won Best Banking-as-a-Service Platform at Africa Bank 4.0 Summit
items.quote: PureSoftware has been selected by leading American multinational investment bank to drive their digital transformation progra m. Recently, PureSoftware's Arttha banking platform was awarded Best Banking-as-a-Service Platform of the Year at the 14th Africa Bank 4.0 Summit

items.statement: Closed PureSoftware (40 days revenue consolidated) and Aureus (38 days) acquisitions; integration underway targeting operational synergies
items.quote: We closed two significant acquisitions. PureSoftware of significant size and Aureus, a company which has got deep capabilities in reinsurance space.

items.statement: Acquisitions add BFSI (17%) and Healthcare (16%) as top 3 verticals; new markets in APAC, Africa, Mexico, Hyderabad
items.quote: The BFSI and Healthcare and life science verticals because of these acquisitions are now in the top three industry groups for us with revenue contribution of 17% and 16%, respectively.

items.statement: Cash expended on upfront acquisition consideration ~₹712 crores funded via internal accruals and overdraft on FDs
items.quote: Cash expended on payment of upfront consideration for the two acquisitions was about ₹ 712 crores.

items.statement: Board approved raising up to ₹250 crores via NCDs and term loans to replace existing debt and maintain debt market access
items.quote: We have taken an in -principle approval from the Board to raise up to ₹ 250 crores through a combination of NCD and term loans.

items.statement: Cash balance ₹1,560 crores after acquisition payments; free cash conversion ~100% of EBITDA at ₹116 crores
items.quote: Cash on our books is about ₹1,560 crores. This is after considering upfront payments of PureSoftware and Aureus, which have been funded through a combination of internal accruals and overdraft facilities that we have availed on our fixed deposits.

items.statement: DSO improved to 84 days from 87 days
items.quote: We have improved our DSO from 87 to 84 days.

items.statement: Headcount 6,600 including 1,431 net additions (112 campus hires); attrition down to 13.5% from 16.6%; gender diversity 27.7%
items.quote: Including PureSoftware and Aureus, Happiest Minds is now 6,600 strong with a strong net addition of 1,431. These numbers also include 112 campus hires that we made during the quarter.

items.statement: Over 75% workforce trained in Gen AI tools; target full coverage in couple of quarters; internal Gen AI use cut recruitment lifecycle 30-40%
items.quote: I'm happy to share that over 75% of our workforce is already trained in Gen AI tools and we hope to cover the entire workforce in couple of quarters.

items.statement: Board expanded to 8 members with induction of Mittu Sridhara and Rajiv Shah
items.quote: With these additions, Happiest Minds Board of Directors now comprises eight members.

items.statement: Revenue $55.5M, up 10.9% QoQ and 16.8% YoY (11.4% QoQ, 17.8% YoY constant currency); total income ₹489 crores, up 20.6% YoY
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have delivered exceptional performance with revenues of US $ 55.5 Million for the quarter which is a growth of 10.9% Q-o-Q and 16.8% Y-o-Y.

items.statement: Acquisition integration one-time costs (amortization, unwinding interest, acquisition expenses) and exceptional write-back swing of ~₹20 crores impacted PBT/PAT
items.quote: If you consider the ₹13 crores of exceptional write-back in the previous quarter, take it along with the cash charge of the ₹ 6.5 crores of acquisition cost, we are talking about a swing of ₹20 crores on account of one-time exceptional costs.

items.statement: Net profit growth may take 2-3 quarters to normalize as acquisition accounting costs recoup; cash EPS and ROCE preferred metrics
items.quote: It takes about at least two, three quarters for these one-time costs or amortization of intangibles, unwinding of interest. These kind of accounting costs, as I call it, to get completely recouped from the business growth.

items.statement: Competitive intensity from peers like EPAM not significant; main challenge is Global Capability Centres (GCCs) expansion trend
items.quote: We really have not seen much of competitive intensity from some of our similar size or slightly larger brethren. But what we are seeing is more of the Global Capability Centres or GCCs getting established.

items.statement: Service line mix shift: analytics/AI/security % down due to PureSoftware/Aureus having less exposure; absolute numbers grew; cross-sell opportunity identified
items.quote: If you look at PureSoftware and Aureus, more of the revenues come from digital infrastructure and applications. They have less of analytics AI and security. And that's the reason you see these going down as a percentage of revenues.

items.statement: Customers calibrating spend, seeking targeted ROI interventions; restructuring common; Happiest Minds using agile industry-group structure for consultative account management
items.quote: With customers being careful about their spend and seeking very targeted interventions for better ROI and investment, our ability to identify these priorities and quickly pivot is very critical.

items.statement: Absolute revenue growth target: FY25 to be best year since IPO; at 30% growth implies $50-52M incremental revenue on $196M base
items.quote: At 30%, it would be upwards of $53 million. We closed last year at about $196 million. So at 30%, at the lower end of the range that I'm giving, we should grow in the range $50 million - $52 million.

items.statement: Ashok Soota shareholding ~45% after recent sale; no further sales expected for 2-4 years; committed to not go below 40%
items.quote: The current sale has brought my shareholding down to about 45%. And I do not expect to make any further sale in the next two to four years.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 volume growth guidance maintained at 12%-15% (mid-teens) and 18%-20% CAGR over 3-5 years
items.quote: And of course, the second and the third quarter are actually the larger quarte rs for the company, and category of products that we offer. Actually, these are generally about 60% of the year. So the majority of the growth, we believe, will also happen in the second and third quarter

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin guidance maintained at 11%
items.quote: So for us, annualized, we believe we'll protect the 11%.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 capex guidance confirmed at INR50-60 crores including INR13 crore solar plant
items.quote: So for the full year FY '25, basically, it will be in that range of INR50 crores-INR60 crores kind of capex. Is that understanding right? Rajendra Gandhi: Yes, you're right. Resha Mehta: Including the solar plant, INR13 crores, right? Rajendra Gandhi: Yes

items.statement: Q1 FY25 gross margin improved to 38.2% from 36.9% YoY due to higher sales realization
items.quote: Gross profit margin for the current quarter stood at 38.2% as against 36.9% in Q1 FY '24 and 37.1% in Q4 FY '24. This improvement is due to increase in sales realization.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin expanded to 10.1% from 8% YoY and 7.6% QoQ
items.quote: The EBITDA margin was 10.1% versus 8% in Q1 FY '24 and 7.6% in Q4 FY '24, showing a growth of 210 basis points Y-o-Y and 250 basis points quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: Retail stores operate at 50-52% gross margin vs company average of 38%
items.quote: Yes, we operate at about between 50% and 52% on the retail stores.

items.statement: Export gross margins lower than company average but EBITDA margins at par or better
items.quote: You are right on the exports front, on the gross margin, our margins are lower, but EBITDA is either at par with the company's EBITDA level or sometimes better.

items.statement: Retail store count increased to 191 stores across 11 states and 49 cities; added 20 stores and converted 23 COCO to COFO in Q1 FY25
items.quote: We have continued our aggressive store expansion strategy increasing our total retail store count to 191 stores across 11 states and the footprint in 49 cities. Notably, we have made meaningful inroads into the Delhi NCR region, expanding our operations beyond the Southern states.

items.quote: Overall, when you see it was about 1%.

items.quote: So the m etal prices are stabilizing now. It's just happened recently. And if this continues, definitely, if not for the second and third quarter, but we'll definitely pass on if the metal prices continue to be at the same level

items.quote: Wherever we have seen substantial correction before the beginning of this quarter, we would have definitely done. Example, I would want to give you tha t the -- some electronic parts that we were importing in the past, over the previous year, we have seen some substantial price reduction. So, we have passed on some of our products like our induction cooker.

items.statement: Channel mix Q1 FY25: General trade 31%, e-commerce 28.4%, modern trade 12.1%, corporate sales 4.4%, retail outlets 4.8%, exports 19.2%
items.quote: 31% was contributed by general trade, eCom contributed 28.4%, the modern trade contributed 12.1%. Our corporate sales contributed 4.4%. The retail outlets contributed 4.8% and our exports business contributed 19.2%.

items.statement: Working capital debt to be eliminated by end of FY25; only working capital debt remains
items.quote: We believe that we can also get to being rid offthe net of our complete debt by the end of this year itself, particularly the working capital debts. We only have working capital debt.

items.statement: Finance cost to reduce as working capital debt eliminated; lease accounting notional impact INR1.5 crore in Q1 FY25 (rent INR4.5 crore vs accounted INR5.9 crore)
items.quote: In the earlier question I think -- I will tell you, the overall rent for this quarter was about INR4.5 crores, but actual accounted as per India's lease accounting, it is INR5.9 c rores interest and depreciation both. items.statement: No major external senior hires; focusing on internal leadership development; adding human capital as needed
items.quote: So we are continuously adding human capital with the capabilities that the company believes the right kind of capability, but we are more excited with growth within the company, and we believe that the company is well poised to handle the growth.

items.statement: Marketing spend maintained at 3-3.5% of revenue across all channels including e-commerce
items.quote: So we will continue to invest between 3% to 3.5% on our overall revenue towards marketing and advertisement spend.

items.statement: Black & Decker license: 10+10 year arrangement with automatic renewal; relationship very strong
items.quote: So we have a 10 -plus 10-year arrangement with them. It's an automatic renewal mechanism. And currently, we are very confident, the relationship is very strong.

items.statement: No returns taken from online channels; returns managed by platform sellers
items.quote: So the way the business is structured for us, we do not take any returns from our online channels. This is absorbed by the sellers on the channel.

items.statement: EBITDA margin guidance of 30% plus for FY25, with concrete guidance post Q2
items.quote: However, looking at the current financial year, 30% plus is something what we see we will be able to maintain. However, a concrete guidance on how upwards of 30% this would be, we will be able to give post Quarter 2 results.

items.statement: CMO/CDMO to contribute ~20% of revenue in 3-4 years
items.quote: We anticipate moving forward, let's say in the next 3 to 4 years, CMO should contribute about 20% of the total revenue.

items.quote: See, as of now, the CapEx allocated for Ambernath would be somewhere around Rs. 75 crores. items.statement: European revenue share surged from 43% in Q4 FY24 to 51% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In quarter 4, Financial Year '2 4, the European market accounted for 43% of the Company's revenue. This figure surged to an impressive 51% in Q1 Financial Year '2 5.

items.quote: EBITDA in Q1 FY25 stood at Rs. 62.5 crores, as against Rs. 44.5 crores in Q1 FY24. And the EBITDA margin stood at 39% for Q1 FY25, as against 34% in Q1 FY24.

items.quote: With the newer product launches coming in, in the latter half of the year and their concentration being in more semi -regulated markets, we expect the margin to sort of normalize.

items.quote: We already have 2 CMO contracts in place. The DSM Firmenich is one. We already have started supplying them for their validation quantity and some part of their food application demand. items.quote: We will start seeing the CMO revenues kick in probably by 3rd Quarter of this financial year. So, 3rd and 4th Quarter will have some revenues from some of the CMO contracts. From next year onwards is when you will start seeing larger contribution from CMO opportunities.

items.quote: So, in the new product launches, we are looking at therapeutic categories like anti -anxiety and anesthetics. items.quote: As of now, we have a total installed capacity of 80,000 tonnes in sodium dichromate. T hat is our primary finished good in the Chromium chemicals umbrella. We have been contemplating about adding 20,000 tonnes of sodium dichromate and this will be built in phases, about 10,000 tonnes first and then the second phase will be about 10,000 tonnes again

items.statement: Continued demand growth for chemicals despite rising freight costs; Barium export traction improved with entry into premium markets like USA
items.quote: It is encouraging to note tha t despite the increasing freight costs, there is continued demand growth for our chemicals, which underscores the innovation in the use cases of our products

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin 16.4% in Q1 FY25 vs 21.2% in Q4 FY24 due to inventory normalization; standalone EBITDA margin 16.96% vs 17.03% YoY
items.quote: Sequentially, the EBITDA margins were about 16.4% on a consolidated level compared to 21.2% in Q4 FY24. Q4 FY24, we had more inventory of finished goods that was sold during this quarter and thereby there is a reduction of change in inventory, leading to a more normalized EBITDA margin for us during this quarter.

items.statement: Increased realizations across most products to address rising freight and raw material costs
items.quote: To address rising freight and raw material costs, the company increased the real izations of its finished goods across most of the products

items.statement: US prices 8-9% higher than other export markets; export premium typically 3-5% over domestic
items.quote: Now, the U.S. price is close to about 8% higher compared to our prices that we sell to other markets, 8- 9% higher.

items.statement: CO2 plant utilization ~80% of envisaged optimum; saving INR 4-4.5 cr/month; in-house soda ash sourcing 40-45%
items.quote: Our u tilization of CO2 plant is improving and we are now going to hit our optimum levels. Probably, we have achieved close to about 80% utilization levels, whatever we had envisaged. And today, our savings from that is close to about INR 4-4.5 crores a month

items.statement: Reduced key feedstock consumption 7-10% in chromium chemicals via process improvements
items.quote: we have done a lot of process and product level improvements to bring down our feedstock consumed to produce every kg of finished product. And that has helped us, especially in the Chromium chemical vertical, to reduce our overall consumption of key feedstock by close to about 7 -10% in different raw materials.

items.statement: US revenue share grew from 1-1.5% (FY21) to 4-4.5% currently; targeting >5% in coming years
items.quote: At a consolidated level, USA is close to about 4-4.5% of our turnover. Now this was in the range of 1-1.5%, 3 years ago. This has increased by nearly 300 basis points in the last 3 years compared to FY21.

items.statement: India chromium market share 60%; global ~8% targeting 12-13% in 3-4 years; Barium gaining share in US market
items.quote: In India, we have a market share of 60%. And globally, our market share is close to 10%, around 8% to be specific. In the next 3 to 4 years, our target is to become a global market share leader with around 12 -13%.

items.statement: No equity raise planned; CapEx to be funded from internal accruals and debt (debt/equity <0.5)
items.quote: We have no plans to raise any equity. We are quite healthy in terms of our balance sheet as well as debt position. So, with our debt to equity being less than 0.5 and our internal accruals significantly improving, we don't necessarily see any opportunities to raise equity to fund our CapEx now.

items.statement: Chromium standalone revenue range INR 1,100-1,250 cr at optimum 80,000 tpa capacity; FY23 INR 1,222 cr, FY24 INR 1,011 cr
items.quote: in Chromium chemicals, we have 80,000 tonnes of capacity. And the optimum top line that we can achieve from this is close to about in this range of INR 1,100 crores to INR 1,250 crores.

items.statement: Red Sea logistics crisis increased transit time 2-3 weeks, forcing higher inventory holding; risk persists until shipping normalizes
items.quote: Red Sea crisi s had increased th e overall transit time by not just days but between 2 to 3 weeks for us to ship our products to any other target end customer

items.statement: Management says it is too early to give specific top-line or bottom-line guidance; will share projections around Q4 FY25.
items.quote: At this point , we can talk about products and what is the thinking behind the products . So, this is something that more towards the kind of quarter four this year, we will be able to talk more about year-on-year projections.

items.statement: Collections (Cash Management Services) grew 8% QoQ and 31% YoY to ~Rs 8,000 cr in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: In Quarter 1 FY25 we did nearly 7 ,924 nearly Rs.8,000 crores worth of collections, using our platform and 8% growth quarter-on-quarter, and about a 31% growth year-on-year.

items.statement: Bharat Bill Payment System volumes grew 9.4% QoQ and 48.6% YoY to ~Rs 1,300 cr in Q1 FY25.
items.quote: in Quarter 1 FY25 we have made nearly Rs.1300 crores of b ill payments using our merchant points, which is a 9.4% quarter -on-quarter growth and a 48.6% year-on-year growth

items.statement: Credit disbursed to end customers (Grahak) jumped to Rs 29 cr in Q1 FY25 from Rs 12 cr in Q4 FY24.
items.quote: If you look at in terms of the value of loans dispersed in Quarter 1 FY25 to the Grahak , it was nearly Rs. 29 crores for the quarter, compared to Rs. 12 crores in the previous quarter.

items.statement: Service fee gross margin flat QoQ (-0.1%) and YoY (-0.7%) at Rs 40.7 cr despite 6.5% YoY revenue decline.
items.quote: And linked to that the service fee gross margin, which is close to 40.7 crores for the quarter under discussion. Basically, if you see quarter -on-quarter, we have remained relatively flat about negative 0.8% on customer GTV, negative 1% on service fee revenue, but more impo rtantly, about negative 0.1% which is effectively a flat quarter -on-quarter, on the service fee gross margin which is reall

items.statement: No explicit capex guidance; focus on variable tech/marketing spend for UPI wallet launch.
items.quote: When it comes to tech and marketing, we are trying to keep it as variable as possible , but Pritam, this is something that our first goal is to , with our alpha and beta program, to get the product market fit in place.

items.statement: Merchant network grew 3% QoQ to ~1.4 million; focus now on deeper density in existing 19,000 PIN codes.
items.quote: In the last one quarter, we have added nearly 37,000 new merchants to our platform, signifying a 3% growth over what we closed at the end of financial year 24. So, if you look at it as of the end of Quarter 1 , FY25 we have now close to 1.4 million merchants who have been on-boarded on our Spice Money platform.

items.statement: Restructured distribution to district-level distributors to drive deeper merchant density.
items.quote: We have also now restructured our distribution network, where now we have distributors, at a district level focusing on driving deeper density within the district. So, the focus is going to be to get more and more merchants on board and get them to do more business.

items.statement: Launched UPI on PPI wallet (alpha/beta) to serve customers with inoperative bank accounts; differentiation vs bank-account-linked UPI.
items.quote: What we are bringing to the market is a UPI product linked to a wallet. What many of the UPI apps have is a UPI product linked to a bank account . And therefore, there is a large segment of the market that still has inoperative bank accounts especially with respect to enabling digital transactions using the bank account.

items.statement: Plans to launch own NBFC lending to Adhikaris (merchants) using proprietary data and collection infrastructure.
items.quote: Our goal is to try an d get it in place within this financial year so that we can actually start lending. And to your final point, what will be the focus . Our focus will be on the merchant base, which is our own Adhikaris , and that's what we are going to focus on as far as our NBFC is concerned.

items.statement: AePS 2FA mandate removed from 1 July 2024; market share already improving in July.
items.quote: This is something which has now been removed, this transactional base 2 FA so if you look at the box on the right-hand side, the last message transaction 2FA has been removed effectively, 1stJuly, 2024 which is the current quarter that we are in, and we have already started seeing our market share improve in the month of July.

items.statement: Applied for NBFC license (change of control) in June 2024; approval timeline regulator-driven.
items.quote: In the last quarter at the end of the quarter, in Quarter 1 we applied for acquiring an NBFC license from within the group. It's a change of control application, and this is something that has gone to the regulator, and we will be working closely on the process involved in getting the requisite approvals.

items.statement: Board approved merger of Spice Money into DiGiSPICE Technologies; scheme now under regulatory approval.
items.quote: In our last Board meeting which was held on the 8th of August, the Board of DiGiSPICE Technologies, along with its subsidiary Boards, have taken a decision to merge S pice Money with DiGiSPICE Technologies, and the scheme of amalgamation has been approved by the DiGiSPICE B oard, and now we will be going through the process of getting all the requisite approvals to make this merger come through.

items.statement: Company is zero-debt; only OD/FD treasury arrangements; will evaluate capital structure for NBFC expansion.
items.quote: Yes, today we are a zero-debt company. Only for the treasury management, we have some OD and FD arrangements with the banks. That's a better utilization of the funds. So, from that perspective, we are zero debt as of now.

items.statement: No immediate fund raise; will approach Board if growth capital needed beyond internal accruals.
items.quote: Of course, we are not going to compromise growth because of lack of cash, and therefore, whenever we see a need to get access to more growth capital outside of internal accruals, we will go back to the B oard and discuss around formal fundraising plans, and see how to move forward.

items.statement: New CFO Vineet Mahajan (NBFC background) hired to build NBFC business; core team stable with selective additions in risk, tech, compliance.
items.quote: Vineet Mahajan , he has joined us as a CFO at the DiGiSPICE . Effectively, Vineet comes from the NBFC background. He's had tr emendous experience in working at, leading NBFCs in the ecosystem As DiGiSPICE we are looking to enter the NBFC space, and that is the area where we really see Vineet helping us to build out in the space.

items.statement: Welcomes competitor listings (e.g., Relipay/RNFI) as validation and industry consolidation; sees ample headroom for multiple players.
items.quote: We welcome players getting listed in this space becau se it just helps us to see more -and-more of the space get organized a nd when a company gets listed, like we ourselves are a listed company, as we welcome our competition into the listed space, together we can work to organize the space even more.

items.statement: Served ~40 million transacting customers in Q1 FY25 via AePS; 54% repeat rate in BBPS EMI collections.
items.quote: If you look at total transacting customers, and this is an important one for me to highlight, we have nearly four crore, 40 million customers who have transacted, using our platform with their bank account, at the merchant points that we have on-boarded.

items.statement: AePS market share ~17.16% in Q1 FY25; target to grow share as industry consolidates.
items.quote: We are about 17.16% market share this quarter. And our goal is that within the pie, we have still headroom to grow our market share. And we believe that this space will consolidate to a few players, and we will be one of them.

items.statement: AePS fraud/gamification concerns caused Off-us volume decline; 2FA removal expected to reverse trend.
items.quote: We have seen a dip in the way our larger Adhikaris have transacted, and this has basically been because of the implementation of a two factor authentication, by the regulator. And the goal here was to control fraud in the overall space.

items.statement: Discontinued operations PAT Rs 4.2 cr in Q1 FY25; expected to decline further.
items.quote: is also PAT, with respect to discontinued operations, is Rs. 4.2 crores which we have already announced in this quarter that we have discontinued the operations with respect t o the revenue. So, hopefully this will reduce further in the coming quarters

items.statement: Expect 13% to 15% EBITDA margin in near future
items.quote: We expect 13% to 15% EBITDA margin in the near future.

items.statement: Target 10% revenue growth in FY25 driven by volume and price
items.quote: We hope 10% increase in the current year.

items.statement: Target 50% of API revenue from non-ibuprofen in 3-4 years
items.quote: Down the line around 3-4 years, we are targeting 50% turnover of API segment from non-ibuprofen segment which is presently around 20% of overall revenue.

items.statement: Capex of Rs 200 crore in FY25 and Rs 150 crore in FY26
items.value: Rs. 200 crore and next financial year it may be around Rs. 150 crore
items.quote: This financial year it is around Rs. 200 crore and next financial year it may be around Rs. 150 crore.

items.statement: Target export share of 45% to 50% in 3-4 years
items.quote: It is around 45% to 50%.

items.statement: EBITDA margin declined 260 bps YoY to 11.4% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: EBITDA margin for the quarter declined by 260 basis points to 11.4% as against 14% in the correspondence quarter of Financial Year '24 and 11.3% in the previous quarter ended March '24.

items.statement: Pharma segment EBIT margin maintained at 11.8%, Specialty Chemical at 1% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: With easing of operating expense, EBIT margin for the Pharmaceutical segment was maintained at 11.8% in 1st Quarter of Financial Year '25, while EBIT margin for the Specialty Chemical segment was 1% in 1st Quarter of Financial Year '25.

items.statement: Ibuprofen prices bottomed out, no further reduction expected
items.quote: The prices are already bottom ed out and we are getting regular order at certain prices of ibuprofen. So, we do not fear any more reduction of prices in Ibuprofen

items.statement: Export realization 20-25% better than domestic on average
items.quote: But in any case, around 20% to 25% better realization is observed as compared to domestic prices.

items.statement: Ibuprofen capacity utilization at 80% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Capacity utilization of ibuprofen presently around 80% and for non-ibuprofen it has started increasing which was earlier ranging from 40% to 70%.

items.statement: Expect non-ibuprofen capacity utilization to reach optimum level within 2 years
items.quote: We are expecting a ramp up of our capacity utilization at an optimum level within next 2 years.

items.statement: No immediate capacity expansion planned in chemical segment
items.quote: In chemical as of now there is no immediate plan to expand capacities, but we may have some planning for new launches in the time to come in chemical segment also.

items.statement: Added paracetamol and acetic anhydride manufacturing in last 2 years
items.quote: Also we have added projects manufacturing of paracetamol and acetic anhydride in the last 2 years.

items.statement: Set up new large capacity ETP plant at same location
items.quote: We have ETP plant which is around 10 years old, but we have set up another ETP plant in the location itself with a large capacity.

items.statement: Paracetamol prices fell over 40%, Metformin 15-20% in last year
items.quote: The prices of Paracetamol was reduced by more than 40% in the last 1 year and for Metformin it was reduced up to 15% to 20%.

items.statement: Ibuprofen prices stable at $9-10 vs $12 four years ago
items.quote: Earlier around 4 years back the prices of ibuprofen was ranging around $12, now we are getting the average realization of $9 to $10.

items.statement: Power, fuel and freight costs decreased, lowering other expenses
items.quote: Actually, in last year, our power and fuel expenses are on high side due to coal prices which are now stable and decreased somehow and freight part is also on decreasing side.

items.statement: Agrochemical segment benefited from normal monsoon with good volume growth
items.quote: Normal monsoon and onset of timely rains has benefited Agrochemical Segment with good volume growth.

items.statement: Specialty chemical faces volume and pricing pressure from high channel inventory and China dumping
items.quote: In regard to Speciality Chemical, high channel inventory and destocking has led to continued volume and pricing pressure on the industry. In addition to this continuous dumping by China and lower prices a re hurting profitability

items.statement: Export queries and trial orders increasing from regulated markets
items.quote: has also increased. Various technical people of respective clients of competitors who have had quality issuesare coming for audit purpose and we are getting some trial orders or samples

items.statement: Export contribution started increasing with CEP approvals
items.quote: Yeah, it has started increasing. Q ueries has also increased. Various technical people of respective clients of competitors who have had quality issuesare coming for audit purpose and we are getting some trial orders or samples

items.statement: SI Group reportedly exiting ibuprofen with 4,500-5,000 tonne capacity
items.quote: We have heard from the newspapers that they are exiting, but as per our internal sources, their capacity is around 4500 to 5000 tonnes.

items.statement: Largest ibuprofen player for over a decade, backward integrated advantage
items.quote: We are the largest player of ibuprofen since last more than a decade and we are concentrating only on our clients, our regulatory approvals, our qualities and other after sales services.

items.statement: Export share stable at 30% of revenue in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In this quarter we have 30% export and 70% domestic turnover, which is similar to the last years export and domestic sales.

items.statement: Inventory increased due to new products (paracetamol, acetic anhydride) and bulk alcohol order
items.quote: As we have added new products in the market . So, the inventory has been increased accordingly for the new product s like P aracetamol and acetic anhydride. That may be the reason to increase level of inventories in our finished product and for raw material we have got a good order from one vendor on

items.statement: Net cash of Rs 190 crore as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: That is around Rs. 190 crore in the bank.

items.statement: No buyback planned; cash reserved for organic growth and opportunities
items.quote: Our priority as of now is to enhance the business, increase the capacities of the various products and the cash is there for grabbing any good opportunity in the market.

items.statement: May consider acquisitions if good opportunity arises at proper valuation
items.quote: If any good opportunity, which is benefic ial for the company ’s shareholder or any business comes in the market with a proper valuation, we may consider that , but as of now, our first priority is to go organically

items.statement: No decision on bonus, split or buyback; board to discuss
items.quote: So, bonus and the split, we can discuss this in the board, and board will take decision on it, but as of now, there has not been any decision.

items.statement: R&D team continuously working on new non-ibuprofen products
items.quote: We are having various products in the pipeline and our R&D team is continuously working on those such products.

items.statement: Peak revenue potential at current rates estimated at Rs 2,400-2,500 crore
items.quote: At the current rate, it may be around Rs. 2400 to 2500 crore.

items.statement: Freight rates surge and logistics cost pain expected ahead
items.quote: Freight rates surge continues, imports/exports, logistics cost pain is expected going ahead.

items.statement: Formed 50-50 JV with UPL named Augene Chemical Private Limited for downstream amine derivatives
items.value: Rs. 150 crore each investment; Rs. 400-500 crore peak annual revenue
items.quote: Both the companies are expected to invest about Rs. 150 crore each into this JV over the next two years. The commercial supplies are expected to begin by Q1 FY27, targeting peak annual revenue potential of Rs. 400-500 crore within the next 2-3 years.

items.statement: Suyog Kotecha joined as Executive Director and CEO on June 17, 2024
items.quote: I am delighted to have Mr. Suyog Kotecha joining in as Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of Aarti Industries Ltd. Suyog joined our team on June 17th, 2024 bringing with him extensive expertise in strategy, innovation, and business transformation.

items.statement: Target 20-30% YoY volume growth for FY25; EBITDA guidance withdrawn due to margin volatility
items.quote: I think on demand front, we are pretty confident of delivering growth in the range of 20% to 30% and this is coming with a combination of commissioning of some of the new projects as well as better capacity utilization in some of the existing product chains.

items.statement: EBITDA per kg down vs pre-COVID levels; margin recovery expected to be long-haul due to Chinese competition
items.quote: On a broader level, yes, EBITDA at a rupees per Kg level for many of the products is not equivalent to where it was three, four years back and that's also reflected in our EBITDA margin percentages.

items.statement: FY25 capex Rs. 1,500-1,800 crore; Rs. 270 crore spent in Q1; bulk of remaining spend on Zone-IV Chlorotoluene project
items.quote: From an overall capital expenditure point of view, we had projected Rs.1,500 crore to Rs. 1,800 crore in the financial year and in Q1 we have already spent Rs. 270 crore.

items.statement: Nitrotoluene capacity expanding from 30,000 to 45,000 tons; Ethylation capacity 3x from 8,000-10,000 to ~25,000 tons; commissioning end of Q2 FY25
items.quote: Currently, the capacity is around 30,000 tons and we are looking to ramp it up to around 45,000 tons. And for Ethylation, we have a capacity of around 8,000 tons to 10,000 tons and it is expected to go by around 3x maybe around 25,000 tons roughly around that magnitude.

items.statement: Positive demand momentum in pharma, polymers, additives, dyes, pigments; green shoots in agrochemicals
items.quote: We have been witnessing positive demand momentum in key end use applications like pharma, polymers, additives, dyes and pigments. Even in agrochemicals, there are small green shoots of demand recovery.

items.statement: Chinese pricing pressure across portfolio, most acute in agrochemicals; 70-80% of product basket faces Chinese competition
items.quote: I think the pressure on pricing from Chinese capacity is across the board. It is much more aggravated in the Agchem chain from an application standpoint. But the pressure is there even in other segments.

items.statement: Energy application now significant share (~60% exports in Q1); fuel additive demand linked to gasoline/naphtha cracks
items.quote: Energy as an application has become a relatively large application for us, which is bringing additional volatility to the business performance as it is linked to external factors like crude, gasoline cracks, naphtha cracks which have their own element of volatility.

items.statement: Other expenses fell QoQ due to absence of annual employee benefit costs and lower freight from Middle East/Asia mix shift
items.quote: Some of the annual costs which were there in Q4 related to employee benefits and other stuff would not be there in Q1. So, that is some component and in some pockets the freight has been lower.

items.statement: Current debt ~Rs. 3,300 crore; expected to rise to Rs. 3,500-3,800 crore in FY25 due to capex and working capital
items.quote: So, as regards this year, I expect it to be anywhere between Rs. 3,500 to 3,800 crore. It depends on how the raw material prices and the working capital play, around that.

items.statement: Prioritizing Tier-1 customers as demand recovers; still tactically using Tier-2/3 in some chains including China
items.quote: Yes, broadly speaking, as we see demand recovery on many of the end use markets, we prioritize our sort of Tier-1 customers in those chains. There are some chains where tactically we may still have to go back to Tier-2, Tier-3 customers, sometimes including that in China.

items.statement: No new Chinese capacity seen recently in Ethylation/Chlorotoluene; but broader value chain substitution risk exists
items.quote: No, not at this stage. We haven't seen any new capacity coming in China in the recent times. But what we need to understand is ultimately it's a value chain, right?

items.statement: No direct exposure to Bangladesh (<1% of portfolio); monitoring indirect impact on dyes/textile customers
items.quote: We don't have direct exposure to Bangladesh or any significant exposure to Bangladesh. So, right now we are not seeing any risk from the particular events happening in Bangladesh. And I think the exposure is less than 1% of total business portfolio.

items.statement: Margin volatility from energy application seasonality and Chinese dumping; EBITDA guidance withdrawn until better visibility
items.quote: I think the pressure from China is actually not sort of going away and we have seen that across broader product portfolio, not in a specific chain, but across broader product portfolio, the pressure on margin is still very intense.

items.statement: Target 20-25% EBITDA CAGR over 5 years (~2.5-3x EBITDA); three themes: project execution, R&D in sunrise sectors, culture retention
items.quote: Our goal as stated earlier is to deliver 20% to 25% CAGR growth in EBITDA, which if we take a five-year view, then it is almost 2.5x-3x growth in EBITDA.

items.statement: Nitrotoluene + Ethylation expansion capex ~Rs. 400-500 crore; Zone-IV Chlorotoluene project bulk of remaining FY25 spend
items.quote: It would be in the magnitude of around Rs. 400 crore to 500 crore.

items.statement: Target 50% utilization of new Nitrotoluene/Ethylation capacity in FY25; 60-80% in FY26
items.quote: We are expecting somewhere in the range of targeting up to 50% capacity utilization within this financial year and then taking it all the way up to 60% to 80% capacity utilization level in the next financial year.

items.statement: Benzene and aniline prices rose QoQ/YoY in Q1; some softening seen in current quarter
items.quote: On benzene, we have seen sort of a sequential increase in prices going up to Q1 FY25 level. But in the current quarter, we have started to see some softening in the benzene prices. I think aniline has remained quite volatile.

items.statement: Export share rose to ~60% in Q1 FY25 from ~52% due to energy application mix
items.quote: I think energy application which has now become significant part, their larger share comes from export and that's why you will see compared to last year average where I think our overall share of export was, I think roughly 52%-odd has gone up to 60% now in the Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Long-term contracts (SABIC, other) on track; SABIC plant running at full capacity; revenue/volume trajectory as expected
items.quote: I think both these contracts continue to do very well. In fact, the contract with SABIC has ramped up quite significantly. I think indication of demand from their side, start of this calendar year versus now there has been significant improvement.

items.statement: Zone-IV Chlorotoluene value chain to add 40 downstream specialty products; commissioning phased from FY26
items.quote: We have a portfolio of 40 different products as part of that investment and we will go significantly downstream into specialty derivatives, right? We will not stop at sort of the first two levels of derivatives.

items.statement: PDA production ~206 tons/month in Q1 FY25 vs 135 tons/month YoY
items.quote: The PDA number is roughly around 206 tons per month for the current quarter against last year same quarter this number was 135 tons per month.

items.statement: Pass-through pricing works on benzene downstream; aniline downstream partly exposed to market pricing causing volatility
items.quote: On benzene downstream we have decent amount of portfolio where we have a pass-through pricing mechanism, and we are able to retain that. On Aniline downstream product portfolio, I think some part of it is linked to raw material, some part of it is not directly linked to raw material where we take market exposure.

items.statement: FY25 capex peaks; FY26 capex expected significantly lower
items.quote: No, I think it's only for this FY'25. In fact, I think from a annual CAPEX point of view, we will peak in this financial year. I thin k our CAPEX for the next financial year is expected to be significantly lower compared to current levels

items.statement: Non-MMA volume growth ~5-6% QoQ; YoY growth skewed by energy application scale-up
items.quote: So, if you are talking about QoQ volume growth, then actually the volume growth is quite consistent even in non-MMA portfolio; it still remains in the range of 5% to 6%.

items.statement: Fuel additive demand optimistic long-term despite EV trend; product more sustainable than metal-based alternatives
items.quote: We think from an absolute volume point of view still ICE engine rate capacity remains in the market. This fuel additive is actually much more sustainable compared to other options available today in the market, right.

items.statement: Expects ~12,000 metric tons recycling volume linked to Rs 30-35 crore profit for FY25
items.quote: as I envisaged, about 12,000 metric tons, which I will link with the profitability of about Rs. 30 crores plus, or even Rs. 35 crores is what we envisage out of 12,000 metric tons.

items.statement: Invested Rs 50 crore in new plant, machinery, land and building by June 2024
items.quote: we have invested by 30th June entirely Rs. 50 crores in the plant and machinery and the land building.

items.statement: Total capacity expanded to 25,200 metric tons per annum across two facilities in Vasai East
items.quote: Ecoreco has already expanded its capacity to 25,200 metric tons per annum.

items.statement: New facility inaugurated 5 June 2024; nominal utilization in Q1, expects substantial increase going forward
items.quote: it was a very nominal utilization during the June quarter because on 5th June only we formally inaugurated it.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin improved 298 bps to 76.12%; PAT margin up 125 bps to 60.64%
items.quote: EBITDA margin improving by 298 basis points to 76.12%. The consolidated PAT for the quarter rose by 73.04% to Rs. 8.15 crores, reflecting a PAT margin enhancement of 125 basis points to 60.64%.

items.statement: Reduces waste acquisition cost by insisting producers supply material at nominal price and bear expenses
items.quote: we insist our suppliers, particularly the producers, that if they are following certain practices in the world, in the developed countries, they should follow over here too, like giving the material at a nominal price, bearing other expenses, and all other things put together, we always focus on reducing the cost of acquisition of the waste.

items.statement: CPCB working on higher category-wise EPR fees to bridge formal-informal price gap; fees will be much higher than current market rates
items.quote: CPCB is particularly with the Ministry of Environment, is working on the mechanism of giving us a higher EPR fees, suggesting or mandating v ery shortly that higher EPR fees should be charged by the formal sector so that they can bridge the gap of price difference between formal and informal

items.statement: Expects substantial volume increase as CPCB enforces stricter compliance, driving more material to formal recyclers
items.quote: I am very, very positive about the kind of strictness the CPCB is now demonstrating and using that, rather asking producers to work on the lines of the rules. It's much higher than all the lines strictly, I am very positive.

items.statement: 100% procurement directly from end-users and producers (MNCs, Class A); no imports or market purchases
items.quote: We don't import anything, ne. We don't procure from the market, two. But we directly take it from our end user, which are inclusive of the multinational Company's user admin and the producer board.

items.statement: Revenue mix includes recycled material, refurbished goods, EPR fees, data destruction; mix broadly stable quarter to quarter
items.quote: revenue from operations, it includes both, or rather 3, recycled material, refurbished, EPR fees, and of course, the data restriction service charges. So, it's a combination of all four.

items.statement: Government announced Rs 15,000 crore MSME fund for environment-friendly practices; could leverage Rs 60,000 crore investment and reduce next expansion capex from Rs 50 crore to Rs 37.5 crore
items.value: Rs 15,000 crore grant; Rs 60,000 crore expected investment

items.quote: we are accumulating cash and we will assess the requirement of further investment in plant machineries and the capacity, which will be sometime in September 25, we will evaluate based on the performance of March '25 and half of the year of the next year.

items.statement: Headcount ~50 employees; will add more as capacity utilization increases
items.quote: Now we have about 50. And with the capacity as utilization increases, more number will be added according to the requirement.

items.statement: Implemented remedial measures from past fire incident in both old and new facilities

items.quote: the generation level of e-waste is very, very high in India. It's close to about 4 to 5 million metric tons.

items.statement: Differentiates via full compliance focus vs formality; premium services command higher fees from MNCs

items.statement: TERRA partnership (120 global members) expanding client access and business gradually
items.quote: the addition with the TERRA and TERRA's other members is expanding our wings and is adding to gradually the business.

items.statement: No current plans to monetize proprietary technology; focus remains on core recycling operations
items.quote: one more addition of Ecoreco and deviating from the core action of recycling is not right now on the consideration.

items.quote: those expenses are purely incurred by another Company of mine personally, but not from the Eco Recycling Limited because it's not profitable for Eco Recycling to do that.

items.statement: Gold loan AUM growth guided at 15% for FY25

items.statement: Consolidated AUM growth guided at 15% for FY25
items.quote: 15%. The others will grow in a similar way, other non -gold like vehicles affordable housing, etcetera -- during the first quarter...

items.statement: Targeting 5% ROA over next 4-5 quarters
items.quote: We are targeting 5% ROA. It takes a few quarters to reach that level.

items.statement: Gold loan demand better compared to same period last year, seasonal variations expected
items.quote: Compared to the same period last year, we see the demand is better.

items.statement: Standalone AUM INR31,035 crores, up 20.6% YoY; Consolidated AUM INR44,932 crores, up 21% YoY
items.quote: The stand -alone AUM stands at INR31,035 crores, gr owing by 20.6% year-on-year. With a consolidated AUM of INR44,932 crores, it is an increase of 21% over the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Home Finance AUM INR1,587 crores, up 32% YoY

items.quote: So we can say that margins at least should remain stable now? Bindu A. L: Yes

items.statement: Asirvad Net NPA 1.36%, CRAR 21.81%
items.quote: Net NPA stands at 1.36%, and the CRAR currently stands at 21.81%.

items.quote: INR71 crores write-off. It is already disclosed.

items.statement: Added 4.21 lakh new gold loan customers, outstanding customers up to 24.5 lakhs from 23.76 lakhs
items.quote: During the quarter, we were able to add 4.21 lakh new customers and the number of outstanding customers has gone up to 24.5 lakhs from 23.76 lakhs.

items.quote: Up to INR1 lakh, 42%; INR1 lakh to INR2 lakh, 23%; above INR2 lakh, 35%.

items.statement: Competitor ban impact not significant, business distributed among many players including banks
items.quote: The ban on competition, I don't think the effect is significant. Because even if it is there, it is getting distributed to so many players. And many of these are going to banks.

items.statement: Import duty on gold cut from 15% to 6% in Union Budget, may moderate domestic gold prices
items.quote: The union budget slashed the import duty on gold from 15% to 6%. As a result, there is an expectation that domestic gold prices may see a moderation leading to higher retail sales.

items.statement: Raised US$300 million from dollar bonds in May 2024 for business growth
items.quote: As you may be aware, we have raised US$300 million from dollar bonds in May '24 for business growth.

items.quote: With regard to liquidity, cash and cas h equivalents was at INR5,383 crores on a consolidated basis and undrawn bank line was INR3,530 crores as on 30th September.

items.statement: Interim dividend of INR1 per share declared for Q1
items.quote: Considering the consistent earnings, Board has declared an interim dividend of INR1 for this quarter.

items.quote: There are some challenges in collections because of farmer agitation in Punjab, general election, etc. And connected with that, there were some rumors spread about non-waivers. items.statement: Revenue target of INR 2,900 crore by March 2027 with 16% CAGR over three years remains intact
items.quote: So, regarding the guidance what we have given earlier was of reaching the target of INR 2,900 by March 27 which will remain intact.

items.statement: EBITDA margin expected to be maintained between 16% to 17% for the rest of the year
items.quote: We are quite confident in terms of the margins which we will keep intact between 16% to 17%.

items.quote: And if you see for the whole year basis that is '24 -'25 as the full year , growth is projected to be in single digits.

items.statement: Demand slowdown across all tiers due to elections and heatwave; improvement expected from H2 FY25
items.quote: We anticipate that from Q3 onwards the demand situation should improve.

items.quote: If you look at our project bank size vis-a-vis December and if I compare December ‘23 with June ’24, you will find that there has been an increase of something like 15% -20% on our project bank

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin declined 150 bps to 17.5% due to lower fixed-cost absorption and higher discounts
items.quote: EBITDA margins for the current quarter stood at INR 17.5 as against 19% in Q1 FY 24, registering a decrease of 150 basis points.

items.statement: Power and fuel cost expected to remain at 1.3-1.4% of sales in FY25
items.quote: As a percentage of sale, it is 1.3%, 1.4%.

items.quote: Our budget for regular and routine capex for FY 2024-2025 is INR 25.40 crore, encompassing essential upgrades in our Sanitaryware and Faucetware plants, including machinery replacement, customer touchpoint enhancements and IT

items.quote: I am pleased to report that the plant is running efficiently after the ramp-up period. With adequate inventory levels, we have optimized our production strategy to achieve an ideal balance between production and inventory resulting in faucetware capacity utilization of 84% in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Sanitaryware plant utilization at 76% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: In Q1 FY 25, our sanitary ware plant achieved a capacity utilization rate of 76%, reflecting our balanced approach to production and inventory management.

items.quote: Due diligence is ongoing to secure the remaining land, which is anticipated to be completed by September 2024.

items.statement: Premium segment 44%, mid 32%, entry 24% of sales in Q1 FY25; largely unchanged from Q1 FY24
items.quote: So, premium is 44% in Q1 FY25 and in Q1 FY24 it was 45%, mid was 32%, in the previous quarter it was 31% and entry it is 24% in Q1 FY25 as against 24% in Q1 FY24.

items.statement: New product development accounted for 32% of total sales in Q1 FY25
items.quote: New product development accounted for 32% of the total sales in this last quarter.

items.statement: Weighted average gas cost reduced to INR 31.64/cubic meter in Q1 FY25 from INR 33.91 in Q1 FY24 due to higher GAIL drawal (86% vs 78%)
items.quote: The overall weighted average gas cost in Q1 was at INR 31.64 as against INR 33.91 in Q1 FY24 which is significantly lower as compared to the industry standards.

items.statement: Net working capital days reduced from 72 to 66 days; inventory days 75, receivables 28, payables stretched to 37 days
items.quote: Consequently, the net working capital days were reduced from 72 days to 66 days in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Cash and cash equivalents INR 864 crore as on June 30, 2024, up 14.4% YoY
items.quote: As on June 30, 2024, our cash and cash equivalents stood at INR 864 crore, marking an increase of INR 109 crore or 14.4% compared to the corresponding previous quarters.

items.statement: Dividend trend of healthy payouts to continue; FY24 dividend INR 60 per share amounting to INR 78 crore

items.statement: B2C sales 64% of revenue, B2B projects 36%; project mix slightly up from 35%
items.quote: As of now, the total project to retail ratio, 64:36. It was earlier something like 65:35.

items.quote: Regarding sales distribution, Tier 1 cities accounted for 35% of total sales, Tier 2 cities for 22%, and Tier 3 cities led with 43% of total sales.

items.quote: The figures are not very readily available but what we generally estimate is that the sanitaryware industry size of the organized sector would be INR 5,000 for sanitaryware and INR 8,000 for faucetware. The unorganized for the sanitaryware industry would be something like INR 4,000 crore and faucetware would be INR 6,000 crore.

items.statement: Pollution board becoming stricter on emissions and effluents, challenging unorganized players in Morbi belt
items.quote: Also because of the fact that the pollution board has started becoming more and more strict in respect of the kind of emissions and effluents which are being discharged.

items.statement: Retailer loyalty program enrolled over 20,000 retailers with 3 lakh+ invoices; 37% of INR 217 crore retail sales eligible for rewards
items.quote: Since launching the Retailer Loyalty Program in FY 2022-2023, we have enrolled over 20,000 retailers and accumulated more than 3 lakh invoices on the application.

items.statement: Advertising spend INR 11.5 crore in Q1 FY25 vs INR 11 crore in Q1 FY24, in line with FY25 projection
items.quote: In Q1 FY25, we have spent INR 11.5 crore as compared with INR 11 crore in Q1 of FY24 towards publicity, which is in line with our projected spending for FY25.

items.statement: Demand softness expected to continue in Q2 FY25; recovery anticipated from Q3 FY25
items.quote: We anticipate that the improvement in the demand condition will start from the second half of the year.

items.quote: With our growth levers in pace and despite a muted Q1, we anticipate improved consumer sentiments in second half of the year. This will drive positive growth for FY '25 with an overall consolidated growth expected to be in double digits.

items.statement: Q2 FY25 estimated flattish; Q3 and Q4 expected to show growth
items.period: Q2 FY25, Q3 FY25, Q4 FY25
items.quote: On the organic level, we'll be growing, okay, since quarter 1 was muted. Quarter 2, we estimate it would be flattish. In quarter 3 and quarter 4, we are expecting there will be a growth perspective.

items.statement: Operating profit margin sustainable at 18-19% for FY25
items.quote: Operating profit looks sustainable at 18% to 19%.

items.quote: With an encouraging response to our July '24 trade show for Spring/Summer '25 collection, including Killer, Easies, Kraus and Junior Killer, we are confident in achieving the robust growth in the coming months.

items.quote: Yes, other would be non-apparels.

items.quote: We are just initially starting, that we will try out 3-4 stores first, because we don't know, Kids is very new for us also. items.quote: For the quarter gone by, we saw the LCL business increased by almost 6% compared to the previous quarter. We also witnessed the FCL business up 9% as compared to the last year.

items.quote: So, we have on the utilization index, we have each container utilized 4% better as compared to last year. We have also been able to increase the share of 40 -feet container by almost 9%.

items.quote: all these things combined have allowed us to improve the margins in the business and therefore that has contributed to the positive growth in EBITDA, which on a consolidated basis is about 34% compared to the previous quarter on the back of 13% expansion in the consolidated revenue.

items.quote: We have been noticing that for the month of July as well as August, the volumes have been stronger and we see a similar demand outlook for September and October, and therefore our general belief is that market should see continued sustained recovery in trade volumes until the end of the year.

items.statement: Express business EBITDA up 33% QoQ; operational efficiencies sustained
items.quote: On the Express business, we have seen that operational efficiencies which had been achieved in early part of this calendar year have sustained and that has allowed us to continually improve the operating margins in the express business, and as an outcome of t hat, the EBITDA for the quarter is almost 33% higher than the previous quarter.

items.statement: Contract Logistics revenue up 13% QoQ and 22% YoY; business diversified across chemical, e-commerce, auto
items.quote: we have increased almost 13% as compared to the previous quarter, we have increased almost 22% compared to the previous year, and this is primarily on the back of renewed contracts and now we are expanding in other domains.

items.statement: Expect sequential improvement to continue for remaining quarters of FY25; no specific volume guidance given
items.quote: we have seen sequential improvement, and we expect the same sequential improvements to continue for the remainder of the year on quarterly basis.

items.statement: Target to grow faster than market in both LCL and FCL for FY25
items.quote: we would continue to expand market share, which means that we would grow faster than the market in both LCL and FCL business for FY25.

items.quote: Apart from that in Allcargo ECU we do not have any large CAPEX requirements, only maintenance CAPEX, etc., which is expected. So, the summary is we expect the debt to go down from here, not go up.

items.statement: Working capital expanded due to higher freight rates; DSOs range-bound and controlled

Deepal Shah: I did mention earlier also to rub it in again our DSO have been range-bound, they haven't gone

items.quote: we believe the freight rate should remain stable or more or less range -bound until the end o f the year. Now, beyond that, there is no visibility at this point in time. But typically, around the Chinese New Year around February, there is then a little bit of a slackness, there could be some decline as well.

items.statement: Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay volumes could double in 9-12 months after new leadership appointment
items.quote: we appointed a new leadership team in Argentina, Uruguay and Paraguay. Three markets where we felt we were underrepresented and now we have a very strong commercial team which has come onboard toge ther as one team, and we expect that the volumes in these three countries could potentially double from the current levels in next nine to 12 months.

items.statement: Cost savings from standardization and outsourcing from US to Mexico; automation drive to offset inflation
items.quote: We have achieved lot of cost savings as discussed in the past calls through standardization and then outsourcing of operations from the United States into Mex ico, and we continue to evaluate other such opportunities on how we could standardize operations and then outsource to reduce costs. And the second opportunity in that category is to continue to drive automation, because standardization also

items.quote: Sandeep joined us as Chief Operating Officer last year in the GATI business and there is clearly bee n a strong outcome. We have had senior commercial leaders join in the company recently and we remain confident that they would steer company towards some future growth. items.quote: We don't see a si gnificant upward or downward revision in the margin profile. It should sustain from a two to three-year horizon. items.quote: the biggest challenge is on the supply side, with the whole red sea crisis, the additional turnaround transit time, also the US ports have been congested. items.statement: LCL yield (gross profit per CBM) range-bound; FCL yield (gross profit per TEU) volatile with freight rates

items.statement: Revenue CAGR guidance of 12-14% over three years to FY28 with double-digit EBITDA margin by FY28
items.quote: we would like to keep our guidance of 12 % to 14% CAGR in revenue growth and EBITDA of 10% to 12% by FY28 if we will -- we are optimistic about achieving that.

items.statement: Expects double-digit adjusted EBITDA margin by end of FY25 and sustained in FY26
items.quote: I think as we go into summer and spring season, we are optimistic about hitting a double digit EBITDA, I guess by the end of th is year, and the next year should be in line with those double digit as well.

items.statement: Order flow much greater than last year; growth plan on track across US, UK, Europe, Australia, Japan

items.statement: Order book is as per plan and thoroughly on track
items.quote: Order book is as per our plan. I think we are on track, thoroughly on track.

items.statement: Consolidated adjusted EBITDA grew 18.8% YoY to INR100.4 crores; margin in line with revenue growth
