items.statement: Indonesia facility ramped up to full production to cater to Asian market and export orders
items.quote: To further support our operations, our Indonesia facility has been ramped up to full production and will cater to the Asian market and export orders.

items.statement: New Vanavate facility will replace two Mulund factories on leasehold land, expected operational before end of year
items.quote: The new facility will replace our two existing factories in Mulund which a re currently operated on leasehold land. It is expected that the new facility will be operational before the end of this year.

items.statement: Currently at more than 85%-90% capacity utilization, technically even 100%
items.quote: Because we are now at more than 85% -90% capacity utilization. If you look at it technically probably even 100% capacity utilization.

items.statement: Solid margin improvement driven by stable raw material environment and favorable product mix
items.quote: Moving on to our Margin Performance, we reported solid improvement this quarter driven by a stable raw material environment and favo urable product mix.

items.statement: European entity restored gross margin to expected 45%-47% range after inflation-related decline
items.quote: So, this is a continuing gross margin as what we should be in normal range at 45% to 47% gross margin. Our European entity, 2 years ago we had sort of not corrected for inflation in time and given the market situation at the time , the cost increases were uncertain, what would be the way forward. So, we had a decline in gross margin from the historical average. We have now restored that gross marg

items.statement: Global Ingredients gross margin sustainable at 35% ballpark, now in positive EBITDA territory
items.quote: I think the Global Ingredient business in terms of gross margin has been kind of in that 35% ballpark sustainable margin level like any other specialty chemical. And as you see from this year's first quarter result, it is in a positive EBITDA territory.

items.statement: Early signs of some raw material prices going up and shortages in natural products, but contracts and inventory expected to counter volatility
items.quote: I think there are early signs of some raw material prices going up. There are also some shortages or some natural products where there are concerns. We are in our business always looking at higher inventory to offset such variations. We expect that our con tracts and inventory will be sufficient to counter this volatility.

items.statement: If further adverse raw material movements, will pass on additional cost to customers as customary
items.quote: If there are further adverse movements in raw materials, we will try and pass on that additional cost to our customers as is customary.

items.statement: Flavour segment revenue grew 57% YoY (excluding NuTaste divestment), driven by market revival and increased engagement with existing customers
items.quote: Moving on to the Flavour segment, we experienced significant growth during this quarter with a 57% increase in revenue year-on-year. The strong performance was primarily driven by revival in the markets and an increased engagement with our existing customers.

items.statement: Global Ingredients segment demonstrated strong turnaround, revenue Rs. 19 crore vs Rs. 13 crore last year, EBIT +0.3 vs -3.1
items.quote: The Global Ingredients revenue was Rs. 19 crore in this Quarter 1 as against as against Rs. 13 crore last year and the EBIT number is (+0.3) as against (-3.1) last year.

items.statement: Top five customers contribute less than 15% of total revenue
items.quote: It's less than 15% of the total.

items.statement: More than 95% of business is repeat business year-on-year, 90% proprietary with strong stickiness
items.quote: But in terms of our stickiness, in terms of our business more than 95% of our business is repeat business year-on-year and if I take even beyond 5 years, beyond ten years, almost (+90%) of our business is repeat business.

items.statement: China Plus One de-risking benefiting Global Ingredients, structural long-term trend not 1-2 years
items.quote: I think on the Global Ingredients that is to my mind structural change that movement away from China dependency, it's not 1- or 2-years trend, it's a longer-term trend and we will benefit from that.

items.statement: Inventory replenishment of over Rs. 100 crore in May-June due to fire, payments due this quarter causing temporary net debt increase
items.quote: The debt levels actually are rising because the inventory losses in Vashivali factory of over Rs. 100 crore. We have replenished those inventories in May and June and those payments will be due in this quarter.

items.statement: Peak net debt expected around Rs. 600-620 crore, insurance recovery expected to offset
items.quote: I think our peak net debt as you mentioned could be around Rs. 600-620 crore, that range. Obviously, we have over Rs. 100 crore of inventory which we have replenished in this quarter and there will be an effect of that to the working capital cycle. We are expecting and hopeful that we get a cover from the insurance at least partly if not fully. So, I would still think of Rs. 600 crore maximum net

items.statement: If insurance money comes back, will reduce debt by about Rs. 100 crore immediately
items.quote: If the insurance money comes back, we will reduce our debt by about Rs. 100 crore immediate basis.

items.statement: Entered Share Purchase Agreement to divest majority stake in NuTaste Food and Drink Labs, retaining 40% strategic stake
items.quote: We have excluded NuTaste Food a nd Drink Labs from the figures as the Company has entered into a Share Purchase Agreement to divest its majority stake. We will continue to hold a 40% stake as a strategic partner in this business.

items.statement: Fragrance division posted 7% YoY growth, overall revenue grew 11.3% YoY despite fire impact
items.quote: Despite this we achieved an 11.3 % Q1 FY25 Concall Transcript year-on-year revenue growth in Quarter 1, with our fragrance division posting 7% year-on-year

items.statement: Exceptional loss of Rs. 120 crore net of tax recorded due to fire, insurance expected to fully offset financial losses
items.quote: As part of the financial impact on account of the fire, we have recorded an exceptional loss of Rs. 120 crore net of tax during the quarter which includes damages to plant and machinery building and inventory. As we have mentioned earlier in our comprehensive insurance coverage, all risk policy also includes protection for loss of profit. This insurance we expect will fully offset the financial lo

items.statement: Targets ~10% revenue growth and ~18% EBITDA margin for FY25
items.quote: We expect that the current year should be a much better year as compared to the last year. We should be on target to achieve close to about 10% of incremental revenue over the last year. And the operating profit should also be significantly higher than what we had reported last year.

items.statement: India CRAMS revenue target Rs 325-350 crore for FY25
items.quote: So, Tarang, what we're expecting is that in the current year, we should be closer to about Rs. 325 crores to Rs. 350 crores in terms of the revenue coming out of CRAMS that is what our target is.

items.statement: Swiss entity revenue expected to exceed CHF 200 million in FY25
items.quote: I am extremely confident that Switzerland is going to grow even beyond CHF200 million for the activity to take for sure.

items.statement: French entity EBITDA loss expected at negative €5 million for FY25
items.quote: As far as the French entity is concerned, yes, I think, based upon the current forecast, the impact on the EBITDA should be about negative €5 million for the current financial year.

items.statement: Q1 EBITDA margin below 18% target; expects run rate from Q2
items.quote: Yes, I mean eventually, for the remaining 3 quarters, we need to be above that in order to achieve the annual target

items.statement: Netherlands wool grease cost renegotiated down ~35%; benefit from Q3
items.quote: So, what we have been able to successfully do in the immediate past was to renegotiate this contract with the existing suppliers wherein the prices have been renegotiated by almost 35% as compared to what the earlier contract was.

items.statement: Goodwill amortisation reduced from Rs 45 crore to ~Rs 6 crore per annum from Q1 FY25
items.quote: So, what we are now saying is that the goodwill will be written off over a period of 99 years, which would mean that the hit to the P&L would be close to about Rs. 6 crores per annum instead of the earlier Rs. 45 crores per annum.

items.statement: India CRAMS revenue up 114% YoY to Rs 82 crore in Q1 after EDQM clearance
items.quote: After that, we saw an uptick in the India CRAMS revenue, which increased substantially as compared to Q1 of last year. So, from Rs. 38 crores, it has increased to Rs. 82 crores, which is almost 114% increase.

items.statement: Swiss entity had ~CHF 9.8 million orders deferred from Q1 to later quarters
items.quote: On the negative side, there was unfortunately about 9.8 million worth of orders, which according to the customers' requirements had to be deferred to the next quarters as compared to Q1.

items.statement: Netherlands revenue down 16% YoY in Q1 due to lower vitamin D analogue sales
items.quote: As far as our Dutch entity was concerned, there was a dip in revenue by about 16% as compared to Q1 of last year. And that was largely on account of lower sales of the vitamin D analogues.

items.statement: Large order portfolio across drug substance, drug product and specialty gives confidence to meet FY targets
items.quote: We were having a large number of purchase order in our global portfolio, in drug substance or product or product activities, which give us a very high confidence that although the third quarter was a bit disappointed, we were able to match our targets by the end of the fiscal year.

items.statement: India sites (Bavla+Naroda) can do ~Rs 1,000 crore revenue on existing asset base
items.quote: So, now because the changes that have been made between the Bavla and the Naroda site, including the operational excellence that has been brought in both sites put together can do a revenue on the existing asset base of close to about Rs. 1,000 crores.

items.statement: Swiss entity at ~85% utilisation; can go to 90-95%
items.quote: As far as the Swiss entity is concerned, currently, it is running at roughly about 85% in terms of the capacity. So, it can go a bit higher to maybe around 90% to 95%.

items.statement: Maintenance capex ~CHF 17-18 million per year; no significant growth capex expected
items.quote: And essentially our any spend on the CAPEX on the maintenance side is roughly about 17 million to 18 million, and that is something that we will have to keep incurring going into the future.

items.statement: Net debt CHF 164 million as of 30 June 2024
items.quote: So, the net debt stood at about CHF164 million as of 30th of June.

items.statement: Netherlands Q1 mix 60% cholesterol (low margin) vs historical 55% vitamin D analogues
items.quote: If we talk about this particular quarter, roughly around 60% was contributed by cholesterol and the rest was contributed by the vitamin D analogues. Historically, what we have seen is that the ratio is about 55% vitamin D analogues and about 45% cholesterol.

items.statement: Swiss entity revenue split ~55-60% development, 40-45% commercial historically
items.quote: So, at the Swiss entity, if you take a ballpark roughly about 55% to 60% comes from development work, this has been the historical trend and about 45-odd percent is what comes from commercial.

items.statement: India Bavla site received EDQM certification in Feb 2024; US FDA inspection measures completed
items.quote: We have already cleared the EDQM inspection. And post that even the U.S. FDA inspection, we have already taken the measures in order to reduce the COGS at that side.

items.statement: French facility EBITDA loss €2.5 million in Q1; expects turnaround from Q3
items.quote: We had a negative impact of about €2.5 million in Q1. And even the operations have begun from June of this year where the revenue was about €1.2 million for Q1. So, what we are expecting is that the revenues will progressively keep on increasing quarter-over-quarter. And while there would still be a loss in Q2, we would start seeing a turnaround from Q3 onward where we would see the losses coming

items.statement: Targets 25-26% EBITDA margin in 2-3 years
items.quote: And all of our overseas entities, we do expect that we would be able to reach the 25%, 26% margin in the next 2 to 3 years' time.

items.statement: Contracts renegotiated to Swiss franc to match cost base; hedging on rolling basis
items.quote: Because most of our costs are in Swiss franc. So, to the extent that we can have a matching against the cost in terms of the revenue, we are trying to do that to the extent possible and then whatever exposure is open in terms of the revenue, that is something that we are hedging.

items.statement: Dollar cash balance reduced to $20-30 million from $120 million to limit FX impact
items.quote: What we have tried to do with many of our customers used to renegotiate our contracts in Swiss francs, which means that the balance sitting on the U.S. dollar account is not much at max, it might be $20 million, $30 million.

items.statement: Reorganised Carbogen Amcis into Drug Substance, Drug Products and Specialty from 1 July 2024
items.quote: So, now we look at our global activities into 3 different activities, Drug Substance, as I mentioned, Drug Products and Specialty, which is our product business. Thanks to the 3 organizations, we will leverage more, as I said, accurate strategy for each business segment.

items.statement: Gross margin improved 220 bps YoY to 47.1% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Gross margin for the quarter stood at 47.1% up by 220 basis points year on year as higher contribution from retail led to favourable product sales.

items.statement: Retail EBITDA margin at 16.37% in Q1 FY25, on track for 17-19% target
items.quote: This quarter, we have -- in retail, we have done EBITDA margin of 16.37%.

items.statement: Distribution gross margin improved but EBITDA margin dropped to 0.8% due to expense corrections
items.quote: Distribution sales was not as regard to last quarter, the sales was less co mpared to last quarter this year. And there was a margin improvement in distribution in the gross margin. But the expenses and there was a lot of correction that has been done in this quarter. So that has led to the drop in the margin

items.statement: Expect retail growth of 7-8% for FY25 after Q1 de-growth
items.quote: So I think we will be closing this financial year with a growth of around 7% to 8%.

items.statement: Expect festive season demand recovery in Q2 and Q3 FY25
items.quote: And since this year the puja is in the first week of October, so the demand will rise in the month of September and in Diwali in month of October. So we think that after this muted sales for the first quarter, we will have a good demand for the festive season.

items.statement: Plan to open 25 new COCO stores in FY25, 8-9 already opened
items.quote: We have planned for opening of 25 stores. We are in that plan. We've already opened around 8 to 9 stores. So by this year end, we'll be opening 25 new stores.

items.quote: No, we have planned to renovate around 20 stores. Already we have around 7 to 8 stores already renovated. And we are in the plan. That plan is on.

items.quote: Around INR4 crores to INR5 crores.

items.statement: 136 inactive stores not included in total count
items.quote: Now I think the inactive stores would be how much? Just a minute. We have 136 inactive stores.

items.quote: Quarterly performance: On quarterly performance, revenue from operations for Q1 FY '25 was at INR153.9 crores as against INR158.0 crores same period last year, down by 2.6% year on year.

items.statement: Same-store sales degrowth of 5-6% in value terms currently vs pre-COVID 4-5% growth
items.quote: Generally, now the trend is that in the same store we are not seeing any volume growth or a sales growth. There is a degrowth around 5% to 6% in the value.

items.statement: Retail contribution 56.8%, distribution 33.4%, other/B2B 9.8% in Q1 FY25

This includes 228 company -owned COO stores and 650 sto res under the franchisee model. Our distribution business contributed 33.4% to revenue in Q1 FY '25.

items.statement: Sports footwear grew 5-6% YoY, contributes ~20% of retail sales
items.quote: Sports, we have seen a growth of around 5% to 6% has been sports sale. And athleisure, we have just launched -- athleisure means garments. We have just launched in the Independence Day week. And it's a good response we are seeing.

items.quote: We have taken it in a very small way. Aro und 50 lakhs of inventory we have taken for this introduction and we have launched it in around 40 to 45 stores.

items.statement: May reduce MRP on Khadim mother brand lower price points after festive season
items.quote: So maybe we have to take some correction in the MRP for the Khadim brand. But that will be done after the festive season. In the next spring-summer season, we will try to reduce some of the MRP in the mother brand.

items.quote: It's a mixture of both the things.

items.statement: Average bill value INR 940-945 in Q1 FY25, stable vs last year
items.quote: It was the same last year. In the same range, 900, 920. It was like that. Now it was around 940, 945.

items.statement: Conversion rate improved to 65-70% from pre-COVID 40% due to lower footfall of assured buyers
items.quote: Now the conversion ratio is high because compared to last, when pre-COVID it was around 40% but now it's around 65% to 70%.

items.statement: Punjab government receivable of INR 32 crores expected recovery in FY25
items.quote: It's around INR32 crores.

items.statement: Distributor credit cycle ~45 days, focusing on working capital improvement
items.quote: Distributors' credit cycle is around 45 days. And we are trying to squeeze as much money in the distribution business.

items.statement: De-merger process awaiting NCLT approval, targeting completion by Nov-Dec 2024
items.quote: So we can have the de -merger in the third quarter, maybe in the month of November or December.

items.statement: BIS implementation extended to end of CY2024 for small suppliers (<INR 50 cr turnover)
items.quote: The government still has given an extension till the end of this year. I mean, the normal year not financial year. So after that, let's see what the government says for the smaller suppliers whose t urnover is less, INR50 crores and below

items.statement: Holding market share despite macro challenges; unorganized sector pressure remains short-term
items.quote: We cannot say that we are losing market share. But when there is a festive like Independence Day, in the last week of Independence Day, we have got good sales numbers. So whenever there is a footfall in the market, we are getting the sales.

items.statement: Post de-merger, manufacturing/distribution staff move to new entity; management oversees both
items.quote: Specifically, the manufacturing and the distribution sales people will go to the resulting entity. And the management will look at both the companies. So there will be no new introduction in that company at the management level.

items.statement: Franchisee operating cost increased post-COVID due to lower sales and higher rentals/salaries
items.quote: Because the sales have reduced, that's why the cost has increased. Cost as a percentage has increased. Indrajit Chaudhuri: And also with the inflation coming in, the cost of rentals, the salaries, the other costs has increased

items.quote: Coming to the order book position, our total order book stands at 25,231.29 crore as on 30th June 2024.

items.statement: P17 Alpha project order value enhanced to Rs 21,000 crore from initial Rs 19,293 crore; Rs 14,392 crore remaining to be executed.
items.quote: Now, that means the order value of P17 Alpha is 21,000 crore. Of these, 21,000 crore, 15% of the order value comprises of Base and Depot spares i.e. 85% of this 21,000 crore is the ship construction cost and 15% is the Base and Depot spares.

items.statement: Targeting 25-30% revenue growth in FY25 and similar growth in FY26; FY26 likely to be peak revenue year.
items.quote: Last time also I mentioned that we will deliver growth between 25 to 30%.

items.statement: Aim to maintain PAT margins of 7.5-8% on yearly basis despite revenue growth; quarterly fluctuations possible due to project maturity.
items.quote: The PAT margin will maintain a minimum of 7.50% to 8% on a yearly basis, we can assume there will be marginal fluctuations up or down a quarter to quarter depending upon the project maturity, but we'll maintain a PAT margin of a 7.50% to 8%.

items.quote: by the end of this calendar year, I repeat by the end of this calendar year, our ship building capacity will enhance from 20 to 24 ships.

items.statement: Near-term pipeline includes Navy RFPs for 2 Multi-purpose Vessels (~Rs 1,000-1,200 crore), 5 Next Gen Survey Vessels (~Rs 3,000 crore), 22 Water Jet FACs (~Rs 2,200 crore) and Coast Guard RFPs for 22 Interceptor Boats (~Rs 1,200 crore) and

items.statement: P17 Alpha: Ship 1 at ~75% progress, delivery mid CY2025; Ship 2 at ~62%, delivery Feb 2026; Ship 3 at ~50%, delivery Aug-Sep 2026.

items.quote: We intend completing this project that means delivery of the balance 3 ships, all the three ships by the first quarter of FY26.

items.statement: Anti-Submarine Shallow Water Craft (8 ships): Ship 1 at ~90% progress, delivery in 3 months; subsequent ships at 65%, 55%; project completion by FY27.
items.quote: As far as this project is concerned, we intend completing this project by FY27 that means delivery of all the 8 ships.

items.statement: Next Generation OPV (4 ships): First two ships at ~25% progress; production started on last two ships; contract signed March 2023.
items.quote: The progress is good and the first two ships have already touched around 25% of construction and we have already started production of the last two ships also.

items.statement: Four export contracts signed in last 3 months: 4 Multipurpose Vessels (option for 4 more) for European client, 1 Ocean-going Tug, 1 Advanced 1000 M3 Hopper Dredger, 3 Fast Patrol Boats; total export orders ~Rs 750 crore.
items.quote: Among these, in the last 2-3 months, we have concluded the four contracts, the Multi-purpose Vessel contract for four ships was concluded with the European client and there is an option for enhancing this quantity by another four.

items.statement: Ship repair revenue share increased from ~1% to ~5% over last two years; Portable Steel Bridges turnover grew from Rs 60 crore to Rs 140 crore; delivered India's largest 150-passenger electric ferry to West Bengal; won order for 13 Advanced
items.quote: In case of ship repairs, we started in a very modest fashion around two years back and at the point of time around 1% or just about 1% of our revenue was being generated through ship repair and over the last two years we have enhanced it almost 5%.

items.statement: No let-up in government pace post-elections; Next Generation Corvette RFP issued ahead of DAP 30-month timeline; 64 of 66 Navy ships and 100% Coast Guard ships built in Indian yards.
items.quote: In our appreciations, there has been no letup in a pace. Since you specifically mentioned the next generation corvettes, as per the DAP from the time the AON is obtained to RFP, 30 months' time is there and the Government has issued the tender ahead of that thirty month.

items.statement: Declared L1 for DRDO Acoustic Research Vessel, GSI Coastal Reference Vessel, and two West Bengal Advanced Hybrid Service projects; contract negotiations in progress, expected signing in 3-6 months.
items.quote: We have also been declared L1 for a project for the DRDO Naval Physiological and Oceanographic Laboratory for an Acoustic Research Vessel, for the Geological Survey of India to coastal reference vessel and for the Government of West Bengal, 2 projects for advanced hybrid service.

items.statement: Capacity enhancement initiated: one shipbuilding unit completely revamped to raise concurrent capacity to 24 by end CY2024; three dry docks leased from Kolkata Port Trust; PPP model with private yards for concurrent construction.

items.statement: Bangladesh orders constitute only 1.2% of order book; no impact seen on execution as preparatory activities ongoing in India and delivery lead time ~2 years.

items.statement: Expects alternate revenue streams to deliver positive results from Q3 FY25 onwards
items.quote: However, alternate revenue streams are vigorously being followed up and we expect to see positive results from Q3 onwards.

items.quote: So total revenue is Rs. 86.01 crores as compared to Rs. 100.63 crores, that is down by 14%. items.quote: We don't see any reason to hit the capital markets again in next 2, 3 years' time frame.

items.statement: Organic cash flows expected to turn positive from FY26 onwards
items.quote: Yes, definitely, I think by next year, organics should start delivering positive cash flows, organic division from FY '26 onwards.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 revenue growth guidance of 30% on FY24 base of INR850 crores
items.quote: The overall guidance that we had given was that we will grow from about INR850-odd crores that we did for the full fiscal '24 by 30%. So, that guidance continues to remain.

items.statement: FY25 seat addition guidance of 40,000 seats to reach 135,000 total seats
items.quote: We had, last earnings call, we had given a capacity addition of 40,000 seats. We had ended the year at 95,000 seats. We are looking to add about 40,000 additional to reach 1,35,000 seats total.

items.statement: Full-year FY25 EBITDA margin improvement guidance of 1.5 percentage points maintained
items.quote: That said, we stick to our guidance of 1.5% for the year because we will keep on adding new centers and cities to our portfolio. And hence, there could be a short-term impact. But however, we continue with our guidance of 1.5% for the year as a whole.

items.statement: FY25 capex guidance similar to FY24 at around INR142 crores
items.quote: We had given a similar guidance on the capex as was last year. So last year was around in INR142 crores. We gave a similar guidance on the capex for current year.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 capex cash outflow of INR35 crores
items.quote: On the capex side, we have done an operating cash outflow of around INR35 crores on the capex.

items.statement: Operational seats reached 100,398 across 169 centers as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: As of June 30, 2024, our total operational seats stand at 100,398 and we have 169 operational centers.

items.statement: Pipeline of 11,640 seats under fit-out and 15,688 seats under LOI for total visibility of 127,726 seats
items.quote: Currently, we have 11,640 seats under fit-out and letter of intent in place for 15,688 additional seats, providing us with strong visibility on achieving our growth targets.

items.statement: Construction and fit-out segment revenue grew 55% YoY to INR67 crores with healthy order pipeline
items.quote: Our construction and fit-out projects, which encompasses our design and build business, have shown remarkable performance with a growth rate of 55%, culminating in a revenue of INR67 crores. This segment is gaining significant traction, buoyed by a healthy order pipe line and favourable market outlook

items.statement: Reported EBITDA margin improved 1.8% QoQ to 30.7% in Q1 FY25
items.quote: As you can see, our EBITDA margin has improved from 28.9% to around 30.7%, which in itself is a 1.8% improvement quarter-on-quarter.

items.statement: IGAAP equivalent EBITDA margin at 11.5% in Q1 FY25, up 249% YoY
items.quote: Our operating EBITDA on IGAAP Equivalent basis stood at INR30 crores, which is showing a robust growth of 249% year-on-year. Our margins are at 11.5%.

items.statement: Construction and fit-out gross margin improved to 16% from 15.5%
items.quote: In fact, we have slightly improved our margins on construction business at the gross level. So it was around 15.5%, and now has increased to 16% and thereabouts.

items.statement: New seats sold at 3-5% YoY escalation; existing portfolio sees 3-8% annual escalation based on cohort size
items.quote: The new seats which are being sold are being sold at 3% to 5% year-on-year escalation as compared to the earlier seats. Similarly, what we see is annual escalation, which in our case ranges from about - on average about 5% for smaller cohorts between 5% to 8% and for larger cohorts between 3% to 5%.

items.statement: Signed demand contracts for 11,000 new seats in Q1 FY25, exceeding supply additions
items.quote: On the demand side, we signed demand contracts for 11,000 new seats in Q1 FY25.

items.statement: Exit month blended occupancy at 71%; mature centers (>12 months) at 84% occupancy
items.quote: Our exit month occupancy rate was 71%, indicating strong demand for flexible workspaces, aligned with our supply additions. It is important to note that this is a blended occupancy level. Occupancy typically increases as new centers mature. For centers older than 12 months, the occupancy rate stands at 84%.

items.statement: Client base: 65% large corporates/MNCs, 22% SMEs, 13% startups; 36% multi-center clients; 56% revenue from 100+ seat cohorts
items.quote: In terms of occupied seats, approximately 65% of our client base consists of large corporates or MNCs, 22% are SMEs, 13% are startups and the remainder are freelancers. In our portfolio, we have 36% multi -centre clients. The contribution of 100 -plus seat c ohorts to our total cohort remains robust at 56

items.statement: Average client tenure 34 months with 24-month lock-in; 100+ seat cohorts average 46 months tenure with 36-month lock-in
items.quote: The total average client tenure in our portfolio is 34 months, with a lock-in period of 24 months. For greater than 100-seat cohorts, the average tenure is 46 months, with a lock-in tenure of 34 months.

items.statement: Gross debt INR30 crores, debt-to-equity 0.08, net debt-to-equity negative 0.41 as of June 30, 2024
items.quote: As of 30th June, our liquidity position stood at a very comfortable INR185 crores. The gross debt at consolidated level stood at INR30 crores. As a result, our debt-to-equity is INR0.08, which was INR0.20 in Q1 of FY '24. And our net debt-to-equity stood at negative INR0.41, which was negative INR0.13 in Q1 of last fiscal.

items.statement: ROCE improved from 43% in FY24 to 68% annualised in Q1 FY25
items.quote: Our ROCE has improved from 43% in FY'24 to 68% (on an annualised basis) for Q1 of the current financial year.

items.statement: Managed aggregation model at 67% of seats; target 65-68% MA vs SL mix for FY25
items.quote: Out of the new seats added or under-fit out, 79% were under our asset-light managed aggregation model, reinforcing our commitment to this effective business model. We continue to maintain a strong portfolio of 67% seats under this risk-averse model.

items.statement: Differentiated strategy focusing on sub-500 seat cohorts (30-54% CAGR 2020-22) with mid-size centers creating operational moat
items.quote: According to a CBRE report, the demand for flexible workspaces across these sub-500 seat cohorts, which is 1 to 50, 51 to 100 and 100 to 500 seats had been growing consistently with a CAGR of almost about 30%, 41% and 54% between 2020 and 2022. Why we get excited about this cohort is because this cohort helps us with better price realization. Then we are able to manage it's a manageable churn and

items.statement: New seat additions (20,000 in last 6 months) temporarily impact profitability until seats mature and fill up
items.quote: We have added around 20,000 seats in the last six months. The seats typically get filled up over a period. So we are seeing some impact maybe in the current quarter. And as I mentioned in my opening remarks that it has to be seen over a longer period. The quarter may not reflect the numbers.

items.statement: Focus on leadership and talent development through learning and development initiatives
items.quote: Some other exciting things on the anvil for Awfis include a more enhanced user experience incenters and online with mobile app and website revamp, more focus on leadership and talent development through learning and development initiatives.

items.statement: Targets double-digit volume growth for FY25 with Mass Premium at mid-to-high single digit and P&A at mid-double digit
items.quote: Our outlook for a double-digit growth for the Financial Year FY25, we are of the view that we are on the right track.

items.statement: Expects to exit FY25 with EBITDA margin better than Q1's 10%, targeting early double digits
items.quote: Our outlook is that we should exit the year better than the Q1 EBITDA, maybe early double digits.

items.statement: Maintenance CAPEX guided at Rs 15 crore annually for Telangana distillery; growth CAPEX of ~Rs 450 crore for two 150 KLPD distilleries to achieve near 100% captive ENA
items.quote: Our CAPEX guidance is largely in form of our strategy CAPEX for our distillery in the state of Telangana which is about 15 crores on annualized basis.

items.statement: Backward integration CAPEX of ~Rs 450 crore for two 150 KLPD distilleries expected to yield 450 bps gross margin improvement; benefits likely from FY27
items.quote: The capital required for this is we believe that what we need are two distillers of 150 KLPD each and the capital required for this will be roughly Rs. 450 crores.

items.statement: ICONiQ White annual run rate at ~4 million cases in Q1 FY25, up from 2.3 million cases in FY24; expects to double FY24 volume
items.quote: Currently the annual run rate for ICONiQ White is between 4 to 5 million cases and is expected to double its volume from last year's base of 2.3 million cases.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA margin at 10% vs 6.5% in Q1 FY24; gross margin improved to 38.7% from 34.5% YoY driven by packaging savings and price hikes
items.quote: We also delivered a double-digit EBITDA margin at 10% in Q1 FY25 as compared to 6.5% EBITDA margin in Q1 of FY24.

items.statement: Gross margin expansion in Q1 FY25: ~3.1% from price increases, ~1% from COGS savings after netting incremental costs
items.quote: It's around 3.1% on the price and around (+1%) on the overall COGS after netting off the incremental cost.

items.statement: Annualized price hike benefit ~Rs 40 crore; Q1 FY25 benefit Rs 18-20 crore vs Q1 FY24; further hikes expected in Telangana, West Bengal, Himachal
items.quote: The total aggregate price increase on an annualized basis, Ramki can I leave on you if my number is off, but I think it's just about Rs. 40 crores on an annualized basis.

items.statement: ENA prices range-bound at Q4 FY24 exit levels, marginally lower; 30% captive from 60M LTR Telangana distillery at 100% utilisation; need 300 KLPD more for ~100% captive
items.quote: As we shared earlier , our outlook was that the ENA prices for FY25 would be range bound. This is the exit price of Q 4 of FY24 which is the last Financial Year and so far, the prices are holding on to that level, maybe marginally lower

items.statement: Packaging savings: mono-carton removal on Sterling B7, OC Blue, ICONiQ; PET conversion on Officer's Choice in 6 states; market bottle utilisation target 20% vs 12-13% last year; glass/PET light-weighting
items.quote: We are this year planning our market bottle utilization at about 20% which was about 12%-13% last year. So, that's about a 7% increase in our market bottle utilization.

items.statement: P&A volume salience rose to 36.9% in Q1 FY25 from 33.5% in Q1 FY24; value salience rose to 46.1% from 43.2%
items.quote: Our P &A volume salien ce has increased to 36.9% in Q1 of FY25 as compared to 33.5% in Q1 of FY24. That is an increase of roughly 3.5% and the value salience has increased to 46 .1% in Q1 of FY25 as compared to 43.2% in Q1 of FY24

items.statement: Q1 FY25 industry growth ~2-3%; early signs of recovery in July; rural consumption improving with normal monsoon; Mass Premium segment saw low single-digit degrowth
items.quote: The overall industry growth was about 2% or 3%. We are seeing some sign of recovery in early July. So, that's a good sign for us.

items.statement: Telangana overdue receivables ~Rs 384 crore as of June 30; expect resolution over next quarter with improvement from September; working capital access improved post-IPO
items.quote: The total receivables from Telangana outstanding as on 30th June is around Rs. 384 crores which is overdue.

items.statement: Repaid ~Rs 800 crore gross debt from IPO proceeds; zero long-term debt; fresh working capital debt of Rs 325 crore at 8.5% vs prior 10-10.5%; annual interest cost to fall ~50%
items.quote: We repaid around Rs. 800 crores of gross debt which was there from the IPO proceeds. As on date we have around Rs. 325 crores of working capital debt which is a fresh debt after repayment of all the debt.

items.statement: IPO completed July 2024; proceeds used to repay Rs 720 crore bank debt and clear all VAT overdues; now raising low-cost working capital facilities for growth
items.quote: With the successful completion of the IPO process in July '24 in line with the main purpose of use of the IPO proceed being repayment of debt amounting to Rs. 720 crores. Accordingly, all the bank debt has been repaid.

items.statement: Andhra Pradesh new excise policy expected Oct 1; includes retail privatization and national brand entry, enabling ICONiQ launch; currently ~1.9M cases sold in AP
items.quote: Andhra Pradesh policies yet to be out . A s and when it is announced it will be effective 1 st October. But from what we understand there are three important elements of the policy. The first element is privatization of retail which is a positive for a Company like ABD

items.statement: India-UK FTA still under discussion; no firm timeline; closure would significantly reduce bulk scotch cost as India's largest user after Pernod and Diageo
items.quote: India-UK FTA is still at a discussion stage. Of course, the new prime minister of UK has made a positive statement about the FTA but timelines are not yet formed.

items.statement: Launched Zoya luxury gin in Maharashtra (Mumbai, Thane, Pune, Nashik, Nagpur); ICONiQ White expanded to Madhya Pradesh, Meghalaya, Chandigarh and paramilitary channel; launched 180ml PET Hippy pack in UP, Maharashtra, Daman
items.quote: We successfully launched Zoya ABD's first luxury gin and the inaugural product in our Prem brand portfolio which focuses only on the premium and the luxury portfolio in the state of Maharashtra.

items.statement: Partnership model (not distribution) for premium/luxury brands with global companies; seeking partners with serious India intent, pan-India distribution access, and co-investment in brand building
items.quote: We have maintained a position that we are looking for a partnership model and not a distribution model. In the partnership model we are looking at global companies which have serious intent about India as a territory.

items.statement: Increased employee cost due to new hiring for premium/luxury vertical (Prem brand division) and general overhead increases
items.quote: Controlled advertising and marketing A&P spend which was largely offset by increased employee cost on account of new hiring mainly on account of setting up the vertical catering to our premium brand, focused on premium and luxury portfolio.

items.statement: Adopted new 25% tax regime; effective rate marginally higher in first year due to deferred tax; 25% from March 2026
items.quote: We have opted for the new regime of taxation which is 25%. So, the first year of shift there will be some deferred tax. So, it could be marginally higher by a percent. But after that from March '26 onwards it will be 25%.

items.statement: Telangana receivables delay impacted Q1 volume; if resolved, Q1 would have shown double-digit growth; expect resolution over next quarter
items.quote: If you have the right working capital access in Q1 which of course has been resolved post the IPO, we should have been in a double-digit growth. We should have been able to post a double-digit growth.

items.statement: Global sugar production estimated at 184 MMT vs consumption of 180.8 MMT for SY24-25, showing a surplus
items.quote: As per Czarnikow, the total global sugar production is now estimated at 184 MMT , while consumption is expected to be 180.8 MMT .

items.statement: India sugar production for SY23-24 estimated at 34 MMT, net production close to 32 MMT after ethanol diversion
items.quote: the sugar production for the SY 2023-24 is estimated to be 34 MMT as a few mills are still operational as the special season is in progress in Tamil Nadu. With diversion to ethanol is expected to be just over 2 MMT , the net sugar production will be close to 32 MMT.

items.statement: India closing stock by September 2024 expected at healthy 9 MMT, significantly above 2.5 months consumption norm
items.quote: Considering an opening stock last year of about 5.5 MMT and forecasted domestic consumption of 28.5 MMT, the closing stock by September '24 is expected to be a healthy 9 MMT.

items.statement: FRP increased by Rs. 25 per quintal for SY24-25, no policy clarity on ethanol diversion rollback or MSP revision
items.quote: The FRP increase which has already been announced for SY 2024-25 by Rs. 25 a quintal will also attract more farmers to plant sugarcane which aug urs well for the industry

items.statement: No policy clarity on rollback of ethanol diversion and revision of MSPs despite industry representations
items.quote: We still don't have any policy clarity with regard to the rollback of ethanol diversion and revision of MSPs despite number of representations from the industry.

items.statement: Standalone Q1 FY25 revenue Rs. 751 crore up 7.58%, EBITDA loss Rs. 28.59 crore vs loss Rs. 14.63 crore, loss after tax Rs. 78.59 crore vs Rs. 45.77 crore
items.value: Revenue 751 cr, EBITDA -28.59 cr, PAT -78.59 cr
items.quote: The standalone revenue from operations for the quarter ended 30th June 2024 at Rs. 751 crores registered an increase of 7.58% as against Rs. 698 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The EBITDA for the quarter ended was loss of Rs. 28.59 crores as against the loss of Rs. 14.63 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. The standalone loss after tax for the quarter

items.statement: Cane cost increased to Rs. 3,491/MT from Rs. 3,267/MT previous year
items.quote: So, overall cane cost is about Rs. 3,491 per MT and last corresponding year was Rs. 3,267 per MT.

items.statement: Refinery long-term loan Rs. 200 crore unchanged, short-term loan reduced to Rs. 220 crore from Rs. 596 crore
items.quote: So far as long-term loan of the refinery is concerned, including EID Loan is Rs. 200 crores. The same was Rs. 200 crores in the last year. As far as the short-term loan is concerned it was about Rs. 220 crores for the current quarter as against the previous year's corresponding quarter of Rs. 596 crores.

items.statement: Short-term borrowings increased due to working capital needs, inventory up ~Rs. 300 crore year-on-year
items.quote: term loan is basically the working capital. Since our networking capital has gone up, thereby, your short-term loans also have gone up. Because even if you look at inventory also, inventories has gone up around Rs. 300 crores, in line with the short-term loans also increase

items.statement: Aspire to match last year's crushing numbers in current fiscal despite Tamil Nadu challenges
items.quote: In the fiscal that we are currently in, we would aspire to almost match last year's number; however, there could be some challenges in Tamil Nadu on that, but we are working towards trying to match last year's number.

items.statement: Nutra Europe certification expected in next couple of weeks, billing to Europe from Q3 FY25 onwards
items.quote: So, yes, we do have some good news that is coming through in the next couple of weeks. So, I think we should be able to start billing to Europe towards the end of sort of Q3. Gautham: Q3 you said? Muthiah Murugappan: I think we should be billing from Q3 onwards

items.statement: Tamil Nadu recovery challenged by last year's deficient monsoon, El Nino impact takes 24 months to normalize, Karnataka area under cane slightly down but yields strong
items.quote: The deficient rainfalls of last year have certainly had an impact on Tamil Nadu. We are already seeing that, Venkat talked about the lower recoveries that we are experiencing, and it is only now that once the monsoons have picked up, we are starting to see some plant coming in. Tamil Nadu will remain challenging.

items.statement: Distillery margins fallen from target 20-21% EBITDA to single digits due to no ethanol price increase for sugarcane feedstock despite FRP hike
items.quote: When I talked about our dis tillery segment margins, we would have been very happy with 20 %-21% EBITDA business. That is what we were really building towards in the old policy framework. But I think once there was a reconsideration of this and the fact that prices were not taken up, these margins have fallen substantially and gone in sort of closer to single digit

items.statement: Brown sugar 'Amrit' launched at Rs. 80/kg under Parry Gold brand as penetrative pricing vs existing Rs. 100/kg product
items.quote: So, we are looking at pricing the new brown sugar which is nothing but your crystal brown sugar under the ‘Par ry Gold’ brand name and this is priced lower more as a penetrative pricing into the market in order to generate more trials from consumers

items.statement: Green Grow media from bagasse for soilless growing medium, large export and domestic potential, product and customer development ongoing
items.quote: The Green Grow Media is from bagasse, the residual bagasse. It is a soil-less growing medium, which you would find in greenhouses, got a lot of potential in the export market and in India. Product development and customer development is ongoing.

items.statement: LST division revenue growth expected at 5-8% for FY25; Chemical division revenue growth targeted at 8-10% for FY25
items.quote: For LST, since the capacities are always as of now, maxed out, anywhere our expectation is that it will be between 5% to 8%. And even for Chemical that we will try to get closer to 8% to 10%.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA expected to grow 7-8% to around INR120 crores in FY25 from INR110 crores last year
items.quote: Last year, we made an EBITDA of INR110 crores consolidated. So obviously, you can take a growth of 7% to 8%. So, of that, it comes to around INR120 crores.

items.statement: Chemical division EBITDA margin target raised to 8-9% from current 5-6%; PAT margin target around 6%
items.quote: Last year, we are making an EBITDA of around 5% to 6% in Chemical division, but our forecast for the coming years is to make EBITDA of around 8% to 9% in Chemical division. And PAT is around 6%.

items.statement: LST rental business maintains steady EBITDA margin of 48-52%
items.quote: In rental business in LST, we are constantly keeping an EBITDA of around 48% to 52%, between 40% to 52%.

items.statement: LPG terminal capex estimated at INR700-750 crores for 64,000 ton capacity at JNPT
items.quote: So, it's around INR700 crores -- INR700 crores to INR750 crores, that is the capex required for building that 64,000 capacity of LPG.

items.statement: 18,000 KL capacity addition at JNPT fully utilized at 100%
items.quote: And this result also include your 18,000 KL capacity which has already come into the existence. So, there is a 100% capacity utilization there? Rishi Pilani: Yes

items.statement: LPG terminal capacity tied up with BW LPG and CPIL; orders for such tanks typically roll in near completion
items.quote: So, see, we already have a certain capacity that is tied up with BW LPG and CPIL. And generally, the orders for such type of LPG tanks start rolling in once they come nearer to completion.

items.statement: Chemical division focusing on niche products like food preservatives and lube oil additives; pursuing FDA and REACH certifications for export expansion
items.quote: The product mix we have is a very niche product mix, like food preservatives, the lube oil additives, where the custom -- and what we are doing is we are also getting new certifications, like FDA and REACH and all we are in the process of that, so that we can maximize the sale of the products to not only within the domestic region, but also export it.

items.statement: Exploring new products including methyl benzoate and lube oil additive derivatives; details proprietary
items.quote: See, we are exploring a lot of other products like methyl benzoate and we are also looking at some derivatives of the lube oil additives.

items.statement: Raw material purchasing system modified to achieve better pricing benefits in Chemical division
items.quote: The raw material purchasing has been also modified the system of purchasing to give us benefits of better pricing in raw material purchasing.

items.statement: Chemical division demand remained intact in Q1 FY25; volume and margin growth expected from Q3 FY25
items.quote: Chemical division demand remained intact. So, you can see there is a June to June, Chemical division has performed steadily. And overall EBITDA, you're talking, yes, you can take INR500 crores revenue and EBITDA of INR100 crores, so 20%, 23%.

items.statement: LST growth limited to 5-7% range until new LPG terminal commissioned; Goa terminal not at full capacity but capturing available market share
items.quote: In JNPT and Cochin also, we are now -- the tank capacities are fully utilized. So, for us to expect that we can get step jumps even by doing changes in products and all is not really tactical beyond the 5% to 7% range.

items.statement: New JNPT capacities not competing for A/B/C class high-margin products; new berths reduce vessel waiting time benefiting JNPT attractiveness
items.quote: Currently, the capacities that are coming up in JNPT, none of them are of the same class as us. So, they are not there to handle the A class, B class and the C class products, which are the high revenue margin products.

items.statement: Chinese competition exists but quality preference and established customer base provide protection
items.quote: Yes. So, we always keep facing competition. But like I said, that in terms of quality, we are being favoured by our customers. So, we are -- so though China is giving us competition but we have our own customer base, and we are growing that.

items.statement: Chemical division capacity utilization increased steadily over 5-7 years without fresh working capital infusion
items.quote: If you see year-over-year basis for the last 5 to 7 years, the capacity utilization has steadily gone up without any infusion of fresh working capital into the company.

items.statement: No fresh debt or equity needed for capex; LPG equity contribution already secured; internal resources sufficient for tank additions
items.quote: It can be easily funded through internal resources. And thirdly is the LPG capex, which we are working on, for which we have already secured the -- whatever is the equity contribution that is required from GBL has been already secured by us.

items.statement: Legal steps ongoing against NBFC lenders; one lender dropped recovery; discussions with another lender progressing
items.quote: We are continuously taking all the legal steps to make sure that there is no impact on the company. And so far, we've not seen any impact. You must have seen that actually one of the lenders has dropped all its -- recover money from the company.

items.statement: Demerger of Chemical and Tank divisions pending court judgment; hearings not controlled by company timeline
items.quote: There is a legal issue with this diversification. We are waiting to get the court judgment in this matter. And we are -- unfortunately, the hearings are happening in a space that is not controlled by us in terms of time.

items.statement: Wharfage revenue decline due to jetty repair for 3 months (dredging during JM Baxi handover); one-in-a-decade event with no financial loss as pass-through
items.quote: This is like probably once -in-like-a-decade event. What happened is JNPT handed over the operations to of the jetty to JM Baxi and as per the handover clause, JNPT had to complete some maintenance, dredging and et c etc, on the jetty, which is like a part of the handover process

items.statement: EPC business being transferred to subsidiary; no fresh EPC projects until transfer complete; EPC not viewed as profit centre
items.quote: we are doing is slowly, slowly, we are transferring the entire EPC business into our EPC subsidiary. So, because of that, we are not taking any fresh projects into the EPC until this transfer is getting over

items.statement: Standalone PAT up 14% YoY to INR157 million; Consolidated PAT up 6% YoY to INR164 million in Q1 FY25
items.quote: During the Q1 of FY '25 on a stand-alone basis, profit after tax is 157 million as against 138 million for Q1 of financial year '24 with an increase of 14% Y-to-Y. And for consolidated basis during the quarter 1 of FY '25, profit after tax is 164 million as against 155 million for Q1 of financial year '24 with an increase of 6% Y-to-Y.

items.statement: Expects booking value growth of at least 20% annually, historically growing 30-35%
items.quote: We have been growing very significantly and we expect the growth to continue at least 20% and generally we have been growing at 30%, 35%.

items.statement: Plans to launch 5.8 lakh sq ft carpet area across Bhandup, Monte South, and Nexzone in next four quarters with GDV of INR1,300 crores
items.quote: So, this, in the next four quarters we intend to launch something in Bhandup around 1.5 lakh square feet carpet area. Monte South around 2 lakh square feet carpet area. Nextzone around 2.5 lakh square feet carpet area. The totalling figure comes, the GDP of the whole becomes around INR1,300 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 area sold 72,912 sq ft, booking value INR158 crores, collections INR186 crores
items.quote: Area sold stood at 72,912 square feet, booking value stood at INR158 crores, collection stood at INR186 crores.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 EBITDA INR69 crores at 40% margin, PBT INR44 crores, PAT INR38 crores
items.quote: Consolidated Q1 FY25 financial performance, total revenue stood at INR173 crores. EBITDA stood at INR69 crores which translates at 40% margin. Profit before tax stood at INR44 crores. Profit after tax stood at INR38 crores.

items.statement: Net debt reduced to INR718 crores as on 30 June 2024 from INR751 crores at end of FY24
items.quote: The net debt position — net debt has reduced to INR718 crores as on 30th June 2024, as against INR751 crores as at the end of FY24.

items.statement: Enabling resolution for INR500 crores fundraise via QIP or other routes; proceeds for debt repayment, asset acquisition, and new projects
items.quote: currently, the enabling resolution has been cleared. It is to raise funds, not necessarily through QIP route, but any QIP and other possible options are open. So, that is how enabling resolution has been made. Our committee has also formed on that and we are exploring all the possibilities. Once the money is raised the ultimate use is going to be one to repay a little bit of debt, one to acquire n

items.statement: Potential equity dilution of ~15% if INR500 crores raised at INR3,000 crores market cap
items.quote: Well, if you consider the enabling resolution of INR500 crores, that percentage will come to around 15% if you consider INR3000 crores as a market gap, but it will exactly, exact number will depend on when it is happening and how much it is happening.

items.statement: Process ongoing to merge private company assets/projects into listed entity; will follow QIP process
items.quote: So, we are in the process of consulting with our consultants and legal lawyers and others on how to go about bringing some of the assets from the outside listed company into the listed company. So, that process is going on. We will come back with all those announcements very soon. First, the process is going to be the QIP process. Then there is going to be a process which will immediately follow o

items.statement: Bhandup prices increased ~5% YoY historically; plan to continue at least that pace without hampering sales
items.quote: In the past, we have increased about 5% year-on-year, which is exactly not hampering the sales at all. So, we want to continue at least that pace.

items.statement: Realisation trend likely to continue in FY25 but at slower pace across projects due to OC readiness and market demand
items.quote: The trend is likely to continue. It may be at a slower pace, but still the price are likely to rise.

items.statement: Panvel demand booming due to Mumbai Trans Harbour Link and airport nearing completion; sustained sales despite township competition
items.quote: Nexzone as an area, Panvel is just booming. Hence the market is actually accepting the price hike. Bhandup as an area we are very confident of this area as per sales. So, we have been pushing the rates higher.

items.statement: QIP proceeds (Rs 100 Crores) for 3 Mumbai redevelopment projects; GMP sale proceeds (Rs 100-110 Crores) for growth capital, Baner-Pashan project, and EPC working capital collateral

items.statement: Ticket size qualification increasing; Raipur project completion will enable bidding for Rs 700+ Crore projects; targeting Rs 600-800 Crore projects
items.quote: We are in the process of almost finishing the Raipur, Chhattisgarh project, which will give us a single certificate of upwards of Rs 500 Crores which therefore will enable us to start bidding for projects upwards of Rs 700 Crores going forward.

items.quote: We are currently at 80% government. We would like to hopefully be at 70% government, 30% private or 65% government, 30%, 35% private. We do want to have private exposure. We do not want to be exposed only to government.

items.statement: Strategy to avoid projects in states with elections due in 12-18 months; prefer hospital projects in non-metro locations to reduce political risk
items.quote: And the second thing we also do is the elections are due for the last 12 months to 15 months, 18 months, we do not bag any order in that state because that is where time where people are busy with elections, and then there are risks.

items.statement: Net debt risen to Rs 38 Crores due to real estate JV investments; bridge loan of ~Rs 40 Crores taken for project launches pending QIP/GMP proceeds
items.quote: This fiscal year, we have seen our total debt go up because we are involved in new real estate joint ventures. As a result, our net debt has risen to Rs 38 Crores over the past last year.

items.statement: GMP divestment to Shinryo for Rs 155-157 Crores (net Rs 100-110 Crores) expected to close by end of month/early September; QIP approved, 6 months validity remaining

items.statement: Real estate sales booking Q1 FY25: 12,244 sq ft, Rs 7 Crores sale value, Rs 11 Crores collections
items.quote: In Q1 FY '25, we achieved new sales booking totalling 12,244 Square Feet, generating a sale value of Rs 7 Crores and a total collection of Rs 11 Crores.

items.statement: Labor availability shrinking; mitigating via design-build EPC (60-80% of projects) to improve labor efficiency 15-20% at drawing board level
items.quote: And the only other thing in our industry that is pulling us back is the availability of labor which is shrinking regularly. And so therefore, to counter that, we are focusing 60 % - 70% - 80% of our projects on design and build EPC mode.

items.statement: Political risk mitigated by avoiding orders in election-bound states 12-18 months prior; hospital projects in non-metro areas less prone to political interference
items.quote: What happens is these projects are generally not in the radar of politicians. The fund is allocated by the departments in their health care projects, there is very little risk of them being stalled or cancelled if there is any political change in the state.

items.statement: Promoter holding at 31%; company prioritizes growth over maintaining promoter stake percentage; promoter may or may not participate in fund raises
items.quote: See when the company needs capital to grow and if it has to come from beyond the promoter and if it means there is a plus minus some dilution to the promoter stake, I think we, as a firm, are ready to face that because I think the company is a bit more important than the exact ratio of the promoter holding in the company.

items.statement: No significant legal cases with material financial liability; routine contingencies only
items.quote: We don't envisag e any that kind of payment or something is coming up in the system. We can -- it is a normal routine kind of thing. So there has been a good 60% growth in the overall air freight sector on quarter-to-quarter basis.

items.statement: Management expects growth to continue in Q2 FY25 and coming quarters due to a good pipeline and tailwinds.

items.quote: Our EBITDA margin has also increased on quarter-to-quarter basis. EBITDA has increased by 10.6% and almost two times what it was year on year.

items.quote: we are not present in the LCL segment as of now. I think that is the only segment which is not there with us, but we are looking at organic growth through that segment, maybe through if we can work closely, you know in some acquisition and all.

items.statement: Strategy includes regular roadshows in US and LatAm countries to acquire overseas clients and agents for export business growth.

Similar activity we keep on doing for LatAm countries also and that is going to continue for us.

items.quote: So, Maheshji as we have already started our commercial production with introduction of 3,000 metric tons of capacity at New Anjar facility and with effect from 1st October, we shall be rolling out another 9,000 metric tons of capacity.

items.quote: With a strong order book outlook, coupled with our strategy to capitalize on the increasing capex by our customer segments, we expect strong top-line as well as bottom-line growth in near-medium term.

items.statement: Power sector orders expected earlier, possibly Q4 FY25 or Q1 FY26, driven by 80 GW thermal expansion
items.quote: Now, we are expecting it to get those orders much earlier maybe in the last quarter of this fiscal or maybe the first quarter of the next fiscal.

items.statement: Fully qualified for supercritical power plants with BHEL and NTPC, approved by NPCIL for nuclear, pursuing overseas nuclear opportunities
items.quote: We are qualified with BHL. We are qualified with NTPC. We are qualified as any other player in the Indian power sector market, who shall be putting up these supercritical power plants.

items.statement: Advanced discussions with global EPC player for step-two agreement, may formalize in weeks, discussing 2-3 large jobs
items.quote: We are in very, very advanced stage of discussion for that particular matter. We are calling that as step two. In that step two, we shall be formalizing all of our agreements and that is very much on the pipeline.

items.statement: 40-45% of business from exports, orders on FOB basis so freight cost impact not borne by company
items.quote: So, as far as our orders are concerned, our orders are FOB basis. So, the impact of the cost increase in terms of freight cost does not come to us

items.statement: IPO proceeds Rs 3,250 million, utilized Rs 935.32 million so far: Rs 179.82 million working capital, Rs 755.50 million debt repayment
items.quote: Of the total IPO proceeds of 3,250 million, we have already utilized 935.32 million so far, towards 179.82 million towards working capital needs and 755.50 million towards repayment of debts.

items.statement: Full Rs 175 crore debt repayment completed before 10 July 2024, though only Rs 75.5 crore reflected as of 30 June
items.quote: We had already made a payment of INR175 crores towards repayment of working capital. However, the amount of working capital demand loan, which were actually paid out post-30th June, that is why this amount is shown as INR75.5 crores.

items.statement: Full-year revenue, margin and order inflow guidance to be provided in about a month after Anjar capacity rollout and customer approvals
items.quote: So, in a month's time, we will make sure to give you a good guidance in this respect

items.statement: Revenue: piping division 81.3% (13.2% YoY growth), heavy fabrication 7.4% (295.2% YoY growth)
items.quote: Revenue from piping division saw a 13.2% year -over-year growth, contributing 81.3% over revenue, whereas heavy fabrication division saw a year -on-year growth of 295.2% with sales contribution of 7.4% of the growth.

items.statement: Heavy fabrication unit fully occupied, no order booking challenges
items.quote: our heavy fabrication unit is also fully occupied. So, we do not have any challeng e as far as the order booking is concerned for that particular unit

items.statement: Not pursuing Indian nuclear sector aggressively due to long project durations, focusing on overseas nuclear opportunities
items.quote: However, since the jobs which come from the nuclear sector, particularly from Indian customers, they run for years and years together. So, we are not very keen to go full blast, particularly for the nuclear sector in India.

items.statement: Expects capacity utilization close to 75% for full year FY25 despite weak global steel demand
items.quote: For Q1 '25, which means April, May, June we were close to 80% capacity utilization, and we hope to be close to 75% for the full year despite steel not doing very well in the world.

items.statement: Graphite anode plant capex spent so far is around INR 60 crores, mainly for land and pre-operative expenses
items.quote: So on the graphite anode part of it, the total capex that the company has done till now is around INR 60 crores, out of which between INR 30-35 crores is purely on account of land.

items.statement: Graphite electrode expansion from 80,000 to 100,000 tons per annum is fully complete and all new facilities are running smoothly
items.quote: As you are aware, our expansion from 80,000 to 100,000 tons is fully complete and all the new facilities are running very smoothly.

items.statement: Over 100 million tons of new greenfield electric arc furnace capacity announced globally, with ~64 million tons likely operational by 2027
items.quote: As we speak, more than 100 million tons of new Greenfield capacities have already been announced, which will be in operation between now and 2030, out of which about 64 million tons is likely to be in operation by as early as 2027.

items.statement: Electrode demand likely to increase by 100,000 to 125,000 tons in next 3 years due to new EAF capacities
items.quote: So that is likely to give a boost to electrode demand to the extent of 100,000 to 125,000 tons in the next 3 years or so.

items.statement: Spread between electrode prices and needle coke prices narrowed, pressuring margins over last 6-7 quarters
items.quote: But the spread between electrode prices and needle coke prices did narrow down, bringing pressure on margins as is evident when you look at our margins for the last 6-7 quarters.

items.statement: Anode project EBITDA margin estimated at 30-35% at $10,000/ton anode price, falling to ~20% at $7,000/ton, but could reach 25-26% with lower power costs
items.quote: So right now, I mean it's just a temporary blip right now, which you -- if you see at USD10,000 per ton, our EBITDA margin was coming to around 30%, 35%. And the same prices go down to USD 7,000, the EBITDA margins go down to around 20%.

items.statement: Needle coke prices corrected through past year; electrode pricing remains under pressure due to reduced demand from Chinese steel exports
items.quote: The electrode pricing continues to remain under pressure due to reduced demand. The needle coke prices kept correcting through the past year due to difficult market conditions.

items.statement: Graphite anode powder prices fell from $10,000-12,000/ton to $6,000-8,000/ton as battery prices dropped from $85-100/kWh to $50-60/kWh
items.quote: Today when the prices have gone down for the batteries up to $50 to $60 per KWH, the price of anode too today, you are getting between $6,000 to $7,000 per KWH depending from application to application.

items.statement: Power cost is 30-35% of variable cost for anode plant; negotiating with state governments for cheaper power (targeting INR 5-5.5/kWh vs current higher rates)
items.quote: We are trying to renegotiate with the state government and different other state governments in India on the power prices because power constitutes around 30% to 35% of the variable cost in this particular project.

items.statement: Current HEG power cost INR 5-5.5/kWh at existing site due to thermal plant shutdown subsidy; not automatically transferable to new anode plant location
items.quote: HEG's current cost of between INR5 to INR5.5 is on the basis of HEG shutting off its thermal power plant. So when HEG shuts off its thermal power plant, in lieu of that, the government has given a subsidy and giving power at INR5 to INR5.5.

items.statement: Anode customers like Exide and Ola require 15-18 month qualification process; once qualified, switching is difficult due to 42 raw materials in battery production
items.quote: So once they select between an HEG or an Epsilon or Himadri or any other company that they want to buy the anode from, then it is very difficult or I'd rather say, not worthwhile to try and consider a change.

items.statement: Chinese anode producers selling below variable cost due to overcapacity; China has 90% of global anode manufacturing
items.quote: Right now, they would be importing this from China or any other company. I mean, obviously, China has 90% of the anode manufacturing around the world.

items.statement: Scheme of arrangement for restructuring and demerger progressing with SEBI and stock exchanges; expects completion by middle of next year after NCLT approval
items.quote: After the stock exchange approval, the scheme will also require approval from the NCLT, National Company Law Tribunal. We expect the process to be completed by middle of next year.

items.statement: GST show cause notice for INR 282 crores received; company evaluating and will respond shortly, prima facie demand not correct
