items.statement: Tomato capacity expansion done outside PLI scheme as PLI commitments already overshot
items.quote: So, we have actually done it outside the PLI, because whatever we had committed under the PLI, we had already overshot that. So, the expansion of tomato is outside PLI.

items.statement: Frozen category seeing huge surge in demand globally post-COVID; business development with big brands in US, UK, Europe, Gulf takes minimum 8 months; spray dried powder seasoning business flat for 1-1.5 years
items.quote: across the world we are seeing a huge surge in demand for frozen categories, especially post-COVID, we would like to enter. But for business development and I mean the start of business, there's a huge time requirement.

items.statement: Exploring new geographies: Russia (banana/pulp opportunity from Ecuador political tension), Sri Lanka, UK, Spain (sold tomato pulp to Spain in FY23)
items.quote: Russia is one of the markets that we are actually exploring. Sri Lanka is another market that we are exploring. The UK is another market that we are actually exploring for tomatoes. In FY'23, we even sold to Spain.

items.statement: Alphonso realization 2.5x Totapuri per metric tonne; portfolio has more Totapuri as it sells globally; farmer relations provide procurement price advantage (x-1 vs industry 1x)
items.quote: If realization per metric tonne for Totapuri is 1x, then realization per metric tonne for Alphonso will be 2.5x. This depends on the raw material price.

items.statement: Pastry line business: first container exported to UK; 2 more lines by Oct-Nov, 5 more to follow; targets 10 lines generating >Rs 100 crore business; good EBITDA margins, in-house consumption advantage
items.quote: I believe that if we are able to put these 10 lines, this can generate more than 100 per business. We did see, in the pulping business, this year around or this quarter around that the prices of Totapuri were slightly higher and almost double.

items.statement: Total export shipment deferment approximately Rs 25 crore (Rs 10.76 crore accounting deferment + Rs 9.8-10 crore lost shipments due to vessel unavailability)
items.quote: Approximately Rs. 25 crores. All put together, as in, all put together including the Rs. 11 crores would have been around Rs. 25 crores.

items.statement: Tomato and guava expected to drive volume growth in FY25 due to good monsoon and doubled tomato capacity; mango sales volume similar to FY24 despite 25% lower processing
items.quote: Because of a good monsoon this year we are expecting tomatoes to be good and since we have also more than doubled our capacity in tomato, I think that should help us push through.

items.statement: Revenue CAGR of around 20% over next three years driven by ATBS, antioxidants and VOPL products
items.quote: We expect our revenue to have a CAGR of around 20% over the next three years, which will be mainly driven by ATBS, antioxidants, and other products from VOPL.

items.statement: On track for 20% CAGR revenue guidance over three years
items.quote: Yes, I think we are on track for that one. We have basically guided for a 20% CAGR over a period of three years.

items.statement: Overall FY25 capex approximately INR570 crores including VOPL and ATBS expansion
items.quote: The overall capex to be spent in FY '25 would be approximately INR570 crores. This includes VOPL.

items.statement: VOPL capex plan exceeding INR500 crores for MEHQ, Guaiacol, anisole, 4-meth and Iso Amylene derivatives
items.quote: VOPL has outlined a capital expenditure plan exceeding INR500 crores, focusing on production of MEHQ, Guaiacol, anisole, 4-meth, and other Iso Amylene derivatives.

items.statement: ATBS expanded capacity to come into play from FY26
items.quote: The expanded capacity for ATBS will come into play from FY'26, and this will aid further growth in ATBS.

items.statement: MEHQ plant meaningful revenue contributions expected from FY26 onwards
items.quote: Meaningful revenue contributions from the MEHQ plant can be expected from FY26 onwards.

items.statement: Remaining VOPL products scheduled for commissioning in second half of FY25
items.quote: Additionally, the remaining products under capex are scheduled for commissioning in the second half of FY '25.

items.statement: Antioxidant capacity utilization expected to reach 50% in FY25
items.quote: Secondly as far as 50% capacity utilization, yes, for FY25 I think we should be coming closer to that one year.

items.statement: ATBS witnessing robust growth in FY25 with demand exceeding supply for high-grade ATBS
items.quote: ATBS, which is our largest product, is witnessing a robust growth in FY '25.

items.statement: Butylphenol and IB derivatives performing well with sustained growth expected
items.quote: The butylphenol business, along with other IB derivatives like PTBBA, Ester, continues to perform well, and we expect the growth to be sustained going ahead as well.

items.statement: Antioxidant sales showing good growth in FY25 despite weak global demand
items.quote: In antioxidants, we had recorded approx. INR130 crores of sales in FY24, and even though the overall global demand for antioxidants is going through a weak period, we are seeing a good growth in our AO sales in FY '25.

items.statement: Normalized EBITDA margins of 26% to 27% expected on sustainable basis from Q2 onwards
items.quote: I think one can expect normalized EBITDA margins of 26% to 27% on a sustainable basis.

items.statement: Q1 margin dip due to raw material price increases, logistics issues, inventory in transit, and missing high-margin customized products
items.quote: The raw material prices increased during Q1. So you will see some price increase happening in Q2. Secondly, there were a lot of logistics issues in Q1, a lot of delays, unavailability of tankers. So we had a lot of inventory in transit, which actually reflect a sale in Q2. Then, of course, other than the regular shutdowns that Kaviraj mentioned, we also have some customized products, which are qui

items.statement: Prices stabilized with raw material cost changes passed through contracts
items.quote: Prices are presently stabilized. It's not, there is not much of a moment as such, because anyway, we have our, you know, contracts in place. So whatever price change that happens in terms of the raw materials, that is passed on.

items.statement: Freight costs increased but passed on to customers; lead times increased
items.quote: Well, one, the lead times have increased. One has to keep that in mind. So the delivery time has increased. Secondly, while the freight costs have gone up, we are thankfully in a position to pass on most of that to our customers.

items.statement: Electricity cost up ~10% per unit; coal prices also risen; renewables cover 40-50% of energy
items.quote: One is the electricity cost itself has gone up because there is a raise in prices that has happened in electricity. So that's almost like a 10% kind of a raise that has happened on a unit basis. Secondly, there is also some rise in coal prices which is there, which is seen and that's essentially why the...

items.statement: High-grade ATBS constitutes over 70% of ATBS volumes; margin difference minimal due to higher production cost
items.quote: So, yes, 70% and 70% more than 70% is the high-grade ATBS because that is essentially what is being now asked by the customers.

items.statement: IBB, IB, HPMTBE and customized products revenue expected to remain steady in FY25
items.quote: The revenues from IBB, IB, HPMTBE, and customized products is expected to remain steady during FY'25.

items.statement: ATBS 90-95% export; domestic growing as customers realize benefit of local ATBS production
items.quote: ATBS, well, it's 90% - 95% export, but domestic is also growing because our customers are realizing since the ATBS producer is in India, it makes sense to make the ATBS polymer in India also.

items.statement: MEHQ main demand in China; Guaiacol demand in India and export; sampling through traders for exports
items.quote: Well, the main demand is in China for MEHQ. Guaiacol there is demand in India as well. So it does cater to local as well as export. We have started sampling through traders, which will be used in export sales.

items.statement: ATBS demand exceeds supply; high-grade quality requirement limits production capacity
items.quote: See, in ATBS right now, the demand exceeds the supply. Because the demand, which is there, it's for a very, very high grade ATBS quality, which restricts our production capacity.

items.statement: Q1 FY25 net income INR533.98 crores (19% YoY), EBIT INR114.8 crores (23% YoY), PAT INR86 crores (24% YoY)
items.quote: On a standalone, Y-on-Y basis, the net income for quarter ended 30th June, 2024 is INR533.98 crores as against INR448.5 crores, registering a 19% growth. The EBIT increased by 23% to INR114.8 crores as against INR93.44 crores, and the PAT increased by 24% from INR69.42 crores to INR86 crores on a Y-on-Y basis.

items.statement: Product revenue mix: ATBS 33%, butylphenol/IB derivatives 21%, IBB 15%, IB/HPMTBE 12%, AO 8%, customized 4%
items.quote: ATBS is roughly around 33%, IBB is around 15% odd, butylphenol and IB derivatives is roughly around 21%. The customized products is around 4% and IB & HPMTBE those products are around 12%. AO is around 8% and rest is others.

items.statement: VOPL established as 100% owned subsidiary for niche specialty chemicals manufacturing
items.quote: Vinati Organics Limited has established a 100% owned subsidiary Veeral Organics Private Limited (VOPL), dedicated to the manufacturing of niche speciality chemicals.

items.statement: New antioxidant product timeline uncertain; typical new project gestation 12-18 months
items.quote: Very difficult to answer this as of now without knowing what kind of AOs would be getting added to the entire lineup. But typically, the range is around 12 to 18 months is essentially what happens with any new project.

items.statement: Revenue growth guidance for FY25 is north of 15%
items.quote: Our revenue guidance for the year though still remains at north of 15%.

items.statement: EBITDA margins expected to improve YoY for next 2-3 years
items.quote: I think an improving trend is what we should expect YoY for the next 3 odd financial years.

items.statement: Total capex commitment of Rs 30 crore for capacity expansion and brand building, Rs 5 crore for cultivation expansion, Rs 45-50 crore for hospitality over next 2 years
items.value: Rs. 30 odd crore... Rs. 5 odd crore... Rs. 45 crore - Rs. 50 crore
items.quote: In our CAPEX outlay for the next 2 years, all of it will get committed in this financial year, but some will get spend this year and some in the year after. But we expect to spend about Rs. 30 odd crore in capacity expansion and brand b uilding. We are expecting to spend ~Rs. 5 odd crore in expanding area under cultivation. I mentioned already about Rs. 45 crore - Rs. 50 crore in building the hosp

items.statement: Current capacity 4.5 million liters, expanding by ~25% to north of 5.6 million liters by end of FY25, commercialization by December 2024
items.value: 4.5 million liters to north of 5.6 million liters
items.quote: Our existing capacity at the moment is roughly 4.5 million liters. This year we are looking to expand that by approximately 25% and that will be north of 5.6 million liters by end of this financial year.

items.statement: Current utilization disproportionately high, above healthy 80-85% range, capacity constraint held back growth last 6-9 months
items.quote: Our utilization right now is disproportionately high. Normally, in a wine business about 80%-85% capacity utilization is considered very healthy. We are actually operating at higher than that, which is not ideal and we are adding capacity so that we do not feel the capacity constraint that we are feeling today.

items.statement: Sales volume ~4.2 million liters in FY24, volume CAGR ~30% from FY21-24
items.quote: Our sales in million liter s for last year was approximately 4.2 million liters. And our sales approximately as I mentioned earlier, have grown at about 30% at a CAGR level over the last three odd financial years

items.statement: EBITDA margin ~13.5% in FY24, improving trend for 3 years, gross margins maintained strong momentum in Q1 FY25 despite election disruptions
items.quote: Our EBITDA for the last financial year was ~13.5% and like I said earlier, it has been an improving trend from the last 3 years.

items.statement: Gross margins for Wine-in-Can slightly better than bottles by a couple of percentage points due to lower packaging cost
items.value: a couple of percentage points better
items.quote: On a gross margin level, it is fairly consistent with bottles as well, slightly better. You can say a couple of percentage points due to the lower packaging cost which is there in Cans.

items.statement: Premium and Luxury segments contribute 73% of revenue in FY24 (up from 70% in FY21), Super Premium + Luxury above Rs 1,200 contribute 14-15%, Premium Rs 600-1,200 contributes 55-60%, Value Rs 250-550 contributes 20-25%, Cans contribute ~5%
items.quote: If you look at our numbers for FY21, we had 70% contribution from the premium and super premium segments, and this has risen to 73% in FY24 on an expanded operating base.

items.statement: Top brands: Cabernet Sauvignon and Cabernet Franc-Shiraz each contribute 8-8.5%, Sparkling Noi contributes 5.5-6%, portfolio has 7-8 major brands each contributing 5-7%
items.quote: brands in the Red Wine segment, one with Cabernet Sauvignon a nd the other being Cabernet Franc-Shiraz both contribute roughly 8%-8.5% to our overall business. And then we have a bunch of other brands which are also contributing roughly 5%-6%, one being, for example, our Sparkling brand Noi, which is approximately number 3, which is also contributing about 5.5%-6% for us

items.statement: Geographic revenue split: South, West, North each 25-30%, East fourth; Top 6 states: Maharashtra, Karnataka, Delhi, Telangana, West Bengal, Goa
items.quote: The South, the West and the North regions contribute handsomely of course to our overall topline. And they are all within the range of 25%-30%. And then of course, that is followed by the East region in number 4.

items.statement: Channel split: 75% retail (off-trade), 25% HoReCa (on-trade); HoReCa share increasing over last 3 years; HoReCa leadership in Delhi, West Bengal, Karnataka, Odisha
items.quote: Currently as of last year, the split is roughly 75-25 with 75% coming from retail and 25% coming from HoReCa.

items.statement: 22,000 touch points pan India including Army Canteen; exclusive brands for Taj (Svara), ITC (Ghungroo), Living Liquidz (Amaris)
items.quote: We have now over 15 years developed a skill to build good, powerf ul brands and become a pan India business. Our deep relationships in the HoReCa segment are our key advantage that we have on our side and that has now resulted in us having 22,000 touch points pan India including the Army Canteen and leadership in certain states like Delhi etc

items.statement: Beneficiary of Maharashtra WIPS scheme, received Rs 14 crore in FY24
items.quote: Yes, we are availing WIPS scheme in Maharashtra like other wineries are and last year we received around Rs. 14 crore in FY24.

items.statement: Total debt ~Rs 90 crore (Rs 15 crore long-term, balance working capital); may add Rs 10-15 crore long-term debt for planned capex
items.quote: At this point of time, we have roughly Rs. 90 crore of debt in our balance sheet. About Rs. 15 crore is long term debt, and the balance is working capital. We may take an additional Rs. 10 crore - Rs. 15 crore of long-term debt going forward to complete all the CAPEX that we have planned over this year and the next year.

items.statement: Trading business contributed ~Rs 100 crore revenue in Q1 FY25, will reduce dramatically in Q2, shut down completely in Q3
items.quote: While in Q1, the trading business of the listed entity contributed approximately Rs. 100 crore in reve nue, t his will reduce dramatically in Q2 and will completely shut down in Q3

items.statement: S&D spend at ~30% of revenue, trending 28-30% over last 3-4 years; efforts underway to reduce S&D spend
items.quote: Basically we are at below 30% in the S&D trends and basically if you see from last 3-4 financial years, we are between 28% and 30%.

items.statement: 95% of packaging material procured domestically, improving trend over last few years
items.quote: 95% of all our packaging material at the moment is procured domestically and that has been an improving trend for the last few financial years.

items.statement: Imported and adapted ~12 varietals from best wine regions, successfully cloned; process of identifying new varietals ongoing; recently imported new varietals yet to be planted
items.quote: We have imported now and adapted approximately 12 varietals from the best wine growing regions in the world and have successfully cloned them as well. The process of identifying and incorporating new varietals is still ongoing.

items.statement: CAGR FY21-24: Net revenue ~25%, Gross profit ~26%, EBITDA ~100%, PAT ~300%
items.quote: Our net revenue as you can see has grown at a CAGR of ~25%, our gross profit at a CAGR of 26%, our EBITDA at a CAGR of 100% and PAT which is almost 300%.

items.statement: Crop failure risk from natural calamities mitigated by geographic diversification of vineyards (new 150-acre parcel 200km away)
items.quote: Something we have done recently and we will continue to do more of is that we have recently taken a new parcel of 150 acres of land under active farming which is approximately 200 kilometers away from our winery. Now, what that does is that it slightly derisks us from an agro-climate risk perspective.

items.statement: Vineyard tourism: Phase 1 - 40-key property on 170 acres at Akluj, capex within Rs 50 crore, ARR Rs 20,000-25,000, occupancy 40% first 3 years then 60-70%; city-based outlets planned for wine tasting and D2C
items.quote: We are expecting to build a 40 key property in Phase-1 at our location. We expect our ARRs to be around Rs. 20,000 - Rs. 25,000 per room night. In terms of occupancy rates, I think first maybe up to 3 years, it may be around 40% odd, but after 3 years it will pick up to about 60%-70% is our expectation.

items.statement: Wine-in-Can (TiLT) grew 30% YoY in Q1 FY25, record quarter; >90% retail channel; gross margins slightly better than bottles; major focus for future growth
items.quote: On the Cans currently, if we look at our business model, firstly we are very happy with our Can performance in quarter 1 of this year as we recorded a 30% growth over Q1 of last year. It was a record Q1 for us in terms of Cans.

items.statement: Investing in brand development and augmenting middle management, reflected in current EBITDA margins
items.quote: We are continuously investing towards brand development and augmenting middle management, and this is getting reflected in our EBITDA margins at the moment.

items.statement: Kolkata plant for pulses and grains to be commissioned in February 2025
items.quote: we plan to commercialize our new plant in Kolkata, dedicated to pulses and grains. Within, I think, it will be commissioned in the month of Feb 25.

items.statement: Surat plant land acquired, commissioning expected next financial year
items.quote: Additionally, we are also trying to launch a new plant in Surat, for which we have already acquired land and it will be commissioned in the next financial year.

items.statement: Kolkata plant capacity 100,000 tons per year for Masoor; edible oil capacity 50,000 tons per year
items.quote: Like we are already trying to install, we are installing 100,000 tons per year of Masoor. And around, edible is around 50,000 tons per year.

items.statement: Surat plant to process lentils, channa, and matar pulses
items.quote: We are putting for pulses. Like we can process three types of pulses in that unit. One is lentils. One is channa. And the third one will be matar.

items.statement: Edible oil refining operating margin targeted at 2% to 2.5% on processing only
items.quote: So, our operating margin will be around 2% to 2.5%. We will be just trying to have that on processing thing only.

items.statement: Processing margins expected to increase profit by 1.5% to 2% of revenue once plants operational
items.quote: So, we think our profit may increase like 1.5%, 2% of the revenue. It may increase.

items.statement: Domestic demand for food grains and pulses increasing enormously, driving shift from exports
items.quote: our domestic demands have increased very much enormously. You can say like, yes, our domestic demands have increased very much.

items.statement: Government prohibiting sugar and rice exports, encouraging ethanol production from grains, discouraging agri-commodity exports
items.quote: government prohibited the export of Sugar. If you see the results of March ending 23, the major revenue was from sugar exports. So, we were not mentally ready, to, like, the government will prohibit the export of Sugar and Rice from India.

items.statement: Shifting from exports (22% of Q1 FY24 revenue) to imports and domestic processing, developing own brand for retail
items.quote: reducing our Reliance on exports, which accounted for approximately 22% of our revenue in Q1 FY '24.

items.statement: Top five export markets identified as Bangladesh, Iraq, Dubai, Saudi Arabia, Egypt
items.quote: Bangladesh, we have been doing tenders. So, like, if we export, the number one country is Bangladesh. Iraq is buying international tenders. We can go to -- we can supply to Iraq. Then Dubai, Saudi Arabia, Egypt.

items.statement: Surat plant located 18 km from Hazira port at Navsari Surat Road industrial park for logistics advantage
items.quote: Navsari Surat Road is 18 kilometers from Vesu. There is an industrial park coming up, green industrial park. So, we have taken land over there.

items.statement: Will not exit quota-dependent sugar/rice export business but will wait for government quota opportunities
items.quote: We are not going to shut down our old business. We are not going to go away from that business because that is already there. That is already established. So, we are not going to switch off anything which we are having.

items.statement: Entering edible oil refining as related agri-commodity with ready market and conversion margin from crude to refined
items.quote: this edible oil is also something related to this agri-commodity which is used for consumers -- which are used by consumers. So, the trade is same and there is always margin of conversion from crude to refine.

items.statement: Textile brand Pakhi Commercial (Youmaa) and Luma brand showing good demand, repeat orders from MBOs, expansion plans underway
items.quote: In the initial stages, like, in Pakhi, they have launched the product somewhere in March or April. So, they are doing good. As for the results, I have seen on June and like, they are doing good. There is good demand coming, repeat orders coming from various MBOs, and we are doing very good on the other fronts also.

items.statement: Plan to add another processing unit in Bombay after Kolkata and Surat plants commission
items.quote: We plan to increase our processing units. One, after this two commissioning, we'll be planning to have one more unit at Bombay.

items.statement: Management reiterated prior full-year guidance; Q1 on track with confidence in market tailwinds for remainder of year
items.quote: I think we will stay with the guidance we provided last time. There is nothing that requires a review at this stage. Q1, w e have largely stayed on track with that projection, and we expect with some, and there is strong confidence that there will be market-related tailwinds to help in achieving whatever minor deficit that might be there

items.statement: Double-digit EBITDA margin targeted over two years, not in FY25, due to continued investments in brands, people and marketing
items.quote: the double digit is about a two-year journey. And so, it was not for this year. Bear in mind, again, I am saying that there are, the reason why it's a two-year journey because in these two years, we are also investing on brands and promotions and advertisement. We are investing in people ahead of the curve.

items.statement: India demand modest-to-sluggish in Q1 due to elections and weather; bounce-back expected from September driven by government infrastructure and housing spend
items.quote: Looking ahead in Quarter 2, we expect the demand scenario to be moderate in India and challenges on pricing to continue. However, we expect a bounce back from September onwards driven by government spends on infrastructure and housing, and this will all have a positive impact overall when we assess the full financial year in March-April.

items.statement: B2G pipe segment revenue at only 30% of normal in Q1 due to election-related fund delays; 50% budget increase for Jal Jeevan Mission expected to drive catch-up from September
items.quote: Overall, what we estimate is, and Ajay, you can help me, I think from steady state, the revenue was only about 30% of normal. So, the erosion was to the extent of 70%. It is something that we are reliably told that was experienced by other players also in the industry.

items.statement: Parador order bookings remain strong; third straight quarter of positive momentum on billings and order bookings
items.quote: Despite ongoing market sluggishness, Parador's order bookings remain strong. We have also introduced several new products ac ross categories to capture a larger market share

items.statement: Contribution margins improved across most segments despite price realization drops: Blocks +220 bps, Boards +170 bps, Putty +90 bps, Construction Chemicals +1000+ bps, Parador +370 bps YoY
items.quote: In Blocks, we improved our contribution margin by 220 basis points, in Boards by 170 basis points, in Putty by 90 basis points, in Construction Chemicals by over 1,000 basis points. And at Parador, the contribution margin improved by 370 basis points. All of these are in comparison with the same quarter last year.

items.statement: Consolidated EBITDA margin down ~290 bps YoY due to strategic investments in product mix shift, manpower, technology and marketing; other costs reduced ~100 bps
items.quote: Overall, the drop in EBITDA level, nearly about 290 basis points compared to last year, is attributed to strategic investments for the future. Essentially three categories, there is a shift in product mix, manpower costs, while we have already shaved off nearly 100 basis points on other costs, we have sufficient line of sight to guide this EBITDA percentage beyond 10% plus over the next couple of

items.statement: Price realizations fell across categories: Pipes -12%, Putty -6%, Parador -5.7%, Blocks -3%, Panels -3.5% YoY due to aggressive competitor pricing and sluggish demand
items.quote: In Blocks, the price realization dropped by about 3%, for Panels by about 3.5%, in Putty by nearly 6%, in P ipes and Fittings by about 12%, and in Parador by about 5.7%. This is largely attributed to aggressive price play by industry players in wake of sluggish demand and increased competitive activity

items.statement: Revenue mix shifted ~5% away from Roofing strategically; Pipes & Fittings crossed Rs 150 cr quarterly revenue for first time (78% YoY growth); Construction Chemicals grew 35% YoY with Tiling ~100%
items.quote: Significantly, in this quarter, we at HIL have made a nearly 5% swing away from Roofing in our overall revenue mix. It's a metric that we had highlighted we want to strategically shift, and the first signs of those impacts are now visible.

items.statement: Chennai AAC block plant commissioning in H2 FY25 adding 2 lakh tons (phase 1) with capacity for another 2 lakh tons; aims to be India's largest single-location AAC plant
items.quote: The Chennai plant that will get commissione d in the second half of this year, we are adding 2 lakh tons in the first wave of that expansion, and we have capacity for another 2 lakh tons after that, which can be quickly switched on. That site is being prepared with the view that it will be India's largest single location AAC block plant anywhere in the country by any player

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings capacity sufficient to reach Rs 800-1,000 cr revenue; further expansion planned to achieve Rs 1,500 cr milestone; capacity investments on drawing board
items.quote: See, we have shared that the aspiration for us is, first milestone on the Pipes and Fitting segment is to get near the Rs. 1,500 crore mark. At the moment, we feel we have the capacity which will take us to 800 to 1,000 with small incremental, but after that we need to put capacity. We are already on the drawing board to plan for those capacity expansion.

items.statement: Building Solutions serviced 1,500+ projects in Q1; Parador gained significant market share in Engineered Wood, Resilient Flooring, DIY and commercial channels across Germany, Nordics, Spain, North America, Middle East, China
items.quote: We have significantl y grown our customer base, having serviced over 1,500 plus projects in this period

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings volume grew 103% YoY (43% standalone excl. Crestia) vs industry 10-20%; Roofing maintained 25% market share with highest Q1 sales and price premium; Parador gained share in declining European markets
items.quote: This business, Pipes and Fittings, crossed the Rs. 150-crore quarterly revenue mark for the first time. It represents a 78% growth year-on-year on revenue. The business has grown twice as much in volume terms over last year to cross the 10,000 metric ton in sales for this quarter. You would recognize and appreciate that this growth rate is significantly higher than the overall industry growth and

items.statement: Jal Jeevan Mission budget hiked ~50% to Rs 75,000 cr for FY25; AMRUT 2.0, gram panchayat broadband, piped gas expansion create new B2G pipe opportunities
items.quote: If you recall, in this year's budget, the allocation, budgetary allocation for Jal Jeevan Mission has been hiked up by nearly 50%. So, last year, the government spent about Rs. 50,000 crore. The allocation this year is about Rs. 75,000 crore.

items.statement: Key hires: Manish Khandelwal as Head of Putty & Construction Chemicals (20+ yrs exp, grown businesses 0-1,000 cr); Pranav Desai as Head of Innovation; dedicated B2G sales organization built; ranked #12 Great Place to Work 2024, #1 in manufa
items.quote: I am happy to share that we have recently onboarded Mr. Manish Khandelwal as the new head of our Putty and Construction Chemical business. With that dedicated bandwidth and the strong experience of over 20 years that he brings in, in the home and Building segment, and having grown businesses from 0 to 1,000 crore, we feel the Construction Chemical and Putty business is poised for strong growth in

items.statement: Crestia acquisition integrated successfully; Topline (Crestia) contributed Rs 45 cr revenue in Q1; retail sales accelerated to highest ever in June
items.quote: The successful acquisition and integration of Crestia has been a major milestone and augurs well for our future inorganic pursuits. Our new product development engine is rolling with several new product launches in this quarter.

items.statement: Pipes & Fittings volume 10,000+ metric tons in Q1 (2x YoY); standalone volume growth 43% YoY (retail 37%, B2B 70%) vs industry 10-20%
items.quote: The business has grown twice as much in volume terms over last year to cross the 10,000 metric ton in sales for this quarter. You would recognize and appreciate that this growth rate is significantly higher than the overall industry growth and of other larger players in this segment.

items.statement: Parador volumes: FY22 10.8M sqm, FY24 6.8M sqm, Q1 FY25 run-rate ~7.6M sqm; prices up 20-25% since 2019 offsetting ~30-35% volume erosion
items.quote: So, we did around 10.8 million square meter in FY '22. Last year we did 6.8 million square meter. Right now, we are at the top 7.6 million square meter.

items.statement: PVC price decline since July creates headwind for Pipes & Fittings in Q2; Roofing margin recovery needs market price support and raw material stabilization; Putty faces intense price competition from paint companies
items.quote: However, we need to watch out for headwinds being created by the declining trend in PVC prices since July.

items.statement: Parador Q1 revenue Rs 313 cr (+7% YoY, +12.5% volume) despite key markets declining 5-10%; growth driven by Germany, Nordics, Spain, North America, Middle East, China
